# PROJECT GUIDE - Contributing & Priorities
Take it with a grain of salt, it's AI generated.


## How to read this

**Scope.** Everything under `cmd/` and `pkg/` at the commit above, tests ignored: 7,662 files — 5,872 Go files (1,572,472 lines) in 230 package directories, plus 1,790 embedded or bundled non-Go files (skill trees, plugin manifests and payloads, locale catalogs, data tables). The 3,965 `*_test.go` files are not described. Non-`_test.go` test scaffolding is listed once each, tagged `[test-support]`, with no detail.

**Structure.** Fourteen areas, then one section per package directory, then groups of related files inside the package, then one bullet per file or tight file family. The package layout is inconsistently flat (one directory can hold hundreds of files on unrelated concerns), so the groups are by concern, not by filename. In a bullet, the backticked names before the dash are paths relative to the package directory in the nearest package heading; `{a,b}` lists alternatives, `*` matches within one path segment and `**` any depth. Every one of the 7,662 files is matched by exactly one bullet; that was checked mechanically against the file list.

**The five biggest flat packages** (`pkg/gateway`, `pkg/provider`, `pkg/tools`, `pkg/agent`, `pkg/gatewayrun`) were mapped in alphabetical file ranges. Each has one package overview followed by a bold paragraph per file range that introduces that range's groups. A concern that spans ranges therefore appears under more than one range; the range paragraphs cross-reference each other.

**Status tags.** A tag sits at the start of a group description or right after a bullet's dash. No tag means implemented and reachable from non-test code as far as it was verified.

| Tag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `[stub]` | Declared, but the body is empty, returns a fixed value, or only returns an "unsupported" or "not implemented" error. The text says what it was meant to do. |
| `[partial]` | Real on some paths, missing on others. The text names what is missing. |
| `[unwired]` | Implemented, but nothing outside tests calls it. |
| `[py-shim]` | Reproduces Python stdlib, third-party or runtime behaviour instead of implementing a product feature. The text says what it stands in for and what depends on it. |
| `[port-artifact]` | Structure that exists only because of the port: `*_export.go` re-export shims, mixin structs, module-global emulation, compatibility aliases. |
| `[data]` | Embedded data, generated tables, bundled assets. |
| `[test-support]` | Non-`_test.go` test scaffolding. |
| `[stray]` | Should not be in a source tree: runtime databases, lock files, leftovers. |

**How it was produced, and its limits.** The descriptions come from reading the code: for every group the central files were opened, and unclear files were read until their role was clear. "No caller" and `[unwired]` claims were established by searching non-test code for callers. Not every one of the 1.57 million lines was read; where a file is small, a re-export shim, or one of many near-identical siblings, its bullet rests on its declarations and doc comments. Two things in the code make names unreliable and are called out wherever they bite: many files are named after the Python module they were ported from rather than what they now do, and word counts of `stub`, `todo` and `placeholder` in the source are almost all product vocabulary (todo lists, placeholder rows), not unfinished code.

## The system in one page

**What it is.** `icebath` is one Go binary (`cmd/icebath`) that is at once a tiling terminal UI, a headless CLI, and a long-lived background gateway that connects chat platforms, an OpenAI-compatible HTTP API, scheduled jobs, a kanban board and the terminal UI to one agent core. The Go code is a port of a Python application (the upstream name `hermes` still appears in 37 non-test files, in accepted header names, signing domains and metadata keys), and the terminal UI is a port of a Node terminal client.

**Processes.**

- *The gateway* is where agent turns run. It is the same binary re-executed with the hidden argv word `__icebath_gateway_run__` (`pkg/gatewayrun`), normally installed as a systemd unit, launchd agent or Windows Scheduled Task. It owns the platform adapters (28 compiled in), the session model (`pkg/gateway/session_*`: a routing index plus a per-profile session authority with a durable admission FIFO in `state.db`), the HTTP API server (`pkg/gatewayapi` over the HTTP layer in `pkg/gateway`), a per-home control socket and a loopback WebSocket, the cron scheduler's canonical owner, the kanban dispatcher, relay, webhooks and hosted multi-bot rooms. One gateway can serve several profiles ("multiplexing").
- *The CLI* (`cmd/icebath`, `pkg/commands`, `pkg/app`) runs no agent loop of its own: `icebath chat` and the one-shot modes are clients of the gateway, and `pkg/app` impersonates the old in-process agent on top of that client. The only in-process agent path left is the legacy `icebath-agent` runner.
- *The terminal UI* (`pkg/tui`) is a thin client: every session, tool, setting and screen is served over one loopback, ticketed WebSocket carrying JSON-RPC 2.0. `pkg/tuigateway` is the typed wire contract. `pkg/tuiserver` and `pkg/tuihost` run inside the gateway process: the runner hands the socket to `tuiserver.HandleWS`, which forwards to the session authority in `pkg/gateway` and answers 134 service methods itself. There is no stdio JSON-RPC child and no unix socket any more.
- *Children of the same binary*, selected by hidden argv words: the managed session worker (`__icebath_managed_worker__`), the cron external worker, the kanban worker client, the ACP adapter, the Bot Mode DM runner, the bot desktop idle watch, the tools MCP server for the Codex runtime, the Google Meet bot, the DuckDuckGo search worker, the ggml device probe, the self-update custody helpers, cgroup cleanup, the legacy agent runner (`__icebath_run_agent__`), and small helpers (commit-graph refresh, default-plugin install, scratch prune, stderr timestamping, the systemd stop mark). `cmd/icebath-init` is a separate entry for the container init in `pkg/containerinit`.
- *Foreign children*: plugin guests (external programs speaking line-delimited JSON on stdio; WebAssembly guests run in process), a `llama-server` router for local models, Chromium over CDP, the `cua-driver` for computer use, language servers, MCP servers, a Node sidecar for the Photon platform, `relay-host` embedding CPython for the `nemo_relay` wheel, Python interpreters for `execute_code`, `browser_exec` and several speech engines, and external CLIs that some platforms and providers require (`signal-cli`, `simplex-chat`, `buzz`, `raft`, `brv`).

**Layers, as they actually depend on each other.** `pkg/agent` (the `AIAgent` object, turn phases, context compression, delegation) calls models through `pkg/provider` and tools through `pkg/tools`, and persists through `pkg/state`. Around that core sit the tool-providing packages (`pkg/browser`, `pkg/codeexec`, `pkg/mcp`, `pkg/lsp`, `pkg/media`, `pkg/memory`, `pkg/skills`, `pkg/cron`, `pkg/kanban`), the plugin system (`pkg/plugins`, `pkg/pluginsdk`, `pkg/plugintree`, `pkg/builtin`), and the gateway packages that drive it. The packages are not layered cleanly: about 140 hook variables assigned in `cmd/icebath/wiring.go` are the real dependency graph, `pkg/plugins` reaches everything else through one 53-field `Services` struct, 311 `*_export.go` files re-export unexported symbols to siblings, and `pkg/gateway` and `pkg/gatewayapi` run their own SQL against `pkg/state`'s database.

**Data.** A *home* is the root icebath directory; a *profile* is `<root home>/profiles/<id>` with the same layout (`default` is the root home itself). The centre of a home is `state.db` (SQLite: sessions, messages, full-text search, the admission FIFO, worker executions, gateway routing, hosted rooms, delivery obligations, async delegations, key-value meta), beside `config.yaml`, `.env`, `auth.json`, the encrypted vault, memory files, `skills/`, `plugins/`, `cron/`, the kanban database, `checkpoints/`, `cache/`, `logs/` and a large number of marker, lock and pid files that the gateway, updater and package manager use to survive restarts. Each package section lists the paths it owns.

**Build tiers.** Three tiers hang off the link files in `cmd/icebath` and the build tags `icebath_core` and `icebath_noextras`; 243 files are tier-gated. A core build (`icebath_core`) has no chat platforms and only the `local` execution backend. The plugins tier (everything except `icebath_core`) adds the chat platforms, the other execution backends and the `send`, `slack` and `whatsapp` commands. The extras tier (the default build) adds cron, kanban, browser, LSP, computer use, voice and wake word, the Python environment manager, pets and the voxel arena, backup, batch runs, ACP, the vault command and the self-update steps. Matrix end-to-end encryption additionally needs the `goolm` tag.

## Port scaffolding at a glance

The rewrite deletes every translation layer, so each package section separates product behaviour from scaffolding. The overall picture:

- **`pkg/internal/py*`** is 88,846 lines emulating Python: 2,877 of the 5,872 Go files import at least one of these packages. Three of them are the port's data model rather than helpers: `pyjson.Object` is the ordered dict that values travel in (1,472 importing files), and `pyrepr` (1,624) and `pystr` (1,460) exist because those values are `any`. Removing them means typing the data, not swapping a helper.
- **Real product code sits under `py*` names** and must not be deleted with the shims: process identity and kill trees (`proc`), the IPv4 preference (`netpref`), Entra broker sign-in (`msalruntime`), wake-word engines (`pvporcupine`, `pyopenwakeword`, `sherpaonnx`), complete IMAP and SMTP clients for the email platform (`pyimaplib`, `pysmtplib`), PortAudio capture and playback (`pysounddevice`), SQLite backup and deadlines (`pysqlite`), all non-TUI terminal rendering (`pyrich`), atomic file replace and tar extraction policy (`pyfs`), the vault's on-disk format (`pyfernet`), and the embedded CPython host (`pyhost`).
- **Stored formats depend on Python encodings**: `json.dumps`-style text for message content, tool calls and metadata; canonical-JSON digests for admissions, receipts and mutations; a display identity that is the SHA-256 of a tuple `repr`; `local-<sha256>` ids.
- **Shape carried over from Python**: messages, requests and results as `map[string]any`; constructor options as keyword maps; handlers reading an argparse-shaped namespace (about a third of `pkg/commands` is argparse emulation); errors carrying Python exception class names that retry logic matches on; "mixin" structs (the gateway runner is eight of them); hand-made asyncio loops, tasks and futures; an aiohttp-shaped HTTP router; SDK-emulating model clients that reproduce header and JSON key order.
- **Whole libraries were ported rather than replaced**: a CPython 3.14 parser (`pyast`, about 22,000 lines), `httpx`, `requests`, `difflib`, `tomllib`, libyaml and ruamel, `croniter`, python-telegram-bot, `ddgs` with an XPath engine and a libxml2 tree builder, botocore's credential chain, azure-identity/MSAL, google-auth, Pillow pieces and numpy's random generator.
- **The terminal UI's scaffolding is JavaScript, not Python**: UTF-16 string offsets, `slice`, `toFixed`, `replace` and `parseInt` semantics, a WHATWG URL parser and promise-style continuations.
- **Python-era subsystems that a Go binary cannot use are still present**: the source-checkout updater (git pull, virtualenv sync, bytecode cleanup, `.py` syntax gate) in `pkg/selfupdate`; most of the uv and virtualenv manager in `pkg/pm`, whose inputs (`pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`) are not in the repository; pip entry-point discovery and Python AST audits in `pkg/plugins`.

## Missing, half-built, dead and stray

An index of what the sections below record in detail, so that intentions are not lost and dead weight is not rebuilt. Each item names the package section that describes it.

**Declared or advertised, but not built**

- Config migrations: no version key and no `config migrate` verb, although `icebath update` help mentions one. The remote config backend's `postprocess` is an empty stub and its plane server is not in the repository (`pkg/config`, `pkg/config/remote`).
- Settings: the workspace scope is not writable, the `Secret` kind is never registered, unknown-key notices never fire (`pkg/settings`).
- A top-level `icebath setup` wizard: its sections exist but no command reaches them; `SetupGateway`, the asker-driven tools flow, the terminal-backend wizard and the Blank Slate config writers are likewise unreachable (`pkg/provider`, `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/tools`).
- Shared-session attach has a client and no server; the quiet turn report has no reader (`pkg/app`).
- `manage_connections` declares `mcp`, `plugin` and `skill` targets and only ever creates `mcp` ones (`pkg/tools`).
- The Docker egress proxy: `icebath egress` and its proxy backend exist, but nothing installs `tools.EgressProxy`, so enabling it makes container creation fail unless `proxy.enforce_on_docker` is off (`pkg/tools`, `pkg/provider`).
- The `openai-native` web backend is a picker entry whose search only returns an error; there is no crawl and no page summarisation behind `web_extract`; Tool Search ignores `threshold_pct` when activating, so its `auto` and `on` modes behave the same (`pkg/tools`).
- Timed session auto-reset: only `suspended` triggers a reset; `idle` and `daily` survive as vocabulary and rely on a plugin, `icebath-session-reset-policy`, that is not in the repository (`pkg/gateway`, `pkg/plugins`).
- Hosted rooms capture work evidence on every driver hand-over, but the receiving side has no writer; a linked profile home is refused as "not supported yet" (`pkg/gateway`).
- ACP server: `session/close`, extension methods and the editor's `fs/*` and `terminal/*` capabilities are not implemented (`pkg/acp`).
- icebath as an MCP server: nothing ever records a pending approval, so its two approval tools are inert; no resources or prompts are exposed (`pkg/mcpserve`). As an MCP client, `roots` is never advertised and prompt and resource list-changed notifications are ignored (`pkg/mcp`).
- LSP is diagnostics after file writes only: no definition, references, hover or model-callable tool (`pkg/lsp`).
- Browser automation is four tools (`browser_exec`, `browser_cdp`, `browser_dialog`, `browser_vault`); the per-action tool family the descriptions still mention, recording, downloads and console capture do not exist (`pkg/browser`).
- Kanban: the manual-move table and drag flag are never read, the v2 workflow routing fields are never set, a gate message recommends a `kanban_edit` tool that does not exist, and there is no HTTP or dashboard surface (`pkg/kanban`). Cron suggestion sources `usage` and `integration` have no producer (`pkg/cron`).
- Memory providers: only ByteRover and RetainDB are compiled in (`pkg/memory`). Speech: the sherpa Whisper, Silero VAD and Kitten TTS branches are unwired (`pkg/internal/sherpaonnx`).
- Agent import migrates no sessions; several OpenClaw options have no CLI flag (`pkg/agentimport`). `skills publish --to clawhub` only prints a link (`pkg/skills`).
- Google Meet remote node drops `mode`, so node-hosted bots only transcribe and their speech queue is never drained; the Teams meeting pipeline has no retry (`pkg/builtin/googlemeet`, `pkg/builtin/teamspipeline`).
- Chat platforms: Slack feedback buttons only log, Slack reads a `slack_tokens.json` nothing writes, Discord's skill-group refresh has the wrong signature and is never called, Telegram subscribes to Business updates but never sends a business connection id, Matrix room creation, invites, presence and diagnostics and WhatsApp location sending have no caller (`pkg/gateway/platforms/*`).
- Backup has no scheduler and no signature verification, and `icebath import` skips `cache/`, so cache directories a backup archives are never restored (`pkg/backup`). `update --force` and `--force-venv` are declared and never read (`pkg/selfupdate`).
- The trajectory compressor's default config file is absent, three of its config keys are parsed and never read, and nothing builds `cmd/trajectory_compressor` (`pkg/trajectorycompressor`).

**Implemented but unreachable**

- About half of `pkg/tuiserver` (roughly 93 of 188 files) is the retired in-process session runtime: its RPC handlers were deleted and nothing ever inserts into the `pkg/tuihost` session registry, so it cannot execute. Its leftover idle reaper still runs and, as written, releases leases the gateway holds. The wire contract in `pkg/tuigateway` still lists 14 methods with no handler anywhere (`session.branch`, `session.undo`, `session.compress`, `terminal.resize`, `clipboard.paste` and others), and `rendered` fields are never filled because both render functions are stubs.
- The typed provider `Client` adapters' `Complete`, `Stream` and `CountTokens` have no production caller and `codex_responses.go` is unwired; the agent uses only the Python-shaped path (`pkg/provider`).
- About sixty exported `pkg/state` functions, including durable steer transfer, the session timeline, foreign-history import and donor lineage adoption.
- `pkg/ui/render/recap` in full, the voxel renderer's whole-frame post passes, several window-manager intents (`pkg/ui`, `pkg/vxl`); the gateway's typed stream-event union (`pkg/gateway`); the local runtime's Hugging Face browser (`pkg/provider`); the LSP blocking baseline path (`pkg/lsp`).
- CLI leftovers: the `curator` and `completion` group handlers never run, three console rows name kanban commands that do not exist, an `rl` command is still referenced (`cmd/icebath`, `pkg/app`, `pkg/commands`).
- Many `*_export.go` shims have no caller left; each section names its own.

**Stray files in the source tree**

- `pkg/gatewayrun/default/`: a seeded profile home committed by accident (default `SOUL.md`, a schema-only `state.db`, two zero-byte lock files). Nothing embeds or reads it.
- `pkg/pm/.lock.json.lock`: a zero-byte lock file created by the lockfile writer.
- `pkg/mcp/TODOS.md`: a project-wide port tracker (392 of 2,779 Python files checked), not MCP notes.
- `pkg/tui/testdata/worktree-fixture.bundle` is referenced by no Go file; `pkg/builtin/googlemeet/SKILL.md` is never embedded; `pkg/skills/bundled_manifest.txt` and `optional_manifest.txt` are read by no code; `pkg/i18n/locales/_keys.tui.json` is not embedded.
- Test scaffolding outside `_test.go` files: `pkg/config/roundtrip`, `pkg/termlab`, `pkg/testfakes`, `pkg/testguard`, `pkg/internal/fakellm`, `pkg/internal/hermetic`, and `pkg/internal/homeguard`, which is linked into production and routes thirteen production files' user lookups through itself.

**Where things are not where the name says**

- The API server's routes, auth and handlers are in `pkg/gatewayapi`; `pkg/gateway/api_server_*` is stores and request helpers. `GatewayRunner` is in `pkg/gatewayrun`; `pkg/gateway/run_*` is mostly shims and seams for it. "Hosted" in `pkg/gateway` means multi-bot group rooms, not relay.
- The "auxiliary" files of `pkg/provider` hold the clients the agent uses for every request. `pkg/acpclient` is a model provider (`copilot-acp`), not a general ACP client.
- `pkg/selfupdate` also houses `doctor`, `status`, `dump`, `debug share`, `security audit` and `fallback check`. `pkg/plugins/verify` is the `icebath verify` project smoke test. `pkg/plugins` holds shell hooks, hook directories and outbound webhooks.
- `pkg/memory` holds the skill curator, the learning graph behind `icebath journey`, insights and session export, while session search is in `pkg/tools`, the background memory review in `pkg/agent`, and vision in `pkg/tools`.
- `pkg/pm` holds the launchers and home pinning that run first in `main`. `pkg/app` holds the offline SQLite salvage behind `sessions recover` and a Hugging Face hub client. `pkg/commands` holds the whole `profile` command body. `pkg/gateway/messagetools` holds a Microsoft Graph client.
- `pkg/tools` holds the child-process environment factory and the secret redaction engine used by the whole application, self-update git repair, and the emergency stop. `pkg/skills` holds the OSV malware check for MCP launches.
- The kanban dispatcher loop, worker client and notifier are in `pkg/gatewayrun` and `pkg/gateway`. Feishu's document-comment agent, the Teams meeting-summary writer and the A2A, Home Assistant and Yuanbao tools are inside their platform adapter packages.
- `pkg/state` is also the project's general SQLite toolkit, the home of the in-memory message types, and a runtime ledger (admissions, worker executions, mutation receipts).

## 1. Entry points and CLI shell

### `cmd/icebath` — the main binary: process startup, build-tier link files, cobra tree binding and cross-package wiring

*30 files, 4,282 Go lines*

Owns `main`, the order in which the process comes up, the three build tiers, the binding of every cobra command path to the package that implements it, and one very large function that assigns the package-level hook variables the lower packages leave empty. It persists nothing itself except a Termux skills-sync stamp; it reads `ICEBATH_HOME`, `<root>/active_profile`, the home `.env` and `config.yaml`. Three binaries come out of this one package: no tags is the full build (core, plugins and extras tiers), `icebath_noextras` is core plus plugins, `icebath_core` is core only (`Makefile` targets `build-full`, `build-noextras`, `build-core`; every build also passes `goolm`). The package is real product code, but its shape is the Python `main.py` import-time sequence: hidden re-exec child modes, exit hooks emulating `atexit`, and argparse-namespace dicts handed to handlers.

#### Process entry and startup sequence

`main` runs these steps in order, each able to end the process. (1) Tier argv entries: in the plugins tier the binary acts as container init when invoked as `init`, `tini` or an s6 verb. (2) Hidden pre-parse verbs `nix-config-render`, `nix-config-merge`, `sqlite-runtime`. (3) `startProcess`: stamp the ldflags version, bridge slog, install all wiring, then dispatch about twenty hidden re-exec child modes (scratch prune, relay host, restart watchers, update helper, cgroup cleanup, DDGS worker, Codex tools MCP server, cron worker, managed worker, gateway-run module, ACP module and more). (4) `pm` launcher: choose the runtime, restore an interrupted update, pin the launcher home. (5) Legacy runner argv. (6) `--print-runtime-command`. (7) Expand `ICEBATH_HOME`. (8) Register the CLI argv splitter with `pm` and finish an owed source update. (9) For `gateway run`, mark the process and arm the startup watchdog. (10) Switch terminal mouse tracking off before a TUI launch. (11) Fast `--version`. (12) Profile override. (13) Export the scratch tmp env (not for `uninstall`). (14) `pm` commands dispatch here, before dotenv and logging. (15) Load `.env`, cap malloc arenas for server processes, set up file logging, apply the force-IPv4 setting. (16) `run`: process title, PID 1 warning, `AI_AGENT`/`ICEBATH_AGENT` env, OS trust store, update debts, three chat fast paths, NixOS container-mode re-exec, then the full cobra parse. `exit` always runs the exit hooks and restores the terminal.

- `main.go` — `main`, `run`, `runCLI`, `beforeDispatch` (root `--version`, `--yolo` to `ICEBATH_YOLO_MODE`, stdin-as-query, agent startup discovery, top-level `-z` oneshot) and `exit`
- `startup.go` — `startProcess` and the ordered hidden child-entry dispatch; process title, unsupervised PID 1 warning, agent env advertisement, early mouse-mode reset, fast `--version`, dotenv, logging, container-mode exec, launcher runtime command
- `fastpaths.go` — `chatArgs` namespace read from cobra flags; the rule that a chat with a TTY on both ends and no query, image or stream format opens the TUI; safe-mode and ignore-user-config env; plugin, MCP, shell-hook and outbound-webhook discovery per command; fast chat launch on a light parser (`ICEBATH_DISABLE_FAST_CHAT_LAUNCH`), Termux fast CLI and TUI launches. Its agent-command table still names an `rl` command that no longer exists in the tree
- `profile_override.go` — pre-parses `-p/--profile` into `ICEBATH_HOME`, falls back to the sticky `<root>/active_profile` file unless a supervisor (systemd `INVOCATION_ID`, s6, `ICEBATH_SUPERVISED_CHILD`, `ICEBATH_GATEWAY_PROFILE_PIN`) launched the gateway, resolves `sudo icebath -p` against the invoking user, and lets `profile list`, `profile use default` and data-keeping `uninstall` run when the saved profile is gone
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `cmd/icebath`

#### Hidden pre-parse verbs

Verbs answered before any wiring exists, used by packaging and update tooling rather than people.

- `nix_module.go` — `nix-config-render SETTINGS_JSON` prints config rendered from Nix settings; `nix-config-merge NIX_JSON CONFIG_YAML` merges Nix-managed keys into a config file; both called by the Nix modules at build and activation time
- `sqlite_runtime.go` — `sqlite-runtime` prints a report of the SQLite library linked into this binary (version probe used by session-store safety checks)

#### Process title

Shows `icebath` instead of the binary path in `ps` and `top`; never fatal.

- `proctitle_{darwin,linux,other,windows}.go` — per-OS title setter: `prctl(PR_SET_NAME)` capped at 15 bytes on Linux, `pthread_setname_np` through purego on macOS, no-op elsewhere (4 variants)
- `proctitle_ptr_linux.go` — unsafe pointer helper for the raw prctl argument
- `proctitle_thread{,_other}.go` — locks the main goroutine to the main thread at init on Linux and macOS until the title is set, no-op elsewhere

#### Build tiers and link files

Each tier has one link file whose `init` calls `linktier.Link`, blank-imports the packages of that tier, and appends to slices declared in `link_core.go`: argv entries, startup-phase steps, hidden child entries, wiring functions, CLI binders, exit hooks and plugin-service extensions. A command whose tier is not linked stays in the tree as a hidden command that prints which build carries it.

- `link_core.go` — always linked; declares the tier extension slices and the seven startup phases (`phaseBeforeStart` through `phaseRun`); links `pkg/builtin/delegationdefault` and `pkg/profiles/manage`
- `link_plugins.go` — plugins tier (absent under `icebath_core`): links bundled messaging platforms, web backends, camofox, disk cleanup, langfuse, MCP-serve, security guidance, spotify, teams pipeline, ACP client, remote config; binds `send` (pkg/gatewaycli), `slack` (platforms/slack), `whatsapp`, `whatsapp-cloud`; installs container init as an argv entry and root-drop step; feeds Slack, Matrix, Telegram and Feishu adapters their views of the slash registry
- `link_extras.go` — extras tier (full build only): binds `acp` (pkg/acp), `backup` and `import` (pkg/backup), `batch` (pkg/batchrun), `browser` and `vault` (pkg/browser), `kanban` (pkg/kanban), `cron` (pkg/cron), `lsp` (pkg/lsp), `computer-use` (pkg/codeexec), `security`, `update` and the hidden `update-takeover`, `update-finish`, `update-restart-recovery`, `update-completion`, `venv-sync`, `source-completion`, `import-health` (pkg/selfupdate), `pets` (pkg/app); adds update restore, relaunch-marker, owed-update and boot-bootstrap startup steps; wires speech output, cron worker boot, kanban budget hook, agent importer runner and the update check behind `--version`

#### Cobra tree binding

`newCLI` takes the unbound tree from `pkg/commands`, binds chat, login/logout, each tier's commands, then every remaining path by its first word, then attaches plugin-provided top-level commands. Handlers receive an argparse-style `map[string]any` namespace with the subcommand written under a per-group dest key (`auth_action`, `tools_action`, `sessions_action` and so on).

- `bindings.go` — `newCLI`; binds `chat`, `resume` (lift emergency stop), `login`, `logout`; discovers plugin CLI commands only when argv's first word is not a builtin, attaching memory-provider commands then plugin-manager commands, each either parsed by cobra or handed raw argv to the plugin's own parser
- `host_commands.go` — core-tier group table: `approvals`, `checkpoints`, `pause`, `project`, `tools`, `worktree` (pkg/tools); `auth`, `codex-runtime`, `egress`, `fallback`, `migrate`, `model`, `proxy`, `secrets`, `usage` (pkg/provider); `gateway` (pkg/gatewaycli); `pairing`, `peer` (pkg/gateway); `debug`, `doctor`, `dump`, `status` (pkg/selfupdate); `journey` (pkg/memory); `monitoring`; `prompt-size` (pkg/agent); `verify` (pkg/plugins); `console`, `logs`, `sessions`, `uninstall` (pkg/app); `install-self`. Its `curator` and `completion` handlers never run because those commands' own RunE bypasses dispatch. `requireTTY` exits 1 for interactive commands on a pipe
- `install_self.go` — hidden `install-self`: runs the installer from a release binary (pkg/install), `--from-checkout` publishes a source build and syncs bundled skills, `--release-info` prints tag and VCS commit as JSON, `--show-resolved-paths` prints the install paths
- `command_tree.go` — builds the exported CLI tree (with loaded plugin commands, cached by plugin set) that the TUI gateway serves for running CLI commands from inside the terminal UI
- `helpers.go` — [port-artifact] Python `str`/truthiness wrappers and argparse-namespace readers (`nsBool`, `nsString`, `nsInt`) plus small stderr and realpath helpers

#### Chat launch decision

`icebath` with no subcommand is `chat`. A TTY on both ends with no query opens the terminal UI in process; everything else is headless and runs its turn in the gateway.

- `chat.go` — `cmdChat`: routes stream-json, headless safe-mode/ignore-user-config and `--list-tools/--list-toolsets` to the gateway transport launcher, else resolves `--in`, `--resume latest`, `-c [name]` (terminal breadcrumb, then workspace-scoped most recent session), `--create-if-missing`, `--resume @claude|@codex` foreign import, recreates a removed worktree, restores the session cwd, refuses headless runs with no provider, syncs bundled skills, confirms costly or data-training model overrides, then launches the TUI or the one-shot client
- `tui_dev.go` — `--dev`: finds the icebath source checkout above the binary or cwd, runs `go build -tags goolm ./cmd/icebath` into a temp dir and executes the result as the TUI

#### Cross-package wiring

Lower packages expose nil function variables instead of importing upward; this group assigns all of them at startup. It is the only place where the dependency graph of the product is visible in one file.

- `wiring.go` — `installProcessWiring` assigns about 140 hooks across gateway, gatewayrun, tuiserver, tui, tools, state, agent, mcp, pm and commands (slash confirm store, personality, quick commands, status reads, clipboard, prefill, banner, registry lookups); builds the `plugins.Services` struct; `runAtExit` runs the ordered teardown (terminal environments, kernels, MCP servers, provider clients, outbound webhooks, leases, logging)
- `wiring_session_controls.go` — builtin-only slash registry used for name and alias lookups, and the catalog rows (localized description, usage suffix, aliases, gateway-only flag, subcommand table) the TUI server lists
- `plugin_hooks.go` — gives pkg/provider the plugin-manager entry points for catalog lookup, unattended install, load errors and dependency homes
- `agent_import.go` — lets setup and `icebath migrate` install or enable the `agent-importers` plugin on demand
- `session_socket.go` — adapts an admitted gateway WebSocket to the TUI server session handler, mapping peer close to a disconnect error
- `tui_widgets.go` — converts plugin-registered widgets (render, input, refresh, zone, width) into the shape the terminal UI draws and reports plugins that failed to load

### `cmd/icebath-init` — container init and s6 supervisor shim

*1 file, 20 Go lines*

A second binary shipped by goreleaser and the Dockerfile, where it is symlinked as `/init`, `tini` and the s6 control verbs.

#### Container init entry

- `main.go` — dispatches to `pkg/containerinit` by its own name or first argument (`init`, `tini`, `s6-svscan`, `s6-svc`, `s6-svstat`, `s6-svwait`, `s6-svscanctl`, `s6-setuidgid`, `with-contenv`, `s6-log`, `container-init`, `container-health`); prints usage and exits 100 otherwise

### `cmd/packtree` — build-time packer for embedded trees and the plugin catalog document

*2 files, 162 Go lines*

Developer tool, still in use: `go:generate` lines in `pkg/skills/embed.go`, `pkg/builtin/gen.go` and `pkg/plugintree/tree.go` run `pack`, and `site/build.sh` runs `catalog`.

#### Pack, unpack and catalog verbs

- `main.go` — `pack -dir -out [-manifest] [-shebang-exec]` writes a deterministic zstd tar of a tree plus its manifest through `pkg/tarzst`; `unpack -archive -dir` extracts one
- `catalog.go` — `catalog -dir -out` reads one YAML file per plugin catalog entry plus `removed.yaml`, checks each file name equals its `name`, and writes the JSON catalog document with a `generated_at` stamp

### `cmd/pypiwheels` — release-time PyPI wheel builder

*1 file, 193 Go lines*

Used only by `.github/workflows/release.yml`. Wraps each release binary in a platform wheel so `pipx install icebath-cli` installs the Go binary.

#### Wheel assembly

- `main.go` — `pypiwheels <version> <binaries dir> <out dir> <license>` writes six `icebath_cli-<version>-py3-none-<tag>.whl` files (linux, darwin, windows on amd64 and arm64) holding the binary as a script, an `.install_method` stamp of `pip`, METADATA, WHEEL, LICENSE and a sha256 RECORD, with fixed 1980 timestamps

### `cmd/trajectory_compressor` — standalone trajectory compressor command

*1 file, 13 Go lines*

A thin main over `pkg/trajectorycompressor`. No Makefile target, goreleaser build, Dockerfile or workflow references it, so it exists only for `go run`.

#### Entry

- `main.go` — passes argv to `trajectorycompressor.Main` and exits with its status

### `pkg/linktier` — registry of which build tiers this binary links

*1 file, 99 Go lines*

Tiny leaf package that the link files write and everything else reads to hide, refuse or reword features of an unlinked tier.

#### Tier registry

- `linktier.go` — `Link`, `Linked` (every tier counts as linked when no link file ran), build names (`core build`, `plugins build`, `full build`), refusal and missing-feature lines, the `Build:` line printed by `--version` and doctor, and `SlashTiers`: `voice`, `wake`, `pet`, `hatch`, `cron`, `blueprint`, `suggestions`, `kanban`, `browser`, `update`, `arena` in extras and `handoff`, `egress`, `topic` in plugins

### `pkg/startupfast` — version output and cheap startup probes

*1 file, 193 Go lines*

Holds the code that must run before config and logging load. Called from `cmd/icebath/startup.go`; extended by the plugins tier (Matrix E2EE version line) and the extras tier (update check).

#### Version block and container-mode probe

- `startup_fast.go` — `PrintFastVersionInfo` prints the version label, install directory, install method (config or the `.install_method` stamp), Go version, build tier line, tier-added lines and an update status line (up to date, N commits behind, rollback available); `ContainerModeMayBeActive` checks `.container-mode` and `active_profile` without loading config so fast `--version` never bypasses container routing

### `pkg/commands` — slash-command registry and the complete cobra CLI tree

*58 files, 14,707 Go lines*

Two things live here. The first is the slash-command table: 105 builtin definitions (name, aliases, category, argument hint, subcommands, terminal-only flag, busy policy) that the TUI, the gateway and every chat platform read; it is metadata only, since builtin definitions carry no handler and the behaviour lives in `pkg/gatewayrun` and `pkg/tuiserver`. The second is the whole `icebath` command tree as cobra commands with handlers bound by path, wrapped in a thick layer that makes cobra parse, report errors and print help exactly like Python argparse. Close to a third of the package by line count is that argparse emulation. It also holds a few shared behaviours that sit oddly here: personalities, the pending-confirm store, quick-command shell execution and the `profile` command body.

#### Slash command registry

`Default` is the process registry, filled from `Builtin` at init; plugins add definitions with `Register`. The 105 builtins, grouped by what they control, with aliases in parentheses:

Session lifecycle (17): /start, /new (clear, reset), /history, /save, /retry, /undo, /rewind, /title, /resume, /sessions (switch, session), /branch (fork), /compress (compact), /handoff, /discard, /topic, /sethome (set-home), /quit (exit).

Turn control (13): /stop, /queue (q), /steer (s), /busy, /bg (background), /btw, /agents (tasks), /processes (ps), /approve, /deny, /pause, /restart, /platform.

Standing and delegated work (10): /goal, /subgoal, /heartbeat (hb), /loop (proactive), /plan, /refine, /review, /moa, /learn, /init.

Workspace and attachments (10): /worktree, /rollback, /snapshot (snap), /diff, /export, /import, /prompt (compose), /copy, /paste, /image.

Model and run policy (12): /model, /codex-runtime (codex_runtime), /reasoning, /fast, /personality, /yolo, /approvals, /voice, /wake, /footer, /autoprune, /verbose.

Terminal UI display (15): /settings (config, preferences), /logins (login, accounts), /language (lang), /mouse (scroll), /detail (details), /statusbar (sb), /battery, /timestamps (ts), /skin, /indicator, /redraw, /palette, /keys (keybinds, hotkeys), /pet, /hatch (generate-pet).

Tools, skills and extensions (15): /tools (toolsets), /skills, /memory, /bundles, /curator, /cron (jobs), /suggestions (suggest), /blueprint (bp), /kanban, /reload, /reload-mcp (reload_mcp), /reload-skills (reload_skills), /browser, /plugins, /journey (learning, memory-graph).

Information (13): /status, /context (ctx), /whoami, /profile, /egress, /usage, /insights, /commands, /help, /chat-apps (platforms, gateway), /update, /version (v), /debug.

Thirty-eight are terminal-UI only: redraw, history, prompt, rewind, handoff, worktree, snapshot, export, import, processes, journey, settings, logins, language, mouse, detail, statusbar, battery, timestamps, verbose, skin, indicator, wake, tools, skills, pet, hatch, cron, reload, browser, plugins, palette, chat-apps, keys, copy, paste, image, quit. Two of those reach gateway surfaces behind a config gate: verbose when `display.tool_progress_command` is set and skills when `skills.write_approval` is set. Eleven are gateway-surface only and hidden from terminal help: start, topic, discard, pause, approve, deny, sethome, verbose, commands, restart, platform.

Busy policy, meaning what happens when the command is typed mid-turn, is reject by default; /new and /stop interrupt the turn and then run; these run alongside the turn: start, discard, pause, approve, deny, bg, btw, agents, queue, steer, goal, subgoal, heartbeat, loop, status, egress, context, profile, verbose, footer, yolo, busy, autoprune, kanban, commands, help, palette, restart, update, version.

- `def.go` — `Def`, `Invocation`, `Registry` (register, alias lookup, names, remove), the three busy policies, and `Describe`, which prefers the i18n catalog key `slash.<name>.description`
- `table.go` — the `Builtin` table itself, the five categories, per-command `Meta` (gateway-only, config gate, executor key), plugin command entries, the subcommand map (explicit list or the `a|b|c` pattern in the hint), gateway-known names and the categorized help rows
- `dispatch.go` — classifies a typed line as prompt, slash, bang or skill candidate and runs a definition's bound handler; in practice only plugin-registered definitions (the bundled `impeccable` command) carry a handler, so the bang and skill branches are never reached through this path
- `bang.go` — recognises `!command` shell-mode lines; used only by `dispatch.go`
- `route.go` — POSIX-style `Shlex` splitter, `ResolveSlashKey` (underscores read as hyphens) and stacked-skill constants; `QuickCommand` and `DestructiveSkipTokens` are [unwired] leftovers
- `skills_resolver.go` — tells pkg/skills which names are builtin commands so skill slash commands can report collisions

#### Shared slash behaviours

Surface-independent pieces of slash commands that gatewayrun and tuiserver call through hooks assigned in `cmd/icebath/wiring.go`.

- `slash_exec.go` — the seven registry-owned executors that return plain or markdown text without touching a session: `version`, `egress`, `profile`, `bundles`, `autoprune`, gateway `help` (first ten skill commands) and paginated `commands` (page size option, default 20)
- `confirm.go` — per-session pending confirm store with a 300 second timeout and supersede-on-register, used for destructive slash confirmations on chat platforms; the `DestructiveChoices`, message constants and `DestructiveDetails` are [unwired]
- `approval_mode.go` — `/approvals [manual|smart|off]`: reads the effective mode and persists `approvals.mode` through the config facade, reporting a managed-config refusal
- `personality.go` — 14 builtin personalities, user ones from `personalities` and `agent.personalities`, neutral names (`none`, `default`, `neutral`), structured prompts with tone and style, `display.personality` persistence (config chmod 0600), and the ephemeral system prompt fallback to `agent.system_prompt`
- `quick.go`, `quick_{unix,windows}.go` — runs a user `quick_commands` exec entry on gateway surfaces: scrubbed child env, new session or hidden console, 30 second timeout that kills the whole tree, stdout else stderr, secrets redacted; half the code reproduces Python `subprocess` error text

#### Platform command catalogs

Derives each chat platform's native command menu from the registry.

- `platforms.go` — config gates for terminal-only commands; Telegram name sanitising, 32-character clamp, menu cap (default 60, API limit 100) and priority list with `platforms.telegram.extra.command_menu`; Discord skill groups by top-level folder with collision report; Slack native slashes capped at 50, reserved names, the `/icebath`-only list, app manifest fragment and subcommand map; gateway help lines
- `gateway_skills.go` — enumerates skills eligible as gateway slash commands for a platform and fills leftover menu slots with them

#### Composer completion

Completion served to the terminal UI through the TUI gateway.

- `completion.go` — `SlashCompleter`: command names with category rows, subcommands, stacked skill tokens (max 5), bundles, plugin commands, dynamic values for /skin, /personality, /tools and /handoff, `@diff`, `@staged`, `@file:`, `@folder:`, `@git:`, `@url:` references, path completion and fuzzy project-file matching from `rg --files` or `fd` (5 second cache, 5000 files)
- `completer_live_sources.go` — live rows for skins, toolsets with their CLI enable state, and connected platforms with home channel
- `tui_slash_completer.go` — builds the completer over one session's skill and bundle tables for the TUI gateway

- `shell_completion.go` — generates bash, zsh and fish completion scripts from the tree with profile-name completion for `-p`; hand-written rather than cobra's generator

#### Argparse emulation layer

[py-shim] Stands in for Python `argparse`: abbreviation of long options, `nargs` shapes, SUPPRESS and None defaults, `store_false` into a shared dest, mutually exclusive groups, exact usage and error wording (exit 2), and help formatting. Every handler in the product depends on it, because handlers read an argparse-shaped namespace map rather than typed arguments.

- `cli_namespace.go` — `CLI.Namespace`: flag and positional values of every parser level as a `map[string]any` keyed by argparse dest, honouring suppress, None and const-True annotations
- `cli_argparse.go`, `cli_argparse_nargs.go`, `cli_argparse_store_false.go`, `cli_argparse_values.go` — dest renaming, subparser dest, repeatable and `nargs='+'` flags, empty-list defaults, choice-restricted values with Python-repr error text, non-negative integer types, and parse-order tracking so the last of two opposing flags wins
- `cli_parse_errors.go` — `ArgparseError` and the translation of pflag failures, unknown options, missing or mutually exclusive arguments into argparse's usage-plus-error output
- `argparse_help.go` — renders `--help` and usage lines in argparse's layout and wrapping, deriving actions from cobra for plugin commands
- `cli_argparse_table.go` — [data] hand-maintained argparse shape of all 426 parsers (option order, dests, metavars, nargs, choices, subcommand help rows) that help, completion and the tree export read; duplicates the cobra declarations
- `console_execute.go` — `ExecuteParsed`: parse and run without the profile scan, used by the console
- `legacy_agent_cli.go` — argparse-faithful parser for the legacy `icebath-agent` runner flags (`--query`, `--model`, `--max-turns`, `--enabled-toolsets`, `--save-trajectories`, underscore spellings)

#### Package plumbing

- `log.go` — package logger tagged `pkg/commands`
- `help.go` — generic sorted-map-keys helper

### `pkg/app` — CLI application layer: chat launch paths, console, sessions command, uninstall and terminal handling

*122 files, 30,129 Go lines*

The port of the Python `cli.py` and its neighbours, flattened into one package of 122 files. It owns the three ways a chat starts (in-process terminal UI, one-shot client, gateway transport launcher), the `console` REPL, the whole `sessions` command including offline database recovery, `uninstall`, `logs`, `pets`, the banner and version label, clipboard images and terminal identity. Callers are `cmd/icebath` directly and, through hook variables, gatewayrun, gateway, tuiserver and acp. It reads and writes under the home: `state.db`, `terminal-sessions/`, `session-exports/`, `logs/`, `config.yaml`; it talks to the gateway over its WebSocket RPC and to Hugging Face for trace upload. No agent loop runs here any more: every turn executes in the gateway, and the `CLI` struct still carries the state of a removed interactive prompt (input queues nobody feeds, status-bar and TUI-mode flags).

#### One-shot chat client: construction and lifecycle

`ChatMain` serves `icebath chat -q` in text format. It builds a `CLI` value from flags over env over config, claims the active-session slot, opens or resumes a gateway session and exits with a turn-derived code.

- `cli_main.go` — `Main`/`ChatMain`, `NewCLI`, background skills preload (auto-load plus `-s`), active-session claim and release, security advisory banner, `-w` worktree creation with tool prewarm and clean-tree removal on exit
- `cli.go` — the `CLI` struct, `inputQueue`, process-wide cleanup run once with terminal input-mode reset, active agent reference, `SaveConfigValue`; `pendingInput`, `interruptQueue` and `tuiInputModesActive` are remnants of the removed interactive prompt
- `cli_init.go` — resolves display options; model (flag, then config, then auto-detect on a localhost base URL); provider (flag, startup route, config, `ICEBATH_INFERENCE_PROVIDER`, else `auto`); base URL (flag, route, config, `OPENROUTER_BASE_URL`); turn limit, run budget, toolsets, checkpoints, prompt, reasoning, session id and store
- `cli_init_gateway.go` — opens the gateway session with this launch's explicit flags as its policy, adopts the gateway's resolved toolsets, records shell-hook consent, hands the active-session lease over during attach
- `cli_agent_setup.go` — credential check, per-turn route and rebuild signature, fallback runtime, resume (compression-chain following, history restore, size guard) and `initAgent`, which builds the gateway-backed agent
- `cli_agent_surface.go` — the agent interface the client drives and the atomic slot that publishes it to signal and render goroutines
- `cli_model_switch.go` — on resume restores the model and provider recorded on the session unless the launch named one, healing a bare `custom` provider
- `cli_session.go` — writes the terminal breadcrumb, prints the exit summary (resume commands, title, duration, message counts), restores a session's cwd and yolo state
- `cli_shutdown.go` — exit watchdog (`ICEBATH_EXIT_WATCHDOG_S`, default 30, doubled on a signal), session-finalize hook messages, aux client and terminal cleanup, wait for background completions before a one-shot exits
- `cli_browser_commands.go` — extras tier: adds the browser session reaper to shutdown
- `active_session_lease.go` — claims a slot in the shared active-session registry (pkg/activesessions)
- `gateway_recorded_worktree.go` — hands the gateway session store the worktree recorded for `-w`

#### One-shot chat client: turn execution

Runs the single turn, in loud mode (`-q`) with rendered progress or quiet mode (`-Q`) printing only the reply and `session_id:` on stderr.

- `cli_single_query.go` — `runSingleQueryMode`: SIGINT/SIGTERM/SIGHUP interrupt the gateway turn then wait `ICEBATH_SIGTERM_GRACE`; image routing native or via vision pre-description; pops `ICEBATH_TURN_AUTHOR`; exit code from the turn result
- `quiet_single_query.go` — exit unwinding, follow-up turns for `notify_on_complete` background work (8 rounds under one linger budget), and a turn report written to `ICEBATH_QUIET_TURN_REPORT_FILE`. [partial] nothing in the Go code sets that variable or reads the report; `ReportedTurn` is unused
- `cli_chat_turn.go` — loud-mode `chat`: stage the user row, run the agent on a worker, poll for interrupts, settle and render the turn, print reasoning box and response panel, keep `fallback_providers` edits in sync mid-chat
- `cli_chat_error_copy.go` — turns agent-init and turn errors into a two-line panel: plain sentence with the fix command, then a details line
- `cli_tool_callbacks.go` — answers every tool question form as undelivered because a `-q` run has nobody to ask
- `cli_terminal_input.go` — resolves attachment paths (quotes, tilde, env vars, `file://`), detects a dragged file path at the start of input, collects images for the query
- `cli_tui_keys.go` — `submittedInput`, a message bundled with image paths
- `stream_json.go` — `--format stream-json`: JSONL `system`, `text`, `tool_use`, `tool_result` (output capped at 5000) and `result` events; also stdin-as-query and the no-query usage error (exit 2)
- `oneshot_usage.go` — `-z` exit codes (130 interrupted, 2 failed or partial, 1 no text, 0) and the `--usage-file` JSON cost and token report, written even on failure

#### Kanban worker mode of the one-shot client

A one-shot run with `ICEBATH_KANBAN_TASK` set is a kanban card worker. The hooks are nil outside the extras tier, where a worker run is refused.

- `kanban_worker_hooks.go` — hook variables and their callers: register as the card's worker, rerun failed turns with a nudge, drive the goal loop, add task-body images
- `cli_single_query_kanban.go` — extras tier: binds those hooks to pkg/kanban and pkg/goals (`ICEBATH_KANBAN_GOAL_MODE`)
- `cli_commands_kanban.go` — extras tier: parses `/kanban ...` on the CLI tree and renames `icebath kanban` to `/kanban` in usage and errors, installed as `kanban.ParseSlash`

#### Gateway-backed agent stand-in

`GatewayAgent` exposes the surface of the old in-process agent but submits `prompt.submit` to the gateway and replays the session event stream into the client's callbacks.

- `gateway_agent.go` — construction over the session store connection, model, reasoning, service-tier and tool-progress setters that write through to the session, interrupt, usage and rate-limit figures, todo store mirror
- `gateway_agent_events.go` — handlers for `message.delta`, `message.interim`, `tool.*`, `todo.updated`, `thinking.delta`, `reasoning.*`, `moa.*`, `notification.*`, `agent.print`, `review.summary`, `approval.request`, `clarify.request`; with no user to ask, dangerous-command approvals are denied at once, sudo and vault prompts declined, and only a skill's secret is read at a masked console prompt
- `gateway_agent_turn.go` — `RunConversation`: submit, drop stale frames, pump events, recover a turn across a gateway restart or reconnect, report an unadmitted turn so the caller can resend
- `gateway_agent_result.go` — builds the turn result dict (history, usage, failed, interrupted, voice-stop), paints text owed after a replay gap, review summary line, MoA events
- `gateway_replay_gap.go` — decides from a receipt and snapshot whether a turn that ended inside a reconnect hole settled, and which part of its reply is still unpainted
- `gateway_tools_notify.go` — remembers a queued admission's start seen outside its turn and lets a run adopt an already admitted turn instead of resubmitting
- `gateway_plugin_commands.go` — asks the gateway for plugin toolsets and portable MCP servers, cached per gateway life
- `gateway_side.go` — returns the CLI's gateway connection while its session is open

#### Gateway transport launcher

`LaunchFromArgs` serves top-level `-z`, `chat --format stream-json`, headless `--safe-mode`/`--ignore-user-config` and `--list-tools/--list-toolsets`. It talks to the gateway directly and refuses rather than falling back to a local run.

- `gateway_chat.go` — validates options (bypass launches need `--model`), provider check, Ctrl-C detaches with exit 130 while work continues, `session.create` under the launch policy and caller cwd, resume latest (breadcrumb, then workspace) or by id then title, `session.mutate` relaunch overrides, `--image` staging into the media cache, `-w` worktree, error-to-exit-code mapping
- `gateway_chat_view.go` — the session view: pending and lost-turn listing on attach, event rendering, reattach and replay-gap recovery, the finite one-shot wait, usage file, exit ids and resume footer; refuses to send while an unknown admission blocks the session
- `gateway_chat_listing.go` — prints the tool or toolset catalog for the profile's CLI selection without a session or gateway
- `gateway_chat_commands.go` — refusal text for commands the shared gateway does not serve, and the rewind payload naming the Nth newest user turn
- `gateway_mutations.go` — `PreparedMutations`: retains the identity of a `/model` or `/compress` control across ambiguous replies and re-sends with a confirmation token for guarded targets; the view only retires entries, the ACP adapter applies them
- `acp_adapter_export.go` — [port-artifact] re-exports the mutation table, slash-to-mutation mapping, refusal texts and replay-gap helpers to pkg/acp
- `main_session_lookup.go` — workspace key: git repo root of the cwd, else the cwd

#### Terminal rendering for the one-shot client

Everything loud `-q` prints. The rest of the product renders through the terminal UI instead.

- `cli_render{,_other,_unix}.go` — ANSI from skin colours, light-terminal detection ladder (`ICEBATH_LIGHT`, `ICEBATH_TUI_THEME`, `ICEBATH_TUI_BACKGROUND`, `COLORFGBG`, OSC 11 query fenced by DA1 and skipped over SSH), markdown stripping, the `ChatConsole` rich-console stand-in, and `ReleaseDate`
- `termios_{bsd,linux}.go` — per-OS termios ioctl constants for the OSC 11 query
- `cli_stream.go` — streamed reply rendering with table buffering and a response box, reasoning preview and box, tool generation and progress lines, long-tool hint, credit notices, vision pre-description of images
- `cli_modern_layout.go` — the default glyph layout (accent bars, brand glyph from the skin, thought and tool rows, gutter and diff printing) versus the `classic` boxed transcript
- `cli_status_bar.go` — display width of text in terminal cells and the scrollback box width floor of 32
- `cli_modal.go` — rings the bell and emits the turn-complete notification when `display.bell_on_complete` allows
- `terminal_notify.go` — OSC 9 notification with control characters stripped, plus Warp's OSC 777 agent payload when the Warp build supports it
- `cli_commands.go` — [unwired] `cp`, `dimText`, `dimLine` print helpers left from the removed in-process slash commands

#### Terminal UI launch

`LaunchTUI` runs the Go terminal UI (`pkg/tui`) inside this process, passing launch flags through environment variables, and supplies the host callbacks the UI cannot own.

- `tui_launch.go` — builds the launch env (`ICEBATH_TUI_*`, `ICEBATH_CWD`, `TERMINAL_CWD`, client env JSON, active-session temp file), requires `--model` for bypass launches, sets up and settles the `-w` worktree, then after exit runs CLI commands the UI queued (stopping the gateway first for `uninstall`, `sessions`, `gateway`) and reopens icebath
- `tui_launch_argv.go` — `TUILaunch` argument struct and the `LaunchTUI` entry
- `tui_host.go` — ensures or discovers the gateway owner and mints a `session-ticket` over its control socket for the WebSocket attach; replaces an idle owner of another build; restores a quick snapshot with the gateway handed off; settles `/worktree new` trees after exit
- `shared_session_attach.go` — [partial] when a resumed session is held by another process, looks up its owner's `shared_runtime_url` and performs a loopback-only `/api/session-attach` handshake. Nothing writes that metadata or serves that endpoint, so it always ends in the "not available in this build" refusal
- `relaunch{,_unix,_windows}.go` — re-executes icebath carrying the flags tagged inherit-on-relaunch and `-p`; `execvp` on Unix, spawn and wait on Windows; used by the queued-command reopen and `sessions browse`

#### Console REPL

`icebath console` is a curated command prompt that is not a shell: one supported command per line, shell syntax refused, mutating commands confirmed, output capped at 20000 characters.

- `console_engine.go` — engine, REPL, help table, history, block lists (`chat`, `gateway`, `model`, `update`, `uninstall` and others), and the family table mapping CLI subcommands to console rows dispatched through a freshly bound cobra tree. Three rows name commands that do not exist (`kanban diagnose`, `kanban assignments`, `kanban boards set-workdir`)
- `console_builtins.go` — native rows: `status`, `version`, `doctor`, `logs`, `sessions list|stats|export|rename|optimize|repair`, `config show|path|set`, `profile`
- `console_builtins_cron.go` — extras tier: `cron list|status|pause|resume|run` rows
- `console_capture.go` — swaps process stdout and stderr for pipes around a command and maps exit status and Python-named exceptions to a console error
- `console_argparse.go` — [py-shim] a second small argparse emulation for the builtin rows' own flags
- `cli_loops_commands.go` — hook through which the console's `version` row reaches the version printer
- `cli_resume.go` — sources hidden from in-chat session listings: `kanban`, `tool`, `oneshot`

#### Sessions command

`CmdSessions` routes 25 actions. Read-only actions open `state.db` observationally; `prune` goes through a running gateway (`session.prune`) when there is one; `optimize`, `optimize-storage` and `prune` refuse while another process holds the store unless `--force`.

- `sessions_cmd.go` — shared plumbing, `list` with source and workspace filters and a truncation footer, `recover` front end with live progress and verdict, `import` front end
- `sessions_cmd_storage.go` — the action router, `optimize` (FTS merge plus VACUUM), `clean-markers`, `optimize-storage` (compact FTS layout rebuild with progress), `repair-routing`, `repair-prompts`, `refresh-prompts`, `stats`
- `sessions_cmd_prune.go` — `delete`, `prune` and `archive` with preview and confirmation (pinned rows spared, `--never-active` keyed rows), `rename`, `pin`/`unpin`/`pinned`, `retitle-skills`, `browse`
- `sessions_cmd_export.go` — `export` as jsonl, html, trace, a user-prompts view, or one md/qmd file per session with lineage, redaction and delete-after-verified
- `sessions_cmd_browse.go` — full-screen searchable session picker showing each session's lifecycle status tag, with a numbered fallback; the choice relaunches `icebath --resume`
- `session_filters.go` — duration and ISO time parsing and the filter set shared by prune, archive and export
- `sessions_owner.go` — finds a ready gateway for the home and runs the prune there with a 600 second timeout
- `sessions_discard.go` — `discard`: acknowledges turns lost in a gateway crash via `prompt.resolve_unknown`
- `sessions_adopt.go` — `adopt`: brings pre-gateway local chats under the gateway by resuming then detaching each

#### Offline session database recovery

`sessions recover` rebuilds canonical tables from a copy of a damaged `state.db` into a new database and never replaces the live one.

- `session_recovery.go` — path and overwrite guards, 256 MiB disk headroom check, source bundle copy with WAL/SHM sidecars, table inventory, chunked copy with bisecting rowid salvage under `--allow-partial`, orphan cleanup, placeholder sessions for orphaned messages, FTS and row-count verification, JSON report
- `session_lost_and_found.go` — last-resort salvage when `sessions` or `messages` is unreadable: runs a `.recover`-capable `sqlite3` CLI (refusing versions with the WAL-reset bug), infers column layouts of `lost_and_found` rows from value shapes, reinserts them, fabricates missing parents and rebuilds FTS

#### Cross-profile state repair

`sessions repair-profiles` settles session and routing rows that landed under the wrong profile.

- `sessions_repair_profiles.go` — scans every profile store plus voice-mode and `sessions.json` files for crossed rows, plans moves (export, import parents first, delete), and reports, rekeys or moves legacy `agent:main` rows per `--legacy-main`
- `sessions_cmd_repair_profiles.go` — the command front end: grouped report, JSON output, refusal to apply while a gateway runs for an affected store, confirmation and a snapshot of every store before `--apply`

#### Foreign session import

- `foreign_sessions.go` — discovers Claude Code (`~/.claude/projects`, `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`) and Codex CLI (`~/.codex/sessions`, `CODEX_HOME`) JSONL sessions, flattens them to alternating user and assistant text turns, offers a picker and imports through a gateway request
- `foreign_sessions_import.go` — `sessions import [--from claude|codex] [path]` front end

#### Session trace upload

Reached only through `sessions export --format trace --upload`; the user-facing text still names a `/upload-trace` slash command and an `icebath trace upload` command that do not exist.

- `trace_upload.go` — converts a session to Claude Code style trace JSONL with forced secret redaction (upload refused if redaction fails) and pushes it to the token owner's `icebath-traces` dataset as `sessions/<id>.jsonl`
- `hf_hub.go` — [py-shim] stands in for the `huggingface_hub` client: token discovery, whoami, dataset repo creation, preupload, LFS batch and multipart upload, commit, retry and rate-limit handling

#### Uninstall and data wipe

`uninstall` offers keep-data, full and `--data` modes with `--dry-run`. It removes gateway services, PATH entries, wrappers and launchers, and only deletes a code tree the installer created.

- `uninstall.go` — interactive and `--yes` flows; systemd, launchd and Windows gateway service removal; shell rc PATH stripping; wrapper script and node symlink removal; XDG leftovers; named-profile removal on request; keeps a non-installer source tree that sits inside the home
- `uninstall_support.go` — platform name, line and box printers, typed-`yes` confirmation
- `uninstall_registry_{other,windows}.go` — strips icebath entries from the user PATH and deletes `ICEBATH_HOME` and `ICEBATH_GIT_BASH_PATH` in the Windows registry; no-op elsewhere
- `data_cleanup.go` — `--data` plan: lists what to remove and keep, refusing a filesystem root or user home and protecting code, venv, package store, lock files and sibling profiles
- `data_cleanup_holders.go` — refuses or drains live holders first: gateway identity check, drain over the control socket, cron writers, multiplexed profiles

#### Logs command

- `logs.go` — `icebath logs [name]`: tail N lines of agent, errors, gateway, mcp or update logs with level, session, component and `--since` filters (continuation lines follow their record), `-f` follow, and `logs list` with sizes and ages

- `banner.go` — version label with channel or upstream and local revisions and carried commits, background update check with a waitable result, skills by category, toolset availability, all memoised per process
- `tips.go` — picks a random startup tip from the i18n catalog

- `config_load.go` — `CLIConfig`: home `config.yaml`, else `cli-config.yaml` beside the executable, merged over registry defaults with env expansion and the managed overlay; exports `TERMINAL_CWD` except in the gateway process; prefill message file resolution and loading; reasoning and service-tier parsing
- `config_load_export.go`, `prefill_exports.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers for gatewayrun, gateway and tuiserver

#### Text reports served to the gateway and terminal UI

Renderers the gateway calls for slash commands whose output is built here.

- `session_tui_reads_render.go` — `/status` and `/context` output for a TUI session, and the exported toolsets and platforms reports
- `status_report.go`, `status_report_tui.go` — the shared status field set (session, title, model, provider, tokens, created, last activity, profile path), the live agent winning over stored values

### `pkg/cliui` — line-mode terminal prompts, menus and console output

*21 files, 3,863 Go lines*

The interactive widgets every non-TUI command uses: inline text and secret fields, single and multiple choice lists with search, a full-screen surface for pickers, coloured status lines. It replaces Python `curses`, `prompt_toolkit` and `getpass` usage and keeps their names (`CursesRadiolist`, `CursesChecklist`), but the implementation is native and in wide use (setup flows, auth, uninstall, sessions browse, skills and tools pickers). It owns terminal raw-mode state and restores it on exit and on signals.

#### Console and input plumbing

- `console.go` — `Console` (streams, env, TTY and size probes), the process default console, one shared input pump per stream so several consoles never race for bytes, masked secret prompt hook, replayable line answers
- `pump_gate_{unix,windows}.go` — wait for input readiness that a wake pipe or event can cancel when no console is waiting
- `keys.go` — decodes raw input into key presses, bracketed pastes and resizes, gathering escape-sequence bursts and hearing SIGINT
- `tcflush_{bsd,linux,other}.go` — discards unread terminal input; no-op where termios is absent
- `termguard.go`, `termguard_{unix,windows}.go` — reference-counted raw mode and screen modes per terminal, restored when the last hold ends, on a terminating signal, and around Ctrl-Z suspend; `RestoreTerminal` is called from the binary's exit

#### Inline prompts and lists

- `prompt_input.go` — inline text field with emacs keys, one-entry kill ring, masked mode, default value shown beside the caret
- `prompt_select.go` — inline single or multiple choice list with headings, slash search ranked by fuzzy score, scrolling, descriptions and back/cancel keys
- `prompt_layout.go` — fits list rows into columns or a stacked form for the terminal width with the fewest wrapped lines
- `lists.go` — `CursesRadiolist`, `CursesChecklist`, `CursesSingleSelect`: live form on a terminal, numbered text fallback otherwise, replayed answers printed as a finished line
- `menu.go` — styled row segments, fuzzy scoring and filtering, numbered fallbacks, and scoped navigation events (begin, resolve, cancel, back) through which a setup flow can replay recorded answers or allow going back
- `live.go` — region below the cursor repainted in place and replaced by lasting lines when the prompt ends

#### Output, text and theme

- `output.go` — info, success, warning, error and header lines, truncated-listing footer, `Prompt`, localized `PromptYesNo`, line and secret input with a plain fallback
- `colors.go` — colour on or off (`NO_COLOR`, dumb `TERM`, not a terminal) and the `Color` wrapper
- `theme.go` — prompt palette as hex tones, colour depth detection, Unicode or ASCII glyph sets
- `text.go` — grapheme-aware measuring and word wrapping of plain and styled text

#### Full-screen surface

- `screen.go` — `Screen` interface and an ANSI implementation with curses-style colour pairs, keypad translation and timeouts, used by the session browser and the plugins toggle screen

A leaf package with one interface, so the tools setup flow in `pkg/tools` can ask questions without knowing who answers. The asker is supplied by `pkg/tuiserver` when the flow runs from the terminal UI.

#### Asker interface

- `setupflow.go` — `Asker` (say a line, choose one option, check several items with a token estimate, enter text or a secret), `ErrCancelled`, and a writer that forwards finished lines to an asker
