*1 file, 119 Go lines*

Split out of pkg/app so the gateway side can build the prompt without importing the CLI layer.

#### Prompt builder

- `init_command.go` — builds the `/init` instruction telling the agent to inspect the repo and write or merge `AGENTS.md` (under 100 lines, verified commands only, merge discipline when a file exists, user notes appended), resolving the target directory from the session's recorded cwd

## 2. Foundation: config, settings, home, logging, i18n, host info

### `pkg/config` — the configuration system: `config.yaml` load, merge and save, `.env` secrets, the administrator overlay, config backends, skins and the `icebath config` command

*80 files, 16,657 Go lines*

Owns the per-profile `<home>/config.yaml` and `<home>/.env`, plus `<home>/backups/config/`, `<home>/skins/*.yaml`, the home directory skeleton and the seeded `<home>/SOUL.md`. The effective config is the built-in defaults, deep-merged under the user document, with `${VAR}` references expanded, with the administrator's `/etc/icebath/config.yaml` merged on top; there is no generic "env var overrides config key" layer. Every read and write goes through a `ConfigBackend` chosen by `ICEBATH_CONFIG_BACKEND` (`file` by default, `remote` from `pkg/config/remote`). About 700 files import the package: the `Load` family has roughly 215 call sites, `NewSecrets` about 100, the `Py*` value helpers about 255 and the mapping-order helpers about 110. Because the package sits below its consumers, behaviour owned by `pkg/provider`, `pkg/tools`, `pkg/settings`, `pkg/commands` and `pkg/gateway` is injected through registered hook structs and package variables (`RegisterConfigFacade`, `RegisterSettingsHooks`, `RegisterRedactionSwitch`, `RegisterPolicyNote`, `RegisterConfigBootstrapEnv`, `RegisterSkillConfigVars`, `IsMultiplexActive`, `EnvWriterLaunchDenylist`, `SuppressWarningsOn`). Roughly a third of the code is port scaffolding: Python value semantics, a ruamel constructor and emitter, Python exception class names on errors. Config schema versioning and migrations do not exist: there is no version key, `icebath config` has no `migrate` verb although `icebath update` help text still mentions one, and the only migration seam (`ConfigBackend.ApplyInMemory`) has no caller.

#### Backend abstraction and selection

`ConfigBackend` is the 20-method store of a profile's user layer (read, version, write changes, locks, boot, env-name lists, doctor warnings, destination text). `route` sends any path named `config.yaml` to the selected backend and every other path to a local `FileBackend` on that explicit file. An unknown backend kind is a `ConfigBackendUnavailable` error carrying a process-exit message; the code never falls back to defaults. Before the first selection a registered env loader (from `pkg/provider`) publishes the deployment env once, so `.env` can carry the backend selection variables.

- `backend.go` — `ConfigBackend`, `FileBackend`, backend registry and bootstrap, path routing, the `ReadConfigDoc`, `ConfigVersion`, `WriteConfigKeys`, `WriteChanges` and `WriteConfigDocument` doors, write error types (`ConfigWriteError`, `ConfigLockedError`, `ConfigValueError`), context flags `PinningKeys`, `RefusingLockedOmissions`, `KeepingReadBase`; `FileBackend.ApplyInMemory` is a [stub] that only returns an error
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `logger=config`

#### Default schema

`Defaults()` is the full default document: 91 top-level keys, hand-maintained as one Go literal, and it is a second defaults table beside the per-entry defaults of `pkg/settings`. Model selection and routing: `model`, `providers`, `fallback_providers`, `fallback`, `model_overrides`, `model_catalog`, `models_dev`, `openrouter`, `bedrock`, `vertex`, `prompt_caching`, `local_runtime`, `x_search`, `moa` (mixture-of-agents presets) and `auxiliary` (per-task side models: vision, compression, approval, review, mcp, title_generation, memory_query_rewrite, tts_audio_tags, voice_chat, triage_specifier, kanban_decomposer, profile_describer, goal_judge, curator, monitor, background_review, moa_reference, moa_aggregator). Agent loop: `agent` (turn caps, budgets, timeouts, guidance switches, agent cache, reasoning overrides), `compression`, `context`, `delegation`, `goals`, `loops`, `tool_loop_guardrails`, `tool_output`, `tools` (tool search), `toolsets`, `code_execution`, `streaming`, `personalities`, `prefill_messages_file`, `context_file_max_chars`, `context_file_read_timeout`, `file_read_max_chars`. Tools and execution environment: `terminal` (backend, cwd, images, container limits, env passthrough, home mode), `web`, `browser`, `computer_use`, `bot_desktop`, `lsp`, `mcp`, `mcp_discovery_timeout`, `mcp_single_query_discovery_timeout`, `worktrees`, `checkpoints`, `proxy`, `network`, `image_gen`, `vision`, `attachments`. Voice: `tts`, `stt`, `voice`, `wake_word`. Memory, sessions and skills: `memory`, `sessions`, `session`, `max_concurrent_sessions`, `max_live_sessions`, `database`, `skills`, `curator`. Safety and secrets: `approvals`, `command_allowlist`, `security`, `privacy`, `hooks`, `hooks_auto_accept`, `auth`, `secrets` (Bitwarden and 1Password sources), `vault`. Gateway and chat platforms: `gateway`, `slack`, `discord`, `whatsapp`, `telegram`, `mattermost`, `matrix`, `platform_hints`, `quick_commands`, `human_delay`, `hosted_rooms`, `bot_mode`, `cron`, `kanban`, `plugins`. Interface: `display` (theme, skin, language, tool progress, status bar, pet, per-platform overrides), `paste_collapse_threshold`, `paste_collapse_char_threshold`, `timezone`. System: `logging`, `monitoring`, `runtime`, `updates`, `doctor`, `onboarding`.

- `defaults.go` — the 1,200-line default document literal and the constants `DefaultToolset` (`icebath-cli`), `DefaultSandboxImage`, `DefaultVercelImage`, `LegacyVercelRuntime`; `LegacySandboxImage` and `LegacySandboxImages` are unreferenced leftovers of a removed migration step
- `defaults_order.go` — `Defaults()` plus a table of the declared key order of every default mapping, so dumps and `MappingKeys` iterate in schema order

#### Loading the effective config

Load order is defaults, then the user document deep-merged in (a null over a default section is ignored), then `${VAR}` expansion, then the managed overlay. The result is cached per config path on the user file's signature, the managed file's signature and the value of every referenced env variable, and rebuilt under one process-wide config lock. A frozen worker process skips the file entirely and serves its bound JSON snapshot merged over defaults. Three views exist: effective with defaults (`Load`, `LoadContext`, `LoadReadonly`), raw user document (`ReadRawConfig`, `ReadUser`) and effective user layer without defaults (`LoadUserEffective`).

- `facade_load.go` — `FacadeHooks` registry, config lock, signature cache, `LoadContext`/`LoadReadonly`/`Load`, raw-document cache, last-known-good fallback, records `security.redact_secrets` for the log redactor; the hook fields `SkipDeepMerge` and `MaskedSecretPrompt` are never called
- `load.go` — `ReadDocument`, `ReadUser`, `Save`, `SaveUser`, `SplitModelDefault` (model default as string or mapping), `Canonicalize` (only checks that `agent` is a mapping), `InvalidUserConfigError`
- `effective.go` — `LoadUserEffective` and the fail-closed variant: user layer with references expanded and managed overlay applied, no defaults; recovers from the last good parse or newest good backup
- `tree.go` — `Tree` type: dotted-path `Lookup`/`Set`/`Unset` with list indices, backslash-escaped dots, literal dotted keys and phantom-key refusal; typed getters, `Clone`, `DeepMerge`, `ExplicitPaths`, `StripDefaults`
- `config_paths.go` — `GetConfigPath`, `GetEnvPath`, `IsManaged`, worker snapshot accessor

#### `${VAR}` references in config values

Any string value may contain `${NAME}` or `${env:NAME}`; unresolved references stay literal, and a non-env source such as `${bitwarden:...}` is left alone with a warning because external secret sources inject env vars at startup. Lookup goes through the profile's secret scope when one is bound, otherwise the process environment.

- `expand.go` — `ExpandString`, `Expand`, `RefSnapshot` and `SnapshotCurrent` (cache invalidation on env change), `EnvRefLookupContext`
- `env_ref_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrapper `EnvRefVarName`

#### Administrator-managed layer

The managed scope is a directory, `/etc/icebath` on POSIX or the path in `ICEBATH_MANAGED_DIR`, holding an optional `config.yaml` and `.env`; it is disabled under test runs. Every non-null leaf of the managed `config.yaml` is pinned over the user's value, with its references expanded against the process env only so a user cannot shadow a pinned literal; names in the managed `.env` are pinned env vars. Pinned keys are refused by every writer and stripped from saves with a notice. A malformed managed file is ignored with a loud warning.

- `managed.go` — `ManagedDir`, `LoadManagedConfig`, `LoadManagedEnv`, `ApplyManagedOverlay`, `ManagedConfigKeys`, `IsKeyManaged`, `IsEnvManaged`, `PinnedTerminalBackend`; `InvalidateManagedCache` has no caller

#### Change detection and parse caches

A file's version is mtime, size, inode and ctime in nanoseconds, plus a content digest while the newest timestamp is under two seconds old, so a same-tick rewrite is still seen.

- `file_version.go` — `FileSignature`, `RacyContentDigest`, `FileCacheVersion`, `FastSafeLoad`, `LoadYAMLFileReadonly` shared parse cache, Python `OSError` subclass names for file errors
- `file_version_{linux,bsd,windows}.go` — inode and change time from the platform stat structure; zero inode and creation time on Windows

#### Parse failures, last-known-good fallback and backups

A config that cannot be read or parsed never stops interactive use: readers get the last good expansion from this process, else the newest good backup, else defaults, and the served map is marked as a failed read so every writer refuses to persist it. The user is warned once per file version on stderr and in the log, with the YAML line and the repair commands. Backups live in `<home>/backups/config/config.yaml.<reason>.<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>` with reasons `good` (taken after each successful parse whose bytes differ from the newest) and `corrupt`, five kept per reason, each chmod 0600.

- `config_read_errors.go` — failure message text, once-per-version warning, `ActiveConfigParseFailure`, `RefuseFailedRead`, `RefuseOverwrite`, `SystemExitError`, the `RuntimeError` class the CLI turns into a clean refusal
- `config_backups.go` — `BackupConfig`, `ListConfigBackups`, `LoadNewestGoodBackup`; moves legacy siblings (`config.yaml.bak.N`, `config.yaml.corrupt.*.bak`, `config.yaml.bak-pre-migrate-*`) into the backups directory

#### Saving and comment-preserving edits

This is the code behind `icebath config set` and every programmatic save; `pkg/config/roundtrip` is only its test generator. The file is parsed into a `yaml.v3` node tree after being validated by the ruamel round-trip constructor, edited by dotted path, re-emitted with two-space indent, and then every untouched source line is restored byte for byte, with a final check that the document still decodes to the same value. Strings a YAML 1.1 reader would retype (`yes`, `no`, `on`, `off`, `null`, `~`, `y`, `n`, `true`, `false`) are quoted. Writes go through a synced temp file and rename that keeps mode and owner, then world permission bits are dropped.

- `facade_save.go` — `SaveConfig`: refuses managed installs and failed reads, strips managed keys, restores `${VAR}` templates, strips values equal to defaults unless the user wrote them, appends commented example blocks on file creation (one documents a `fallback_model` key the schema no longer has); `AtomicConfigWrite` refuses writes that would drop existing paths, `AtomicConfigReplace` allows it
- `config_write.go` — `RequireReadableConfigBeforeWrite`, node-level set and unset by dotted path, whole-document merge that reassigns only changed nodes, atomic write helpers
- `icebath_yaml.go` — `SafeLoad`/`SafeLoadText` (C-style then pure-style compose through `pkg/internal/ruamelyaml`), Python-style load warnings, `RoundtripYAML` load and dump, scalar style selection, `%YAML 1.2` directive handling
- `config_write_restore.go` — restores untouched source lines after an emit and unescapes astral code points the emitter escaped
- `worker_save.go` — `RebaseForSave`: a frozen worker lands only its own edits on the live file through a three-way merge; `MergePartialSave` for partial documents

#### `icebath config` command and related entry points

Verbs are `show` (default), `edit`, `get <key> [--json] [--raw]`, `set <key> <value>`, `unset <key>`, `check`, `path` and `env-path`. `set` and `unset` route credential-shaped dotless keys (`*_API_KEY`, `*_TOKEN`, `*_SECRET`, `TERMINAL_SSH*` and 24 named ones) to `.env`, registered settings to the `pkg/settings` writer, and refuse unknown keys with a closest-match suggestion; managed and remotely locked keys are refused. `get` prints the value in effect and masks secret-shaped values unless `--raw` or redaction is off.

- `facade_cli.go` — `ConfigCommand` dispatcher, `SetConfigValue`, `GetConfigValue`, `UnsetConfigValue`, CLI value coercion, difflib-style key suggestion, stale `model.base_url` clearing on provider change, skin file touch on `display.skin`
- `facade_cli_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exported `WriteUserConfig`
- `config_show.go` — `ShowConfig`: managed banner, paths, masked API keys, every settings group, messaging platform status, skill settings
- `config_check_diagnostics.go` — `config check` findings: saved toolset problems and disabled bundled platform plugins whose credentials are configured
- `config_language.go` — validates a `display.language` value against the i18n and plugin language layers
- `config_key_notices.go` — ANSI colour helpers honouring `NO_COLOR` and `TERM=dumb`
- `facade_misc.go` — `EditConfig` (`$EDITOR`, `$VISUAL`, then nano, vim, vi, code, notepad), `SeedConfigFile` from `cli-config.yaml.example`, `RequireParseableUserConfig` for non-interactive runs (`ICEBATH_IGNORE_USER_CONFIG=1` bypass), `GetProjectRoot`, `GetContainerExecInfo`, `WritePlatformConfigField`, startup warnings for config issues and deprecated `MESSAGING_CWD`/`TERMINAL_CWD`

#### Structure validation

Validation is advisory: it yields `ConfigIssue` records printed at gateway start and by `icebath doctor`, and never blocks a load. Type checking of individual keys happens in `pkg/settings`, not here.

- `config_structure.go` — `ValidateConfigStructure`: runs the checks below and flags root-level `base_url`, `api_key`, `rate_limit_delay`, `api_mode` as misplaced
- `config_value_checks.go` — `voice.submit_mode` must be `direct` or `draft`, `timezone` must be a loadable IANA zone, web backends naming removed providers, container slots holding a quoted string that parses as a list or mapping
- `config_issues.go` — `ConfigIssue` type and `AddIssue`

#### `.env` file: parsing, cache and writers

`<home>/.env` is the secrets file: `KEY=value` lines with optional `export`, quotes and inline comments; a BOM is dropped and invalid UTF-8 is read as Latin-1. Two writers coexist. The current one (`SaveEnvValueContext`, `RemoveHomeEnvValue`) holds the cross-process lock `<home>/.env.lock` for up to 15 s, refuses managed keys and a denylist of names that steer execution or icebath policy (`PATH`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`, `GIT_CONFIG_*`, `PYTHONPATH`, `NODE_OPTIONS`, `EDITOR`, `ICEBATH_HOME`, `ICEBATH_YOLO_MODE` and others), strips newlines and non-ASCII characters with a warning, writes atomically (an existing file keeps its mode, a new one gets 0600 unless managed or in a container) and publishes the value to the process env or the profile's secret scope. The older one (`SetEnvValue`, `RemoveEnvValue`) validates the name, rejects a non-ASCII value and writes at 0600, but has only an in-process mutex: no cross-process lock, no denylist, no managed-key refusal and no publication. `SetEnvValue` and the `Secrets.Set`, `Remove` and `First` methods have no callers, but `RemoveEnvValue` is still called by the settings writer, WhatsApp registration and the TUI hub setup, bypassing those guards.

- `env.go` — dotenv parser and quoting, `SetEnvValue`/`RemoveEnvValue`, `AtomicWrite`, the `EnvVar` type and the 134-entry optional env-var catalog (description, prompt, URL, category, tools unlocked), `Secrets` resolver that reads `.env` before the process env
- `env_file_cache.go` — `LoadEnvFile`: parse memo keyed on a file's exact bytes, 64 files, least recently used evicted
- `env_save.go` — `SaveEnvValueContext`, writer denylist, managed-install and managed-key refusal text, `ManagedSystem` passthrough
- `env_lines.go` — atomic line-level `.env` replace keeping the prior mode or securing a new file; the exported `ReadEnvLines`, `WriteEnvLines`, `EnvLineDefinesKey` have no callers
- `env_value_error.go` — `EnvValueError`, the refusal a `.env` write returns
- `env_credential_check.go` — strips non-ASCII characters from a credential and prints which positions were removed
- `credential_file_perms.go` — warns with a `chmod 600` hint when a credential file is group or world readable

#### Secret lookup, masking and the env-var catalog

`GetEnvValue` reads the process env (through the profile secret scope when registered) before `.env`, the opposite order of `Secrets.Get`; `GetEnvValuePreferDotenv` prefers `.env` unless it holds an unresolved `op://` reference. Masking shows the first and last four characters of values of twelve or more characters and `***` otherwise. A config key is secret-shaped when its last segment is one of fifteen names (`api_key`, `token`, `password`, ...) or ends in `_api_key`, `_token`, `_secret`, `_password`, `_key`, `_access_key`.

- `facade_secrets.go` — `GetEnvValue`, `RemoveHomeEnvValue`, `SaveEnvValueSecure`, `CustomEndpointKeyEnv`, `MaskSecret`, `RedactConfigValue`, `IsEnvConfigKey`, redaction switch registration; `SaveAnthropicOAuthToken` and `SaveAnthropicAPIKey` have no callers
- `facade_env_vars.go` — `.env` write lock, stdout and stdin seams, empty `RequiredEnvVars`; [unwired] `GetMissingEnvVars`, `GetMissingSkillConfigVars` and `SanitizeEnvFile` were the setup checklist and `.env` line normaliser
- `optional_env.go` — `OptionalEnvTable`: insertion-ordered catalog with a lazily run "fill" so provider and platform entries join on first read
- `env_number.go` — `EnvInt`, `EnvFloat` and the shared truthy spellings `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`
- `env_var_enabled.go` — [port-artifact] exported `EnvVarEnabled`

#### Terminal config to environment bridge and `.env` reload

Terminal tools read `TERMINAL_*` env vars, so 33 `terminal.*` keys are mirrored into the environment (`terminal.backend` as `TERMINAL_ENV`, the rest as `TERMINAL_<KEY>`); a key written in the file overrides an existing env value, a default only fills an unset one, and `cwd` values `.`, `auto` and `cwd` are never bridged.

- `facade_env.go` — `ApplyTerminalConfigToEnv`, `TERMINAL_DOCKER_IMAGE_PINNED` flag, `LoadEnv`, `ReloadEnv` (re-reads `.env` into the process and unsets known keys that were removed); `TerminalConfigEnvVarForKey` has no caller
- `facade_env_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exported `TerminalEnvValueText`

#### Platform plugin manifests as env-var declarations

Chat platform plugins declare `requires_env` and `optional_env` in `plugin.yaml`; at package init these are read from the bundled plugin tree (compiled into the binary, or `ICEBATH_BUNDLED_PLUGINS`) and from `<home>/plugins/` and added to the env-var catalog. A declared name is a secret when marked `password` or `secret`, or when it ends in `_TOKEN`, `_SECRET`, `_KEY`, `_PASSWORD` or `_JSON`.

- `facade_platform.go` — manifest discovery, env entry parsing, `PlatformManifestSecretEnvs`, `PlatformManifestSecretScan`, `PlatformManifestStamp` change key, `BundledPlatformManifests`
- `facade_platform_compiled.go` — reads platform manifests out of the embedded `pkg/plugintree` archive
- `platform_manifest_names.go` — directory names of readable platform plugins, bundled and user

#### Home skeleton and `SOUL.md` seeding

`EnsureIcebathHome` runs before every config load and write: it refuses a deleted named profile, creates the home and the subdirectories `cron`, `sessions`, `logs`, `logs/curator`, `memories`, `pairing`, `hooks`, `image_cache`, `audio_cache`, `skills` as owner-only, and never creates the missing target of a symlinked component. A managed install requires the directories to exist already and uses a group-shared umask of 007 instead of chmod.

- `config_home.go` — `InitializeHome`, `EnsureIcebathHome`, `HomeInitializationError`, `SecureDir`, `SecureFile` (0600 unless managed or in a container), `DropOtherAccess`
- `config_home_{unix,windows}.go` — managed umask switch; no-op on Windows
- `soul.go` — `DefaultIdentity` text, writes `SOUL.md` on first run and replaces it only when it still matches one of six earlier auto-seeded texts

#### Install method detection and update guidance

The install method comes from a `.install_method` stamp beside the binary, then one in the home, then the managed marker, a Nix store path, a package-manager layout (Homebrew, winget, Scoop, Chocolatey, pipx) and finally a git checkout; eighteen method names are recognised.

- `facade_install.go` — `DetectInstallMethod`, `RecommendedUpdateCommand` and the per-method command table, Nix and Docker guidance text, `TermuxInstallCommand`
- `facade_install_table.go` — test seam that patches one method's update command

#### NixOS integration: container routing and settings merge

When the NixOS module runs icebath in a container it writes `<home>/.container-mode` (backend, container name, exec user, binary path); the host CLI then replaces itself with `<backend> exec` (docker unless the file names another runtime) of the same command, retrying through `sudo -n` when the container is not visible. Routing is off inside a container and when `ICEBATH_DEV=1`. The hidden Nix verbs in `cmd/icebath/nix_module.go` merge module settings into `config.yaml`.

- `container_exec.go` — `ExecInContainer`: 15 s inspect probe, sudo fallback with NixOS sudo-rule guidance, forwards `TERM`, `COLORTERM`, `LANG`, `LC_ALL`
- `container_exec_{unix,windows}.go` — process replacement by `execve`; child process with inherited stdio on Windows
- `nix_module.go` — `NixMergeConfig` deep-merges Nix settings JSON over `config.yaml`; `NixRenderSettings` only reserialises the JSON although its comment promises to add a config version

#### Frozen worker config policy

A gateway-managed worker process binds its whole config once, as JSON, before any config read; afterwards loads return that snapshot, `.env` reads return nothing, and plugin manifests are skipped in safe mode. Binding after a config read, binding twice, or using the policy across a fork is an error.

- `safe_worker_policy.go` — `BindWorkerConfig`, `BindSafeWorkerPolicy`, `SafeWorkerEnabled`, `WorkerConfigSnapshot`, `NoteRuntimeImport`

#### Skins

A skin is a named palette (32 colour keys, optional light and dark variants), spinner, branding strings (agent name, welcome, goodbye, response label, prompt symbol, help header), tool prefix, tool emojis and banner art. User skins in `<home>/skins/<name>.yaml` win over built-ins, and missing keys fall back to the default skin `blackwall`. `display.skin` selects the active one, tracked per routed home.

- `skin_engine.go` — `LoadSkin`, `ListSkins`, `GetActiveSkin`, `InitSkinFromConfig`, colour filter hook for light mode, custom CSS capped at 32,768 characters
- `skin_cmd.go` — `icebath skin list|use|set`: `set` writes one `#rrggbb` colour into a user skin or forks a built-in as `<name>-custom` and activates it
- `skin_reset_export.go` — [port-artifact] test reset of the active skin state
- `builtin_skins.json` — [data] seven embedded skins (`blackwall`, `taro`, `light`, `contrast`, `plain`, `cyberpunk`, `dracula`), consumed by the skin engine

#### Domain helpers parked in this package

Product rules that have nothing to do with configuration storage but live here so that low-level packages can share them.

- `reasoning_config.go` — reasoning effort levels (`minimal` to `ultra`), per-model `agent.reasoning_overrides` and provider routing matched across spelling variants of a model id
- `turns.go` — `ResolveTurnLimit`: `agent.max_turns` parsing with the unlimited spellings `none`, `unlimited`, `inf`, `0`, `-1`
- `utils_proxy.go` — rewrites `socks://` proxy env vars to `socks5://`, cleans IPv6 entries in `NO_PROXY`, and names OpenAI model families that need `max_completion_tokens`
- `icebath_time.go` — configured timezone from `ICEBATH_TIMEZONE` (not honoured under profile multiplexing) or else the `timezone` key, cached per profile; `TimeNow`, surrogate-safe `strftime`
- `warning_notifications.go` — policy deciding whether diagnostic notices and diagnostic-only wake-ups are shown or muted on a chat platform

#### Atomic JSON and YAML file writers

General-purpose atomic writers used well beyond config (about 70 call sites for the JSON ones): synced temp file beside the target, rename, existing mode and owner kept.

- `atomic_json.go` — `AtomicJSONWrite` and variants with dump options, forced mode and directory fsync
- `safe_dump.go` — `AtomicYAMLWrite` plus [py-shim] an 1,100-line port of the ruamel safe representer and emitter (`SafeDump`), so written YAML matches Python output byte for byte

#### Python value and YAML construction emulation

[py-shim] Reproduces PyYAML and ruamel loading and Python value semantics so that config values, error texts and key order match the Python original. Real dependencies hide inside: every config map's key order and "failed read" marker live in a side table keyed by map identity, and about 110 call sites outside the package rely on `MappingKeys`, `SetMappingKeys` and `AppendMappingKey`.

- `pyvalue.go` — `PyRepr`, `PyStr`, `PyTruthy`, `PyTypeName`, `ShlexQuote` for YAML-shaped values
- `pyvalue_helpers.go` — Python equality across bool and numbers, `OSError` text, `Path.resolve` and `expanduser` equivalents, UTF-8 decode error text, the unrelated `BotProfile` struct
- `map_meta.go` — weak-pointer side table giving a plain Go map its insertion order, failed-read error, dict subclass and non-string keys
- `yaml_construct.go` — port of ruamel `SafeConstructor`: merge keys, duplicate-key refusal, YAML 1.1 ints, floats, timestamps, binary, sets, recursion limits
- `yaml_construct_rt.go` — round-trip constructor variant used to validate a file before it is edited
- `yaml_pyvalues.go` — Python ordering of mixed-type keys for sorted dumps

- `key_order.go` — `MappingKeyOrder`: key order of one mapping read straight from a YAML file

### `pkg/config/remote` — "Remote Config" backend: a profile's user layer served by an external HTTP config plane

*9 files, 2,646 Go lines*

Registers the `remote` backend at init and is linked into the binary by a blank import in `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go`. With `ICEBATH_CONFIG_BACKEND=remote` each profile's user layer is held in memory, fetched from `ICEBATH_CONFIG_REMOTE_URL` (https, or http on loopback only) under the agent identity `ICEBATH_CONFIG_INSTANCE_ID`, authenticated by an OAuth2 client-credentials token from `GATEWAY_RELAY_IDP_TOKEN_URL`, `_CLIENT_ID`, `_CLIENT_SECRET` and `_SCOPE`. There is no local fallback: a failed boot fetch stops the process, the administrator's `/etc/icebath/config.yaml` is ignored with a warning, and file tooling (`config edit`, backups) is refused. The plane server is not in this repository; only a test double exists. The code is complete and wired, with one dead helper and an empty migration step.

#### Backend state, boot, polling and writes

One `profileState` per profile home holds the fetched document, etag, profile version and lock list. Boot fetch retries after 10 s and 20 s, honouring `Retry-After` up to 20 s, then fails closed; a poller goroutine re-fetches every 300 s with ten percent jitter (minimum 30 s) using `If-None-Match` and keeps the loaded config on any error. A write is one `PATCH` carrying `expectedVersion`; a 409 triggers one re-read and retry. Locked keys are dropped from whole-document saves with a notice and refused for keyed sets.

- `backend.go` — `remoteBackend` implementing `ConfigBackend`; `postprocess` is a [stub] that only sets a flag where config migrations were meant to run in memory; `firstChange` is dead code; `PollAll` has no caller
- `remote.go` — process-wide backend singleton and `RegisterConfigBackend("remote", ...)`

#### Wire protocol and transport policy

Requests go to `<url>/v1/config/self?profile=<name>` with `Authorization: Bearer`, `X-Icebath-Instance-Id` and a 15 s timeout. `GET` answers `config`, `profileVersion`, `locks` (path and level) and an etag; `PATCH` sends `set` (encoded path to value) and `unset`. Refusal codes handled: 403 `config_key_locked`; 400 `config_secret_literal`, `config_value_invalid`, `config_path_invalid`, `config_path_reserved`; 413 `config_level_too_large`, `config_body_too_large`. Credentials are never sent to a non-https host, a URL with user info, query or fragment, or across a redirect.

- `client.go` — `Request`, `Bearer`, response and transport error types, strict JSON decoding, failure wording that mimics CPython's urllib messages
- `credentials.go` — `PlaneToken`: client-credentials grant with a token cache that expires 30 s early; `PlaneCredentialEnvNames`, the env names protected from secret sources
- `destination.go` — `CheckedURL`, `DisplayURL`, the no-redirect HTTP client, a port of `urllib.parse.urlsplit`
- `paths.go` — dotted path codec with backslash escapes; limits of 32 segments, 256 bytes per segment, 2,048 bytes encoded; `__proto__` reserved; lock coverage test
- `diff.go` — set and unset diff between documents, intent replay over a newer base, lock stripping and `WriteCheck`, JSON equality with exact number comparison

#### Value conversion and the secret-key rule

Values are converted to JSON (integers beyond 2^53-1 become strings, NaN and infinities are refused, datetimes become ISO text). A secret-shaped key may hold only a `${VAR}` reference, an empty string or null; a literal is refused before anything is sent.

- `values.go` — `ToWire`, `IsSecretPath`, `SecretLiteralPath`
- `config-secret-keys.json` — [data] vendored contract fixture embedded by `values.go`: 15 secret key names, secret and non-secret suffixes, 24 env-style keys with suffixes and the `TERMINAL_SSH` prefix, the placeholder pattern, three non-secret path exceptions, and conformance vectors read only by tests

### `pkg/config/roundtrip` — generators and oracles for config round-trip property tests

*4 files, 985 Go lines*

Despite the name this is not the comment-preserving writer (that is `pkg/config/config_write.go` and `icebath_yaml.go`); nothing outside test files imports it.

#### Round-trip test generators

[test-support] Seeded config and dotenv generators, a difflib port and tree comparison helpers.

- `gen.go`, `tree.go`, `diff.go`, `dotenv.go` — [test-support] random config documents, path and equality helpers, line-diff assertions, dotenv cases

### `pkg/settings` — typed registry of every user setting, its layered resolution and its single writer

*33 files, 7,363 Go lines*

A typed layer over the same `config.yaml`, not a second file: it reads the raw user document through `pkg/config`, never calls `config.Defaults()`, and carries its own default on each registered entry, so two default tables exist in the codebase. About 1,120 settings are registered at package init as exported variables, read as `settings.X.Get(ctx)` from about 520 call sites, while about 215 call sites still read the merged tree from `config.Load`. `Set` and `Reset` are the only writers and feed `icebath config set`, the terminal UI's `/settings` screen and slash shortcuts. It also persists `<home>/settings_state.json` and session-scoped values through a store registered by `pkg/tuihost`. No port scaffolding; this is native Go. Unfinished parts: the workspace scope is declared but not writable, the `Secret` kind has no registered setting, and unknown-key notices are gated on a call nothing makes.

#### Registry, types and metadata

Each setting has a dotted key, label, one-line description, one of twelve screen groups (Model, Agent, Tools, Terminal, Safety, Voice, Images and media, Appearance, While it works, Memory and sessions, Chat apps, System), allowed scopes, an apply mode (live, next turn, new session, restart) and optional slash shortcut, env override, validator, companion keys and derivation. The registered top-level namespaces are: auxiliary (135), tts (72), display (66), agent (58), gateway (48), terminal (45), discord (43), stt (37), compression (34), delegation (24), telegram (22), sessions (22), cron (22), kanban (21), model (19), secrets (18), browser (17), skills (16), voice (15), slack (15), security (13), matrix (13), wake_word (12), tool_loop_guardrails (11), monitoring (11), lsp (11), computer_use (11), buzz (11), approvals (11), web (10), curator (10), plugins (9), proxy (8), memory (8), yuanbao (7), whatsapp_cloud (7), whatsapp (7), weixin (7), vault (7), updates (7), tools (7), database (7), checkpoints (7), streaming (6), moa (6), image_gen (6), bluebubbles (6), worktrees (5), model_catalog (5), mattermost (5), local_runtime (5), dingtalk (5), context (5), bot_desktop (5), bedrock (5), x_search (4), wecom_callback (4), loops (4), vision (3), tool_output (3), openrouter (3), logging (3), human_delay (3), feishu (3), code_execution (3), wecom, vertex, timeouts, signal, runtime, qqbot, onboarding, hosted_rooms, auth (2 each), and one key each for worktree_sync, worktree, video_gen, toolsets, timezone, session, quick_commands, providers, provider_routing, prompt_caching, privacy, prefill_messages_file, platform_toolsets, platforms, platform_hints, personalities, paste_collapse_threshold, paste_collapse_char_threshold, network, models_dev, model_overrides, mcp_single_query_discovery_timeout, mcp_servers, mcp_discovery_timeout, mcp, max_live_sessions, max_concurrent_sessions, logins, known_plugin_toolsets, known_builtin_toolsets, hooks_auto_accept, hooks, goals, file_read_max_chars, fallback_providers, fallback, doctor, custom_prompt, context_file_read_timeout, context_file_max_chars, command_allowlist, bot_mode, attachments. The registry is a superset of the root keys of `config.Defaults()`; it adds eleven chat platforms and keys such as `mcp_servers`, `platform_toolsets`, `provider_routing` and `logins`.

- `settings.go` — `Kind`, `Scope` (global, workspace, session), `Apply`, `Source`, `Meta`, `Entry`, error values, session context key, the `go:generate` line for `docgen`

- `groups.go` — the twelve groups with titles, summaries and order

#### Resolution, platform overrides and scopes

Precedence, highest first: administrator pin (whole value, or per named part for map and object settings), env override, derived value, session value, per-platform override under `display.platforms.<platform>`, the profile's stored value, platform tier default, registry default. Only two settings declare an env override (`ICEBATH_STARTUP_WATCHDOG`, `ICEBATH_STARTUP_WATCHDOG_TIMEOUT_S`). Stored values that do not fit their type are reported once and replaced by the default. The layers of a home are cached on the signatures of `config.yaml`, the state file and the managed file.

- `resolve.go` — `Resolve`, layer cache, managed pins, misfit notices, derived companions, `DefaultsOnly` context; the unknown-key notice needs `PluginKeysRegistered`, which only a test calls, so it never fires

- `state.go` — `<home>/settings_state.json`: runtime state settings the app writes for itself and no install can lock (currently only `voice.chat_modes`)

#### Writing and change notification

`Set` coerces and validates, refuses administrator-pinned, managed-install and remotely locked keys, writes to the global or session scope and notifies subscribers with old and new values and the apply mode. Global writes go through the comment-preserving `config.WriteChanges` under the config lock; derived settings write only their companion keys. [partial] The workspace scope returns "not writable yet"; it was meant to be a per-project settings file.

### `pkg/home` — icebath home directory: location, profiles, layout paths, permissions, scratch space and subprocess home

*28 files, 3,879 Go lines*

Resolves which directory is "the home" for a process or a request and names the files inside it. About 1,000 files import it; `Dir`, `Key`, `Display`, `Mkdir` and `ProfileNameFor` are the main entry points. The default home is `~/.icebath` (on Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\icebath`), with `ICEBATH_DATA_DIR_SUFFIX` appended; `ICEBATH_HOME` relocates it, and a per-request context override (`WithOverride`) lets one gateway process serve many profiles. The package also owns directory permission policy, Windows ACL repair, the per-home scratch directory with its detached pruner, and the `HOME` given to subprocesses. It leans on `pkg/internal/pypath` for pathlib semantics but the behaviour is product behaviour. It also holds a few unrelated constants.

#### Home resolution and profiles

The root home owns `profiles/<name>/`, each a full home; the profile named `default` is the root itself. Profile ids match `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`. A directory counts as a live profile when it holds one of `config.yaml`, `.env`, `SOUL.md`, `profile.yaml`, `auth.json`, `state.db` and has no tombstone at `profiles/.deleted/<name>`. `Mkdir` refuses to recreate a deleted or missing named profile or a home this process erased.

- `home.go` — `Process`, `Dir`, `Root`, `RootOf`, `ProfileHome`, `NamedProfileHome`, `ProfileNameFor`, `ListProfiles`, tombstones, `AssertProfileLive`, `Mkdir`, `Display` (tilde form), `Key` (resolved, cached identity of a home)
- `constants_extra.go` — `RootForEnvironment` (home another process would resolve from its env), `SudoInvokerDefaultHome`, one-time warning when `ICEBATH_HOME` is unset but `<root>/active_profile` names a profile, `PinProcess`, `OptionalSkillsDir` (`ICEBATH_OPTIONAL_SKILLS`), legacy `<home>/node` tree detection, `InstallRoot`; also unrelated constants `ConnectorDownloadsSubdir`, `PartialStreamStubID`, `FinishReasonLength`
- `identity_markers.go` — [port-artifact] exported copy of the profile identity marker list
- `profile_cli_selector.go` — `-p <name> ` prefix for commands shown to a user of a named profile
- `record_key.go` — `icebath_home` key in pid, lock and runtime records, still reading the pre-rename spelling `hermes_home`

#### Layout paths

Paths the package names: `config.yaml`, `.env`, `auth.json`, `SOUL.md`, `state.db`, `memories/`, `skills/`, `skill-bundles/`, `plugins/`, `plugin-data/`, `cron/`, `logs/`, `cache/`, `cache/scratch/`, `pending/`, `sessions/`, `locales/`. Elsewhere in this slice the home also holds `backups/config/`, `skins/`, `settings_state.json`, `.env.lock`, `.managed`, `.install_method`, `.container-mode`, `home/` (profile-private `HOME`), `downloads/connectors/`, `optional-skills/`, `node/`, and on the root home `active_profile`, `install_id`, `spawn-ledger.json`, `cache/fetch/` and `logs/update.log`.

- `layout.go` — one function per path above; `CronDir` has no caller
- `icebath_dir.go` — `IcebathDir`: returns a legacy directory name when it already has content, else the new subpath
- `constants_values.go` — unrelated shared constants: TUI indicator styles, 16 MiB attachment cap, local runtime root dirs (`models`, `runtimes`, `node`), OpenRouter and AI Gateway base URLs, OpenRouter variant suffixes

#### Directory permissions and managed installs

Home directories are chmod 0700 unless the install is managed (`ICEBATH_MANAGED` or a `<home>/.managed` marker naming the package manager; a bare marker means `nixos`), or the process runs in a container or with `ICEBATH_SKIP_CHMOD` or `ICEBATH_CONTAINER` set, in which case modes are left to the deployment. `ICEBATH_HOME_MODE` sets an explicit octal mode, and `ICEBATH_UID` and `ICEBATH_GID` chown each directory.

- `secure_dir.go` — `ManagedSystem`, `ContainerOrChmodSkipped`, `ApplySecureDirPolicy`
- `secure_parent.go` — `SecureParentDir`: chmod 0700 on a credential file's parent, never on `/`, a top-level directory or the install tree

#### Windows ACL repair for elevated runs

A directory created by an elevated Windows process is owned by Administrators and unusable by the same user unelevated, so `MakeUserDir` grants the user an inheriting full-control entry on every directory it creates under the home, and `icebath update` repairs the whole tree afterwards. Grants never pass through a junction, symlink or hard link.

- `dir_acl.go` — `MakeUserDir`, `GrantUserAccess`, `GrantTreeUserAccess`, link-free tree walk, `icacls` fallback, `PathMkdir`, `UnusableDirRemedy` hint text
- `dir_acl_{unix,windows}.go` — native ACL writer, token elevation probe and `lstat` facts on Windows; stubs returning "not elevated" elsewhere
- `update_acl.go` — `RepairWindowsHomeACL`, called after an elevated update

#### Scratch directory and detached pruner

`<home>/cache/scratch` is exported as `TMPDIR`, `TMP` and `TEMP` (with the marker `ICEBATH_SCRATCH_DIR`) for every icebath process and child unless the user set those variables. At most once per process and once per hour (stamp file `.last_prune`) the binary re-executes itself detached with the hidden first argument `__icebath_scratch_prune__` and removes entries idle for 24 hours. Before deleting, it signals same-user processes whose working directory is inside a doomed entry (TERM, then KILL after 3 s), sparing the launcher's ancestry and anything registered in `spawn-ledger.json` or `processes.json`, and runs `git worktree prune` for repositories with worktrees there. Entries it may not delete are recorded in `.prune_stuck.json` and skipped for up to seven days or until their ownership or permissions change, and are reported with a removal command.

- `scratch.go` — `EnsureScratchDir`, hourly prune latch, `PruneScratchDir`, `ScratchDirUsageBytes`
- `scratch_env.go` — `ApplyScratchTmpEnv`, `ExportScratchTmpEnv`, `SocketSafeTmpdir` (falls back to `/tmp` when the temp root exceeds 50 characters, for AF_UNIX socket paths)
- `scratch_detach.go` — `DispatchScratchPruneEntry` (must be called first in `main`), detached child spawn, lineage encoding, `RunScratchPrune`
- `scratch_prune.go` — idle scan, process reaping with birth-time checks against pid reuse, ledger readers, worktree release, audit log `logs/scratch-prune.log` (5 MiB, three backups)
- `scratch_stuck.go` — stuck-entry records, permission-error collection, `RemovalHint` (plain or docker-based command), `StuckEntries` for the doctor report
- `scratch_stuck_{unix,windows}.go` — inode fingerprint, access probe and `flock` on the stuck lock file; no stuck tracking on Windows
- `detach_{unix,windows}.go` — detached child attributes: new session on POSIX; new process group, hidden console and job breakaway on Windows

#### Subprocess home and path translation

`TERMINAL_HOME_MODE` (`auto`, `profile`, `real`, with aliases) decides the `HOME` a tool subprocess receives: the profile's private `<home>/home` directory, the OS user's real home (also exported as `ICEBATH_REAL_HOME`), or unchanged; in a container `auto` prefers the profile home.

- `subprocess_home.go` — `RealHome`, `SubprocessHome`, `ApplySubprocessHomeEnv`, `NormHomePath`
- `wsl_paths.go` — maps Windows drive paths and `\\wsl$` UNC paths to POSIX when running inside WSL
- `wsl_probe.go` — test seam replacing the WSL probe
- `ipv4_preference.go` — passthrough applying the `network.force_ipv4` setting to the process resolver
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `logger=home`

### `pkg/logging` — log files, rotation, redaction and the logger hierarchy behind `slog`

*19 files, 2,599 Go lines*

A port of Python's `logging` module shape (named loggers with levels and propagation, handlers, filters, `%(name)s`-style formats) that receives every `slog` and standard `log` record through a bridge installed at process start. It writes `<home>/logs/agent.log` (level from `logging.level`, default INFO; rotated at `logging.max_size_mb`, default 5 MB, with `logging.backup_count`, default 3), `errors.log` (WARNING and above, 2 MB, two backups) and, in gateway mode only, `gateway.log` (INFO, 5 MB, three backups, gateway packages only). Every line passes a redacting formatter whose hooks are installed by `pkg/tools`; setup fails if they are missing. Callers are `cmd/icebath`, `pkg/gatewayrun`, `pkg/gatewaycli` and `pkg/agent`. The logger hierarchy and format strings are scaffolding; the files, limits, redaction and per-profile routing are product behaviour.

#### Setup and log file catalog

- `setup.go` — `SetupLogging`, `SetupVerboseLogging` (DEBUG console handler), `ComponentPrefixes` mapping six components (gateway, agent, tools, cli, cron, gui) to package names for filters and `icebath logs --component`
- `log_files.go` — names for `icebath logs`: `agent`, `errors`, `gateway`, `update` (kept on the root home), `mcp` (`mcp-stderr.log`)
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Logger hierarchy, formatting and the slog bridge

Each package logs through `slog.Default().With("logger", "<package>")`; the bridge turns that attribute into a named logger whose level, handlers and propagation can be set separately. Line format is `<time>,<ms> <LEVEL> [<session id>] <logger>: <message>`; the session tag comes from a goroutine-local set by `SetSessionContext`, and each record carries the resolved home so it can be routed after its context is gone. The redaction policy of a profile comes from `security.redact_secrets` and from `ICEBATH_REDACT_SECRETS` in `.env`, which `pkg/config` reports to the redactor as it loads them.

- `logger.go` — levels (DEBUG 10 to CRITICAL 50), `Record`, `Handler`, `Filter`, `Logger` with slash-separated names, `GetLogger`, `Shutdown`
- `handler.go` — `Formatter` rendering Python logging format fields, redaction capture, stream handler
- `session.go` — redaction hook variables, session context, record construction, `slog` handler and standard `log` writer feeding the hierarchy, attribute rendering as `key=value`
- `session_export.go` — [port-artifact] `InstallSlogBridge` and an unused `MakeRecord`

#### Rotating file handler

Size-based rotation with numbered backups. It reopens the file when it was renamed, deleted or replaced externally, gives the file mode 0660 on managed installs, restores owner and mode after rollover, and reports an unavailable destination once instead of per record. On Windows it takes a cross-process lock file (`.__agent.lock` beside `agent.log`, twenty attempts) and falls back to no rollover when locking is unavailable.

- `rotating.go` — `managedRotatingFileHandler` with plain and Windows locking emit paths
- `owner_{unix,windows}.go` — uid and gid of a file for owner restoration; none on Windows

#### Queue and per-profile routing

File handlers sit behind one unbounded queue and listener goroutine so logging callers never block on file I/O. When a process serves several profile homes, a routing handler opens one file set per home and sends each record to the home it carries.

- `queue.go` — queue handler and listener, `DrainLogQueue` for hard exits, `EnableProfileLogRouting`, `ReleaseProfileLogHandlers` before a profile is deleted; `FlushLogQueue` has no caller
- `router.go` — `profileRoutingFileHandler`: per-home handler set, retires a home deleted out of band
- `queue_reset_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] test reset

#### Stdio redaction and stderr handlers

- `stdio.go` — `RedactDetachedStdio` pipes stdout and stderr of a detached gateway through secret redaction; UTF-8-safe stderr writer; line buffering for piped stdout
- `stderr_encoding_{other,windows}.go` — stderr encoding from the locale, or the console and ANSI code page on Windows
- `acp_stderr_export.go` — `NewRedactingStderrHandler` for the ACP server and `Logger.Exception`
- `gateway_stderr_export.go` — `AddGatewayStderrHandler`: console handler for foreground gateway runs
- `tool_calls_export.go` — `NewRedactingRotatingFileHandler`, used by the gateway for `logs/tool_calls.log`

### `pkg/i18n` — message catalogs and translation lookup for the CLI, gateway and terminal UI

*39 files, 1,623 Go lines*

`T(ctx, key, lang, kwargs)` is called from about 190 files, mostly `pkg/gatewayrun` and `pkg/gateway`. The active language is the `display.language` setting of the home in context, default `en`; lookups fall back to English and then to the key itself. Catalogs come in two surfaces: `core` (strings formatted in Go with Python `str.format` named placeholders) and `tui` (strings shipped to the terminal UI client, which formats positional `{0}` placeholders itself). Three layers merge per language, later winning: bundled catalogs, the user overlay `<home>/locales/<lang>[.tui].yaml`, and language packs registered by plugins. `ICEBATH_BUNDLED_LOCALES` replaces the embedded tree with a directory.

#### Lookup, language resolution and layers

- `i18n.go` — embeds `locales/*.yaml`; `T`, `GetLanguage`, `ResolveLanguageID` (ids, about 75 aliases such as `deutsch` or `pt-br`, regional fallback to the base tag), `SurfaceCatalog` for the TUI, `LanguageOptions` with endonym and RTL flag
- `layers.go` — locale file name grammar `<lang>[.<surface>].yaml`, flattening nested YAML to dotted keys, `RegisterPack` and `UnregisterPack` for plugin language packs, user overlay reader, per-layer caches
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Python-compatible parsing and formatting

[py-shim] Catalogs were authored for PyYAML and `str.format`, so both are reproduced; every translated string with arguments depends on them.

- `yaml11.go` — YAML 1.1 loader over `yaml.v3` nodes: `yes`/`no` booleans, octal and sexagesimal numbers, timestamps, merge keys, duplicate-key refusal
- `pyformat.go` — `PyFormat`: `str.format` with keyword arguments, attribute and index access, nested format specs

#### Catalogs

Seventeen languages: af, ar, de, en, es, fr, ga, hu, it, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr, uk, zh, zh-hant; Arabic is the only right-to-left one.

- `locales/{af,ar,de,en,es,fr,ga,hu,it,ja,ko,pt,ru,tr,uk,zh,zh-hant}.yaml` — [data] core surface catalogs, nested YAML, one per language (17); `en.yaml` is the reference with about 2,700 lines
- `locales/*.tui.yaml` — [data] terminal UI surface catalogs, flat dotted keys with positional placeholders, one per non-English language (16); English TUI strings live in the TUI client, not here
- `locales/_keys.tui.json` — [data] list of every TUI key (about 3,800), the reference `pkg/plugins` validates language packs against; not embedded (the embed pattern is `*.yaml`), so a release binary has it only when `ICEBATH_BUNDLED_LOCALES` points at a directory

### `pkg/fetch` — pinned, resumable downloads into a verified cache

*2 files, 286 Go lines*

Used by `pkg/media` (wake word engines, Piper voices) and `pkg/internal/sherpaonnx` to fetch model assets on first use.

#### Asset cache

- `fetch.go` — `File`: downloads an asset pinned by name, size and sha256 into `<root home>/cache/fetch/<sha256>/`, resuming with `Range`, four attempts 2 s apart on transient failures, digest verified; `Tree`: unpacks a verified `.tar`, `.tar.gz`, `.tgz` or `.tar.bz2` and refuses entries or links that leave the directory
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/tarzst` — deterministic zstd tar archives served as a read-only file system

*2 files, 394 Go lines*

The packaging format for trees compiled into the binary: bundled skills (`pkg/skills/embed.go`), bundled plugins (`pkg/plugintree`), the built-in payload (`pkg/builtin`) and hermetic archives, produced by `cmd/packtree`.

#### Archive codec and embedded file system

- `tarzst.go` — `Collect`, `Encode` (path order, zero times and owners, single-threaded zstd), `Decode`, `Extract`, `Manifest` and `ParseManifest` (path, sha256, mode per line)
- `fs.go` — `FS`: `fs.FS` over an archive decoded on first use, with file mode 0444 and directory mode 0555 like `embed.FS`

### `pkg/installidentity` — stable anonymous id of this installation

*1 file, 201 Go lines*

Used by `pkg/gateway` for hosted-room authority and group controls.

#### Install id

- `install_identity.go` — `GetInstallID`: reads or mints a 32-hex-digit UUID in `<root home>/install_id` under the cross-process lock `.install_id.lock`, cached per process

### `pkg/gitcred` — git credentials for HTTPS clones and fetches

*4 files, 518 Go lines*

Used by `pkg/plugins/git.go`, `pkg/skills/hub_github.go` and `pkg/provider/git_credentials.go`. It imports the large `pkg/tools` package for one helper (`NoninteractiveGitEnv`), and `pkg/provider` must register the secret reader before GitHub tokens resolve.

#### Credential lookup and retry

For an HTTPS URL the candidates are, in order: `GITHUB_TOKEN` then `GH_TOKEN` from the profile's secret scope (GitHub hosts only), `gh auth token`, then `git credential fill` without prompting. A git network command runs anonymously first and is retried with each credential while the output says a credential is required.

- `gitcred.go` — `IterGitBasicAuth`, `ResolveGitBasicAuth`, `WithGitAuth` (adds an `http.<origin>/.extraheader` through `GIT_CONFIG_*` env), `IsCredentialRequiredError`, `RunGitWithCredentialFallback`
- `hide_{other,windows}.go` — starts helper processes without a console window on Windows
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/testfakes` — test doubles exported for packages outside `pkg/internal`

*3 files, 528 Go lines*

#### Test doubles

- `fakellm.go`, `configplane/plane.go`, `configplane/remoteplane/remoteplane.go` — [test-support] scripted loopback LLM provider aliases and an in-process Remote Config plane with its fixture

### `pkg/testguard` — links the test home guard into test binaries

*1 file, 4 Go lines*

#### Test guard
