## 3. Agent core

### `pkg/agent` — agent core: the `AIAgent` object, the turn loop and its phases, system prompt, context compression, delegation, and the ways an agent is driven

*330 files, 80,728 Go lines*

One flat package of 330 files holding everything between "a user message was admitted" and "a final response was persisted". `AIAgent` is a single struct (several hundred fields plus about 25 embedded per-concern state structs) that mixes configuration, session state and turn state. The turn-loop skeleton and the compression subsystem sit in the first half of the alphabet, the body of every turn phase, the system prompt builder and the transcript flush in the second, purely because of file naming. The agent calls models only through the Python-shaped kwargs path of `pkg/provider` and tools through `pkg/tools`; it persists through the `SessionStore` interface, which is either `pkg/state` directly or, inside a managed worker child, a facade that forwards every write to the owning gateway. It is driven in process inside the gateway by `pkg/gatewayrun`, `pkg/gatewayapi` and `pkg/cron`, as a managed worker child (`__icebath_managed_worker__`), and by the legacy `icebath-agent` direct runner in `pkg/app`; the code in `pkg/tuiserver` that also builds and drives an agent belongs to a session runtime that can no longer execute. Prompt-cache stability shapes the design: the system prompt is built once, stored on the session row and reused verbatim, and all per-turn context rides in the user message. Port scaffolding is heavy but thin: 48 `*_export.go` shims (the `run_*`, `tui_*` and `gateway_*` files are accessors named after Python modules, not run modes), `map[string]any` messages and requests, Python keyword-map constructors, and `internal/py*` coercions in nearly every file.

**Files `acp_*` through `forensics_*`** (143 files, 40,087 Go lines). This part holds the `AIAgent` struct (several hundred unexported fields plus about 25 embedded per-concern state structs) and its constructor ladder, the skeleton of the turn loop (the per-phase bodies are in `turn_*.go` in the other part), the in-package model client layer and fallback chain, the whole context compression subsystem (the `ContextEngine` contract, the built-in `ContextCompressor`, and the attempt/lease/fence/commit orchestration around it), the `delegate_task` subagent runtime, the background memory and skill review fork, `@` context references and `/context` accounting. Callers are `pkg/gatewayrun`, `pkg/tuiserver`, `pkg/app`, `pkg/gatewayapi`, `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/cron` and `cmd/icebath/wiring.go`. It persists through the session store (`state.DB`: transcript rows, system prompt, model config, compression lock, cooldowns, session meta) and writes `sessions/request_dump_*.json`, `logs/subagent-timeout-*.log`, `cache/delegation/` (live transcripts and spilled summaries) and `.codex_gpt55_autoraise_notice` under the icebath home. Port scaffolding is heavy: messages and requests are `map[string]any` dicts, constructor options arrive as Python keyword maps, engine attributes and store methods are addressed by Python name, fifteen `*_export.go` shims re-export unexported members (several have no caller left), and nearly every file uses `internal/py*` for Python truthiness, `str`, `repr`, regex and int coercion. Every stub marker the digest counted here is a false positive (todo lists, stub tool results and placeholders are product terms); the real dead code is a handful of export shims, one regex file and the Windows socket probe.

#### Agent object, options and constructor sequence

`NewAIAgent(ctx, AIAgentOptions)` fills defaults (unlimited max iterations, tool progress mode `all`, checkpoints 20 snapshots / 500 MB total / 10 MB per file) and runs `initAgent`, a fixed ladder: safe-worker clamps, route and API mode, callbacks, control state, logging, prompt-cache policy, client, fallback chain, tools, session state, display config, memory, `agent.*` knobs, compression config, context length, context engine, Ollama `num_ctx`, the 64,000-token minimum-window check, engine tools, usage counters, primary runtime snapshot. Configuration, per-session and per-turn state all live on the one struct; the public surface is plain getters, setters and callback installers. Config keys read here include `agent.api_max_retries` (3), `agent.auto_recovery_cycles` (5), `agent.run_budget_seconds`, `agent.budget_warning_ratio`, `agent.text_verbosity`, `agent.stall_guards`, `agent.environment_probe`, `agent.bot_mode_protocol`, `memory.nudge_interval` (10), `memory.memory_char_limit` (2200), `memory.user_char_limit` (1375), `skills.creation_nudge_interval` (10), `model.streaming`, `model.lmstudio_load_mode`, `tool_loop_guardrails` and `platform_hints`.

- `aiagent.go` — `AIAgent` struct, `AIAgentOptions`, `RunConversationOptions`, `NewAIAgent`; accessors; tool snapshot (definitions, valid names, registry generation, selection key); side-agent tool drops; stream-writer claim tokens
- `agent_init_engine.go` — `initAgent` ordering; selects the plugin engine named by `context.engine` or builds `ContextCompressor`; enforces the 64K minimum window (explicit LM Studio pin exempt); injects engine tool schemas
- `agent_init_params.go` — copies passthrough options, gateway identity (user, chat, thread, session key) and platform callbacks onto the struct
- `agent_init_state.go` — fresh interrupt, steer, redirect and child-list state; activity clock; stream scrubbers; log setup; masked key banner; `prompt_caching.cache_ttl` (`5m`, `1h`, `auto`, or disabled)
- `agent_init_session.go` — tool surface load and startup banner, session id, `sessions/` dir, checkpoint manager, todo store, display and streaming switches, tool-loop guardrails, built-in memory store, external memory manager, `agent.*` knobs
- `agent_init_kwargs.go` — [port-artifact] `AIAgentOptionsFromKwargs` maps Python keyword names to options with TypeError-style refusals; still how `pkg/gatewayrun` builds its agents
- `agent_init_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports `NormalizeRunBudgetSeconds` for the gateway session policy
- `agent_init_memory_provider.go` — loads the configured external memory provider plugin; warns once per home, provider and kind when it is parked, missing, fails to load or reports unavailable

#### Route, API mode and client construction at init

Decides which wire protocol the agent speaks and builds the first client. API modes are `chat_completions`, `codex_responses`, `anthropic_messages`, `bedrock_converse` and `codex_app_server`; an explicit mode wins, otherwise provider name and base-URL host decide. With no explicit key and URL the provider router resolves a client, then the init-time fallback entries are tried, then a "provider not configured" or "credentials exhausted" error is raised.

- `agent_init.go` — `resolveAPIMode` ladder; context-pin route mismatch test; custom-provider `extra_body` merge into request overrides; run-budget, int and flag config parsing; checkpoint-required refusal on Codex app-server
- `agent_init_routing.go` — drops a credential pool for another provider, normalizes the model name (aggregators keep vendor prefixes), upgrades direct OpenAI and GPT-5 routes to Responses, one-time background OpenRouter catalog prewarm
- `agent_init_client.go` — per-mode client build: native Anthropic (OAuth, MiniMax token source), Bedrock binding, MoA facade, or OpenAI-wire from explicit or routed credentials; per-host default header table (OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM, RouterMint, Kimi, Qwen, ChatGPT, xAI)
- `agent_runtime_helpers_client.go` — `createOpenAIClient`: provider-profile and Gemini-native clients, Bedrock Mantle, TLS verify, proxy and base-URL validation, keepalive HTTP client, SDK retries forced to 0, required Codex headers
- `agent_init_fallback.go` — keeps fallback entries naming a provider and model, prints the chain, binds the credential pool entry id, re-detects API mode for an init-time fallback

#### Context window and compression settings at init

Resolves the context window the agent plans against and parses `compression.*`. Defaults: `threshold` 0.50, `target_ratio` 0.20, `protect_first_n` 3, `protect_last_n` 20, `max_attempts` 3 (cap 10), `tail_mode` lean, `min_tail_user_messages` 1, `in_place` true, `enabled` true, `proactive_prune_tokens` 0, `proactive_prune_min_result_chars` 8000, `proactive_prune_min_reclaim_tokens` 4096, `micro_compact` false, `prepare_ahead` false, `checkpoint_required` false, `abort_on_summary_failure` false, `idle_compact_after_seconds` 0, `codex_app_server_auto` native, `codex_responses_native` false, plus `threshold_tokens`, `model_thresholds` and `codex_responses_compact_threshold`.

- `agent_init_compression_config.go` — parses the `compression` section into `CompressionSettings`; Codex GPT-5.x threshold autoraise; invalid-integer warnings to log and stderr
- `agent_init_compression_notice.go` — `CompressionSettings` struct; context-limit startup banner; one-time autoraise notice latched in `<home>/.codex_gpt55_autoraise_notice`
- `agent_init_context_length.go` — `model.context_length` pin scoped to the default route, custom-provider per-model `context_length`, `auxiliary.compression.context_length`, LM Studio loaded length
- `agent_init_ollama.go` — `model.ollama_num_ctx` or the server-detected Ollama `num_ctx`, capped by the pin; clamps the compressor window to it
- `context_pin.go` — "pinned" label when the shown window equals the pin; warns once per model when the pin and the provider-advertised window disagree (the pin wins)

#### Turn loop skeleton and shared turn texts

`runConversationLoop` calls `runConversationTurn`, which builds the turn context, short-circuits plugin-blocked turns and the Codex app-server mode, plays any scripted prelude, then iterates while API calls stay under `max_iterations` and the shared iteration budget remains (plus one grace call). One iteration is: begin, prepare, assemble request, preflight gate, API retry loop (`agent.api_max_retries`), retry restarts, response intake, then a tool round or a text finish; phases return `return`, `break` or `continue` verdicts and a phase panic becomes an outer-loop error (at most 8). The phase bodies themselves are in the other part of this package.

- `conversation_loop_turn.go` — `LoopState` (every turn local), `PhaseVerdict`, iteration driver, API retry loop with interrupt and error handlers, Codex app-server turn with fallback hand-off, failed-turn boundary row carrying redacted error metadata
- `conversation_loop.go` — nudge and notice texts (length continuation, Codex ack, degenerate final, run-budget wrap-up at 80%); system prompt restore-or-build with session-row persistence and pinned tools; mid-turn user redirect checkpoint; billing guidance; turn result builders; failover prompt-cache redecoration; context-engine hooks

#### Turn-ending heuristics

Decide whether a text reply really ends the turn or the model should be nudged to continue, and how often an empty completion is retried.

- `agent_runtime_helpers_ack.go` — detects a short planning or acknowledgement reply (future-tense action, under 1200 chars, no tool results yet) so the turn continues instead of ending
- `agent_runtime_helpers_continuation.go` — degenerate-final and trailing-intent detection; `agent.intent_ack_continuation` mode (`off`, `all`, model-substring list, default `codex_only` on Responses)
- `empty_response_guard.go` — `agent.empty_response_guard`: empty-completion streak with 3 retries (1 once an attempt costs `cost_threshold_usd`), deterministic-empty detection by identical model, provider and finish reason

#### Pre-call transcript sanitizing and tool-call repair

Runs before every model call on the wire copy of the transcript so a malformed history never produces a provider 400, and normalizes what the model sends back.

- `agent_runtime_helpers_sanitize.go` — repairs corrupt tool-call argument JSON, drops invalid roles and thinking-only turns, merges adjacent user rows, fills empty non-final rows, pairs and dedupes tool calls and results, stubs unanswered calls; heal counters with escalation
- `agent_runtime_helpers.go` — tool-call orphan classification and role-alternation repair that keeps the DB flush cursor on the surviving rows
- `agent_runtime_helpers_tool_repair.go` — maps a mismatched tool name to a real one (XML trim, alias, case, separators, CamelCase, tool suffix, fuzzy match at 0.7) and words the invalid-tool result
- `agent_runtime_helpers_think.go` — strips reasoning blocks and tool-call XML from visible text; extracts reasoning from structured fields or inline tags
- `assistant_message.go` — builds the stored assistant row: reasoning text, redacted content, tool-call dicts with call and Responses item ids, replay carriers
- `anthropic_thinking_replay.go` — per-session tracker of thinking blocks the provider rejected; filters them from request copies and carries the fingerprints onto a compression child session

#### Request building and the provider-facing agent surface

`buildAPIKwargs` dispatches on API mode to the Anthropic Messages, Bedrock Converse, Codex Responses or Chat Completions builders of `pkg/provider`. The actual HTTP clients, transports, streaming and retry helpers are in `pkg/provider`; this package owns the client objects, credentials and request state, and `AIAgent` implements `provider.ChatCompletionAgent` through 66 exported methods (46 more serve the Codex runtime) so those helpers can call back into it.

- `chat_completion_kwargs.go` — per-mode request kwargs: reasoning config, OpenRouter provider preferences, prompt-cache scope, native compaction `context_management`, fixed temperatures, one-shot max-output cap, xAI tool-search alias
- `chat_completion_agent.go` — [port-artifact] `provider.ChatCompletionAgent` implementation: retry session, request abort hook, Codex stream state, reasoning rejection flags, Ollama thinking probe cache (60 s), wrappers over sanitizers and client slots
- `chat_completion_helpers.go` — rate-limit header capture, stale-timeout cap at half the remaining run budget, high-effort Codex silence floor
- `chat_completion_local.go` — lets one attempt past the stale-stream breaker once a local llama-server answers its health check again
- `api_request_hooks.go` — sanitized request and response payloads for the `post_api_request` and `api_request_error` plugin hooks; API error one-liner; estimator calibration from real usage
- `agent_runtime_helpers_debug.go` — writes a force-redacted `sessions/request_dump_<session>_<timestamp>.json` on non-retryable or retry-exhausted API errors, and per request under `ICEBATH_DUMP_REQUESTS`; `ICEBATH_DUMP_REQUEST_STDOUT` echo; pool socket enumeration
- `fast_mode_agent.go` — per-session fast window (service-tier override for `agent.fast_auto_seconds`, default 60), Daybreak opt-in, fast-unavailable latch, provider-hook failure set

#### Client lifecycle, credential refresh and transport recovery

The agent keeps one shared primary OpenAI-wire client and/or one Anthropic client, plus per-request client slots: a warm cached client is checked out per call, and another goroutine aborts it by shutting its sockets and poisoning the slot. Recovery paths refresh rotating credentials and rebuild clients after auth failures, dead sockets and transient transport errors.

- `client_lifecycle.go` — shared client create, replace and retire under a reentrant lock; request-slot checkout, store, release and abort for both client kinds; RouterMint and Qwen Portal identity headers; socket drain after an abandoned worker
- `client_lifecycle_anthropic.go` — direct Anthropic client with the route timeout; OAuth flag only on native Anthropic; refreshes a rotated token and moves the context engine key off the revoked one
- `client_lifecycle_oauth_refresh.go` — adopts a re-minted Codex or xAI OAuth token (refusing an account change) and re-mints the Vertex token
- `client_lifecycle_provider_refresh.go` — re-mints the credential through a provider profile refresh hook and rebuilds the shared client
- `client_lifecycle_refresh.go` — recomputes TLS material and default headers after the base URL moves (AI Gateway attribution, host table, profile, user and custom-provider extras)
- `client_lifecycle_swap.go` — adopts a credential pool entry as the live key and base URL, refusing an entry whose route cannot serve the model
- `client_lifecycle_fallback_swap.go` — installs a fallback route's client in place with that route's request timeout
- `credential_pool_recovery.go` — pool rotation on billing (402), rate limit (retry the same key once, then rotate), model entitlement and auth errors; aggregator upstream 429s defer to the fallback chain
- `agent_runtime_primary_transport.go` — rebuilds the primary client from the recorded primary runtime once after a transient transport error, waits 3 to 8 s; never for OpenRouter or while on a fallback
- `agent_runtime_helpers_dead_connections.go` — turn-start sweep that rebuilds the primary client or retires the cached request client when pooled sockets are half closed
- `agent_runtime_helpers_dead_connections_unix.go` — socket probe with `MSG_PEEK|MSG_DONTWAIT`: EOF or an OS error is dead, EAGAIN healthy
- `agent_runtime_helpers_dead_connections_windows.go` — [stub] probe only returns an error (mirrors Python lacking `MSG_DONTWAIT`), so the sweep never fires on Windows

#### Model fallback chain

Switches the live agent to the next configured backup model when the primary is rate limited, out of credit, unentitled or returning incomplete responses, and decides when it may return.

- `fallback_activation.go` — walks the ordered chain skipping unavailable, unentitled, pool-exhausted and same-backend entries; primary cooldown (provider reset time or 60 s doubling to 4 h); `fallback.min_switch_reset_seconds` stay-put; rewrites Model and Provider lines of the cached prompt

#### Codex app-server runtime binding

Lets the Codex app-server runtime in `pkg/provider` drive a turn against agent state when the API mode is `codex_app_server`.

- `codex_runtime_agent.go` — [port-artifact] accessor surface that runtime reads and writes: Codex session handle and prompt, usage counters, callbacks, compaction status and provider-native compaction events
- `codex_session_db.go` — adapts the session store to `provider.CodexSessionDB` (model config values, token-count deltas)

#### Context engine contract and plugin-hosted engines

A context engine decides when and how the conversation is compacted, may select per-request context, tracks usage and may expose tools. The built-in engine is `ContextCompressor`; `context.engine` can name a plugin engine instead.

- `context_engine.go` — `ContextEngine` interface, `ContextEngineBase` defaults (75% threshold, protect 3 first and 6 last), memory-context sanitizer (redacted, 6000-char cap with middle elision)
- `context_engine_hosted.go` — engine whose object lives in the plugin host: every method is a host call, base counters mirrored both ways, optional keywords passed only when its signature accepts them

#### Built-in compressor: state, thresholds and gate

The trigger is the input window (window minus the output reservation) times the threshold percent, where the percent is the config value, raised to at least 0.75 for windows under 512K, or a `compression.model_thresholds` override (longest matching key, provider-scoped keys outrank bare ones); it is floored at 64K, capped at 85% of the window, by `compression.threshold_tokens` and by the summariser's own window. Automatic compaction is blocked by a summary-failure cooldown (600 s with no summary provider; a 60, 300, 900 s ladder for timeouts and truncations; 30 s for empty, non-JSON or dropped-stream replies; 60 s otherwise), a 300 s structural no-op backoff, and an anti-thrash breaker that trips after two provider-confirmed ineffective compactions and allows one probe per 300 s. Cooldown, streaks and breaker counts persist per session in the session store; the streaks and breaker count carry over to a compression child session.

- `context_compressor.go` — `ContextCompressor` struct and options, per-session reset, usage update, exported engine methods and accessors
- `context_compressor_state.go` — durable per-session guards read and written by Python method name; trigger, tail budget and summary budget derivation; model update; summary-model benching after two fallback summaries
- `context_compressor_gate.go` — should-compress verdict with block reasons, real-versus-rough token pairing after a compaction, tail budget walk, tool-result dedupe and demotion, pressure demotion of an oversized protected tail
- `context_compressor_prune.go` — proactive tool-result-only prune above `compression.proactive_prune_tokens`, committed to the store in place with a rearm watermark and a minimum reclaim
- `context_compressor_telemetry.go` — content-free per-attempt telemetry record (regions, aux call, method, effect) and rough token estimators over dict rows

#### Built-in compressor: window selection, tail protection and assembly

One pass prunes old tool results (MD5 dedupe, bodies over 200 chars replaced by a one-line summary, all but the newest 3 tool images stripped), protects the head (system prompt plus `protect_first_n` rows, decaying to zero once the session was compressed) and a token-budgeted tail (lean mode: 2.5% of the window within 10K to 25K tokens, never over 20% of the window), and summarizes the middle. The tail cut never splits a tool-call group and always keeps the newest user message and newest assistant reply unless that region alone exceeds the soft ceiling. The result is head, summary handoff and tail with tool pairs repaired, an unfinished user task restated, historical media stripped and stale reasoning replay pruned.

- `context_compressor_compress.go` — the compress pass: structural no-op results, tail cut with anchors, rescan of earlier handoffs, summary placement that keeps role alternation, in-flight task replay
- `context_compressor_window.go` — middle-window planning and adoption of a summary prepared in the background ahead of time
- `context_compressor_tail.go` — lean tail budget; demotes tail tool results older than six rounds to one-line recovery hints pointing at `session_search`; skill safety rule appended to summaries
- `context_compressor_handoff.go` — summary prefix and end-marker normalization, user-attribution validation, blank echo removal, tool call and result pair sanitizing
- `context_compressor_turn_views.go` — tells human-authored user turns from compaction scaffolding; rewind-prefix helper used by `/retry` and the gateway session store
- `context_compressor_helpers.go` — constants and shared helpers: refusal detection, summary failure classification, anchor index, verbatim user section, pruned-skill markers, image stripping and eviction, row budget pricing, grown-transcript salvage
- `context_compressor_leaf.go` — dependency-free primitives: skill-pruned marker, summary-line test, model threshold key ranking, pinned and deterministic summary routes, terminal summary failure table

#### Built-in compressor: summary generation

One auxiliary LLM call turns the middle window into a structured handoff (historical task snapshot, goal, constraints, completed actions, active state, blockers, decisions, errors and fixes, relevant files, critical context, pruned skills; lean mode adds a session log, verbatim user messages and an anchor index). A previous summary makes it an iterative update; a focus topic biases the budget. On failure it retries once on the main model, then either aborts with the transcript unchanged or inserts a deterministic fallback summary.

- `context_compressor_summarize.go` — summary budget, redacted turn serialization bounded to 160K chars, prompt template, the aux call with empty, refusal and truncation checks, main-model fallback, static fallback summary
- `context_compressor_summary.go` — pins the summary route onto the call and dispatches the window, rolling back handoff self-heal on cancellation
- `context_compressor_summarizers.go` — one-line per-tool summaries used when a tool result is pruned (terminal, file, patch, browser, delegate, skills, cron, process and others); memory-provider prompt section

#### Compression orchestration: attempt, lease, fence and commit

`AIAgent.compressContext` runs one attempt: claim the compressor and snapshot its state; route Codex app-server sessions to their own compaction; check the automatic gate and summariser feasibility; take the durable per-session compression lock (TTL 300 s, refreshed, with a message watermark) or sit out when another path holds it; adopt a parent that was already rotated; gather the pre-compress memory checkpoint; run the engine; reject no-progress or would-grow candidates after one salvage pass; enter the commit fence (a hard interrupt before it cancels cleanly, after it waits); then commit in place (archive and compact, the default) or by rotating to a child session. A failed commit rolls back to the snapshot and arms a 60 s cooldown.

- `compression_facade.go` — `AIAgent.compressContext` entry: commit fence stack, choice of timed or direct run, mirroring the result onto live lists, session context rebind
- `conversation_compression_commit.go` — the attempt body, summary phase, candidate rejection, in-place or rotated commit with rollback, post-commit boundary bookkeeping
- `conversation_compression_dispatch.go` — binds engine compress to the keywords it accepts, repairs rows, folds the todo snapshot, rebuilds the prompt, carries goal, loop, heartbeat, title and rejected-thinking state to the child session
- `conversation_compression_lease.go` — durable lock lease with refresher, activity heartbeat that republishes the compacting status, status lifecycle edge, rotated-parent adoption, pre-compress memory checkpoint
- `conversation_compression_fence.go` — `CompressionCommitFence` (cancel-before-commit against commit-in-flight, shared deadline, progress clock), compressor snapshot and restore, routine status wording for the gateway noise filter
- `conversation_compression_attempt.go` — per-compressor attempt generations so a superseded or detached attempt cannot mutate compressor state
- `conversation_compression_guards.go` — gate evaluation with durable refresh, message snapshot restore, per-goroutine timeout outcome, transient-block and lock-skip signals
- `conversation_compression_watermark.go` — archive watermark capped at the newest held row so concurrent appends are not archived
- `conversation_compression.go` — message text extraction and the real-user-message test that excludes synthetic scaffolding rows

#### Compression timeouts and stall retry

Bounds how long a compaction may run and what happens when the summary model stalls.

- `conversation_compression_timeout.go` — runs the attempt on a 4-worker process-wide pool under an idle budget and total ceiling; cancels before commit, waits out an admitted commit, retries a stall once on `auxiliary.compression.fallback_chain`, then with the deterministic summary
- `conversation_compression_deadline.go` — `compression.context_timeout_seconds` (2 min idle) and `compression.context_total_ceiling_seconds` (10 min), floored at the aux timeout; deadline extended while the server reads the prompt

#### Post-compaction transcript integrity and session recovery

Guarantees the compacted transcript still drives a sensible next model call and that a stale agent finds the session a compaction moved to.

- `conversation_compression_anchor.go` — keeps a real user turn in the compacted transcript (merging busy-steer text, todo snapshot and pruned-skill reload notice), stamps persisted twins, sets the flush baseline
- `conversation_compression_reply_anchor.go` — reinserts the newest visible assistant reply when an engine folded it away
- `conversation_compression_boundary.go` — resets read and skill-view dedup caches at a boundary; keeps a gateway-seeded system prompt; warns once on a summary or aux-model fallback
- `conversation_compression_recovery.go` — moves a stale live agent onto the compression child session, reopens an orphaned parent, defers and finalizes the engine's compression-complete notification

#### Compression preconditions and alternative routes

Checks made before the built-in path may run, and the route used when Codex owns the thread.

- `conversation_compression_feasibility.go` — checks the summariser's window: lowers the trigger to it with a notice, refuses one under 64K, reprobes after a model switch
- `conversation_compression_checkpoint.go` — `compression.checkpoint_required` fail-closed gate: needs a memory provider implementing the pre-compress checkpoint API; startup warning when none does
- `conversation_compression_codex.go` — Codex app-server route: asks the Codex thread to compact itself (mode `icebath` or forced), local transcript unchanged, shared failure cooldown

#### Image-too-large request recovery

Misnamed as compression: an API-error recovery step called from the turn recovery code.

- `conversation_compression_image_shrink.go` — re-encodes inline image parts over 4 MB or over the model's max dimension; refuses the retry when an oversized image cannot be shrunk

#### Manual /compress and compaction reporting exports

The `/compress` slash command path used by the gateway and TUI.

- `conversation_compression_manual.go` — `/compress` argument parsing (preview, aggressive, keep-last N, focus topic), `CompressNow` on a copy of history, request token estimates, result rendering
- `compression_count_export.go` — [port-artifact] compaction count read and seed, last billed prompt tokens, for the gateway
- `compression_notification_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the deferred compression-notification finalizer

#### Compaction event schema and attempt telemetry

Every compaction exit path produces one content-free record that plugins and the relay can observe.

- `compaction_events.go` — `icebath.compaction` v1 record with closed value sets (kind, trigger, method, outcome, failure class); fires the `post_compaction` plugin hook and relay mark for attempts, micro-compaction, prunes and provider-native compaction
- `conversation_compression_telemetry.go` — builds, logs and publishes one attempt record per exit (committed, aborted, bypassed, blocked)

#### Context accounting for the /context command

Estimates where the context window is going. The system prompt builder itself is in the other part; these files only measure and list.

- `context_breakdown.go` — token estimate per category (system prompt, tool definitions, rules, skills, MCP, subagent definitions, memory, conversation), per-skill and per-toolset costs, 20 by 5 glyph grid and tables
- `context_file_sources.go` — manifest of context files considered (project files in priority order, profile `SOUL.md` last) with status loaded, truncated, shadowed, suppressed, flagged, blocked, empty or unreadable

#### @ context references

Expands `@diff`, `@staged`, `@file:path[:start-end]`, `@folder:path`, `@git:N`, `@url:...` and plugin-registered `@prefix:value` references in a user message into an attached-context block. Limits: 16 references per message, a warning at 25% and refusal at 50% of the context window. Paths must resolve inside the allowed root or the composer-paste and gateway staging directories and pass the credential deny list.

- `context_references.go` — parser, concurrent expanders (bounded line-window file read, binary detection, folder listing through `rg --files`, hardened git, `web_extract` fetch), path security checks, plugin provider registry
- `context_references_gateway_export.go` — gateway-shaped wrapper assigned to `gateway.ExpandContextReferences` in `cmd/icebath/wiring.go`
- `context_references_quiet_{other,windows}.go` — hides the console window of git and rg children on Windows; a no-op elsewhere (2 per-OS files)

#### delegate_task: entry, routing and child construction

The `delegate_task` tool handler, with actions `spawn` (default), `list`, `steer` and `stop`. Spawning is limited by `delegation.max_spawn_depth`, the concurrent-children cap, a global spawn pause and `delegation.oneshot_max_children`; a child's iteration cap always comes from `delegation.max_iterations` (default 250). A child is a fresh `AIAgent` with platform `subagent`, quiet mode, an ephemeral system prompt (task context, workspace path and that workspace's context files, completion instructions), SOUL identity only on a profile route, no memory provider unless `compression.checkpoint_required` is on, its own session row linked by `parent_session_id`, toolsets never wider than the parent's and without `delegate_task`, `clarify`, `memory`, `send_message` and `cronjob_manage` (an orchestrator-role child keeps `delegate_task`), and a route inherited from the parent or overridden by `delegation.*` config, a profile route or a delegation provider plugin.

- `delegate_tool.go` — handler and registration into `tools.DelegateTask`, role normalization (leaf or orchestrator), child cache-TTL and compression-cap rules, batch build
- `delegate_tool_routes.go` — per-task route through the session's delegation backend; profile routes run inside that profile's home and secrets; `delegation.fallback_providers`; effort validation
- `delegate_tool_credentials.go` — child runtime resolution (direct endpoint, runtime provider or inherit parent), credential pool sharing, request-override merge, reasoning effort precedence
- `delegate_tool_toolsets.go` — child toolset computation, blocked-tool toolsets per role, MCP toolset inheritance
- `delegate_tool_child.go` — `buildChildAgent` (id `sa-<index>-<hex8>`, weak parent link, dedicated session DB handle, `subagent_start` hook) and the single-child runner entry
- `delegate_hooks.go` — wires delegate service-tier gates to the provider fast-mode resolvers; request-override accessors
- `delegation_agent.go` — per-session frozen inline-delegation decision and pinned delegation backend; turn-start tool rebuild after a backend switch
- `delegation_registry_wiring.go` — delegation provider registry hooks: plugin-hosted providers and compiled-in `delegation/<name>` strategy plugins

#### delegate_task: running children, progress and results

Children run in parallel on worker goroutines. A 30 s heartbeat touches the parent's activity clock and declares a child stale after 15 idle or 40 in-tool cycles; the child timeout bounds inactivity, not runtime, and a child that times out before its first API call leaves `logs/subagent-timeout-*.log`. Each child may get its own git worktree, a leased pool credential and output-schema validation with one retry turn; summaries are trimmed to the parent's remaining context headroom (static ceiling 24,000 chars) with the full text spilled under `cache/delegation`, costs roll up into the parent, and `subagent_stop` hooks and memory providers are notified. With `background: true` units go to an async pool and the result arrives later as a session wake.

- `delegate_tool_child_run.go` — one child's run: registry entry, worktree, credential lease, liveness wait, timeout diagnostic, late-steer merge, schema validation, result entry with tool trace, tokens and cost, background-process accounting, cleanup
- `delegate_tool_dispatch.go` — parallel batch execution with parent-interrupt polling, aggregation, synchronous fallback notes, background unit dispatch and wake-session resolution
- `delegate_tool_results.go` — tool-output tail, sanitized tool history for hooks, summary budget and disk spill, memory notification, `subagent_stop` hooks, cost roll-up
- `delegate_tool_progress.go` — child system prompt text, child-to-parent progress relay (tree lines, batch tags), plain-language failure descriptions
- `delegation_live_log.go` — append-only credential-redacted live transcript per task under `<home>/cache/delegation/live/deleg_<id>/` with a manifest; directories pruned after 7 days unless a stored session references them

#### Subagent registry and control

Process-wide table of live subagents that steer, stop, list and attribution lookups go through.

- `delegate_tool_registry.go` — live subagent records, global spawn pause, interrupt and steer by id with session-lineage ownership checks, list payload, background-process handoff to the parent
- `delegate_registry_tui_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] owned and visible subagent record copies and live transcript path, meant for a TUI agents view; nothing calls them

#### Background memory and skill review fork

After a turn (nudge intervals) or on an explicit refine request, the agent forks a cache-parity copy of itself (same model, prompt and tool surface so the provider prompt cache hits, or a route from `auxiliary.background_review` with a 24-row history digest) and runs one review prompt over the conversation snapshot. The fork gets 16 iterations, a tool whitelist (skills toolset, optionally memory, `read_file`, `search_files`, configured `extra_tools`), auto-denied dangerous commands and an input budget of 75% of its window capped at 600K tokens; a new live turn cancels it. Reviews are off for safe workers and finite turns.

- `background_review.go` — run handshake and cancellation, `auxiliary.background_review` settings, routed runtime resolution with fallback warning, input budget, history digest
- `background_review_fork.go` — builds and releases the cache-parity fork (also used by side questions), isolates its env, records fork usage against the parent session
- `background_review_thread.go` — review worker: whitelist, fork conversation, summary publication, prompt choice by memory and skills scope
- `background_review_prompts.go` — the memory, skill and combined review prompt texts
- `background_review_summary.go` — turns the fork's tool calls into user-visible action lines and memory-write metadata
- `background_review_run_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported `RequestDone` and `CancelForLiveTurn` on the run handle for the gateway
- `curator_review.go` — installs `memory.CuratorHooks.RunReview`: runs the skill curator's prompt on a fresh silent agent and returns its transcript

#### Bot Mode agent-to-agent messaging

Lets an agent in a Bot Mode install message a teammate profile or an agent on a peer gateway.

- `bot_mode_dm.go` — `message_agent` tool schema, injected only into a Bot Chat session of a Bot Mode managed install with `agent.bot_mode_protocol` on
- `bot_mode_dm_send.go` — resolves a teammate or `<peer>/<agent>` target, writes a DM file, launches `icebath -p <profile>` or `peer dm` as a background terminal process; fire-and-forget ack with a delivery id; 16,000-char limit
- `bot_screen.go` — build-tagged init (absent from core and no-extras builds) wiring bot desktop env and lease reads into the prompt builder's Bot Screen line

#### Activity tracking

The busy and liveness signal that watchdogs, the gateway and parent agents read.

- `activity_tracking.go` — activity clock (time, description, provenance) under a lock, kanban bridge when `ICEBATH_KANBAN_TASK` is set, session-row heartbeat at most every 60 s, activity summary
- `activity_tracking_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] `SetLastActivityTS` setter of the activity timestamp; no non-test caller

#### Session control state and launch flags

Goal, loop and heartbeat state as the clients see it, plus one-turn launch flags.

- `agent_cli_flags.go` — one-turn model pick state, reasoning-level pin to the session row, finite flag, and the control revision that triggers a `session.control.update` push when a tool changes goal or loop
- `control_snapshot_export.go` — `ControlSnapshot`: goal, loop and heartbeat cards from session meta with a revision and newest timestamp, for the gateway
- `automation_managers.go` — `LoopAutomation` and `HeartbeatAutomation` interfaces over the loop and heartbeat managers, answered in process or by the gateway

#### Model switch, session boundary and adapter export shims

Exported entry points other packages use to mutate a live agent; a large share is dead.

- `cli_model_switch_export.go` — in-place `SwitchModel` (once and restore), reasoning config setter, primary snapshot restore, preflight-compression warning after a switch; `RestoreReasoning`, `CustomProviderEntries`, `SyncToSession` have no non-test caller
- `cli_new_session_export.go` — [port-artifact] in-process new-session and rewind helpers; only `NotifyMemoryRewound`, `MemoryStore` and `SpawnExplicitBackgroundReview` still have non-test callers
- `acp_adapter_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] setters meant for the ACP adapter (thinking callback, delegation backend, session reset, compression flag, detached session store); no non-test caller
- `api_server_export.go` — [port-artifact] session token counters and `AdoptUnansweredTurn` for the gateway API and turn runner
- `busy_steer_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] `SetExecutingToolsForTests` setter of the executing-tools flag; no non-test caller

#### Error surface descriptors

Turns a failed turn into the structured card a client renders.

- `error_surface.go` — descriptor from a failed turn result: layer (provider, endpoint, streaming, auth, billing, gateway, disk), code, retryable, provider label, auth kind and API key env var
- `error_surface_exception.go` — the same for an error that escaped the turn, classified by Python-style exception class and module names and HTTP status
- `error_surface_export.go`, `error_surface_exception_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers used by `pkg/tuiserver`

#### Terminal status display

Classic-terminal feedback while a request or tool runs.

- `display_spinner.go` — braille status spinner with elapsed time, skin faces, wings and thinking verbs, single-line mode off a TTY, `ICEBATH_SPINNER_PAUSE`
- `display_cute.go` — forwards tool completion lines to the tools display layer

#### Trajectory export

Training-data export of a finished conversation.

- `agent_runtime_helpers_trajectory.go` — converts a transcript to ShareGPT-style turns (`system`, `human`, `gpt`, `tool`) with `<think>`, `<tool_call>` and `<tool_response>` blocks, for trajectory saving

#### Cross-package wiring singletons

Small files that exist to connect this package to another one.

- `cron_link.go` — build-tagged init (absent from core and no-extras builds) giving `pkg/cron` an agent factory, hard interrupt, turn explanation, client cleanup and worktree recorder
- `finite_turn_scope.go` — binds the gateway admission's finite and unattended flags onto the tool env for one turn
- `forensics_logcalls.go` — [unwired] four regexes parsing the per-call `API call #N` log line (model, tokens, latency, cache, request id, upstream); no non-test reference, no parser or command around them

**Files `gateway_*` through `worker_*`** (187 files, 40,641 Go lines). This part holds the body of a turn (admission under a durable session lease, the once-per-turn prologue, every per-iteration phase, API error recovery, the tool round, stop gates and finalization), the system prompt builder, the transcript flush into the session store, and the ways an agent is driven: in process inside the gateway by `pkg/gatewayrun`, `pkg/gatewayapi` and `pkg/cron`, as a managed worker child process re-executed from `cmd/icebath/startup.go`, and by the legacy `icebath-agent` direct runner in `pkg/app`. `pkg/tuiserver` also holds code that builds and drives an agent, but that session runtime can no longer execute (see the `pkg/tuiserver` section). It also owns the `/loop` and heartbeat automations, mixture-of-agents, `/btw` side questions, session titles, verify-on-stop, voice and vision handling, model switching, trajectory files, and the plugin host services installed by `cmd/icebath/wiring.go`. It persists through the `SessionStore` interface (the canonical `state.SessionDB`, or a worker facade that forwards to the owning gateway), session meta rows `loop:<session>` and `heartbeat:<session>`, `<home>/verification_evidence.db`, `<home>/moa-traces/`, `<home>/worker-outboxes/<execution>/`, and `trajectory_samples.jsonl` / `failed_trajectories.jsonl` in the working directory. Port scaffolding is wide but thin: 33 `*_export.go` shims (the `run_*`, `tui_*` and `gateway_*` files are accessors named after Python modules, not run modes), results and requests as `map[string]any`, Python exception names on errors, `internal/py*` coercions in nearly every file, and `wire_key_order.go`, which only emulates dict insertion order; `native_responses_preflight.go`, `placeholders.go` and `surface_switch.go` are product behaviour despite their names. Every stub marker the digest counted is a false positive (todo list, placeholder row and stub result are product terms); the real dead code is the scripted prelude, a registered `commit_message` template, the `StatusBarUsage` snapshot and about a dozen exported accessors.

#### Turn admission, durable session lease and liveness watchdog

One turn is one user message driven to a final response; `RunConversation`, `RunConversationContent` and `Chat` are the only entries, and the result is a dict (`final_response`, `messages`, `api_calls`, `completed`, `failed`, `interrupted`, `turn_exit_reason`, token and cost totals). Admission moves the credential pool onto the session's login choices, cancels a running background review, takes the per-session turn lease in the session store (TTL 300 s, renewed by a timer, up to 1800 s waiting on another process with status lines, transcript reloaded after contention), opens the Relay conversation and turn scopes of `pkg/tools`, then runs the loop and reports `success`, `failed`, `cancelled` or `timed_out`.

- `turn_facade.go` — admission bracket: task and Relay turn ids, lease, Relay scopes, accounting and cache-affinity context, loop call, outcome mapping, guaranteed lease release
- `turn_facade_lease.go` — lease holder `pid=…:turn=…:platform=…`, refresh inside an authority deadline, hard interrupt on a lost lease, early results (stop notice or retryable `session_busy`)
- `turn_liveness.go` — `agent.turn_liveness.timeout_s` (600) and `poll_s` (15): samples the activity clock, warns, dumps goroutine stacks (40 max), force-aborts a silently stalled turn
- `relay_cwd.go` — logical session and turn working directories reported on Relay scopes, remote backend paths kept as declared

#### Turn prologue: per-turn setup before the first model call

`buildTurnContext` runs once per turn, in order: adopt a session rotated by compression, restore the primary runtime after a fallback, refresh MCP tools, bind task and turn ids, reset retry counters, guardrails and the iteration budget, sweep dead connections, stage the user row, hydrate the todo store and usage anchor from history, tick the memory nudge, refresh or restore-or-build the system prompt, ensure the session row, run `pre_llm_call` plugin hooks, run idle and preflight compaction, merge turn notes, bind the interrupt scope, start memory providers and prefetch, fire the turn-start auto title, and persist the user row. Per-turn context (fenced memory prefetch, plugin context, gateway notes, plugin notices, surface-switch and skills-index notes) is appended to the user message and stored as its `api_content` sidecar, never added to the system prompt. A plugin `block` verdict ends the turn with the plugin's message and stores withheld stand-in text instead of the typed prompt.

- `turn_context.go` — the prologue and its helpers; `buildAPIMessages` (wire copy per call: sidecar substitution, reasoning replay, placeholder fill, strict tool-call fields, ephemeral system prompt); `TurnContext`
- `turn_context_compaction.go` — idle compaction (`compression.idle_compact_after_seconds`), preflight passes bounded by `compression.max_attempts`, fail-closed on timeout or no progress, managed-local window growth, overflow warning re-arm
- `turn_scripted_prelude.go` — [unwired] plays scripted assistant tool-call steps through the tool round before the model is called; no non-test caller sets `RunConversationOptions.Prelude`
- `reactions.go` — regex for thanks, affection and heart emoji in the typed message; fires the reaction callback with kind `vibe`
- `session_client_env_hooks.go` — copies the client environment bound on the turn context onto the agent tool env its tool calls read
- `subagent_lifecycle.go` — binds the agent as the weakly held parent of the turn for plugin subagent launches
- `logging_session.go` — tags log records of the turn goroutine with the session id

#### Iteration start, transcript preparation and request assembly

Each iteration first applies a pending redirect, checks interrupt, review input budget and iteration budget (one grace call allowed), then repairs the transcript, builds the wire copy and measures request pressure before a preflight gate decides whether to compress. Assembly order is fixed: wire copies, inline MoA context, prefill messages, context-engine selection, rejected-thinking suppression, sanitizer, stale tool-image eviction, thinking-only drop and user merge, tool-call canonicalization, prompt cache plan last, MoA request preparation, token estimate.

- `turn_iteration_prep.go` — `beginIteration`, `prepareIteration` (step callback, steer drain after the newest tool row, run-budget and iteration-budget notices, argument repair, alternation repair), spinner announce, restart flags
- `turn_request_assembly.go` — `assembleAPIRequest` in the order above; cache plan inputs are TTL, native Anthropic layout, the stable prompt tier as static prefix and tool markers (skipped for MoA); pressure anchored on real usage
- `turn_api_request.go` — per-attempt payload: cache redecoration after failover, image strip for rejecting models, kwargs build, Responses preflight, LLM request middleware, `pre_api_request` hook, `ICEBATH_DUMP_REQUESTS`
- `turn_preflight_gate.go` — Ollama context floor refusal, overflow recheck arming, insufficient-progress blocker, then preflight compression
- `turn_preflight.go` — pre-call compression pass with call refunds; post-tool compression on real prompt pressure, else blocked warning and tool-result prune
- `iteration_budget.go` — thread-safe iteration counter with refunds (rounds of only `execute_code` are refunded); `agent.budget_warning_ratio` normalizer
- `turn_retry_state.go` — one-shot recovery guards and the four restart signals (compressed, rebuilt, redirected, length continuation) of one API attempt
- `native_responses_preflight.go` — token estimate of the Responses payload as replayed from a persisted native compaction checkpoint
- `placeholders.go` — interrupt placeholder text substituted into empty non-final assistant rows, its legacy spelling, and the hidden placeholder row
- `wire_key_order.go` — [port-artifact] tracks Python dict insertion order of each wire message through the builder steps so the encoded request keeps byte-stable key order

#### Model call, stream delivery, response check and intake

The request goes through the plugin LLM execution middleware and is streamed whenever possible (off when streaming was disabled for the session, for ACP transports, for provider profiles and external-process providers that do not stream, and for MoA or mock clients with no stream consumer). The response is shape-checked, given a finish reason per API mode, routed to refusal or truncation handling, folded into usage, then normalized into an assistant message.

- `turn_api_call.go` — `performAPICall` inside the model-request bracket a redirect can cross; `handleAPIInterrupt` keeps the streamed partial or a waiting notice
- `stream_delivery.go` — scrubbed text and reasoning deltas to display and TTS callbacks and `on_stream_delta` hooks, superseded-writer fencing, interim messages (deduped, `on_interim_message` hook), held-turn row hiding
- `turn_response_check.go` — invalid-response retry (backoff 5 s to 120 s, pool rotation, eager fallback), finish-reason derivation, refusal and truncation routing, Relay completion
- `turn_response_intake.go` — content coercion, `post_api_request` hook, reasoning preview relay, incomplete `REASONING_SCRATCHPAD` retry (2), Codex `incomplete` continuation
- `provider_projection.go` — appends transcript rows a provider-run tool loop projected and ticks the skill nudge counter by its iterations
- `header_capture.go` — rate-limit state captured from Anthropic Messages response headers
- `served_model.go` — records the proxy-reported served model header of each 2xx response; `requested_model` and `served_model` result fields

#### Usage accounting and usage reads

Every response's usage is normalized, priced, added to session counters, queued to the session row as a token delta, fed to the context engine and the usage anchor, and logged as one `API call #N` line.

- `turn_usage.go` — `recordResponseUsage`: MoA advisor usage fold-in, estimator calibration, anchor capture, rolling latency and output histories, cache hit percentage in the log line
- `usage_anchor.go` — usage anchor (real prompt tokens tied to a transcript prefix) mirrored to the session row and restored on resume
- `usage_stats_export.go` — frozen session usage dict, context occupancy figures, last rate-limit buckets and viewer-turn output base, for the gateway and TUI server
- `status_bar_usage.go` — `ContextDisplaySource` (local estimate versus provider reading) is used by `pkg/gatewayrun`; the `StatusBarUsage` snapshot and `TodoItems` have no caller

#### API error recovery

`handleAPIError` runs a fixed ladder: pre-classification repairs, classification by `pkg/provider`, the `api_request_error` hook, one-shot post-classification repairs, interrupt check, routed recoveries, overflow recovery, then settlement into terminal client error, fallback, an auto-recovery wait, or jittered backoff (2 s to 60 s, `Retry-After` honoured, 200 ms interruptible slices). Retries are bounded by `agent.api_max_retries`; after exhaustion comes one primary transport rebuild, the fallback chain, then `agent.auto_recovery_cycles` waits of 15, 30, 60 s for transient transport errors when no answer text has streamed.

- `turn_api_error.go` — the ladder driver and `settleUnrecoveredError`; stale-credential refresh through a provider profile; shutdown abandonment
- `turn_recovery_before.go` — surrogate strip and ASCII-only fallback for encode errors, fast-mode unprovisioned 429, image-content rejection strip
- `turn_recovery_after.go` — 401 credential refresh per provider, thinking-signature, stale Codex reasoning, native-compaction and llama.cpp grammar repairs, affordable 402 output clamp, image shrink
- `turn_recovery_route.go` — overflow with compaction disabled, long-context-tier cap, eager fallback on rate limit, transport and auth failures
- `turn_overflow.go` — payload-too-large and context-length recovery: adopt the provider-reported window, clamp the output cap, compress scored by bytes or tokens, fail as `context_overflow`
- `turn_recovery.go` — shared helpers: interrupt abort, backoff sleep, response shape validation, Codex soft-failure classification, image strip, Codex app-server fallback
- `turn_recovery_attempt.go` — attempt logging with buffered retry trace, missing vendor-prefix hint, backoff choice, fast-fail when a rate limit outlasts the retries
- `turn_recovery_autorecover.go` — the auto-recovery ladder and its countdown notice
- `turn_recovery_results.go` — terminal failed-turn results with delivered partial text, limit-reset time, auth and billing guidance
- `turn_recovery_codex.go` — re-enables Codex reasoning replay when the route changes
- `turn_loop_errors.go` — errors escaping response processing: classify, fill unanswered tool results, end the turn once deterministic
- `thinking_timeout_guidance.go` — detects a reasoning model timing out before its first token and words the `/reasoning low` and `stale_timeout_seconds` advice

#### Truncated, empty and refused responses

Handles the three ways a 200 response is not an answer.

- `turn_truncation.go` — `finish_reason=length`: up to four text continuations stitched together, four boosted-cap reruns of a cut tool call, three Codex continuations, repetition and thinking-exhausted aborts; safety refusals get one fallback try
- `turn_empty_response.go` — empty final: recover the streamed partial, reuse a housekeeping reply, one post-tool nudge, two thinking prefills, budgeted retries, fallback, then `empty_response_exhausted`

#### Tool round and tool executor binding

A tool round validates and repairs tool names, splits batches, caps `delegate_task` calls at the concurrent-children limit, dedupes identical calls, persists the assistant tool-call row before any side effect, executes sequentially, concurrently or in planned segments through `tools.Executor`, then checks guardrail halts and post-tool compression. The agent implements the executor's host interface, and plugin hooks reach every tool call through the process-wide dispatcher.

- `turn_tool_round.go` — `runToolRound`, tool-call validation host, mixed invalid batch results, pre-execution flush, guardrail halt exit
- `run_agent_tools.go` — `executeToolCalls` segment planning, todo store hydration from history, delegate cap, dedupe, guardrail observations and halt text, `delegate_task` dispatch
- `tool_executor_host.go` — [port-artifact] `tools.ExecutorHost` over the agent: flush, interrupt, progress callbacks (Codex-shaped ones adapted), accessors the executor reads
- `tool_plugin_bridge.go` — installs `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`, `transform_tool_result` hooks and the `tool_request` and `tool_execution` middleware chains on the dispatcher
- `inline_tool_executors_clarify.go` — `clarify` through the agent's clarify callback, else the session asker
- `inline_tool_executors_connections.go` — `todo_list`, `manage_connections` (scopes newly connected MCP servers into the turn) and the legacy `setup_mcp` alias
- `inline_tool_executors_memory.go` — `memory` writes through the built-in store, mirrored to external memory providers
- `inline_executor_host_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] `InlineExecutorHost` accessor; no non-test caller

#### Text finish, stop gates and verify-on-stop evidence

A text reply ends the turn only after: reasoning-only promotion, empty recovery, stall, degenerate-final and acknowledgement re-prompts (two at most), a runaway-repetition abort, a dropped-tool-call re-prompt (three), and four stop gates in order: late LSP verdicts, verify-on-stop, a plugin `pre_verify` hook, and the kanban terminal-call nudge. Verify-on-stop (`agent.verify_on_stop`: `on`, `auto` meaning off on messaging surfaces) re-prompts up to twice when this turn edited code paths and the ledger holds no fresh passing check for that workspace.

- `turn_final_response.go` — `finishTextResponse`, silence-marker handling beside a housekeeping reply, continuation stitching, `transform_llm_output`, final flush
- `turn_stop_gates.go` — the four gates; each appends the attempted answer as interim and a synthetic user nudge
- `verification_stop.go` — enabled test, non-code path filter (docs and prose), workspace status snapshot, nudge text naming up to three verify commands
- `verification_evidence.go` — SQLite ledger `<home>/verification_evidence.db`: shell segment parsing, lint, typecheck, build, format and test detection, stale-on-edit marking; kept 30 days, 100 events per session and workspace
- `kanban_stop.go` — dispatcher-owned worker stopped without `kanban_complete`, `kanban_request_review` or `kanban_block`; `ICEBATH_KANBAN_STOP_NUDGE` disables it

#### Turn finalization, explainers and failure copy

`finalizeTurn` resolves budget exhaustion, starts the deferred title upgrade, saves the trajectory, cleans task resources, strips scaffolding, micro-compacts, persists, appends the file-mutation footer and an abnormal-exit explanation, runs `transform_llm_output` and `post_llm_call`, notifies the context engine, builds the result dict, syncs external memory, spawns the background memory and skill review at its nudge interval, starts a prepared compaction pass, and fires `on_session_end`. A failed turn carries `failure_reason`, `failure_retryable` and user-facing copy.

- `turn_finalize.go` — the finalization sequence, pending-tool-result exit, stream recovery of an empty final, side-question token issue, result fields
- `turn_finalizer.go` — once-per-turn output transform record, held-turn transforms (a plugin holds the stream and only the rewrite leaves), review snapshot clone
- `turn_explainers.go` — per-turn failed `write_file` and `patch` record with on-disk recheck (`display.file_mutation_verifier`), exit explanations (`display.turn_completion_explainer`)
- `turn_failure_copy.go` — exit-reason to failure-verdict table, exhausted, non-retryable, content-policy and limit-reset copy, failed-turn notices, launch-credential refusal
- `persisted_turn_receipt.go` — committed row ids of the current turn for the client's `message.complete` event

#### Interrupt, steer and redirect

Three ways to intervene in a running turn: an interrupt (soft, or hard which also cancels compaction before its commit fence) stops the loop and tool workers and propagates to child agents; a steer queues user text delivered as its own marked user row after the current tool batch; a redirect aborts the in-flight model request and restarts it with the correction appended, degrading to a steer while tools run. A Codex app-server turn is interrupted and steered through its own session.

- `interrupt_control.go` — interrupt publication under the redirect lock, tool-worker and execution-thread signalling, ticketed steer buffer with withdraw and requeue, redirect, interrupt issuer labels
- `interrupt_compat.go` — [port-artifact] duck-typed hard-stop call over four agent method shapes, used by the gateway and TUI teardown

#### System prompt assembly and prompt cache stability

`BuildSystemPrompt` joins three tiers in order, the first being the stable tier: identity (`SOUL.md` of the agent's profile home, else the default identity), Icebath help line, `agent.task_completion_guidance` and `agent.parallel_tool_call_guidance` blocks, tool-aware memory, session-search, skills and kanban guidance, the steer channel note (not one-shot), `agent.tool_use_enforcement` and `agent.execution_guidance` blocks gated by model-name lists, the Alibaba model identity line, `skills.auto_load` blocks, coding posture. The context tier is: the caller's system message, project context files (first kind found of `.icebath.md`, the `AGENTS.md` chain from git root to cwd, `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursorrules` with `.cursor/rules/*.mdc`; threat-scanned and truncated), workspace snapshot, `agent.environment_probe` line, Bot Mode protocol, platform hint with `platform_hints` overrides (without a workspace snapshot the last three end the stable tier instead). The volatile tier is: skills index, built-in memory and user profile blocks, external memory block, plugin sections, active profile line, date-only conversation start with session, model, provider and platform trailer, runtime environment block. The prompt is built once, stored on the session row and reused verbatim; the stable tier is the cache prefix, and plugin sections, workspace snapshot and auto-load skills are frozen per session, so later changes arrive as turn notes.

- `system_prompt.go` — tier builders, model gates, platform hint resolution (built-in, platform registry, cron delivery target), plugin section freeze and restore, invalidation, static prefix reconstruction
- `prompt_builder.go` — execution guidance filtered by available tools, steer marker and channel note, HUD and Bot Screen notes, runtime environment hints (host, home, cwd, scratch dir, or remote backend)
- `prompt_builder_text.go` — [data] texts the tier builders insert: guidance blocks, model lists for the gates, platform hints for `cron`, `cli`, `tui`, `api_server`, WSL and Windows shell hints
- `prompt_context_files.go` — context file discovery and precedence, YAML frontmatter strip, `SOUL.md` load with distribution-manifest ownership check, install-tree fallback suppression
- `prompt_host_{unix,windows}.go` — host label for the environment block: WSL, macOS product version, kernel release, or Windows 10 versus 11 (2 per-OS files)
- `prompt_refresh.go` — operator-requested prompt rebuild: compares the session's `prompt_refresh_epoch` with the requested epoch and rebuilds from current sources once
- `skills_index_delta.go` — stages a turn note when the skills index differs from what the stored prompt told the model
- `surface_switch.go` — stages a turn note with the new platform hint when a session moves to another surface; notes pinned tools the surface did not build
- `prompt_size.go` — `icebath prompt-size [--platform] [--json]`: offline agent, per-tier sizes, per-skill index cost and per-toolset schema bytes

#### Session row, transcript flush and replay canonicalization

The agent creates its session row lazily (source, model, model config, system prompt, gateway identity, parent session, launch cwd, profile) and flushes only unpersisted transcript rows, identified by durable markers and message uids, in one transaction. The current user row is written with its clean text plus the exact sent bytes as `api_content`; ephemeral retry scaffolding never reaches the store; a failed flush gets one retry after adopting a compression tip or healing a missing row. Resume is driven by the caller, which passes the stored transcript as conversation history; the prologue rehydrates the todo store, usage anchor, native compaction checkpoint and user turn count from it. Nothing here forks a session: the store's `IsExplicitForkChild` only feeds the provider's prompt-cache scope.

- `session_persistence.go` — flush collect and write, shared-row stamp bookkeeping, persist overrides, CLI staged user row, close-time flush, unanswered-turn adoption, trajectory save hook
- `session_store.go` — `SessionStore` interface (about 45 methods) satisfied by `state.SessionDB` and the worker stores; auxiliary usage recorder; release-or-close
- `run_agent_session.go` — `ensureDBSession`, session reset for a new session id, context-engine session transition hooks, gateway origin JSON
- `session_activity.go` — activity snapshot shape, iteration progress text, 60 s persist rate limit bypassed by terminal compression stamps
- `session_source.go` — source sets: CLI-family sources for resume, owner-local sources allowed OpenAI Daybreak
- `replay_cleanup.go` — replay transforms on prior history: drop interrupted read-only tool blocks, mark side-effecting ones unknown, redact dangerous confirmations older than 60 s

#### Managed worker child process

A gateway can run a session's turn in a child process: `icebath __icebath_managed_worker__` writes framed events on a private duplicate of stdout (stdout itself is pointed at stderr) and reads controls from stdin. The child sends `hello`, validates the version 1 bootstrap frame, freezes the owner's config and policy process-wide, adopts the execution over the owner's WebSocket, builds the agent, runs one chat turn or kanban attempt, then sends `result` and waits up to 30 s for `finish`. Frames out are `delta`, `tool.start`, `tool.complete`, `approval`, `clarify`, `ready`, `result`, `finished`, `error`; controls in are `stop`, `finish`, `approval` and `clarify` answers.

- `managed_worker_execute.go` — entry dispatch, bootstrap, adoption with epoch check, MCP connect without OAuth prompts, agent construction from policy, turn run and settlement
- `managed_worker.go` — frame writer, bootstrap validation, policy binding, outbox path, stdin control reader with approval and clarify prompts, agent retirement
- `managed_worker_die_{unix,windows}.go` — after the owner's pipe closes, exits after a 10 s grace; kills its own process group on Unix (2 per-OS files)
- `managed_worker_stdio_{unix,windows}.go` — duplicates stdout as the frame channel and redirects stdout to stderr (2 per-OS files)
- `session_worker_turns.go` — worker turn: surface notes armed, chat turn in the session workspace, or a kanban attempt
- `session_kanban_worker_turns.go` — build-tagged (extras only) kanban attempt: preloaded skills, card context, failed-turn recovery under the claim, goal loop, exit code booked on the board; board heartbeat and comment injection bridge
- `worker_automation_codecs.go` — registers goal, loop and heartbeat state codecs the worker rotation uses to migrate automation rows

#### Worker-side session store over owner RPC

Inside a managed worker the agent's `SessionStore` is a facade: every write is a synchronous call to the owning gateway, journaled first in a private outbox so it can be replayed after a reconnect or owner replacement. The RPC is one reused authenticated WebSocket to the gateway endpoint discovered for the profile; it never starts a daemon.

- `runtime_session_store.go` — outbox `pending.json` under an exclusive `owner.lock` (0700, symlinks refused, 4 MB bound), replay, reconciliation onto an adopted epoch, finish and close
- `runtime_session_store_rpc.go` — `WorkerRPC`: endpoint discovery, `worker-adoption` ticket, single reader goroutine, self-RPC refusal, row annotation mirroring, worker-process flag
- `runtime_session_store_methods.go` — message append, turn lease, token and auxiliary usage, model config, system prompt and tool-name writes forwarded to the owner
- `runtime_session_store_lifecycle.go` — session row backfill, titles and title provenance, activity stamps, billing route, user content rewrites, end session
- `runtime_session_store_compression.go` — compression lineage reads, archive-and-compact, child publish, compression lock, cooldown and streak rows through the owner
- `runtime_session_child.go` — store of a delegated child inside a worker: owner-reserved session id, own claim, settles the execution on close

#### /loop and heartbeat automations

`/loop [interval] <prompt> [--times N] [--until <condition>]` repeats a prompt or slash command in a session, at a fixed interval or self-paced (delay doubles while the reply digest is unchanged); a heartbeat is a recurring instruction of at least 60 s. Both are stored as JSON in session meta, and the gateway polls them and injects the wakeup turn. A loop stops on `LOOP_COMPLETE`, a goal-judge verdict on `--until`, `--times`, or pauses at `loops.max_ticks` (100); an active goal defers loop ticks.

- `loop_command.go` — argument parser, control words (`status`, `pause`, `resume`, `stop`), help text, dispatch shared by gateway and TUI
- `loop_state.go` — `SessionLoopState`, `loop:<session>` meta row, `loops.min_interval_seconds` (30), `max_ticks`, `self_paced_floor_seconds` (60), `LoopManager` controls
- `loop_ticks.go` — due check, tick claim and abandon, wakeup prompt templates, completion evaluation, self-paced backoff up to `self_paced_ceiling_seconds` (900), status line
- `loop_state_store.go` — whether a store holds an active or unparseable loop row, for the gateway idle gate
- `heartbeat_manager.go` — interval parser (`10m`, `every 2h`), set, pause, resume, clear, due-prompt claim under a lock, abandon of an unstarted fire
- `heartbeat_state.go` — `HeartbeatState` JSON and the `heartbeat:<session>` meta row
- `viewer_automation_invoke.go` — [port-artifact] calls goal, loop and heartbeat manager methods by Python name with keyword binding, for the gateway's viewer automation RPC
- `run_goals_export.go` — [port-artifact] `LoopManager.IsDueAt` for the gateway scan

#### Mixture of agents (MoA)

Provider `moa` installs a client facade whose aggregator slot is the acting model: reference (advisor) models from a preset are fanned out in parallel on a plain-text view of the transcript, and their numbered outputs are appended as a trailing user message to the aggregator request. Fan-out cadence is per user turn, per iteration or `every_n:N`; advisor cost is priced per slot and folded into usage. A second, inline mode decodes a preset from the user message: on each iteration the advisors run, an auxiliary `moa_aggregator` call synthesizes their answers, and the synthesis is appended to the last user row of the session model's own request.

- `moa_loop.go` — preset and slot resolution, parallel fan-out with timeouts, interrupt and late accounting, window trimming, `degraded_reference_policy`, `privacy_filter` redaction, prepared-request handshake, display events
- `moa_alternation.go` — retries the aggregator once with adjacent user rows merged when the destination rejects same-role turns
- `moa_trace.go` — `moa.save_traces`: one JSONL record per turn under `<home>/moa-traces/` or `moa.trace_dir`, per-slot metrics for hooks

#### Side questions

`/btw` answers a question about the conversation without disturbing it: first through a cache-parity fork of the live agent with every tool denied (3 iterations), else one auxiliary call over a rendered transcript digest (24,000 chars). Separately, a plugin granted `llm.side_question` receives a single-use 60 s token in the `post_llm_call` hook of each attended turn and may redeem it for one text-only question (4096 chars) against that turn's exact request.

- `side_question.go` — `/btw` entry, fork and one-shot paths, transcript rendering, `auxiliary.side_question` config, defaults 2048 tokens, 180 s, temperature 0.3
- `side_question_lease.go` — token issue at turn finalization, expiry, purge and redemption checks (same turn, same profile home, parent alive)
- `side_question_request.go` — frozen request capture, refusals (MoA, agent-as-provider, server-side tools), fork build pinned to the captured prompt and tools, audit log

#### One-shot runs and the direct runner

A one-shot session (a flag frozen from the launch policy at the first tool build) differs from an interactive one: no steer channel note in its prompt, its own disabled toolsets, a `delegate_task` variant without live controls, no turn-end prepared compaction, and auxiliary usage attached to the result. The `icebath-agent` direct runner builds a bare agent for one query and prints a summary.

- `oneshot.go` — `RunOneshot`: one stateless auxiliary LLM call with fence stripping, used by `/btw`; its `commit_message` template has no caller
- `oneshot_footprint.go` — one-shot session flag frozen at first tool build; swaps `delegate_task` for its variant without live control parameters
- `oneshot_aux_usage.go` — per-task auxiliary usage delta of a one-shot run attached to its result as `auxiliary_usage`
- `run_agent_cli.go` — `icebath-agent` direct runner: one query, toolset listing, summary print, `--save-trajectories`, `--save-sample` writing `sample_<id>.json`

#### Session titles

At turn start a session without a title gets an instant derived title (first meaningful line, 48 chars), then a background model call upgrades it; the upgrade is deferred to turn end when it would share the turn's self-hosted endpoint. Title provenance (`derived`, `llm`, `user`) decides what may overwrite what; cron sessions stay untitled and subagent sessions get a `Subagent` prefixed title.

- `title_generator.go` — `auxiliary.title_generation` (`enabled`, `language`, `model_upgrade_enabled`), opener cleaning, JSON title extraction, example-echo and greeting rejection, lineage-suffixed collisions
- `title_generator_exports.go` — [port-artifact] `GenerateTitle` for the `icebath sessions` retitle of skill-opened sessions; skill safety heading constant for its stored-prompt check

#### Reasoning replay policy and outbound sanitizing

Decides which reasoning fields of earlier assistant turns are replayed to the current route and repairs what a provider rejects.

- `reasoning_params.go` — replay decision per route (cached), `agent.reasoning_echo` opt-in, reasoning field copy onto wire rows, Codex-only tool-call field strip
- `reasoning_params_endpoint.go` — reasoning support probes per model and endpoint (60 s recheck), LM Studio reasoning options, endpoint profiles, must-echo padding
- `reasoning_promotion.go` — whether a clean stop with reasoning but no content may be returned as the answer (custom provider capability, local Nemotron parser models)
- `message_sanitization.go` — image strip for rejecting models, JSON-safe outbound strings, reasoning carrier shaping, rejected carriers persisted as `reasoning_rejected_carriers`

#### Vision fallback and image replay

Lets image input work on models and routes that cannot take it.

- `vision_message_prep.go` — replaces image parts with cached `vision_analyze` descriptions for non-vision models, downgrades image tool results, Qwen Portal message shaping
- `image_replay.go` — `vision.replay_recent_images`: reattaches retained images from the profile's `native-inputs` cache to earlier user rows, in batches
- `image_eviction_policy.go` — per-session set of tool call ids whose images the send path retired

#### Voice turns and surface notes

A turn marked as spoken runs on the `auxiliary.voice_chat` route and effort for that turn only, with the session route restored afterwards.

- `voice_turn_route.go` — route capture, bind, fit check against the route's compression threshold, lowest valid effort, restore, one user notice when the route cannot be used
- `voice_turn_route_session_view.go` — reports the session's own route while a voice turn is live
- `session_surface_turn.go` — arms a turn from the gateway admission's surface: voice marker, HUD or voice-live note, barge-in note

In-place route changes on a live agent and the bookkeeping to undo them.
