## 4. Model providers

### `pkg/provider` — model-provider layer: wire adapters, sign-in flows, credential pool and stores, provider profiles and plugins, model catalogs, local runtimes, and several unrelated CLIs

*470 files, 166,684 Go lines*

One flat package of 470 files. It holds the wire adapters for Anthropic Messages, OpenAI chat completions, OpenAI Responses (Codex), Bedrock Converse and native Gemini; every sign-in flow; the "auxiliary" side-call subsystem; the Codex app-server runtime; the provider profile contract with 34 built-in registry rows and 38 bundled provider plugins; runtime resolution of provider, credential and protocol; the credential pool and the `auth.json` store; secrets sources; the managed llama.cpp runtime; model catalogs, context-length metadata, pricing and the `/model` switch pipeline. No vendor SDK is used: botocore's credential chain, azure-identity/MSAL and google-auth are reimplemented here. There are two parallel request paths, and only the Python-shaped one (kwargs maps through SDK-emulating clients) is driven by `pkg/agent`; the typed `Client` adapters' entry methods run only under tests while their builders and stream loops are shared. The package also houses the bodies of `icebath auth`, `fallback`, `egress`, `codex-runtime`, `migrate`, `proxy`, `moa`, `usage`, `secrets` and `model`, plus general utilities (file locks, deadlines, env loading) used across the codebase. Port scaffolding is heavy: Python exception class names and MROs on errors, SDK header and JSON key-order reproduction, function-variable seams standing in for patched module attributes, and psutil, urllib, httpx, requests and difflib emulation.

**Files `account_*` through `gemini_*`** (213 files, 87,415 Go lines). This part holds the wire adapters for Anthropic Messages, OpenAI chat completions, OpenAI Responses (Codex), Bedrock Converse and native Gemini; every sign-in flow and the `icebath auth`, `icebath fallback`, `icebath egress`, `icebath codex-runtime` and `icebath migrate <agent>` command bodies; the whole "auxiliary" side-call subsystem (`CallLLM`); the Codex app-server runtime; user-configured ("custom") providers; dotenv loading; and hand-written replacements for botocore, azure-identity/MSAL and google-auth (no vendor SDK is a direct dependency). It reads and writes `auth.json` (through the store in the other half of the package), `config.yaml`, `.env`, `.op.env`, `cache/model_catalog.json`, `cache/oauth_heal_clean.json`, `.copilot_jwt.json`, and other tools' files (`~/.claude/.credentials.json`, the macOS Keychain, `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.qwen/oauth_creds.json`, `~/.aws/*`, gcloud ADC). There are two parallel request paths: typed `Client` adapters registered per api mode (`Complete`/`Stream`/`CountTokens` over `*Request`) and a Python-shaped path that passes `map[string]any` kwargs through SDK-emulating clients. `pkg/agent` drives only the kwargs path (`InterruptibleStreamingAPICall`, `InterruptibleAPICall`, `RunCodexStream`, `CallLLM`); `NewClient` has one production caller (`BindBedrockRuntime`), and the only non-test code that builds a typed `Request` is `auxiliary_client_provider_adapter.go`, for plugin-hosted provider clients. So the built-in adapters' typed entry methods run only under tests, while their builders, normalizers and parts of their stream loops are shared with the kwargs path. Port scaffolding is heavy: Python exception class names and MROs on errors, "async twin" clients and event-loop keys, SDK header and JSON key-order reproduction, `repr`-formatted messages, and doc comments that still name the Python modules a section came from.

#### Account usage and quota windows

Fetches per-account quota for the `/usage` surfaces and the credential picker: Codex (`<backend>/wham/usage`), Anthropic OAuth (`api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage`), OpenRouter credits and key quota, or a plugin profile's usage hook bounded at 10 seconds. Also redeems a banked Codex rate-limit reset credit (`/usage reset`).

- `account_usage.go` — fetchers per provider, snapshot and window types, text and markdown rendering with bars and reset phrases, Codex reset-credit redeem with one 401 refresh retry
- `account_usage_cache.go` — in-process snapshot cache keyed by home, provider, account identity and base URL; 120 second refresh throttle, 15 minute staleness, async background refresh per pool entry
- `account_usage_json.go` — [py-shim] Python `json.loads` plus `repr` of the decoded value (exact ints, lone surrogates, last duplicate key wins); used for error text of usage bodies and by the plugin router

#### ACP agent backend bridge

Lets an external ACP agent (for example the Copilot CLI) stand in as a chat-completions backend: tools and transcript are flattened into one text prompt, and tool calls are parsed back out of `<tool_call>{...}</tool_call>` blocks. Called from `pkg/acpclient` and `pkg/acp`.

- `acp_client_prompt.go` — builds the single ACP prompt: fixed preamble, forwarded tool schemas, role-labelled transcript, continue instruction
- `acp_openai_bridge.go` — tool-call contract text, extraction of tagged or bare JSON tool calls from response text (missing ids become `acp_call_N`), one-shot completion reshaped as a data chunk plus a usage chunk
- `acp_model_catalog_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers over model-list helpers (declared ids, allowlist test, live picker fetch, configured custom ids) for `pkg/acp`

#### Agent seams and importing other agents' setups

Two dead hook variables, a notice type, and the `icebath migrate <agent>` body that imports another agent's setup through the `agent-importers` catalog plugin.

- `agent_hooks.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] two function variables `pkg/agent` assigns at init (outbound kwargs sanitizer, per-model image strip) that nothing ever reads; the summary code calls the same operations through the `ChatCompletionAgent` interface instead
- `agent_notice.go` — `AgentNotice` struct (text, level, kind, TTL, key, id) that gateway and TUI drivers render
- `agent_import.go` — detects OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Grok Bot and OpenBot by home directories, installs or enables the plugin, runs the import and reports whether `config.yaml` or `.env` changed; only `icebath migrate` calls it, the setup-wizard variant of the offer has no caller

#### Anthropic Messages wire

Request building, message conversion, streaming and response normalization for Anthropic and Anthropic-compatible endpoints (Kimi, MiniMax, DeepSeek, OpenCode, Azure, plus Bedrock and Vertex transports defined elsewhere). Registered for `anthropic_messages`; in production its builders, headers and transport are reached through the SDK-shaped client in the auxiliary group and the agent transport, while `anthropicClient.Complete`/`Stream`/`CountTokens` over a typed `Request` have no production caller.

- `anthropic.go` — model tables (max output, adaptive versus budget thinking, mandatory-thinking and no-sampling families), beta headers, auth style (x-api-key, Bearer, OAuth, Kimi), Claude Code OAuth identity (system prefix, tool renames to `mcp__`, product-name rewrite, detected CLI version), fast mode, `response_format` to `output_config`, 1M-context beta drop on rejection, request timeouts, usage and stop-reason mapping
- `anthropic_convert.go` — OpenAI-shaped messages and tools to Messages blocks: tool id sanitizing, image blocks with SVG rasterizing, ordered thinking replay from a live sidecar, orphan tool pair repair, role alternation merge, per-route thinking signature policy, screenshot eviction (20 images, 24 MB, 2000 px many-image rule), blank-text guard
- `anthropic_stream.go` — SSE event decoding and message accumulator (out-of-order event error, null usage fill, malformed tool JSON error), both live; plus the typed path's stream state, delta emission and watchdog loop, which only tests drive
- `anthropic_endpoints.go` — host and model classifiers: third-party versus native, Kimi, DeepSeek, MiniMax, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex, OAuth token shape, Claude family version, thinking-replay route
- `anthropic_cache.go` — prompt cache planning: up to four `cache_control` breakpoints (system prefix plus latest cacheable messages or last tool plus two completed transactions), stable user-message scaffold registry, TTL choice (5m for machine-paced sources, 1h otherwise, clamped per provider), marker stripping
- `anthropic_thinking.go` — remembers sha256 fingerprints of thinking blocks an endpoint rejected, per session under model-config key `_anthropic_rejected_thinking`, and strips them from later replays
- `anthropic_wire_order.go` — [py-shim] rebuilds request bodies in the exact key order the Python Anthropic SDK emits (params, blocks, tools, `extra_body` merge); used by the direct, Bedrock and Vertex transports
- `anthropic_plain_data.go` — [py-shim] SDK-object to plain maps and lists with cycle and depth-20 guards, used when normalizing responses

#### Anthropic credentials and the Claude Code login

Resolves an Anthropic token in order: `ANTHROPIC_TOKEN` or `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, the credential pool, then the borrowed Claude Code login. Runs icebath's own Claude Pro/Max PKCE sign-in (client id `9d1c250a-…`, `claude.ai/oauth/authorize`) and `claude setup-token`.

- `anthropic_credentials.go` — reads `~/.claude/.credentials.json` and the macOS Keychain item `Claude Code-credentials`, refreshes OAuth tokens, writes rotated pairs back to file and Keychain, tracks spent single-use refresh tokens in an `.icebath-spent-rotations.json` sidecar, PKCE login and setup-token runners

#### `icebath auth` command

Credential-pool management CLI: `add`, `list`, `remove`, `reset`, `priority`, `refresh`, `status`, `logout`, `use`, `rename`, `rotation`, and an interactive menu when called bare. Entry point `AuthCommand` is called from `cmd/icebath`.

- `auth_commands.go` — shared CLI state, provider normalization and aliases, `add` for API keys, OAuth (Anthropic, Codex, xAI, Qwen, MiniMax, OpenRouter, plugin providers) and a Vertex service-account path, exhaustion labels, `priority`
- `auth_commands_interactive.go` — bare `icebath auth` menu (add, remove, reset, rotation strategy), action dispatch, `AuthCommand` exit-code mapping
- `auth_commands_logins.go` — named logins: `use <provider> <login|@rotate>`, `rename`, `rotation`, naming a newly added login, adopting stored logins, logout of one login, suppressing env sources
- `auth_commands_manage.go` — `list` with free-tier hints and external-login notices, `remove`, `reset`, `refresh`, `status` including Bedrock caller identity and Azure Entra detail, `logout`; strategies fill_first, round_robin, least_used, random

#### Auth status, flow registry and login side effects

Per-provider OAuth plumbing table (resolve, status, terminal refresh codes) for Codex, xAI, Qwen and MiniMax; `GetAuthStatus` for every auth type; and the `config.yaml` edits that login and logout make.

- `auth_flows.go` — `OAuthProviderFlows` registry, status snapshots (pool first, then legacy state; API key, external process, AWS SDK, Azure Foundry), `model.provider` and `base_url` writes on login, reset to `auto` on logout, `LogoutLogin`, retired `login` command notice, auth-error copy
- `auth_constants.go` — client ids, token and device URLs, default base URLs, refresh skews, no-auth placeholder keys, `AuthError` type with relogin hints, unverified JWT claim decode
- `auth_error_copy.go` — user-facing copy for failed sign-ins: device-code expiry, network, cancel, generic rules
- `auth_store_source_labels.go` — the `icebath_pkce` source label constant for icebath's own Anthropic sign-in
- `auth_external_process.go` — installs into `pkg/config` the denylist of launch env names (external-process providers plus left-core rows) the env writer refuses

#### OAuth transport helpers

Shared machinery for device-code and loopback-redirect flows.

- `auth_device_flow.go` — PKCE pair, RFC 8252 loopback callback server, RFC 8628 polling loop with cancel hook, remote-session and console-browser detection with SSH tunnel hint, TLS-verify selection, form POST helpers, offer to reuse existing credentials
- `auth_loopback_{unix,windows}.go` — sets `SO_REUSEADDR` on the loopback callback socket (2 per-OS files)

#### Vendor sign-in flows

One file per vendor flow; each returns a credential map that the auth command or setup flow stores in the pool.

- `auth_codex.go` — OpenAI Codex device-code login at `auth.openai.com`, token refresh with reuse and quota error classification, runtime credential resolution from the pool, quota probe that clears pool cooldowns, `ICEBATH_CODEX_BASE_URL` override
- `auth_codex_browser.go` — Codex authorization-code plus PKCE login on `127.0.0.1:1455`, chosen by flag or `auth.codex_login_flow`, falling back to device code when the port is busy
- `auth_xai.go` — xAI Grok OAuth: OIDC discovery at `auth.x.ai`, device-code login, refresh, endpoints and inference base URL pinned to the x.ai origin over HTTPS
- `auth_minimax.go` — MiniMax user-code plus PKCE login against the global or China portal, expiry normalization (epoch ms or TTL), refreshing token provider for the Anthropic-wire route
- `auth_qwen.go` — borrows the Qwen CLI login at `~/.qwen/oauth_creds.json`, refreshes it at `chat.qwen.ai` and writes it back to that file
- `auth_openrouter.go` — OpenRouter PKCE flow that mints an API key, by loopback callback locally or pasted code in remote sessions
- `auth_zai_kimi.go` — probes the four Z.AI endpoints (global, China, and both coding plans) in parallel and caches the winner per key in `auth.json`; despite the name it contains nothing for Kimi

#### Plugin-declared providers and their auth

Mirrors provider plugin profiles into the provider registry as each profile home sees them, and routes auth actions to plugins.

- `auth_plugin_registry.go` — home-scoped registry: built-in rows plus lazily mirrored plugin profiles, alias ownership rules, row insertion order, inference base URL lookup
- `auth_registry_view.go` — [port-artifact] exported read-only views: registry keys and rows, profile env vars, Anthropic probe betas, Bedrock model count, AWS error class
- `auth_plugin_providers.go` — dispatches the `add`, `status`, `logout` and `refresh` actions to a plugin's OAuth client or auth handler, generic device-code login from profile metadata, pooled-row expiry check
- `auth_oauth_pkce_plugin.go` — generic public-client PKCE login and refresh from plugin-declared endpoints, with host allowlist, HTTPS-only rule and no-redirect token client

#### Single-use OAuth grants across profiles

Keeps a rotating refresh token from being forked between the root home and profile homes.

- `auth_oauth_grants.go` — strips cloned single-use OAuth logins from a new profile, merges snapshots without reviving spent grants, heals a forked grant back into the root store (fresher pair wins), records clean marks in `oauth_heal_clean.json`

#### Post-login model picker

Interactive model choice shown after a sign-in; called from the model setup flows in the other half of the package.

- `auth_model_picker.go` — model selection prompt used by setup flows: price columns per million tokens, current-model marker, numbered fallback off a terminal, selection-guard confirmation, saving the choice to config

#### Auxiliary calls: entry, task routing and policy

"Auxiliary" means every model call that is not the main agent turn: compression, vision, title generation, approval, goal judge, memory query rewrite, kanban decomposer and triage specifier, curator, background review, profile describer, MoA reference and aggregator, MCP sampling, plugin LLM calls (config also defines `monitor`, `review`, `video`, `voice_chat` and `tts_audio_tags` blocks). `CallLLM`/`AsyncCallLLM` take Python-style kwargs; the route is explicit arguments, then `auxiliary.<task>` config (provider, model, base_url, api_key, key_env, api_mode, reasoning_effort, timeout, no_progress_timeout, max_concurrency, fallback_chain, extra_body), then `auto`.

- `auxiliary_client_call.go` — `CallLLM` and `AsyncCallLLM`: kwarg validation, per-task semaphore, latency stamps, transient same-provider retries, recovery ladder (parameter strip, credential refresh or rotation, provider fallback)
- `auxiliary_client_task.go` — task route resolution, compression fast lane (certified non-reasoning route), per-task `max_concurrency` semaphores, request kwargs build (profile projection, extra body merge, tool-name dedupe), response validation
- `auxiliary_task_config.go` — task config lookup: session-frozen `auxiliary` section, plugin-declared task defaults, `inherit_from` chains with cycle guard, route-authoritative tasks
- `auxiliary_client_timeout.go` — task timeout (default 30 seconds, compression floored at 300) and `no_progress_timeout`
- `auxiliary_client_policy.go` — provider alias table, fixed-temperature models, temperature rejection memo, Codex compaction thresholds (0.85 and 0.70), cheapest aux model per provider (live fast-family pick, profile default, static table), vision model defaults
- `auxiliary_client_max_tokens.go` — picks `max_tokens` versus `max_completion_tokens` for the route
- `auxiliary_client_message.go` — pulls the first choice message, content or reasoning fallback, out of dict- or struct-shaped responses
- `auxiliary_client_runtime_main.go` — binds the live main runtime (provider, model, base URL, key, api mode) on the context so aux routing follows the running agent
- `auxiliary_client_main.go` — reads main provider and model from that binding or config, unwraps a MoA preset to its aggregator, reuses the main key only for the same origin

#### Auxiliary calls: provider client resolution

Turns a provider name into a client and model. `auto` tries the main provider route, the task `fallback_chain`, the main `fallback_providers` chain, then discovery (OpenRouter, local or custom endpoint, first healthy API-key provider).

- `auxiliary_client_resolve.go` — `ResolveProviderClient` dispatcher with branches for auto, OpenRouter, Codex, xAI OAuth, custom, named custom, Azure Foundry, API-key, external-process and registry providers; async client wrapper; effective-provider stamping
- `auxiliary_client_custom.go` — custom endpoint, Codex, xAI, Azure Foundry and Anthropic branch builders, proxy env and base URL validation, the discovery chain order
- `auxiliary_client_credentials.go` — xAI and Codex credential pairs, first healthy API-key provider scan, OpenRouter client with the free-only policy and paid-lane warning, endpoint and profile default headers
- `auxiliary_client_registry.go` — registry auth-type arms: Vertex, Bedrock, MiniMax OAuth, plugin OAuth
- `auxiliary_plugin_oauth.go` — client for a plugin OAuth provider from its signed-in pool entry and configured endpoint
- `auxiliary_client_pool.go` — credential pool load, peek and select for aux use, runtime key and base URL of an entry
- `auxiliary_client_hosts.go` — host-to-provider tables for pool recovery and auth refresh (chatgpt.com, openrouter.ai, api.anthropic.com, api.kimi.com, api.x.ai)
- `auxiliary_client_route.go` — returns the provider stamped on an auto-routed client, else a fallback name
- `auxiliary_client_normalize.go` — key normalization (callable passed through) and per-provider model id rewrite
- `auxiliary_client_vision.go` — vision route: explicit endpoint, main provider when its model sees images, then OpenRouter and DeepInfra; Z.AI vision forced onto its OpenAI-compatible URLs; the exported backend lister has no caller
- `auxiliary_local_runtime.go` — resolves a bare llama.cpp alias to the profile's local server endpoint
- `auxiliary_managed_local.go` — reads the managed llama-server address from the supervisor state file (15 second cache) and tests whether a URL targets it
- `auxiliary_client_headers.go` — OpenRouter, NVIDIA NIM and Vercel AI Gateway attribution headers, `model.default_headers` merge, Anthropic-to-OpenAI base URL rewrite for dual-surface hosts
- `auxiliary_client_cache.go` — client cache of 64 entries keyed by provider, endpoint, key identity, api mode, task and pool hint; eviction on connection errors; stale async client cleanup and shutdown
- `auxiliary_client_factory.go` — availability-probe mode that returns a client which errors on any real use; log-once set; chat stream interface

#### Auxiliary calls: failure handling and health

Classifies aux failures and decides between retry, parameter strip, credential recovery, fallback and quarantine.

- `auxiliary_client_fallback.go` — fallback candidates: task `fallback_chain`, main fallback chain, payment fallback, main agent model; minimum context length check; per-entry timeout and key; auto route
- `auxiliary_fallback_recovery.go` — caller-owned send that retries a parameter 400 through the strip rungs
- `auxiliary_client_recovery.go` — same-provider recovery: pool refresh or rotation, Codex, Anthropic, xAI and Vertex credential refresh, rebuilt client retry
- `auxiliary_rate_limit_backoff.go` — one same-credential retry after a rate limit, honouring Retry-After up to 5 seconds
- `auxiliary_client_classify.go` — predicates for payment, overload, rate limit, timeout, connection, auth, unsupported parameter, structured output, reasoning field, model not found
- `auxiliary_call_outcome.go` — detects error objects in HTTP 200 bodies, cancellation versus failure, classifier input
- `auxiliary_error_shapes.go` — [py-shim] error types carrying Python SDK class names and MROs (`APIError` family, `RuntimeError`), status and body accessors
- `auxiliary_unavailable.go` — "no auxiliary client" and "credentials exhausted" errors with pool cooldown, billing and missing-credential remedy text
- `auxiliary_health.go` — unhealthy-cache key per home and endpoint, quarantine TTL per fallback reason (60 seconds for transient)
- `auxiliary_client_unhealthy.go` — in-process table that hides a provider endpoint for a TTL (600 seconds after a payment error, 60 for an unavailable OpenRouter, per-reason for quarantined fallbacks), with once-a-minute skip logging
- `auxiliary_reasoning_floor.go` — remembers routes that refuse a reasoning disable and lifts later requests to effort `low`
- `auxiliary_structured_output.go` — remembers routes that reject a `response_format` type and drops it on later requests
- `auxiliary_key_rotation.go` — swaps a revoked main key inside the bound runtime map

#### Auxiliary calls: clients and wire adapters

Every client exposes `CreateChatCompletion(kwargs)`. Despite the "auxiliary" filenames, the OpenAI and Anthropic clients here are also the request clients the main agent loop uses.

- `auxiliary_client_sdk.go` — [py-shim] OpenAI-compatible HTTP client written as an emulation of the Python `openai` SDK: 2 retries with 0.5 to 8 second backoff and Retry-After, per-phase timeouts, SSE chunk stream, Stainless headers, SDK error classes; real behaviour inside is the chat-completions and Responses transport
- `auxiliary_client_openai.go` — builds that client for a route: TLS verify from config, environment-only proxy, SDK retries off
- `auxiliary_client_anthropic_sdk.go` — Anthropic SDK-shaped client over the Messages transport: raw kwargs in, raw Message maps out, stream-then-create fallback, Bedrock variant
- `auxiliary_client_anthropic_adapter.go` — chat-completions facade over Anthropic Messages and over Bedrock Converse, with async twins
- `auxiliary_client_anthropic_images.go` — rewrites OpenAI image and video URL parts into Anthropic source blocks
- `auxiliary_client_codex_adapter.go` — chat-completions facade over a streamed Responses request, shared async-twin base
- `auxiliary_codex_response.go` — converts a final Responses object to text, tool calls, usage and finish reason
- `auxiliary_client_gemini.go` — chat-completions facade over native Gemini with per-read and per-write socket deadlines and a chunk stream
- `auxiliary_client_provider_adapter.go` — wraps a profile-built typed `Client` as an aux client; `AuxAdapter` implements `tools.Aux` and MCP sampling through `CallLLM`
- `auxiliary_async_rebuild.go` — [port-artifact] key source and default headers used to build the "async twin" of a sync client
- `auxiliary_wire.go` — sanitizes chat messages at the client boundary and builds Relay metadata for an attempt

#### Auxiliary calls: progress, watchdogs and cancellation

Aux calls are streamed and re-aggregated when a progress hook is installed or the provider is stream-only, so silence can be detected.

- `auxiliary_client_progress.go` — stream-and-aggregate create, chunk accumulator (content, reasoning, tool calls), credit-limited 402 retry with a lower output cap, gateway envelope unwrap
- `auxiliary_client_stream.go` — absolute stream ceiling: max of 600 seconds and four times the timeout
- `auxiliary_stream_watchdog.go` — first-token and inter-chunk windows on an awake clock that shut the attempt socket when they lapse
- `auxiliary_client_codex_guard.go` — Codex aux stream deadline and stall guard, pooled-connection tracking and forced TCP close so a killed attempt never poisons the pool
- `auxiliary_client_interrupt.go` — explicit host cancel sources, interrupt protection scope, cancel-versus-timeout arbitration, per-call progress and timing hooks, host stream deadline

#### Auxiliary calls: hooks, Relay records and usage accounting

Observability of aux calls: plugin lifecycle hooks, records in Relay (the LLM-call interception runtime in `relay_llm.go`), and per-session token rows in the session store.

- `auxiliary_hooks.go` — fires plugin hooks `pre_auxiliary_call` and `post_auxiliary_call` per physical attempt with task, route, request view, usage and parent turn identity
- `auxiliary_client_relay.go` — one Relay call record per aux call: route stamping, attempt counting, completion or failure
- `auxiliary_accounting.go` — records aux token usage and estimated cost against the ambient session, skipping MoA tasks
- `auxiliary_accounting_state.go` — converts an aux usage row to the session-store row type

#### AWS credential chain, signed client and event streams

A Go reimplementation of the botocore pieces Bedrock needs; no AWS SDK is used directly.

- `aws_credentials.go` — default chain (explicit keys, env, assume role with MFA and source profiles, web identity, SSO with token refresh, shared credentials, `credential_process`, config, ECS/EKS container, IMDSv2), shared config INI parsing, refresh windows, STS calls
- `aws_client.go` — SigV4-signed service client with connect and read timeouts, legacy, standard and adaptive retry modes, token-bucket rate limiter, JSON error parsing
- `aws_eventstream.go` — binary event-stream frame decoder with CRC checks, mid-stream exception mapping, Anthropic events out of InvokeModelWithResponseStream
- `aws_tty_unix.go`, `aws_tty_{bsd,linux}.go`, `aws_tty_windows.go` — hidden terminal line read for the MFA code, with per-OS termios ioctls and a Windows console variant

#### Bedrock: routing, discovery and wires

Three Bedrock surfaces: Converse, Anthropic Messages over InvokeModel, and the "Mantle" OpenAI Responses endpoint.

- `bedrock.go` — region and guardrail config, per-home client cache, Mantle base URL and SigV4 or API-key auth, AWS auth source detection, model and inference-profile discovery cached an hour, context windows (static table or live overflow probe), application-profile ARN resolution, reasoning replay policy per model family; `BindBedrockRuntime` stores a typed Messages client on the agent that `CreateAnthropicMessage` would reject, requests use a per-request SDK-shaped client instead
- `bedrock_converse.go` — Converse calls from kwargs (Converse and ConverseStream, latch to non-streaming once IAM denies streaming, response validation), used by the agent and aux paths; the typed Converse client around them is built only by its factory, which nothing invokes
- `bedrock_converse_convert.go` — messages and tools to Converse blocks, cachePoint placement with per-model rejection memo, redacted reasoning recovery, Claude and Nova reasoning config
- `bedrock_converse_stream.go` — Converse response and stream events normalized to OpenAI shape with usage including cache tokens and ordered reasoning blocks
- `bedrock_converse_wire.go` — [py-shim] Converse request JSON in botocore member order with base64 blobs
- `bedrock_transport.go` — Anthropic Messages over InvokeModel and InvokeModelWithResponseStream: body reshaping, bearer or SigV4 auth, guardrail headers, `ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_BASE_URL` override, SSE frames from AWS events

Azure OpenAI and Foundry request shaping plus a Go reimplementation of azure-identity and MSAL.

- `azure_identity_broker.go` — brokered sign-in through the native `msalruntime` library fetched under the icebath home (Windows and WSL), VS Code Azure Resources `authRecord.json` credential, public-client token cache

A Go reimplementation of google-auth, used by Vertex and by the Google Chat platform.

- `gcp_auth.go` — Application Default Credentials order, service account JWT grant, authorized user refresh, GCE metadata, gcloud ADC and project, impersonation, GDCH, external account federation (file, URL, X.509, AWS, executable)

#### Native Gemini wire

`generateContent` and `streamGenerateContent` adapter, also selected for chat routes whose base URL is a native Gemini or Vertex express host.

- `gemini.go` — client, API-key or token auth, base URL normalization, error mapping with free-tier and wrong-surface guidance, tier probe, multi-hop long decode, stream producer; the agent and aux paths enter through its kwargs `CreateChatCompletion`, the typed `Complete`/`Stream` have no production caller

#### Model catalog manifest and curated lists

The remotely refreshable model manifest behind the pickers (`model_catalog` config: enabled, url, refresh interval, `providers.<name>.url`) and the static curated lists used when it is unavailable.

- `catalog_list.go` — model catalog manifest: embedded copy, fetch from `icebath.app/api/model-catalog.json` with a GitHub fallback, disk cache at `cache/model_catalog.json`, stale-while-revalidate, per-provider override URLs, failure backoff
- `catalog_static.go` — curated per-provider model lists, provider groups folded into one picker row, aggregator set, aliases, plugin provider admission, xAI list from the models.dev cache
- `chat_catalog.go` — filters image and video generation models out of chat catalogs by id shape, tags or output modalities

#### Error classification, retry state and failover identity

Turns a failed provider call into a recovery decision. `ClassifyError` is called by `pkg/agent`, the gateway and the aux ladder.

- `classify.go` — staged classifier from status, body, headers and error chain to a `FailoverReason` (31 reasons) with retry, rotate, fallback and compress hints; plugin classifier hook; timeout phase; summaries, key masking
- `do.go` — `RetrySession` latches across calls, reset-time extraction from Retry-After and vendor headers, non-retryable labels, ladder stop hints per platform, local validation error
- `chain.go` — backend identity (provider, model, endpoint) and the rule for skipping fallback candidates that share the failed credential, endpoint or deployment
- `cooldown.go` — reasons that arm a rate-limit cooldown and conversion of a provider reset instant to a wait
- `billing_links.go` — billing-wall descriptor with the provider's add-credits URL by slug or host
- `bounded_response.go` — reads a streaming error body under a byte cap and hard deadline

#### Deadlines, locks and small caches

General utilities that live here but are used across the codebase.

- `deadline.go` — bounded execution of a function with timeout, abandonment cleanup and blocked-loop stack dump; `timeouts.*` config lookup; `PollUntil`
- `deadline_tree.go` — [port-artifact] re-export of the process-tree kill in `internal/treekill`
- `file_lock.go` — cross-process advisory file lock, reentrant per goroutine, with pid written into the lock file and a timeout error; used by sessions, gateway and config
- `cache_bounds.go` — TTL drop, oldest-entry eviction and LRU publish helpers for map caches

#### OpenAI chat completions wire

Request shaping for every OpenAI-compatible provider, plus the typed chat adapter. The kwargs builders, quirk tables and guards are live; `chatCompletionsClient.Complete`/`Stream` have no production caller, but its stream state and consume loop are reused by plugin-hosted provider clients, and its request builder, timeouts and response normalizer by the Gemini adapter.

- `chat_completions.go` — registers the chat-completions and Codex Responses adapters; typed client with request preparation, HTTP errors, non-streaming and streaming calls, reasoning extraction, response normalization
- `chat_completions_convert.go` — per-provider quirk tables: reasoning effort ladder and clamps, provider-specific reasoning and extra-body shapes for about 20 providers, think-tag stripping, tool id digests, Moonshot schema subset, temperature and output-cap rules, prompt cache key, OpenRouter reasoning-capability catalog and provider routing, LM Studio and Ollama probes, user agent
- `chat_completions_transport.go` — kwargs builder for the agent path: message sanitizing, developer-role swap, max-tokens parameter choice, profile-driven build
- `chat_completions_stream.go` — typed stream attempt: timeouts, stale patience scaled by context size, chunk handling, tool call assembly, partial-stream stub response
- `chat_completions_stream_guards.go` — tool-call delta accumulator, streaming think-tag scrubber, runaway repetition detector, truncated tool-argument JSON repair, stream lifetime cap, llama-server prompt progress
- `chat_completions_tool_args.go` — turns non-string tool call arguments into compact JSON text
- `chat_wire_order.go` — [py-shim] keeps message, tool call and content-part keys in the order the builder recorded so the request body matches the Python one

#### Agent request execution: streaming

The path `pkg/agent` actually uses. `InterruptibleStreamingAPICall` dispatches by api mode to chat completions, Anthropic Messages, Codex passthrough or Bedrock, and returns a non-streaming-shaped response.

- `chat_completion_agent.go` — `ChatCompletionAgent` interface (83 methods the helpers call back on), inline and worker non-streaming dispatch, stale kill, reasoning config for the wire, per-turn VM and browser cleanup
- `chat_completion_streaming_call.go` — one streaming request: attempt ids, single-writer fence, chunk accounting, delta callbacks, retry loop (`ICEBATH_STREAM_RETRIES`, default 2), replay of non-stream responses, cut-stream response
- `chat_completion_streaming_monitor.go` — 300 ms poll loop: heartbeat, sleep skip, local model load notice, stale kill, `agent.stream_max_lifetime` cap, interrupt abort, wedged-worker abandonment
- `chat_completion_streaming_errors.go` — stream error status and transport classification, `stream_options` rejection retry, disabling streaming, unmasking a server error with a non-streaming call
- `chat_completion_streaming_anthropic.go` — Anthropic message stream object over SSE with snapshot accumulation and OS-level connection error mapping
- `chat_completion_stream_agent.go` — stream start and end emitters, Codex passthrough, Bedrock ConverseStream run with IAM fallback and Relay recording
- `chat_completion_stream_diag.go` — per-attempt chunk and byte diagnostics, attaching the failed wire request to errors

#### Agent request execution: non-streaming, waits and summaries

- `chat_completion_nonstream_agent.go` — agent non-streaming request on a worker with Codex time-to-first-byte, idle and stale watchdogs (`ICEBATH_CODEX_TTFB_*`, `ICEBATH_CODEX_EVENT_STALE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`), request-client registry, interrupt handling
- `chat_completion_nonstream.go` — wait notices and heartbeats while polling a worker, stale-kill reporting, worker join after a kill, the typed path's non-stream runner
- `chat_completion_direct.go` — rule for running a request inline: cron turns and delegated children
- `chat_completion_direct_call.go` — socket backstop timeout for inline calls and stale-streak reset
- `chat_completion_wait_notice.go` — neutral status line naming the wait phase and the watchdog about to reconnect
- `chat_completion_local.go` — stale-streak breaker (`ICEBATH_STREAM_STALE_GIVEUP`, default 5), recovery check of a local server, managed model load notice
- `chat_completion_fallback_mode.go` — detects the wire (chat, Responses, Messages) of a fallback entry from provider, base URL and model
- `chat_completion_summary.go` — at the iteration limit, asks the model for a tool-free summary per api mode with one retry on empty output

#### Typed-path stream supervision and Relay streams

Supervision for the typed adapters' stream loops, reached in production only when an auxiliary call goes to a plugin-hosted provider client. No non-test code installs the per-call context these read (`streamCall`), so the Relay identity and writer fence they consult are always empty there.

- `chat_completion_stream_monitor.go` — wait monitor (heartbeat, prompt-progress and local-load lines), stale and lifetime watchdog, and abandoned-stream error for typed stream attempts
- `chat_completion_relay_stream.go` — Relay-managed stream sources for the typed chat and Messages adapters and writer-claim checks; its chunk accumulator that rebuilds a completion is also used by the agent streaming call

#### Credential lifecycle, sources and recovery

Where a credential came from, how it is saved or removed everywhere it was mirrored, and what happens when a provider rejects it mid-turn.

- `credential_persistence.go` — secret-key detection in payloads, fingerprints, stripping secrets from borrowed pool rows before persisting

Parses `.env` files and publishes them into the process environment at startup and on reload; `LoadIcebathDotenv` is called from a dozen entry points.

Glue that exists because `pkg/config`, `pkg/cron` and `pkg/gateway` cannot import this package.

**Files `git_*` through `xai_*`** (257 files, 79,269 Go lines). This part holds the provider profile contract and registry (34 built-in registry rows, 38 bundled "model provider plugin" directories ported to Go functions, and home-installed provider plugins run as guests of the plugin host), runtime resolution of provider, credential and wire protocol, the credential pool with named logins and the `auth.json` store, per-profile secret scoping and the external secret sources behind `icebath secrets`, the managed llama.cpp runtime, model catalogs and context-length metadata, the `/model` switch pipeline and the `icebath model` wizard, pricing and token estimation, Relay-managed LLM calls, and the bodies of `icebath proxy`, `icebath moa`, `icebath usage`, `icebath migrate xai` plus the iron-proxy backend of `icebath egress`. On disk it owns `auth.json` and `auth.lock`, `provider_models_cache.json`, `models_dev_cache.json` with an `.etag` sidecar, `context_length_cache.yaml`, `ollama_cloud_models_cache.json`, `bws_cache*.json`, `op_cache.json`, several files under `cache/`, the machine-scoped `runtimes/llamacpp/` and `models/` trees, and `proxy/`. Entry points are called from `cmd/icebath`, `pkg/commands`, `pkg/agent`, `pkg/gateway*`, `pkg/tuiserver`, `pkg/tuihost`, `pkg/tools`, `pkg/plugins`, `pkg/profiles/manage` and `pkg/acp`. Port scaffolding is everywhere: function-variable "seams" standing in for Python module attributes that tests patch, Python `int()`/`float()`/`repr`/`json.dumps` reimplementations inlined per file, psutil, urllib, httpx, requests, botocore and difflib emulation, and `*_export.go` wrappers. Two subsystems are implemented but unreachable: the classic setup wizard sections and the tool-feature status report; the Hugging Face model browser of the local runtime and the left-core install backoff are also unwired.

#### Core route, request and transport types

The vocabulary every other group uses: a resolved route, the provider-neutral request and response, and one transport object per wire protocol that `pkg/agent` fetches with `GetTransport`.

- `types.go` — `APIMode`, `AuthKind`, `Route`, `Reasoning`, `Request`, `Response`, `Usage`, `StreamEvent`, the typed `Client` interface, `APIError` with retryable kinds and Retry-After, and the `RegisterFactory`/`NewClient` table keyed by wire protocol
- `transport.go` — `Transport` interface (convert messages and tools, build kwargs, normalize and validate a response, cache stats, finish reason) with built-ins for Anthropic Messages, Bedrock Converse, Responses and chat completions; chat transport remembers aliased tool names to reverse them
- `resolve.go` — `Credential` (key, token source, base URL, source label, owning pool) and the `CredentialSource` interface the resolver reads logins through
- `log.go` — package-named logger accessor

#### Provider profile contract and built-in table

A `Profile` is the whole description of one inference provider: about 65 data fields (base URL, env key names, aliases, wire mode, auth type, default and fallback models, hostnames, capabilities, Responses quirks, external-process command) and about 50 optional hook functions with default bodies. Everything provider-specific in request building, credential handling, catalogs and pickers is asked of a profile. This is unrelated to user profiles (separate icebath homes), which appear in this part as secret scopes, model seeding and distribution manifests.

- `profiles.go` — `Profile`, `IcebathOverlay` and `ModelsProbe` types, alias index per home, `NormalizeProvider`, `ProfileFor`, host helpers (loopback, official OpenAI host, host-mandated wire mode), `UserAgent` and attribution headers
- `profile_base.go` — default body of every profile hook (aux model, extra body, reasoning config, headers, max tokens, model listing, context length, usage cost, pool seeding, credential refresh) and `LazyHeaders`, an insertion-ordered header map with values computed on first read
- `profiles_table.go` — the 34 registry rows in auto-detection priority order, no-key placeholder constants, the `moa://local` virtual endpoint, Azure Foundry Responses-only detection, OpenCode Zen and Go family, per-model wire and relay URL healing
- `providers.go` — icebath overlays over models.dev provider ids, alias groups and label overrides, `GetProviderDef`, aggregator tests, wire-mode determination, the `llamacpp` provider definition, and `ResolveProviderFull` (user providers, registry, built-ins, custom, llamacpp, models.dev, profiles)
- `profiles_plugins.go` — [port-artifact] one-line `url.Parse` wrapper used by two callers

#### Provider plugin registry and hook dispatch

"Plugin" inside this package means a model-provider plugin: a directory that registers one or more profiles. The 38 bundled directories of the Python original are Go functions keyed by directory name; a user's own plugins under `<home>/plugins/model-providers/<name>/`, or any installed plugin whose manifest declares kind `model-provider`, are loaded as guests of the plugin host (`pkg/plugins`: a WebAssembly module or an external program, since Python plugin source is refused) and every overridden method runs there, addressed by its Python-era name. Registration is process-wide for bundled and runtime profiles and per home for user plugins, which shadow the process-wide ones.

- `registry.go` — bundled directory table, process-wide and per-home layers, lazy discovery, plugin directory mtime stamps with a rescan TTL, remembered misses, host-to-profile lookup, load-error record per plugin, registry generation counter for memo keys, mirror into the auth registry and picker catalog
- `plugins_bundled.go` — map from bundled directory name to its Go profile function, plus helpers hooks share: caller context carried in the hook map, reasoning config as map or ordered object, attribution headers
- `plugin_hosted_profiles.go` — builds a `Profile` from a plugin-host extraction: copies declared fields, installs a host call per overridden hook, converts verdicts, usage snapshots and costs, and wraps a host-side SDK client and its chunk iterator as a typed `Client`
- `provider_route_hooks.go` — `AskProfile`, `AskOnErrorPath` and `RouteAnswer`: call a named hook on the profile for a provider or for the base URL host, memoize pure answers, turn a panic into a fallback that sticks for the session scope, log once
- `provider_route_hooks_registry.go` — registry ids paired with their inference base URL in registry order, hidden rows omitted
- `pool_plugin.go` — credential hooks a plugin profile may ship (refresh, auth action handler, expiry test, terminal refresh error test, recovery after a failed refresh) and their lookup for the credential pool
- `plugin_entry_bridge.go` — [port-artifact] one-line forward to the plugin manager's entry-directory lookup

#### OAuth clients and signed-in requests for installed plugins

Lets a non-provider plugin use credentials without ever seeing them. A plugin manifest may declare `oauth` clients (authorize and token URLs, scopes, env variable names for client id and secret) and `requires_auth` providers; icebath runs the sign-in, stores grants under `plugin_oauth` in `auth.json`, and attaches the bearer only to declared HTTPS origins.

- `plugin_oauth.go` — manifest `oauth` block validation, admission problems and warnings for the plugin catalog, grant read, write, refresh and revocation keyed by plugin path and client fingerprint, granted-scope check, origin allowlist, and the `auth add|status|refresh|logout` actions for a plugin client
- `plugin_oauth_unattended.go` — reports a gateway, cron, single-query or unattended session where no terminal sign-in can run
- `plugin_provider_requests.go` — `CredentialedProviderRequest`: sends a plugin's request with the Codex sign-in attached (origins `chatgpt.com` and `api.openai.com`) or a plugin OAuth bearer; caller must be an installed plugin that declared the provider; no redirects, per-phase timeouts, errors detached from their chains

#### Runtime resolution: provider, credential and wire

Turns a requested provider name into a `Runtime` (provider, api mode, base URL, key or token source, headers, pool). Requested provider precedence: explicit argument, `model.provider`, `ICEBATH_INFERENCE_PROVIDER`, else `auto`. `auto` resolves to explicit endpoint arguments (OpenRouter), the config-pinned provider, an OpenRouter key, the first registry provider with an env key, the signed-in provider, AWS credentials (Bedrock), else a "not connected" error. The credential ladder is: name shortcuts (`moa`, Azure, Vertex), a named custom provider, a local endpoint in config, explicit key or URL, the credential pool (refusing when the selected login is unavailable), OAuth providers, external-process providers, Anthropic, Bedrock, registry API-key providers, then OpenRouter.

- `resolve_auto.go` — the `resolver` and `Runtime` types, both precedence ladders, api-mode detection per URL and per model, placeholder-key rejection, host-gated env key candidates, key-prefix checks, disabled-provider and missing-endpoint refusals, error formatting, and `ResolveRuntimeWithFallback` walking `fallback_providers` on a credential failure
- `resolve_azure.go` — Azure Foundry runtime (API key or per-request Entra token) and `AzureDetector`, which probes an endpoint for OpenAI versus Anthropic transport and its model list
- `resolve_local.go` — routes `auto` with a non-cloud `model.base_url` through the OpenAI-compatible resolver, Z.AI base URL choice, rate-limit-shaped auth error test
- `runtime_provider_backends.go` — OpenRouter and bare custom terminal rung, Bedrock runtime (Mantle Responses, Anthropic Messages or Converse by model id), external-process provider launch spec and command resolution from profile and env
- `home_credentials.go` — credential source for one home combining pool rows, auth-store logins and the signed-in provider; `HomePoolEnv` for callers outside the package
- `resolve_bridge.go` — canonical provider id that auth resolution picks for a requested name
- `runtime_fallback_export.go`, `runtime_readiness_export.go`, `tui_server_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers for gateway and TUI: resolve with fallback, named custom rung, runtime-has-credentials test, missing-credentials hint, routable-provider test, fallback entry key

#### Route identity, affinity and request timeouts

- `route_identity.go` — canonical base URL for route identity, whether a base URL is a provider's own endpoint, dropping `base_url` and `api_mode` left by a previous provider, deciding when a context-length pin no longer matches the route
- `routing_scope.go` — context values for the declared routing affinity scope and the conversation lineage root id
- `opencode_affinity.go` — rotation-stable conversation affinity key, `x-opencode-session` header for OpenCode targets, opt-in affinity header for custom providers
- `provider_timeouts.go` — `providers.<id>.request_timeout_seconds` and `stale_timeout_seconds` with per-model overrides under `models.<model>` (`timeout_seconds`, `stale_timeout_seconds`), `agent.api_timeout`, stale patience scaled by context size with reasoning-model floors, capped at half the remaining run budget

#### Credential pool and rotation

One pool per provider key (or `custom:<name>`), stored under `credential_pool` in `auth.json`. Rows are seeded from env keys, config, other tools' logins and plugin hooks, then selected by strategy (`fill_first`, `round_robin`, `random`, `least_used`). A failed row cools down: 5 minutes after 401, 1 hour after 429 or other errors, 1 minute when it is the only credential, 365 days for a per-model entitlement bench; terminal OAuth errors mark it dead, and dead manual rows are pruned after 24 hours.

- `pool.go` — `Pool` and `PoolEnv`, OAuth refresh under the cross-process store lock with adoption of a pair another process rotated, fail-closed quarantine when a rotated pair cannot be persisted, Claude Code credentials-file sync, Codex quota-restored probe throttled to 5 minutes
- `pool_entry.go` — `PooledCredential` row and its JSON form with borrowed secrets stripped, auth-type inference from token shape, labels from token claims, cooldown TTL rules, per-model cooldown maps
- `pool_select.go` — select, peek, reclaim, `MarkExhaustedAndRotate` (model-scoped bench versus whole-row exhaustion, siblings sharing a key), leases capped per credential, resync of rows another process reset, pool-wide and per-model limit state for pickers
- `pool_persist.go` — `LoadPool` with seeding from singletons, env and custom entries, suppression of removed sources, strategy from config, pool-key matching for custom providers, session-frozen config scope, `PoolCredentials` source for the resolver, explicit-configuration test per provider
- `pool_admin.go` — reset status, remove by index, reorder priorities, resolve a target by id, label or index, add an entry
- `pool_timestamps.go` — epoch seconds, milliseconds or ISO 8601 parsing, expiry-within-skew test, swappable pool clock
- `pool_key_source.go`, `xai_credential_pool_source.go` — pool readers the tool layer installs (`tools.PoolKeys`, `tools.CredentialPools`): default login key per provider, selected and force-refreshed xAI bearer

#### Named logins and login selection

A user-facing layer over pool rows: each row has a login name, account identity and rotation flag. Per provider, `logins.<provider>.default` (a login or `@rotate`), `.on_exhausted` (`fail` or `rotate`) and `.strategy` live in config; a session can pin its own login in its stored `model_config`. A pinned login never fails over to another account unless `on_exhausted` allows it.

- `logins.go` — list, find, add API key login, name, rename, remove with source-specific cleanup, set default, rotation membership, link an env variable or another tool's login, convert a linked key to an owned one
- `logins_selection.go` — session and profile login choice resolution, narrowing a pool to the chosen login or rotation set, typed "login unavailable" refusal, exhaustion events with reset time and ready alternatives, change stamp
- `logins_oauth.go` — background OAuth sign-in job for hosted clients (output buffer, prompt answer, cancel, snapshot) and the terminal variant, reusing the device-code and PKCE flows
- `xai_oauth_section_login.go`, `setup_tts_xai.go` — xAI Grok OAuth device sign-in stored as an owned login without becoming the active provider, for the TUI section and the tools setup hook
- `setup_qwen_device.go` — Qwen device-code sign-in that writes the Qwen CLI credentials file
- `qwen_auth_status_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported Qwen OAuth status

#### `auth.json` store

- `store.go` — `Store` for one home with the global root as read-only fallback: version 2 document (`providers`, `credential_pool`, `suppressed_sources`, `updated_at`), goroutine-reentrant process lock plus `auth.lock` file lock (15-second timeout, holder hint), corrupt-file quarantine, 0600 atomic writes, merge of concurrent disk rows, token generations and cooldowns on pool write
- `store_credential.go` — a provider's singleton login from `providers`
- `store_lock_{unix,windows}.go` — non-blocking exclusive flock or one-byte range lock, contention test, pid liveness (2 per-OS files)
- `store_tombstones.go` — records removed pool row ids so a stale writer cannot resurrect a deleted login, and prunes old records

#### Secret scope and multi-profile hosting

A process that serves more than one profile home (gateway, TUI server) is "multiplexed": credential reads must go through a per-profile mapping carried on the context, and an unscoped read fails closed with `UnscopedSecretError`. A scope is built from the profile `.env`, its external secret sources and the administrator-managed env, excluding process-wide names (`ICEBATH_KANBAN_*`, `ICEBATH_TELEGRAM_*`, `TERMINAL_*` and a fixed list).

- `secret_scope.go` — scope context values, multiplex flag and pinned launch home, `GetSecret`, global-name test, scope build and refresh
- `launch_profile_policy.go` — freezes the launch process env at first capture, activates multiplexing, launch-profile secret and `TERMINAL_*` overlays, wrappers that bind the launch profile scope only when multiplexed
- `launch_profile_policy_export.go` — [port-artifact] test-only reset of the frozen launch env
- `profile_secret_source.go` — installs the scope readers into `pkg/tools` at init, `ProfileSecretSource` for child environments and output redaction, `ToolRuntimeCredentials`

#### External secret sources

Pulls secrets from external stores into the environment at startup, once per home, in `secrets.sources` order. Sources are bulk (Bitwarden Secrets Manager, command helper) or mapped (1Password `op://` references), plus plugin-registered ones. Rules: a source may not overwrite protected names or its own token variable, values with non-ASCII characters are sanitized, each fetch has a wall-clock budget, results are cached in memory and on disk, and writes are tracked so they can be revoked.

- `secret_sources.go` — `SecretSource` interface and spec, error taxonomy from CLI text, `RunCLI`, ANSI scrub, two-layer cache (0600 file at the home root), source registry with global and per-scope layers, ordered apply with provenance and profile-suffixed alias mapping
- `secret_source_loader.go` — `ApplyExternalSecretSources` into the process env via a staging copy, `HydrateProfileSecretSources` into a private mapping, per-variable source attribution, revocation of stale writes, refusal to let a source supply the remote config backend's credential
- `secret_source_bitwarden.go` — `bws` binary lookup and install through PM, `bws secret list` per project, plaintext cache `bws_cache.json` replaced by AES-GCM `bws_cache.enc.json` keyed from the access token, stale entry served only after a transport failure
- `secret_source_onepassword.go` — `op read` per reference with an env allowlist, pinned binary path never falling back to PATH, cache `op_cache.json` keyed by auth and reference fingerprints, only complete pulls cached
- `secret_source_onepassword_exports.go` — [port-artifact] exported `op` stderr scrub and env allowlist for `pkg/browser`
- `secret_source_command.go` — `command` source: helper printing a `KEY=VALUE` blob, dotenv-style unquoting
- `secret_source_command_unix.go` — runs the helper through `/bin/sh -c` in its own session with a scrubbed child env, output cap and timeout that kills the process group
- `secret_source_command_windows.go` — [stub] always resolves no value; the helper contract is a POSIX shell command line, so the `command` source does nothing on Windows
- `secret_source_plugins.go` — adapts a plugin-host object as a `SecretSource`, the scoped registry handed to plugin services, and the lister and cache reset `cmd/icebath` installs
- `secret_sources_hub.go` — state, setup, token rotation, preview and disable operations for Bitwarden and 1Password as the TUI server calls them, without console output
- `secret_source_attribution_export.go` — [port-artifact] test-only attribution setter

#### `icebath secrets` command

`icebath secrets bitwarden|bw` (`setup`, `status`, `token`, `sync [--apply]`, `disable`, `install [--force]`) and `icebath secrets onepassword|op|1password` (`setup`, `status`, `token`, `set`, `remove`, `sync [--apply]`, `disable`). Tokens are stored in the home `.env`; `sync` is a dry run unless `--apply`.

- `subcommands_secrets.go` — parser tree with both integrations, argparse-style help, `SecretsCommand` dispatch
- `secrets_common.go` — shared CLI state, subcommand registration, status panel and table printing, CLI version probe, token rotation with verification, enable-required guard, disable
- `secrets_cli.go` — Bitwarden handlers: four-step setup wizard (binary, token, region or self-hosted URL, project pick), status with token validation, project listing with region or token diagnosis
- `onepassword_secrets_cli.go` — 1Password handlers: setup, reference mapping under `secrets.onepassword`, `op whoami` verification, sync

#### Managed llama.cpp runtime: engine, boot and supervision

Icebath's own local model server: one `llama-server` in router mode per machine, shared by all profiles. Engines are PM packages `llamacpp-{cuda,vulkan,metal,hip,cpu}`; backend `auto` picks metal on macOS, cuda for NVIDIA, vulkan for AMD or Intel, else cpu. Config section `local_runtime` (`enabled`, `backend`, `models_max` default 4, `port`, `detect_ports`). State lives under `<root>/runtimes/llamacpp/` (`server.json`, `.api_key`, `presets.ini`, `boot.lock`, `window_overrides.json`) with logs in `<root>/logs/llama-server.log`.

- `local_runtime_binaries.go` — backend resolution against PM pins, installed-engine lookup, explicit install through PM with progress and pause, one-time adoption of pre-PM installs from `runtimes/llamacpp/b*/<backend>/` verified by manifest digests
- `local_runtime_bootstrap.go` — `EnsureLocalRuntime`: staged GGUF listing in `<root>/models` (split files need every part), migration of per-profile model dirs, cross-process boot lock, replacing a server with stale presets, residency cap, idle sweeper every 120 seconds and window re-plan every 30
- `local_runtime_supervisor.go` — `LlamaServerSupervisor`: spawn on 127.0.0.1 port 18434 (ephemeral if taken) with a persistent API key, health wait, crash restart backoff of 1, 5, 15, 60 seconds, model load, unload and preset reload, 15-minute idle unload, readiness proof by a temperature-zero touch generation
- `local_runtime_supervisor_{posix,windows}.go` — port bind without address reuse, live pid enumeration, boot-file lock (2 per-OS files)
- `local_runtime_supervisor_reap.go` — kills processes running the engine binary whose parent is gone; never on Windows
- `local_runtime_recovery.go` — reads `server.json` and matches the recorded server and owner to live processes by pid plus start time and executable, so another process can route to it or stop an orphan; legacy records matched by launch arguments
- `local_runtime_processes.go` — strips variables whose names contain credential markers from the server's environment
- `local_runtime_processes_{posix,windows}.go` — spawn in its own process group under the owner-death supervisor, or suspended inside a kill-on-close job object
- `local_runtime_psproc.go`, `local_runtime_psproc_{bsd,darwin,linux,posix,windows}.go` — [py-shim] `psutil.Process` stand-in (create time as incarnation identity, parent, children, cmdline, terminate, kill, wait) with per-OS backends; the supervisor and recovery code depend on it

#### Managed llama.cpp runtime: hardware budget

Measures what the machine can hold so models are priced before download and launch.

- `local_runtime_hardware.go` — `ProbeBudget` and `LaunchBudget`: RAM from `/proc/meminfo`, `sysctl` and `vm_stat` or `GlobalMemoryStatusEx`; VRAM from `nvidia-smi` (cached 4 seconds), the CUDA driver, or the engine's `--list-devices`; unified-memory detection with 20 percent headroom, Windows commit room and prompt-cache sizing
- `local_runtime_hardware_{other,windows}.go` — Windows memory status call and hidden console window, no-ops elsewhere
- `local_runtime_devices.go` — lists GPU devices by loading the engine's ggml libraries in a child: at package init the icebath binary re-executes itself when argv[1] is `__icebath_ggml_devices__` and prints the devices as JSON
- `local_runtime_native_{dl,other,windows}.go` — shared-library open, symbol lookup and calls through purego or Windows DLL loading; the fallback file refuses on platforms without a loader binding
- `local_runtime_native_cstring.go` — reads a NUL-terminated C string at a returned address

#### Managed llama.cpp runtime: model facts, context policy and presets

Decides the context window and launch flags per model from its GGUF header and the hardware budget. Every model is guaranteed a 64K floor; windows grow by 1.5x rungs up to the trained context; a model is refused only when weights plus floor KV exceed VRAM plus RAM.

- `local_runtime_gguf.go` — GGUF header reader summed across split parts: architecture, layer and head counts, sliding-window pattern, vocab, sampling defaults, lazy tensor bytes; split-part naming regex and model id from a file stem
- `local_runtime_estimator.go` — `ModelProfile` and `HardwareBudget`, KV bytes per token by layer kind (full, sliding window, recurrent), q8 versus f16 KV factor, footprint estimate and `PhysicsCheck`
- `local_runtime_context_policy.go` — window ladder, initial window (largest zero-spill rung), prefill posture, fit to free memory, end-of-turn growth verdict (85 percent occupancy, idle, 6 tokens per second floor), spill overrides moving FFN weights to host, per-model launch flags
- `local_runtime_presets.go` — plans every staged model and writes `presets.ini` atomically at 0600 with a decision comment per model; companion files (vision projector, MTP head, DFlash draft), residency count, read-back of the decisions the running server was given
- `local_runtime_growth.go` — `MaybeGrowWindow`, called by the agent loop before compression: records the next window in `window_overrides.json`, restarts the server and confirms the grant; `ClearWindowOverride` has no caller

#### Managed llama.cpp runtime: catalog, downloads and the Local models flow

The curated model list and the job machinery that installs an engine, downloads a model and makes it the default. The exported `LocalModels*` handlers are written as HTTP-route bodies for a dashboard pane, but the only caller is the terminal flow reached from `icebath model` (Local models row).

- `local_runtime_catalog.json` — [data] schema version 3, five model families with repo, quant variants and exact file sizes, layer facts for the estimator, projector, draft and MTP head companions, sampling defaults, minimum engine build; embedded by `local_runtime_catalog.go`
- `local_runtime_catalog.go` — catalog parsing, variant fit per machine, predicted decode speed from measured baselines or memory bandwidth, recommended entry above a 20 tokens-per-second floor, background refresh from `icebath.app/api/local-runtime-catalog.json` every 6 hours
- `local_models.go` — status, hardware and priced-catalog payloads; job registry with phases, rate and ETA, pause; resumable Hugging Face downloads through PM; `quickstart` (engine, model, default), `runtime install`, `activate`; writes `local_runtime.enabled` and assigns the main model
- `model_setup_flows_local.go` — terminal flow: machine and engine summary, model pick with recommended marker, download confirmation, live progress line with Ctrl-C pausing a download
- `local_runtime_hf_browse.go` — [unwired] Hugging Face GGUF repo search, per-repo quant listing with split parts collapsed, and coarse fit verdicts, behind a 5-minute cache; wired into the route dependency table but no route uses it (two text helpers are reused elsewhere)

#### Managed llama.cpp runtime: endpoint, capabilities and progress

- `local_runtime_endpoint.go` — resolves the `llamacpp`, `llama.cpp`, `llama-cpp` aliases: the managed server from `server.json` first, else a detected server; kicks a background boot and waits up to 8 seconds when the runtime is enabled with an engine installed
- `local_runtime_detect.go` — probes 127.0.0.1 port 8080 and configured ports for a running `llama-server` via `/props`, then `/models` to learn whether it is a router
- `local_runtime_capabilities.go` — whether a provider and URL are the managed server, vision capability from the loaded child's props, else whether the catalog entry's projector file is on disk, accepted image types (PNG, JPEG)
- `local_runtime_load_progress.go` — follows the router's `/models/sse` stream to report per-model load stage and composite percent, and reads prompt prefill progress from `/slots`
- `local_prompt_progress.go` — asks llama-server for prompt-progress chunks and clocks time spent reading the prompt

#### Model catalogs: listing, caching and other local servers

Answers "which models does this provider offer". `ProviderModelIDs` tries a provider-specific live fetcher, then the profile's fetch hook or generic `/models` listing, then the curated static list merged with models.dev. Results are cached per provider in `provider_models_cache.json` keyed by a credential fingerprint: fresh for 1 hour, served stale up to 7 days with a background refresh, curated fallbacks for 60 seconds.

- `model-catalog.json` — [data] manifest version 1 with one provider (`openrouter`, 75 curated ids with picker descriptions and a `default` marker); embedded by `catalog_list.go` in the other part and refreshed from `model_catalog.url`
- `models.go` — static catalogs, silent default model per provider, `provider:model` input parsing, provider detection ladder for a bare model name, per-provider fetchers (Codex, Anthropic, OpenAI, custom, Bedrock, Azure Foundry, StepFun), disk cache with stale-while-revalidate, `/models` probe at base and `/v1` with a 60-second negative memo
- `models_fetch.go` — OpenRouter curated list filtered live by tool support and free pricing (disk `cache/openrouter_curated_catalog.json`), Vercel AI Gateway list, DeepInfra catalog by surface tag, effort clamping to supported levels
- `models_dev.go` — models.dev registry client: `models_dev_cache.json` at the home root with ETag, 4-hour freshness, 15-second fetch cap, 5-minute failure backoff, corrupt-cache quarantine; capability, context, cost and provider lookups patched by `model_overrides` config and plugin declarations; noise and hidden-model filters
- `models_local.go` — Ollama (`OLLAMA_HOST`, default `localhost:11434`, native `/api/tags` and `/api/show`), LM Studio (native model list, cold load with a target context, published reasoning options), Ollama Cloud list cached an hour in `ollama_cloud_models_cache.json`; carries its own BLAKE2b
- `models_detect.go` — whether the current provider's cached catalog or vendor already owns a model name; `ProviderHasCredentials`
- `models_cache_lock.go` — thread lock plus cross-process lock for the provider models cache file
- `models_fileid_{darwin,unix,windows}.go` — inode and change time (file index and creation time on Windows) for the cache fingerprint
- `models_profile_cache.go` — generic per-home slot for an in-process catalog cache
- `models_seams.go` — [port-artifact] function variables bound at init so tests can replace catalog, detection and cache functions

#### Model names: normalization, search, validation and selection guards

- `model_normalize.go` — rewrites a model name for a target provider: vendor prefix for aggregators, dots to hyphens for Anthropic, prefix stripping, retired DeepSeek aliases, catalogue-based prefix repair, profile hook first
- `model_normalize_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported aggregator-provider test
- `model_search.go` — extra search tokens and canonical slugs for bare wire ids, used for picker search and dedup only

#### Model switch pipeline

The shared engine behind `/model` in the CLI, TUI and gateway, and behind startup model resolution. Flags: `--provider`, `--reasoning`, `--login`, `--global`, `--session`, `--once`, `--refresh`, and the word `reset`. A switch routes the text, resolves credentials for the target, validates the model, derives the wire mode and returns capabilities, warnings and config updates.

- `model_switch_parse.go` — flag and argument parsing (Unicode dashes tolerated), conflict error copy, persist rule (`--global`, no configured model, or `model.persist_switch_by_default`), effective model from session, channel and global config
- `model_switch.go` — short family aliases (`sonnet`, `opus`, `gpt`, `grok` and others) resolved against live catalogs, direct aliases from `model.aliases` with their own endpoint and key, session-credential reuse rule (same origin, https or loopback), `ResolveStartupModelRoute`
- `model_switch_alias.go` — alias resolution with version-aware sort and ambiguity error, external-process model aliases, authenticated-provider fallback, configured-provider matching, display context length
- `model_switch_route.go` — routing steps: explicit provider, MoA presets, vendor-colon slugs, configured provider declarations, detection; credential resolution for a changed or unchanged provider; wire-mode choice
- `model_switch_apply.go` — `SwitchModel`, validation with config-declared models accepted, model-derived api mode, config update list, `PersistModelSelection` under the config lock preserving YAML aliases, refusal when an upper config level locks a model key
- `model_switch_providers.go` — `ListAuthenticatedProviders` and `ListPickerProviders`: built-in providers with credentials, user `providers` entries and custom endpoints with live or declared models, discovered models written back to config, background cache prewarm

#### Context length and remote model metadata

`GetModelContextLength` resolves a window in this order: explicit config value, MoA member walk, `model_overrides` and custom provider entries, endpoint-scoped table, profile hook, persisted cache, Bedrock probe, endpoint metadata, Anthropic models API, provider-aware sources (profile live catalog, Codex catalog, Ollama show, OpenRouter metadata, models.dev), local server probe, family table, then 256,000 with a one-time warning. Minimum usable context is 64,000.

- `metadata.go` — family default table with longest-key matching, provider prefix stripping, host-to-provider inference, local endpoint tests, reasoning-support predicates for Grok and OpenAI models, context and pricing extraction from model payloads
- `metadata_resolve.go` — the resolver, validation and repair of persisted entries (known 32K under-reports), Bedrock path with a 5-minute failed-probe memo, custom endpoint path
- `metadata_probe.go` — probe client sharing chat TLS policy, OpenRouter models metadata fetch, endpoint `/models` metadata, Ollama `/api/show`, LM Studio and llama.cpp `/props` context reads, Anthropic context query, server-type waterfall (LM Studio, Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM)

#### Relay-managed LLM calls

"Relay" is an optional native runtime binding (`tools.NemoRelay`, loaded by `pkg/relayhost`) that observes and can intercept tool and LLM calls. When a session runs managed execution, each provider attempt is wrapped as a Relay call with a codec for its wire.

- `relay_llm.go` — `RelayExecute`, managed stream wrapper, codec selection per api mode, request and response conversion, error recording, logical-call completion, Anthropic message rebuild from intercepted SSE events; carries async-generator emulation from the Python original

#### `icebath proxy`: subscription proxy

A local OpenAI-compatible HTTP server (default `127.0.0.1:8645`) that lets other tools use an icebath-managed subscription: the client sends any bearer, the proxy attaches the real credential from the pool and forwards to the upstream. Only the xAI Grok OAuth upstream exists.

- `proxy_cli.go` — `icebath proxy start [--provider xai] [--host] [--port]` in the foreground, `status`, and `providers` (alias `list`); a bare call prints short help

- `proxy_sse_done.go` — scans forwarded SSE chunks to decide whether a terminal `[DONE]` frame must be appended after a clean end

#### iron-proxy backend of `icebath egress`

Manages the external `iron-proxy` binary as an egress firewall that swaps sandbox-visible proxy tokens for real provider credentials on allowlisted hosts. State under `<home>/proxy/` (`ca.crt`, `ca.key`, `proxy.yaml`, `mappings.json`, `management.token`, `iron-proxy.pid`), plus an audit log at a path the CLI passes in. The CLI is in the other part; `pkg/tools` declares a hook for sandboxes to consume the proxy, but nothing assigns it.

- `iron_proxy.go` — binary lookup and PM install, CA generation by shelling out to `openssl` (4096-bit RSA, 10 years), token minting, `proxy.yaml` generation with allowed hosts and denied upstream CIDRs, mapping discovery from env names, daemon start with a credentials-free allowlisted env, optional fresh Bitwarden secrets, reload through the management API, stop, status
- `iron_proxy_{unix,windows}.go` — no-follow file open, owner check, daemon detach and terminate (2 per-OS files)

MoA is a virtual provider `moa` whose "models" are named presets: several reference models answer first and an aggregator model produces the turn. This part owns only the config, presets and CLI; orchestration is in `pkg/agent`.

- `moa_config.go` — normalizes the `moa` config block into named presets (reference slots, aggregator, temperatures, reference timeout, fan-out, degraded-reference policy), default preset, preset lookup, decoding of the hidden one-shot `__ICEBATH_MOA_TURN_V1__` marker, `ParseReasoningEffort`
