## 5. Tool runtime

### `pkg/tools` — agent tool runtime: registry and toolsets, dispatch, approvals, execution backends, terminal and background processes, file and web tools, checkpoints, worktrees

*396 files, 131,524 Go lines*

One flat package of 396 files that is both the tool runtime and a dumping ground inherited from the Python `tools/` module. The runtime part is the `Def`/`Call`/`Env` types and the process-wide registry with its scoping and availability layer, the toolset table and the `icebath tools` configurator, the Tool Search bridge, the dispatcher and executor that `pkg/agent` drives, the tool-loop guardrails, the dangerous-command approval system, every terminal execution backend (local, Docker or Podman, SSH, Modal, Daytona, Vercel Sandbox, Singularity or Apptainer) on one shared shell-snapshot engine, the background process registry, the shadow-git checkpoint store behind `/rollback`, secret redaction and result spill storage. The model-callable tools registered here are `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files`, `terminal`, `process_manage`, `web_search`, `web_extract`, `x_search`, `vision_analyze`, `video_analyze`, `session_search`, `todo_list`, `desktop_project`, `clarify`, `manage_connections`, `delegate_task`, `discord`, `discord_admin`, `feishu_doc_read`, four `feishu_drive_*` tools and the three synthetic bridge tools `tool_search`, `tool_describe` and `tool_call`; other tools are registered from `pkg/browser`, `pkg/codeexec`, `pkg/media`, `pkg/memory`, `pkg/skills`, `pkg/cron`, `pkg/kanban`, `pkg/mcp` and the platform and built-in plugin packages. Unrelated subsystems parked here include self-update git repair, Windows `schtasks` helpers, Bot Chat relay helpers, the emergency stop, git worktree management, projects, the NeMo Relay integration and the child-process environment factory used by the whole application. Port scaffolding is heavy: 36 `*_export.go` shims, ports of Python `difflib`, `tomllib`, libyaml, `ddgs`, `lxml`, `httpx`, `requests`, `ElementTree` and Pillow, and dozens of hook variables other packages assign at init. The product logic is implemented and wired; the dead spots are named in the groups.

**Files `acp_*` through `lsp_*`** (171 files, 62,750 Go lines). This part holds the core of the tool runtime: the `Def`/`Call`/`Env` types and the process-wide registry, the dispatcher and executor that `pkg/agent` drives, the tool-loop guardrails, the dangerous-command approval system, every terminal execution backend (local, Docker/Podman, SSH, Modal, Daytona, Vercel Sandbox, Singularity/Apptainer) on one shared shell-snapshot engine, the shadow-git checkpoint store behind `/rollback`, and the file tools with their fuzzy matcher, lint and LSP checks. Model-callable tools registered in these files are `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files`, `clarify`, `manage_connections`, `delegate_task`, `discord`, `discord_admin`, `feishu_doc_read` and four `feishu_drive_*` tools; everything else is helper code. Under the profile home it owns `checkpoints/`, the `async_delegations` table of `state.db`, the `ESTOP` sentinel, `command_allowlist` in config, `modal_snapshots.json`, `vercel_sandbox_snapshots.json`, `sandboxes/`, `cache/blocked-scripts/`, `cache/terminal-output/`, `cache/terminal/`, `cache/discord_capabilities.json` and `.sync.lock`, plus `bot_relay/locks/` under the install root. The directory is also a dumping ground inherited from the Python `tools/` module: self-update git repair, Windows `schtasks` helpers, Bot Chat relay helpers, the coding-posture prompt and the child-process environment factory used by the whole application all live here. Port scaffolding is heavy (17 `*_export.go` shims plus `doctor_exports.go`, ports of Python `difflib`, `tomllib`, libyaml and `json`, and about 35 hook variables that other packages assign at init), but the product logic is implemented and wired and nothing here is a stub. The dead spots found are the Docker egress-proxy hook that nothing installs, the `plugin` and `skill` connector kinds that nothing creates, one kanban guard with no caller, and a handful of exports only tests use.

#### Tool registry, call types and dispatch pipeline

Each tool file calls `Register(Def{...})` from `init` to fill the process-wide `Default` registry. `Dispatcher.DispatchWith` is the single path a call takes outside the agent loop: schema-driven argument coercion, legacy alias mapping (`todo`, `cronjob`, `process`), unwrapping of the `tool_search`/`tool_describe`/`tool_call` bridge, relay intercepts and request middleware, plugin `pre_tool_call` hooks (block, approve via the approval gate, or modify args), the ACP edit-approval guard, execution middleware, the handler with panic-to-JSON-error recovery, then `post_tool_call` and `transform_tool_result` hooks. The four `AgentLoopTools` (`todo_list`, `memory`, `session_search`, `delegate_task`) are refused here because the agent loop must run them with live agent state.

- `def.go` — `Def` (name, toolset, schema, handler, availability check, required env, emoji, result cap, dynamic schema, timeout, plugin), `Call`, per-session `Env`, `Aux`, `Asker` form types, `Registry`, JSON result helpers
- `incomplete.go` — package `init` that registers the file, web, vision, todo, clarify, session-search and project tool families and the checkpoint git timeout in a fixed order; despite the name nothing in it is unfinished
- `dispatch.go` — `Dispatcher` with hook and middleware slices, `DispatchWith`, `HandleFunctionCall` (used by the `execute_code` RPC), alias table, `SanitizeToolError` (strips framing tags, 2,048-character cap), `manage_connections` availability gate
- `coercion.go` — repairs model-emitted args against the JSON Schema: JSON strings into arrays and objects, numeric and boolean strings, nulls, local `$ref` resolution, sanitized key names mapped back to wire names
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `tools`

#### Tool-call executor, interrupts and result budgets

`Executor` runs one assistant turn's tool calls for `pkg/agent` through the `ExecutorHost` interface: sequentially, concurrently (at most 8 workers; `image_generate` capped by `image_gen.max_parallel_requests`, default 4) or as planned parallel and sequential segments. A start-order gate makes prompts appear in call order, and an authorization gate serializes policy prompts and excludes human wait time from the deadlines `timeouts.tools.concurrent_batch` and `timeouts.tools.sequential_call` (`delegate_task` and `manage_connections` supervise themselves and are exempt from the sequential deadline). Before dispatch it refuses calls whose arguments carry a context-compression marker, asks the guardrail controller, fires progress callbacks and takes checkpoints for `write_file`, `patch` and destructive `terminal` commands; after dispatch it classifies failure, spills oversized results to disk, wraps untrusted output, appends the tool message, flushes to the session DB and enforces the per-turn budget. Interrupts are per worker so stopping one session never kills another session's tools, and every skipped, timed-out or abandoned call still gets a synthetic result message.

- `executor.go` — `Executor`, `ExecutorHost`, `ExecuteToolCallsSequential`, `ExecuteToolCallsConcurrent`, `ExecuteToolCallsSegmented`, `StartOrderGate`, `AuthorizationGate`, inline executors for agent-level tools, 30-second activity heartbeats, keyboard-interrupt handling, result commit
- `executor_invoke_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports `InvokeTool` (no non-test caller) and `RunTaskList`, the `todo_list` entry point `pkg/agent` calls
- `executor_begin_export.go`, `inline_executor_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exported wrappers of the pre-execution step and the inline-executor lookup; no non-test caller
- `budget.go` — result persistence budgets: 100,000 characters per result, 200,000 per turn, 1,500 preview, 50,000 for `mcp_*` tools (`tool_budget.mcp_result_size_chars`), scaled to 15% and 30% of the context window; `read_file` is pinned unlimited
- `compression_marker.go` — the context-compression elision marker text (legacy HERMES spelling still recognised) and the `Elide`/`ElideMiddle` truncation helpers used by the compressor, skills and verification code
- `interrupt.go` — per-worker interrupt bits with a user-safe reason, acting-for links for deadline workers, and the yield request that hands a foreground command to the background instead of killing it
- `finite_turn.go` — records on the session env that the admitted turn is finite (treated as single-query for approvals) or finite and unattended (approvals pass without a prompt)
- `daemon_pool.go` — [py-shim] bounded worker pool with futures standing in for Python's `ThreadPoolExecutor` on daemon threads; used by async delegation and the agent's compression timeout

#### Tool-loop guardrails, batch planning and result framing

One 2,200-line file holding several policies the agent loop consults every turn. The guardrail controller counts per-turn repeats by a hash of tool name plus canonical args and warns or halts on exact repeated failures (warn 2, block 5), same-tool failures (warn 3, halt 8) and idempotent no-progress calls (warn 2, block 5), configured under `tool_loop_guardrails`; hard stops are off by default on attended surfaces and forced on for gateway and cron sessions. It also caps web searches and subagent spawns at 50 each per turn, notes the third consecutive identical call and repeating cycles of up to four calls, and replaces byte-identical duplicate results of 512 characters or more with a reference stub.

- `guardrails.go` — the controller above; tool classification tables (read-only, mutating, idempotent, failure-tolerant, parallel-safe, never-parallel); `PlanToolBatchSegments` (parallel only when reserved paths do not overlap); `ValidateToolCalls` (name repair and strike rules); `tool_call` batch expansion (10 entries); tool-call id normalization; untrusted-result wrapping for `web_*`, `browser_*` and `mcp_*` output; provider elision notices; `IsDestructiveCommand`

#### Command approval policy: detection, floors, modes and grants

What needs approval: a `terminal` command matching one of 110 `DangerousPatterns` regexes (recursive deletes, world-writable chmod, SQL drops, pipe-to-shell, secret upload by curl or wget, writes to system, credential, shell-rc and project `.env`/`config.yaml` files, git force push and hard reset, gateway self-termination, Docker daemon redirects, package uninstalls, invisible Unicode), an `execute_code` script on gateway surfaces, writes to approval-gated paths, and any tool a plugin hook escalates. `CheckAllCommandGuards` evaluates in this order: isolated container backends skip everything except `approvals.deny`; unconditional floors (12 hardline patterns, deleting the running runtime, `sudo -S` without `SUDO_PASSWORD`, oversized or unparseable commands, `approvals.deny` globs) block even under yolo; then bypass by `ICEBATH_YOLO_MODE`, session `/yolo`, an unattended finite turn or `approvals.mode: off`; then `command_allowlist` (exact text or glob, never for compound commands); then session grants; then, when no human can answer, the unattended policy (`approvals.single_query_mode`, `approvals.cron_mode`, `approvals.unattended_mode`): the command runs unless the matching mode is `deny`; otherwise the human gate, preceded in `smart` mode by an auxiliary-model guardian whose consecutive denials trip a circuit breaker (`approvals.denial_breaker_threshold`). Answers are `once`, `session`, `always` or `deny`: `session` lives in memory per session key, `always` is merged into `command_allowlist` in the profile config, and a timeout or undeliverable prompt is a denial. The mode is `manual`, `smart` or `off`, and a hosted-room execution policy can override it.

- `approval.go` — per-session approval state, gateway queue registry, permanent allowlist load and save, yolo flags, the shared human-decision engine with its three gate wordings (command, code, action), `CheckAllCommandGuards`, `CheckExecuteCodeGuard`, `RequestToolApproval`, `RunApprovalGate`, the container-guard skip (Modal, Daytona, Vercel, flagged plugin backends, and Docker only without host mounts), runtime self-delete detection, dry-run `EvaluateCommand`
- `approval_context.go` — decides who can answer: interactive CLI, gateway session, cron, single-query, unattended platforms (`webhook`, `msgraph_webhook`, `api_server`), delegated child; reads modes and `approvals.timeout`; fires `pre_approval_request` and `post_approval_response` plugin hooks
- `approval_detection.go` — hardline and dangerous pattern tables plus a quote-aware shell scanner that normalizes commands (escapes, full-width forms, home spellings, `bash -c`, `env -S`, command substitution, grep operands) into variants before matching; parser limits of 128,000 characters and 25,000 segments
- `approval_floors.go` — `approvals.deny` glob matching over deobfuscated variants, hardline and sudo block messages, saving a parser-limit command to `cache/blocked-scripts/blocked-*.sh` (kept 7 days), allowlist shortcut rules
- `approval_smart.go` — guardian call on the auxiliary model (`approval` task, 16 tokens, `auxiliary.approval.timeout`) answering APPROVE, DENY or ESCALATE, with operator rules from `approvals.smart_policy`; shell comments are stripped first
- `approval_yolo.go` — session yolo toggle, persistence through the surface's own persister, restore in a fresh process, launch seeding for gateway sessions, transfer to a continuation session id
- `approval_mode_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports mode normalization for the gateway and TUI server

#### Approval surfaces: prompts, plugin transports, gateway queue, editor edits

A pending approval reaches a human by one of four routes. Local sessions use the session `Asker` (one question with once, session, always and deny choices) or an `ApprovalCallbackAsker`, falling back to a stdin menu with localized strings. Gateway, API and TUI-server sessions append an `ApprovalEntry` with a random request id to the session's FIFO queue, call the notifier the front end registered with `RegisterGatewayNotify` (gateway turn runner, API server runs, TUI server, managed worker), and block until `ResolveGatewayApproval` (called by the `/approve` and `/deny` slash commands, the gateway's pending-control handler, the Telegram, Teams, WhatsApp Cloud, QQ Bot and Google Chat adapters, the relay adapter, the API run routes and the TUI server) answers, the session closes, the turn is interrupted or the timeout passes; identical concurrent requests coalesce onto one prompt, reconnecting clients can list, acknowledge and replay entries, and with no notifier the tool returns a `pending_approval` result telling the model to stop and wait. `security.approval.transport` can instead name a plugin-registered transport whose decision must echo the request id and digest before the deadline, with `security.approval.transport_fallback: builtin` the only way a transport failure does not deny. ACP editors approve `write_file` and `patch` calls as a diff proposal.

- `approval_prompt.go` — terminal and asker prompts, plugin transport host (8 workers, request digest validation), MCP elicitation consent (`RequestElicitationConsent`, used by `pkg/mcp` and the browser vault), display sanitizing that shows hidden and bidirectional characters as escapes
- `approval_wait.go` — blocking gateway wait with coalescing and settle hooks, withdrawal causes, and per-session accounting of seconds spent waiting on a human (capped at the timeout plus 60) that the executor subtracts from deadlines
- `acp_edit_approval.go` — builds an `EditProposal` (old text, new text, every touched path, including V4A patches) and applies the auto-approve policy `ask`, `workspace_session` or `session`; `.git`, `.ssh`, `.env` and key files always ask
- `editor_edit_approval.go` — waits on the session's gateway approval queue for one editor edit; only a one-time grant approves
- `approval_display_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports approval-text redaction (gateway and ACP) and the resolved flag of a clarify entry (gateway pending controls)

#### `icebath approvals` command and allowlist mining

CLI behind `icebath approvals suggest` and `icebath approvals test`, also reachable as a gateway slash command.

- `approvals_command.go` — `suggest` (options `--days`, `--min-count`, `--limit`, `--apply 1,3`, `--json`, `--db`) and `test` (`--env-type`, `--json`, exit 0 allow, 2 ask, 3 deny) with the normalized variants the detectors saw
- `approval_suggest.go` — mines `state.db` for dangerous-classified terminal commands that ran with consent, derives narrow globs, never proposes destructive classes or root binaries such as `rm`, `sudo`, `kill`, and merges chosen entries into `command_allowlist`

#### Gateway lifecycle guard

Blocks the agent from stopping, restarting or killing the gateway that hosts it, which would cause respawn loops under launchd or systemd. The terminal tool, `execute_code` and the cron scheduler call it.

- `lifecycle_guard.go` — token-aware detection of `icebath gateway stop|restart|uninstall`, `launchctl` and `systemctl` actions on the gateway label, `pkill`/`killall`/`taskkill` aimed at the gateway or the host executable, and `launchctl submit|bootstrap`, with data-argument exemptions
- `lifecycle_scan.go` — follows scripts a command executes (depth 8, 1 MiB per file, 1,024 paths, 64 remote reads) and fails closed on unreadable, binary or cloud-synced scripts; `CheckGatewayLifecycle` refuses cron jobs containing such commands

#### Emergency stop

`icebath pause [reason]` writes a JSON sentinel `ESTOP` in the profile home (the fleet root sentinel is also honoured) and `icebath resume` removes it. While engaged, cron dispatch, kanban dispatch, goal loops and new gateway turns are held; in-flight work continues. A stat error counts as engaged.

- `estop.go` — sentinel path, `Engage`, `Disengage`, `IsEngaged`, `GetState`, `PausedReply` for new gateway turns, `CheckPaused` with one log line per component per engagement
- `estop_command.go` — the `pause` and `resume` command bodies

#### Execution backend contract and shared shell engine

`Environment` is one terminal backend instance and `BackendProvider` describes and creates one; built-in providers register under reserved names and plugins add more through `RegisterTerminalBackend`. Selection from `terminal.backend` and the per-backend config shaping live in `terminal_backends.go` and `terminal_config.go` in the other part. `baseEnv` gives every backend the same contract: a login-shell bootstrap captures env, functions and aliases into a per-session snapshot file, each command runs in a fresh `bash` that sources the snapshot, changes directory, runs, dumps env again and prints cwd and `PIPESTATUS` markers, so cwd and exports persist across calls without a long-lived shell. It also provides timeouts with a wall-clock backstop and tree kill, interrupt and yield-to-background handling, bounded output capture, stdin by pipe, heredoc or staged file, sudo password piping, base64 file fetch, exec streams and loopback port forwarding into sandboxes.

- `backend.go` — `Environment`, `BackendProvider`, `ExecOptions`, `ExecResult`, `ProcessHandle`, `CreateOptions`, `DoctorCheck`, the built-in and plugin backend registries, POSIX `shlex` quote and split helpers
- `environment_base.go` — `baseEnv` snapshot and wrapper scripts, `Execute`, wait loop, 40/60 head-tail output window bounded by `tool_output.max_bytes` with a spill file under `cache/terminal-output` (5,000,000 characters, pruned after 7 days), `SandboxDir`, JSON snapshot stores, `RunIn`, `OpenStream`, `ForwardPort`, exit fence that kills live foreground commands
- `environment_base_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS store-file lock, stat identity, console hiding, terminating-signal lookup and timed pipe reads
- `environment_ctime_{bsd,linux}.go` — per-OS change-time field of a stat result
- `backend_remote_common.go` — captured CLI runs with timeout for the docker, ssh and apptainer clients, profile `.env` passthrough values and the `unset` prefix for scoped names
- `backend_teardown.go` — runs backend cleanups on tracked workers and joins them at shutdown
- `backend_tiers.go` — names the build tier that carries a backend missing from this binary (`icebath_core` builds link only `local`) and runs scratch sweeps at exit

#### Local backend and the child-process environment factory

The local backend runs commands on the host in their own session and process group. The same file holds the factory every subprocess in the application goes through (`BuildSubprocessEnv`, `IcebathSubprocessEnv`, `ServedProfileChildEnv`, `HostGatewayChildEnv`): it strips provider credentials and platform secrets from children in two tiers (platform and dashboard secrets always, provider credentials unless the caller asks to inherit them), re-admits names a skill registered or `terminal.env_passthrough` lists, bridges `ICEBATH_HOME` and twenty session-context variables (`ICEBATH_SESSION_*`, `ICEBATH_CRON_*`), removes supervisor identity, kanban worker identity and platform authorization gates, and fails closed on unscoped secret reads when one gateway process multiplexes several profiles.

- `backend_local.go` — `localEnv` (bash lookup, Git Bash path handling on Windows, cwd recovery, shell init files, sane PATH with managed Node and the icebath bin dir), secret tiers and scrub rules, session-context bridging, routed-profile env stripping, terminal temp cache prune after 24 idle hours
- `backend_local_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS process-group start, descendant snapshots keyed by start time so recycled pids are never signalled, and tree kill
- `backend_local_run_env_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exports the local run-env builder; no non-test caller
- `env_passthrough.go` — provider and adapter secret blocklist built from static lists, the optional-env catalogue and platform manifests; skill and config passthrough allowlist; multiplex flag and scoped secret resolution
- `local_pythonpath.go` — removes the runtime's own site-packages and repo root from a child's `PYTHONPATH` and drops `VIRTUAL_ENV`, `CONDA_PREFIX` and `PYTHONHOME`, so user Python never imports the harness runtime
- `env_probe.go` — background probe producing the one-line "Python toolchain" hint (missing pip, PEP 668, `uv`, version mismatch) the system prompt carries on local backends

#### Docker and Podman backend

Runs each task in a hardened long-lived container and executes commands with `docker exec`. Defaults: all capabilities dropped except `DAC_OVERRIDE`, `CHOWN` and `FOWNER`, `no-new-privileges`, pids limit 2048, 1 GB shm, size-limited tmpfs for `/tmp`, `/var/tmp` and `/run`, optional cpu, memory and disk limits, optional run-as-host-user, host cwd auto-mount, read-only mounts of credential files, skills and cache dirs. Containers are labelled with profile, task and a fingerprint of image and mounts so later processes reattach instead of recreating; a per-process reaper removes stale exited containers, and a container removed out of band is recreated once. The egress-proxy integration (`proxy.enabled`, CA mount, proxy env, token swapping for `icebath egress`) is fully coded here but the `EgressProxy` source is never assigned anywhere, so enabling it makes container creation fail unless `proxy.enforce_on_docker` is false.

- `backend_docker.go` — [partial] `dockerEnv`, option shaping from `terminal.docker_*` config, security and resource args, mount planning, env forwarding with collision checks, reuse and recreation, session-scoped isolation, setuid and file-capability stripping, ownership hand-back of sandbox files, orphan reaper; the egress-proxy path is dead for lack of an installed source
- `docker_cli.go` — locates `docker` or `podman` once per process (`ICEBATH_DOCKER_BINARY` override), runtime display name and start hint, label sanitizing, container identity per profile or shared key

#### SSH, cloud sandbox and Singularity backends

All are real implementations excluded from the `icebath_core` build. The three cloud backends and SSH push skills, credential files and caches into the sandbox through the file sync manager and pull changes back on cleanup. Modal, Daytona, Vercel and Singularity skip dangerous-command prompts because they are isolated.

- `backend_ssh.go` — one `ssh` process per command over ControlMaster sockets in the temp dir (persist 300 seconds, batch mode, accept-new host keys, no multiplexing on Windows); needs host and user; detects the remote home and seeds `~/.icebath` there
- `backend_ssh_{unix,windows}.go` — whether a symlink failure while staging a bulk upload means Windows lacks symlink privilege, in which case files are copied instead
- `backend_modal.go` — Modal sandbox through the Go SDK in app `icebath-agent`; persistent mode snapshots the filesystem on cleanup and records the image id in `modal_snapshots.json`; needs `MODAL_TOKEN_ID` and `MODAL_TOKEN_SECRET` or `~/.modal.toml`
- `backend_daytona.go` — Daytona sandbox `icebath-<task>` through the Go SDK; persistent mode stops and later resumes it, otherwise deletes; disk capped at 10 GB; needs `DAYTONA_API_KEY`
- `backend_vercel.go` — hand-written REST client for Vercel Sandbox with retries, snapshot restore via `vercel_sandbox_snapshots.json`, token tuple or OIDC auth, deprecated `terminal.vercel_runtime` versus `terminal.vercel_image`; also registers the ssh, modal, daytona and vercel providers
- `backend_singularity.go` — Apptainer or Singularity instance with `--containall`, optional persistent overlay under the scratch dir, SIF build cache, memory and cpu limits; registered through the plugin registry rather than as a built-in name

#### Sandbox file sync and credential, skill and cache mounts

Decides which host files a sandbox may see and keeps remote copies current.

- `file_sync.go` — `FileSyncManager`: uploads changed and deletes removed files at most every 5 seconds (`ICEBATH_FORCE_FILE_SYNC` forces), and on teardown downloads a tar, applies only files changed remotely, capped by `terminal.sync_back_max_bytes` (2 GiB), three attempts, under `.sync.lock`
- `file_sync_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS pid liveness check and interrupt deferral during sync-back
- `credential_files.go` — registry of credential files from skill frontmatter and `terminal.credential_files`, skills directory mounts (symlink-free copy when needed), cache directory mounts, and host-to-sandbox path translation for media and documents

#### Tool-provider selection and credential lookup

Despite its name this is not terminal backend selection: it answers which third-party provider backs each web and media capability and where that provider's key comes from, for the web and browser tools in the other part and the media tools in `pkg/media`.

- `backend_select.go` — reads which provider the user picked for browser, web search and extract, image, video, TTS and STT; resolves provider keys through config, profile secrets, `.env` and the credential pool; Modal credential check; uniform "configured but broken" error text

#### Checkpoints: snapshots and restore in a shared shadow git store

Checkpoints are automatic pre-mutation snapshots of a project directory, taken at most once per directory per turn before `write_file`, `patch` and destructive `terminal` commands, only on host-filesystem backends and only when enabled. Storage is one bare git store per profile at `checkpoints/store`: a project (nearest registered root, else nearest directory holding a marker such as `.git`, `go.mod` or `package.json`, else the file's directory; never `/` or the user home) is keyed by the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 of its path and owns a ref `refs/icebath/<hash>`, a private index, a metadata file and an agent-write ledger. A snapshot stages everything with default excludes (dependency, build and VCS directories, binaries, archives, `.env*`, logs), drops files over 10 MB, skips trees over 50,000 files, notes nested git repositories as uncaptured and commits without touching the user's repository or git config. Restore (`/rollback <N> [file]`, also from the TUI) validates the hash and path, refuses when uncaptured nested repositories are in scope, takes a pre-rollback snapshot first, and in safe mode reverts only files whose current hash still equals what the ledger says icebath wrote, reporting user-edited, oversize and undeletable files separately.

- `checkpoint_manager.go` — `CheckpointManager`: per-turn dedup, `EnsureFileCheckpoint`, `EnsureTerminalCheckpoint`, list, diff, session diff, restore, agent-write ledger, project-root resolution, numbered listing text
- `checkpoint_store.go` — store layout and initialisation, exclude list, hardened git environment and runner (timeout from `ICEBATH_CHECKPOINT_TIMEOUT`, 10 to 60 seconds), project metadata, ledger capped at 2,000 entries, migration of the older one-repo-per-project layout into `legacy-*` archives
- `checkpoint_changed.go` — lists files changed since the snapshot a time span started from, for the TUI undo hint
- `checkpoint_gitlinks.go` — finds nested repositories recorded as gitlinks and narrows a restore selection around them
- `checkpoint_json.go` — [py-shim] strict `json.loads`/`json.dumps` equivalents for metadata and ledger files, keeping exact numbers and surrogate-escaped path bytes
- `checkpoint_fsutil.go` — tree removal that clears read-only bits (also used for plugin, profile and MCP catalogue removal) and BOM-tolerant marker reads
- `checkpoint_lock_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS non-blocking exclusive lock on the store lock file
- `checkpoint_stat_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS device and inode identity and mount-point test used to prove a workdir was deleted
- `checkpoint_refusal_export.go` — explains that checkpoints are not taken when file paths belong to a container backend

#### Checkpoints: pruning, maintenance, CLI and profile rename

Retention is by count (20 snapshots per project, history rewritten), by store size (500 MB default; the oldest snapshot per project is dropped per round, one is always kept, garbage collection is deferred behind a marker), by age (`checkpoints.retention_days`, default 7) and by orphan detection (workdir observably deleted from a present parent). The gateway runs an automatic prune when `checkpoints.auto_prune` is set, at most once per `checkpoints.min_interval_hours` (24) through `checkpoints/.last_prune`, and never deletes orphans unattended. The whole store is guarded by a lock file beside the base directory.

- `checkpoint_pruning.go` — `CheckpointPruner` (trim to count, drop-one-round size enforcement, reflog expiry and gc) and the store lock
- `checkpoint_maintenance.go` — `PruneCheckpoints`, auto prune from config, store status, clear all, clear legacy archives, and the footprint notice shown by `doctor` and `update` when the store exceeds its cap
- `checkpoints_cli.go` — `icebath checkpoints status|list|prune|clear|clear-legacy` with confirmation prompts and `--keep-orphans`
- `checkpoint_profile_rename.go` — re-keys projects and rebases ledger paths when a profile rename moves workdirs
- `checkpoint_store_lock_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the store lock for `pkg/app` data cleanup

#### File tools: `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files`

All four are in toolset `file`, need a usable terminal backend and run through the task's backend, so they work inside containers and over SSH. `read_file(path, offset=1, limit=2000)` returns `LINE_NUM|CONTENT` pages capped at `file_read_max_chars` (100,000) with `next_offset`; documents (notebooks, Office, PDF, OpenDocument, RTF, EPUB, SQLite) are extracted to text, other binaries show as 16-byte hex rows, images are redirected to `vision_analyze`, and device files, `/proc` secrets, FIFOs, icebath credential stores, token and vault directories and any `.env`-family file are refused; a repeated identical read returns an "unchanged" stub and then a hard block. `write_file(path, content)` replaces a whole file but refuses when the task has no current full read of an existing file or it changed on disk, and hints toward `patch` when most lines are unchanged. `patch(path, old_string, new_string, replace_all)` does a fuzzy unique replacement and returns a unified diff; for OpenAI-family models the schema adds `mode` and `patch` for multi-file V4A patches. `search_files(pattern, target, path, file_glob, limit=50, offset, order, output_mode, context)` is the ripgrep-backed content and filename search whose engine lives in `search_files*.go` in the other part; write guards, read tracking and the V4A parser are also there.

- `file_tools.go` — schemas, handlers and registration of the four tools; per-task file backend cache; read guards, document and hex rendering, dedup stubs; shared write prechecks; stale-overwrite refusal; rewrite hint; search result filtering and redaction; hidden `cross_profile` argument on writes
- `file_results.go` — `ReadResult`, `WriteResult` and `PatchResult` with their pinned JSON key order
- `file_paths.go` — resolves model-supplied paths per task: workspace root from the session cwd record, a registered override or `TERMINAL_CWD`; pure POSIX paths for containers; remote-home tilde for SSH; warning when a relative path lands outside the workspace; MSYS drive translation
- `file_paths_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports task path resolution and the container-backend check for `pkg/agent`
- `file_state.go` — process-wide read stamps and last-writer records (4,096 paths each) that warn when a sibling agent wrote a file after this agent read it, plus per-path write locks; `ICEBATH_DISABLE_FILE_STATE_GUARD=1` turns it off
- `file_lock.go` — cross-process advisory lock file with timeout and holder pid, reentrant per goroutine; used by the skills hub and the TUI worktree record

#### File backend over a terminal environment

`shellFileOps` implements every file operation as shell snippets run through the task's `Environment`, with native host I/O fast paths when the backend is local.

- `file_ops.go` — `fileOperations` interface and `shellFileOps`: command execution with stdin, command availability cache, binary sniffing, tilde expansion, shell escaping, atomic write, fenced reads with sentinels, host Python lookup
- `file_ops_read.go` — paged and raw reads, UTF-16 detection and transcoding (files up to 10 MB), long-line flags, similar-filename suggestions including Unicode confusables, byte and range reads
- `file_ops_write.go` — `WriteFile` (deny check, fail-closed parse of structured files, CRLF and BOM preservation, sha256 verification, lint, LSP), `DeleteFile`, `MoveFile`, `patchReplace`, `patchV4A`, re-read verification
- `file_ops_native.go` — host-side write-target probe, temp-file atomic replace, sha256, Python-shaped OS error text
- `file_ops_common.go` — search, lint and exec result shapes, line-ending and BOM helpers, pagination coercion, merge-conflict block counter, terminal fence leak stripping
- `binary_extensions.go` — binary and opaque-document extension sets, SQLite sidecar detection
- `json_wtf8.go` — [py-shim] `os.fsencode` surrogate-escape encoding of paths that are not valid UTF-8

#### Fuzzy patch matching and diffs

`patch` tries nine strategies in order and stops at the first that matches: exact, line-trimmed, whitespace-normalized, indentation-flexible, escape-normalized, trimmed-boundary, Unicode-normalized, block-anchor (first and last line anchors, middle similarity 0.70, or 0.50 with a single candidate) and context-aware (every line at least 0.80 similar). Several matches without `replace_all` is an error listing locations, `replace_all` refuses the two similarity strategies, and an edit that is already applied returns success with no write.

- `fuzzy_match.go` — `FuzzyFindAndReplace`, the strategies, replacement re-indentation, Unicode preservation in replacements, no-match hints with closest lines and visualized whitespace; also used by skill editing
- `escape_drift.go` — corrects doubled backslashes and spurious quote escapes in `old_string`/`new_string` when the corrected anchor is verified in the file, and refuses ambiguous cases
- `difflib.go` — [py-shim] port of Python `difflib.SequenceMatcher` and `unified_diff`; feeds similarity scoring, patch and edit diffs, LSP line deltas, skill sync and cron monitors

#### Path deny lists and secret redaction

One file with two jobs, both described in its own messages as defence in depth rather than a security boundary because the terminal tool can bypass them. File tools may never write SSH keys, `.netrc`, `.pgpass`, `.npmrc`, `.pypirc`, `.git-credentials`, `/etc/sudoers`, `/etc/passwd`, `/etc/shadow`, the `~/.ssh`, `.aws`, `.gnupg`, `.kube`, `.docker`, `.azure`, `gh` and `gcloud` config directories, `/etc/systemd`, the profile `.env`, OAuth files and secret caches, or the profile's `state.db`, `sessions`, `mcp-tokens`, `pairing`, `vault`, `browser-profile` and `webapp`; `ICEBATH_WRITE_SAFE_ROOT` confines writes to listed roots and `~/.ssh/config` needs approval. Reads are refused for icebath credential stores, `mcp-tokens`, `vault`, `browser-profile`, `webapp`, the `skills/.hub` cache and any `.env`-family file anywhere. When `security.redact_secrets` is on, the redaction engine masks vendor-prefixed tokens, auth headers, database and token URLs, JWTs, private keys, Telegram tokens, webapp session links and up to 64 registered vault values per profile in file content returned to the model, adding env, config, JSON and YAML assignment passes for secret-bearing files; the terminal redactor in the other part reuses its patterns.

- `file_safety.go` — write and read deny classification, running-binary protection, sandbox-mirror write warnings, the redaction passes and masking helpers, vault value registry, and the config-tree accessors other tool files use

#### Post-write lint and LSP diagnostics

After every write the backend runs a syntax check and reports only errors the edit introduced. In-process checks cover `.py`, `.json`, `.yaml`, `.yml` and `.toml` (the last four also block the write when the new content does not parse); shell linters cover `.py`, `.js`, `.ts`, `.go` and `.rs`, with Node tools run under the managed Node, `.ts`, `.go` and `.rs` skipped when an LSP server handles the file, and `.ts` and `.rs` skipped outside trusted workspaces (`lsp.trusted_workspaces` plus operator worktrees). LSP diagnostics follow on host-filesystem backends only, waiting briefly inline and otherwise delivering a late verdict into a later tool result or at turn end.

- `lint.go` — linter tables, delta lint, JSON constant guard, LSP hand-off and late-verdict queuing in its first 750 lines; the remaining 4,000 lines are py-shim ports of CPython `tomllib` and of the libyaml scanner and parser, kept so error messages match the Python original
- `lsp_layer.go` — function seams that stay unset in builds without the LSP layer, and trusted-workspace resolution
- `lsp_bridge.go` — binds the seams to `pkg/lsp` (excluded from `icebath_core` and `icebath_noextras` builds): per-profile service, child env, managed package lookup, diagnostics formatting
- `lsp_deferred.go` — queue of undelivered late verdicts per owner session (64 owners, 32 notes each) with a 5-second wait at turn end

#### `clarify` tool

`clarify(questions[])` asks the user one to five questions in one form; each question has text, up to four `choices` (the first is marked "(Recommended)" and an "Other" row is added by the UI) and optional `multi_select`. The result lists per-question status (answered, skipped, unanswered) and an outcome (submitted, cancelled, timed_out, undelivered). It never runs in parallel with other tools and subagents cannot call it.

- `clarify.go` — schema, question normalization, mapping of picked display choices back to raw choices, result JSON, registration
- `clarify_callback.go` — binds a surface callback to a turn's context and runs the tool through it; used by the agent's inline executor and MCP elicitation forms
- `clarify_gateway.go` — pending clarify entries per gateway session, blocking wait (`agent.clarify_timeout`), resolution from buttons or typed replies (numbers, labels, `skip`), free-text mode

#### `manage_connections` tool and connection operations

`manage_connections(action, connectors[])` with action `install`, `enable` or `authorize` connects the user to MCP servers. On surfaces with a card it shows an approval card and blocks until every target is connected or skipped or a 600-second deadline passes; elsewhere targets run at once. It cannot remove servers, and delegated side agents never see it. The MCP runner is installed by `pkg/mcp`. The contract declares target kinds `mcp`, `plugin` and `skill`, but only `mcp` targets are ever created, so plugin and skill connection cards were intended and never built.

- `connectors_tool.go` — schema, argument validation, registration, the side-agent drop list
- `connectors_targets.go` — target normalization, action validation, session key choice, the `MCPOperationRunner` hook
- `connectors_contract.go` — [partial] target states (pending, initiated, connected, skipped, failed, not_connected), settle reasons, and the table of which actor (user or backend watcher) may make each transition; the `plugin` and `skill` kinds have no producer
- `connectors_operation.go` — `ConnectionOperation`: targets, legal transitions, deadline, frozen result, change notifications for the card renderer
- `connectors_run.go` — drives an operation: prepare, emit the card, watch every 5 seconds until settled by resolution, deadline or interrupt
- `connectors_live.go` — one open operation per profile session, looked up by the gateway when the user acts on a card

#### `delegate_task` tool surface and delegation settings

The tool layer owns the schema and policy; `pkg/agent` installs the `DelegateTask` implementation and builds the children. `delegate_task(tasks[], action, subagent_id, message)` spawns one subagent per task (each with `goal`, optional `context`, `output_schema`, up to 8 `images`, and `group` when independent completions are on), or with `action` `list`, `steer` or `stop` controls running children; one-shot sessions get a variant without live control. The description is rebuilt on every definition build from `delegation.*` settings: concurrency, spawn depth and orchestrator mode, child idle timeout, gateway inline or background mode, worktree isolation, subagent auto-approve (subagents otherwise auto-deny dangerous commands), and the pluggable routing backend.

- `delegate_tool_schema.go` — static schema, dynamic description and parameter overrides, one-shot variant, stripping of model-hidden `acp_command`/`acp_args`, registration; the handler still reads legacy top-level `goal`, `context`, `role`, `max_iterations`, `images` and `output_schema`
- `delegate_tool_config.go` — readers for the delegation settings, the subagent approval callback, gateway inline decision frozen per agent, child credential bundle shape
- `delegate_tool_tasks.go` — task list normalization (JSON-string recovery, legacy single `goal`), batch quality gate rejecting filler, template and terse goals, per-task schema and image validation
- `delegate_tool_routes.go` — `TaskRoute`, provider-declared extra task parameters and their enum validation, route key filtering
- `delegate_tool_tuning.go` — per-task service-tier (speed) pinning on the child route
- `delegation_provider.go` — `DelegationProvider` interface: a strategy that turns one task into a child route, with default method implementations
- `delegation_registry.go` — resolves the active provider from `delegation.backend`, loading bundled strategies on first use and honouring disabled plugins
- `delegation_backends.go` — lists backends for pickers, persists a backend switch and queues a next-turn tool rebuild
- `delegation_output_schema.go` — validates a child's final answer against `output_schema`, extracts JSON from fenced or prose answers, builds one bounded retry message; carries Python frame-depth emulation
- `delegation_redaction.go` — redacts child-produced text, results and completion events before the parent or persistent sinks see them
- `delegation_predicates.go` — reports whether code runs for a delegated child or its subprocess, and whether a kanban worker identity is owned by this execution

#### Background delegation ledger and completion delivery

Background subagents run on a daemon pool and are recorded in the `async_delegations` table of the profile `state.db`, so a completion survives a crash or restart. On startup, rows whose owner process died are marked outcome-unknown with transcript tails and git state as recovery hints, undelivered completions are re-queued, and a sweep every 30 seconds re-offers orphans; delivery uses claims with a 300-second lease and at most 8 attempts, rows are kept 7 days and replayed up to 48 hours. A monitor flags children quiet for 450 seconds (1,200 inside a tool), and closing a session interrupts its children and refuses new dispatches.

- `async_delegation.go` — ledger schema access, dispatch of single and batch units, completion events, claim, release, defer and drop of deliveries, orphan sweep, stall monitor, listing for `/status`, session interrupt and refusal
- `async_delegation_worker.go` — in a managed worker process, forwards every ledger operation to the owning process through the worker's session store
- `async_delegation_recovery_hints.go` — last 20 lines (2,000 characters) of child transcripts and a branch, head and dirty-count line for abandoned delegations
- `async_delegation_completion_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exports the completion persister; no non-test caller

#### Discord tools

Two tools gated on `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, calling the Discord REST API v10 directly. `discord(action, ...)` offers `fetch_messages`, `search_members` and `create_thread`; `discord_admin(action, ...)` offers guild, channel, role and member listing plus pin, unpin, delete message and add or remove role. Parameters are ids (`guild_id`, `channel_id`, `user_id`, `role_id`, `message_id`), `query`, `name`, `limit`, `before`, `after` and `auto_archive_duration`.

**Files `magic_*` through `xai_*`** (225 files, 68,774 Go lines). This part holds the registry's scoping and availability layer, the toolset table with the `icebath tools` configurator, the Tool Search bridge, the `terminal` tool with its policy and environment cache, the background process registry with its owner-death supervisor, the web search and extract stack with eleven provider backends, secret redaction, result spill storage, the document extractors behind `read_file`, the `search_files` engine, vision, session search, the todo list, projects, git worktree management and the NeMo Relay integration. Model-callable tools registered here are `terminal`, `process_manage`, `web_search`, `web_extract`, `x_search`, `vision_analyze`, `video_analyze`, `session_search`, `todo_list` and `desktop_project`, plus the three synthetic bridge tools `tool_search`, `tool_describe` and `tool_call`; everything else is helper code. Under the profile home it owns `processes.json`, `logs/process-results/`, `logs/process-output/`, `logs/<tool>_debug_<id>.json`, `cache/spillover/`, `cache/web/` with `extract-index.json`, `cache/worktree_merge_verdicts.json`, `hook_outputs/`, `pending/memory/` and `pending/skills/`, `projects.db` and `tui_worktrees.json`; under the root home shared by all profiles `spawn-ledger.json`; inside user repositories `.worktrees/`, a `.gitignore` line and `refs/icebath/archive/*`; and in the OS cache directory `icebath/wazero`. Port scaffolding is heavy: 18 `*_export.go` shims, ports of the Python `ddgs`, `lxml`/libxml2, `httpx`, `requests`, `ElementTree`, Pillow and Porter2 stemmer libraries, Python context-variable and thread-local emulation, and dozens of hook variables other packages assign at init. The product logic is implemented and wired; the dead spots found are the console terminal-backend wizard, the asker-driven variant of the tools configurator, the Blank Slate config writers, the `discovered_repos` table, one skill-app availability function and a handful of exports nothing calls.

#### Tool registry: scopes, plugin ownership and availability checks

Extends the `Registry` of the first part with three lookup layers: a process-global map, one overlay per profile home (`ScopeKey`), and a per-execution session overlay bound on the context; reads merge session over profile over global. Plugin registrations go through `RegisterScoped`: a plugin may not shadow a global tool or replace a tool of another toolset without `override` and without the operator opt-in `plugins.entries.<plugin_id>.allow_tool_override`, and may deregister only tools it owns. A tool's availability check (`Def.Check`) is cached per check function and profile for 30 seconds, a failure within 60 seconds of the last success is treated as transient and the tool kept, a panic counts as unavailable, and checks marked `NoCacheCheck` always run. A safe-worker policy hides every built-in except `read_file`, `write_file`, `patch`, `search_files`, `terminal` and `process_manage`.

- `registry_scope.go` — scope layers, generation counter, toolset aliases (MCP server names), plugin override policy records, `RegisterScoped`, `Deregister`, `MoveToScope`, restore helpers, `AvailableToolsets`, `CheckToolAvailability` (unavailable toolsets with missing env vars)
- `registry_register.go` — schema validation at registration and the refusal texts for shadowing, cross-toolset override and foreign deregistration
- `registry_check.go` — availability verdict cache (30 s TTL, 60 s grace, 512 entries), verdict windows that give definition caches an expiry, per-pass memo, `CheckToolsetRequirements`
- `registry_safe_worker.go` — records which global entries are built-ins and hides those outside the six reviewed tools while `config.SafeWorkerEnabled` holds
- `registry_requirements.go` — one consistent snapshot of entries and toolset checks; `ToolsetRequirements` rows for `icebath doctor` and the startup banner; `ToolResult` JSON encoder
- `registry_toolset_order.go` — [port-artifact] remembers first-registration order per slot so listings iterate like a Python dict; `AvailableToolsetNames`
- `registry_errors.go` — caps error text a tool returns at 2,048 code points for the model (8,192 in the debug log)
- `registry_result.go` — `NormalizeHandlerResult`: a string result is bounded, the multimodal envelope kept as JSON, any other value becomes a contract error
- `registry_check_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the cached availability check for `pkg/gateway`
- `registry_scope_export.go` — [test-support] test-only scope reset

#### Model-facing tool definitions and provider schema sanitising

`Registry.ToolDefinitions` builds the tool list sent to the model: select tool names from enabled and disabled toolsets, drop tools whose check fails, apply per-tool dynamic schema overrides, run the description rewriters, sanitise every schema, then let Tool Search replace deferrable tools with its bridge. Quiet builds are memoised (8 entries) on scope, selection, registry generation, config file version, kanban and delegation flags and context length, and expire with the earliest availability verdict consulted. Rewriters drop `browser_exec` when the session has no `terminal`, and adjust the `browser_cdp`, `browser_vault` and `delegate_task` descriptions to the sibling tools actually present.

- `registry_defs.go` — `Definitions`, `ToolDefinitions`, the rewriter table and `RegisterSchemaRewriter`, definition cache, `tool_selection` notice events, kanban toolset auto-selection for dispatcher-owned workers, active model context-length lookup through provider hooks
- `schema.go` — `SanitizeToolSchemas`: property keys forced to `[a-zA-Z0-9_.-]{1,64}` with collision suffixes, bare and array `type` normalised, nullable unions collapsed, `default` beside `$ref` dropped (Fireworks), top-level `allOf`/`anyOf`/`oneOf`/`enum`/`not` dropped (Codex); `CollapseConstUnions` for MCP; reactive `StripPatternAndFormat` (llama.cpp) and `StripSlashEnum` (xAI)
- `schema_rewriter_lookup.go` — [port-artifact] exports the rewriter lookup for `pkg/mcp`

#### Toolsets, platform bundles, distributions and build tiers

The static table defines 23 platform bundles and 33 feature toolsets: `web`, `search`, `x_search`, `vision`, `video`, `image_gen`, `video_gen`, `computer_use`, `terminal`, `skills`, `browser`, `cronjob`, `file`, `tts`, `todo`, `memory`, `context_engine`, `session_search`, `connections`, `project`, `bot_room`, `clarify`, `code_execution`, `delegation`, `kanban`, `discord`, `discord_admin`, `yuanbao`, `feishu_doc`, `feishu_drive`, and the composites `debugging`, `safe` and `coding`. Bundles named `icebath-<platform>` carry the 41 `CoreTools` plus platform extras (`icebath-cli`, `-cron`, `-telegram`, `-discord`, `-slack`, `-whatsapp`, `-signal`, `-bluebubbles`, `-email`, `-mattermost`, `-matrix`, `-dingtalk`, `-feishu`, `-weixin`, `-qqbot`, `-wecom`, `-wecom-callback`, `-yuanbao`, `-sms`), with reduced sets for `icebath-acp`, `icebath-api-server` and `icebath-webhook` (four safe tools) and the union `icebath-gateway`. `PlatformTools` resolves a platform's enabled toolsets from `platform_toolsets.<platform>`, falling back to the bundle, then applies default-off toolsets (`discord`, `discord_admin`, `video`, `video_gen`, `x_search`, `kanban`, `spotify`, `a2a`), platform restrictions (`discord` toolsets only on Discord), plugin toolsets, enabled MCP servers (`mcp_servers`, `no_mcp`), the context engine and `agent.disabled_toolsets`; `x_search` turns on by itself when xAI credentials exist, and disabling a bundle or posture toolset removes only its non-core tools. Legacy `hermes-` bundle names and `*_tools` toolset names are still accepted.

- `toolsets.go` — the tables above, `ResolveToolset` with includes and `all`/`*`, `SelectToolNames`, `PlatformTools`, `SavePlatformTools` (also writes `known_plugin_toolsets` and `known_builtin_toolsets`), `ValidatePlatformToolsets` warnings, 17 probabilistic `Distributions` for batch data generation, session-start availability notices
- `tools_config_platform.go` — platforms with a configured token (`cli` first), per-platform enabled summary, tolerant parsing of saved toolset lists with one warning per platform, plugin toolset defaults, offline xAI credential check
- `tool_tiers.go` — maps toolsets, tool name prefixes and platforms to the `plugins` or `extras` link tier; `DropUnlinkedToolsets` prunes the tables in smaller builds and the refusal lines name the build that carries a missing toolset
- `setup_blank_slate.go` — [unwired] writes a minimal toolset state (file, terminal, vision, skills) and turns compression, memory, checkpoints and smart routing off; the TUI setup hub implements its own Blank Slate and nothing calls these

#### Tool Search bridge for deferred tools

When `tools.tool_search.enabled` is not `off` and any deferrable tool is present, deferrable schemas are removed from the request and replaced by `tool_search` (parameters `queries`, at most 7, and `limit`), `tool_describe` (`names`, at most 10) and `tool_call` (`calls`, an array of `{name, arguments}`; exactly one entry for local tools). Deferrable means: named in `tools.tool_search.defer` (default `computer_use`, `session_search`, `image_generate`, `todo_list`, `process_manage`, `cronjob_manage`, `browser_vault`, `desktop_project`), or any non-core tool outside the client-surface `project` toolset, including every `mcp-*` tool. The `tool_search` description embeds a catalog listing that degrades from full, to names only, to mixed, to server summaries, to none within a token budget of the smaller of `listing_max_tokens` (4,000) and `threshold_pct` (5) of the context window. `threshold_pct` only sizes that listing: activation no longer depends on it, so `auto` and `on` behave the same.

- `tool_search.go` — config parsing and clamps, classification, bridge schemas, `AssembleToolDefs`, `DispatchToolSearch`, `DispatchToolDescribe`, `ResolveUnderlyingCall`, scope block reasons
- `tool_search_catalog.go` — catalog entries with source labels, BM25 search gated on the rarest query term and a 50% term-coverage floor, exact-name matches first, listing renderer, hidden unavailable MCP servers
- `tool_search_stem.go` — Porter2 English stemmer used on both index and query tokens
- `tool_search_validation.go` — validates `tool_call` arguments against the deferred tool's schema (no external `$ref` fetch), normalises call entries, and builds the model-facing reasons for disabled, unoffered, deferred or setup-needing tools

#### `icebath tools` configurator

`icebath tools` opens an interactive menu (TTY required) with one row per configured platform, a global row, a provider reconfigure row and an MCP row; `--summary` prints enabled toolsets per platform; `list`, `enable` and `disable` with `--platform` are delegated to `pkg/commands`; `post-setup <key>` runs one install hook non-interactively (exit 0 ok, 1 hook failure, 2 unknown key). Enabling a toolset that has a provider category prompts for a provider, its API keys (saved to the profile `.env`), its config keys and an optional post-setup install. A second, asker-driven variant of the same flow was built for the setup wizard (`RunToolsFlow`, with every prompt routed through a `setupflow.Asker`), but nothing outside tests calls it, so the asker branches inside the flow files are dead in production.

- `tools_config_command.go` — `CmdTools` dispatcher and the returning-user menu loop
- `tools_config.go` — `ToolCategories` provider catalog (TTS: Edge, OpenAI, xAI, ElevenLabs, Mistral, Gemini, KittenTTS, Piper, DeepInfra; STT: local Whisper, OpenAI, Groq, xAI, ElevenLabs, Mistral, DeepInfra; web; image and video generation; X search; browser; computer use) and plugin toolset sources
- `tools_config_flows.go` — per-platform checklist with estimated schema tokens, first-install pass, diff printing, reconfigure flow, save through `SavePlatformTools`
- `tools_config_providers.go` — provider pickers fed by plugin registries (web, image, video, TTS, browser), active-provider detection, model pickers (FAL, plugin catalogs, STT, Piper voices), key prompts, vision backend and model picker over `auxiliary.vision`
- `tools_config_post_setup.go` — install hooks: Chromium via the package manager, Lightpanda check, cua-driver, xAI Grok OAuth or key, OpenAI Codex device login, and Python extras `stt-whisper` and `kittentts` synced into the managed venv
- `tools_config_tokens.go` — cl100k_base token estimate per registered tool schema, cached per home and registry generation
- `tools_config_hooks.go` — `ToolsCommandHooks` installed by `pkg/provider` and `pkg/commands`, console seams
- `tools_setup.go` — `ToolsSetup` run state, `ToolsConfigHooks` (29 hooks installed by `pkg/provider`, `pkg/media`, `pkg/browser` and `pkg/codeexec`), env and config read and write
- `tools_setup_flow.go` — [unwired] `RunToolsFlow`, meant for `/setup tools`: backs up `config.yaml`, runs the menu through an asker instead of the console, saves; no non-test caller

#### The `terminal` tool: request planning and pre-execution guards

`terminal` (toolset `terminal`, result cap 100,000 characters) takes `command` (required), `background`, `timeout` (default `terminal.timeout`, 180 s; foreground cap 600 s or `TERMINAL_MAX_FOREGROUND_TIMEOUT`), `workdir`, `pty`, `notify` (true or a list of output patterns), `heartbeat` (seconds, minimum 60) and `persist_on_release`. A foreground timeout above the cap is promoted to a tracked background process with completion notification; a lone trailing `&` is run as background; `nohup`, `disown`, `setsid`, inline `&` and known server commands (`npm run dev`, `docker compose up`, `uvicorn`, and others) are refused with guidance. Before execution a guard chain bounded by the command deadline (minimum 30 s) runs the gateway lifecycle guard, the workdir character allowlist, the self-repository guard and the locked-skill guard, then the dangerous-command approval system of the first part; a denied or pending approval returns `status: blocked` or `pending_approval` without running anything.

- `terminal.go` — schema, `handleTerminal` argument mapping (legacy `notify_on_complete` and `watch_patterns` accepted), `planExecution`, environment acquisition, `runForeground`, `TerminalTool`, error envelopes
- `terminal_guards.go` — workdir allowlist, foreground-versus-background guidance, trailing-ampersand rewrite (only when the approval identity is unchanged), script reads for the lifecycle guard, `launchctl submit` block inside a supervised gateway
- `shell_heredoc.go` — quote-aware heredoc scanner that blanks provably inert heredoc bodies before keyword guards run

#### Terminal execution and result shaping

Foreground execution runs in the cached environment, retries transport errors three times with 2, 4 and 8 second waits, returns exit code 124 on timeout, and on the local backend can be yielded to the background mid-run. Background execution hands the command to the process registry and returns a `session_id`; notify flags are dropped with a note on sessions that cannot receive a later message, and `pty` is switched off with a note for `gh auth login --with-token`, which needs piped stdin. The foreground result carries `output` (plugin `transform_terminal_output` hook, head and tail truncation to `tool_output.max_bytes`, ANSI stripped, secrets redacted), `exit_code`, and optional `cwd`, `exit_code_meaning`, `hint`, `approval`, `full_output_path`, `verification_evidence`, `environment_recreated` and sudo flags. An unreachable backend returns `status: degraded` and evicts the cached environment unless `terminal.degraded_mode` is `fail`.

- `terminal_result.go` — signal and per-command exit-code notes (`grep` 1, `diff` 1, `curl` 6/7/22/28, and others), sudo annotations, spill-file redaction, result assembly
- `terminal_hints.go` — one recovery hint per failure from output patterns (command not found, missing Python module, merge conflict, rate limit, permission denied) and exit codes 124, 126 and 137; warning when exit 0 hides an upstream pipe failure
- `terminal_background.go` — `spawnBackgroundProcess`: local spawn or sandbox spawn, routing stamps from the session (platform, chat, thread, user, message), completion watcher registration, watch-pattern versus notify conflict, heartbeat arming, subagent notes, yield-to-background handler
- `terminal_macos_open.go` — appends an AppleScript raise sequence to a bare macOS `open` command so the opened document comes to the front

#### Sudo password handling

A command with real `sudo` words is rewritten to `sudo -S` with the password on stdin when one is known: `SUDO_PASSWORD` from the profile secrets or process env, else a password cached per session key (or per worker), else a prompt through the session asker, a registered surface callback or a hidden read from `/dev/tty` with a 45-second timeout. No prompt is made in delegated children or single-query sessions, or when passwordless sudo is detected. A rejected cached password is dropped and the result flags `sudo_auth_failed`; headless failures append a tip to set `SUDO_PASSWORD`.

- `terminal_sudo.go` — shell scanner, `sudo` rewrite through `env` wrappers and assignments, cache scopes, prompt flow, failure detection, `RewriteCompoundBackground` (wraps `A && B &` as `A && { B & }`)
- `terminal_sudo_callback.go` — per-thread sudo prompt callback slot the TUI and CLI install, propagated to worker goroutines
- `tty_password.go`, `tty_password_unix.go`, `tty_password_windows.go` — boxed terminal prompt and echo-off line read from the controlling terminal or Windows console
- `tty_password_termios_{bsd,linux}.go` — termios ioctl numbers per OS (2 variants)

#### Terminal policy, backend selection, environment cache and working directories

A `TerminalPolicy` is the frozen set of `terminal.*` settings of one profile, keyed by legacy `TERMINAL_*` names (`TERMINAL_ENV` for `terminal.backend`), built from defaults, `config.yaml`, managed pins and a launch overlay; a profile whose policy cannot be resolved gets a refusal scope and commands fail closed. The shipped backend names are `local`, `docker`, `modal`, `daytona`, `vercel_sandbox` and `ssh`; `singularity` and plugin-registered backends resolve through the same provider registry. Environments are cached under a key derived per call (`session:<key>`, a per-profile container key with `:ws:<digest>` for a bound workspace, `shared:<name>` from `terminal.docker_shared_container_key`, `home:<path>` for a routed profile, the raw task id when it registered image overrides, else `default`; subagents alias to the parent's container) and reaped after `terminal.lifetime_seconds` (default 300) of inactivity by a 60-second loop that skips environments with running processes or calls in flight; persistent Docker workspace containers are stopped rather than removed. The working directory of a command is the explicit `workdir`, else the cwd the session last ended in, else the configured cwd; host paths are translated to the container mount or remapped to `/workspace`, and `.`, `auto` and `cwd` are placeholders resolved per surface.

- `terminal_scope.go` — policy type, config-key to policy-name map (40 settings), layered build, per-home cache invalidated by `config.yaml` and `.env` changes, context binding, session and profile isolation predicates for Docker
- `terminal_config.go` — session flags, setting parsers, host-versus-container path tests and translation, SSH tilde cwd, subprocess `HOME` contract, default sandbox image names
- `terminal_state.go` — environment pool, per-task overrides (image, cwd), per-session cwd records, container aliasing, cache-key derivation, `resolveEnvConfig` (the flat config map every backend reads)
- `terminal_backends.go` — config shaping per backend (SSH host, user, port, key; container CPU 1, memory 5,120 MB, disk 51,200 MB; Docker volumes, env, network, shm), `createEnvironment`, requirement checks with a remembered failure reason, Vercel runtimes `node24`, `node22`, `python3.13`
- `terminal_lifecycle.go` — creation locks, in-flight holds, idle reaper, `EnsureTaskEnv` and `CreateTaskEnvironment` shared with `execute_code`, eviction after infrastructure failure, shutdown teardown
- `terminal_env_registry.go` — plugin terminal-backend registry view and safe attribute reads (`is_remote`, `strip_env_keys`)
- `terminal_env_provider_defaults.go` — default method set a plugin backend provider embeds (display name, remote and container flags, default cwd, requirement check, setup lines, doctor checks)
- `prompt_backend_probe.go` — runs an OS probe inside a throwaway non-local backend and caches the summary for the system prompt; `TerminalSetting` and `TerminalEnvRead` accessors
- `runtime_cwd.go` — logical session cwd pin, install-tree test, `ResolveAgentCwd` and `ResolveContextCwd` used across the application
- `terminal_scope_export.go`, `terminal_workspace_export.go` — [port-artifact] export the cwd-placeholder test, task-key qualification and the unbinding of a turn's workspace override

#### Terminal backend setup and the default sandbox image

Setup helpers for choosing where commands run. The TUI setup section uses the SSH probe and the plugin post-setup runner; the full console wizard is orphaned. The default sandbox image is built locally from the Dockerfile embedded in `docker/sandbox` and labelled with its digest, and the same Dockerfile is translated for Modal, Daytona and Apptainer.

- `setup_terminal.go` — [unwired] console wizard `SetupTerminalBackend` (choose backend, write `terminal.backend` and `TERMINAL_ENV`); `pkg/provider` installs its console adapter but nothing calls the wizard; only its SSH probe runner, post-setup hook interface and venv-sync failure test are used elsewhere
- `setup_terminal_backends.go` — [unwired] wizard steps for Docker (runtime detection, image, egress firewall), Modal, Daytona, Vercel Sandbox and SSH; reachable only through the wizard above; excluded from the `icebath_core` build
- `terminal_backend_setup.go` — plugin backend rows for the setup menu, Docker or Podman detection, nearest `.vercel/project.json`, `TestSSHConnection` (batch-mode `ssh ... echo ok`), `RunTerminalBackendSetup`
- `vercel_auth.go` — reports the Vercel auth mode (OIDC token first, else token, team and project) without exposing values, for doctor and status
- `sandbox_image.go` — `EnsureSandboxImage` (docker or podman build, 45-minute limit, digest label check) and the Modal, Daytona and Apptainer SIF equivalents; excluded from the `icebath_core` build
- `sandbox_image_switch.go` — detects labelled containers still running a previous default image and lets the user pin the old image or switch and evict the cached sandbox

#### Terminal guards for the running source checkout and locked skills

Two guards the `terminal` pre-execution chain applies on the local backend. The self-repository guard is active only on Windows, where git operations that rewrite the checkout icebath runs from are blocked. The skill lock guard refuses any command that would write into a user-locked skill directory, change `skills/.usage.json` or run the unlock command.

- `self_repo_guard.go` — shell parser with heredoc, subshell and alias tracking that finds worktree-mutating `git` and `gh` commands aimed at the running source root
- `skill_lock.go` — locked skill lookup through a hook installed by `pkg/skills`; analysis of file verbs, in-place editors, `find -exec`, git mutations, archive extraction and interpreter one-liners; path refusal used by the file tools

#### `process_manage` and the background process registry

`process_manage` (toolset `terminal`) has actions `list`, `poll`, `log` (last 200 lines by default), `wait`, `kill`, `write`, `submit`, `close` and `handoff`, with `session_id` (any unique prefix), `data`, `timeout`, `offset` and `limit`. The registry tracks at most 64 processes, each with a 200,000-character rolling output buffer; finished entries are pruned 30 minutes after their start time, or oldest first at the cap. Local processes run through a login shell in their own session, in pipe mode without stdin or on a PTY, so `write` and `submit` work only for PTY sessions; sandbox processes run under `nohup` with log, pid and exit files polled through the backend. `wait` is clamped to `terminal.timeout` and ends early on a user interrupt, and a subagent may hand a running process to its parent with `handoff` (3 per subagent), since its processes are otherwise killed when it finishes.

- `process_manage.go` — schema, action dispatch, output transform and redaction, `handoff`
- `process_registry.go` — `ProcessSession`, `ProcessRegistry`, event queue, local, PTY and sandbox spawns, reader and poller loops, watch patterns, heartbeats, `poll`, `log`, `wait`, `kill`, stdin operations, listing, ownership transfer, pruning, one-shot exit linger (`terminal.oneshot_completion_wait_seconds`, 600 s)
- `process_registry_views.go` — read-only projection of tracked processes for gateway owners
- `process_dock_export.go`, `process_session_exited.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exported dock snapshot, forget-finished and exited accessors with no caller
- `process_registry_export.go` — [test-support] registry isolation helpers

#### Process spawn isolation, output logs and termination

Under a supervised gateway on Linux each local spawn is wrapped in a transient `systemd-run --user --scope` unit named `icebath-worker-<id>.scope` with memory accounting and a `MemoryMax` limit; availability is probed and cached for 60 seconds, and without it the process shares the gateway cgroup. Processes spawned from a per-turn worker write to `logs/process-output/proc_<id>.log` with an `.exit` file so another process can adopt them. Kill sends TERM to the process and its descendants, escalates to KILL after `terminal.daemon_term_grace_seconds` (2 s), verifies survivors, and refuses to signal a pid whose start time no longer matches.

- `process_registry_io.go` — systemd scope probing and argv, worker memory limit (`TERMINAL_LOCAL_MEMORY_MAX_MB`, half of RAM capped at 4 GiB), output log files under `logs/process-output/`, stdin-unavailable explanations, tree termination and survivor checks, restart-safe gateway child launch
- `process_registry_{unix,windows}.go` — runtime-dir and socket ownership checks for the systemd user bus, `taskkill` tree kill, PTY availability (2 variants)
- `process_registry_{linux,bsd}.go` — physical memory size per OS (2 variants)

#### Process checkpoint, result receipts and completion notifications

Running processes are checkpointed to `processes.json` in the profile home and re-adopted at startup as detached sessions when pid and start time still match (a recycled pid is never adopted or signalled); completed results are kept as redacted receipts in `logs/process-results/` for 7 days, newest 64 per profile, readable by the owning conversation. Completion, watch-pattern and heartbeat events go to one queue that the CLI, TUI server and gateway drain into the conversation as an injected message, requeueing events that belong to another session. Watch matches are rate limited (15 s per session, 3 strikes disable watching, 8 lifetime hits, a global breaker of 15 per 10 s with a 30 s cooldown) and heartbeats tick every 60 s or more with at most 2,000 new characters. Two consecutive waits or polls with no new output promote a running process to notify-on-complete (`terminal.process_wait_auto_notify`), and a one-shot session lingers up to `terminal.oneshot_completion_wait_seconds` for pending completions.

- `process_registry_state.go` — checkpoint write and recovery, log tailing for worker-spawned processes, result receipts, event ownership and requeue, wait and poll policy, notification text for process completions, heartbeats and async delegation batches
- `process_registry_owns_export.go`, `run_notifications_export.go`, `run_notifications_watcher_export.go`, `run_turn_persistence_export.go` — [port-artifact] export event routing, notification surfacing, watcher field snapshots and pending-watcher takeover for `pkg/gatewayrun` and `pkg/tuiserver`

#### Pseudo-terminals for interactive background processes

PTY sessions back `terminal(background=true, pty=true)`: the child is a session leader on a 30 by 120 terminal, and terminal status queries it emits are answered so interactive CLIs do not hang.

- `process_pty_unix.go` — spawn on a fresh PTY, read, write, EOF character, staged termination (HUP, CONT, INT, TERM, KILL)
- `process_pty_{linux,darwin,bsd}.go` — opening the PTY pair per OS (3 variants)
- `process_pty_windows.go` — ConPTY spawn, resize and termination
- `pty_query.go` — strips and answers device status, cursor position and window size queries in PTY output

#### Process identity, spawn ledger and owner-death supervisor

Makes long-lived children die with the icebath process that owns them, however it dies. On POSIX one resident `sh` supervisor per icebath process holds a pipe: icebath writes `register <pgid>` and `unregister <pgid>` lines, and on EOF the script sends TERM to every registered group, waits 3 seconds and sends KILL; on Windows kill-on-close job objects do the same. A `spawn-ledger.json` in the root home, shared by every profile and tagged with an install id derived from the executable's directory, records each long-lived process with pid, birth time, boot id, purpose and spawner, so later runs can prove whether a pid is still the same incarnation before signalling it. Children are tagged with the `ICEBATH_SPAWN` env var.

- `process_identity.go` — install id, spawn tags, ledger read, prune and append with quarantine of corrupt files, incarnation matching, supervisor lifecycle (restart with replay, idle release), `SpawnOwned`, `OwnProcessGroups`
- `process_supervisor.sh` — [data] the embedded POSIX supervisor script described above
- `process_identity_unix.go`, `process_identity_{linux,darwin,bsd}.go` — supervisor spawn, group signalling and per-OS process facts (birth, boot start, zombie, parent, cmdline, children)
- `process_identity_windows.go` — job-object supervisor and Win32 process facts
- `subprocess_compat_kill.go`, `subprocess_compat_kill_{unix,windows}.go` — `KillChildTree` and `KillAndDrain` for helper subprocesses, reaped command handles, pid existence test

#### `web_search` and `web_extract`: tools, backend selection and the keyless tier

`web_search` (toolset `web`) takes `query` and `limit` (1 to 100, default 5) and returns titles, URLs and snippets; `web_extract` takes `urls` (at most 5) and `char_limit` and returns page content as markdown, with no crawl tool and no LLM summarisation anywhere. The backend is `web.search_backend` or `web.extract_backend`, else `web.backend`, else autodetected from credentials in the order Tavily, Perplexity, Exa, Parallel, Keenable, Firecrawl, SearXNG, Brave, DuckDuckGo, then any other registered provider, then the keyless tier. The keyless tier is a round-robin ring of anonymous endpoints (Exa MCP, Parallel MCP, Firecrawl, Keenable) with failover on rate limits, controlled by `web.keyless_fallback`, `web.keyless_rescue` and `web.provider_tier.<name>`; a failed keyed call gets one rescue through the ring. Every extract URL is checked for embedded secrets (which refuses the whole call), SSRF and the website blocklist before fetch, and the final URL after redirects is checked again.

- `web_tools.go` — schemas, backend selection, `WebSearchTool`, `WebExtractTool`, URL validation, final-URL gating, extract timeout `web.extract_timeout` (120 s), registration with availability check `CheckWebAPIKey`
- `web_providers.go` — `WebProvider` contract and result shapes, provider registry per profile scope, provider resolution, keyless ring and its MCP and HTTP clients, origin HTTP status detection, shared HTTP helpers
- `web_rescue.go` — one-shot keyless rescue of a failed search or extract, never for website-policy refusals

#### Web result caching, truncation and debug logs

Searches are memoised and single-flighted in memory per provider, normalised query and bucketed limit. Extracts are cached on disk under `cache/web/` for `web.cache_ttl_minutes` (20, clamped 1 to 1,440; `web.cache_enabled` turns both caches off), except local development hosts and `web.cache_exempt_hosts`. A page over the character budget (`char_limit`, else `web.extract_char_limit`, else 15,000) returns a head and tail window with a footer naming the full text stored under `cache/web/` (capped at 2,000,000 characters) and the `read_file` call to page it, and inline base64 images become `[IMAGE: alt]` placeholders.

- `web_cache.go` — search memo, extract index `cache/web/extract-index.json` (500 entries), cache gates, result-count buckets 10, 20, 50, 100
- `web_truncate.go` — character budget clamps (2,000 to 500,000), head and tail truncation with footer, full-text storage, binary payload detection
- `web_debug.go` — `DebugSession`: when `WEB_TOOLS_DEBUG` or `VISION_TOOLS_DEBUG` is true, records tool calls to a JSON file in the profile `logs/` directory

#### Web provider backends

One provider per vendor, registered as bundled plugins by `pkg/builtin/webbackends`; each returns the shared search and extract shapes and a setup schema for the tools picker. Vendor SDK request shapes, retries and headers are reproduced over plain HTTP.

- `web_provider_firecrawl.go` — Firecrawl search and scrape for keyed (`FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`), self-hosted (`FIRECRAWL_API_URL`) and keyless routes
