- `web_provider_tavily.go` — Tavily search and extract with `TAVILY_API_KEY` or keyless access
- `web_provider_exa.go` — Exa search and contents with `EXA_API_KEY`
- `web_provider_parallel.go` — Parallel search and extract with `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, `PARALLEL_BASE_URL`, `PARALLEL_SEARCH_MODE` and SDK-style retries
- `web_provider_perplexity.go` — Perplexity Search API with `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY`; extract returns per-URL snippets from a relevance query
- `web_provider_keenable.go` — Keenable search and fetch, keyed or keyless
- `web_provider_brave.go` — Brave free-tier search with `BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY`, count 1 to 20, search only
- `web_provider_searxng.go` — user-hosted SearXNG instance at `SEARXNG_URL`, search only
- `web_provider_xai.go` — search through the xAI `/responses` endpoint with Grok's `web_search` tool, config under `web.xai`, one OAuth refresh on 401
- `web_provider_openai_native.go` — [stub] picker entry for provider-side search on the Codex Responses transport; its own `Search` only returns an unsupported error
- `web_sdk_client.go` — provider credential lookup that fails closed when profiles are multiplexed without a bound secret scope, cached vendor clients, timeouts
- `web_httpx.go`, `web_requests.go` — [py-shim] stand-ins for `httpx` calls (Tavily, Brave, SearXNG, Perplexity, xAI) and `requests` calls (Exa, Keenable) with their exception types

#### DuckDuckGo metasearch provider

[py-shim] A port of the Python `ddgs` library that gives a free search backend with no key: it queries Brave, DuckDuckGo, Google, Mojeek, Startpage, Yahoo, Yandex, Bing, Wikipedia and Grokipedia HTML endpoints with browser-like headers, parses results with an XPath engine, deduplicates by URL and ranks by how many engines agree. Each search runs in a re-executed copy of the icebath binary (hidden first argument `__icebath_ddgs_worker__`) so it can be killed at the 30-second cap or on interrupt; `DDGS_PROXY` sets a proxy.

- `web_provider_ddgs.go` — provider, worker spawn, bounded wait and reap, worker main, `DispatchDDGSWorkerEntry` called from `cmd/icebath` startup
- `web_ddgs_client.go` — engine table, HTTP client, per-engine result extraction, aggregation and ranking
- `web_ddgs_html.go` — XPath 1.0 parser and evaluator over an lxml-style tree
- `web_ddgs_libxml2.go` — libxml2-compatible HTML tree construction over an HTML5 token stream
- `web_ddgs_libxml2_data.go`, `web_ddgs_impersonate_data.go` — [data] libxml2 element tables and the browser user-agent and header profiles of the `primp` client
- `web_ddgs_{unix,windows}.go` — worker process attributes and termination per OS (2 variants)

#### URL safety and website blocklist

Shared by the web, vision, browser and media tools. `IsSafeURL` fails closed: only http and https, authority ambiguity rejected, cloud metadata hosts and addresses (169.254.169.254 and peers, `metadata.google.internal`) always blocked, private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT and reserved ranges blocked unless `security.allow_private_urls`, with `security.fake_ip_ranges` for local proxies. `NewSSRFSafeClient` re-validates DNS at connect time, dials the vetted address and checks every redirect. The website policy reads `security.website_blocklist` (`enabled`, `domains`, `shared_files`) with a 30-second cache and fails open on a malformed policy.

- `url_safety.go` — URL normalisation, address classification, `IsSafeURL` (a DNS failure passes only when a proxy env var is set; one hard-coded host may resolve privately), `IsAlwaysBlockedURL`, SSRF-safe HTTP client (8 connect addresses, IPv4 first)
- `website_policy.go` — rule normalisation to hosts, wildcard and parent-domain matching, shared blocklist files, `CheckWebsiteAccess`

#### xAI: `x_search` and shared credentials

`x_search` (toolset `x_search`, off by default, excluded from the `icebath_core` build) takes `query`, `allowed_x_handles`, `excluded_x_handles` (10 each), `from_date`, `to_date`, `enable_image_understanding` and `enable_video_understanding`, and calls the xAI Responses API with the built-in `x_search` tool, returning text and inline citations. Config: `x_search.model` (default `grok-4.5`), `reasoning_effort`, timeout 180 s, 2 retries.

- `x_search.go` — schema, handle and date validation, request, retry, citation extraction, error envelopes
- `xai_http.go` — bearer resolution (explicit `XAI_API_KEY` over SuperGrok OAuth from the credential pool), base URL override pinned to the `x.ai` origin (`ICEBATH_XAI_BASE_URL`, `XAI_BASE_URL`), icebath user agent
- `xai_default_headers.go` — default headers for every xAI client in the application

#### Secret redaction for tool output, logs and egress

Layered on the pattern tables of the first part (`file_safety.go`). `RedactSensitiveTextWith` masks known key prefixes, assignments, `Authorization` and secret headers, Telegram tokens, private key blocks, URL credentials, JWTs, session links, form bodies and phone numbers; vault-registered values are always scrubbed, the rest follows the profile's `security.redact_secrets` setting (on by default) unless forced. Terminal output gets the assignment pass only for environment dumps and reads of secret files, so source code is not mangled. Plugins may add token patterns, which are rejected when unbounded or structurally unsafe.

- `redact_terminal.go` — `RedactOptions`, the main pass order, `RedactTerminalCommandOutput`, `RedactForEgress` (forced, with a bearer sweep, returning a fixed marker on failure), `IsEnvDumpCommand`, `CommandApprovalIdentity`
- `redact_plugin_patterns.go` — active prefix matcher, `RegisterRedactionPatterns` with validation and rejection rules, prefix search used by the URL secret guard
- `redact_policy.go` — per-profile switch, `ForceSecretRedaction`, `RedactingHandler` that redacts every log record under the record's profile
- `redact_logging.go` — hands the redacting handler and policy resolver to `pkg/logging` at init
- `redact_profile_text.go` — redaction of text under the context profile's switch
- `redact_cdp.go` — masks query credentials and userinfo passwords in browser CDP endpoint URLs
- `redact_sub_scan.go` — [py-shim] match scanning with Python `re.sub` lookbehind semantics
- `redact_key_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the secret-keyword key test for `pkg/tuihost`

#### Result persistence, spill files and truncation

A tool result over its threshold is written to disk and replaced by a `<persisted-output>` block with a preview and the path; `EnforceTurnBudget` keeps persisting the largest results until the turn's total fits. Host-side files go to `cache/spillover/` in the profile home (verified size, exclusive create that never follows symlinks), remote sandboxes get the file under a temp `icebath-results` directory. Spill files are pruned once per process when older than the session retention window (`sessions.retention_days`, default 90, floor 24 hours) and no transcript row still references them. Hook output over `hooks.output_spill.max_chars` (10,000) spills to `hook_outputs/<session>/`.

- `result_storage.go` — `MaybePersistToolResult`, `EnforceTurnBudget`, MCP envelope unwrapping, spillover cleanup, `SpillIfOversized`, `OpenExclusive`, `WriteTextExclusive`
- `result_storage_{unix,windows}.go` — the no-follow open flag per OS (2 variants)
- `truncate.go` — `tool_output.max_bytes` (50,000), `max_lines` (2,000) and `max_line_length` (2,000) per profile, `TruncateHeadTail` with a 40% head and 60% tail split

#### Document extraction for `read_file`

`read_file` renders documents as text. Notebooks, `.docx`, `.xlsx` and SQLite files have in-house extractors; other office formats, PDF, EPUB, RTF and CSV go through the embedded anydoc converter. A PDF with pages lacking a text layer goes to Firecrawl Parse when `FIRECRAWL_API_KEY` is set and `file_tools.hosted_ocr` is not false, else to local `pdftoppm`, `pdftotext` and `tesseract` when installed, else returns a warning naming the scanned pages.

- `read_extract.go` — extractor routing by signature then extension, anydoc call, OCR paths, PDF coverage note, notebook cells with compact outputs, docx paragraphs, xlsx sheets as tab-separated rows, SQLite schema with row counts and first rows
- `read_extract_xml.go` — [py-shim] `ElementTree`-style XML tree used by the docx and xlsx extractors
- `read_extract_json.go` — [py-shim] Python `repr` and `str` of decoded JSON values for notebook rendering
- `magic_signatures.go` — binary signature table (PNG, JPEG, PDF, ZIP, ELF and others) shared by the file and web tools
- `utf16_bom.go` — strict UTF-16 decoding of files that start with a byte order mark

#### File tool state: read tracking, write guards, patches and directory hints

Helpers behind `read_file`, `write_file` and `patch` of the first part. Per task, the tracker remembers what was read (dedup of unchanged rereads, a 60-second not-found cache, read coverage per file version) and refuses `write_file` over a file the task has not fully read or that changed since. Write guards block system paths and the Docker socket, ask a human for every write to `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `SOUL.md` and `.cursorrules` (`security.protected_instruction_files`, `security.protected_instruction_extra_patterns`), refuse text writes over binary documents, and reject content that is read_file display output.

- `read_tracking.go` — per-task tracker with capped ordered maps, file version hashing, full-write baselines carried across own patches, staleness warnings, consecutive patch failure counts
- `write_guards.go` — sensitive path, protected instruction, approval-required path, cross-profile mirror, binary document and stale overwrite checks
- `path_security.go` — control-character test for paths and `ValidateWithinDir` with symlinks resolved
- `patch_parser.go` — parser and applier for V4A patches (`*** Begin Patch` with Add, Update, Delete and Move operations), validation before any write, hints on no-match and ambiguity
- `subdirectory_hints.go` — when a tool call first touches a subdirectory, loads its `AGENTS.override.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` or `.cursorrules` (32,000 characters, 5 ancestors) and returns it for the executor to attach to the result

#### Staged write approval for memory and skills

When `memory.write_approval` or `skills.write_approval` is on, writes from background review forks and all skill writes are staged as JSON records under `pending/<subsystem>/` instead of applied, and foreground memory writes ask the user inline (staged when nobody can answer); the user reviews staged records with `/memory pending` or `/skills pending`.

- `write_approval.go` — gate decision, record staging, listing, discard and counts, one-line skill gist, unified diffs for pending skill writes including batches

#### `search_files` engine

Implements content and filename search for the `search_files` tool on any backend through shell commands. Content search uses ripgrep (the package-manager-pinned binary or one on the host, version 14 or newer) with a `grep` fallback; filename search uses ripgrep or `find`. Dependency and cache directories (`node_modules`, `.git`, `venv`, `dist` and others) are pruned, macOS protected home folders are skipped on broad searches, and unreadable paths are summarised instead of failing.

- `search_files.go` — entry and dispatch, pagination, output parsing with context lines, multi-path queries, diagnostics and warnings, not-found suggestions
- `search_files_rg.go` — ripgrep resolution and capability check, bounded native run with capped stderr, zero-match hints
- `search_files_find.go` — `find` and `grep` paths, prune expressions, gitignore filtering, modified-time ordering, single admission per search root
- `search_files_{unix,windows}.go` — chdir error probe per OS (2 variants)

#### Vision: `vision_analyze`, `video_analyze` and image routing

`vision_analyze` takes `image_url` (http, https, local path or data URL), `question` and an optional `region` crop; `video_analyze` takes `video_url` and `question` (about 50 MB maximum). When the main model accepts images in tool results the image is attached natively to the conversation; otherwise an auxiliary vision model answers. Capability is decided by config override, the managed local runtime, the models.dev catalog and an Ollama probe; an explicit `auxiliary.vision` backend wins in auto mode, and `auxiliary.vision.download_timeout`, `auxiliary.vision.max_concurrency` and `auxiliary.video.model` tune the calls. Images are downloaded through the SSRF-safe client with the website blocklist applied before and after redirects, normalised to a supported format, downscaled to 1,568 pixels and `vision.embed_target_bytes`, and limited to 20 MB of base64; a subagent may embed one image at most 3 times.

- `vision.go` — schemas, media download with retry, native tool-result envelope, auxiliary model call, resize on size rejection, bounded CPU worker pool, private cache directory
- `vision_routing.go` — `DecideImageInputMode` (native or text), capability probes, per-provider tool-result image support
- `vision_history.go` — embed byte budget, per-session repeat cap, detection of images already attached to the user turn
- `vision_image_prep.go` — [py-shim] Pillow-compatible decoding of PNG, APNG, GIF, WebP and JPEG/MPO frames, decompression-bomb check, MIME sniffing, resampling and re-encoding
- `vision_raster_size.go` — [port-artifact] exports first-frame dimensions for `pkg/agent`

#### Speech text preparation

The `text_to_speech` tool lives in `pkg/media`; this part only prepares text for speech and marks voice turns.

- `tts_text_normalize.go` — strips markdown and code, expands symbols, units, currencies and temperature ranges into words, drops dense identifiers, caps at 4,000 characters by default
- `tts_tool.go` — table of platforms that need Ogg Opus voice notes (Telegram, Matrix, Feishu, WhatsApp, Signal)
- `voice_live_turn_note.go` — system note prepended to a turn delegated from live voice conversation

#### `session_search`

`session_search` reads the session database with no LLM. Arguments select one of four shapes: `query` runs FTS5 discovery (default 3 sessions, maximum 10, top hit hydrated, lineage roots deduplicated, `sort`, `after`, `before`, `role_filter`, `exclude_session_ids`, `detail`); `session_id` with `around_message_id` and `window` scrolls; `session_id` alone reads a session; no arguments lists recent sessions. `profile` reads another profile's database. Kanban, subagent and tool sessions are hidden and cron sessions ranked lower.

- `session_search.go` — schema, argument handling, discovery, read, scroll and browse, `@session:<profile>/<id>` links, inline executor registration

#### `todo_list`

In-memory revisioned task list, one per agent session, rehydrated by the agent from session history and re-injected into the prompt after context compression. Parameters `todos` (items with `id`, `content`, `status`, optional `parent`) and `merge`; at most 256 items of 4,000 characters; calling with no parameters reads the list.

- `todo.go` — `TodoStore`, write, merge and restore, parent sanitising, injection text for the prompt, legacy alias `todo`

#### Projects: database, `icebath project` and `desktop_project`

Named workspaces with folders, stored per profile in `projects.db` (tables `projects`, `project_folders`, `project_meta`, `discovered_repos`). The CLI offers `create`, `list`, `show`, `add-folder`, `remove-folder`, `rename`, `set-primary`, `use`, `archive`, `restore` and `bind-board`. The model tool `desktop_project` (toolset `project`, folded in only by the TUI) has actions `create`, `switch` and `list` and moves the live session's workspace through a callback the TUI server installs. The `discovered_repos` table is created but never read or written.

- `projects_db.go` — schema, slug rules, CRUD, primary folder, archive, active project, path lookup, branch name helper
- `projects_db_errors.go` — argument rejection error type
- `projects_command.go` — `icebath project` subcommands, with board binding through a hook from the extras build
- `project_tool.go` — tool schema and handlers, workspace callback

#### Git worktrees: creation per session, resume and exit

`icebath -w` and the TUI create an isolated worktree at `<repo>/.worktrees/<name>` on branch `icebath/<name>` (name `icebath-<8 hex>` unless given, sanitised to 40 characters), based on the fetched upstream or default branch when `worktree_sync` is on, else local HEAD, with a retry from HEAD when the remote base fails. `.worktrees/` is added to `.gitignore`, entries of `.worktreeinclude` are copied or linked in, and the tree is locked with reason `icebath pid=<pid>` plus the session database path when the launcher retains it for a session. At exit, on a real terminal, a dirty or unpushed tree that no other process is using prompts keep (the default), archive or discard; removal of clean trees is done by the launcher in `pkg/app`. Trees the TUI created are recorded so a resumed session whose tree was removed gets it recreated.

- `worktree_ops_setup.go` — `SetupWorktree`, base resolution with fetch timeout, failed-add cleanup, bounded geometric repack and commit-graph maintenance
- `worktree_ops_repo_root.go` — repository root lookup with Git Bash path normalisation
- `worktree_exit.go` — exit-time state and the keep, archive or discard prompt
- `tui_worktree_resume.go` — `tui_worktrees.json` record (500 entries) of trees the TUI created, and recreation of a removed tree when its session is resumed
- `worktree_tui_launch_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports retention and in-use tests for `pkg/app`

#### Worktree retention: sweep, archive, audit and `icebath worktree`

A sweep at launch and from cron removes trees idle past 24 hours (72 hours for trees not named `icebath-*` or `subagent-*`; kanban `t_<hex>` trees are skipped) when clean and pushed or merged, never when locked by a live process or served by a resumable session or cron job. With `worktrees.archive_dirty` (default true) dirty or unpushed trees are first snapshotted to `refs/icebath/archive/<name>` and stay restorable until `worktrees.archive_retention_days` (30) passes, and `worktrees.max_total_gb` sets a size budget. With archiving off and no budget the older pruner runs instead, which keeps dirty or unpushed trees and warns about ones older than 7 days; either path warns at 10 trees or 5 GB and deletes orphaned `icebath/` branches. `icebath worktree list|prune|restore` (aliases `ls`, `audit`; options `--repo`, `--older-than`, dry run, trees or branches only, JSON, `--path`) reports the plan, reclaims trees and branches, and recreates an archived tree.

- `worktree_ops.go` — git helpers, dirty and unpushed tests, shallow-clone deepening, patch-equivalence verdict cache, merged pull-request probe through `gh`, lock liveness, served-tree test against the session database and cron store, prune tiers, orphaned branch cleanup
- `worktree_sweep.go` — `worktrees.*` settings, live-process detection per tree, sweep planning and budget, archive-then-remove, `RunSweep`
- `worktree_archive.go` — snapshot of tracked, staged and untracked content through a temporary index (per-file cap `worktrees.archive_max_file_mb`, 50; trees with submodule work refused) into an archive ref, listing, pruning, `RestoreArchive`
- `worktree_retention.go` — removal blockers: embedded repositories, hidden index edits, refs no branch reaches
- `worktree_gc.go` — tree size through `du` and directory summary
- `worktree_gc_audit.go` — attended audit and reclaim of trees and local branches, external worktree registrations
- `worktree_cmd.go` — `list`, `prune` and `restore <name>` command bodies and their text and JSON output

#### Git status probes and working diff

Read-only git helpers for display surfaces: the branch and repository root shown in the TUI and session lists, and the diff behind the gateway `/diff` command.

- `tui_git_probe.go` — branch name and repository root lookups (1.5 s git timeout, single-flight cache, misses cached 30 s) for the TUI status line and session inventory
- `tui_git_probe_swap.go` — [test-support] probe runner swap
- `working_diff.go` — `CollectWorkingDiff` for the gateway `/diff` command in modes `working`, `staged` and `all`, with git hooks, fsmonitor and external diff drivers disabled; `HardenGitArgv`

#### NeMo Relay integration

Optional instrumentation through NVIDIA NeMo Relay, a Python runtime loaded by `pkg/relayhost` and provisioned with `icebath pm install --extra nemo-relay`. One Relay host exists per profile; it maintains a scope stack (`icebath.session`, `icebath.turn`, `icebath.logical_llm_call`), rotates session segments, parents subagent scopes under the spawning turn, and lets Relay plugins intercept tool requests or run tool and LLM calls through a managed pipeline. Relay is active only when a `plugins.toml` is discovered (user or system `nemo-relay` config directory) or `ICEBATH_NEMO_RELAY_PLUGINS_TOML` is set; otherwise a no-op host is used and failures never break a turn. Twelve legacy `ICEBATH_NEMO_RELAY_AT*` exporter variables are only detected to warn.

- `relay_runtime.go` — binding surface types, `RelayRuntime` with session scopes, operation leases, plugin configuration lifetime, scope operation timeout (10 s), exit handlers
- `relay_coordinator.go` — host registry, no-op host, conversation leases, `BeginTurn` and `EndTurn`, compaction notice, current-turn lookup
- `relay_tools.go` — runs one tool dispatch through the Relay tool pipeline and reports the final arguments
- `relay_binding_llm.go` — LLM binding types, codecs and awaitable handling for provider calls
- `relay_demand.go` — readiness check, demand detection, plugin file discovery, unprovisioned notice
- `relay_plugin_cutover.go` — plugin config env var name and the legacy exporter variable list

#### Desktop application requirements for plugin servers

A plugin MCP server or skill may declare an `app` block per OS and a `requires` block (app, minimum version, GPU). The resolver locates the application (paths, commands, Windows uninstall registry), reads its version (PE resource, registry, macOS plist), reads a runtime `server.json` for a live endpoint and token, and can probe it with an MCP initialize on loopback; the verdict (`available`, `missing_app`, `version_too_old`, `unsupported_os`, `unsupported_gpu`) decides whether the server is offered.

- `platform_declaration.go` — parsing and validation of declarations, process-wide declaration registry with change callback
- `platform_resolver.go` — `PlatformAppResolver` (locate, inspect, endpoint, probe), version comparison, `PlatformAvailabilityOf`; `PlatformSkillAppAvailability` has no caller
- `platform_resolver_{unix,windows}.go` — pid liveness, PE version and uninstall registry reads per OS (2 variants)

#### Session identity, per-thread callbacks and plugin dispatch context

Per-turn session identity (platform, chat, thread, user, session key and id, message id, profile, cwd) is bound on the tool `Env` and read by tools through `ICEBATH_SESSION_*` names; the storage mechanics emulate Python context variables and thread locals.

- `session_context.go` — `SetSessionVars`, forked contexts for spawned tasks, async-delivery and history-delivery capability flags, messaging-surface test
- `thread_context.go` — [py-shim] goroutine-local storage and `PropagateContextToThread`, standing in for `threading.local` and `contextvars.copy_context`
- `thread_scoped_output.go` — [py-shim] stdout and stderr proxy that silences output per context, standing in for swapping `sys.stdout`
- `vault_prompts.go` — per-thread callbacks for password-manager unlock, one-time code and save-login prompts used by the browser vault
- `plugin_dispatch.go` — `DispatchForPlugin`: runs a tool by name in a profile scope for a plugin, carrying task, session and tool-call ids
- `owned_kanban_task.go` — binds the tool env on a context; `ICEBATH_KANBAN_TASK` ownership and the fence that denies kanban mutations from delegated children
- `oneshot_footprint.go` — freezes whether a session is a one-shot query and supplies the skills guidance used in that case
- `worker_persistence.go` — worker persistence error type and the non-dispatcher-owned context marker

#### Turn outcome, onboarding and user-facing copy

Fixed texts and small mappings that the CLI, gateway and TUI share so every surface reports an outcome the same way. None of it is tool code.

- `turn_exit.go` — process exit codes from a turn result: 0, 1, 130 on interrupt, and for kanban workers 75 for transient provider failures and 78 for ones needing an operator
- `turn_failure_copy.go` — plain-language failure clauses per classified reason and chat copy per failure code (context overflow, truncated reply, invalid response and others); English templates with `{field}` substitution, not localised
- `tool_outcome.go` — `RefusedResult` and `ToolOutcome` (failed, refused, reason) for display surfaces
- `tool_progress_relay.go` — throttled `tool.progress` events (500 ms) with percent when a total is known
- `onboarding.go` — first-contact system note with an optional profile-building offer (`onboarding.profile_build`), one-time busy-input and tool-progress tips recorded under `onboarding.seen`
- `markdown_tables.go` — realigns markdown tables to display width, switching to a vertical layout when wider than the terminal

#### Prompt-injection threat scanner

Advisory text scanner that returns the ids of matched attack patterns (instruction override, role hijack, command-and-control phrasing, secret exfiltration, agent config tampering). Context files and the output of untrusted tools (`web_*`, `browser_*`, `mcp_*`) are scanned with it; `pkg/memory` has a separate scanner of its own.

- `threat_patterns.go` — 36 regex patterns in three nested scopes (`all`, `context`, `strict`) plus invisible-character detection, over the first 65,536 characters of NFKC-normalised text

#### Reviewer subagent and subagent transcripts

Two helpers around delegation: the `/review` slash command of the gateway and TUI, which sends recent conversation to an independent reviewer subagent, and the lookup of a finished child's transcript log for display.

- `review_engine.go` — `/review`: snapshots recent messages, carries the parent's loaded skills, and dispatches a background reviewer through `delegate_task` with credentials from `auxiliary.review`
- `subagent_transcripts.go` — finds the live transcript log a delegated child stored, walking up to 8 spawning sessions

#### Sleep-aware clock

There is no sleep tool; this is a clock for timeouts that must not count time the machine spent suspended.

- `sleep_clock.go`, `sleep_clock_{other,windows}.go` — a clock that stops while the machine sleeps and `SleepWatch`, used by the provider stream watchdogs so a suspended laptop does not trip timeouts

#### Shims and small shared helpers

Leftovers with no concern of their own: one init hook, a bridge to the package manager, Python value helpers, and re-exports of unexported symbols defined in the first part of the package.

- `platform_secret_env.go` — names of secrets declared by bundled and user platform plugin manifests, fed to the child-environment scrubber and the gateway
- `pm_bridge.go` — thin calls into the package manager for managed binaries and isolated Python tools
- `py_values.go`, `py_parse.go`, `smallutil.go` — [py-shim] ordered dict literals, `json.dumps` without ASCII escaping, Python `int()` and `float()` parsing, list helpers
- `managed_worker_env_export.go`, `msys_path_export.go`, `python_call_args_export.go`, `run_active_work_verb_export.go`, `run_inbound_export.go`, `secret_scope_export.go` — [port-artifact] re-exports of credential scrubbing, Git Bash path conversion, call-argument decoding, async delegation states, session context copy and scoped secret lookup

### `pkg/tools/anydoc` — embedded WebAssembly document-to-Markdown converter

*2 files, 199 Go lines*

Wraps the anydoc 0.2.4 Rust crate compiled to `wasm32-wasip1` and run in-process with the wazero runtime; no external binary is needed. The module is compiled once per process with native code cached under the OS cache directory at `icebath/wazero`, and each conversion runs in a fresh module instance. Its only caller is the `read_file` document extractor in `pkg/tools`.

#### Converter and module

One Go wrapper and the module it embeds; the guest exports `anydoc_alloc`, `anydoc_dealloc` and `anydoc_to_markdown` and returns a status of ok, error or no-format.

- `anydoc.go` — `ToMarkdown(data, path)`: format from content with the extension as fallback; accepted extensions doc, docx, docm, odt, pdf, ppt, pps, pot, pptx, pptm, ppsx, ppsm, rtf, epub, xlsx, xlsm, xlsb, xls, ods, odp, csv; typed errors for needs-OCR (with page list), no text layer and encrypted
- `anydoc.wasm` — [data] the 5.9 MB compiled module, embedded with `go:embed`

## 6. MCP, LSP, code execution, browser

### `pkg/mcp` — Model Context Protocol client: connects configured servers, registers their tools, runs their OAuth, and backs `icebath mcp`

*156 files, 31,464 Go lines*

The MCP client of the harness (the MCP server mode behind `icebath mcp serve` is not here). It reads `mcp_servers` from the profile `config.yaml` plus servers declared by portable plugins, connects each one over stdio, Streamable HTTP or legacy SSE, and registers every tool into the `pkg/tools` registry as `mcp__<server>__<tool>` under toolset `mcp-<server>`. Callers: `cmd/icebath` and `pkg/gatewayrun` (startup, background discovery, reconcile on reload, shutdown), `pkg/agent` (tool snapshot refresh, late connections), `pkg/tuiserver` and `pkg/gateway` (OAuth sessions, connection cards, editor-session servers, event webhooks), `pkg/commands` (`icebath mcp`, `icebath tools`), and `pkg/codeexec` (reuses the stdio transport for the cua-driver). It owns, under the profile home: `mcp-tokens/` (OAuth tokens, client registrations, metadata, refresh locks), `cache/mcp_schema_cache.json`, `logs/mcp-stderr.log`, `.mcp-discovery.lock`, `mcp_event_subscriptions.json` and `mcp-installs/`. All connection state is process-global maps guarded by one mutex and keyed by `(scope, server name)` so one gateway process can serve several profiles and editor sessions. The protocol, transports and OAuth are hand-written (no SDK); much of the remaining bulk reproduces Python SDK text and pydantic or urllib behaviour byte for byte.

#### JSON-RPC session and protocol negotiation

One `Session` per connection: request and response matching, server-to-client requests, notifications, and the handshake. The client offers handshake revision `2025-11-25`, accepts `2024-11-05` through `2025-11-25`, and also knows a stateless `2026-07-28` era reached through `server/discover`, where every request carries protocol version, client info and capabilities in `_meta`. Per-server `protocol` selects `auto` (handshake first, discover only when the server rejects it as modern-only), `stateless` or `legacy`. Client identity is `icebath-agent`. `roots` is not implemented: the capability is never advertised and a `roots/list` request is answered "Method not found"; `prompts/list_changed` and `resources/list_changed` are logged and ignored; only `tools/list_changed` triggers work.

- `jsonrpc.go` — JSON-RPC 2.0 message type, constructors, id normalisation (numeric and string ids share one pending map), batch decoding, standard error codes
- `protocol.go` — wire structs for initialize, tools, resources, prompts, sampling, elicitation, logging and progress; supported and latest protocol version constants; the method-name table (including the unused `roots/list`)
- `session.go` — `Session`: read loop, pending-request map, answers `ping`, `sampling/createMessage` and `elicitation/create`, routes list-changed, log, progress and cancel notifications, paginated `tools/list`, `resources/list`, `prompts/list` (50-page cap), `tools/call` with progress; also the package's goroutine "loop" that every server task runs on, `runOnLoop` with timeout and user-interrupt polling, the cross-process `.mcp-discovery.lock`, reconnect signalling, connection keys and their rekeying under a scope, and credential redaction of error text
- `session_inputs.go` — 2026-era extras: `_meta` stamping, "input required" results answered through the elicitor or sampler (16 rounds max), and the `-32042` URL-elicitation-required error retried every 10 s until the browser step completes
- `errors.go` — failure classification (permanent, auth, session expired, stream error, non-MCP endpoint, invalid URL), exception-group unwrapping carried over from Python, and the user-facing connect error text

#### Transports and HTTP plumbing

Three transports behind one `Transport` interface. Remote connects try Streamable HTTP first and fall back to SSE once when the initial connect is rejected (the fallback is latched for later reconnects, and the log tells the user to pin `transport: sse`). Every response body and every SSE event is capped at 10 MiB, a stdio line at 64 MiB, SSE reads time out after 300 s. Before a non-OAuth HTTP connect a 5 s HEAD/GET/POST preflight refuses URLs that answer 2xx with a non-MCP content type (`skip_preflight` disables it).

- `transport.go` — `Transport` interface, SSE event parser with per-event byte cap, and the body-capping `RoundTripper`
- `transport_stdio.go` — spawns the server in its own process group, newline-framed JSON-RPC over stdin and stdout, stderr handed to a sink, exposes pid and pgid
- `transport_http.go` — Streamable HTTP: POST per message, JSON or SSE answers, `Mcp-Session-Id` handling, `MCP-Protocol-Version` header, optional standalone GET stream, session-expired detection
- `transport_sse.go` — 2024-11-05 HTTP+SSE: GET stream, waits for the `endpoint` event, POSTs to the announced URL, one retry after a handled 401
- `httpclient.go` — the HTTP client all remote transports and probes share: TLS (`ssl_verify` as bool or CA path), mTLS, proxy mounts, a redirect boundary that drops configured credential headers on cross-origin redirects (`strict_redirect_headers`), last 4xx/5xx recorder, the `Authenticator` hook OAuth plugs into
- `tlscert.go` — loads `client_cert` and `client_key`, including PBES2/PBKDF2-encrypted PKCS#8 keys decrypted in-package
- `proxy.go`, `proxy_system_{darwin,other,windows}.go` — [py-shim] urllib `getproxies` and `proxy_bypass` semantics: `*_proxy` and `no_proxy` env vars, then macOS and Windows system proxy settings; decides whether a server URL dials through a proxy

#### Server configuration, rendering and child environment

`mcp_servers.<name>` keys read by the code: `command`, `args`, `env`, `cwd` (stdio); `url`, `headers`, `transport`, `auth`, `oauth{client_id, client_secret, scope, redirect_uri, redirect_host, redirect_port, client_name, client_metadata_url, cimd, flow, timeout, user_agent, token_endpoint_auth_method, application_type}`, `ssl_verify`, `client_cert`, `client_key`, `strict_redirect_headers`, `identity_header{name, value, value_from}`, `skip_preflight` (remote); `enabled`, `timeout`, `connect_timeout` (60 s), `keepalive_interval` (180 s for remote), `lazy`, `idle_timeout_seconds` and `max_lifetime_seconds` (also under `lifecycle`), `protocol`, `trust` (`full` or `untrusted`), `tools{include, exclude, resources, prompts}`, `sampling{...}`, `elicitation{enabled}`, `events`, `supports_parallel_tool_calls`, `tool_costs`, `spend_limit`, `cost_unit`. Global keys: `timeouts.mcp.tool_call` (300 s default), `mcp.discovery_concurrency` (4), `mcp_discovery_timeout`, `mcp_single_query_discovery_timeout`. Nothing loads in safe mode (`ICEBATH_SAFE_MODE` or the safe worker).

- `config.go` — loads and renders entries (`${VAR}` from profile secrets, Cursor-style `${env:VAR}`, `${userHome}`, `${workspaceFolder}`, `${workspaceFolderBasename}`), remembers which references missed so a reconnect re-renders only those, refuses remote entries with unresolved references; builds the stdio child env from a fixed allowlist plus secret-source vars and the entry's `env`; resolves the command (managed `npx`/`npm`/`node`/`uv`/`uvx` from `pkg/pm` first, then the child PATH), swaps `npx -y pkg` for an already cached bin; tees child stderr into `logs/mcp-stderr.log` with a readable tail; identity header and trust normalisation; merges portable-plugin servers (native entries win); a `ServerConfig` struct that nothing constructs
- `security.go` — `ValidateServerEntry`: drops entries containing indicators of a June 2026 backdoor campaign (an SSH public-key fragment, the string `hermes-0day`, one IP prefix and two IP addresses) and entries whose command is a shell interpreter with network egress or writes to SSH keys, PAM, sudoers, cron, systemd or shell rc files
- `nodeabi.go` — recognises a Node native-addon ABI mismatch in a dead server's stderr and replaces the connect error with the exact rebuild or npx-cache-delete command for the host shell
- `access_{unix,windows}.go` — executable-bit check used by command resolution

#### Connection lifecycle: server tasks, discovery, reconnect and shutdown

Each server is a long-lived `serverTask` goroutine that connects, serves, reconnects, parks or recycles. Rules: 3 initial connect attempts, and after a first success up to 5 consecutive unhealthy reconnects, each with jittered exponential backoff capped at 60 s, then the server parks; a permanent error (auth, non-MCP endpoint) parks at once, except one grace reconnect for an auth error on a session that had proven healthy. A parked server drops its tools and self-probes every 300 s (with interactive OAuth suppressed) while it is still configured and enabled; a discovery pass does not nudge an OAuth-parked server until its token or client file changes. Remote sessions get a keepalive `ping` (30 s RPC timeout, `tools/list` instead when the server lacks ping); stdio sessions can be recycled after `idle_timeout_seconds` or `max_lifetime_seconds` and respawn lazily on the next call. Failed connects get a per-server cooldown doubling from 30 s to 10 min; tool calls have a circuit breaker (3 consecutive failures, 60 s cooldown) that distinguishes "server unreachable" from "server rejected the calls". `lazy: true` servers register from the schema cache without connecting and connect on first tool use.

- `server.go` — `serverTask` state machine: run loop, park and revival, retry budgets, keepalive, stdio recycle deadlines, in-flight call tracking so a teardown fails calls fast, stdio child death watcher, tools refresh scheduling, start and shutdown
- `server_transport.go` — per-transport runners: resolves launch inputs, OSV malware preflight on the stdio argv (12 s budget, proceeds on timeout), spawns and ledgers stdio children, content-type preflight, OAuth provider attach, HTTP-to-SSE fallback, handshake then `tools/list` then registration
- `manager.go` — the global connection ledgers (servers, owners, errors, cooldowns, breaker counters, trust levels, read-only hints, cost policies, lazy configs), scope resolution for multiplexed profiles, breaker and cooldown bookkeeping, `mcp.discovery_concurrency`, the discovery-lock retry
- `discovery.go` — `Connect`, `ConnectAll`, `Reconcile` (tear down removed or disabled servers, connect new ones), `Restart` (only servers whose resolved launch inputs changed), `Status` (connected, disabled, connecting, failed, lazy, configured), `Probe` (connect, list, disconnect, register nothing), lazy registration from cache and lazy connect on first use, 120 s per connect wave and 300 s per pass
- `health.go` — on `tools/list_changed`: re-list and swap registry entries in place so live handlers survive, deregistering only names this server still owns
- `lifecycle.go`, `lifecycle_{unix,windows}.go` — `ShutdownMCPServers` (parallel close under a caller-given timeout, 15 s from reconcile and editor disconnect), re-registration of profiles that had adopted a shared connection, and the orphan sweep that SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs stdio children by process group, guarded by recorded start times against pid reuse and never touching gateway children
- `proc_{unix,windows}.go` — process-group creation, group signalling (taskkill on Windows), liveness probes and the advisory file lock primitive
- `liveness.go` — "application-backed" servers declared by portable plugins: liveness kinds `static`, `server_json` (URL, token and pid read from a runtime file the app writes) and `interactive_session`; produces the unavailable state, user action sentence and live endpoint override

#### Startup and background discovery

One background discovery goroutine per profile home, started at process start with interactive OAuth suppressed; agent construction waits a bounded time for it (1.5 s by default, 15 s for single-query runs). A toolsets selection given at launch (`SetServerFilter`, called from `cmd/icebath/fastpaths.go`) restricts which servers spawn.

- `startup.go` — `StartBackgroundDiscovery`, `WaitForDiscovery`, `JoinDiscovery`, `DiscoveryInFlight`, `SetServerFilter`, retry when a previous run connected nothing; `EnsureDiscoveryBeforeAgentBuild` has no caller outside tests
- `startup_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports `HasConfiguredServers` (config or enabled plugin MCP packages present)

#### Tool registration, naming, schema cache and call dispatch

Names are `mcp__` + sanitised server + `__` + sanitised tool (non `[A-Za-z0-9_]` becomes `_`), clamped to 64 characters with an 8-hex hash suffix. Beside native tools each server gets generated utility tools when it advertises the capability and config allows: `list_resources`, `read_resource`, `list_prompts`, `get_prompt`, and (only with `events: true`) `list_event_types`, `subscribe_event`, `unsubscribe_event`. `tools.include` is a whitelist that wins over `tools.exclude`; both take exact names or globs. A native tool shadows a colliding utility; other collisions skip every colliding entry; a built-in tool is never displaced. Tool descriptions are scanned for ten prompt-injection patterns (warning only) and stripped of Unicode tag characters. `trust: untrusted` servers require user approval (once, session, always) for every tool lacking `readOnlyHint: true`, showing masked arguments.

- `schema.go` — name sanitising and clamping, input-schema normalisation for every provider (`definitions` to `$defs`, object shape repair), utility tool schemas, include and exclude matching, the injection scan
- `registration.go` — builds candidates, resolves collisions, registers under toolset `mcp-<server>` with a server-name alias, records trust, read-only hints and cost policy, writes the schema cache, adopts an already connected server into another scope when the connection identity digest matches, freezes the manifest of an editor-session server (a changed manifest is refused as `acp_mcp_schema_changed`)
- `schemacache.go` — schema cache file under the home cache dir keyed by server name and a fingerprint of the connection-defining config; what makes `lazy` servers register without a connect
- `handlers.go` — the tool handler: trust gate and spend check, circuit breaker, wait for a session, serialised RPC per server, progress relay, recovery by one retry after a stdio child exit, a 401 (through the OAuth manager) or session expiry (write-capable calls are not replayed and report an unknown outcome); also the resource and prompt utility handlers and their rendering, and the registry availability check per server
- `content.go` — renders `CallToolResult`: text truncated head and tail at 2,000,000 characters, images, audio and embedded resources (50 MB cap) written to the media cache and referenced by path, up to 4 images attached natively for vision models, capped `structuredContent`, reserved `_meta` keys stripped
- `media_cache_bridge.go` — writes MCP image, audio and document bytes into the gateway media caches of the right profile home
- `costs.go` — declared tool costs (`tool_costs`, `spend_limit`, `cost_unit`): per-chat tally, reservation, booking and refund around a call, approval prompt once a call would pass the limit, tally moved when a session id rotates

#### Sampling and elicitation

Both are advertised by default per server (`sampling.enabled: false` or `elicitation.enabled: false` turns one off). Sampling runs through the auxiliary model client with `max_rpm` (10), `timeout` (30 s), `max_tokens_cap` (4096), `max_tool_rounds` (5), `allowed_models`, `model` override, `expose_client_tools` and `log_level`. Elicitation goes through the approval surface of the calling session and fails closed.

- `sampling.go` — `samplingHandler` (sliding 60 s rate limit, model allowlist, message and tool-call conversion to an OpenAI-shaped chat call, metrics) and `elicitationHandler` (consent prompt, schema summary, metrics, binding to the in-flight tool call's session)
- `elicitation_form.go` — form-mode elicitation: one question per property of a flat schema (string, number, integer, boolean, enum, titled choices) with range and format validation of each answer
- `elicitation_url.go` — URL-mode elicitation: consent text showing the full link and registrable domain with spoofing warnings, opens the link on accept, tracks the elicitation id until the server sends `notifications/elicitation/complete`

#### MCP events extension

Opt-in per server (`events: true`). The model subscribes to a server event; each occurrence is delivered by the server to a gateway webhook route and starts an agent run with the stored instructions. Requires `platforms.webhook.extra.public_url` to be HTTPS. Route names are `mcp-<server-slug>-<12 hex>`; each route gets a `whsec_` Standard Webhooks secret. Subscriptions are refreshed at 80% of their TTL (24 h default) with 30 s to 1 h backoff, and the route is removed when the server refuses with a terminal code.

- `events.go` — `events/list`, `events/subscribe`, `events/unsubscribe` calls, the three utility tool handlers, route writing, the per-server refresh loop, state in `mcp_event_subscriptions.json` (grants and cursors), `StoreEventCursor` and `DropEventState` for the gateway webhook handler
- `webhook_store_bridge.go` — locked read and atomic mutate of the webhook subscription store owned by `pkg/webhooksubs`

#### OAuth 2.1 for remote servers

`auth: oauth` attaches an `OAuthProvider` to the HTTP client. On a 401 it discovers protected-resource metadata (from `WWW-Authenticate` or well-known URLs), then authorization-server metadata, validates issuer and resource, identifies the client (a configured `client_id`; else, by default and unless `cimd: false`, custom client or redirect settings, or an earlier refusal by that server, the published Client ID Metadata Document `https://icebath.app/oauth/client-metadata.json` on loopback ports 27890 to 27894; else dynamic registration as "Icebath Agent"), runs authorization code with PKCE and the `resource` parameter, and stores tokens. A 403 `insufficient_scope` triggers step-up with the union of scopes. Refresh is fenced across processes by a lock file so a single-use refresh token is spent once. Non-interactive contexts (background discovery, gateway) never prompt and report `icebath mcp login <server>` instead. Special cases: Figma's remote MCP is registered under client name "Claude Code" with scope `mcp:connect`; Google authorization servers get offline-access parameters.

- `oauth.go` — resolves an `oauth` block into provider options: callback port choice (relay flow, cached redirect, CIMD port, configured, cached, ephemeral), redirect URI, client metadata, provider defaults, invalidation of tokens when the configured client changes, pre-registered client seeding, humanised registration errors, login timeout
- `oauth_flow.go` — `OAuthProvider`: discovery ladders, issuer and resource checks, CIMD or dynamic registration, PKCE authorization, code exchange, refresh with the fence and disk reload, 401 and step-up handling, a request clock that stops while waiting on a person
- `oauth_manager.go` — process-wide cache of one provider per home and server, reloads tokens when the file changes on disk, de-duplicates concurrent 401 recoveries, prefetches metadata, detects a client the server no longer knows
- `oauth_storage.go` — `mcp-tokens/<server>.json`, `.client.json`, `.meta.json`, `.cimd-off` and `.json.refresh.lock` (0600 in a 0700 directory), issuer binding, absolute expiry rebasing, snapshot and restore for rollback, credential stamp used to detect re-authorization
- `oauth_callback.go` — loopback callback listener on 127.0.0.1, port reservation, browser open, the stdin paste path (full redirect URL, bare query, or `skip`), SSH-session hints, interactive and non-interactive context flags
- `oauth_cimd.go` — Client ID Metadata Document support: the published URL, pinned ports, per-process port claims, and the `.cimd-off` marker when a server declines it
- `oauth_device.go` — device authorization grant (`icebath mcp login --flow device`): discovery, optional registration, device code display, polling with `slow_down` handling, token storage
- `oauth_sessions.go` — RPC-driven flows for the TUI and dashboard: start (returns session id and authorization URL), poll (pending, approved with tools, error), cancel; ownership checked against the caller's profile
- `client_oauth_flow.go` — the relay object that carries an authorization URL out to a remote client and its browser callback back in, with state check, timeouts and cancellation
- `oauth_models.go` — [py-shim] pydantic-compatible validation and ordered dumping of token, client metadata, client info, authorization-server and protected-resource documents; holds the real field sets and lax coercions the stored files depend on
- `oauth_url.go` — [py-shim] urllib.parse `urlsplit`, `urlparse`, quoting and query encoding plus pydantic URL normalisation, used for redirect, issuer and resource comparison
- `oauth_ctime_{bsd,unix,wasm,windows}.go`, `oauth_inode_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS change time and inode of a stat result, the signature that detects a rewritten token file

#### `icebath mcp` and `icebath tools` commands

`icebath mcp` with no arguments opens the catalog picker. Subcommands: `catalog`, `install <name>`, `add <name> --url|--command|--preset [--auth oauth|header] [--env K=V] [--connect-timeout]` (one preset exists: `codex`), `remove`, `list`, `test`, `configure` (re-pick tools), `login [--flow browser|device]`, `reauth <name>|--all`. `add` validates the entry, sets up auth (bearer tokens are saved to `.env` as `MCP_<NAME>_API_KEY` and referenced from `headers`), probes the server, lets the user pick tools and writes `mcp_servers`. `icebath tools list|enable|disable [--platform]` also lives here; a `server:tool` target edits that server's exclude list.

- `cliconfig.go` — every `icebath mcp` subcommand, config save and remove (removal deletes OAuth files), the single-server probe with redacted errors and failure classes, bearer and OAuth setup, tool checklist, `MCPCommand` dispatcher
- `tools_config_mcp.go` — interactive per-server tool checklist used by the tools configurator, toolset enable and disable per platform, the `icebath tools` list, enable and disable command
- `probe_timeout.go` — `ProbeSingleServerTimeout` for the doctor's live check
- `cliconfig_bearer_export.go`, `cliconfig_servers_export.go`, `tools_config_mcp_export.go`, `tuiserver_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers (`StripBearerPrefix`, `BearerAuthHeaders`, `GetMCPServers`, `ApplyMCPChange`, `BuildServerConfig`, `ApplyMCPPreset`, `EnvKeyForServer`, `HeadlessUI`, `ProbeSingleServerDetails`, `OAuthTokensPresent`) for `pkg/tuiserver` and `pkg/commands`

#### Bundled server catalog and picker

A reviewed catalog embedded in the binary (overridable with a directory in `ICEBATH_OPTIONAL_MCPS`). A manifest holds `manifest_version` (1), `name`, `description`, `source`, optional `connector_slug`, `transport` (`http` with `url`, or `stdio` with `command`, `args`, `env`), `auth` (`none`, `oauth` with optional `provider`, pre-registered `oauth` client fields and `env` prompts, or `api_key`), `tools.default_enabled` or `tools.default_excluded`, an optional `install` block (git URL, pinned ref, bootstrap shell commands, cloned into `mcp-installs/<name>`) and `post_install` notes. Installing prompts for declared credentials (secrets to `.env`, non-secrets inlined), writes the `mcp_servers` block, probes for tools and applies the default or previous tool selection. All 66 bundled entries are remote HTTP, 56 OAuth and 10 unauthenticated; none uses `stdio`, `api_key` or `install`, so those manifest paths are exercised by no shipped entry.

- `catalog.go` — manifest parsing and validation, `ListCatalog`, `GetEntry`, installed and enabled checks, git clone and bootstrap, credential prompts, server-config translation, tool selection, `InstallEntry`, `UninstallEntry`, `CardInstallConfig`; defines the `TerminalUI` interface all interactive commands use

#### Connection cards: MCP backend of the `manage_connections` tool

Lets the model install a catalog entry, enable a configured server or authorize one from inside a chat. With an interactive surface it draws a "connection card" per target and drives OAuth through the relay flow; without one it returns connect URLs as text. Tools of a server that finishes connecting after the turn are adopted into the running agent.

- `connectors_mcp.go` — `RunMCPOperation` (installed as `tools.MCPOperationRunner`), name validation per action, the per-target state machine (declare required env, start OAuth or install, observe, connect, fail), card answers, retry, `AdoptLateConnections`

#### Live agent tool snapshot and session tool pin

Not MCP-specific despite its location: rebuilds a running agent's tool array from the registry when tools appear or disappear, without breaking the provider prompt cache. It preserves the existing prefix order and bytes, appends new names, and persists a per-session "tools pin" so a resumed session restores the same tool definitions.

- `agentsnapshot.go` — `RefreshAgentMCPTools`, `ReprobeToolAvailability`, `PersistAgentToolNames`, `RestoreAgentToolPrefix`, `PinnedToolDefs`, pin versioning by build identity, re-injection of memory-provider, context-engine and `message_agent` tools after a rebuild

### `pkg/lsp` — language servers over stdio, used only to report diagnostics after file writes

*19 files, 7,282 Go lines*

Runs language servers per profile and turns their diagnostics into a lint verdict attached to file-write and patch tool results. It is reached through `pkg/tools/lsp_bridge.go` (compiled out of core and no-extras builds), which hands it a `Runtime` of callbacks, and through `icebath lsp` bound in `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go`. The only LSP features used are document sync and diagnostics (push and pull); there is no definition, references, hover, rename or symbol request and no model-callable LSP tool. Server binaries are staged under `<home>/lsp/bin`, PowerShell session files under `<home>/lsp/pses`. The logic is real; an asyncio-style cooperative loop, an ordered dict and Python value coercions are carried along as scaffolding.

#### Server registry, root detection and spawn commands

28 built-in servers matched by extension or basename, first match wins, with user-declared servers (`lsp.servers.<id>` having `command` and `extensions`, optional `root_markers`, `language_id`, `description`) searched first. Each server resolves its project root from marker files and builds its own spawn command. Built-ins: pyright, typescript (typescript-language-server), vue-language-server, svelte-language-server, astro-language-server, gopls, rust-analyzer, clangd, bash-language-server, yaml-language-server, lua-language-server, laravel-lsp, intelephense, ocaml-lsp, dockerfile-ls, terraform-ls, dart, haskell-language-server, julia, clojure-lsp, nixd, zls, gleam, elixir-ls, prisma, kotlin-language-server, jdtls, powershell.

- `servers.go` — the registry, extension-to-languageId table, marker-based root resolvers (JS roots exclude Deno projects), spawn builders (pyright with an interpreter chosen from the operator venv, then the project venv, then the managed Python, typescript and vue with a located TypeScript SDK and a warning that `@vue/language-server` 3.x cannot work here, bash with a warning when shellcheck is missing, a manually installed PowerShell Editor Services bundle), custom servers from config, and the 8-server set allowed in untrusted workspaces (pyright, typescript, svelte, bash, yaml, dockerfile, intelephense, clangd)
- `spawn_{unix,windows}.go` — child in its own session or process group, hidden console on Windows, and a stdin pipe whose closure by the child is detected (overlapped named pipe on Windows)

#### Server installation

`lsp.install_strategy` `auto` (default) installs on first need; anything else only probes. Lookup order: staging dir, npm's bin dir on Windows, managed Python tool envs, then PATH. One install attempt per package per process.

- `install.go` — recipes: npm for pyright, typescript-language-server, `@vue/language-server@2`, svelte, astro, yaml, bash, intelephense, dockerfile (through `lsp.package_manager`: npm by default, pnpm or yarn, on a located Node); `go install` for gopls; manual-only for rust-analyzer, clangd, lua-language-server, laravel-lsp, PowerShell; a pip strategy exists but no recipe uses it; `DetectStatus` for the CLI

#### Client and wire protocol

One `Client` per server process and workspace root; pyright is multi-root and shares one process across trusted roots. Sends `initialize` (45 s), `initialized`, `workspace/didChangeConfiguration`, `didOpen`, `didChange` (whole-document), `didSave`, `didClose`, `workspace/didChangeWatchedFiles`, `workspace/didChangeWorkspaceFolders`, pull `textDocument/diagnostic`, `shutdown`, `exit`; answers `workspace/configuration`, `workspace/workspaceFolders`, capability registration, progress creation and diagnostic refresh; consumes `textDocument/publishDiagnostics`. At most 64 open documents per client.

- `protocol.go` — `Content-Length` framing, envelope builders, message classification, request, protocol, decode and timeout error types
- `client.go` — process spawn and stderr tail, reader loop, write buffer with back-pressure, document versions as freshness tags, push debounce (150 ms), pull with content-modified retries, waiting for diagnostics in `document` (5 s) or `full` (10 s) mode, file URI conversion
- `sync_diagnostics.go` — for typescript only: asks tsserver synchronously (`workspace/executeCommand` `typescript.tsserverRequest` with `syntacticDiagnosticsSync` and `semanticDiagnosticsSync`) and converts the answer to LSP shape

#### Service: per-profile lifecycle, workspace trust, failure handling

One `Service` per profile home, built on first use from the `lsp` config section: `enabled`, `wait_mode`, `wait_timeout`, `install_strategy`, `idle_timeout` (600 s, minimum 30), `broken_retry_seconds`, `warmup_timeout`, `exclude_roots` (globs; a malformed value disables LSP everywhere), `trusted_workspaces`, and per server `command`, `env`, `initialization_options`, `disabled`. Servers that can run project code start only in workspaces the operator launched Icebath or opened a session in, or listed as trusted. A server and root pair that fails is marked broken and skipped until its retry deadline; idle clients and clients whose roots were deleted are reaped.

- `manager.go` — `Service`: config parsing, trust and exclusion checks, client spawn with shared in-flight spawns, broken-pair tracking, idle reaper, status snapshot, `ReleaseWorkspace` when a worktree is removed, delta filtering against a pre-edit baseline; the blocking `SnapshotBaseline` and `GetDiagnosticsSync` pair has no caller outside tests (the live path is `StartEditCheck`)
- `service.go` — registry of started services by home, `ServiceFor`, package-level `ReleaseWorkspace`, `ShutdownServices`, `AtExitShutdown`
- `runtime.go` — `Runtime`: the callbacks the host supplies (config section, managed-package env and binaries, Python tool installer, child env, process-group ledger, difflib opcodes, JSON decoder, config key order)
- `eventlog.go` — one-time and repeat-suppressed log lines for server active, unavailable, timeout, spawn failure, root excluded, untrusted skip, reap and release
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Post-write checks and the diagnostics block shown to the model

After a write the file tool schedules a non-blocking check and waits only until 80 ms after the write began (80 ms flat when the start time is unknown) for a verdict; a verdict that arrives later is carried as a note into a later tool result. Only diagnostics that were not in the pre-edit baseline are reported, with baseline line ranges shifted through the edit's diff. The model sees an `lsp_diagnostics` field holding a `<diagnostics file="…">` block of error-severity diagnostics, at most 20 per file and 4,000 characters in total.

- `edit_check.go` — `StartEditCheck` and `EditFuture`: one newest check per session and file, supersession of older checks, verdict cache of 256 entries keyed by text digest, 60 s spawn ceiling, disk resync
- `range_shift.go` — maps pre-edit lines to post-edit lines from diff opcodes and remaps or drops baseline diagnostics
- `reporter.go` — formats one diagnostic per line (1-based position, severity, code, source) with newline collapsing, control stripping, length caps and HTML escaping, and builds the per-file block

#### `icebath lsp` command

Bound in `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go`; operates on the process home's service and the install recipes.

- `cli.go` — subcommands `status [--json]`, `list [--installed-only]`, `install <server>`, `install-all [--include-manual]`, `restart`, `which <server>`; warns when bash-language-server is installed without shellcheck; exit code 130 on interrupt

#### Port scaffolding

Three files that exist because the Python original was asyncio code over ordered dicts and dynamically typed config values. The service, client and edit checks are written against them, so they cannot be removed without restating that logic.

- `loop.go` — [py-shim] asyncio stand-in: a cooperative scheduler where each task holds one mutex while running, with futures, sticky events, cancellation and a 2 s stop join; all client and service concurrency is written against it
- `omap.go` — [py-shim] insertion-ordered map with Python dict semantics, used for clients, broken pairs and baselines so eviction follows insertion order
- `pyvalue.go` — [py-shim] Python `int()` and `float()` coercion, exception class names and texts, UTF-8 `errors=replace` decoding and percent-unquoting, used by config parsing, URIs and the reporter

### `pkg/codeexec` — the `execute_code` tool (model-written Python with an RPC bridge to tools) and the `computer_use` desktop tool

*41 files, 13,396 Go lines*

Two unrelated tool families share this package. `execute_code` (toolset `code_execution`) runs Python in a persistent per-session kernel process on the host, or on the terminal backend when that is not local, and lets the code call a fixed set of seven agent tools over an RPC channel. `computer_use` (its own toolset) drives a desktop through a pluggable backend whose built-in implementation talks MCP over stdio to the external `cua-driver` binary installed by `pkg/pm`. Both register at init; `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go` binds `icebath computer-use` and the shutdown hooks. The package also exports a one-shot child runner that only `pkg/browser` uses. There is no OS-level sandbox for local code execution: isolation is a scrubbed environment, an owned process group, an approval guard and call limits. Config sections: `code_execution` and `computer_use`.

#### `execute_code` tool and the local session kernel

Language: Python only (3.8 or newer). The kernel is a generated Python runner that `exec`s each cell into one persistent globals dict, so variables survive across calls for the same owner, mode, interpreter, working directory and tool set; a timeout or interrupt kills the kernel and loses state, `reset: true` discards it. `code_execution.mode` is `project` (default: session working directory, the active venv or conda Python when usable) or `strict` (own temp directory, Python from PATH). Limits: `timeout` 300 s, `max_tool_calls` 50 per cell, `max_session_kernels` 4, `kernel_idle_timeout` 1800 s, stdout shown as 40% head and 60% tail around 50 KB with the full text spilled to a file (5 MB cap), stderr 10 KB, tool result 100,000 characters. Before running, an approval guard inspects the code, and inside a supervised gateway process code that would restart or stop the gateway or kill the host interpreter is refused.

- `execute.go` — tool registration, schema text listing only the tools enabled this session, argument checks (redirects a `command` argument to the terminal tool), lifecycle and approval guards, local versus remote dispatch, session-close hooks that kill a session's kernels
- `kernel.go` — the embedded Python runner sources (sentinel-framed JSON replies on stdout, Windows parent-death watchdog), kernel registry keyed by owner, per-cell authority that refuses tool calls once its cell settled, spawn into a private staging directory under the temp root, stdout and stderr readers, idle and over-cap eviction, background reaper, stale staging directory sweep (7 days), kernel shutdown for a session or a delegated child
- `gen.go` — generates the `icebath_tools` Python module the code imports: one stub per allowed tool (`web_search`, `web_extract`, `read_file`, `write_file`, `search_files`, `patch`, `terminal`) plus helpers `json_parse`, `shell_quote`, `retry`, in a Unix-socket (or loopback TCP) variant and a file-polling variant; also the recovery hints matched against a failed cell's stderr
- `rpc.go` — the bridge server: token-authenticated requests (constant-time check), allow list and call budget shared across transports, per-call log returned with the result, dispatch through the normal tool registry under the cell's session identity, `terminal` parameters for background, pty and notifications stripped; socket server loop for local kernels and file-polling loop for remote ones
- `env.go` — child environment: only safe-prefix variables (PATH, HOME, LANG, XDG_, VIRTUAL_ENV, CONDA and similar), five allowlisted `ICEBATH_` variables (home, profile, config, env, delegated-child marker), configured passthroughs and Windows essentials, with every name containing a credential fragment dropped; interpreter and working directory resolution with a bounded cache of interpreter probes
- `tool.go` — output shaping: byte-capped stdout with spill path and truncation metadata, ANSI stripping, secret redaction, interruption and timeout notices, error result JSON, `code_execution` config loading and mode validation
- `proc_{unix,windows}.go` — hidden console window, executable check and the inheritable parent-process handle for the Windows watchdog

#### Remote execution on the terminal backend

When the terminal `env_type` is not `local` (Docker, SSH, Modal, Vercel sandbox and the other terminal backends), the code runs inside that environment. Python 3 must exist there. A detached kernel runner is shipped and started remotely with a file-based cell protocol polled every 500 ms, and tool calls from the remote code travel back through request and response files that the host polls. If the remote kernel path fails the call falls back to shipping and running a one-off script.

- `remote.go` — per-task environment lookup, owner-only file shipping with payloads on stdin, env file sourcing, result assembly, timeout application, the per-call fallback path
- `kernel_remote.go` — remote kernel runner source, registry keyed by owner, backend, task environment and tool set, liveness probe by `kill -0`, idle exit, eviction, cell submission and reply polling, shutdown at session close and process exit

#### One-shot Python child runner (used by `browser_exec`)

Separate from the kernel: a single run of an interpreter whose helper requests the caller answers in Go. `execute_code` does not use it.

- `child.go`, `child_{unix,windows}.go` — `RunChild`: runs a Python interpreter in its own process group with stdin fed and an extra inherited pipe pair (fds 3 and 4, or handles on Windows) on which the caller serves requests from the child; kills the group on timeout or cancel; no caller in this package, `pkg/browser/exec_helpers.go` is the only user

#### `computer_use` tool: schema, safety gates and capture handling

Actions: `capture`, `click`, `double_click`, `right_click`, `middle_click`, `drag`, `scroll`, `type`, `key`, `set_value`, `wait`, `list_apps`, `list_windows`, `focus_app`. Capture modes: `som` (screenshot with numbered element overlays plus the accessibility tree, default), `vision` (image only) and `ax` (tree only); `app='screen'` grabs the full screen. Input is delivered in the background by default; `delivery_mode: foreground` and `bring_to_front` need separate approval. `capture`, `wait`, `list_apps` and `list_windows` are free; every input action and `focus_app` goes through the approval gate keyed `cua:<action>:<mode>` and fails closed with no human present. Hard blocks: typed text matching pipe-to-shell, `sudo rm -r`, `rm -rf /` or a fork bomb, and nine destructive key combos (empty trash, log out, lock screen on macOS and Windows, Ctrl+Option+Delete, Option+F4). Screenshots are deduplicated per session and target, downscaled for vision (`computer_use.max_image_dimension`, 1456 px ceiling), attached natively when the main model accepts tool-result images and otherwise described by the auxiliary vision model; the image and the full element list are also written to the home cache (20 files kept each) so the model can read or share them.

- `payload/computer_use_schema.json` — [data] the frozen function-calling schema of `computer_use` (23 parameters, only `action` required), embedded by `computer_use_schema.go`
- `computer_use_schema.go` — embeds and decodes the schema once
- `computer_use_register.go` — registers the tool with the active provider's availability check and the session-release hooks
- `computer_use_tool.go` — blocked patterns and combos, per-session backend cache with per-backend call locks and permission mode, screenshot dedup state, approval request and one-line action summaries, verdict classification of action results; also a recording `noopBackend` that exists for tests
- `computer_use_dispatch.go` — `handleComputerUse`: argument coercion, the Bot Desktop lease fence (refuses or voids the action while a human holds the shared screen), per-action handlers, optional follow-up capture (`capture_after`, `computer_use.capture_after_mode`)
- `computer_use_capture.go` — capture summaries and element lists, MIME sniffing, dedup digest, multimodal envelope, cache files, image shrinking, auxiliary-vision routing
- `computer_use_hooks.go` — function variables binding `pkg/botdesktop` (placement, lease epoch, screen start, package install) so tests can replace them

#### Backend interface and provider plugins

`computer_use.backend` names a provider (default `cua`). The built-in provider is compiled in; other providers are plugin directories under the user plugins tree that offer a computer-use provider and run in the plugin host.

- `computer_use_backend.go` — `ComputerUseBackend` (start, stop, capture, click, drag, scroll, type, key, list apps and windows, focus, set value, wait) and `ComputerUseProvider` interfaces with default method sets, plus the capture, element and action result types
- `computer_use_plugins.go` — provider discovery (bundled first, then user plugin directories), loading, the active-provider lookup and the built-in `CuaDriverProvider`
- `computer_use_hosted.go` — adapters that drive a provider and backend object living in the plugin host child, decoding its dict and dataclass results
- `tools_config_bridge.go` — init hook giving the tools picker the computer-use provider list and the cua-driver install action

#### cua-driver backend

The default backend speaks MCP (newline-framed JSON-RPC via `pkg/mcp`'s stdio transport) to `cua-driver`, with a CLI fallback transport when the MCP stream is down, and re-declares its session after a transport reset. `computer_use.permission_mode` is `standard` (default) or `bounded`; an approval bypass (`--yolo`) escalates the session to `unrestricted` with a one-time warning. Outside `standard` the backend runs its own private driver daemon, on macOS launched through `open` so TCC permissions stay on the signed `CuaDriver.app`, whose bundle identifier and signing team are verified (`allow_unsigned_driver` permits an unsigned local build). Other keys: `ax_max_elements`, `no_overlay`, `cua_telemetry`, `native_wayland`, `capability_manifest`. Works on macOS, Windows and Linux, including a desktop running inside the terminal sandbox for the Bot Desktop.

- `cua_driver_backend.go` — `CuaDriverBackend`: start (runtime contract check, daemon, session, identity declaration), stop, sticky target app and window, launch app, bring to front, agent cursor toggle, driver config
- `cua_backend.go` — subprocess helpers, `computer_use` config readers, sanitised driver child env (secrets stripped), stale-display detection, Linux session-lock check
- `cua_backend_session.go` — the MCP client over stdio, lazy start and rebuild on drop, capability and input-schema discovery, CLI fallback, transient daemon error retry, fail-closed envelope for unknown outcomes
- `cua_backend_daemon.go` — private embedded daemon: app bundle resolution and signature check, spawn, socket readiness, stderr tail, graceful stop then kill
- `cua_backend_driver.go` — driver binary resolution through `pkg/pm` without installing (an explicit override is never replaced), WSL path translation, MCP invocation from the capability manifest, runtime contract status
- `cua_backend_capture.go` — window selection (skips the driver's own and shell helper windows, prefers the X11 active window), window state and vision captures, full-screen capture, app listing and focus
- `cua_backend_input.go` — click, drag, scroll, type, key and set-value against the sticky target, addressing by element index or pixel, delivery mode handling and refusal codes
- `cua_backend_parse.go` — parses driver results: structured verdicts, element trees, window lists, image dimensions, key combos
- `cua_proc_{unix,windows}.go` — signal number of a dead child and terminate

#### `icebath computer-use` command

Paths: `install`, `status`, `doctor`, `permissions status`, `permissions grant`, and `screen status|start|stop|install` (the per-profile Bot Desktop screen).

- `computer_use_cli.go` — argument namespace, parser tree and the install, status, doctor and permissions commands; plugin backends report through their own doctor
- `computer_use_config_cua.go` — install and repair of the pinned driver: contract cache (30 s), version summary, Windows logon autostart task (`cua-driver-serve`, opt-in, registered through elevated PowerShell), per-platform post-install notes

An exported setter that exists only so tests in other packages can seed package state.
