### `pkg/browser` — browser automation tools over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, plus the credential vault tool

*64 files, 17,508 Go lines*

Registers four model-callable tools: `browser_exec` (toolset `browser-use`), `browser_cdp` and `browser_dialog` (toolset `browser-cdp`, offered only when a static CDP endpoint is configured or attached), and `browser_vault` (toolset `browser`). There are no per-action tools (navigate, snapshot, click, console, vision): the model writes Python that calls helper functions, and Go answers each helper over CDP. Backends: an Icebath-launched local Chromium, Lightpanda, an attached browser (`/browser connect`, `browser.cdp_url`, `BROWSER_CDP_URL`), a managed copy of the user's real Chromium profile, Chromium inside the terminal sandbox, and the cloud providers Browserbase, Browser Use and Firecrawl (or a plugin provider). Not present: agent-browser, any Camofox implementation (`cloud_provider: camofox` is only accepted as a synonym for local), recording, download handling, console capture. It owns `<home>/cache/browser/` (throwaway profiles and launch records), `<home>/cache/browser-use/` (workspaces, screenshots, Lightpanda state), `<home>/browser-profile/`, `<home>/chrome-debug/` and a shared-profile state directory beside the gateway lock. Also used by `pkg/tuiserver` and `pkg/app` (`/browser`), `pkg/builtin/googlemeet` (launcher, CDP and websocket clients) and the doctor.

#### Tool registration and configuration

Config section `browser`: `engine` (`auto` or `lightpanda`), `headed`, `executable_path`, `user_data_dir`, `chromium_args`, `command_timeout` (30 s, launch floor), `inactivity_timeout` (minimum 30 s; legacy env `BROWSER_INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT`), `cloud_provider`, `cdp_url`, `use_real_profile`, `allow_private_urls`, `auto_local_for_private_urls` (default true), `dialog_policy` (`must_respond` default, `auto_dismiss`, `auto_accept`), `dialog_timeout_s` (300).

- `tools.go` — init that registers the four tools
- `config.go` — `settings`: typed readers of the `browser` section and profile secrets, CDP override precedence (live `/browser connect` endpoint, then `BROWSER_CDP_URL`, then `browser.cdp_url`)
- `runtime.go` — which Chromium to run: the configured pin, then `pkg/pm`'s install, then a path baked into the build, then a system browser where pm builds none; the "Chromium missing" hint
- `registry.go` — registers the plugin kinds "browser provider" and "browser page backend" and finds the page backend holding a task's page
- `tools_config_bridge.go` — init hook giving the tools picker the browser runtime and provider facts
- `log.go` — package logger

#### `browser_exec`: Python helpers answered over CDP

The model's `code` runs on the user's Python (fresh interpreter per call, default 300 s, 5 s to 1800 s) with pre-imported helpers; each helper is one JSON line over an inherited pipe that Go executes on the session's attached tab. Helpers: `new_tab`, `goto_url`, `wait_for_load`, `wait_for_element`, `wait_for_network_idle`, `page_info`, `js`, `fill_input`, `type_text`, `press_key`, `dispatch_key`, `click_at_xy`, `scroll`, `capture_screenshot`, `upload_file`, `list_tabs`, `current_tab`, `switch_tab`, `activate_tab`, `close_tab`, `ensure_real_tab`, `iframe_target`, `drain_events`, raw `cdp(method, **params)`, `http_get`, `wait`. The accessibility tree is reached only through `cdp('Accessibility.getFullAXTree')`. Browser session and a per-task workspace (`cache/browser-use/workspace/<task>`, with auto-imported `agent_helpers.py` and an optional `.env`) persist across calls; Python variables do not. Optional `session` names an isolated browser or tab set; `local: true` (offered only with `use_real_profile`) forces the user's own profile. A printed screenshot path is returned as `screenshot_path` and attached as an image when the main model takes tool-result images. Output and stderr (4,000 characters) are secret-redacted.

- `browser_use_cli.go` — schema and description variants (vision, text-only, Lightpanda), the dynamic `local` parameter, handler and registration
- `browser_use_exec.go` — `browserExec`: URL screening of the code, backend routing (existing endpoint, CDP override, forced local sidecar, cloud provider with local fallback, local engine, real profile), per-route memory of sidecar and fallback state, child env, workspace, Bot Desktop fencing, result assembly
- `exec_helpers.go` — the Python preamble that defines every helper and a `browser_harness` module alias, the run driver that connects the session, attaches a tab and serves helper calls through `codeexec.RunChild`, screenshot directory choice
- `exec_steps.go` — Go implementation of each helper on a per-session CDP connection: tab selection and marking, navigation, JS evaluation with unserialisable values, key and mouse input, element and network-idle waits, event buffer for `drain_events`, open-dialog tracking, screenshot capture and shrinking
- `harnessdirs.go`, `harnessdirs_{unix,windows}.go` — [port-artifact] runtime and temp directory rules of a "browser harness" daemon (`BH_RUNTIME_DIR`, `BH_TMP_DIR`, `BU_NAME`, AF_UNIX path-length budgets, private short directories); no daemon process is started by this package, the values now key the in-process CDP session and give each served profile its own directories in the Python child's env

#### `browser_cdp`, `browser_dialog` and the per-task supervisor

`browser_cdp` sends one raw CDP command (`method`, `params`, optional `target_id` or `frame_id`, timeout 30 s up to 300 s) on a fresh websocket, or through the supervisor's live session for an out-of-process iframe. `browser_dialog` accepts or dismisses a pending JavaScript dialog (`action`, `prompt_text`, `dialog_id`). The supervisor is one persistent CDP connection per task that tracks dialogs and the frame tree; beside native `Page.javascriptDialogOpening` events it injects a script that replaces `alert`, `confirm` and `prompt` with a synchronous request to `icebath-dialog-bridge.invalid`, which it intercepts through the Fetch domain and answers per the dialog policy or the agent's reply. The tool description still tells the model that cloud backends are not wired for `browser_cdp` and refers to "dedicated browser tools" that do not exist here.

- `browser_cdp_tool.go` — schema, the private-page guard (on a non-local backend only inspection and tab-management methods run against a private-address page; URLs in params are screened for SSRF), redaction of page-originated result text while leaving binary payloads intact, websocket error text matching the Python client
- `browser_dialog_tool.go` — schema and handler that answers through the task's supervisor
- `supervisor.go` — `cdpSupervisor`: attach to the first page with flattened auto-attach, dialog policy and watchdog, recent-dialog ring (20), frame table (30 entries, OOPIF depth 2), reconnect with a 5-failure budget, `Runtime.evaluate` and page re-focus used by the vault, the process-wide registry by task
- `browser_session_cdp.go` — starts and stops a task's supervisor on the override or session endpoint

#### CDP and websocket clients, endpoint resolution

Hand-written protocol clients with no external websocket or CDP library, shared by the tools here and by the Google Meet plugin.

- `ws.go` — RFC 6455 client written in-package: handshake, proxy tunnelling for non-loopback hosts, frame reassembly, ping replies, close handshake
- `cdp.go` — `CDPConn`: command and event multiplexing over one websocket with flattened sessions, target listing, attach, detach, create
- `endpoint.go` — normalises a CDP endpoint to a websocket URL through `/json/version`, the per-home live endpoint published by `/browser connect` with a generation counter, debug-port readiness and port probes

#### Session table, janitor and cleanup

One session record per task and session name, reused while its backend is alive and unexpired. A janitor thread reaps sessions idle past `inactivity_timeout` (a human holding the shared screen counts as activity) and periodically reaps orphaned browsers of dead processes; every session is closed at process exit, and cloud sessions are released through the provider.

- `browser_session.go` — session creation in precedence CDP override, forced local sidecar, cloud provider, local; browser child env (no credentials, loopback `NO_PROXY`, short `TMPDIR`); reuse or evict; Bot Desktop sharing and the lease fence wrapper
- `browser_session_lifecycle.go` — activity tracking, provider expiry, single, per-profile and global cleanup, emergency cleanup, orphan reaping, the janitor
- `browser_session_cloud.go` — resolves the cloud provider of a profile: explicit `cloud_provider`, else auto-detect Browser Use then Browserbase from credentials; cached per home and registry generation
- `browser_session_sandbox.go` — Chromium started inside the terminal sandbox container for the Bot Desktop "terminal" placement: seeds the quiet profile remotely, reads the DevTools port through an exec, one browser shared per container
- `bot_desktop.go` — init that hands `pkg/botdesktop` the browser config readers, packaged Chromium and sandbox policy; lease and placement accessors

#### Local Chromium launcher and cross-process holders

Launches Chromium with `--remote-debugging-port=0`, the quiet switches, `--headless=new` unless `headed` (a Linux host without a display stays headless), and `--no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage` when running as root, in Docker or under AppArmor user-namespace restrictions. Without `user_data_dir` each launch gets a throwaway profile under `cache/browser/chromium/` that is deleted afterwards; a persistent profile is one shared Chromium that several keys and processes attach to and only the last holder stops. Chromium is auto-installed through `pkg/pm` once per process, never in Docker, on Termux or over a pinned path.

- `launcher.go` — argv construction, sandbox-bypass detection, headed resolution, profile, record and shared-state directory layout, `DevToolsActivePort` reading, liveness of an endpoint
- `launcher_run.go` — launch or attach under a per-profile cross-process lock, launch records written before readiness so a crash stays reapable, foreign-namespace browsers leased but never adopted, stop and last-holder logic, reaping of dead owners' browsers and throwaway profiles; `RunningInstance` has no caller
- `launcher_spawn_{unix,windows}.go` — detached spawn attributes so a shared browser outlives its launcher
- `holders.go`, `holders_{unix,windows}.go` — lease files and the records lock for a launcher state directory, PID-namespace and boot identity, handover to a successor holder

#### Lightpanda engine

An alternative local engine without a graphical renderer, selected by `browser.engine: lightpanda`. State lives in `<home>/cache/browser-use/lightpanda`.

- `lightpanda.go` — `browser.engine: lightpanda`: finds the binary on PATH or installer locations (not on Windows), runs one `lightpanda serve` per session on a loopback port with a shared HTTP cache, records and reaps orphans, kills the process tree on stop; no screenshots and one page per session

#### Cloud browser providers and plugin extension points

`browser.cloud_provider` selects a provider that creates a remote browser and returns its CDP endpoint; a provider failure falls back to a local session marked as a fallback. Plugins can add providers and page backends.

- `browser_provider.go` — `BrowserProvider` interface: availability, create session, close, emergency cleanup, setup schema
- `cloud_provider.go` — shared REST lifecycle for the bundled vendors: one create request, one release request, error mapping
- `cloud_vendors.go` — Browserbase (`BROWSERBASE_API_KEY`, `BROWSERBASE_PROJECT_ID`; env knobs `BROWSERBASE_PROXIES` default on, `BROWSERBASE_ADVANCED_STEALTH` default off, `BROWSERBASE_KEEP_ALIVE` default on, `BROWSERBASE_SESSION_TIMEOUT`; retries without each paid feature a 402 refuses), Browser Use (`BROWSER_USE_API_KEY`, `api.browser-use.com/api/v3/browsers`), Firecrawl (`FIRECRAWL_API_KEY`, `/v2/browser`, `FIRECRAWL_BROWSER_TTL` 300 s, explicit selection only); registers the three as bundled backend plugins
- `browser_provider_hosted.go` — adapter for a provider registered by a plugin running in the plugin host
- `browser_page_backend.go`, `browser_page_backend_hosted.go` — interface and hosted adapter for a plugin browser that owns its pages outside CDP, so `browser_vault` can evaluate scripts on them

#### Real profile browsing, `/browser connect` and `icebath browser`

With `browser.use_real_profile` the agent drives a managed copy of the user's default Chromium-family browser profile (Chrome, Brave, Edge, Chromium and channels) so logins carry over. The copy lives in `<home>/browser-profile/<browser>`; cookies, logins and web data are taken with an online SQLite backup, never a raw copy. If the source profile is locked the tool reports it and names `icebath browser close-profile`, which kills the browser holding the profile and is the only `icebath browser` subcommand. `/browser connect` (implemented in `pkg/tuiserver` and `pkg/app`) uses this package to launch a debug browser on a profile in `<home>/chrome-debug` and publish its endpoint.

- `browser_connect.go`, `browser_connect_{other,windows}.go` — Chromium product table (executables and profile directories per OS), default-browser detection (LaunchServices on macOS, xdg on Linux, registry and shell association on Windows)
- `browser_connect_launch.go`, `browser_connect_launch_{unix,windows}.go` — debug browser candidates, free port search above the preferred port (default endpoint `http://127.0.0.1:9222`), detached launch with stderr log, readiness wait, the manual command shown when launch fails
- `browser_connect_snapshot.go` — profile snapshot: last-used profile, auth file mirroring with bounded database backup, lock detection, finding and closing the processes holding a profile, reuse and cleanup of snapshots
- `browser_session_real_profile.go` — launches the real-profile browser once per profile home, fallback note when it cannot load, consent revocation
- `browser_command.go` — `icebath browser close-profile`

#### URL policy

Applied to every URL literal found in `browser_exec` code and in `browser_cdp` parameters before anything runs.

- `urlpolicy.go` — refuses cloud-metadata addresses always, private, loopback, LAN and CGNAT addresses on non-local backends unless `allow_private_urls`, URLs embedding an API key or token, and sites blocked by the website policy; when a cloud provider is configured and `auto_local_for_private_urls` is on, private URLs route to a local "sidecar" browser instead of being refused

#### Credential vault: `browser_vault` tool, backends and `icebath vault`

Fills saved logins, one-time codes, cards and addresses into the current page without the secret entering the conversation. Actions: `list`, `fill`, `save_login`, `enter_code`, `unlock`. A fill is refused unless the page origin matches the item; card fills need user confirmation; secrets are sent over the supervisor socket or page backend, never through argv. Sources: the local encrypted vault (`pkg/vault`), 1Password through the `op` CLI (handles `op:`), Bitwarden through `bw` (handles `bw:`), and plugin backends wrapped so a plugin cannot claim another namespace or leak its own error text. Manager session tokens are kept in memory per profile and backend with a 30-minute idle TTL and are dropped when the unlocking gateway session ends.

- `browser_vault_tool.go` — schema, the five actions, page inspection and fill scripts evaluated on the page, origin binding, masked save prompt, payment confirmation, Bot Desktop fencing
- `vault_login_classifier.go` — classifies inspected page controls as username, password, one-time-code, card or address fields (autocomplete tokens, names, labels, adjacency of OTP boxes) and builds the inspection and fill JavaScript
- `vault_backend.go` — `LoginBackend` interface and defaults, manager CLI runners that pass secrets on stdin or env, enabled and installed checks (`vault.<name>.enabled`, `binary_path`), backend lookup by handle
- `vault_backend_local.go` — the always-on local vault as a backend, including TOTP codes from a stored seed
- `vault_backend_managers.go` — 1Password and Bitwarden backends: item listing, origin extraction, password and OTP resolution, unlock with the master password or a service-account token, allowlisted child env
- `vault_backend_plugin.go`, `vault_backend_hosted.go`, `vault_backend_registry.go` — core-owned wrapper around plugin backends with validated item copies and fixed failure text, the hosted adapter, and the registry that reserves built-in names and prefixes
- `vault_unlock.go` — session token store with idle expiry and lock generations so a stale unlock cannot commit; `LockAllVaultProfiles` has no caller
- `vault_view.go` — item, source and key views and mutations for the TUI vault hub (list, add, remove, enable a source, move the key between file and keychain)
- `vault_command.go` — `icebath vault` with `list`, `add` (login, card or address wizard), `rm`, `sources [--enable|--disable]`, `key`

#### Export shims

Thin exported names over unexported functions, present because callers sit in other packages.

- `exports.go`, `cdp_override_export.go`, `cli_browser_exports.go`, `doctor_exports.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers over unexported functions (`ChromiumExecutable`, `LaunchChromium`, `StopBrowser`, `CDPOverrideRaw`, `CleanupProfileBrowsers`, `CleanupAllBrowsers`, `ChromiumMissingHint`, Lightpanda status helpers) for the TUI, gateway, doctor and Google Meet plugin

### `pkg/browser/quiet` — switches and profile preferences that stop agent-launched Chromium from contacting Google services

*1 file, 209 Go lines*

A small dependency-free package used by the local launcher, the debug-browser launcher, the sandbox session and `pkg/botdesktop`. It keeps a Chromium started for the agent from doing first-run, sync, component update, field-trial, push-messaging, sign-in, translate and new-tab network calls by disabling them or pointing their endpoints at a dead loopback port.

#### Quiet launch arguments and profile seeding

- `quiet.go` — `Args` (the switch list and one merged `--disable-features`), `MergeFeatureSwitches` (joins repeated feature switches in an argv), `Files` and `Merge` (preference keys written into `Local State` and `Preferences`, sign-in left alone for the user's own profile), `SeedProfile` for a local user data directory and `SeedRemoteProfile` for one inside a container through a command runner

## 7. State and persistence

### `pkg/state` — SQLite session store (`state.db`): schema, transcripts, search, runtime ledger, locking and repair

*219 files, 54,606 Go lines*

Owns `<home>/state.db` (one per profile home, opened through `modernc.org/sqlite`) and everything stored in it: sessions, message transcripts, FTS indexes, usage accounting, compression lineage, the gateway's durable admission and worker ledger, routing index and a large `state_meta` key-value space. The central type is `SessionDB` (alias `DB`), built from five embedded "mixin" structs; about 30 packages import it, chiefly `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/agent`, `pkg/gatewayrun`, `pkg/kanban`, `pkg/tuiserver` and `pkg/app`. The package is also the project's general SQLite toolkit (`OpenDB`, `ConnectSQLite`, `Transaction`, `AddColumnIfMissing`, WAL policy) for the other databases (kanban, cron, async delegation, delivery ledger), and it holds a lot that is not persistence: the in-memory `Message` type and dict codec the agent loop uses, context-compressor marker text, transcript sequence repair, session export renderers, the session client-environment policy and the low-disk prune advisor. Code that needs `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/tools` or `pkg/agent` reaches them through package-level hook variables assigned by the process wiring (`cmd/icebath/wiring.go`, plus init code in `pkg/gateway` and `pkg/agent`); most panic when unassigned. Port scaffolding is heavy: Python exception class names on every error, private `py*` re-implementations of `json.dumps`, `repr`, `str` and `os.path`, 27 re-export shim files (`*_export.go`, `*_exports.go`), duplicated ported and Go-style method sets, and many test seams kept as package variables. The code is real and wired; no stubs were found, but about sixty exported functions and methods have no caller outside tests and are named below.

#### Store handle, connections and write serialisation

`SessionDB` holds one writer connection behind a mutex plus a pool of read-only connections. Every write runs in `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` and is retried on lock contention with jitter (20 to 150 ms, then 250 ms to 1 s after two seconds) inside a patience budget of 20 s by default, 60 s for transcript, session-row and usage writes, 0.5 s for activity stamps and 5 s for a session busy under compression; when the budget runs out the holders of the write lock are logged. A passive WAL checkpoint runs every 50 writes and a bounded FTS merge every 1000. Open order for a writable handle: create the directory, writability preflight, quarantine of a zero-byte or non-SQLite file, refusal of a deleted WAL generation, chmod 0600, connect, journal mode, pragmas, `foreign_keys=ON`, CJK tokenizer, schema init, one automatic repair attempt on a malformed schema, generation stamp, WAL lock guard.

- `session_db.go` — `SessionDB` and `sessionCore`: open and close, `executeWrite` retry loop, read routing, replaced-file and lost-WAL-generation halts, corruption quarantine, `state_meta` get, set and prefix listing, `AsyncSessionDB` goroutine wrapper; the one-time `RetagKanbanWorkerSessions` migration and the retry-sleep test seams have no callers
- `db.go` — `DB` alias, `Open` and `OpenHome`, `Tx` and `querier` wrappers used by the thin Go-style methods, `NewUID` (32 hex), `NewSessionID`, swappable wall clock
- `session_db_module.go` — default path resolution (`<home>/state.db`, overridable `DefaultDBPath`), resume and export message caps from `sessions.max_resume_messages` and `sessions.max_export_messages`, dead-pid test for lock holders, filters that strip old curator harness prompts and bare `[tool]` marker turns on load
- `session_db_support.go` — the "can't open its session history" notice with network-drive hint, deletion of unreferenced `system_prompts` rows, session row dict shaping (resolved prompt, reset and branch markers lifted from `model_config`)
- `async_session_db_borrowed.go` — [port-artifact] marks an async wrapper as borrowed so the gateway's handle sweep does not close a handle another owner closes
- `session_trace.go` — [unwired] installs a per-statement trace callback on the writer and every pooled reader
- `session_db_read_only_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] `IsReadOnly` accessor
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `logger=state`

#### Process-wide shared handle registry

Reference-counted sharing of one `SessionDB` per database path inside a process, so the gateway, cron and tools do not each open a writer. A registry entry is a "generation": when the file at the path is replaced, the old generation is retired and a new one opened, and closes are serialised per path behind a teardown barrier.

- `registry.go` — `Acquire`, `Release`, `ReleaseOrClose`, `CloseAll`, `CloseAllUnder(dir)`, `BorrowLiveSharedSessionDBs` for housekeeping; `RegistryStats` and `LiveSharedSessionDBs` have no callers

#### Read connection pool and descriptor budget

Read-only connections exist only while WAL is active; otherwise reads run on the writer under its lock. Limits: 8 read connections per database path shared by every handle on that path, 24 per process, and none when fewer than 64 file descriptors of headroom remain under the soft `RLIMIT_NOFILE`; an idle connection of a peer is reclaimed before a request is refused, and a failed read-only open backs off for 60 s. Transient disk I/O errors on reads are replayed three times 50 ms apart.

- `readpool.go` — per-path and per-process permit accounting with weakly held members, descriptor census through `/proc/<pid>/fd`, warning when more than four writable handles share a path
- `readpool_{unix,windows}.go` — soft descriptor limit through `getrlimit`; unmeasurable on Windows

#### Generic SQLite toolkit shared with every other database in the project

Connection helpers that are not specific to `state.db` and are called from `pkg/kanban`, `pkg/cron`, `pkg/tools`, `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/backup` and `pkg/selfupdate`. A process-wide registry counts live connections per file so that raw file reads and copies are refused while a connection is open (closing any descriptor on a file drops the process's POSIX locks on it).

- `sqlite_util.go` — `OpenDB` (mkdir, busy timeout 5000 ms, WAL with fallback, optional foreign keys, `synchronous=FULL`, init callback), `Transaction`, `AddColumnIfMissing`, and a wrapper emulating Python sqlite3's implicit `BEGIN` before DML
- `sqlite_safe_read.go` — `ConnectSQLite` (one connection in its own pool, autocommit), `ConnectTracked` and the live-connection registry, `OfflineFileAccess`, `ReadHeaderBytesPreopen`, `FileLengthMatchesHeader`
- `sqlite_raw.go` — reaches the modernc driver's unexported handle by reflection for `sqlite3_get_autocommit`, `total_changes`, extended error codes and the online backup API
- `secure_state_db_{unix,windows}.go` — creates or tightens the database and its `-wal` and `-shm` files to 0600 without following symlinks; no-op on Windows
- `secure_state_db_export.go`, `tracked_db_export.go`, `sqlite_autocommit_export.go`, `sqlite_safe_read_live_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers (`SecureStateDBFiles`, `ConnectTrackedDB`, `InTransaction`, `LiveConnectionCount`, `HasWriterConn`); the last two functions have no callers

#### Raw SQL doors handed to other packages

[port-artifact] Besides `ReadCtx`, `ExecuteWrite` and `ReadAll`, these shims let other packages run their own SQL against `state.db`, so the schema is effectively shared with `pkg/gateway` and `pkg/gatewayapi`: `QueryRowObject` has about 100 external call sites and `QueryObjects` about 40.

- `sessions_read_all_export.go` — `SessionDB.ReadAll`, every row of one read-only statement as ordered objects
- `api_server_export.go` — `QueryRowObject`, `ResolveTitleConflictOnConn`, `CompactionInternalFields`, `RetryHorizonS` (seven days)
- `api_run_admissions_export.go` — `QueryObjects`, `AdmissionRow`, `RetryTerminalAdmission`
- `mutation_control_exports.go` — `ConnObject`, `OwnerUser`, `ValidateImportPayload`, `LocalLineageOwner`
- `worker_reservation_exports.go` — `ConnRow`, `RuntimeSession`, `SecretDigest`, `CompactTerminalReceipts`, `InsertSessionRowInTransaction`

#### Journal mode, WAL policy and pragmas

WAL is the default (`database.journal_mode`, with `delete` as the operator opt-out). The policy never downgrades an on-disk WAL file from a live connection, falls back to DELETE where the filesystem refuses WAL, keeps new databases out of WAL when the linked SQLite carries the WAL-reset bug (3.7.0 up to the fixed 3.44.6, 3.50.7 and 3.51.3), warns about WAL on virtiofs or 9p mounts, caps the WAL at 64 MiB and forces `checkpoint_fullfsync` and `synchronous=FULL` on macOS. Optional pragmas come from `database.cache_size`, `mmap_size`, `temp_store`, `wal_autocheckpoint`, `journal_size_limit` and `synchronous`.

- `wal.go` — `ApplyWALWithFallback`, `ApplyDatabasePragmas`, on-disk mode detection from the header, cross-VM filesystem detection through `/proc/self/mountinfo`, once-per-database warnings, update hint by install method
- `sqlite_runtime.go` — hidden `icebath sqlite-runtime` verb: prints the linked SQLite version, source id and missing store features as one JSON line; `ProbeSQLiteRuntime` runs another binary's verb for `icebath update`
- `sessions_cmd_journal_mode.go` — `icebath sessions set-journal-mode`: switches the on-disk mode of a store no other process holds and verifies the file header

#### Declared schema, schema version and migrations

`SchemaSQL` is run on every writable open (all `CREATE ... IF NOT EXISTS`), then missing declared columns are added by `ALTER TABLE` from a column map parsed out of an in-memory copy of the schema and cached in `<home>/cache/schema_columns.json` keyed by the DDL hash, then two primary-key heals rebuild `gateway_routing` (scope added) and `session_model_usage` (task added), then `DeferredIndexSQL` (triggers and indexes on later columns) runs with a skip for triggers whose stored body already matches. `schema_version` holds a single integer, 34 in this build: a store stamped with a higher number is refused before any statement runs, a fresh store is stamped directly and gets `store_instance_id`, `store_created_at_utc` and `message_uid_backfill` in `state_meta`, and an older store runs the version-gated data migrations (below 16 delegate markers, 18 gateway metadata from `sessions/sessions.json`, 20 and 22 per-model usage, 23 FTS storage upgrade flag, 25 prompt dedupe into `system_prompts`, 30 trigram exclusion of cron and subagent rows, 33 retired account labels, 34 reasoning carrier type rename) plus a resumable `message_uid` backfill that works in 2000-row slices for at most one second per open. The version is only advanced when FTS5 is present and no FTS step is unfinished.

Table `sessions`: `id` (PK), `runtime_revision`, `runtime_generation`, `source`, `created_source`, routing peer (`user_id`, `session_key`, `chat_id`, `chat_type`, `thread_id`, `display_name`, `origin_json`, `expiry_finalized`, `profile_name`, `transport_profile`), `model`, `model_config` (JSON), `system_prompt` (legacy inline), `system_prompt_hash`, `tool_names` (hash of the tools pin), `parent_session_id`, `started_at`, `ended_at`, `end_reason`, counters (`message_count`, `tool_call_count`, `api_call_count`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `cache_read_tokens`, `cache_write_tokens`, `reasoning_tokens`), workspace (`cwd`, `git_branch`, `git_repo_root`, `git_metadata_generation`), billing (`billing_provider`, `billing_base_url`, `billing_mode`, `estimated_cost_usd`, `actual_cost_usd`, `cost_status`, `cost_source`, `pricing_version`), `title`, `title_source`, activity (`last_activity_at`, `last_activity_description`, `last_activity_provenance`), handoff (`handoff_state`, `handoff_platform`, `handoff_error`), compression state (`compression_failure_cooldown_until`, `compression_failure_error`, `compression_fallback_streak`, `compression_ineffective_count`, `compression_recovery_deadline`, `compression_overload_streak`), `rewind_count`, sidebar flags (`archived`, `auto_archived`, `pinned`, `hidden`, `last_read_at`), `transcript_revision`.

Table `messages`: `id` (autoincrement), `session_id`, `role`, `content`, `tool_call_id`, `tool_calls` (JSON), `tool_name`, `effect_disposition`, `timestamp`, `token_count`, `finish_reason`, reasoning carriers (`reasoning`, `reasoning_content`, `reasoning_details`, `codex_reasoning_items`, `codex_message_items`), `platform_message_id`, `observed`, `_compressed_summary`, `active`, `compacted`, `api_content`, `display_kind`, `display_metadata` (JSON), `display_identity` (BLOB), `display_order`, `message_uid`, `absorbed_message_uids`, `tool_call_uids`, `tool_call_uid`.

Other tables: `schema_version(version)`; `system_prompts(hash, prompt)` content-addressed by SHA-256; `session_model_usage` keyed by (session, model, billing provider, base URL, billing mode, task) with token, call and cost counters, cascading on session delete; `runtime_epoch` (singleton row: epoch, instance id); `session_admissions` (`seq`, `admission_id`, `request_id`, `principal_id`, `target_session_id`, `lineage_json`, `payload_json`, `payload_digest`, `intent` queue, steer or redirect, `status` queued, started, unknown or terminal, `outcome`, `owner_epoch`, `generation`, unique per principal, target and request); `worker_executions` (`execution_id`, `session_id`, `kind` cron, child, compute or kanban, `owner_epoch`, `generation`, `status`, `adoption_digest`, `last_sequence`); `worker_receipts` (execution, sequence, payload digest, result JSON); `state_meta(key, value)`; `gateway_routing` (scope, session key, entry JSON, updated at); `gateway_hygiene_state` (session key, failure streak); `conversation_generations` (source, session key, generation; never garbage-collected by design); `gateway_heartbeats` (backend id, pid, started, last heartbeat, profile, host); `compression_locks` and `session_turn_leases` (key, holder, acquired, expires); `async_delegations` (declared here, operated by `pkg/tools` and `pkg/gateway`). Created lazily outside `SchemaSQL`: `telegram_dm_topic_mode` and `telegram_dm_topic_bindings`.

Indexes: sessions by source, (source, id), parent, started, session key, gateway peer tuple, handoff state, prompt hash, tool names, effective activity `COALESCE(last_activity_at, started_at)`, local rows by created source, and a unique partial index on `title`; messages by (session, timestamp), (session, id), (session, active, timestamp), assistant rows with tool calls, display page, display backfill, display identity, NULL active, (session, message_uid) for active rows, and platform message id; admissions pending by (target, status, seq) and a partial cron-request index for principal `cron-owner`; worker executions by (session, status); model usage by session and by model; lock and lease expiry; async delegation delivery.

Non-FTS triggers: `sessions_runtime_ledger_delete_guard` aborts deleting a session that still has admission or worker rows; `messages_transcript_revision_update` bumps `sessions.transcript_revision` on any payload rewrite; `messages_message_uid_insert` mints a uid when a writer bound NULL; `messages_display_order_insert`, `messages_display_visibility_update`, `messages_display_identity_update` and `messages_display_identity_delete` maintain `display_order` so every copy of one logical message shares the lowest row id of its visible copies.

- `common_schema.go` — [data] the DDL itself: `SchemaSQL`, `DeferredIndexSQL`, current FTS DDL (`FTSSQL`, `FTSTrigramSQL`) and the legacy inline FTS DDL
- `schema_sql.go` — [data] heal and migration SQL: `session_model_usage` rebuild and seed statements, scoped `gateway_routing` DDL, gateway metadata backfill
- `schema_init.go` — `initSchema` sequence, newer-schema refusal, fresh stamp, data migrations, uid backfill, duplicate-title repair before the unique index, FTS init; `ApplyDeclaredSchema` and `ReconcileStateSchema` for raw connections
- `schema_mixin.go` — `sessionSchema` mixin: column map and its disk cache, read probes that fail exactly when a store lags the schema, prompt dedupe, FTS trigger narrowing and source realignment migrations, admitted startup rebuild
- `session_schema_history.go` — [data] `SchemaHistory`: every column order each table ever shipped with, used by `pkg/app` lost-and-found recovery to recognise physical layouts in damaged files
- `carrier_type_migration.go` — v34 migration renaming the retired native assistant carrier type inside stored `reasoning_details`

#### Shared SQL fragments, identifiers and key formats

Building blocks reused by most queries: the predicates that classify a child session, the "last active" expression, the listing preview expression, end-reason sets and key builders. Session ids are `YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<6 hex>`; other recognised shapes are `cron_<job>_<stamp>`, `bg_...`, `room_<32 hex>`, `api_...`, `api-<16 hex>`, `run_<32 hex>`, a UUID4, and `local-<sha256>` for local sessions.

- `common.go` — child classification SQL (branch, reset, compression, delegate), end-reason sets (reset, boundary, recoverable, automatic), preview and last-active SQL, `SchemaVersion`, FTS constants, `on_session_delete` hook dispatch, IN-list chunking at 900
- `ids.go` — session id minting and the recognisers for every id shape the project mints
- `keys.go` — cron request ids `cron:<job>:<execution>` under principal `cron-owner`, prefix ranges, `AdmissionFingerprint` (SHA-256 of sorted compact JSON), `LocalIdentity`, profile from an `agent:<namespace>:...` session key
- `shape_preview_export.go`, `session_last_active_export.go` — [port-artifact] `ShapePreview` and `SQLSessionLastActive` for gateway listings

#### Error taxonomy, corruption latch and user-facing failure copy

Errors carry a Python `sqlite3` class and many implement `PyTypeName`, because callers still branch on Python exception names. `ClassifyPersistenceError` buckets any failure into locked, compression, compression_closed, turn_lease, corrupt, fts_index, replaced, deleted_wal, disk, session_row_missing, newer_schema, store_dir or unknown, and each bucket maps to a stable code, a plain-language gloss and an action line (wait and retry, free disk space, `icebath doctor --fix`, `icebath sessions recover`, stop the gateway).

- `errors.go` — SQLite class mapping, parameter binding checks, marker tables for lock, malformed, disk-full and FTS-scoped corruption, typed refusals (lease lost, compression busy or closed, held row rewritten, store replaced, WAL generation deleted, newer schema, corrupt), fatal message texts
- `health.go` — process-wide latch marking a database path corrupt after structural corruption so every handle on it stops writing; read by gateway readiness
- `user_copy.go` — `DescribeStorageFailure` (cause, stable code, gloss, profile-pinned action), `StoreUnavailableError`, `IsStoreFailure`

#### File identity, replaced-file and lost-WAL-generation detection, quarantine

Each handle records the device and inode of the main file and its `-wal` and `-shm` sidecars, and a per-file generation token (`state_meta` key `db_file_generation`, mirrored into the header `application_id`). A replaced main file or a deleted sidecar generation stops all writes with a sticky error, skips the close-time checkpoint and, for a lost WAL, copies the still-open WAL (and SHM, and the main file up to 512 MiB, else its header) into `<state.db>.retired-wal-<UTC stamp>-<pid>/` with a `manifest.json`. A zero-byte or non-SQLite `state.db` found at open is renamed to `state.db.{zeroed,notadb}-<stamp>-<pid>.bak` with its sidecars under `state.db.quarantine.lock` (flock, 5 s wait) and a fresh database is created.

- `dbfile.go` — header reads through a cached never-closed descriptor, sidecar identity, deleted-sidecar holder scan (procfs on Linux, libproc on macOS), `CaptureRetiredWALGeneration`, quarantine, read-only `CollectStateDBStats` and `CountDBHolders` for doctor
- `dbfile_{darwin,nodarwin,unix,windows}.go` — libproc syscalls on macOS and their absence elsewhere; per-OS file identity, positioned read and the quarantine lock primitive

#### Cross-process holders, lock owners and liveness probes

Answers "who else has this database open" and "is the recorded holder of a lock still alive". Holders are found by walking `/proc/*/fd` on Linux, open-file lists on other Unix systems and the Restart Manager on Windows; a failed scan reports an unknown holder (pid -1) rather than quiescence. Any process with a descriptor on the database or a sidecar is a holder; a process whose descriptors cannot be inspected is reported as a possible holder when its argv runs icebath (or, as a port leftover, a Python interpreter on an icebath module) and does not prove it serves another home or profile. Lock and lease holder strings carry `pid=<n>` and `pidns=<inode>` tokens, and a pid is only probed from the same PID namespace.

- `holders.go` — `ForeignStateDBHolders`, `InProcessStateDBHolders`, `HeldStoreRefusal` (operator text for held-store commands), `LiveWriterHoldsDB`, argv home and profile scoping, read-only file URI builder
- `holders_{linux,psutil,unix,windows}.go` — the per-OS scans: procfs, generic open-file list, shared stat helpers, `rstrtmgr.dll`
- `lockowners.go`, `lockowners_{linux,nolinux,unix,windows}.go` — parses `/proc/locks` to name the processes holding write locks on the database or sidecars when a writer gives up; empty off Linux
- `pidns.go` — PID namespace identity from `/proc/self/ns/pid`, holder token and the "may this pid be probed here" rule
- `psutil_pid_{unix,windows}.go` — [py-shim] `psutil.pid_exists`: signal zero plus the Linux thread-id filter; a process handle probe on Windows

#### WAL lock guard

While WAL is active the handle takes open-file-description (OFD) read locks on SQLite's SHARED byte range of the main file and on the deadman byte of the `-shm` file, through the descriptors this process already holds on them, and re-asserts them before each periodic checkpoint. Unlike the POSIX locks SQLite takes itself, OFD locks are not cancelled when the process closes some other descriptor on the same file, so other processes keep seeing the store as in use. On release the last handle per inode converts the lock back to a POSIX one and unlocks.

- `lockguard_unix.go` — guard ranges, own-descriptor lookup, hold and release with per-inode handle counts
- `lockguard_{ofd,noofd,windows}.go` — `F_OFD_SETLK` on Linux and macOS; a no-op on other Unix systems and on Windows

#### Corruption repair, doctor support and schema-drift reconcile

`RepairStateDBSchema` runs behind `state.db.repair.lock`, copies a forensic backup `state.db.malformed-backup-<stamp>` (newest three kept, identical content reused, free-space checked), then applies escalating strategies to a scratch snapshot `state.db.repair-scratch` and promotes the first one that opens cleanly: rebuild FTS, `REINDEX`, de-duplicate `sqlite_master`, drop the FTS schema and `VACUUM`. Automatic repair is tried once per process and at most three times per file fingerprint across restarts (`state.db.repair-attempts.json`). A store that merely lags the declared schema is caught up additively under the profile's `gateway.lock`: `icebath sessions repair` backs it up, reconciles a `state.db.reconcile-scratch` snapshot behind an exclusive guard and promotes it; a TUI browse of another profile's store first runs a read-only integrity scan, then adds the missing tables and columns in place in one transaction within a three-second budget, and refuses with a restart hint when a running gateway owns the store.

- `repair.go` — repair lock, backups, ledger, disk budget, exclusive guard connection, snapshot copy through the backup API, integrity classification (structural versus FTS-only), the four strategies, journal-mode restore
- `repair_seams.go` — swappable repair collaborators, 120 s lock timeout, 10 MiB/s minimum snapshot throughput
- `repair_lock_{unix,windows}.go` — non-blocking flock with holder record and orphan break on Unix; first-byte lock without holder record on Windows
- `reconcile.go` — `SchemaDriftReason`, `ReconcileDriftForBrowse`, `RepairDeclarativeSchema`, typed drift, budget and corrupt-store errors, owner and restart remedies read from the gateway lock record
- `sessions_cmd_repair.go` — `icebath sessions repair` (also bound as `pm repair`): check-only mode, backup unless `--no-backup`, session count after repair
- `doctor_exports.go`, `schema_not_built_export.go` — [port-artifact] wrappers for `icebath doctor` and session adoption (`DBOpensCleanly`, `ExclusiveRepairDBGuard`, `BackupSQLite`, `PathOnCrossVMFS`, `SchemaNotBuilt`)

#### Test-isolation guard and last init error

Refuses to open a production `state.db` (`<root>/state.db` or `<root>/profiles/<name>/state.db`) from a process that looks like a test run by environment (`ICEBATH_TEST_ISOLATION`, pytest variables), by being a Go test binary, or by having a test runner ancestor; `ICEBATH_STATE_DB_GUARD_BYPASS` opts out.

- `guard.go` — the guard, the last-init-error record surfaced in "session history unavailable" notices, and a leak sweep of handles opened under the isolation marker (`CloseLeakedTestInstances`, no callers)

#### Full-text index layout, tokenizer and lifecycle

Three FTS5 external-content indexes, each over a view and kept in sync by insert, delete and update-of triggers on `messages`: `messages_fts` (default tokenizer; content, tool_name, tool_calls; tool rows cut to their first 8192 characters) over `messages_fts_src`; `messages_fts_trigram` (content, tool_name; non-tool rows of sessions that are not cron, subagent or delegate children) over `messages_fts_trigram_src`; and `messages_fts_cjk` (tokenizer `cjk_unicode61`, non-tool rows) over `messages_fts_cjk_src`. Triggers are gated by `state_meta` rebuild markers (`fts_rebuild_high_water`, `fts_rebuild_progress` and the `fts_cjk_` pair) so a chunked backfill and live writes never double-index. FTS corruption fails open: the breadcrumbs `fts_stale` and `fts_cjk_stale` are written, every FTS trigger is dropped, canonical writes continue and search falls back to `LIKE`. Layout version 3 is recorded in `fts_storage_version`; older inline layouts are recognised from a registry of every shipped definition.

- `fts_cjk.go` — CJK DDL and triggers, and the tokenizer itself registered on the raw SQLite handle: unicode61 tokens with Hangul, Han, Hiragana and Katakana runs re-emitted as overlapping bigrams; gated by `sessions.cjk_fts`; `ICEBATH_FTS5_CJK_SO` and `<home>/lib/libfts5_cjk.so` survive only as a leftover existence check
- `fts_setup.go` — `sessionFTSSetup` mixin: table probes, missing-module and missing-tokenizer handling, orphan shadow-table cleanup, fail-open detach, adaptive rebuild chunk sizing (50 to 100000 rows, 0.25 s target)
- `fts_layout.go` — [data] `FTSVTableLayouts` registry and the drift checks (`FTSLayoutDrift`, `FTSLayoutCurrent`, `BaseSourceViewIsStale`)
- `fts_lock.go`, `fts_lock_{unix,windows}.go` — `state.db.fts_rebuild.lock`: cross-process admission for full rebuilds (120 s wait) with a JSON holder record and a break of locks held only by an orphaned descriptor of a dead process
- `schema_fts_recovery.go` — stale-index recovery at open and from the gateway's periodic tick with doubling backoff, deferral while foreign processes hold the store (`fts_rebuild_deferral` record), startup watchdog progress lease hook
- `update_maint_export.go` — [port-artifact] `DBHasLegacyInlineFTS` for `icebath update`

#### Message search and index maintenance

`SearchMessages` backs the `session_search` tool. Input is capped at 2048 characters and sanitised for FTS5 (paired quotes kept, dotted and hyphenated terms quoted). Routing: role filter `tool` or a stale index goes to a boolean `LIKE` scan; CJK queries go to the bigram index, then trigram (every token at least three characters), then `LIKE`; other queries go to `messages_fts`, then on no hits to the CJK and trigram indexes, then to an OR-relaxed retry; rows a deferred rebuild has not reached are supplemented by a `LIKE` scan of the gap. Filters cover sources, excluded sources, roles, time window and inactive rows; ordering is BM25 rank or time; hits can carry 200 characters of each neighbouring message, and searches slower than `sessions.search_slow_ms` log their route.

- `search_messages.go` — `SearchMessages` options and routing, CJK route, unindexed-gap supplement
- `search_query.go` — query sanitiser, CJK detection, OR relaxation, MATCH and LIKE SQL builders, context attachment, `OptimizeFTS` (merge to one segment), `RebuildFTS` (admitted full rebuild, used by gateway transcript repair)
- `search_mixin.go` — `sessionSearch` mixin: incremental merge after writes, deferred rebuild status and chunk steps (`FTSCJKRebuildStatus` has no callers), CJK reset, `OptimizeFTSStorage` (`icebath sessions optimize-storage`: demote legacy tables to `fts_v22_trash_*`, recreate, backfill, drain trash, optional `VACUUM`, pacing while other processes hold the store)
- `search_helpers.go` — progress payloads for backfill, teardown and vacuum, foreign-holder watch, filter clause builder, token quoting
- `search_views.go` — `GetAnchoredView` (window around a hit plus first and last messages outside it); `ListRecentUserMessages` has no callers

#### Session rows: create, end, reopen, flags and maintenance sweeps

A session row is created by a keep-existing upsert, so a later writer never overwrites routing columns an earlier one set, and a child inherits cwd, git facts and profile from its parent. Relationship is `parent_session_id` plus a marker: `end_reason='compression'` on the parent makes an unmarked child its continuation, while `model_config` keys `_branched_from`, `_reset_from` and `_delegate_from` mark branches, resets and subagent runs; `source='tool'` children are never continuations. `source` is the routing label (`local`, `cli`, `tui`, `acp`, `cron`, `kanban`, `subagent`, `api_server`, `bot_room`, a platform name) and `created_source` the surface that made a local row. Ending keeps the first `end_reason`; a reset-class reason also bumps the peer's `conversation_generations` counter. Sidebar flags (`archived`, `pinned`, `hidden`, `last_read_at`) are always written across the whole compression lineage.

- `sessions_mixin.go` — `CreateSession`, `EnsureSession`, `GetSession`, parent inheritance, content-addressed prompt and tools-pin storage, activity stamps that never move backwards, `EndSession`, `FindSessionByOrigin`
- `sessions.go` — the typed `Session` row and Go-style methods: `ListSessions` (tips only, filters, preview, last active), `ResolveSessionID` (unique prefix), `UpdateSessionCwd`, `CompressionTip`; `UpdateSessionModel` has no callers
- `sessions_ops.go` — `WorkspaceKey` (git root else cwd), `PromoteToSessionReset`, `UpdateSessionMeta` keeping session-owned config keys, runtime lock persistence, `UnarchiveRecoverableSession`, export size fence; `SetExpiryFinalized` has no callers
- `sessions_flags.go` — pin, hide and read flags per lineage (a pin unhides, except the canonical "Bot Chat"), filter-driven bulk `ArchiveSessions`
- `sessions_archive.go` — `ReopenSession`, deliberate versus sweep archive (`auto_archived` provenance) with delete-hook notification, retirement of undrained busy-queue rows (`RetireUndrainedQueueRows`, no callers)
- `session_maintenance.go` — `SweepOrphanedSessions` (ends idle open rows of given sources as `startup_orphan_reap`, honouring backend heartbeats, pins and live leases) and `ArchiveStaleSessions`
- `sessions_workspace.go` — cwd claim with a git-metadata generation so late async git enrichment is dropped; `BackfillRepoRoots` has no callers
- `session_activity.go` — activity description clamp (120 code points), provenance labels, `AwakeIdleMeter` that subtracts host sleep from watchdog idle readings
- `sessions_backfill.go` — stamps the owning profile on rows with a blank `profile_name`
- `recoverable_end_reason.go` — [unwired] `IsRecoverableEndReason`
- `end_and_bump_export.go` — [port-artifact] `EndAndBump` for gateway and TUI end writers

#### Titles

Titles are unique across the store (partial unique index), at most 100 code points after stripping control and invisible characters, and carry a provenance ranked derived, llm, user: a lower rank never replaces a higher one. A conflict is resolved by taking the title from a compression ancestor or an empty ended ghost, otherwise refused; continuations and branches get `<base> #N` numbering, and "Bot Chat" is a reserved canonical title.

- `titles_mixin.go` — `sessionTitles` mixin: `SanitizeTitle`, `SetSessionTitle`, `SetAutoTitleContext`, title source get and set, `GetSessionByTitle`, `ResolveSessionByTitle`, `GetNextTitleInLineage`
- `titles.go` — second, smaller implementation of the same rules on the `Tx` API; `SetTitle` is used by cron, while `SetAutoTitle`, `Title` and `ResolveByTitle` have no callers and `SetAutoTitle` shadows the mixin method of the same name

#### `model_config` JSON column and per-session settings

`sessions.model_config` is a free-form JSON object used as a per-session key-value store: lineage markers, runtime route, YOLO flag, `session_settings`, login state, compressor sidecars. Two parallel accessor sets exist, a ported one and a Go-style one.

- `model_config_patch.go` — atomic merge patch (nil deletes a key), tolerant parse, `SessionModelConfig`, `UpdateSessionModelConfig`, `SessionsWithModelConfigKey`, `SessionYoloEnabled`
- `model_config.go` — `GetModelConfigValue`; `UpdateConversationModelConfigValue` and `SessionIDsWithModelConfigKey` have no callers
- `session_model_set.go` — `/model` switch: writes the model and route in both stored shapes and drops the browser runtime lock
- `session_yolo.go` — persists the per-session approval bypass so it survives a resume
- `prompt_refresh.go` — `icebath sessions refresh-prompts`: a shared epoch counter in `state_meta` (`prompt_refresh.epoch`, per session `prompt_refresh.epoch:<id>`) that makes the next turn rebuild a stored system prompt

#### Session listing, counting and browse queries

Listing surfaces show one row per conversation: compression ancestors are collapsed onto their live tip, earlier reset segments of a local conversation are hidden behind the latest, and subagent, empty and archived rows are filtered unless asked for. Each row carries a preview (first eligible user message, compaction summaries and skill scaffolding unwrapped, cut to 60 characters) and `last_active` (freshest of activity stamp, newest message and start).

- `session_list.go` — projection of each compression root onto its live tip's fields
- `local_listing.go` — index of local reset lineages built from creation receipts, cached per connection by change counter, used to hide superseded segments
- `portability.go` — misnamed: the shared "rich row" SELECT, batched rich-row fetch and `ListCronJobRuns` (cron run history by request-id range); `GetSessionRichRow` has no callers
- `sessions_recent_bounded.go` — `ListRecentSessionsBounded` for the session-search tool: 20 rows under a row ceiling and a three-second cooperative deadline
- `sessions_search.go` — `SearchSessions` scoped by source and workspace key, skipping empty launch stubs; `SearchSessionsByID` has no callers
- `sessions_count.go` — counts matching the list filters, `SessionCountGE`, `DeclaredScopeIdentity`; `SessionCountBySource` has no callers
- `sessions_status.go` — lifecycle status from the last message row: error, interrupted or complete
- `session_listing_query.go`, `session_listing_args.go` — the gateway resume and sessions listing commands: argument parsing (`list`, `ls`, `browse`, `all`, `full`, `search <query>`, `find <query>`, else a resume target), source scoping, unnamed and current rows hidden by default, markdown rendering for messengers
- `session_listing_scope.go` — [unwired] reads `sessions.show_subagents`
- `session_timeline.go` — [unwired] human-prompt timeline and page-around-prompt reads using SQL functions registered on the connection

#### Usage and cost accounting

Token and cost totals live on the session row and, per (model, provider, base URL, billing mode, task), in `session_model_usage`. Main-loop reports are queued and applied by a background writer that coalesces adjacent deltas with the same route, retires after 30 idle seconds and is drained at process exit and before reads that need fresh counters; auxiliary model calls are recorded under a task name without touching session totals.

- `usage.go` — `QueueTokenCounts`, `FlushTokenCounts`, `UpdateTokenCounts` (delta or absolute, cost status and source, first-route stamping), `RecordAuxiliaryUsage`, `AuxiliaryUsageByTask` over the compression lineage, billing route update, exit hooks; `UsageTotals` has no callers

#### Message model and in-memory dict codec

Not persistence: the `Message` and `ToolCall` structs every agent and provider package passes around, with a lossless conversion to and from Python-style dicts that preserves unknown keys and key order. Identity is carried by `message_uid` (stable across clones and compactions), `absorbed_message_uids` (rows merged into this one), and per-occurrence tool-call uids so a provider that reuses a call id still pairs correctly.

- `messages.go` — `Message`, `ToolCall`, `ContentText`, the `"\x00json:"` prefix marking structured content stored as JSON text
- `message_dict.go` — [port-artifact] `MessageToDict` and `MessageFromDict` by reflection, per-role key build orders, a registry remembering the key order of the last eight store loads
- `message_metadata.go` — uid minting and stamping, tool-call uid indexing and resolution, withheld-prompt handling, persistence-only field stripping, timestamp stamping
- `identity.go` — stored identity columns to live keys and back, `CoalesceToolCallID`, the Python-repr display key of a tool-calling assistant row
- `tool_call_ids.go` — every wire spelling of a tool call id, including the parts of a bridged id
- `message_content.go` — `FlattenMessageText` over chat and Responses content parts
- `message_sanitization.go` — lone-surrogate replacement and non-ASCII stripping over messages, payloads and tool schemas

#### Transcript writes: append, replace and row-addressed repair

Every transcript writer runs the same admission checks inside its transaction: a live compression lock held by someone else refuses the write, a named turn-lease holder must still own the lease (an expired one is extended, 300 s default), a parent already closed by compression refuses unless allowed, and stale locks of dead processes are reclaimed on the way. Rows are soft-state: `active=1` is the live transcript, `active=0, compacted=1` is history summarised by compaction and still shown, and `active=0, compacted=0` was removed by rewind, undo or edit. Live dicts carry `_row_id` and a BLAKE2b snapshot of the stored row so a later flush rewrites that exact row only if nobody else changed it.

- `messages_mixin.go` — guards, content and metadata encoding, display identity (SHA-256 of a Python-repr tuple) and generation dedupe, `AppendMessage`, counters, reactions, compaction-checkpoint pruning, platform-message and input-owner lookups, `LatestConversationBoundary`; `ClearMessages`, `GetMessageReactions` and `LatestMessageRowID` have no callers
- `messages_rows.go` — `AppendMessagesBatch` and the in-transaction append: serialisation, row-state rollback between retries, parent timestamp carry, insert
- `messages_rewrite.go` — `ReplaceMessages` (delete or soft-archive the dropped rows, kept-prefix detection), `SetUserMessageContent`, `DeactivateMessage`, `ResolveActiveRowID`, active watermark; `DisplayMessageCount`, `FindPRURLMessages` and `HasArchivedMessages` have no callers
- `messages_host.go` — row decoding (content prefix, double-encoded metadata) and `GetMessagesAround`
- `transcript_repair.go` — row snapshot digest, resolution of row-addressed rewrites against concurrent winners, re-insert guard by uid, display index restore, `SyncFlushedMessageMarkers`
- `sequence_repair.go` — `RepairMessageSequence`: merges consecutive assistant or user turns, drops stray tool results, prunes unanswered tool calls, recording which durable rows each survivor stands for
- `api_content.go` — backfills the exact text sent to the API onto a user row whose content still matches
- `detached_results.go` — "detached" results: an async delegation result or a completion note appended between turns as a user row, once per delegation or admission across the lineage, refused under a live turn
- `discarded_turn_exports.go` — [port-artifact] exports the gateway uses to close a discarded (failed or refused) turn's open tail with a boundary row inside the settlement transaction

#### Transcript reads, display projection and resume

Two views are read from the same rows: the model view (active rows of the tip session, repaired) and the display view (active plus compacted rows across the whole compression lineage, one row per logical message, model-only rows hidden). Resume resolves an id to the deepest descendant with messages and refuses transcripts beyond the resume cap.

- `messages_read.go` — `GetMessages`, `GetMessagesAsConversation`, display paging through `display_order` with a legacy fallback, `ConversationRevision`, replayed-user-turn dedupe, compression chain and tip walks, `ResolveResumeSessionID`, `AssertResumeSafe`; `GetResumeConversations`, `GetResumeMessageCount` and `GetAncestorDisplayPrefix` have no callers
- `messages_lineage.go` — fork classification, verified resume lineage, `IsKanbanOwnedSession`
- `compaction_display.go` — drops display rows that repeat an archived tool result, model-only row test
- `compaction_projection.go` — `ProjectCompactionMessageForDisplay`: the authentic transcript content of a row, nothing for a pure compaction handoff
- `todo_result.go` — `GetLatestTodoResult`: newest valid Todo tool result in the resume scope (512000 character cap), skipping copies that were removed

#### Rewind

Rewind soft-deletes every active row from a chosen user turn onward and bumps `rewind_count`; a composite compaction carrier keeps its handoff part. The user-ordinal variant first checks that the caller's in-memory history still matches the durable rows.

- `messages_rewind.go` — `RewindToMessage` by row id with expected-content fence; `PurgeStaleToolCallMarkers` (`icebath sessions clean-markers`) with optional `VACUUM INTO` snapshot
- `user_turn_rewind.go` — `PlanUserTurnRewind` and `RewindUserTurn` by user ordinal, retryable-text extraction, durable content projection (multimodal envelopes to summaries, images to markers), ephemeral scaffolding test
- `slash_commands_session_export.go` — [port-artifact] `RewindInTransaction` for the gateway retry command

#### Compression lineage and rotation

One of the two shapes `pkg/agent`'s context compression persists: rotation ends the parent with `end_reason='compression'` and publishes a child session holding the summary handoff plus any rows appended after the compressor's watermark, in one transaction that also requires the compression lease, moves the local receipt and route to the child and un-hides a sweep-archived lineage. Chain walks follow the preferred continuation child and are capped at 1000 hops.

- `compression_publish.go` — `PublishCompressionChild`, lineage CTE, `GetCompressionLineage`, orphan handling (`ReopenOrphanedCompressionSession`, `FinalizeOrphanedCompressionSessions` marking `orphaned_compression`), `ReopenIfExplicitlyClosed`, `created_source` stamping of old chains; `FindLiveCompressionChild` has no callers
- `compression_chain.go` — preferred-child step SQL and `created_source` propagation to ancestors
- `compression_tip_export.go` — [port-artifact] `CompressionTipOn`

#### In-place compaction, coverage proof and tool-output pruning

The other shape: the session id stays, covered rows become `active=0, compacted=1`, and the summary plus carried tail are inserted as fresh active rows. Because the compressor works on an in-memory copy while other writers may append, the commit proves which durable rows each held message stands for (by row id, uid, row snapshot, or an explained rewrite) and clones concurrent tail rows forward; a held row rewritten underneath aborts the commit.

- `messages_archive.go` — `ArchiveAndCompact`: lease check, config patch, compare-and-swap on held rows, named-row archive or watermark fallback, tail clone, display order reconcile
- `coverage.go` — the matching rules: carried tail claims, merged user runs, image-part replacement, retired rows without ids, timestamp-prefix stripping
- `compression_archive.go` — `CoverageForCommit`, `HeldArchiveCoverage`, `NewestExactHeldID` used by the agent before committing
- `prune_rewrite.go` — `RewritePrunedRows` for the agent's tool-output pruning: rewrites a row in place behind an archived twin, with held-row checks (`RewrittenHeldRowIDs`)

#### Compression locks, turn leases and failure counters

Two TTL locks stored as rows: `compression_locks` per session and `session_turn_leases` per conversation (the root of the compression chain). A holder that expired or whose local pid is provably dead is reclaimed; turn leases long expired are swept after a day. The blocking acquire polls every second for up to 30 minutes and reports waiting every 15 s.

- `compression_leases.go` — try, refresh, release and holder reads for both locks, `AcquireSessionTurnLease`
- `compression_leases_polling.go` — the polling loop factored out for worker-side stores
- `compression_counters.go` — per-session compressor state: failure cooldown (record, read, restore, clear), fallback streak, ineffective count, recovery deadline, overload streak; each exists as a ported method and as a Go-style twin
- `worker_store_checked.go` — [port-artifact] error-returning variants of lock, cooldown and token-flush calls for interface parity with the worker store

#### Compaction markers and synthetic turn text shared with `pkg/agent`

Not persistence: the byte-pinned strings the compressor and agent loop write into transcripts, kept here because listing previews, display dedupe and rewind must recognise them in stored rows.

- `scaffold.go` — current and legacy summary prefixes and delimiters, skill-invocation scaffolding parsers (`DescribeSkillInvocation`), the accepted epoch window for stored timestamps
- `compressor_markers.go` — every historical handoff prefix, `ClassifySummaryContent` (standalone or merged)
- `compressor_turns.go` — continuation, nudge and length-continuation texts, synthetic-versus-real user turn tests, `SplitUserOriginatedTurn`, `StripContextSummaryHandoffMessage`
- `turn_display_copy.go` — failed-turn display kind, the out-of-band steer marker and its extraction, reference quoting
- `context_compressor_display_keys.go`, `control_frame_openers.go` — [data] the `model_only` metadata key and the bracket openers of agent control frames
- `memory_context.go` — `SanitizeContext`: strips memory-context fence tags and recalled-memory system notes from provider output

#### Runtime ledger: admissions FIFO and terminal tombstones

The gateway's durable input queue. An owner process begins a `runtime_epoch`; each input is admitted once per (principal, target session, request id) with a payload digest, so an identical retry replays and a changed one is refused; the queue holds at most 32 per session. The FIFO head is claimed (`started`, bound to epoch and generation), settled to `terminal` with an outcome and compacted result, cancelled while queued, or marked `unknown` when a later epoch finds it started. Results and tombstones of retired admissions live in `state_meta` under `gateway.admission.result.v1.`, `gateway.terminal_admission.v1.`, `gateway.terminal_identity.v1.` and `gateway.terminal_worker.v1.`.

- `runtime_admissions.go` — `BeginRuntimeEpoch`, `AdmitSessionInput`, `ClaimSessionInput`, `SettleSessionInput`, `CancelSessionInput`, `RecoverSessionInputs`, `ResolveUnknownSessionInput`, steer transfer settlement; `SteerSessionInput` and `RevertSteerInput` (handing a queued input to the running claim) have no callers
- `runtime_queue_moves.go` — replacement bindings (`gateway.queued_replacement.v1.`) that cancel a still-queued input in favour of its successor, `RehomeQueuedInputs` and `RetargetLocalAutomation` after reset or rotation, mutation receipt keys and replay
- `runtime_errors.go` — `RuntimeStoreError` with bounded wire reason codes (`invalid_params`, `not_found`, `admission_conflict`, `storage_unavailable` and others), the retired-session key prefix
- `terminal.go` — `CompactResult` (keeps replay and accounting, drops cumulative history), exact retry against a retired target, adoption secret digest; `TerminalWorkerReceipt` has no callers
- `session_admissions_list.go`, `terminal_reanchor_export.go` — [port-artifact] `ListSessionAdmissions` and `ReanchorCurrentTurnUserIdx` wrappers

#### Runtime ledger: worker executions and the `worker.persist` receipt protocol

Worker processes (cron runs, delegated children, compute, kanban) do not write the store themselves: they register an execution against a session generation and send sequence-numbered receipts that the owning gateway applies, each receipt and its result stored so an exact retry replays. The closed operation table lives here.

- `runtime_worker_executions.go` — `RegisterWorkerExecution`, `AdoptWorkerExecution` (new epoch adopts a proven worker by secret)
- `runtime_worker_receipts.go` — `ApplyWorkerReceipt`, the operation table, `transcript.append`, `turn.acquire`, `turn.renew`, `turn.release`, `usage.main`, `usage.auxiliary`, `execution.finish`
- `worker_context.go` — `session.context`, `session.prompt`, `session.sidecars`, `session.tools`, `session.tail_role`, `session.row_role`
- `worker_lifecycle_handlers.go` — `session.create`, `session.end`, `session.lifecycle`, title, activity, billing route and api-content operations
- `worker_compression.go` — `compression.*` operations: lock, cooldown, counters, lineage and history reads, archive, publish (moving worker, admissions and goal, heartbeat and loop automation state to the child), reopen, cleanup; `WorkerClaimOrigin`, `WorkerRetryTarget`
- `runtime_workers.go` — lineage-wide worker state probes, retirement of child executions (`<parent>/child:<id>` prefix), receipt compaction to a retired marker
- `worker_lifecycle.go` — session row upsert on the receipt connection that refuses to recreate a retired session
- `worker_lifecycle_constructor_export.go` — [port-artifact] `IsWorkerConstructorConfigKey`

#### Runtime mutations (`session.mutate`)

One transaction per closed operation, with an exact-retry receipt stored in `state_meta` (`gateway.mutation.v1.<digest>`), an expected-revision check against `sessions.runtime_revision`, and a generation bump for operations that fence running work. Operations: `sidebar`, `rename`, `archive`, `model`, `reasoning`, `workspace`, `launch`, `editor_mcp`, `edit_policy`, `branch`, `reset`, `compress`, `rewind`, `delete`, `import`.

- `runtime_mutations.go` — `MutateRuntimeSession`: prepare or commit, live guard, receipt, shell-line carry for branches, delete event; one-time legacy admissions import (`ImportLegacySessionAdmissions`, no callers)
- `mutations.go` — payload validation for every operation, dispatch, metadata edits, rewind and import handlers
- `mutation_prepared.go` — policy edits against a prepared snapshot (model, reasoning, launch, workspace, editor MCP, edit policy), deferred model picks (`gateway.deferred_pick.v1.`), `PolicyPicks`, `CommitRefreshedPolicy`
- `mutation_guards.go` — `RequireIdle`, `RequireNotExecuting`, `RequireTargetAdvanceable`, busy refusal mapping, delete target expansion
- `mutation_branch.go` — copies the transcript through a boundary into a new local session with its own route, policy and receipt
- `mutation_reset.go` — publishes a reset child (`_reset_from`) and advances the receipt and route to it
- `mutation_compress.go` — commits a prepared summary, target and generation
- `mutation_delete.go` — retires the delete targets, then removes their rows
- `mutation_chat_pick.go` — model or reasoning pick applied to the messaging chat mounted on a local session, fenced by that row's revision and generation and stored as a retry receipt
- `mutation_binding.go` — who may control unrouted history rows: owner binding in `state_meta` (`gateway.history_control.v1.`), claim on first authorised use

#### Local sessions: creation receipts, lineage, lane handoff and legacy adoption

A "local" session is one a client surface (CLI, TUI, ACP, desktop app) creates through the gateway. It has a deterministic id `local-<sha256(profile, principal, request)>`, a row whose `source` comes from the creation policy and whose `created_source` is the surface that label maps to, its own entry in `gateway_routing`, and a frozen creation receipt in `state_meta` under `gateway.local_policy.v1:<id>` holding its policy, route, routing entry and lineage. The id is the logical session; its "physical target" is the transcript currently written, which moves on compression and reset and is validated edge by edge against stored rows. A conversation taken over by a messaging lane releases its receipt, and old unrouted rows written before receipts existed can be adopted (`gateway.local_legacy.v1:`).

- `local_commit.go` — `CommitLocalSession` (row, route and policy reserved together, exact retry replays), `EndIdleLocalSession`
- `local_create_requests.go` — comparison of a create retry with the frozen request, client environment included
- `local_lineage.go` — canonical runtime JSON, lineage validation, `localPhysicalTarget`, target advance, `AdoptUntrackedCompression`, `ResetLocalTarget`
- `local_handoff.go` — `HandoffHead`, release of receipts whose row a messaging lane now routes, title following the conversation head, `LocalReceipt`
- `local_migration.go` — legacy local source labels, client-app history detection, retired `nous:` account label cleanup, `ValidateLegacyRow`, legacy target binding
- `local_recovery_exports.go`, `local_conversation_ids_export.go`, `legacy_local_sources_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports for gateway recovery (`ValidateLocalLineage`, `AdoptableCompression`, `ReleaseHandedOffReceipts`, `RuntimeJSON`, `LocalConversationIDs`, `LegacyLocalSources`); `RetireRoutes` has no callers

#### Session client environment

Not persistence: which environment variables a client may hand to its session's tool subprocesses. Names containing credential fragments (`KEY`, `TOKEN`, `SECRET`, `PASSWORD` and others) or icebath control names never travel, `terminal.client_env_passthrough` adds names, and a client not proven local keeps only values that name nothing on the gateway host. The rules are frozen into the session policy at creation.

- `session_client_env.go` — rule building and parsing, collection and normalisation, context binding (`ClientEnvScope`), `ToolEnv`, `ToolchainEnviron`, `SessionEnv`, `IsSecretEnvName`

#### Deletion and retirement fences

Deleting a session removes it, its whole compression lineage and local conversation, and its subagent children; branch children are orphaned, sessions under a live turn lease or compression lock are refused, and the session's files in the sessions folder (`<home>/sessions/`) are removed (`<id>.json`, `<id>.jsonl`, `session_<id>.json`, `<id>.shell.jsonl`, `request_dump_<id>_*.json`). "Retired" means a deleted id leaves a marker in `state_meta` (`gateway.retired_session.v1.<id>`) so it cannot be recreated or re-routed: user deletes are permanent, prune sweeps expire after the seven-day retry horizon. Terminal admissions and workers shrink to digest tombstones, mutation receipts lose their content, routes are fenced (`gateway.retired_route.v1.`), and referenced media and tool-output spillover files become deletion candidates collected later.

- `session_delete.go` — `DeleteSession` with drift fences, `DeleteSessions`, delete target listing, file removal; `DiscardUnadmittedSession`, `DeleteSessionIfEmpty`, `CountEmptySessions` and `DeleteEmptySessions` have no callers
- `session_retirement.go` — retirement markers, tombstone compaction and expiry, route fences, local receipt and API binding cleanup, media and spillover collection, `FirstGeneration` for derived API session ids, `CreateConflict`
- `retire_media_export.go`, `session_guarded_export.go` — [port-artifact] `RetireMedia`; `GuardedIDs` has no callers

#### Pruning, retention, archiving and vacuum

Retention deletes only ended sessions whose last activity is older than the bound (90 days by default from `sessions.retention_days`, `sessions.auto_prune` gating the automatic pass), always whole lineages (an ancestor stays while one of its continuations is not matched), and never pinned ones or the continuations a pinned segment covers; the automatic pass also skips sessions under a live turn lease or compression lock. The startup pass runs at most daily under `state.db.auto-maintenance.lock`, also ends stale open rows of state-owned sources (`cli`, `cron`, `kanban`, `acp`, `api_server`, `subagent`, `tool`, `recovered`), and vacuums at most every 30 days when rows were pruned, more than 25 percent of pages are free and no other process holds the store; stamps are `last_auto_prune`, `last_vacuum` and `last_auto_archive` in `state_meta`.

- `session_prune.go` — `PruneFilters` (age, source, title, model, provider, chat, cost, token and message bounds), dry-run listing and counts for `icebath sessions prune` and `archive`, `PruneSessions`, `MaybeAutoArchive`, `MaybeAutoPruneAndVacuum`, `Vacuum` (`icebath sessions optimize`: FTS merge, `VACUUM`, WAL truncate), size and freelist readings; `PruneEmptyGhostSessions` has no callers
- `prune_kwargs.go` — converts a CLI or API filter dict into store arguments
- `prune_advisor.go` — low-disk advisor: when free space is under 2 GiB (or under 10 percent and 20 GiB) and auto-prune is undecided, estimates reclaimable bytes and raises a question on every surface, repeated after the snooze window; `/autoprune on|off|later|status`; snooze in `<home>/.auto_prune_prompt.json` (seven days), estimate cache in `<home>/.auto_prune_estimate.json`

#### Gateway routing index, peers, platform handoff and backend heartbeats

Persistence for the messaging side of the gateway: the session-key to session routing index (scoped, entries skipped when their route is retired), the routing identity stamped on session rows, recovery of the latest session for a chat peer, adoption of rows that lost their routing identity, the cross-platform handoff state machine (`pending`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`) and liveness rows for TUI and serve backends consulted by the orphan sweep.

- `gateway_routing.go` — `RecordGatewaySessionPeer`, routing entry save, replace and load, `FindLatestGatewaySessionForPeer`, orphan find and adopt (900 s contiguity gap), never-active keyed row pruning, hygiene failure streak, handoff request, claim, complete, fail and stale reclaim
- `gateway_heartbeats.go` — `RegisterBackendHeartbeat` and `ClearBackendHeartbeat` (used by the TUI server reaper); `PruneStaleHeartbeats` and `ListBackendHeartbeats` have no callers

#### Telegram DM topic mode

Per private chat, Telegram forum topics can each be bound to one session. The two tables are created on first use, keyed by profile (bindings also unique per session id), and a pre-profile layout is rebuilt in place (`telegram_dm_topic_schema_version` = 3 in `state_meta`).

- `telegram_topics.go` — enable and disable topic mode, bind, look up and delete topic bindings, list a user's Telegram sessions not bound to any topic

#### Profile identity rekey, purge and cross-profile repair

Profile names are baked into stored data (`profile_name`, `agent:<namespace>:` session keys, origin JSON, routing entries, heartbeats, topic tables and the gateway's `delivery_obligations` table when present). Renaming or deleting a profile rewrites or removes all of them in one transaction, and `icebath sessions repair-profiles` finds rows whose key profile, label and owning store disagree and relabels them or moves them to the right store.

- `profile_identity.go` — `RekeyProfileState` and `PurgeProfileState` with per-table counts
- `profile_repair.go` — `FindCrossedProfileSessions`, relabel and sever operations, `ExportSessionForMove`, `ImportMovedSession`, `DeleteMovedSession` (refused for sessions the runtime ledger references), routing row adoption, topic row relabel

#### Export, import, save and the HTML page

Export produces one dict per session with every message (optionally compacted and removed rows), timing evidence and the shell lines the user ran, either per row or as a whole compression lineage. `icebath sessions export` renders JSONL or Markdown (whole sessions or user prompts only) or a self-contained HTML page; `/save <json|md|html>` writes one session, default name `icebath_session_<id>.<format>`.
