- `runtime_bootstrap.go` — `TicketStore`: 32-byte tickets stored by SHA-256, 30 s lifetime, at most 1024 outstanding, redeemed once, bound to instance, profile, subject, purpose (interactive, native-http, native-profile-create, native-profile-registry, exposure, worker-adoption) and scope (profile or host)
- `runtime_bootstrap_pipe.go`, `runtime_bootstrap_windows.go`, `runtime_bootstrap_native_other.go` — Windows named-pipe control server and client with same-user checks (pipe owner SID and DACL, client token SID, logon session, elevation, impersonation revert) and deadline-bounded overlapped I/O; an error on other hosts
- `runtime_bootstrap_refused.go`, `runtime_bootstrap_probe_{other,windows}.go` — explains why this user's own gateway refused a client (elevated gateway, or another Windows logon session) with the remedy text
- `tui_bootstrap_query_{unix,windows}.go` — one request line to the private control socket or pipe and its bounded response (65537 bytes), for the TUI bootstrap
- `tui_server_export.go`, `tui_session_identity_bind.go` — [port-artifact] exported approval-command redaction and purpose capabilities (`PurposeCapabilities` has no caller); binds the identity checks into `pkg/tuihost`

#### Relay: connector enrolment and configuration

The relay is an outbound connection from this gateway to an external connector service that owns the real bot identities on chat platforms. The connector relays platform messages to the gateway and the gateway's sends, edits, drafts, prompts and media back to the platform, so the gateway needs no platform credentials and no inbound port. It is unrelated to "hosted" rooms, which are multi-bot group rooms this gateway itself hosts for local profiles and peer gateways. Settings come from env first and then the `gateway` config block: `GATEWAY_RELAY_URL`, `_ID`, `_SECRET`, `_ENDPOINT`, `_ROUTE_KEYS`, `_INSTANCE_ID` and `_WAKE_URL` (config keys `relay_url`, `relay_id` and so on), plus env-only `GATEWAY_RELAY_DISPLAY_NAME`, `GATEWAY_RELAY_PLATFORMS` and `GATEWAY_RELAY_BOT_IDS`; an explicit `platforms.relay.enabled: false` vetoes all of it.

- `relay_config.go`, `relay_init_config.go` — env-then-config readers for the connector URL, gateway id and secret, public endpoint, route keys, instance id, wake URL and display name (the skin's agent name unless stock, 64 characters)
- `relay_identity.go` — fronted platform and bot id pairs (the generic `relay` pair when none are named) and the explicit-disable check
- `relay_identity_token.go` — caller identity bearer for provisioning: OAuth2 client-credentials against `gateway.idp.token_url` (or `GATEWAY_RELAY_IDP_*`), or a plain GET of an ambient token endpoint when no client id and secret are set; urllib-shaped HTTP error types
- `relay_init_provision.go` — boot-time self-provision: `POST /relay/provision` per fronted platform with gateway id (default `gw-<hostname>`), endpoint, route keys, instance id, wake URL and display name; puts the returned id, secret and delivery key into the process env without writing them to disk (the explicit enrolment command is in `pkg/gatewaycli`); background retry until credentials exist
- `relay_init_policy.go` — `POST /relay/policy` declaring each fronted platform's relevance policy (require-mention and free-response scopes from config)
- `relay_init_register.go` — registers the builtin `relay` platform entry whose factory builds the WebSocket transport and the adapter
- `relay_auth.go` — bearer token: unpadded base64url of `<gateway id>:<expiry>:<hex HMAC-SHA256>`, 300 s lifetime
- `relay_http_diagnostics.go` — bounded, secret-redacted description of connector HTTP errors; detects an answer that came from a proxy hop

#### Relay: WebSocket transport and wire protocol

The gateway dials `ws(s)://<connector>/relay` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>` and exchanges newline-terminated JSON text frames. Gateway to connector: `hello` (platform, botId, and for Discord a slash-command manifest), `outbound` (requestId, optional platform and botId, an action whose `op` is send, edit, delete, typing, draft, follow_up, get_chat_info, prompt, react, send_media, thread_create, thread_rename, task_card or task_card_stop), `inbound_ack` (bufferId), `going_idle`, `interrupt`. Connector to gateway: `descriptor`, `inbound`, `outbound_result`, `going_idle_ack`, `interrupt_inbound`, `passthrough_forward`. Close code 4401 after a successful handshake triggers one redial with a fresh token and then latches revocation; other drops reconnect with exponential backoff from 1 s to 30 s.

- `relay_ws_transport.go` — dial with env proxies, keepalive pings, reader loop, request and result correlation with 30 s timeouts and an "ambiguous" verdict for an unanswered `send_media`, per-platform descriptor handshake, inbound ACK deferred until admission commits, fresh-token retry, revocation latch, reconnect supervisor with a 60 s hold during suspends, idle and dormant modes, drain on disconnect
- `relay_ws_wire.go` — dial URL normalisation, decoding of `inbound` frames into `MessageEvent` (media URLs, types and filenames, read-only channel-context block, rewriting of the Slack `/icebath <sub>` parent command) and of passthrough forwards (base64 body, ordered headers), disconnect budget (`ICEBATH_GATEWAY_ADAPTER_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT`, 5 s)
- `relay_descriptor.go` — `CapabilityDescriptor`, contract version 1: platform, label, max message length, draft streaming, edit, threads, markdown dialect, length unit (chars or utf16), emoji, platform hint, PII safety, context, in-channel continuation, block formatting, supported ops (legacy set send, edit, typing, follow_up when none are advertised)
- `relay_command_manifest.go` — the Discord slash-command manifest sent in the hello, mirroring the native command tree

#### Relay: the adapter

`RelayAdapter` is one platform adapter standing in for every fronted platform; it takes limits and abilities from the negotiated descriptor of the chat's platform and treats user authorisation as the connector's job. Per-chat state (scope, platform, profile, DM user, last inbound timestamp, open and sealed draft ids, Slack thread anchors) is kept in bounded insertion-ordered maps.

- `relay_adapter.go` — the struct, descriptor-driven capability answers (message length and length unit per chat, draft streaming, native task cards), the outbound and capability-gated op helpers, send-result projection
- `relay_adapter_connect.go` — connect (wire handlers, dial, adopt the descriptor) and the revocation monitor that marks the adapter fatally disabled
- `relay_adapter_state.go` — ordered bounded maps and sets, descriptor adoption, Slack knobs from config extras (reply in thread, DM top-level threads as sessions, unfurl hints)
- `relay_adapter_inbound.go`, `relay_inbound_admission.go` — inbound path: scope capture, replay dedupe by platform, chat and message id, Slack thread stamping, prompt-answer consumption, download of connector-rehosted media, then durable admission serialised per chat; permanent and parked refusals are acknowledged, anything else is left for connector replay
- `relay_adapter_send.go` — send, edit, delete, typing, follow-up, chat info, format hints, Slack thread anchoring, per-platform sends, disconnect (go idle, then close within the budget), dormant mode and redial hold for scale-to-zero
- `relay_adapter_draft.go` — draft-stream frames with a draft id, sealing the open stream with the final content (one retry on a lost ACK), swallowing stragglers after a seal
- `relay_adapter_cards.go` — native task-card progress frames (Slack only inside a thread) and sealing an orphaned open stream
- `relay_adapter_prompts.go` — exec-approval, slash-confirm and clarify prompts through the `prompt` op with owner-nonce ids, expiry and a 256-entry resolved memory; processing reactions, handoff thread creation, thread rename
- `relay_adapter_discord_interaction.go` — turns forwarded Discord interactions (slash commands with options, component presses, modal submits) into message events, remembering chat name and topic labels in the session store
- `relay_adapter_media.go`, `relay_media.go` — the `send_media` lane and the connector media client: upload to `/relay/media` and download of `/relay/media/<id>` with the signed bearer, 25 MiB cap, retries after 2 s and 5 s on 403, 408, 429 and 5xx

#### Relay egress authorisation and scale-to-zero

Two policies layered on the relay: where the agent may send through the shared bot identity, and when a relay-only gateway may suspend itself.

- `relay_egress.go` — decides whether a send to a platform would leave through the relay (fronted, with no live native adapter) and, for agent-initiated sends through the shared identity, allows only attested targets (home channel, channel directory, chats this gateway held sessions in); fails closed when routing cannot be determined; decline detection
- `scale_to_zero.go` — idle suspend for relay-only deployments: armed when `ICEBATH_SCALE_TO_ZERO` is truthy, messaging is relay-only and a wake URL is registered; idle after 2 minutes without work or inbound; suspends through the Fly Machines socket `/.fly/api` or a brokered `GATEWAY_RELAY_SLEEP_URL`

#### Inbound webhook adapter

The `webhook` platform listens on port 8644 by default and serves `GET /health`, `POST /webhooks/<route>`, `POST /p/<profile>/webhooks/<route>` and any `/p/<profile>/…` request forwarded to that profile's shared-listener app. Routes are static (`platforms.webhook.extra.routes`) or dynamic subscriptions written by the agent and `icebath webhook` to `<home>/webhook_subscriptions.json`, reloaded when the file changes, static names winning. Each POST is authenticated (per-route or global secret; `INSECURE_NO_AUTH` only on a loopback bind), rate limited (30 per minute per route), size capped (1 MiB), filtered, optionally transformed by a script, rendered into a prompt and then run as an agent turn, pushed straight to a target (`deliver_only`) or used to fire an existing cron job (`cron_job`).

- `webhook.go` — the adapter: route validation at connect, signature schemes (Svix and Standard Webhooks, Linear, GitHub `X-Hub-Signature-256`, GitLab token, generic `X-Webhook-Signature-V2` over `<timestamp>.<body>` with a 300 s window, legacy body-only V1 with a warning), delivery ids and one-hour idempotency, event allowlist, prompt templates with dotted payload fields, skills, per-route toolsets, reply delivery (`log`, `github_comment` through the `gh` CLI, or another platform through the routed profile's adapter and home channel) and optional transcript mirroring
- `webhook_filters.go`, `webhook_filters_procattr{,_windows}.go` — declarative filters (`all`, `any`, `not`; `exists`, `missing`, `equals`, `not_equals`, `contains`, `in`, `in_file`, `regex` on dotted payload, event and header fields) and route scripts confined to `<home>/scripts`, run with bash or a `python3` found on PATH, payload on stdin, 30 s timeout, secrets scrubbed from the environment
- `webhook_coalesce.go` — per-route debouncing by a rendered key: keeps only the newest event of a group for a quiet window (30 s) up to a maximum wait (300 s), then dispatches once with a note; agent-mode routes only
- `webhook_mcp_events.go` — routes created by the MCP events tool: verification challenge echo, terminated and gap control envelopes, replay cursor storage, `{data}` prompt rendering capped at 32,000 characters

#### Durable producer admission and webhook reply destinations

A producer delivery is committed to the owning profile's session authority before it is acknowledged to the sender. `AdmitProducer` serves the webhook and relay adapters; the Graph adapter resolves the same scope with `ProducerScope` and commits through its own function.

- `webhook_ingress.go` — `AdmitProducer`: plugin pre-dispatch hooks, the offer to the chat's running turn, commit to the authority FIFO, detection of a retry of an already committed provider delivery id, the 503 for a parked profile, finalisation of one-shot webhook sessions and its crash recovery
- `webhook_delivery.go` — validates and snapshots a route's delivery destination (deliver type, chat and thread, GitHub repo and PR number), decodes the delivery chat id `webhook:v2:<base64url JSON of profile, route, delivery id>` and the legacy `webhook:<route>:…` spelling
- `webhook_delivery_retained.go` — reads the destination back from the admitted ingress row and re-checks it against today's route and connector before the reply is sent

#### Microsoft Graph change notifications

A second HTTP listener platform, separate from the generic webhook adapter, for Microsoft Graph subscription callbacks.

- `msgraph_webhook.go` — the `msgraph_webhook` platform: listener on port 8646 at `/msgraph/webhook` with a validation-token echo and a health route; refuses to start without `client_state` or, on a non-loopback bind, without `allowed_source_cidrs`; accepts only configured resource prefixes, dedupes by notification id (5000 remembered), answers 202, 403 or 400 per batch (503 when admission fails), and hands each notification to a plugin-installed scheduler (the Teams pipeline) or, with none installed, renders it through the `prompt` template (else fenced JSON) and commits it as an automation input under principal `msgraph:<route>`

#### Config-declared shell hooks and outbound webhooks

The only outbound-webhook code in this part is the registration call; delivery is implemented in `pkg/plugins`.

- `run_startup_config_hooks.go` — at gateway start and for each secondary profile, loads the scope's config and registers its consented shell hooks and its outbound webhook targets through `pkg/plugins`; the outbound sender itself is not in this package

#### Multi-profile serving: profile routes, shared listener and parked profiles

One multiplexer gateway on the default home can serve named profiles too. Inbound events are assigned to a profile by `profile_routes` rules; a secondary profile's HTTP adapters do not bind ports but publish their apps under `/p/<profile>/…` on the default profile's API-server or webhook listener; a profile that is temporarily unserved is "parked" and answered retryably.

- `profile_routing.go` — `profile_routes` parsing and matching: platform plus optional guild, chat (or parent chat), thread, user and bot profile, most specific rule first; WhatsApp user ids compared across number, JID and LID forms
- `parked_route_refusal.go` — refusal of events routed to a parked profile: a retryable error with headers inside an awaited ingress scope, otherwise an in-channel notice at most once per window per chat; log-and-drop for routes to profiles not served
- `shared_ingress.go` — shared-listener mode: publishes an adapter's HTTP app and callback URL, resolves the default listener base (wildcard hosts mapped to loopback), forwards `/p/<profile>/<tail>` to the first app that routes the path under that profile's runtime scope, 503 for a parked profile
- `multiplex_served.go`, `named_profile_served_export.go` — CLI-side reads of the live default gateway's record: served profiles, platforms deliberately not run for a served profile, per-profile ingress URLs, and the notify-profiles-changed control call
- `run_runtime.go` — parked-profile test against the runner's runtime descriptor
- `run_gateway_config.go` — served-profile list (boot reservation or the live profiles directory), effective `config.yaml` loader that returns an empty map on any failure, model resolution

#### Media directives and delivery path policy

Agent replies name files to attach with `MEDIA:<path>` tags and the markers `[[audio_as_voice]]` and `[[as_document]]`. Before a file leaves the host its path is validated against allowed roots and a denylist, so a prompt-injected reply cannot exfiltrate credentials.

- `media_tags.go` — the tag grammar (quotes and markdown wrappers, CJK terminators, extensionless paths validated on disk), masking of code spans and JSON strings, `ExtractMedia` returning paths with a voice flag, display stripping, the deliverable extension list
- `media_delivery.go` — `ValidateMediaDeliveryPath`: resolves symlinks, translates Docker sandbox paths to host paths through volume mounts, always allows the media cache roots, kanban attachments and operator allow-dirs, denies system prefixes, home credential directories and every profile's secret stores and databases; in strict mode only allowed roots or files produced within the trust-recent window pass
- `media_fetch.go` — filters a response's media and bare local paths per session, routes audio to the voice or audio sender per platform (Telegram: voice notes, MP3 and M4A only), copies a file out of the active remote terminal sandbox under its own denylist
- `media_policy.go` — the settings behind the policy: strict mode, allow-dirs, trust-recent
- `media_repair.go` — rewrites `MEDIA:` paths the model mistyped for computer-use captures to the canonical capture path found in this turn's tool results
- `media_cache.go` — MIME to extension tables in both directions with overrides and a mimetypes fallback
- `tui_history_export.go` — hands the Docker env and volume-mount parsers to `pkg/tuihost`

#### Inbound media notes and small per-home caches

Small JSON caches under the home, and the vision note, that adapters and the runner use to enrich inbound messages.

- `sticker_cache.go` — `<home>/sticker_cache.json`: vision descriptions of Telegram stickers by unique file id, and the text injected for static and animated stickers
- `vision_notes.go` — prepends a vision-tool description and the cached path of each inbound image to the user text, for models that cannot read images
- `rich_sent_store.go` — `<home>/state/rich_sent_index.json`: text and attachment paths by chat and message id (1000 entries, 2000 characters each) so reply-to context can be recovered on platforms that do not return it (WhatsApp Cloud, Telegram, Photon)

#### Streaming agent output to a platform message

`GatewayStreamConsumer` turns the agent's text deltas into a progressively updated chat message. It buffers deltas and flushes when the edit interval (0.8 s by default) has passed or enough text has accumulated (24 characters), with a cursor (` ▉`) until the final edit. Three transports exist: editing a sent message, draft frames through an adapter's `SendDraft` (relay, Telegram, Slack and hosted implement it; on some the draft stream is the message), and an adapter's native frame stream (WeCom). Tool boundaries and commentary start new message segments; text beyond the platform length limit seals the head and continues in a new message; think blocks, `MEDIA:` directives and trailing silence markers never reach the chat. After three consecutive flood-control failures progressive edits stop and the unseen remainder is sent once at the end.

- `stream_consumer.go` — queue, run loop, segment and turn-final bookkeeping (what was delivered, split deliveries, delivered-text checks), approval and clarify boundaries that close the stream before a prompt (the default boundary text is a hard-coded Chinese string), flush barrier, fresh final message for an old preview
- `stream_consumer_transport.go` — transport selection and the send-or-edit, draft and native paths, preview tracking and deletion, degradation from native to a buffered send, entry into fallback on edit failure
- `stream_consumer_fallback.go` — continuation of only the unseen tail after edits stop working, fence-balanced chunking, one flood retry per chunk, cursor removal, commentary sends
- `stream_consumer_think.go` — strips think blocks from deltas at block boundaries, holding partial tags until they resolve
- `stream_consumer_directives.go`, `stream_consumer_fences.go` — hides image tags delivered as attachments and holds back a pending media directive; closes or escapes code fences
- `stream_events.go` — [unwired] typed event union (`MessageChunk`, `MessageStop`, `Commentary`, `ToolCallChunk`, `ToolCallFinished`, `LongToolHint`, `GatewayNotice`) for the adapter hooks `RenderMessageEvent` and `FormatToolEvent`; nothing outside tests constructs these events or calls the hooks, so the typed per-adapter rendering path was never driven

#### Streaming text-to-speech

Speaks a reply while it is still being generated, for voice turns on adapters that accept streamed PCM.

- `streaming_tts_consumer.go` — (not in the core build tier) consumes reply deltas, splits them into clauses, synthesises PCM through the configured streaming TTS provider and writes it to the adapter while the reply is generated; tracks completed, partial and dropped so the whole-file TTS reply is suppressed only when audio was delivered
- `speech.go` — the `TTSStream` interface and the `OpenTTSStream` and `OpenLocalVoiceTurn` hooks that other tiers bind

#### Turn text shaping: silence markers, timestamps, footer, failure surface

Text rules applied to what enters the transcript and what goes out to the chat.

- `response_filters.go` — silence markers (`[SILENT]`, `SILENT`, `NO_REPLY`, `NO REPLY` and Chinese forms): exact-match detection, trailing-marker stripping, a stream hold for text that may still become a marker, the rule for when silence is allowed (machinery turns, reply not expected, opted-in rooms with a healthy result), display kinds of internal notification turns
- `message_timestamps.go` — bracketed `[Mon 2026-01-02 15:04:05 TZ]` prefixes on user content: coercion of numbers, times and ISO strings, rendering, stripping of stacked leading stamps so exactly one remains
- `runtime_footer.go` — optional footer line under the final reply (reply-footer setting with per-platform override, `display.runtime_footer.fields`): model, requested-to-served model, context percent, latency, working directory
- `turn_failure_surface.go` — stamps `failure_reason` and `failure_retryable` on a failed turn result and builds the ordered client error descriptor through a hook the binary binds

#### Pending-message spool: shutdown flush, transcript overflow and store outages

Messages that cannot reach the transcript are written as private JSON files `<home>/pending_messages/pending-<uuid>.json` (directory 0700, files 0600, atomic write plus directory fsync) and replayed at the next start.

- `shutdown_flush.go` — writers for adapters' pending slots at shutdown and for FIFO overflow tails with their arrival sequence, each with a reason label
- `shutdown_flush_recover.go` — spooling of transcript messages dropped by the in-memory cap and of agent history at teardown, and recovery: ordered replay into the owning session store for the launch home then each served profile, deletion on success, `.bad` quarantine of rows the database rejects, hold-back of a session whose earlier payload failed
- `store_outage_spool.go` — turns store-outage copies back into inbound messages of their chats in arrival order and deletes each copy once its turn settles

#### Managed worker pipe frames and stopping turns

A turn can run in a separate managed worker process (the worker entry is in `pkg/agent`) that talks to the gateway over a pipe of newline-delimited compact JSON frames capped at 4 MiB.

- `managed_worker_frames.go` — frame read and encode, the bounded scalar-only result receipt (final response, status flags, token and cost fields, billing block) and its acceptance on the owner side with usage totals
- `managed_worker_frames_tool.go` — `tool.start` and `tool.complete` frames with bounded args and result
- `run_turn_progress_tool_payloads.go` — tool lifecycle payloads every viewer reads (call id, name, bounded args, error verdict, result text) and republishing of a worker's tool frame as a session event
- `run_runtime_stop_turns.go` — cooperative stop of every turn of one authority or of all served authorities: a `stop` control frame to managed workers, a latch for workers still spawning, hard interrupt of in-process agents and side agents
- `run_runtime_managed_turns.go` — count of managed turns still outstanding

#### Kanban worker client and kanban tier hooks

A kanban worker spawned by the dispatcher is this binary run with the argv word `__icebath_kanban_worker_client__`; it submits its claim to the profile's gateway owner over the control WebSocket instead of running the agent itself. The client and probes are compiled only with the extras tier (`!icebath_core && !icebath_noextras`); `kanban_hooks.go` is always compiled and refuses kanban verbs with `tier_not_linked` in other builds.

- `kanban_worker_client.go`, `kanban_worker_client_detail.go` — reads `ICEBATH_KANBAN_BOARD`, `_TASK`, `_RUN_ID`, `_CLAIM_LOCK` and `_DB` (refusing when `ICEBATH_TUI_GATEWAY_URL` points at a remote gateway), calls `kanban.run`, polls `prompt.receipt` every 200 ms until terminal, reconnects with jittered backoff (1 to 8 s) while the owner restarts, gives up after 180 s of owner silence, prints the reply, exits with the exit code of the `worker_result` event and always writes the exit trailer
- `kanban_hooks.go` — function slots the session host fills for the `kanban.run` verb, worker binding, start-failure booking and worker-loss recording, with the refusals for a build without the tier
- `kanban_dispatch_probes.go`, `kanban_probes.go` — hand `pkg/kanban` the memory sample, pressure classifier, gateway liveness ladder, pid and start-time facts and the instantiation epoch

#### Plugin-facing services and wake turns

Entry points through which plugins and background producers reach a live session from outside a turn.

- `plugin_messages.go` — the process-wide gateway runner reference and the plugin message service: resolves a session key to a chat adapter or to a local session's viewers, posts an interim message fitted to the platform limit or edits one, sticky notices for local sessions, ownership checks so a plugin posts only into its own profile's sessions
- `plugin_adapter_lookup_install.go` — installs the profile-aware adapter lookups that `pkg/plugins` platform actions use
- `plugin_sessions_refresh.go` — hook that appends a newly live plugin's MCP tools to the open chats of a home
- `plugin_injection_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported live-session views, error-kind and callback-loop state accessors
- `wake.go` — `DeliverWake`: delivers a machine-generated turn (kanban wake, delegation result) to a session, by admission to the route FIFO or an internal event on push-capable adapters, otherwise by a chat completion self-posted to the adapter's own listener (600 s cap, retries after 2, 5 and 10 s); persists delegation delivery rows with display metadata

#### Out-of-turn sends: target parsing and transcript mirroring

Support for sends that do not answer an inbound message, such as cron deliveries and send-message tools.

- `send_message_targets.go` — parses a target reference into chat and thread ids (plugin-declared syntax first, then phone, numeric, Matrix and XMPP rules), resolves channel names through the channel directory, home-channel env overrides, unknown-platform error with an install hint
- `send_targets.go` — regex-based target parsers for platform entries and `StandaloneSendPolicy`, the rules for sending through a platform's standalone sender instead of a live adapter
- `mirror.go` — appends a delivered message (cron output, webhook delivery, CLI send) to the target chat's session transcript, finding the session by origin in `state.db` and then in the pre-migration `sessions.json`

#### `icebath peer`: talking to another gateway

A CLI client for other gateways' API servers, used to message or run a bot that lives on another gateway.

- `peer_command.go` — `icebath peer add|set|remove|list|dm|run|status|stop`: peer registry in config `bot_peers`, key from `ICEBATH_PEER_<NAME>_KEY`, requests to the peer's API server (`/health`, `/v1/capabilities`, `/api/sessions`, `/v1/runs`), DM into the peer's Bot Chat session (queued notice when that chat is open, 600 s timeout with do-not-resend guidance), runs with status and stop; urllib-shaped error types

#### Messaging platform setup wizard

Interactive configuration of chat platforms from the CLI setup flow; platform plugins reuse the standard form and the helper tables.

- `setup_wizard.go` — platform rows for the setup menu (one built-in form, Mattermost; everything else from registry entries' `setup_vars` and `setup_instructions`; Matrix hidden on Windows), configured status, the standard form (prompts, allowlist, unauthorised-DM policy, home channel), dispatch to a platform's own setup function
- `setup_platforms.go` — shared wizard helpers (prompt and save a value to its setting or the profile `.env`, allowlist and port prompts, the Telegram token and allowlist flow, webhooks setup); `SetupGateway`, the checklist-driven pass that ends by restarting or installing the service, has no caller outside tests and is [unwired], the reachable menu being `gateway_setup.go`
- `setup_wizard_modules.go` — function tables that platform wizards resolve at call time (CLI output, env file access) and a Ctrl-C watcher for polling steps
- `setup_wizard_standard_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported standard form and env reader for platform plugins

#### Self-update support

Pieces `pkg/selfupdate` needs from this package when `icebath update` pauses and restarts gateways. The update notifications sent to chats are produced in `pkg/gatewayrun`; here there is only the `UpdatePromptSender` adapter interface (in `run_notifications_export.go`) and the helper entry.

- `update_fleet_scope.go` — which homes an update owns (the invoking home, the root and its profiles) and the split of gateway pids into owned and foreign by their live environment or the spawn ledger
- `update_output.go`, `update_hangup_{unix,windows}.go` — output protection for `icebath update`: ignores SIGHUP and mirrors stdout and stderr to `<root>/logs/update.log`, continuing silently once the terminal is gone
- `slash_commands_update_helper.go` — hidden entry `gateway-update-helper <output file> <exit-code file> <cmd…>`: runs the Windows update with output captured (one-hour cap) and writes the exit code by rename
- `update_fleet_exports.go`, `update_pause_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported service helpers (unit refresh, graceful SIGUSR1 restart, wedged escalation, launchd bootstrap and kickstart, exit waits, start attestation, legacy units)
- `update_pause_probe.go` — hands the planned-stop marker TTL, staleness rule and start-time clock to the update pause record

#### Session and turn leaf helpers under `run_` names

The relation to `pkg/gatewayrun`: that package holds `GatewayRunner` and everything it does (startup, inbound handling, turns, slash commands, notifications, shutdown) as the port of `gateway/run.py` split across 250 `run_*` files, and it imports this package, never the reverse. What sits here under `run_` names is of two kinds: small functions that need unexported gateway state (this group) and export shims named after the `pkg/gatewayrun` file that needs them (last group). This package reaches back into the runner only through interfaces.

- `run_runtime_authorities.go` — per-authority helpers: owner-scoped context, serving and all authorities, admission owner of a session row, clearing crash-left turn markers whose admission recovered as unknown, rebinding queued native rows to the adapters connected now
- `run_runtime_bot_mailbox.go` — Bot Chat mailbox recovery at owner startup, skipped with a warning when the mailbox directory is unusable
- `run_session_key.go` — session key of a source from the store or built from config (group and thread sessions per user, profile namespace); parser of `agent:<namespace>:<platform>:<chat type>:<chat id>[:<thread>]` keys
- `run_cache_busting.go` — the config keys whose change invalidates a cached agent (context length, compression, disabled toolsets, memory provider, checkpoints) plus tool-registry generation and memory-provider identity
- `run_max_iterations.go` — per-turn iteration budget from the max-turns setting, reloading `.env` first outside multiplex mode
- `run_turn_runner.go` — whether an adapter renders native exec-approval buttons
- `run_turn_followup_ack.go` — fires an adapter's processing-start and processing-complete hooks for follow-up messages the runner drains itself, and classifies a cancel
- `run_housekeeping_disk_local.go` — low-disk auto-prune question published once per snooze window to a TUI or GUI local session
- `run_module_entry.go` — the `__icebath_gateway_run__` argv word and its recognition in a command line
- `runtime_readiness.go` — verdict on whether a session's provider runtime has usable credentials, naming the pinned provider and model on failure

#### Runner contracts and package seams

Glue that lets this package call the runner and lets the binary inject functions without import cycles.

- `runner_contract_{delivery,ingress,model}.go` — [port-artifact] composite interfaces listing the runner methods this package calls (adapter delivery and plugin messages; session ingress, restore and worker construction; model picks and policy)
- `run_api_active_runner.go` — [port-artifact] process-global holder of the runner whose session API is mounted
- `slash_registry_seams.go` — function slots filled by the binary's wiring: gateway command list, plugin slash commands, Discord skill commands by category, live adapters and config of a profile; slash commands themselves are handled in `pkg/gatewayrun`
- `state_mutation_routes.go` — installs into `pkg/state` the builders for the routing entry of a local reset and of a local branch
- `log.go` — the package logger

#### Export shims for `pkg/gatewayrun` and other sibling packages

[port-artifact] Exported wrappers and accessors over unexported gateway state, each file named after the consumer file it serves; they carry no behaviour of their own except where noted.

- `run_export.go` — session key generation, gateway model resolution, local policy and live-session lookups, platform section of a config, active authority, multiplex profile homes
- `run_bootstrap_export.go` — pid, pid-record and command-line helpers, child snapshot, planned-stop marker path, runtime profile homes on the config
- `run_startup_export.go` — session task done signal, loaded-entry filter, resume and active-turn timestamps, admission hold test, media directive stripping, conversation head, follow hand-off
- `run_adapters_export.go`, `run_adapters_wire_export.go` — canonical identity of a source, transport adapter pin, busy-text mode and timing, profile name of a secondary adapter, pending-message snapshot, routing home (`BusyTextPolicy` and `HumanDelayRangeMs` have no callers)
- `run_busy_export.go` — busy-accepted hook, pending-slot peek, pop and merge, id hashing and PII redaction test, bot-loop and FIFO-only flags, `AdmitMessage`, `DispatchSharedBusy`
- `run_agent_cache_export.go` — Slack tools gate, profile home for a key, active session interrupt event, pending-message set
- `run_inbound_hooks_export.go`, `run_inbound_transcription_export.go` — executing-admission test and event text replacement; pending speech-to-text clips of an event
- `run_heartbeat_acceptance_export.go`, `run_goals_export.go` — heartbeat resolution flags on an event and the DB for a key; route wake admission
- `run_notifications_export.go` — the internal-notification footer text appended to machine-generated turns, notify metadata, session key parser, committed route envelope, native event restore, completion-route restore, the `UpdatePromptSender` and `RoutingCachePrimer` interfaces
- `run_runtime_profile_export.go`, `run_runtime_settle_export.go`, `run_active_work_verb_export.go` — cron owner binding, bot receipt task cancel, retired-waiter release, API turn recovery, local adapter map, hosted service ensure; ending idle ACP sessions; unserve stop counts (`BindCronOwner` has no caller)
- `run_turn_export.go`, `run_turn_runner_export.go`, `run_turn_persistence_export.go`, `run_turn_prepare_export.go`, `run_turn_progress_export.go`, `run_turn_hygiene_export.go` — turn-path accessors: stream consumer adapter, streaming-TTS turn markers, policy scope and toolsets, terminal and unexecuted failure recording, interrupted execution, terminal sentinel trim, session peer record, auto-TTS test, deferred reset, tool payload builders, execution result, launch policy reads, store save
- `run_topics_export.go`, `run_voice_export.go` — UTF-16 bounded prefix; auto-TTS chat set and default
- `slash_commands_model_export.go`, `slash_commands_session_export.go` — model switch context reads, deferral of a local model pick, the `ChoicePickerSender` interface; retry rewrite binding, route publish, admission-open check, session DB lookup, the queue-full reply text

**Files `session_*`** (244 files, 59,176 Go lines). The 244 `session_*.go` files hold the gateway's session model. Two layers coexist: the older `SessionStore` routing index (a session key built from platform, chat, thread and user maps to the current session id, persisted in the `gateway_routing` table of `state.db` with a legacy `sessions/sessions.json` mirror) and the newer `SessionAuthority`, one per served profile, which keeps live sessions in memory, admits every input into the durable `session_admissions` FIFO and claims, executes and settles one turn at a time. Entry points are `NewSessionStore` and `InitializeSessionAuthority` (called by `pkg/gatewayrun`), `NewAuthorityConnection` and `Dispatch` (called by `pkg/tuiserver` for each `icebath-gateway-v1` WebSocket client), `AdmitNative` and the busy-ingress helpers (called by the base platform adapter), and the API, A2A, cron, kanban, bot and hosted-room admitters. On top sit the frozen launch policy of "local" sessions, managed worker child processes, session mutations, slash commands and about 120 JSON-RPC verbs. Four words recur: a local session is one a client created over the socket, a detached one is a chat conversation its chat has moved past, a managed one runs its turns in a child process, and a hosted one is a hidden per-member session of a group room. Nearly everything is implemented and wired; port scaffolding is pervasive but shallow: ordered `pyjson.Object` dicts, Python exception-class emulation (`pyKeyError`, `PyTypeName`), `pyDatetime` isoformat, generator-style `writeSteps`, runner capabilities probed through one-method interfaces named after `GatewayRunner._method`, twenty `*_export.go` shims and about twenty package-level hook variables (assigned in `cmd/icebath/wiring.go`, `pkg/tuiserver` and `pkg/cron`) that break import cycles.

#### Message source, session key and routing identity

Defines where a message came from and how that becomes a session key. `BuildSessionKey` yields `agent:<namespace>:<platform>:<chat type>[:<slack scope>][:<chat id>]` followed by thread and participant; the namespace is `agent:main` for the default profile, `agent:main~` for a profile literally named main, else `agent:<profile>`. A group chat is one shared session unless `group_sessions_per_user` is set, a thread is shared unless `thread_sessions_per_user` is set, WhatsApp aliases fold to one canonical id, and a pinned detached route wins outright.

- `session_source.go` — `SessionSource`: platform, chat id, name, type and topic, user id and name, thread, scope or guild, profile, role flag, relay flag and detached route pin, with a byte-stable wire dict
- `session_keys.go` — `BuildSessionKey`, `SessionKeyNamespace`, the shared multi-user test and WhatsApp participant canonicalisation
- `session_identity.go` — `RoutingIdentity` resolved once at ingress (transport profile, runtime profile, authorization home, runtime home under multiplexing) and the `auth:v1:` login subject encoding of socket principals
- `session_context.go` — the "Current Session Context" system prompt section: untrusted metadata quoted and capped at 240 chars, chat and sender ids hashed for PII, Slack, Discord and Matrix platform notes, home channels
- `session_export.go` — [port-artifact] re-exports `DiscordToolsLoaded` and the 240 char prompt metadata budget

#### Routing index store

`SessionStore` maps a session key to a `SessionEntry` (session id, origin source, token and cost counters, auto-reset flags, suspended, resume pending, active turn marker, model override, prompt pin, yolo). Entries load from the `gateway_routing` table with `sessions.json` filling gaps; `GetOrCreateSession` single-flights lookup, recovery of a vacant key from a durable `sessions` row, and creation of a fresh row. Only `suspended` causes an auto reset here: the `idle` and `daily` reset reasons still listed in `pkg/state` are never raised by this store. Under multiplexing each key resolves to its owning profile's `state.db`.

- `session.go` — `SessionEntry`, `SessionStore`, the get-or-create routing transition, reset, switch and remove, profile rekey and purge, model override, yolo and metadata setters, listing and lookup, Slack and Discord continuity note
- `session_persistence.go` — DB handle per key and profile, routing load and save (single-entry upsert or generation-stamped whole rewrite), `sessions.json` import and 0600 mirror, startup prune of ended rows, retired-route fences, chat label meta
- `session_persistence_export.go`, `session_routing_export.go` — [port-artifact] expose the store's active `DB` and its `RoutingDB` to other packages
- `session_lifecycle.go` — session id minting, ended-row checks, crash-safe active turn markers promoted to resume pending at boot, `PruneOldEntries` by idle days; `pyDatetime` isoformat; `SuspendSession` has no caller (shutdown sets the flag directly)
- `session_recovery.go` — key generation with profile namespace, recovery of a vacant key (peer tuple fallback, Slack workspace scope check, one-time legacy Slack key adoption), reset promotion, session row creation with its routing peer
- `session_prompt_pin.go` — versioned durable snapshot of the ephemeral prompt inputs pinned on a route, written and read only while the route still names the expected session
- `session_db_recovery.go` — `RecoverableHandleCache`: single-flight DB opens per path with 1 to 60 second retry backoff and an aggregate store-health publication to runtime status
- `session_local_recovery.go` — binds a local authority's runtime epoch to the store so a local route resets onto a fresh child only through its owner's epoch-fenced reset

#### Transcript appends, outage spool and rewind

Transcript writes of the routing store, used by the runner's turn code. A store failure never drops a row: rows queue in memory, overflow to an on-disk spool and replay in order once the store heals.

- `session_transcript.go` — appends through compression reroutes; queues 200 rows per session, spools overflow, escalates after 3 failures, rebuilds FTS at most every 300 s; also rewrite, rewind by user turn, platform message id and tail-role probes

#### Session authority core and wire contract

`SessionAuthority` owns the live sessions of one profile store: `LiveSession` objects (source, route, event stream, subscribers, drain state), the runtime epoch taken from `state.db` at start, and several dozen per-session latch maps. `Authorize` is the central permission check and lazily restores a stored session into memory as a local session, a routed messaging lane, a read-only history mount or an API session.

- `session_contract.go` — wire vocabulary: subprotocol `icebath-gateway-v1`, execution states, intents (queue, steer, redirect), admission statuses (queued, started, unknown, terminal), `Principal`, `SessionRef`, `SessionHandle`, `AdmissionReceipt`, `SubscriptionSnapshot`
- `session_authority.go` — `LiveSession` and `SessionAuthority`, `Authorize`, the admission gate (refuses `runtime_draining`), logical owner (compression root) and physical target (compression tip), drain scheduling, `session.info` pending publish, receipts, queued cancel, 30 s re-retire timer
- `session_authority_init.go` — boot of one authority: begin runtime epoch, recover inputs, settle unattended unknown turns, backfill legacy owner and compression source stamps, bind the cron owner, restore local sessions, re-arm login waits
- `session_authority_turns.go` — FIFO `asyncLock` whose waiters leave on cancellation, and `keyedTurn`, one ordered critical section per route
- `session_events.go` — `SessionEvents`: per-session stream over the TUI host's bounded fan-out and shared replay cache, frames stamped with epoch and sequence, catch-up, `Since` replay, synchronous observers
- `session_schedule_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] swap hook for the drain scheduler, referenced only by tests

#### Served-profile authority registry and runtime scope

One gateway process can serve several profile homes; each gets its own authority, and every owner-side read runs under that profile's home, secrets and terminal policy.

- `session_authorities_registry.go` — `SessionAuthorities`: authorities keyed by profile home, the launch slot, reserved "starting" slots with wait channels, serving and active lookups, the multiplexed flag
- `session_authorities.go` — `requireServing` (refuses `runtime_retired`), `ownerScope` and `ProfileRuntimeScope` binding home override, secret scope and terminal scope of one profile
- `session_authorities_serving.go` — authorities that currently accept work, the single launch authority of a runner without a registry
- `session_authorities_profile_id.go`, `session_authority_export.go`, `session_authorities_registry_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported lookups of an authority by profile home and an alias of the registry runner interface

#### Admission of inputs into the FIFO

Every input becomes one row of the `session_admissions` ledger keyed by principal, session and request id, so a redelivery is idempotent. Messaging inputs are committed in arrival order per route under principal `messaging:<profile,platform,chat,thread,user>` with the platform message id as request id (plus `:edit:<revision>`); viewer inputs accept only intent `queue` and a closed set of payload fields. Per-turn fields are validated at admission, stored in the payload and rebound as context scopes when the turn executes.

- `session_authority_admission.go` — `Register` (route reservation and lane naming), `AdmitNative` with stop and new-session route fences, `AdmitAutomation`, `Submit`, recovery of native sessions after restart, release of captured media on refusal
- `session_finite.go` — `finite` and `unattended` flags (unattended only for the local CLI owner on its own CLI session); binds every per-turn scope and starts execution
- `session_finite_child_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the headless clarify reply of a finite turn for the worker child; `FiniteTurnScope` has no caller
- `session_surface.go`, `session_surface_restore.go`, `session_surface_turn.go` — `surface` (`hud` or `voice-live`), `voice_context` capped at 6000 chars, `interrupted` and `voice_turn` flags, revalidated when crossing into a worker
- `session_display.go` — `display_kind` (only `hidden`) and `title_preview` (1000 chars) committed as `display_v1`, plus the client submission id bound to the executing admission
- `session_cli_turn.go` — one-shot CLI fields `turn_author`, `api_text`, `model_override` and `clarify_batch` committed as `cli_turn_v1`
- `session_turn_scopes.go` — context scopes carrying the committed surface and CLI turn fields, and rebinding of reference-expanded API text
- `session_operator.go` — `local_operator_v1` envelope marking an operator's input on another owner's session, re-checked at claim; test for viewer-typed rows
- `session_retry_admission.go` — a retry's transcript rewrite applied inside the admission transaction of its re-sent message, both refused together

#### FIFO drain: claim, execute, settle

One goroutine per live session claims the queued head, executes it and settles it. Before a claim it applies deferred model and reasoning picks, re-validates the row against its route (hosted membership, automation ownership, native route, API binding) and reopens a finalized row. Execution dispatches to a cron job, a managed worker or the runner's in-process turn handler. A settlement that cannot commit marks the row `unknown`, which pauses the FIFO until someone resolves it; unattended unknown rows settle themselves.

- `session_authority_drain.go` — claim with 0.25 to 5 s storage backoff, classic-turn hold, `session_busy` pause, store-outage notice and input spool, execute, settle, deferred auto reset, reply delivery, 60 s crash-marker release wait
- `session_ingress_execute.go` — rebuilds the event from the committed payload, restores provenance, binds author, viewer and API scopes, calls the runner's `HandleMessage`, records result, usage and the owed reply
- `session_results.go`, `session_results_settle.go` — captured execution result, redaction at the storage boundary, terminal commit with steer transfers, failure records for turns that never ran
- `session_settlement_recovery.go` — settlement retry (0.5 s then 2 s), the `unknown` fence, `message.complete` payload, restart and shutdown interruption notices, media release after settlement
- `session_settlement_recovery_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exports `PublishCompletion`, referenced only by tests
- `session_unattended_unknown.go` — classes cron, automation, kanban and webhook rows as unattended and settles their unknown turns at boot or at the head with an "interrupted, not run again" notice
- `session_completion_notes.go` — a background completion with no viewer attached (a cron result always) is appended to history as a note instead of running a model turn

#### Live turn controls: attach, stop, steer, approvals, clarify, queued rows

Everything a viewer can do to a running or queued turn. Controls are bound to the execution generation, so a late answer to an earlier turn is refused as stale.

- `session_authority_controls.go` — attach and detach with replay cursor and snapshot, interrupt (latched until the turn adopts an agent), steer, agent adoption, approval and clarify registration and response, resolve-unknown
- `session_authority_stops_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exposes the latched stops map, referenced only by tests
- `session_busy_adopt.go` — whether a claimed turn runs an in-process agent that latched steers can reach (false for cron sessions and managed workers)
- `session_busy_correct.go` — [partial] `session.steer` and `session.redirect` reach in-process agents only, managed workers refusing both as `unsupported_control`; replay-safe typed voice stop phrases (newest 256 remembered)
- `session_pending_controls.go` — projection of blocking approval and clarify prompts onto the event stream, credential redaction of approval commands, remote responders
- `session_server_requests.go` — owner-to-viewer requests (`srq-` ids) with a 120 s timeout, clarify batch answer locking, cancel publication
- `session_clarify_lock.go` — `clarify.lock` verb locking one answer of an open clarify batch
- `session_queued_controls.go` — `prompt.replace_queued`, which queued rows are editable (plain text on interactive sources), transfer of queued rows as steers to the running claim

#### Platform ingress: busy input, bursts and reply delivery

Glue between platform adapters (several functions here are methods on the base adapter) and the authority. A non-command message arriving while its session is busy is dispatched as a tracked background admission that returns to the adapter once queued, or once committed for a durable input, while an observer later delivers the reply; same-sender photo bursts and queue-mode text are merged inside a debounce window first. Producer deliveries (webhook-style ingress) are instead offered to the chat's in-flight work (a pending prompt, a plaintext approval, the busy interrupt or steer mode) before anything is committed.

- `session_ingress.go` — busy futures, `dispatchSharedBusy`, final reply delivery with attachments, turn-marker handoff, hold-until-commit for serial readers
- `session_ingress_burst.go` — burst merging by kind (photo or text), hold timer, flush and commit ordering, the gate that makes a serial reader's command wait for earlier commits
- `session_ingress_admission.go` — admits a message and waits for its turn's reply; chat notices for a full queue or refused content; settled delivery registry and post-delivery callbacks
- `session_ingress_live_turn.go` — offers a producer delivery to the chat's running turn or pending prompt, and remembers consumed message ids so a provider re-send is not admitted
- `session_producer_lifecycle.go` — typing indicator and processing start and complete hooks around producer-admitted turns; reflection test of whether an adapter overrides a base hook
- `session_stall.go` — stall rule: one "I seem to be stuck" notice once a session with pending inbound is idle past the timeout, cleared on progress

#### Native envelope and connector provenance

What gets written to the ledger for a chat message and how its origin is proven again at claim time, so a queued row cannot run under a connector, profile or sender it was not received from.

- `session_envelope.go` — `native_text_v1` payload: sender, authorization, media and auto-skill validation, WhatsApp native metadata capped at 16 KiB, restore of event and source, preflight of queued native rows
- `session_ingress_context.go` — native and relay callback bindings, transport home registry, provenance (transport home, runtime home, platform, connector fingerprint, relay HMAC seal), role re-authorization, legacy fingerprint match

#### Ingress media capture, retention and release

Inbound files are copied into a content-addressed store under the profile's document cache (`native-inputs/<sha256>/`), leased while an admission is in flight, referenced by digest in the committed payload and deleted once no retained admission or transcript mentions them.

- `session_ingress_media_capture.go` — capture leases, attachments (at most 10; png, jpeg, gif, webp by sniffed bytes), ingress fingerprint for redelivery reconciliation, bounded copy under the inbound media byte limit, verified restore
- `session_ingress_media.go` — retained store paths, hosted document references in prompts, computation of still-held media, unlink of unleased files
- `session_ingress_media_release.go` — release at terminal settlement, hourly sweep of settled media per store, collection of API images no admission holds
- `session_ingress_media_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS hard link count of a path without following a final link (2 variants)
- `session_ingress_media_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the attachment limit, image extensions and mime sniffing; `BypassLaunchPolicy` has no caller
- `session_images.go` — `image.attach_bytes` verb: decodes, sniffs and stages an uploaded image in the owner profile's image cache

#### Context reference expansion

Expands `@file` style references in a turn's text inside the session workspace before the model sees it; a refused injection ends the turn with the refusal as its result.

- `session_context_refs.go` — expansion with the model's context length, refused-reference and vanished-workspace results, text expansion for a managed worker turn
- `session_context_refs_turn.go` — inbound-turn wrappers the runner calls, choosing the local policy cwd before the terminal cwd

#### Automation producers: process notices, heartbeat ticks, route wakes

Inputs no person typed (background process completions, watch matches, liveness ticks, loop ticks, kanban wakes, cron deliveries, plugin injections) enter the same FIFO with an automation descriptor carrying a producer identity for dedupe. A messaging route's wake borrows the connector provenance of the last human message committed on that route, so nothing can wake a chat no person has spoken in.

- `session_automation.go` — descriptor and metadata whitelist, owner checks, snapshot bound to the route's last committed envelope, `admitAutomation`, `admitRouteWake`, result card text capped at 2000 chars
- `session_automation_ticks.go` — a heartbeat tick replaces its queued predecessor, completions fold into one batch at the FIFO tail, a finished process withdraws its ticks; watch notification text
- `session_automation_routes.go` — after a route rotates: moves queued kanban-wake and loop-tick rows, resets a local route keeping its owner, compression-exhaustion reset that re-homes queued messaging rows
- `session_automation_restore.go` — read-only preflight and event rebuild of a committed local automation row
- `session_viewer_automation.go`, `session_viewer_automation_verb.go` — `session.automation` verb running goal, loop and heartbeat manager calls on the owner, and the record of which attached viewer drives them

#### Detached conversations and route mounting

When a chat starts or resumes another conversation, the previous one may still have a running turn, queued input or background results. It is detached onto its own key `agent:<namespace>:detached:<session id>` and keeps draining there without being the chat's current conversation.

- `session_detached.go` — detached key format and parsing, the synthetic never-stored routing entry at the compression tip
- `session_detached_lanes.go` — running key of a turn, the authority owning a route, the route-announcement watcher that names lanes
- `session_detached_follow.go` — boot recovery of queued input on detached conversations, moving background results onto and off detached keys
- `session_detached_route.go` — live conversation and routing entry behind a detached key
- `session_detached_export.go` — [port-artifact] `SessionEnvSource`, the source a detached turn's session variables name
- `session_route_mount.go` — restores a messaging lane from its row after a restart, detaches superseded conversations, follows a handoff onto a messaging lane
- `session_route_recovery.go` — which source labels name messaging platforms, and a `SessionSource` rebuilt from a session row

#### Local sessions: creation, adapter and limits

A local session is a conversation a client creates over the socket instead of a chat platform delivering it. Its id is `local-` plus the sha256 of profile, principal and request id, so a retried create answers with the same session. A "local receipt" in `state_meta` stores route, routing entry and frozen policy; the source is a `local` platform DM whose chat id is the session id and whose user id is the creating principal, and replies stay in the event stream.

- `session_local.go` — `LocalSessionAdapter`: no-op send, edit and typing, source registration with identity pinning, frozen policy per chat, clarify declined when nobody can answer it
- `session_local_create.go` — staging: capability check, bypass or profile policy, launch route resolution, exact-retry check with constant-time key compare, launch key binding, receipt build, project-plugin warning
- `session_local_commit.go` — commits a staged receipt (row, route and immutable policy together) at the authority epoch
- `session_local_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports `SessionPolicyForSource`; `CreateLocalSession` has no caller
- `session_local_title.go`, `session_local_title_resolve.go` — title validation and uniqueness at create, resolution of a session by id or title, latest session of a surface family with its workspace first
- `session_local_route.go`, `session_local_route_export.go` — decodes an explicit launch model into provider and base URL the way every startup path does
- `session_local_follow.go` — makes a Bot Chat an earlier build froze follow its profile config
- `session_limits.go` — `sessions.max_live_per_connection` and `sessions.max_live_per_profile` refusals (wire code 4019) naming the oldest idle session to close
- `session_worker_prefill.go` — prefill example messages read from the profile config at creation and published by the creating commit

#### Local session restore, history and legacy adoption

Brings stored conversations back into memory and builds what a resuming viewer sees.

- `session_local_restore.go` — receipt validation (owner, route, lineage, policy), compression catch-up and remount; carries Python-traceback-style check location tagging
- `session_local_history.go`, `session_local_history_export.go` — resume history over the compression lineage with archived rows trimmed to 3 MiB, reopen of an ended row, boot recovery of every receipt, release of handed-off receipts
- `session_local_adoption.go` — commits a receipt's compression catch-up off the owner loop before a restore reads it
- `session_local_migration.go`, `session_local_migration_adopts.go` — adopts pre-authority CLI and TUI rows and phone-app history as local sessions, rebuilding launch params from the saved route; refused while another process is live
- `session_history_mount.go` — read-only mount of a stored non-local session for its reader, refusing every non-read verb and deletion of a non-leaf
- `session_controls_transcript.go` — transcript fields of a resume reply: display projection, model-only row filter, reasoning stripping, omitted-count mode
- `session_todo_state.go` — todo list snapshot rebuilt from persisted todo tool results for a cold resume

#### Session info, inventory and listings

Read models for pickers, status bars and banners.

- `session_local_info.go` — `session.info` fields: source, cwd, model, lazy route, reasoning effort, service tier, title, yolo, tool count, masked credential hint
- `session_local_inventory.go` — banner inventory: tools by toolset, skills, MCP server status, project, unknown toolsets, release date, update-behind count, tool availability warnings
- `session_messaging_route.go` — model and effort a messaging chat's next turn resolves, session override over channel over config
- `session_listing.go` — stored picker rows (legacy local and mountable messaging sessions) offered only to the native transport that may resume them
- `session_live_listing.go` — live sessions an actor may read with handle, pending rows and execution state; internal sources hidden (kanban, tool, oneshot)
- `session_active_list.go` — `session.active_list` verb: waiting, working, starting or idle per live session
- `session_local_close_unviewed.go` — verdict that a live row is closed, idle and unviewed, so it lists as resumable

#### ACP editor integration

`pkg/acp` is a socket client that creates sessions with source `acp`. Such a launch may pass an `editor` policy: MCP servers the editor offers and an edit approval policy (`ask`, `workspace_session` or `session`, changed later by the `edit_policy` mutation). The authority holds those connections per session, freezes their tool manifest into the policy, routes file edits to the editor for approval and ends the session when the editor disconnects.

- `session_local_editor.go` — accepts `editor` only from source `acp`, with keys `mcp_servers` and `edit_approval_policy` (`ask` at launch)
- `session_local_mcp.go` — server list validation reproducing pydantic error shapes of the ACP models, sorted-JSON fingerprint, private mutation payload
- `session_local_mcp_bind.go` — binds editor servers into a new policy and borrows them for the authority
- `session_local_mcp_held.go` — held connections per session scope, borrow and release around executions, kept between turns only while viewed, tools-changed announcement
- `session_local_mcp_refreeze.go` — probes borrowed servers before a claim and refreezes a drifted manifest as an `editor_mcp` mutation
- `session_acp_lifecycle.go` — ends an idle ACP session with `acp_disconnect` when its last viewer leaves, reopens on reattach, ends all unviewed ones at shutdown

#### Launch policy: frozen per-session configuration

`LocalSessionPolicy` freezes at creation: source label, platform surface, cwd, model, toolsets, a copy of the profile config with secrets stripped, the create request, terminal policy, editor MCP manifest, kanban context, safe-mode flags, rendered skills prompt and client env. A session keeps the frozen config or, with `follow_profile_config`, re-reads model, providers, fallbacks, toolsets and selected agent keys each turn. Source labels map to agent surfaces (cli, tui, acp; gui runs on tui; tool, oneshot and any free tag of up to 64 characters run on cli), and `a2a`, `cron`, `kanban` and `bot_room` are reserved for sessions icebath files itself.

- `session_policy.go` — the policy struct, surface and label tables, session pins, effective next-turn config and model, stored-policy restore, client env scope, config secret extraction
- `session_policy_build.go` — builds a policy from create params: closed field set, cwd checks, toolset resolution, coding-workspace posture, launch skills, run budget
- `session_policy_build_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exports `BuildPolicy` and `BindLaunchKey`, referenced only by tests
- `session_policy_current.go` — next-turn reasoning and service tier: typed session override, then profile when following, then frozen value
- `session_policy_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported effective-config and route launch key reads, with an ownerless stand-in
- `session_policy_scope.go` — runs a body under the policy's workspace, terminal policy, profile read, editor edit approval and client env; refuses `workspace_unavailable`
- `session_policy_workspace.go` — registers the frozen workspace as the docker terminal cwd of a turn
- `session_policy_resume.go` — shell hook consent for an accept-hooks launch, hook refresh on open, re-supply of a launch-only key after an owner restart
- `session_policy_refresh.go` — refreshes config-derived fields and MCP servers of an idle session from the live profile on resume, committed as a tracked task
- `session_route_identity.go` — canonical provider identity and effective base URL of a model block, used to tell whether a route changed

#### Launch secrets

Secrets never land in the stored policy. A launch-only API key lives in an in-memory slot for the authority's lifetime and the policy keeps a reference with a fingerprint; config secrets are stripped to `None` and recovered from the profile through a `profile-config-v1:` reference.

- `session_policy_credentials.go` — secret paths, slots, recovery of referenced config secrets with drift detection, endpoint and owner binding checks; `pathAt` is dead
- `session_policy_launch_key.go` — binds a launch key and frozen config secrets in memory, refusing a different key for the same slot as `admission_conflict`

#### Session mutations and deferred picks

`session.mutate` carries every durable change to a session: rename, archive, sidebar, delete, import, branch, rewind, reset, compress, model, reasoning, workspace, editor_mcp, edit_policy and launch. Each is fenced on the expected revision (and generation for policy operations), idempotent by request id through a stored receipt, prepared off the commit and projected to runtime afterwards. A model or reasoning pick refused only because a turn is running is deferred and committed at the next claim boundary.

- `session_mutations.go` — writer phase: fenced prepare, receipt commit under the commit lock, projections, owner-built fenced params
- `session_mutations_control.go` — authorization per operation (control, import, cold-history claim), owner resolution, model and reasoning picks on messaging chats applied as chat overrides
- `session_mutation_model.go` — freezes a model pick: provider resolution, alias credentials, reset to the profile default, large-context confirmation guard
- `session_mutation_model_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the policy's stored dict; `PrepareModel` has no caller
- `session_mutation_policy.go` — prepare steps for reasoning, workspace move, ACP edit policy and relaunch flags (a newly set bypass rebuilds the policy from code defaults)
- `session_mutation_compress.go` — compress: summarises off the commit through the `SessionCompress` hook, preview and noop reports, engine notification, post-compaction plugin hook
- `session_mutation_project.go` — runtime projections of a committed receipt: policy republish, agent eviction, terminal environment drop, boundary transcript restore
- `session_mutation_retire.go` — after delete: release of launch secrets, editor servers and workspaces, drop of live sessions, routing fences in the shared index
- `session_deferred_pick.go`, `session_deferred_reask.go` — deferred pick receipts in `state_meta`, commit at the claim boundary, re-ask of a guarded pick when a viewer attaches
- `session_setting_commands.go` — typed reasoning and model commands on a local session routed through the fenced mutation, one-turn model switch restored after its turn
- `session_setting_commands_export.go` — exported live-session lookup and busy mode precedence: session pin, policy `display.busy_input_mode`, then the runner's
- `session_prune.go` — `session.prune` verb: owner-run bulk delete by validated filters for the local operator, retiring matching live sessions
- `session_usage_compression.go` — carries the conversation's compaction count across agent eviction

#### Managed worker processes: owner side

A managed session runs each turn in a child process: the gateway re-executes its own binary with the hidden argument `__icebath_managed_worker__` and talks JSON frames over pipes. Bypass launches (`safe_mode`, `ignore_user_config`) and kanban sessions are always managed; others only when `gateway.managed_workers` is true, and then only on the CLI surface with a custom provider and base URL (`unsupported_managed_policy` otherwise). A lost worker settles the turn as `unknown` and pauses the FIFO.

- `session_managed_policy.go` — decides whether a session executes out of process
- `session_managed_worker.go` — bootstrap frame, child env, spawn and registration, supervision loop (hello 60 s, stop ack 30 s), prompt frame projection, result acceptance, loss handling, child-side `WorkerTurnScope`
- `session_managed_worker_handle.go` — owner handle: control writer, demand-driven frame reader, stop latch with cause, interrupt, verified pid and kernel birth, close
- `session_managed_worker_process.go` — spawn with stdin, stdout and optional stderr pipes, background reap, the latch proving the binary dispatches the worker entry
- `session_managed_worker_signal_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS termination: own process group on unix, handle kill on windows (2 variants)
- `session_managed_worker_log.go` — stderr drained to `<profile>/logs/managed-worker.log`, secrets redacted, 1 MiB rotation, lines cut to 4096 chars
- `session_managed_worker_errors.go` — `ManagedExecutionUnknown`, the error that stops the FIFO without forging a failed settlement
- `session_worker_spawn.go` — spawn off the owner goroutine, closing the child when the acquisition is cancelled
- `session_worker_reservation.go` — verifies the child's pid, birth and parent chain (3 launcher hops), reserves the started admission with a random secret, revokes a lost worker
- `session_worker_construct.go` — agent construction inputs resolved per turn: fallback chain, ephemeral channel prompt plus skills blocks, provider routing

#### Managed worker child helpers

Functions `pkg/agent` calls inside the worker child to rebuild the turn from its bootstrap frame.

- `session_policy_worker.go` — restores the frozen policy, runs under it with no owner authority, restores attachments, registers shell hooks and webhooks
- `session_worker_frame.go` — kanban context of a frame and the workspace scope with session variables bound
- `session_worker_construct_child.go` — validated construct inputs, route overrides (key, base URL, API mode), checkpoint and provider-routing agent arguments
- `session_worker_construct_route.go` — resolves a launch policy route on the frozen config and launch key, walking its own fallback chain
- `session_tool_events.go` — bounds tool arguments and results published to viewers to 64 KiB while keeping them valid JSON

#### Worker execution ledger and delegation

Verbs a worker process uses to prove itself and write through the owner. A worker presents a claim whose digest must match the stored adoption digest; every write is fenced on epoch, generation and sequence.

- `session_worker.go` — `worker.register` (kind `compute` only), `worker.adopt`, `worker.persist`; claim verification; wakes the FIFO on `execution.finish`
- `session_worker_delegation.go` — `delegation.*` persist operations (dispatch, child, read, claim, complete, unscheduled, delivery updates); dispatch only from cli, tui, gui, tool and oneshot sessions
- `session_worker_child.go` — `child.reserve`: reserves a delegated child session and execution under the caps `delegation.max_concurrent_children` and `delegation.max_spawn_depth`

#### Owner work tracking, stop and join

Lets shutdown and profile retirement see and wait for every piece of in-flight work.

- `session_runtime_workers.go` — tracked tasks for mutations and ledger writes, ordered writes off the owner loop, republication of the in-flight count
- `session_runtime_workers_join.go` — turn worker registration, `StopAuthorityWork` (interrupts turns, side agents, cron runs), `JoinAuthorityWork` with timeout
- `session_runtime_workers_uncounted.go` — executing sessions, side agents and pre-bootstrap managed turns that the ordinary agent map does not count

#### Retirement, viewer close and orphan reaping

Idle local and API sessions leave memory and return from their receipts on demand. When the last viewer leaves with an end reason the session is closed at the next idle point: memory commit, finalize hooks and, for `new_session` or `tui_close`, a reset. A session abandoned without a reason is closed after `sessions.orphan_end_grace_s` (older opt-outs `sessions.ws_orphan_reap_grace_s` and `sessions.startup_orphan_sweep` still honoured); ACP sessions are exempt.

- `session_retirement.go` — pin test (viewers, running work, pending closes, reviews), retire at the drain's idle exit, restore of a retired session from its receipt, re-retire when nobody watches, forget of a deleted one
- `session_viewer_close.go` — pending close persisted in `state_meta`, settlement at idle, orphan timers at detach and startup (6 h legacy idle rule), abandoned unknown turns resolved, close lifecycle
- `session_viewer_close_reads.go` — physical transcript a close acts on and the busy test over unsettled admissions and live worker executions
- `session_review_cancel.go` — cancels a background refine review sharing the session before a new turn runs
- `session_refine_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the transcript target, retire-after-review and current toolsets for the review code
- `session_vault_release.go` — on close, locks password manager sessions the conversation unlocked, through a hook the binary assigns

#### Client connection and verb dispatch

`AuthorityConnection` is one authenticated socket projected onto an authority. Default capabilities are read, submit, control, approve and respond, plus create when an identity is present; an identity may instead carry an explicit capability list, and operator is granted only by the transport gate. A connection with no user id or a foreign instance id holds none. A local session is usable only by its owner unless the caller is an operator. `Dispatch` answers JSON-RPC frames: refusals are code 4001 with a reason, unknown methods -32601, storage failures 5001, and a host-scoped connection routes a `profile` param to a sibling authority.

- `session_controls.go` — the connection type, capability derivation, sibling routing across served profiles, refusal data and log levels, native transport binding
- `session_controls_dispatch.go` — the verb table and `Dispatch`: typed param fitting, draining refusal for operators, service-verb fallthrough, error mapping
- `session_controls_handlers.go` — settles an owner request from a viewer's response frame; Python-style dict read helper
- `session_controls_lifecycle.go` — `session.create` (titled create, hidden flag, Bot Chat rule), `session.info`, `session.revision`, `session.resume` (target resolution, editor and key rebind, snapshot), `prompt.submit`, `session.mutate`
- `session_controls_verbs.go` — `session.detach`, `prompt.receipt`, `prompt.cancel`, `prompt.resolve_unknown`, `session.interrupt`, `approval.respond`, `clarify.respond`, `session.list`, `runtime.describe`, `ping`, connection close
- `session_controls_delegates.go` — thin verbs forwarding to cron, bot relay and worker operations
- `session_controls_sqlite.go` — classifies sqlite errors for the storage-failure log
- `session_service_verbs.go` — fallthrough to a service verb table installed by `pkg/tuiserver`, requiring every interactive capability
- `session_listener_boundary.go` — WebSocket handshake checks: Host header against the bound interface (DNS rebinding defence), loopback peer on loopback binds, ticket from the subprotocol list

#### Slash commands on local sessions

Runs registry slash commands for a socket client by classifying each as read, control or refused, then driving the messaging gateway's own command handlers with output captured instead of sent. Commands the service cannot run are refused with a plain hint naming where to do it instead.

- `session_commands.go` — the set of registry commands whose read handlers the owner runs
- `session_commands_exec.go` — `slash.exec`, `command.dispatch` and `command.observe`: verdict tables, owner-only commands, quick commands, skill and prompt directives, plugin toggles, refusal hints, pre-command queue (32)
- `session_command_sink.go` — context sink capturing what a messaging command handler would have sent
- `session_commands_workspace.go` — binds a command to the session's frozen terminal policy and launch cwd
- `session_commands_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports stored id, context id, model history and display projection to `pkg/tuiserver`
- `session_info_reads.go` — toolsets, platforms, cron and TUI status or context reports rendered in the owning profile through assigned hooks
- `session_discovery.go` — `commands.catalog`, `complete.slash` and `plugins.list` verbs
- `session_complete_path.go` — `complete.path` verb: path and context-ref completions in the host folder or the session's sandbox

#### Settings and preference verbs

Reads and writes of settings on behalf of a viewer, always in the owning profile's scope, with session-scoped values layered over profile values.

- `session_config.go` — `config.get` (session controls, full client config, config mtime and MCP revision, reasoning, fast, skin, theme, approvals mode, project, voice) and `model.options`
- `session_tui_config.go` — `config.set`, `settings.groups`, `settings.list`, `settings.set`, `settings.reset`: fast tier, personality, approval mode, display language, skin broadcast to viewers
- `session_busy_controls.go` — session-scoped `busy`, `verbose`, `show_reasoning`, `service_tier` and `yolo` controls and their capability checks; model writes redirected to the mutation
- `session_config_local_voice.go`, `session_config_voice.go` — voice mode of a local session, its viewer transports, and the hook that stops push-to-talk capture when voice turns off
- `session_skin.go` — resolved skin payload of the profile for `runtime.describe`
- `session_readiness.go` — `setup.status` (whether the profile has any provider configured) and the `setup.runtime_check` probe of one provider, failures reported in the answer; both need the create capability

#### Transcript operations: save, export, rollback, shell, side prompts, handoff

Viewer actions on a session's content.

- `session_tui_ops.go` — `session.save` (json under `sessions/saved`), `session.export` (json, md, html, optional redaction), `session.history`, `reload.env`, `delegation.pause`, `rollback.*` over checkpoints, rewind of the last turn
