- `session_tui_undo_hint.go` — start time of an undone span and the hint naming files it changed
- `session_shell.go` — `shell.exec`: one captured command in the frozen cwd for local terminal backends only, dangerous commands refused, line kept beside the transcript
- `session_tui_side.go` — `prompt.background` (a fresh agent runs a prompt to completion on the session's route) and `prompt.btw` (a side question over a conversation snapshot, live history and FIFO untouched)

- `session_handoff_verbs.go` — `handoff.request`, `handoff.state`, `handoff.fail`: queues an idle session for a platform's home channel for the handoff watcher

#### Usage, context breakdown and account limits

Token, cost and context figures a viewer's status bar and usage commands read. The agent-side computations are hooks (`ContextAgent`) assigned in wiring; this group shapes and serves them.

- `session_usage_stats.go` — `session.stats` verb and cumulative counters of a session row, from the live agent once it has called the model
- `session_usage_tui.go` — the status bar usage shape with whole-percent rounding
- `session_usage_frame.go` — session usage event payload combining the TUI view and cumulative counters
- `session_tui_reads.go` — `session.context_breakdown`: category breakdown and context file manifest, cached per agent and transcript revision, stored pin for cold sessions
- `session_tui_account_usage.go` — `session.account_usage`: provider account limit lines for the route a session runs

#### Ancillary projections: processes, subagents, tools, MCP reload, control card

[partial] Per-session views of what the agent has running, and switches for its tools. They read the in-process agent, so control, process and subagent projections are refused as `unsupported_projection` for managed-worker sessions.

- `session_ancillary.go` — `process.list`, `process.stop`, `process.kill`, `subagent.list`, `subagent.tail`, `subagent.steer`, `subagent.interrupt`, `reload.mcp`, `skills.reload`, `tools.show`, `session.control.read`
- `session_ancillary_attach.go` — handler table of the ancillary verbs
- `session_ancillary_target.go` — current physical session of a conversation
- `session_ancillary_tools.go` — `tools.configure`: enables or disables toolsets and MCP tools in the profile and commits the selection into the calling session
- `session_control_actions.go` — publishes `session.control.update` (goal, loop, heartbeat cards) to viewers with ticket ordering so a stale snapshot never paints over a newer one

#### Logins and connector cards

Socket verbs over provider logins and platform connector setup; the shared login code lives in `pkg/tuihost` and runs here in the owning profile's scope.

- `session_logins.go` — `login.*` verbs (list, add key, OAuth start and poll, link, rename, remove, default, rotation, convert), `session.set_login`, `session.login_wait`, retry of the last turn, login inheritance
- `session_connections.go` — connector card verbs `connection.respond`, `connectors.connect`, `connectors.operation.status`, `connectors.operation.wake`, with retry under the session's own context

#### API server sessions

How OpenAI-compatible HTTP requests become session turns; called by `pkg/gatewayapi`. A request binds to a session (declared conversation key, header-less implicit generation, or a hosted room member), is admitted as an `api_turn_v1` payload under principal `api`, and runs through the same FIFO with observers streaming deltas and tool events back to the HTTP handler.

- `session_api.go` — API session identity: declared key registry, implicit generations (`api-<16 hex>`), hosted member ids (`room_<32 hex>`), stored creation label
- `session_api_binding.go` — binding as generator-style write steps, heal of a replaced binding, reopen and restore of an API session
- `session_api_turn_admit.go` — admission of an API turn: parked-profile and scope checks, settings capture, media capture around the write, run ownership, control observation; the inline `AdmitAPITurn` variant has no caller
- `session_api_turn.go` — envelope validation, saved API settings in `state_meta`, execution preparation, per-request observer sinks, "input saved, do not resend" error for a queued admission at restart
- `session_api_turn_recover.go` — at startup reschedules queued API sessions, collects unheld images and compacts settled payloads
- `session_api_media.go` — replaces inline base64 images in settled payloads with `icebath-retained:` digest references (older `hermes-retained:` still read) and drops caller history
- `session_api_media_images.go` — commits up to 10 inline images as immutable media and rehydrates them, a vanished image becoming a text notice

#### A2A forwarding

The A2A platform adapter (`pkg/gateway/platforms/a2a`) hands a peer agent's turn to the profile's owning gateway. Each peer conversation, identified by agent, tenant, peer and context id, owns one hidden session with source `a2a`; clarify is declined for it.

- `session_a2a.go` — `ForwardToOwner`: dials the owning gateway's socket, calls `a2a.forward`, waits for the admission's completion event with 0.25 to 5 s backoff; a timeout never cancels accepted work; the `a2a` policy with its four-part peer identity
- `session_a2a_forward.go` — `a2a.forward` verb: derives the canonical session from agent, tenant, peer and context id, refuses another peer's identity, admits the turn

#### Cron sessions

The scheduler in `pkg/cron` runs agent jobs through the session authority instead of running them itself. Each fire of a job is one hidden session with source `cron` whose frozen request holds the job; any other input sent to that session settles with a read-only error.

- `session_cron.go` — `cron.submit`, `cron.status`, `cron.cancel` and `cron.recover`; cron owner registry per store home; execution through hooks `pkg/cron` installs, cancellable mid-run; result delivery into a local chat as a route wake (60 s wait)

#### Kanban card runs

Built only without the `icebath_core` and `icebath_noextras` tags; bound through hook variables declared elsewhere in the package.

- `session_kanban_run.go` — `kanban.run` verb: verifies the dispatcher's claim against the board read-only, builds a trusted policy with the card's model overrides, admits one finite turn
- `session_kanban_worker_context.go` — binds the adopted worker to its claim and ends the attempt once the dispatcher's spawned worker is gone
- `session_kanban_worker_loss.go` — appends a `worker_lost` event for a card attempt whose worker was lost
- `session_kanban_worker_turns.go` — child side: start-failure booking, `worker_result` event, proof that this process is still the bound worker

#### Bot Chat delivery

Messages from another bot profile or producer land in a profile's titled "Bot Chat" local session. Each delivery has an id and a receipt file in the profile's `runtime` delivery mailbox, so a sender can retry or settle an ambiguous send exactly once.

- `session_bot_deliver.go` — `bot_relay.deliver` and `bot_relay.settle`: receipt pin, admission as automation, legacy ticket migration in FIFO order, owner-state refusals that allow a resend
- `session_bot_mailbox.go` — mailbox lock, guarded receipt writes, pin withdraw, requeue and refuse, receipt scans and refresh tasks
- `session_bot_receipt.go` — receipt projection from admission state, one retry for a transient failure, reply watcher, Bot Chat creation and its generation identity
- `session_bot_scan.go` — shape checks of scanned receipts: canonical, refused, legacy or pre-admission pin
- `session_bot.go` — moves a handed-off Bot Chat aside once its lane switched to another conversation, at runtime and at boot

#### Hosted rooms: service, member producer, attachments

A hosted room ("group") seats several bot profiles as members. Each member binding owns a hidden `bot_room` session, created with clarify disabled, whose turns are admitted with `hosted:` request ids and re-authorized against current membership at claim time.

- `session_hosted_service.go` — `CanonicalHostedRoomService`: room store bound to an authority, attestation of operations, admission check at claim, service start after readiness
- `session_hosted_service_stop.go` — stops every authority's room service within one shared deadline without interrupting accepted turns
- `session_hosted_rpc.go` — member producer over the canonical FIFO: resolve, create, resume, submit, history, results (384 KiB budget), info, interrupt, discard, approve
- `session_hosted_controls.go` — operator discard and retry of exact local attempts and of peer member attempts, room status listing the pending actions; the local-attempt fence refuses a peer member as `unsupported_operation`
- `session_hosted_members.go` — [partial] local bots this process serves and seatable profiles from `hosted_rooms.profiles`; a bot served under a linked profile home is refused a seat as "not supported in groups yet"
- `session_hosted_attachments.go` — composer upload retention, committed downloads, submission payload with bound attachments
- `session_hosted_attested.go` — attachment manifest limits (15 MB each, 16 files and 50 MB per task) and payloads derived from source-attested digests

#### Hosted cross-owner transport

When a room member's profile is served by another process, operations travel over that owner's private control socket and are attested by the room's source owner before they run.

- `session_hosted_transport.go` — authenticated owner exchange (64 KiB request cap), source attestation, durable transport binding in `state_meta`, re-authorization of a remote hosted row before claim
- `session_hosted_transport_producer.go` — installs the control-server verbs, forwards producer calls to the member's owner, pulls attested attachment bytes in 360 KiB chunks
- `session_hosted_owner_exchange_{unix,windows}.go` — one exchange over the private control socket or the Windows control channel (2 variants)

#### Room verbs and the Bots roster

The socket face of hosted rooms plus the list of bots a client can talk to. Room verbs run under the owning profile's scope. Work verbs (send, stop, continue, retry, discard, approve, attachment upload and download) refuse `runtime_coordination_required` unless the room driver is running in this process, and disband refuses it for a room with active work and no driver.

- `session_group_controls.go` — the 20 `groups.*` verbs with per-verb capability and field tables, and `profiles.list` building the Bots roster with each bot's Bot Chat, newest chat and worker

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/bundled` — link-time roster of the 28 compiled-in chat platform adapters

*1 file, 42 Go lines*

One file of blank imports. There is no runtime discovery of built-in adapters: a platform exists in the binary only because this file imports its package, whose `init` calls `plugins.RegisterBundled` with a `Plugin` (manifest key `platforms/<name>`, kind `platform`). When the plugin manager loads that plugin, its `Register` method calls `ctx.RegisterPlatform(plugins.PlatformSpec{...})`, which lands in the gateway platform registry as a `PlatformEntry` (adapter factory, required env vars, install hint, and an `Extra` map of hooks such as `standalone_sender_fn`, `setup_fn`, `apply_yaml_config_fn`, `target_ref_syntax_fn`, `platform_hint`, `max_message_length`, `env_overrides`). Each platform package additionally calls `gateway.RegisterBundledEnv` and `gateway.RegisterEnvSettings` from its own `init` to declare its env-var bridge and the settings its legacy env names map to. The only importer is `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go`, which carries the build tag `!icebath_core`, so a core-only build ships no chat platforms. Third-party platforms do not come through here; they register through the plugin manager and the `hosted` bridge.

#### Bundled platform link list

The 28 linked packages are a2a, bluebubbles, buzz, dingtalk, discord, email, feishu, googlechat, homeassistant, irc, line, matrix, mattermost, ntfy, photon, qqbot, raft, signal, simplex, slack, sms, teams, telegram, wecom, weixin, whatsapp, whatsappcloud and yuanbao.

- `bundled.go` — blank-imports every bundled platform package; its `init` installs `gateway.PlatformRegistryService()` as `plugins.Services.Platforms` when no services are installed yet, so bundled plugins have a registry to load into before process wiring

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/hosted` — bridge that lets a platform adapter living in a third-party plugin's guest process act as a Go gateway adapter

*4 files, 1,686 Go lines*

The "hosted" platform is not a chat service. It is the Go stand-in for a platform adapter that a third-party plugin implements inside its guest, the WebAssembly module or external program that `pkg/plugins` runs through a `PluginHost` (`plugins.HostedObject` and `plugins.HostedCallable` are remote handles into that guest). Python plugin source is refused by the loader, but this bridge still speaks the Python adapter API: method names, keyword arguments and the upstream module paths below. `EntryKeywords` is installed as `gateway.HostedEntryKeywords` by `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go`; the platform registry calls it from `platformRegistryService.NewEntry` whenever a plugin's `register_platform` keywords contain a hosted callable or object, and it converts every keyword into the Go value the matching `PlatformEntry` field holds. The `Adapter` it produces embeds the Go `BasePlatformAdapter` and forwards a method to the child only when the plugin's class defines that method outside the upstream base module `gateway.platforms.base`; everything else runs the Go base behaviour. Arguments and results cross as plain dicts rebuilt on the far side through upstream Python import paths (`gateway.config:PlatformConfig.from_dict`, `gateway.platforms.event:MessageEvent`, `gateway.platforms.base:SendResult`), so the whole package is a compatibility layer for plugins written against the original Python adapter API. Implemented and wired; nothing is persisted.

#### Hosted adapter wrapper

`Adapter` implements the gateway adapter interface by remote call. `NewAdapter` asks the child which of 37 forwarded methods and 31 "surface" hooks the plugin class overrides, binds inbound delivery so the child's `handle_message` reaches the Go base pipeline or the runner's message handler, and mirrors lifecycle hooks (`mark_connected`, `mark_disconnected`, `set_fatal_error`) in both directions.

- `adapter.go` — `Adapter` type and construction; forwards connect, disconnect, send, edit, delete, typing, every media send, private notice, drafts, exec approval, slash confirm, clarify, TTS, processing hooks and toolset selection; converts `MessageEvent` and `SessionSource` to and from field dicts with ISO timestamps
- `adapter_surface.go` — the optional override surface: connection state, message length functions, tool event and preview formatting, plugin handler wiring, text batching hooks, exec-approval card strings and budget, warning emission, and streaming TTS begin, write, finish and abort with handle state copied both ways

#### Registration keyword and env-step conversion

Turns what a hosted plugin passed to `register_platform` into Go registry values. A hook that raises in the guest surfaces as a Go panic that the callers of these hooks recover, mirroring the Go-native hooks.

- `entry.go` — `EntryKeywords`: wraps `adapter_factory`, `validate_config`, `is_connected`, `config_connected_fn`, `ensure_deps_fn`, `setup_fn`, `env_enablement_fn`, `apply_yaml_config_fn`, target-ref parse, validate and syntax functions, `standalone_sender_fn` and `send_message_handler` as Go function types; reads `standalone_send` policy objects and `setup_vars` question lists
- `envstep.go` — converts a plugin's `env_overrides` rows into `gateway.EnvStep` values: upstream `EnvCred` records, fixed and optional env spec tuples with converter functions run in the child, and arbitrary callables that receive the gateway config and whose mutations are written back

### `pkg/gateway/messagetools` — the `send_message` handler, cross-platform send routing, a standalone Telegram sender and a Microsoft Graph client

*9 files, 3,213 Go lines*

This package holds everything behind the tool name `send_message` and one unrelated client. It exposes exactly one tool handler, `SendMessageTool(ctx, args)`, with four actions selected by `args["action"]`: `send` (the default), `list`, `react` and `unreact`. No registration of a `send_message` schema or handler in the agent tool registry exists in non-test code: the name appears elsewhere only in label, guardrail, delegate-blocklist and toolset-description tables, so the agent cannot call it. The handler is reached from the `icebath send` command (through the `gatewaycli.SendMessageTool` hook assigned in `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go`) and from the MCP server's `messages_send` handler. `SendToPlatform` is the router that cron delivery (`pkg/cron/scheduler_delivery.go`) calls directly, and `SendTelegram` is wired into the Telegram plugin as its out-of-process sender. The package reads the gateway config, the channel directory and home channels, mirrors sent text into the target's gateway session, and talks to live adapters of the in-process gateway when one runs. The two `microsoft_graph_*` files are an app-only Graph client used by the Teams adapter and the Teams meeting pipeline and have nothing to do with message sending.

#### The `send_message` handler: arguments, guards and result shape

`send` takes `target` (`platform` or `platform:ref`, the ref resolved through the platform's target syntax and the channel directory) and `message`. A target naming only a platform goes to that platform's home channel. `MEDIA:` tags are extracted from the message and filtered against the media delivery path policy, and `[[as_document]]` forces document delivery. `list` returns the channel directory. `react` and `unreact` take `target`, `emoji` and `message_id` and require a live adapter that implements `AddReaction` or `RemoveReaction`. Results are JSON text in Python `json.dumps` form.

- `send_message_handle.go` — action dispatch; platform and config resolution with a detailed "not configured" error (resolved home, state of each secret source, hint when a running gateway holds the platform); the relay egress authorization guard that fails closed; skips a send that duplicates a cron job's auto-delivery target (`ICEBATH_CRON_AUTO_DELIVER_*` session env); Slack user-id targets opened as DMs; session mirroring; `media_dropped` and `partial_success` reporting
- `tool_error.go` — builds the tool error envelope with a bounded message
- `log.go` — package logger named `gateway/messagetools`

#### Platform routing and send strategies

`SendToPlatform` chooses how one message leaves: Weixin always through its plugin standalone sender; Telegram through this package's own REST sender; platforms whose `StandaloneSendPolicy` asks for it through the plugin's `standalone_sender_fn`; Matrix, Slack and WeCom through a chunked route over the live adapter; otherwise a plugin `send_message_handler`, then the live in-process adapter, then the standalone sender. Text is chunked with the platform's registered maximum length. Native media delivery exists only for Telegram, Discord, Matrix, Weixin, Signal, Yuanbao, Feishu, WhatsApp, Slack and QQBot; other platforms get the text with a warning that attachments were omitted.

- `send_message_tool.go` — `SendOptions` and `SendToPlatform`; live-adapter dispatch onto the gateway loop; `sendLiveAdapterMedia`, which calls an adapter's native image, video, voice and document methods and refuses kinds the adapter does not override; standalone policy lookup and caption-riding for a single captionable file
- `send_message_senders.go` — the one-shot Telegram send (`SendTelegram`): MarkdownV2 or HTML text chunks with plain-text fallback on parse errors, retries with flood-wait and exponential backoff, forum-topic routing with a retry without the topic when it is gone, media by extension as photo, video, voice note, audio or document, 1024-character captions; also the Matrix send through a live or ephemeral adapter, the plugin standalone sender lookup and error-text redaction of tokens and secrets
- `send_message_slack_dm.go` — resolves a Slack user id or user-name target to a DM conversation id with `conversations.open` over the Slack Web API, honouring the Slack proxy

#### Standalone Telegram Bot API client

A minimal HTTP client for `https://api.telegram.org` used only by the one-shot sender above; it is independent of the go-telegram SDK the live adapter uses.

- `telegram_bot_api.go` — `[py-shim]` Bot API client addressed by python-telegram-bot coroutine names and keyword arguments (`send_message`, `send_photo` and so on mapped to camelCase methods); multipart upload of open files and thumbnail paths; maps HTTP status and `parameters.retry_after` to python-telegram-bot exception class names that the retry logic matches on

#### Microsoft Graph app-only auth and REST client

Client-credentials access to Microsoft Graph for Teams features. Callers are `pkg/gateway/platforms/teams/summary_writer.go` and `pkg/builtin/teamspipeline`. It sits in this package only because the Python original kept it under the tools directory.

- `microsoft_graph_auth.go` — credentials from `MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID`, `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_ID`, `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET`, optional `MSGRAPH_SCOPE` and `MSGRAPH_AUTHORITY_URL`; OAuth v2 token fetch with a 20 second timeout; in-memory token cache refreshed 120 seconds before expiry; typed config and token errors; token health inspection
- `microsoft_graph_client.go` — JSON GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE against `https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0`; three retries on transport errors, a token refetch on 401, `Retry-After` honoured on 429 and 5xx; `@odata.nextLink` pagination; streamed and chunked file download; API errors carrying status, request line and decoded body

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/discord` — Discord bot adapter: gateway websocket, slash commands, component prompts, threads and forums, missed-message recovery and a full voice stack

*51 files, 16,528 Go lines*

`DiscordAdapter` embeds the gateway base adapter and drives Discord through the discordgo library for the gateway websocket and REST, while voice is this package's own implementation. It is registered by `register.go` as the bundled plugin `platforms/discord` and constructed per platform config by the gateway. The gateway runner reaches it through small interfaces for voice (`JoinVoiceChannel`, `PlayInVoiceChannel`, `SetVoiceInputCallback`, `PlayAckInVoice`), thread renames, role re-authorization and allowlist resolution. Configuration comes from `DISCORD_*` env vars, the `discord.*` settings and the platform config `extra` map. State on disk, all under `<home>/gateway/`: `discord_message_recovery.db` (SQLite), `discord_command_sync_state.json` and `discord_nonconversational_messages.json`; the update prompt writes `<home>/.update_response`. Voice depends on three things located at run time: `libopus`, `libdave` (Discord's end-to-end encryption library) and `ffmpeg`. Port residue is moderate: error texts rewritten to discord.py wording, a discord.py `View` emulation for components, and a line-for-line port of discord.py's voice client. Features not present: message delete, modals, context-menu commands, stickers and polls (poll intents are requested but nothing handles them).

#### Plugin registration, env bridge and agent hint

Declares the platform to the registry and maps env vars onto config. Required env is `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`. The entry advertises a 2000-character message limit, the send-target syntax `channel_id[:thread_id]`, `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL` as the cron delivery target, a standalone sender that supports media and captions, and display overrides (`reasoning_style: subtext`).

- `register.go` — `discordPlugin` manifest and `Register`; wires adapter factory, setup wizard, YAML bridge, standalone sender and authz declarations
- `gateway_env.go` — env steps for `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL` and `DISCORD_REPLY_TO_MODE`; maps `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS`, `DISCORD_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `DISCORD_ALLOW_BOTS`, `DISCORD_ALLOWED_ROLES` and `DISCORD_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` onto `discord.*` settings; an allowlist suppresses pairing
- `yaml_config.go` — passes only the `allow_mentions` map of the config.yaml `discord` section into the platform extra; every other key is a setting
- `adapter_hint.go` — `[data]` system-prompt hint telling the agent Discord renders markdown but not tables and how `MEDIA:` paths and image URLs are delivered
- `log.go` — package logger named `gateway/platforms/discord`

#### Connection lifecycle, gateway websocket and liveness probe

`Connect` takes the base adapter's scoped lock keyed on the bot token (a second holder is a conflict), builds a discordgo session with a fixed intent set (message content always; server members only when username or role allowlists need it), logs in, and runs a reconnect loop modelled on discord.py: resume on resumable closes, exponential backoff with jitter up to 2^10 seconds on dial failures, fatal on close codes 4004 and 4010 to 4014. Startup failures are classified into fatal codes (`discord_auth_error`, `discord_intents_required` with fix instructions, `discord_connect_timeout`, `discord_connect_error`). A liveness loop samples heartbeat-ack age, latency, socket state and dispatch silence every `discord.websocket_liveness_interval_seconds` and forces a reconnect through a retryable fatal error after `discord.websocket_liveness_failure_threshold` bad samples.

- `adapter.go` — `DiscordAdapter` struct and limits (2000 characters, at most 8 split messages); connect error classification; `gateway_platform_event` emission to plugin hooks for message edits, cached deletes, thread creation and thread renames; clickable tool-preview links
- `connect.go` — constructor reading text-batch delays (`ICEBATH_DISCORD_TEXT_BATCH_DELAY_SECONDS`, `..._SPLIT_DELAY_SECONDS`), voice timeouts and liveness settings; `Connect` and `Disconnect`; gateway event handler wiring; ready handling that waits up to 2 seconds for unavailable guilds; the liveness loop; post-connect slash command sync dispatch
- `gateway_link.go` — `gatewayLink` wrapper over the discordgo session: proxy support (`DISCORD_PROXY`), a socket wrapper that parses websocket frames to capture the server close code, the reconnect loop, and a REST transport that turns a rate-limit sleep longer than a cap into an error
- `helpers.go` — mixed bag: the table of 29 native slash commands and their argument specs, transport-error classification, privileged-intent guidance text, SSRF-guarded image fetch that rechecks every redirect, snowflake time, allowlist id cleaning, allowed-mentions policy (`DISCORD_ALLOW_MENTION_EVERYONE`, `_ROLES`, `_USERS`, `_REPLIED_USER`), and regexes recognising the bot's own status messages

#### Access control, mention policy and channel gates

Decides whether an inbound message, slash command or button click is acted on. Order for people: a pairing-store approval always passes; with no user or role allowlist, `discord.allow_all_users` or `gateway.allow_all_users` opens access, otherwise only messages in `discord.allowed_channels` pass; with allowlists, a listed user id, `*`, or a member holding an allowed role passes. Roles count in DMs only when `discord.dm_role_auth_guild` names the guild to check. Other bots are governed by `discord.allow_bots` (`none`, `mentions`, `all`) and `discord.bots_require_inline_mention`. In guild channels a mention is required unless the channel is in `discord.free_response_channels`, the message is in a thread the bot already joined (and `discord.thread_require_mention` is off) or `discord.require_mention` is off; `discord.ignored_channels` always wins. A message that mentions other bots but not this one is dropped, and with `DISCORD_IGNORE_NO_MENTION` (default true) so is one that mentions other people but not the bot outside bot threads and free-response channels.

- `authz.go` — channel resolution from cache, DM and forum detection, `isAllowedUser`, guild role lookup, the one-time fail-closed warning, and `discordMessageAdmission` (dedup of 2000 ids for 300 seconds, self and system messages dropped, bot policy, mention rules)
- `gate.go` — per-profile settings readers for every `discord.*` gate; live resync of the user and role allowlists when the settings text changes; bot-tag debounce window that lets a bot's follow-up chunks through after it mentioned this bot; channel key sets matching ids, names and `#names` including the parent of a thread
- `adapter_config_readers.go` — `discord.dm_role_auth_guild`, the button prompt timeout (`approvals.discord_prompt_timeout`, clamped to at least 30 seconds), and the optional admin-only gate on exec-approval buttons (`require_admin_for_exec_approval`, `allow_admin_from` in extra)
- `interaction_auth.go` — applies the same channel, user and role gates to slash commands and component clicks; resolves the interaction's channel and user; defers an interaction unless its token already expired
- `reauthorize.go` — `ReauthorizeNativeRoles`: rechecks a session that was admitted by role against the member's current roles and the current role policy, called by the gateway session ingress

#### Inbound message normalisation and attachments

Turns a Discord message into a gateway `MessageEvent`. It strips the bot mention, absorbs forwarded-message snapshots and the replied-to message's attachments, sets chat type `dm`, `group` or `thread`, attaches channel topic, guild and parent ids, per-channel skill bindings and channel prompts from the platform extra, and auto-creates a thread for a mention in a plain channel when `discord.auto_thread` is on. With `discord.history_backfill` on it fetches up to `discord.history_backfill_limit` recent channel messages as context since the bot's last reply, marking authors who fail the allowlist as `[unverified]`. Plain text is debounced through the base text batcher (0.6 seconds, 2.0 seconds after a near-limit chunk).

- `inbound.go` — `dispatchDiscordMessage` and `handleDiscordMessage`; attachment collection (images and audio cached, other files cached as documents under `discord.max_attachment_bytes`, UTF-8 text files up to 100 KiB inlined into the prompt); voice-note detection by waveform; mention cleaning to display names; channel history paging and the context block builder
- `attachments.go` — attachment download through the bot's authenticated session with an SSRF-guarded URL fallback; media cache writers; auto-thread name derivation (mentions stripped, 80 characters); shutdown flush deadline for pending text batches derived from `ICEBATH_GATEWAY_ADAPTER_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT`

#### Outbound text, edits, reactions and typing

`Send` converts markdown tables to bullet lists (Discord renders no pipe tables), splits at 2000 characters, keeps at most 8 messages and appends a truncation notice, and replies to the triggering message according to `reply_to_mode` (`first`, `all`, `off`), retrying without the reference when Discord rejects it. Streaming is edit-based: a mid-stream edit over the limit is truncated to one message, and the final edit is split into the edited first chunk plus reply-chained continuations. A transport failure returns the retryable error `send_path_degraded`. Processing reactions are eyes on start, then a check mark or cross (`discord.reactions`).

- `send.go` — `Send`, `EditMessage`, `EditMessageWithMetadata`, overflow splitting, forum-channel sends that create a new thread post, reaction add and remove, `OnProcessingStart` and `OnProcessingComplete`; `[py-shim]` rewriting of discordgo REST errors into discord.py exception text that other code matches by substring (`error code: 50035`, `10008`)
- `chat.go` — persistent typing loop that reposts every 12 seconds and sleeps out 429s; `GetChatInfo`; resolution of username allowlist entries to ids by paging guild members; Retry-After parsing
- `tracker.go` — persistent set of up to 2000 bot message ids that are status noise (sends marked `non_conversational` in metadata), stored in `gateway/discord_nonconversational_messages.json` and excluded from history context

#### Outbound media

Native attachments for images, video, documents, animations and audio. Uploads are preflighted against the channel's limit (guild boost tier, floor of 20 MiB) and replaced by a size notice when too large. `SendVoice` posts a real Discord voice message (message flag 8192, Ogg Opus, flat waveform, duration read from the Ogg granule position), transcoding other formats through ffmpeg and falling back to a plain audio attachment.

- `media.go` — `SendImageFile`, `SendVideo`, `SendDocument`, `SendImage` and `SendAnimation` (URL downloaded through the redirect-guarded client, then uploaded), `SendMultipleImages` (ten per message, failed batch retried per image), `SendVoice`, upload limit calculation and forum-aware file posts

#### Threads, forums and thread titles

Covers auto-threading, the `/thread` command, session handoff threads and forum channels. A send to a forum channel creates a new thread post whose name is the first line of the message (100 characters). Thread creation tries a direct create and falls back to posting a seed message and threading from it. Semantic session titles rename a thread only while it still carries the provisional name the bot gave it, so a human rename is never overwritten.

- `threads.go` — thread creation REST helper with audit-log reason, `/thread` private thread creation with archive-duration validation, `autoCreateThread` with one retry, `RenameThread` (80 UTF-16 units, guarded by expected current name), `CreateHandoffThread` for text, news, forum and media parents
- `thread_titles.go` — bounded tracker of the bot's own guarded renames fed by raw `THREAD_UPDATE` events, used to show the right thread name during the rename race; readable `guild / #parent / thread` chat names

#### Slash commands and command registration sync

Builds a tree of global application commands on every connect: the 29 native commands (`/new`, `/reset`, `/model`, `/reasoning`, `/personality`, `/retry`, `/undo`, `/status`, `/sethome`, `/stop`, `/steer`, `/plan`, `/compress`, `/title`, `/resume`, `/usage`, `/help`, `/insights`, `/reload-mcp`, `/reload-skills`, `/voice`, `/update`, `/restart`, `/approve`, `/deny`, `/thread`, `/queue`, `/bg`, `/btw`), then every gateway registry command and plugin slash command not already present, then one `/skill` command with autocomplete over the skill catalog, capped at Discord's 100. Each native command is a template rendered into gateway command text and dispatched as a message event after an ephemeral defer. Unauthorized use gets an ephemeral refusal and an operator alert sent to the Telegram, then Slack, home channel of the same profile. Slash commands can be turned off with `slash_commands: false` in extra and hidden from non-admins with `DISCORD_HIDE_SLASH_COMMANDS`.

- `slash.go` — command tree, option payloads in discord.py wire shape, `/skill` autocomplete (25 choices), `/thread` handler, slash event construction, authorization and alerting, interaction routing to commands, autocomplete or component views; `RefreshSkillGroup` is `[unwired]` because it returns two ints while the runner's `/reload-skills` hook asserts a method returning an error, so `/skill` autocomplete is only rebuilt on reconnect
- `command_sync.go` — sync policy from `DISCORD_COMMAND_SYNC_POLICY` (`safe` default, `bulk`, `off`); `safe` fetches existing global commands, diffs canonical payloads and creates, patches, recreates or deletes only what changed, pacing mutations 4.5 seconds apart; a fingerprint of the desired set plus language and any rate-limit deadline persist per application id in `gateway/discord_command_sync_state.json` so an unchanged set is skipped

#### Interactive component prompts

Buttons and select menus bound to one message. Views live only in memory, keyed by message id with random custom ids, so a card posted before a restart no longer responds. Every click is authorized against the user and role allowlists plus the gateway's live check, approval, confirmation and clarify cards resolve only once, and each view has a timeout that disables its components.

- `views.go` — `[port-artifact]` emulation of discord.py's `View`: component rows (five rows, 25 items), timeout timer, dispatch of clicks by custom id, wire payload shape, plus shared helpers for interaction responses, followups and embed stamping
- `views_exec_approval.go` — dangerous-command approval card with Allow once, Allow session, Always allow and Deny; resolves through the gateway approval queue; optional admin-only gate; card retired when the request settles elsewhere or times out
- `views_prompts.go` — slash-command confirmation (once, always, cancel); update prompt whose yes or no is written atomically to `<home>/.update_response` for the detached updater; two-step provider then model select picker with an "expensive model" confirmation step and a two-minute timeout; flat choice picker (25 options); clarify card with up to 24 numbered buttons plus Other, which switches to typed-answer capture
- `prompts.go` — the adapter methods that send those cards (`SendExecApprovalPrompt`, `SendSlashConfirm`, `SendClarify`, `SendUpdatePrompt`, `SendModelPicker`, `SendChoicePicker`); card text duplicated into message content so it is readable without embeds; optional user mentions on approval cards (`discord.approval_mentions`); command-preview budget under the message cap

#### Missed-message recovery ledger

Opt-in catch-up after downtime (`discord.missed_message_backfill.enabled`, off by default). On ready the adapter scans the configured channels and their active and archived threads for messages newer than `window_seconds` (default 6 hours), skips any the ledger shows as completed, claimed or out of attempts, skips any already answered by a bot reply other than an outage notice, and re-dispatches up to `max_dispatches` through the normal ingress gates. The scan joins the gateway's startup-restore gate so recovered turns start before new traffic.

- `recovery.go` — `DiscordRecoveryStore`: SQLite file `gateway/discord_message_recovery.db` with tables `discord_messages`, `discord_recovery_scans` and `discord_recovery_cursors`, WAL with fallback, mode 0600, rows pruned after 30 days
- `recovery_records.go` — settings readers for the backfill window, limit, dispatch and attempt caps; ledger writes for message seen, processing start, completion, bot response, scan start and end, per-channel cursors; outage-notice detection
- `backfill.go` — the scan task, round-robin iteration over channels and threads, hidden-channel filtering, recovered-message dispatch, and the small goroutine task type the adapter's background work uses
- `backfill_checks.go` — decides whether one recent message still needs work: a later bot reply referencing it counts as handled unless it is an outage notice

#### Voice channels: joining, speech in, speech out and effects

`/voice join` makes the runner call `JoinVoiceChannel` for the channel the user sits in. Inbound: per-speaker PCM is buffered until 1.5 seconds of silence (minimum 0.5 seconds of speech), converted to 16 kHz mono WAV with ffmpeg, transcribed through the shared speech-to-text tool, filtered for Whisper hallucinations and handed to the runner callback with the guild and user; only allowlisted speakers are transcribed. Outbound: TTS replies play in the channel through ffmpeg, with the receiver paused during playback. After `discord.voice_channel_inactivity_timeout_seconds` without activity the bot leaves and tells the runner, except that it stays when the runner reports the bound chat's voice reply mode as `off`. Optional voice effects (`discord.voice_fx.*` read straight from config.yaml) add a looping ambient bed, ducking under speech, lead-in silence and short spoken acknowledgements while the agent works.

- `voice_adapter.go` — join, move and leave; `PlayTTS`, `PlayInVoiceChannel` and `PlayAckInVoice`; playback timeout sized from ffprobe duration; mixer installation; inactivity timer; the listen loop that polls the receiver every 200 ms and sends a keepalive packet every 15 seconds
- `voice_state.go` — per-guild voice state maps, voice-state-update handling that refreshes the receiver when members come and go, leave with a final flush of buffered speech, PCM to WAV conversion, transcription and delivery (dropped when the text binding moved meanwhile)
- `voice_info.go` — binding of a voice call to a text channel and source; channel name, members and current speakers for the agent's prompt context
- `voice_runner.go` — runner-facing accessors despite the name: cached guild, channel and member display names, `SendToChannel`, role ids and `IsAllowedUser`
- `voice_config.go` — loads `discord.voice_fx` from raw config.yaml over built-in defaults (lead silence defaults to 200 ms here, while the settings registry declares 0)
- `voice_mixer.go` — continuous 48 kHz stereo PCM mixer summing a looping ambient bed and one-shot speech with ducking and fade-in; ffmpeg decode of clips to PCM; a synthesised default ambient bed built with a `[py-shim]` numpy random generator so it matches the Python output

#### Voice protocol stack

A self-contained client for Discord voice, written here rather than taken from discordgo: voice gateway version 8 over websocket, UDP with IP discovery, the two `rtpsize` AEAD transport modes (`aead_aes256_gcm_rtpsize` preferred, then `aead_xchacha20_poly1305_rtpsize`), and DAVE end-to-end encryption through MLS. A join fails with an install hint when `libdave` cannot be loaded. The structure mirrors discord.py's `VoiceClient`, `VoiceConnectionState` and gateway classes one for one.

- `voice_client.go` — per-guild voice client: connect, move, disconnect, 20 ms frame player thread, ffmpeg PCM source and volume transformer, RTP packet construction and send
- `voice_connection.go` — connection state machine from voice-state and voice-server updates through websocket ready, IP discovery and session description; reconnect and resume handling; DAVE session transitions and recovery from invalid commits
- `voice_gateway.go` — voice websocket: identify, resume, select protocol, speaking, heartbeat with a 60 second ack deadline, and the binary DAVE and MLS opcodes 21 to 31
- `voice_transport.go` — mode selection, AEAD encryption with the RTP header as associated data, RTP header and IP-discovery packets, and the UDP reader thread with listener registration
- `voice_receiver.go` — receive path: transport decryption, DAVE frame decryption with a passthrough grace window during protocol transitions, per-SSRC Opus decoding, SSRC to user mapping from SPEAKING events, silence detection and utterance flushing
- `voice_dave.go` — runtime binding to `libdave` release v1.2.2 (session, key ratchets, encryptor, per-user decryptors, MLS proposals, commits and welcomes) and the per-OS install command shown when it is missing

#### Opus codec and ffmpeg discovery

Opus is loaded dynamically at connect time; without it voice playback is disabled with a warning. The doctor command probes it through `LoadOpusLibrary`.

- `opus.go` — finds and loads `libopus`: a DLL beside the executable on Windows, the system library search, then Homebrew paths on macOS
- `voice_opus.go` — encoder (48 kHz stereo, 128 kbps, FEC at 15 percent expected loss) and per-SSRC decoder over the loaded library
- `voice_opus_ctl{,_darwin_arm64}.go` — per-ABI call shim for the variadic `opus_encoder_ctl` (Apple arm64 passes the variadic argument on the stack); two variants
- `ffmpeg.go` — resolves the ffmpeg executable from `FFMPEG_PATH`, the shared media discovery, or a WinGet install directory

#### Standalone REST sender

Sends without a running gateway, for `icebath send` and cron delivery. It uses the bot token from the platform config or `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN` and plain REST calls.

- `standalone.go` — text and multipart media sends to a channel or thread; probes and caches whether a channel is a forum and, if so, creates a thread post; bounded response reading; proxy-safe error text

#### Setup wizard

The Discord step of `icebath gateway setup`.

- `onboarding.go` — prompts for the bot token, validates it with `GET /applications/@me`, reports app owners and whether the Message Content and Server Members intents are enabled, prints an invite URL with the exact permission bits the adapter uses, collects the user allowlist and home channel, and saves `DISCORD_BOT_TOKEN`, `DISCORD_ALLOWED_USERS` and `DISCORD_HOME_CHANNEL` to the env file

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/telegram` — Telegram bot adapter: long polling or webhook, forum and DM topics, MarkdownV2 and rich messages, inline keyboards and inline queries

*41 files, 14,560 Go lines*

`TelegramAdapter` embeds the gateway base adapter and uses the go-telegram/bot SDK for typed Bot API calls, but owns its HTTP transports, its `getUpdates` loop and its update dispatcher. Those three are a reimplementation of python-telegram-bot (PTB) classes (`Application`, `Updater`, `HTTPXRequest`, handler groups), and errors are classified by PTB exception class names carried on Go error types. It is registered by `register.go` as the bundled plugin `platforms/telegram`; the process wiring in `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go` injects the command catalog reader (`InlineCommands`) and the REST sender (`SendTelegramREST`). Configuration comes from `TELEGRAM_*` env vars, `telegram.*` settings and the platform `extra` map. State on disk: `<home>/telegram_update_receipts_<bot id>.json`, DM topic thread ids written back into config.yaml, and `<home>/.update_response`. The adapter also runs scripts under `<home>/scripts/gmail-triage/` from button taps. Telegram Business updates are subscribed and admitted as ordinary messages, but no send passes a business connection id.

#### Plugin registration, env bridge, config bridge and target syntax

Required env is `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`. The entry advertises a 4096-character limit, `TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL` for cron delivery, display overrides (tool progress off) and a standalone sender that delegates to `messagetools.SendTelegram`. The setup wizard lives outside this package (`gateway.SetupTelegram`).

- `register.go` — `telegramPlugin` manifest and `Register`; adapter factory; `is_connected` check on the token; standalone sender shim over the injected `SendTelegramREST`
- `gateway_env.go` — env steps for `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN`, `TELEGRAM_REPLY_TO_MODE`, `TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_IPS` and `TELEGRAM_HOME_CHANNEL`; maps `TELEGRAM_ALLOWED_USERS`, `TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS`, `TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_CHATS` and `TELEGRAM_ALLOW_BOTS` onto settings
- `adapter_config.go` — YAML bridge passing `disable_topic_auto_rename`, `dm_topic_auto_transfer`, `disable_link_previews`, `proxy_url` and any `extra` key that is not a registered setting into the platform extra; plain-text flattening of the rich-message payload Telegram echoes in replies; notification mode reader (`telegram.notifications`: `important` sends silently unless asked to notify, or `all`)
- `telegram_ids.go` — chat id normalisation, `@username` targets, the send-target syntax `chat_id[:topic_id]`, and reply-anchor parsing to a positive message id
- `adapter_hint.go` — `[data]` system-prompt hint describing markdown conversion, `MEDIA:` delivery and the `[[audio_as_voice]]` tag
- `log.go` — package logger named `gateway/platforms/telegram`

#### Adapter core, connect and disconnect

`Connect` takes the scoped lock keyed on the bot token, builds the request pair and application, initialises with up to 8 attempts (`ICEBATH_TELEGRAM_INIT_TIMEOUT`, default 30 seconds each, exponential pauses capped at 15 seconds), then starts a webhook listener when `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_URL` is set or long polling otherwise. Auth failures become the permanent fatal `telegram_auth_error`; anything else is the retryable `telegram_connect_error`. After connect, off the critical path, it registers the command menu with `setMyCommands` in the default, private and group scopes (skipped when a fingerprint of menu and language is unchanged, and registered lazily per forum supergroup), optionally sets the bot's short description to an online or offline text (`status_indicator`, `status_online`, `status_offline`), and loads or creates configured DM topics. Queued updates from before a cold boot are dropped unless `drop_pending_on_cold_boot` is false.

- `adapter.go` — `TelegramAdapter` struct, constants and constructor reading extras (`typing_cooldown_seconds`, `typing_retrigger_min_interval_seconds`, `dm_topics`, `base_url` raising the document cap from 20 MB to 2 GB) and env batching delays; connected, disconnected and fatal transitions that gate delayed delivery; waiting up to 15 seconds for a reconnect before failing a send; handoff to a replacement adapter instance
- `adapter_connect.go` — `Connect` and `Disconnect` with bounded teardown steps, webhook and polling start, handler registration (text, commands, location, media, forum-topic-created, callback queries, inline queries, and a catch-all that emits `gateway_platform_event` for reactions and edits), plugin handler ordering, command menu, status indicator, raw Bot API request helper
- `adapter_core.go` — authorization helpers: session source for a message, channel post or reaction; callback-button authorization through the gateway's access check; letting an unauthorized private chat through when the profile answers strangers with a pairing code; pruning a DM topic binding Telegram reports deleted
- `adapter_helpers.go` — secret redaction of error text (including proxy URLs), a wall-clock deadline wrapper that abandons a stuck call and cleans up detached, callback toast text
- `errors.go` — `[py-shim]` `TelegramError` and friends carrying python-telegram-bot class names (`BadRequest`, `RetryAfter`, `NetworkError`, `Conflict`, `InvalidToken`, `Forbidden`, `TimedOut`) with subclass matching; real behaviour depending on it is every retry, fallback and fatal classification in the package; `PollingStallError`

#### Bot API transport: request pools, fallback IPs and proxy

Two separate HTTP pools, one for general calls and one dedicated to `getUpdates`, with timeouts from `ICEBATH_TELEGRAM_HTTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT`, `_READ_TIMEOUT`, `_WRITE_TIMEOUT`, `_POOL_TIMEOUT` and `_POOL_SIZE`. When no proxy applies, a fallback transport dials known IPv4 addresses of `api.telegram.org` first (keeping the Host header and TLS server name) and the hostname last, with sticky selection of the last working address; the addresses come from `fallback_ips`, or from DNS-over-HTTPS discovery through Google and Cloudflare, or from two seed IPs. Proxy comes from `TELEGRAM_PROXY`, `proxy_url` or the environment. A custom Bot API server is supported through `base_url`, `base_file_url` and `local_mode` (files read from disk).

- `telegram_network.go` — `TelegramFallbackTransport`, the per-pool HTTP transport with TCP keepalive socket options, DoH discovery, IP validation, request rewriting for a literal IP, and connect-error classification; its `InnerTransport` and limits types imitate httpx
- `ptb_request.go` — `[py-shim]` `ptbRequest`, the PTB `HTTPXRequest` equivalent: per-phase timeouts, client rebuild and shutdown, mapping of transport and HTTP failures to PTB exception classes, and a bot HTTP client that routes `getUpdates` through the polling pool and everything else through the general pool
- `ptb_build.go` — builds the request pair from extras and env, decides between fallback-IP, proxied and direct transports (`ICEBATH_TELEGRAM_DISABLE_FALLBACK_IPS`, `ICEBATH_TELEGRAM_FALLBACK_DISCOVERY_TIMEOUT`), and instruments the polling pool so every response feeds polling-progress tracking

#### Update dispatch, ordering and exactly-once admission

A PTB-shaped application with numbered handler groups sits between the update source and the adapter's handlers. Updates of one chat run in arrival order while different chats run concurrently, bounded by `max_concurrent_updates` (default 32). Each update id is admitted once per bot: a claim tracks in-flight work, and accepted ids are persisted as receipts for 24 hours so a redelivery after a restart is not processed twice.

- `ptb_application.go` — `[py-shim]` PTB `Application`: handler and error-handler registration by group, `TypeHandler`, update processors with slot reservation, task tracking, start and stop, and the handler-stop sentinel
- `ptb_handlers.go` — `[py-shim]` PTB `MessageHandler`, `CallbackQueryHandler` and `InlineQueryHandler` with the filters the adapter uses (text that is not a command, command entity at offset zero, location or venue, any media, forum topic created); effective-message selection that includes edited messages, channel posts and business messages, so an edit runs the same handlers again and carries an edit-revision identity
- `ptb_app.go` — per-connect bundle of the SDK bot, both request pools and the updater; initialise with `getMe`; custom base URL wiring; file download from the file endpoint or local disk
- `update_admission.go` — `UpdateAdmission` claims and receipts file `telegram_update_receipts_<bot id>.json`; `PerChatUpdateProcessor`; `TelegramApplication`, which wraps every handler callback, plugin handlers included, in the admission check

#### Long polling, webhook and connection health

Polling is the default. The lifecycle tracks "generations" of the long poll and proves progress from real `getUpdates` responses; until the first proven round trip after a (re)start, sends fail fast with `send_path_degraded`. Recovery ladders: network errors restart polling with backoff from 5 to 60 seconds up to 10 times, then raise the retryable fatal `telegram_network_error`; a 409 conflict (another poller on the token) stops, waits a growing delay, and goes fatal after 5 tries. A heartbeat every 90 seconds probes `getMe` and `getWebhookInfo` and escalates a stuck consumer, a dispatcher that stopped admitting fetched updates, or a poll silent for 150 seconds. Webhook mode refuses to start without `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`.

- `polling.go` — `pollingLifecycle`: generations, progress events, verifier after reconnect, connection-pool draining and client replacement when a close hangs, stale webhook deletion, cold-start readiness, the network and conflict recovery ladders, the heartbeat loop and its stall checks, fatal handoff to the runner
- `ptb_updater.go` — `[py-shim]` PTB `Updater`: its own `getUpdates` loop (10 second long poll, every update type requested), immediate retry on timeouts, flood-wait handling, abort on invalid token, offset confirmation on stop
- `ptb_webhook.go` — webhook HTTP listener on `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_HOST` and `TELEGRAM_WEBHOOK_PORT` (default 8443) at the URL's path; validates JSON content type and the `X-Telegram-Bot-Api-Secret-Token` header; serves before calling `setWebhook`

#### Inbound messages, group addressing and media intake

Private chats are always processed. Groups pass through topic gates (`telegram.allowed_topics`, `telegram.ignored_threads`), then `telegram.allowed_chats`, then addressing: free-response chats and topics, a reply to the bot, an `@mention` or text-mention entity, or a wake-word regex from `telegram.mention_patterns`; `telegram.require_mention` off answers everything. Related switches: `telegram.guest_mode` (a mention works outside the allowed chats), `telegram.exclusive_bot_mentions` (leave messages addressed only to other bots), `telegram.allow_bots` and `telegram.bots_require_mention`. With `telegram.observe_unmentioned_group_messages` on, unaddressed group chatter and its media are appended to the shared session as context without triggering a turn. Text split by the client is re-joined by an adaptive batcher; photo bursts and albums are merged (0.8 second debounce).

- `adapter_inbound.go` — all group gates and settings readers; bot identity refresh; mention and entity matching; handlers for text, commands, location pins (map link plus prompt) and media; download and caching of photos, voice, audio, video, video notes and documents under the size cap with a user-visible failure reply; text-file inlining; sticker description through the vision tool cached by sticker id; reply context including partial quotes; event construction with topic binding, channel prompt and edit identity; batching and album debounce
- `telegram_context.go` — who a group message is addressed to: mentions of other participants, whether a reply is expected, trigger text with the bot's handle stripped only when it is the sole addressee, and the group identity prompt
- `telegram_entities.go` — UTF-16 offset handling for message entities and inlining of hidden text-link URLs after their anchor text
- `telegram_held_inbound.go` — queue of up to 64 already-acknowledged inbound events that cannot dispatch during a disconnect; redispatched on reconnect or adopted by a replacement adapter
- `platform_event.go` — normalises reaction and edited-message updates into the stable `gateway_platform_event` envelope for plugin hooks
- `media_helpers.go` — the 20 MB `getFile` cap check and its skip note, 1024-character caption cut, cold-boot drop decision logging

#### Forum topics and DM topics

Supports supergroup forum topics and topics inside private chats. Named DM topics can be declared under `dm_topics` in extra; missing ones are created with a seed message and their thread ids are written back to config.yaml. A topic can carry a bound skill and name. When a user creates a topic in a private chat, their next thread-less message is routed into it. With `telegram.extra.dm_topic_auto_transfer`, a plain root DM is moved onto a topic chosen by the runner before the session key is computed. Handoff creates a forum topic.

- `adapter_topics.go` — `CreateDMTopic`, `EnsureDMTopic`, `RenameDMTopic`, `CreateHandoffThread`, DM topic config lookup, reload and persistence, startup topic setup
- `telegram_topic_routing.go` — records authorized client-created private topics and adopts them for the creator's follow-up messages
- `telegram_topic_transfer.go` — applies the runner's root-DM transfer hook to an inbound event, skipping commands, internal events and unauthorized senders
- `adapter_routing.go` — mixed helpers: thread and `direct_messages_topic_id` routing for sends (the General topic sent without a thread id), the reply-anchor rule that a private DM topic send must carry an anchor or be refused, error classifiers for missing threads, polling conflicts, auth, network, connect and pool timeouts, rich-message eligibility checks, notification silencing and per-chunk reply threading

#### Outbound text, streaming and pacing

`Send` formats standard markdown as MarkdownV2, splits on UTF-16 length at 4096 with `(n/m)` markers, sends each chunk with up to three attempts and falls back to stripped plain text when Telegram rejects the entities. Sends per chat are serialised by a FIFO lock and share a one-message-per-second budget with edits; a flood wait is remembered so later sends are refused locally until it passes, and a partially delivered multi-chunk send can be resumed. Streaming is edit-based, with native draft streaming (`sendMessageDraft`) in private chats; oversized final edits split into reply continuations. An opt-in "rich message" path (`telegram.extra.rich_messages`, `rich_drafts`, `allow_cjk_rich_messages`) posts raw markdown through `sendRichMessage` and `sendRichMessageDraft` for content MarkdownV2 degrades (tables, task lists, details blocks, block math), up to 32768 characters, and latches itself off when the endpoint is unavailable. Processing reactions are eyes, then thumbs up or down (`telegram.reactions`, off by default).

- `adapter_send.go` — `Send`, chunk retry and recovery ladder, `ResumePartialSend`, `SendOrUpdateStatus`, `EditMessage` and overflow split, `DeleteMessage`, `SendDraft`, the rich send, edit and draft paths, typing with DM-topic fallback and cooldown, `GetChatInfo`, reactions and processing hooks
- `send_pacing.go` — per-chat FIFO send lock that is re-entrant for nested calls, flood cooldown windows, the shared send and edit slot, typing cooldown after transient failures
- `mdv2_format.go` — `FormatMessage`: markdown to MarkdownV2 with code spans and fences kept verbatim, links preserved and everything else escaped
- `mdv2_text.go` — MarkdownV2 escaping and stripping for the plain fallback, bold-label HTML for approval cards, moving a chunk marker off a closing code fence, rich line-break normalisation

#### Outbound media

Native sends with topic routing and a retry without a stale DM-topic anchor. Voice: Ogg or Opus goes out as a voice bubble, mp3 and m4a as audio, anything else as a document; an explicit voice request transcodes to Ogg Opus through ffmpeg. Images above 1 MiB are recompressed to JPEG (quality 85, longest side 1600) before upload; albums go ten at a time.

- `adapter_media.go` — `SendVoice`, `SendImageFile`, `SendImage` (URL by reference, then SSRF-checked download and upload, then text fallback), `SendMultipleImages`, `SendDocument`, `SendVideo` with probed geometry and thumbnail, `SendAnimation`; missing-file errors that explain the sandbox bind-mount fix
- `media_send.go` — shared routing, reply anchor and notification fields for every media send, run under the chat send lock
- `media_probe.go` — voice duration from the WAV header or ffprobe, video width, height and duration from ffprobe, 320 pixel JPEG thumbnail through ffmpeg

#### Inline keyboards, pickers, approvals and inline queries

Inline-keyboard callbacks are dispatched on a data prefix and every tap is authorized through the gateway's access check before it acts. Pending prompt state is in memory only. Inline mode answers `@bot query` with a searchable list of every dispatchable command and skill (50 per page, 10 second cache); unauthorized users get an empty personal result.

- `adapter_prompts.go` — exec approval card with buttons resolving the gateway approval (`ea:`), slash confirmation (`sc:`), clarify with numbered choices and Other (`cl:`), update prompt answering through `<home>/.update_response` (`update_prompt:`), paginated provider then model picker with provider families folded (`mp`, `mm` and related prefixes), flat choice picker (`cp:`), the inline query handler, and Gmail triage buttons (`gt:verb:arg`) that run `<home>/scripts/gmail-triage/*.sh` (send draft, archive, draft, spam, mute, trust, VIP) with a secret-scrubbed environment and a 60 second timeout
- `inline_picker.go` — builds the inline catalog from core gateway commands plus uncapped plugin and skill commands, ranks by name prefix, name substring, then description, and pages results; `InlineCommands` is the injected command-registry reader
- `telegram_resolved_prompt.go` — rewrites a resolved prompt in place, keeping its original text by rebuilding HTML from the message entities and appending the decision with the buttons removed

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/slack` — Slack adapter over Socket Mode: multi-workspace, threads as sessions, assistant threads, native streaming, Block Kit prompts and slash commands

*23 files, 10,847 Go lines*

`SlackAdapter` embeds the gateway base adapter. Transport is Socket Mode only (slack-go's socketmode client under a small Bolt-like router written here); there is no HTTP Events API endpoint. Web API calls go through a thin client that posts arguments verbatim. It is registered by `register.go` as the bundled plugin `platforms/slack`; `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go` injects the slash subcommand map, native slash names, command busy policies, the known-command predicate and the manifest builder from `pkg/commands`, and binds the `icebath slack` command. Required env: `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` (comma-separated for several workspaces) and `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`. Extra workspaces are also read from `<home>/slack_tokens.json`, a file nothing in the Go code writes. Other state is in memory in bounded caches, except the thread watermark stored in session metadata and `<home>/slack-manifest.json`. Not present: modals, an update prompt, a flat choice picker, and persistence of interactive prompt state across restarts.

#### Plugin registration, env bridge and agent hint

The entry advertises a 39000-character limit, `SLACK_HOME_CHANNEL` (with `SLACK_HOME_CHANNEL_NAME` and `SLACK_HOME_CHANNEL_THREAD_ID`) for cron delivery, a standalone sender with media and captions, and display overrides turning tool progress and long-running notices off.

- `register.go` — `slackPlatformPlugin` manifest and `Register`; send-target syntax parser; adapter factory; no YAML bridge is registered despite the comment
- `gateway_env.go` — env steps for `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` and the home channel (creating a disabled platform entry when only the home is set); maps `SLACK_ALLOW_BOTS` onto `slack.allow_bots`; authz env names `SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS` and `SLACK_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`
- `adapter_hint.go` — `[data]` system-prompt hint: markdown is converted to Slack formatting, tables are unsupported, `MEDIA:` paths upload natively
- `log.go` — package logger named `gateway/platforms/slack`

#### Socket Mode transport, Web API client and connect

`Connect` requires both tokens (a missing one is a permanent fatal error), takes the scoped lock keyed on the app token, runs `auth.test` for every bot token to register a per-workspace client and bot identity (the first token is primary), registers listeners and starts the Socket Mode goroutine. A watchdog checks every 15 seconds and reconnects, without rebuilding adapter state, when the task exited, the transport reports disconnected, or no ping arrived for four ping intervals (60 second grace after connecting). Every envelope is acknowledged, including ones slack-go could not type.

- `adapter_socket.go` — the Bolt-like `slackApp` router (events by type or pattern, slash commands by pattern, block actions by id, pattern or constraints), the Socket Mode handler and ping tracking, watchdog and restart, workspace authentication with scope warnings, `Connect`, `Disconnect` (seals live streams), handoff thread creation by seed message
- `adapter_transport.go` — HTTP clients with the proxy pinned or environment-trusted, proxy resolution that skips unsupported schemes and `NO_PROXY` matches, and the cancellable Socket Mode goroutine type
- `adapter_client.go` — `webClient`: Web API call with JSON or query encoding, typed `slackAPIError` with headers and status, `files_upload_v2` delegated to slack-go, transient-error detection, an `IcebathAgent` user-agent prefix

#### Adapter state, text sends, edits, native streaming and task cards

The struct holds per-workspace clients and a dozen bounded caches (names, channel ownership, processed timestamps, mentioned threads, assistant threads, status lines, picker state). `Send` routes replies to a pending slash command privately through its `response_url` (at most five posts) with `chat.postEphemeral` as fallback, otherwise posts chunks to the channel or thread, with Block Kit only on a single-chunk message and thread broadcast (`reply_broadcast`) only on the first. A rejected Block Kit payload is retried as plain text. Draft streaming uses Slack's native `chat.startStream`, `chat.appendStream` and `chat.stopStream`, reopening a server-sealed stream once, sealing streams older than 15 minutes, and latching off for the process when Slack answers with a missing-scope or unknown-method error. Optional native task cards (`native_task_cards` under extra or `streaming.progress`) show plan progress as a Slack plan-mode stream.

- `adapter.go` — `SlackAdapter` struct, cache caps and constructor; workspace client selection; DM conversation opening for bare user ids; `Send`, `SendPrivateNotice`, `SendOrUpdateStatus`, `EditMessage` (Block Kit only on the final edit), `DeleteMessage`, `SendDraft` and stream commit, native task card start, update and stop, slash reply contexts with a 120 second lifetime

#### Inbound events, gating and content extraction

Listeners: `message` and `app_mention`, `reaction_added` and `reaction_removed`, `file_shared`, `app_home_opened`, `app_context_changed`, `assistant_thread_started` and `assistant_thread_context_changed`; anything else is logged and ignored. DMs are always processed unless `slack.disable_dms`. In channels the bot answers a mention, a wake-word pattern (`mention_patterns` in extra or `SLACK_MENTION_PATTERNS`), any message in a free-response channel (listed in `slack.free_response_channels`, or every channel when `slack.require_mention` is off), or an unmentioned reply in a thread it authored, was mentioned in, or has a live session for; `slack.strict_mention`, `slack.thread_require_mention`, `slack.require_mention_channels`, `slack.allowed_channels`, `slack.ignored_channels`, `slack.ignore_other_user_mentions` and `slack.thread_followup_silence` tighten that. Bot senders follow `slack.allow_bots`, with loop protection against peer agents and an `api_human_users` override. A typed `!command` is rewritten to the gateway slash form when the command is known. A reaction can be routed in as a synthetic message from the reactor (`slack.reaction_triggers`, optional `slack.reaction_trigger_target`). Assistant and agent-view lifecycle events seed a DM session, set up to four suggested prompts and title the thread from the first prompt.

- `adapter_inbound.go` — listener registration including plugin block-action handlers; assistant and agent-view lifecycle; reaction forwarding; the `file_shared` fallback for videos Slack never delivered as message files; the full message pipeline (prefilter of subtypes and `message_changed`, dedup, authorization early reject, channel gate, mention stripping, thread context hydration, name resolution, event build); file download and caching by kind with a 20 MB document cap, text inlining and Slack Connect file resolution
- `adapter_gating.go` — settings readers for every mention and channel gate, wake-word pattern compilation, detection of messages addressed to another user, and authenticated file download restricted to Slack CDN URLs with retry on timeouts
- `adapter_text.go` — text extraction from Block Kit rich text, tables and legacy attachments so content the plain `text` field omits reaches the agent; sanitised block serialisation; link-unfurl summaries; file markers; voice-clip detection; unfurl controls from `unfurl_links` and `unfurl_media`; markdown table alignment and fencing; dedup TTL from `SLACK_DEDUP_TTL_SECONDS`
- `adapter_reactions_context.go` — renders a message's reactions as a `name xcount` marker line inside fetched thread context

#### Threads as sessions, thread context and slash commands

A thread is a session. In channels a reply inside a thread uses that thread, and a top-level message opens its own thread session keyed on its ts unless `reply_in_thread` is false; in DMs each top-level message is its own thread session unless `dm_top_level_threads_as_sessions` is false. On the first message after a restart, and whenever messages were missed, prior thread messages are fetched with `conversations.replies` (1 then 2 second backoff on rate limits, 60 second cache) and injected as context past a per-session watermark; up to four images from the thread root are recovered. Slash commands: the listener matches `/icebath` plus every native slash name the manifest declares, acknowledges within three seconds, maps `/icebath <subcommand>` through the command registry, applies the same channel, DM and authorization gates as messages, and serialises slashes of one session so a later one never reaches the gateway first; commands that control a running turn (`approve`, `deny`, `pause`, interrupt-policy commands) bypass that lane.

- `adapter_threads.go` — thread context fetch, formatting and cache; thread parent text and root images; `handleIcebathCommand` and `handleSlashCommand`; slash context stash; thread session key and source; restart rehydration check; watermark read and write through session metadata; active-session lookup
- `adapter_slash_lane.go` — `SlashHandoffLanes`: per-session FIFO of handoff slots
- `adapter_slash_payload.go` — slash payload to gateway text (native slashes verbatim, `/icebath` subcommands mapped, `compact` aliased to `/compress`, empty text meaning `/help`) and thread anchor extraction; `SubcommandMap` is the injected registry reader

#### Outbound status, uploads, reactions, formatting and name resolution

"Typing" is the assistant thread status line, set through `agents.sessions.setStatus` (falling back to `assistant.threads.setStatus`) and cleared on stop. Files upload through `files_upload_v2` with retries on transient failures and a visible notice when an upload fails; images go ten per call. Processing reactions are `eyes`, then `white_check_mark` or `x` (`slack.reactions`). Markdown is converted to Slack mrkdwn with code protected, tables fenced and `@channel`-style broadcasts escaped; optional Block Kit rendering is off by default (`rich_blocks` for the local renderer, `markdown_blocks` for Slack's native markdown block).

- `adapter_outbound.go` — `SendTyping` and `StopTyping`, thread ts resolution, uploads and every media send method, `SendMultipleImages`, reactions and processing hooks, user and channel name caches, rewriting of user mentions to display names, the bot identity prompt line, assistant metadata caches, cron surface choice (`cron_continuable_surface`), `GetChatInfo`; optional feedback buttons (`feedback_buttons`)
- `adapter_static.go` — stateless helpers: `formatSlackMrkdwn`, cache eviction by timestamp, API and download error descriptions, workspace-scoped keys, native markdown and feedback block payloads, stream text bookkeeping, `users.info` parsing
- `block_kit.go` — `RenderBlocks`: markdown to Block Kit header, rich-text, list, quote, preformatted and table blocks; `SanitizeBlocks` clamps text objects and drops empty blocks to stay within Slack limits

#### Interactive Block Kit prompts

Buttons and selects posted as blocks, authorized per click through the gateway's access checks, with a double-click guard keyed by workspace and message ts. Action ids carry the `icebath_` prefix, and ids posted by an older build are mapped to the current ones.

- `adapter_interactive.go` — exec approval (`icebath_approve_once`, `_session`, `_always`, `icebath_deny`), slash confirmation (`icebath_confirm_once`, `_always`, `_cancel`), clarify with numbered choice buttons plus Other and card retirement, two-step provider then model picker with static selects, and the feedback action, which is `[partial]`: a click is acknowledged and logged but stored nowhere

#### Standalone sender

Out-of-process delivery for `icebath send` and cron.

- `adapter_standalone.go` — loads bot tokens from the env value and `slack_tokens.json`; `chat.postMessage` with mrkdwn formatting and thread ts; DM opening for user-id targets with a bounded cache; external-upload file sends; proxy-safe error text

#### Setup wizard, app manifest and CLI

`icebath slack manifest` prints or writes the Slack app manifest, and the setup wizard writes it to `<home>/slack-manifest.json` with paste instructions before collecting tokens.

- `setup.go` — `BuildFullManifest`: display info, one slash command per gateway command, bot scopes and event subscriptions, Socket Mode on, and the messaging experience (`assistant`, `agent` or `none`) adding the assistant view and events; the interactive wizard saving `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`, `SLACK_APP_TOKEN`, `SLACK_ALLOWED_USERS` and `SLACK_HOME_CHANNEL`
- `slack_cli.go` — `CmdSlack` and `ManifestCommand`: bot name, description, long-description file and messaging-experience options, output to stdout or a file, exit code 2 for input the manifest refuses

#### Fake Slack server

- `slacktest/server.go` — `[test-support]` loopback Slack Web API and Socket Mode fake, imported only by tests

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/a2a` — Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol v1.0: an inbound JSON-RPC server adapter plus five outbound client tools

*7 files, 4,205 Go lines*

A2A is the open inter-agent protocol (Agent Card discovery plus JSON-RPC tasks). This package makes icebath both a server and a client. The server side is a gateway platform named `a2a`: a plain `net/http` listener (default port 9900, `A2A_PORT`, `A2A_HOST`) that serves an Agent Card and routes each peer task into the live gateway session as a DM from user `a2a:<peer>`, so the answering agent is the operator's own session. The client side is five tools in the `a2a` toolset that call peers configured under the `a2a_agents` config key. It persists conversations to `a2a_conversations/<context>.jsonl` and an audit trail to `a2a_audit.jsonl` under the icebath home. Registered as bundled plugin `platforms/a2a`; implemented and wired. Port scaffolding is limited to Python exception and `urlopen` emulation in the HTTP and tool helpers.

#### Inbound server: agent routing, task lifecycle and HTTP surface

`A2AAdapter` binds the listener at connect and answers `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` (legacy `agent.json` too), `GET /health`, `GET /metrics` and JSON-RPC `POST`. One listener can serve several agents: the root agent is the live session, and extra agents from `platforms.a2a.extra.agents`, `a2a_served_agents` or `a2a.served_agents` get a path prefix, a tenant key and a target profile whose owner process receives the task through `gateway.ForwardToOwner`. A task is created, dispatched as a message event, and resolved by the final `Send` (only a `notify` send counts) or by `OnProcessingComplete`; a reply starting with `[INPUT_REQUIRED]` becomes the input-required state.

- `adapter.go` — `A2AAdapter`: served-agent table and tenant routing, Agent Card and advertised skills (`A2A_ADVERTISED_TOOLSETS`), task prepare, dispatch, await (`A2A_REPLY_TIMEOUT`, default 300 s) and finalize, the ten RPC handlers (`SendMessage`, `SendStreamingMessage`, `GetTask`, `ListTasks`, `CancelTask`, `SubscribeToTask`, four push-config methods, each with legacy slash aliases), retry de-duplication by message id, orphan watchdog every 60 s, signed push-notification POST
- `adapter_http.go` — per-request handler: Host-header guard in tokenless mode, ordered POST checks (auth, browser-origin refusal, 1 MiB body cap, `A2A-Version`, tenant route, rate limit, trusted peer, method), SSE writer with 5 s keepalive comments (status `submitted`, `working`, then the terminal event; no token streaming), and the `urlopen`-style redirect-limited POST used for push callbacks

#### Protocol objects, task store, limits and conversation log

- `protocol.go` — Agent Card builder (JSONRPC interface, bearer scheme, provider from `A2A_PROVIDER_ORG` and `A2A_PROVIDER_URL`), JSON-RPC envelopes and error codes, task, status and artifact objects, SSE framing; `TaskStore` (in memory, scoped by agent and tenant, 500 terminal tasks kept, push configs, watches); `TurnTracker` anti-loop cap (`A2A_MAX_PINGPONG_TURNS`, default 5, hard max 20, 1 h TTL); `RateLimiter` (60 per minute per identity, `A2A_RATE_LIMIT`); shared `Metrics`; JSONL conversation persistence and replay

#### Authentication, trust and content safety

Security defaults are easy to lose: with neither `A2A_BEARER_TOKEN` nor `A2A_PEER_TOKENS` set the server binds 127.0.0.1 regardless of `A2A_HOST` and refuses browser-originated POSTs.
