- `security.go` — profile-scoped `A2ASecurityContext`: shared bearer token, per-peer tokens (`alice:tok1,bob:tok2`) compared in constant time, trusted peers from `A2A_TRUSTED_PEERS` or `a2a.trusted_peers`, bind-host resolution, HMAC push signature in `X-A2A-Signature` (`A2A_PUSH_SECRET`), prompt-injection marker filter and the untrusted-peer framing prefix on inbound text, credential and e-mail redaction on outbound text, SSRF check for callback URLs, audit-line writer

#### Outbound client tools

- `tools.go` — `a2a_discover` (fetch and summarize a peer's card), `a2a_call` (one `SendMessage`, optional context id), `a2a_list` (configured peers, persisted conversations, metrics), `a2a_history` (replay a stored conversation), `a2a_orchestrate` (fan one task out to peers matched by capability, at most 6 workers); peers resolve from `a2a_agents` (url, bearer auth, timeout default 120 s, capabilities, tenant) or a literal URL; tools are gated on `a2a_agents` being set or the platform being enabled; carries Python exception emulation for error text

#### Registration and setup

- `register.go` — plugin manifest, platform spec (`A2A_ALLOWED_USERS`, `A2A_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `A2A_HOME_CHANNEL`, `/update` disabled), the model-facing platform hint, and the `icebath gateway setup` flow asking for port, advertised name and peer tokens
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/bluebubbles` — iMessage through a BlueBubbles macOS server (REST out, registered webhook in)

*6 files, 1,677 Go lines*

Talks to a user-run BlueBubbles server: outbound over its REST API under `/api/v1`, inbound through a webhook this adapter registers with the server at connect and removes at disconnect. Credentials are `BLUEBUBBLES_SERVER_URL` and `BLUEBUBBLES_PASSWORD` (or `server_url` and `password` in the platform extra); listener address, port (8645), path (`/bluebubbles-webhook`), read receipts, `require_mention` and wake patterns come from `bluebubbles.*` settings. Typing, read receipts and tapbacks work only when the server reports the Private API helper as connected. Implemented and wired; no edits, no streaming, no threads.

#### Adapter core, REST client and text send

- `adapter.go` — `BlueBubblesAdapter`: server probe (`/ping`, `/server/info`), webhook listener bind and self-registration for `new-message` and `updated-message` with the password in the callback URL, reuse of a registration left by an unclean exit, chat GUID resolution with a 500-entry cache, new-chat creation for an unknown address, text send as one bubble per paragraph (4000 character cap, pagination suffixes stripped), tapback reactions (six fixed kinds), group wake-word matching with defaults `icebath` and `icebath agent`

#### Inbound webhook

- `inbound.go` — authenticates the callback by the password token, accepts JSON or form bodies up to 1 MiB, drops own messages and tapback events, derives chat GUID, identifier and sender across payload shapes, treats `;+;` GUIDs as groups, applies `require_mention`, downloads attachments, dispatches the event and fires a read receipt

#### Media, typing and read state

- `media.go` — multipart attachment upload for images, voice, video and documents with the caption as a follow-up text, remote images cached first, typing start and stop and mark-read through the Private API, attachment download into the media cache

#### Registration, env bridge and setup

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec, one-shot standalone sender for cron, and the setup wizard (server URL, password, allowlist, home chat, webhook port)
- `gateway_env.go` — env-to-config bridge and authorization env names (`BLUEBUBBLES_ALLOWED_USERS`, `BLUEBUBBLES_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `BLUEBUBBLES_HOME_CHANNEL`)
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/buzz` — Buzz (Block's Nostr-based human-and-agent workspace) through the `buzz` CLI and a relay websocket

*8 files, 4,263 Go lines*

Buzz is a community relay built on Nostr. The adapter needs the external `buzz` CLI binary (`BUZZ_CLI_PATH` or PATH): every relay operation except live receive shells out to it with JSON in and out (`users get`, `channels list|get|members`, `dms list`, `messages get|send|edit|delete`, `reactions add`, `media get`). Inbound uses a relay websocket with NIP-42 authentication, falling back to CLI polling. Identity is a Nostr private key (`BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY`, nsec or hex, or a credentials file). Read positions persist in `buzz/channel-cursors.json` under the home. Implemented and wired; typing is a no-op.

#### Adapter core and outbound

- `adapter.go` — `BuzzAdapter`: config (`BUZZ_RELAY_URL`, `BUZZ_CHANNELS`, `BUZZ_POLL_INTERVAL`, `BUZZ_REQUIRE_MENTION` default on, `BUZZ_TRANSPORT` auto, websocket or poll, `BUZZ_REACTION_ONLY_USERS`), connect sequence (own profile, identity lock per relay and pubkey, channel list, cursor restore, DM discovery, transport choice), text send with reply and thread arguments and mention resolution retries, reactions, edit, delete, file attachments for image, document, video and voice, chat info
- `helpers.go` — constants and pure helpers: relay media URL recognition and localization, bech32 npub and hex conversion, CLI path resolution and execution with a 30 s timeout, bounded CLI error text, send-receipt parsing, NIP-10 reply-parent and thread-root extraction, attachment filename sanitizing

#### Inbound: websocket subscription and poll fallback

- `inbound.go` — websocket loop (auth within 20 s, per-channel subscriptions for kinds 9, 45001 and 45003, a membership subscription for kind 44100, ping every 20 s, 300 s idle timeout), CLI poll loop (4 s default, DM discovery every fifth round), event handling with seen-id dedup, DM versus channel classification, mention and addressing gate, NIP-94 `imeta` attachments (at most 4, 20 MiB each) downloaded by direct HTTPS GET from the relay's origin without following redirects and verified against their SHA-256, relay media links inside message text localized through the authenticated CLI for authorized senders, display-name lookup, dispatch with an acknowledging reaction
- `buzz_cursors.go` — `CursorStore`: per-channel high-water mark and last 500 seen ids, keyed to identity and relay, loaded at connect and written after changes
- `nostr_auth.go` — self-contained secp256k1 BIP-340 Schnorr signing, nsec decoding and the kind 22242 relay auth event, plus parsing of the owner attestation tag

#### Registration, credentials and setup

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec, scoped setting lookup, reply mode (`BUZZ_REPLY_TO_MODE` first, all or off; `BUZZ_REPLY_IN_THREAD`), owner attestation validation (`BUZZ_AUTH_TAG`), env seeding, standalone sender that runs `messages send` once
- `setup.go` — private-key resolution from `BUZZ_PRIVATE_KEY`, `BUZZ_CREDENTIALS_FILE` or the CLI's own credential records, and the setup wizard
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/dingtalk` — DingTalk bot over Stream Mode, replying by session webhook or streaming AI cards

*10 files, 3,083 Go lines*

Connects with an app's Client ID and Secret (`DINGTALK_CLIENT_ID`, `DINGTALK_CLIENT_SECRET`). Inbound arrives on a websocket opened through the DingTalk gateway; the stream client is hand-written in this package to mirror the Python `dingtalk-stream` SDK. Replies go to the per-message session webhook as markdown, or, when `card_template_id` is configured, to an AI card that is created, delivered and then updated in place, which is the only path that supports edits and streaming. Session webhook replies cannot upload local files, so outbound media is limited to remote images rendered inline. Implemented and wired.

#### Adapter: gating, send, cards and reactions

- `adapter.go` — `DingTalkAdapter`: stream supervision (backoff 2, 5, 10, 30, 60 s; five identical errors trip a 300 s circuit breaker; repeated SDK log lines collapsed), dedup, allowlist by sender or staff id, group rules (allowed chats as a hard gate, free-response chats, at-mention or wake-word patterns), session webhook cache (500 entries, expiry aware, host must be `api` or `oapi.dingtalk.com`), markdown send with renderer fixes, AI card create, deliver and streaming update, thinking and done emotion reactions, download-code resolution for inbound media; local image and document sends return an explicit unsupported error; 20,000 character limit

#### Stream client and OpenAPI client

- `stream.go` — Stream Mode client: opens a connection via `/v1.0/gateway/connections/open`, serves the websocket with keepalive, routes callback frames for topic `/v1.0/im/bot/messages/get` to a handler, acknowledges each frame, fetches the app access token from `/v1.0/oauth2/accessToken`
- `openapi.go` — OpenAPI calls with the app token: card instance create, deliver and streaming update, robot emotion reply and recall, message file download; `DINGTALK_OPENAPI_ENDPOINT` overrides the base

#### Inbound message model

- `message.go` — maps a callback payload onto `IncomingMessage` the way the SDK does, keeping unmapped fields
- `inbound.go` — text extraction across text, rich text, card and interactive card shapes, media reference extraction and message typing, collection of download codes to resolve

#### Registration, QR onboarding and setup

- `dingtalk_auth.go` — device-flow app registration: begins a registration, renders the verification URL as a terminal QR code and polls until success, expiry or timeout (`DINGTALK_REGISTRATION_BASE_URL`, `DINGTALK_REGISTRATION_SOURCE`)
- `setup.go` — setup wizard offering the QR scan or manual Client ID and Secret entry
- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec and the standalone sender, which posts to a static robot webhook (`DINGTALK_WEBHOOK_URL`) because session webhooks are unreachable outside a live conversation
- `gateway_env.go` — env bridge and authorization env names (`DINGTALK_ALLOWED_USERS`, `DINGTALK_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `DINGTALK_HOME_CHANNEL`)
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/email` — e-mail as a chat platform: polled IMAP in, SMTP out

*5 files, 1,795 Go lines*

One mailbox (`EMAIL_ADDRESS`, `EMAIL_PASSWORD`, `EMAIL_IMAP_HOST`, `EMAIL_SMTP_HOST`) acts as the bot. Each sender address is a chat. The adapter polls IMAP for unseen mail (`EMAIL_POLL_INTERVAL`, default 15 s) and sends threaded replies over SMTP. It runs on the `pyimaplib`, `pysmtplib` and `pyemail` emulation packages. Sender authorization is strict by default and is the part most easily lost. Implemented and wired; no typing, edits or reactions.

#### Adapter: polling, authorization and threaded replies

- `adapter.go` — `EmailAdapter`: IMAP and SMTP connections with `tls`, `starttls` or `plain` security and optional verification bypass (`EMAIL_IMAP_SECURITY`, `EMAIL_SMTP_SECURITY`, `EMAIL_*_TLS_VERIFY`, ports 993 and 587), connect-time probes, seen-UID baseline that survives adapter recreation (capped at 2000), header-only preflight before any body fetch, sender gate (self mail, automated senders, allowlist or pairing, From authentication), reply with `In-Reply-To`, `References`, a `Re:` subject and an `icebath-` Message-ID, file attachments, image URLs as body lines, multi-image batches
- `parse.go` — RFC 2047 header decoding, plain-text body extraction with HTML stripping, automated-sender detection, attachment caching, and `verifySenderAuthentication`, which trusts only the first `Authentication-Results` header of the pinned server (`EMAIL_AUTHSERV_ID`) and requires DMARC pass or aligned SPF or DKIM unless `EMAIL_TRUST_FROM_HEADER` is set

#### Registration and env bridge

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec (50,000 character limit, home target `EMAIL_HOME_ADDRESS`), platform hint, one-shot SMTP standalone sender
- `gateway_env.go` — env bridge and authorization env names (`EMAIL_ALLOWED_USERS`, `EMAIL_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`)
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/feishu` — Feishu and Lark bot over the official lark SDK, plus a document-comment agent and meeting invites

*17 files, 8,859 Go lines*

The largest adapter in this slice. It connects with `FEISHU_APP_ID` and `FEISHU_APP_SECRET` to Feishu (China) or Lark (international, chosen by the `feishu.domain` setting) through `larksuite/oapi-sdk-go`, receiving events over the SDK websocket or over a signed webhook (the `feishu.connection_mode` setting; webhook mode refuses to start without a verification token or encrypt key). Beyond chat it runs a second, separate feature: when someone comments on a Feishu document and mentions the bot, a dedicated agent turn answers inside the comment thread using the Feishu doc and drive tools. It persists inbound dedup ids in `feishu_seen_message_ids.json`, comment access rules in `feishu_comment_rules.json` and comment pairing approvals in `feishu_comment_pairing.json` under the home. Implemented and wired; the comment agent's runner is injected from `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go`.

#### Adapter lifecycle, settings and transports

- `adapter.go` — `FeishuAdapterSettings` (group policy, per-chat `group_rules` with policy, allowlist, blacklist and `require_mention`, admins, bot identity, batching and dedup sizes from `ICEBATH_FEISHU_*`, webhook host, port 8765 and path `/feishu/webhook`, websocket ping and reconnect overrides), event handler registration, connect with three attempts under a per-app-id lock, blocking-call executor (10 workers), disconnect teardown, persisted 24 h dedup of 2048 ids
- `ws.go` — wraps the SDK websocket client: applies reconnect nonce, interval and ping overrides by reflection into unexported SDK fields, tracks inbound byte activity for liveness, supervises and stops the run
- `adapter_webhook.go` — webhook mode: 1 MiB body cap, 120 requests per minute per remote address, verification-token and SHA-256 signature checks (timestamp, nonce, encrypt key, body), URL-verification challenge, per-address anomaly counting, dispatch to the same handlers as the websocket
- `sdk.go` — `larkAPI` interface over the SDK calls the adapter makes (messages, chats, images, files, reactions, users, application, raw tenant requests), client construction per domain, slog-backed SDK logger, interactive card and button builders

#### Inbound pipeline

Events handled: message receive, message read, reaction created and deleted, card action, bot added to or removed from a chat, P2P chat entered, message recalled, `drive.notice.comment_add_v1` and `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1`.

- `adapter_inbound.go` — event queueing until the adapter is ready, admission (self echo, bot-sender policy `FEISHU_ALLOW_BOTS`, DM allowlist, group policy and mention requirement), text debounce (0.6 s, 8 messages, 4000 characters) and media batching (0.8 s), per-chat locks, media and file download with small text files inlined, reply-context lookup, sender-name cache, card-action validation and dedup for approval and update prompts, reactions turned into synthetic events, Typing and CrossMark processing reactions, bot identity discovery
- `normalize.go` — converts Feishu message payloads to text plus resources: post rich text to markdown, merge-forward bundles, shared chats, interactive cards, media references and mentions; also builds outbound markdown post payloads
- `feishu_admission_diagnostics.go` — one-time warning text when group traffic is dropped by the untouched empty-allowlist default

#### Outbound

- `adapter_send.go` — chunked text or markdown post with plain-text fallback, edit and delete, reply and thread routing with fallback when the reply target was withdrawn, three send attempts, image, file, video and Opus voice upload (other audio transcoded, duration read from the Ogg stream), remote image download behind the SSRF guard, exec-approval card and update-prompt card with resolved-state replacements, the update answer written to `.update_response`; no typing indicator exists; 8000 character limit
- `adapter_hint.go` — model-facing platform hint text

#### Document-comment agent

A drive comment event is parsed, checked against the comment rules, expanded into a prompt (document metadata, a selected comment timeline, referenced documents with wiki resolution), run as one agent turn with a per-document session history (50 messages, 1 h TTL), and the reply is posted back in 4000-character chunks; `NO_REPLY` suppresses a reply.

- `feishu_comment.go` — comment event handling end to end: drive and wiki API calls with retries, reaction on the triggering reply, prompt builders for local (quoted-text) and whole-document comments, session history, reply delivery with fallback to a whole-document comment, and the `CommentAgentRunner` hook
- `feishu_comment_rules.go` — access rules for the comment agent (enabled flag, `allowlist` or `pairing` policy, per-document and wildcard rules, mtime-cached JSON files) and the `icebath feishu comment-rules` command (`status`, `check`, `pairing add|remove|list`)
- `feishuclient/feishuclient.go` — context carrier that hands the adapter's lark client to the Feishu doc and drive tools in `pkg/tools` during a comment turn

#### Meeting invites

- `feishu_meeting_invite.go` — parses a `vc.bot.meeting_invited_v1` event and routes it to the gateway as a synthetic DM from the inviter with a prompt asking the agent to join the meeting

#### Registration, env bridge and onboarding

- `setup.go` — QR onboarding: device-code app registration against the Feishu or Lark accounts host, terminal QR rendering, polling, bot probe, then the setup wizard for credentials, connection mode, policies and home chat
- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec, standalone sender that builds a transient adapter and sends text then each media file by kind, and registration of the `feishu` CLI command
- `gateway_env.go` — env bridge (`FEISHU_ENCRYPT_KEY`, `FEISHU_VERIFICATION_TOKEN`, `FEISHU_HOME_CHANNEL`) and authorization env names including `FEISHU_ALLOW_BOTS`
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/googlechat` — Google Chat app: Pub/Sub pull or authenticated HTTP events in, Chat REST API out

*11 files, 4,135 Go lines*

Authenticates as a service account (`GOOGLE_CHAT_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` as a path or inline JSON, else application default credentials). Inbound is either a Cloud Pub/Sub subscription pulled over REST (`GOOGLE_CHAT_PROJECT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CHAT_SUBSCRIPTION`) or Google-signed HTTP callbacks (`GOOGLE_CHAT_HTTP_EVENTS_URL`); the HTTP route itself is mounted by `pkg/gatewayapi/routes.go`, which calls `VerifyHTTPEventRequest` and `DispatchHTTPEvent`. All Google calls are hand-written REST with no Google client library. Native file attachments require a per-user OAuth token, obtained through the in-chat `/setup-files` command or the `icebath google_chat oauth` CLI. State files under the home: `google_chat_bot_id.json`, `google_chat_thread_counts.json`, `google_chat_user_token.json`, `google_chat_user_tokens/`, `google_chat_user_client_secret.json` and pending OAuth state. Platform key is `google_chat`. Implemented and wired.

#### Adapter lifecycle and Pub/Sub intake

- `adapter.go` — `GoogleChatAdapter`: settings snapshot, credential load, subscription check, pull supervisor with jittered exponential backoff (2 s to 120 s, fatal after 10 attempts) and flow control (`GOOGLE_CHAT_MAX_MESSAGES`, `GOOGLE_CHAT_MAX_BYTES`), envelope parsing in both event formats, self-message filter and dedup, bot user id resolution from the home space or `GOOGLE_CHAT_BOOTSTRAP_SPACES` with an on-disk cache
- `api.go` — REST client: message create, patch and delete, space and member reads, media download and upload, Pub/Sub get, pull, acknowledge and nack, three-attempt retry on transient errors, error redaction of resource paths and service-account e-mails, Google ID-token verification against cached certificates
- `credentials.go` — service-account loading with classified errors and a guard against borrowing another profile's default credentials, plus the persisted per-space thread counter behind the DM thread heuristic

#### Outbound, typing marker and attachments

- `outbound.go` — message event construction with attachment caching, HTTP event verification and dispatch, markdown conversion and 4000-character chunking, thread resolution, a visible thinking message that the first reply chunk patches (typing substitute) with cleanup of stranded markers, edit and delete, clarify prompt card, inline image links, native upload of image, document, audio and video as the requesting user with a setup notice when no user token is usable
- `cards.go` — markdown to Google Chat dialect conversion with code protected, and the card-spec to Cards v2 renderer (headers, text, code, decorated text, images, buttons, selection inputs)
- `interactive.go` — exec-approval and slash-confirm cards, card click parsing across add-on and classic event shapes, clicker authorization, settled-card replacement, synchronous or patched click answers

#### User OAuth for attachments

- `oauth.go` — per-user OAuth with PKCE: client secret storage, consent URL, code exchange, token refresh and persistence with owner-only permissions, token listing, status check and revoke
- `setup_files.go` — the in-chat `/setup-files` flow, intercepted before the agent sees the message

#### Registration and setup

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec (`GOOGLE_CHAT_ALLOWED_USERS`, `GOOGLE_CHAT_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `GOOGLE_CHAT_HOME_CHANNEL`), env enablement, standalone sender, the `icebath google_chat oauth` command and platform hint
- `setup.go` — setup wizard with a GCP walkthrough, writing project, subscription, allowlist and home space to the home `.env`
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/homeassistant` — Home Assistant: state-change events in, notifications out, and four smart-home tools

*7 files, 3,079 Go lines*

Unlike the other packages this one is not a bundled plugin: it registers with `plugins.RegisterPort` as the compiled-in port of the `homeassistant` catalog plugin and becomes active only after `icebath plugins install homeassistant`. It talks to a Home Assistant instance with a long-lived token (`HASS_TOKEN`, `HASS_URL`, default `http://homeassistant.local:8123`). The adapter subscribes to `state_changed` on the websocket API and forwards filtered changes as messages in one event channel; agent replies become persistent notifications. Independently of the adapter it registers four tools in the `homeassistant` toolset. Two files are Python and aiohttp emulation. Implemented and wired.

#### Event adapter

- `adapter.go` — `HomeAssistantAdapter`: websocket auth and `subscribe_events`, reconnect backoff 5, 10, 30, 60 s, filters closed by default (`watch_domains`, `watch_entities`, `ignore_entities`, `watch_all`), per-entity cooldown (`cooldown_seconds`, default 30), per-domain message templates, replies posted to `persistent_notification/create` over REST, macOS local-network hint on LAN refusal; 4096 character limit
- `standalone.go` — cron delivery through a notify service: the target's own `notify.<service>` when it names one, the grouped `notify/notify` otherwise

#### Smart-home tools

- `tools.go` — `ha_list_entities` (domain and area filters, registry lookups over the websocket), `ha_get_state`, `ha_list_services` and `ha_call_service`; operator entity filters (`HASS_ENTITY_ALLOWLIST`, `HASS_ENTITY_DENYLIST`, `HASS_MAX_ENTITIES`), a fixed blocklist of code-executing service domains (`shell_command`, `python_script`, `hassio` and others), target validation

#### Registration

- `register.go` — port manifest read from the catalog tree, platform spec (trusted inbound, `HASS_HOME_CHANNEL`, shared `HASS_` env prefix), env enablement, tool registration
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Python and aiohttp emulation

- `http.go` — `[py-shim]` aiohttp session stand-in: error classes, charset and JSON content-type rules, gzip and zstd body decoding, TLS failure tracing; used by the adapter and the tools
- `pyval.go` — `[py-shim]` Python dict, set, int and iteration semantics over decoded config and JSON values, used to reproduce Python error behaviour on malformed config

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/irc` — IRC client over one TCP or TLS connection

*5 files, 1,489 Go lines*

A dependency-free IRC client. Config: `IRC_SERVER`, `IRC_PORT` (default 6697), `IRC_USE_TLS`, `IRC_NICKNAME` (default `icebath-bot`), `IRC_CHANNEL`, optional `IRC_SERVER_PASSWORD` and `IRC_NICKSERV_PASSWORD`. Text only: no media, typing or edits. Implemented and wired.

#### Adapter

- `adapter.go` — `IRCAdapter`: registration (PASS, NICK, USER), nick-collision retry with a numeric suffix, NickServ IDENTIFY, JOIN, PING replies, `CAP REQ message-tags` so server msgids enable `+draft/react` reactions; inbound PRIVMSG gate (channel messages must address the bot's nick, DMs pass, CTCP handled, nick allowlist); outbound markdown stripped and split to the 510-byte line budget and the 450 character limit with 300 ms flood pacing; identity lock; lost stream becomes a retryable fatal error
- `standalone.go` — one-shot connect, register, optional join and PRIVMSG for cron, with CR, LF and NUL stripped from the text to block command injection

#### Registration and setup

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec (`IRC_ALLOWED_USERS`, `IRC_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `IRC_HOME_CHANNEL`), env enablement, platform hint
- `setup.go` — setup wizard writing server, identity, auth and access settings to the home `.env`
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/line` — LINE Messaging API: signed webhook in, reply-token or push out

*8 files, 1,922 Go lines*

Uses `line-bot-sdk-go` with `LINE_CHANNEL_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `LINE_CHANNEL_SECRET`. LINE replies are free only through a single-use reply token that expires in about a minute, so the adapter is built around token economics: it answers with the reply token when it can, pushes (metered) otherwise, and for slow turns sends a button the user taps to fetch the finished answer with a fresh token. Outbound media must be reachable by public HTTPS URL, so the adapter serves local files itself. Implemented and wired; no documents out, no edits, no reactions.

#### Adapter and webhook

- `adapter.go` — `LineAdapter`: config (`LINE_HOST`, `LINE_PORT` default 8646, `LINE_PUBLIC_URL`, `LINE_SLOW_RESPONSE_THRESHOLD` default 45 s, pending, delivered, interrupted and expired texts, user, group and room allowlists), listener with routes `/line/webhook`, its `/health` and `/line/media/{token}/{filename}`, reply-token stash (50 s TTL), loading animation as the typing indicator, slow-response postback firing and interruption handling
- `inbound.go` — webhook handler: 1 MiB cap, `X-Line-Signature` check, redelivery and self-echo drop, source allowlists, text, image, video, audio, file, sticker and location messages with media fetched from the data API, postback events
- `protocol.go` — constants and pure logic: HMAC-SHA256 signature verification, markdown stripping that keeps URLs tappable, splitting into at most five bubbles of 5000 characters, `RequestCache` (pending, ready, error, delivered) for the postback flow, chat resolution, button-template builder

#### Outbound

- `outbound.go` — text send that either fills a pending postback entry or goes on the wire, five messages per call with reply token first and push for the rest, local media registered under expiring tokens (30 minutes) and served by URL, size caps (image 10 MB, audio and video 200 MB), image, voice and video sends with a generated preview image
- `client.go` — SDK-backed client: reply, push, loading animation, content download, bot user id, with a 15 s timeout and proxy-safe error text

#### Registration and setup

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec (4500 character limit), env enablement, platform hint, standalone sender that pushes text only and reports media as undeliverable
- `setup.go` — setup wizard for the two channel credentials
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/matrix` — Matrix on any homeserver via mautrix, with optional end-to-end encryption

*19 files, 5,456 Go lines*

Logs in with `MATRIX_ACCESS_TOKEN` or `MATRIX_PASSWORD` against `MATRIX_HOMESERVER` and runs a sync loop. End-to-end encryption exists only in binaries built with the `goolm` tag (the Makefile and release config set it); without the tag `e2ee_plain.go` compiles instead and encrypted rooms are skipped or refuse connection depending on mode. Crypto state lives in a SQLite store at `platforms/matrix/store/crypto.db` under the profile home. Room policy comes from `matrix.*` settings (allowed rooms, free-response rooms, require mention, auto thread, ignore patterns, max message length, session scope). Implemented and wired, except four exported room-management methods nothing calls. One coupling to note: bang-command recognition uses `IsGatewayKnownCommand`, which `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go` points at the Slack package's function.

#### Adapter state and connection

- `adapter.go` — `MatrixAdapter` construction from config and scoped env, store directory pinning, event dedup, thread mention option parsing, HTTP client with `MATRIX_PROXY`, typing start and stop, chat info, diagnostics snapshot (`GetDiagnostics`, `[unwired]`), text batch delay
- `connect.go` — connect sequence: authenticate by token (`whoami`) or password login, E2EE setup, handler registration, full initial sync seeding joined rooms and the DM cache, then the sync loop; disconnect; per-sync handler batching; warning when encrypted events are dropped

#### End-to-end encryption and device verification

- `e2ee_goolm.go` — build tag `goolm`: Olm machine over the SQLite crypto store, Megolm encrypt with on-demand group session sharing, decrypt with session requests, device-key upload and server re-verification, store reset when the token's device changed, pickle-key migration from a legacy key and removal of a legacy pickle file, cross-signing verification with `MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY` or bootstrap of a new recovery key; `optional` mode degrades, `required` mode refuses to connect
- `e2ee_plain.go` — build without the tag: reports no Olm implementation; optional mode continues unencrypted, required mode refuses to connect
- `e2ee_build.go` — the build command string and the "built without Matrix encryption" fact text
- `e2ee_version.go` — the Matrix E2EE line of `icebath --version` output

#### Inbound

- `inbound.go` — message gating (self, appservice and bridge senders, allowed rooms with DMs exempt, 5 s startup grace with a clock-skew warning), reply-context extraction, text and media handling with encrypted attachment decryption, invite handling and background auto-join with a DM signal, member events
- `rooms.go` — room identity resolution with joined-member count as the DM signal and a TTL cache, `m.direct` cache, display names, read receipts, redaction; also `CreateRoom`, `InviteUser` and `SetPresence`, which are `[unwired]`
- `voice_mention.go` — parks a voice message that arrived without a mention for up to 120 s so a following bare mention from the same sender can claim it (at most 4 per sender)

#### Outbound, formatting and reaction prompts

- `send.go` — text send in UTF-8 byte-bounded chunks with one retry after a key share, edit by `m.replace`, handoff thread seed, external image download with redirect and size guards, image, document, voice and video upload (encrypted upload in encrypted rooms, `MATRIX_MAX_MEDIA_BYTES` default 100 MiB), exec-approval prompt and model and choice pickers presented as seeded reactions
- `reactions.go` — reaction send and redact, eyes, check and cross processing reactions (`MATRIX_REACTIONS`), reaction-driven resolution of approval prompts and pickers with reactor validation (`MATRIX_APPROVAL_REQUIRE_SENDER`) and expiry (`MATRIX_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`)
- `format.go` — markdown to sanitized Matrix HTML (goldmark, tag and attribute allowlist), outbound mention pills and room-mention gating (`MATRIX_ALLOW_ROOM_MENTIONS`), bot-mention detection and stripping, `mxc` to HTTP URL
- `helpers.go` — voice metadata (duration and MSC1767 waveform through ffprobe and ffmpeg), bang-command to slash-command rewriting, reply-fallback stripping, E2EE mode resolution (`MATRIX_E2EE_MODE`, `MATRIX_ENCRYPTION`), recovery-key output file (`MATRIX_RECOVERY_KEY_OUTPUT_FILE`, written once with mode 0600), LaTeX to math markup, limits (45,000 byte event content, default 15,000 character messages)
- `adapter_hint.go` — model-facing platform hint text

#### Registration, env bridge and setup

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec, `room:$event` target syntax for thread sends
- `standalone.go` — cron delivery without a running gateway: plain `m.room.message` events PUT to the Client-Server API in UTF-8 bounded chunks with HTML attached; it has no encryption path
- `setup.go` — setup wizard for homeserver, auth, E2EE, allowlist and home room
- `gateway_env.go` — env bridge (`MATRIX_HOME_ROOM`, E2EE mode mapping) and the settings that `MATRIX_ALLOWED_USERS`, `MATRIX_HOMESERVER`, `MATRIX_USER_ID` and `MATRIX_DEVICE_ID` moved to
- `log.go` — package logger

*6 files, 1,793 Go lines*

Works with a self-hosted or cloud server using a bot token (`MATTERMOST_TOKEN`) and the `mattermost.url` setting. Inbound is the `/api/v4/websocket` stream; outbound is REST. Channel policy comes from settings (require mention, free-response channels, allowed channels). Implemented and wired.

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/ntfy` — ntfy push notifications: topic stream in, one POST per reply out

Subscribes to a topic on `ntfy.sh` or a self-hosted server (`NTFY_TOPIC`, `NTFY_SERVER_URL`) and publishes replies to the same or another topic (`NTFY_PUBLISH_TOPIC`). ntfy has no user identity, so a topic is treated as a single trusted channel. Text only. Implemented and wired.

#### Adapter and registration

- `adapter.go` — `NtfyAdapter`: streaming `GET <server>/<topic>/json` with incremental line decoding, reconnect backoff, 401 and 404 treated as fatal, dedup (300 s, 1000 ids), own messages recognized by the `icebath-agent` tag, publish with Bearer or Basic auth from `NTFY_TOKEN`, optional markdown header (`NTFY_MARKDOWN`), body truncated at 4096 characters
- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec (`NTFY_ALLOWED_USERS`, `NTFY_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `NTFY_HOME_CHANNEL`), env enablement, standalone publisher, platform hint

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/photon` — iMessage through Photon's managed Spectrum service, via a supervised Node sidecar

*10 files, 4,778 Go lines*

Photon Spectrum is a hosted iMessage line service. The adapter does not speak to it directly: it spawns and supervises a Node.js sidecar (running `spectrum-ts`, shipped as an embedded file tree and mirrored to `photon/sidecar` under the home, with `npm install` run on demand) and talks to that sidecar over loopback HTTP on port 8789 with a per-run token header. Credentials are a Spectrum project id and secret (`PHOTON_PROJECT_ID`, `PHOTON_PROJECT_SECRET`) obtained through `icebath photon setup`, which runs a device login against the Photon dashboard. State under the home: `auth.json` entries for the dashboard token and project, and the `photon-sidecar.json` runtime record. Implemented and wired; the sidecar's own source is outside this slice.

#### Adapter, sidecar supervision and inbound stream

- `adapter.go` — `PhotonAdapter`: sidecar spawn (managed or `PHOTON_NODE_BIN` Node, dependency install and refresh, orphan cleanup on the port, readiness on `/healthz`), stop by stdin EOF, `/shutdown` then signal, exit monitoring, liveness probes (`PHOTON_PROBE_*`) with respawn; NDJSON `/inbound` stream with reconnect, dedup (4000 ids, 48 h), content normalization (attachments cached, group content, rich-link previews suppressed for 30 s after a URL-only message, a wait for attachment placeholders), group mention gate (`PHOTON_REQUIRE_MENTION`, `PHOTON_MENTION_PATTERNS`)
- `sidecar_paths.go` — chooses the sidecar directory (`PHOTON_SIDECAR_DIR`, a writable source tree, else the home mirror), copies changed files while leaving `node_modules`, detects a lockfile newer than the install marker, locates the npm error log
- `sidecar_embed.go` — writes the compiled-in sidecar tree to the home mirror
- `sidecar_proc_unix.go`, `sidecar_proc_windows.go` — per-OS signalling: process-group SIGTERM or SIGKILL on Unix, process termination and a hidden console window on Windows

#### Outbound

- `outbound.go` — sidecar calls for text (`/send`, markdown when `PHOTON_MARKDOWN` allows, a URL-only message tried as a rich link first), native polls for clarify prompts, attachments and voice notes, typing with a 5 s cooldown, reactions and their removal on the latest inbound message, retry classification of upstream-overload errors, plain-text fallback; standalone sender that reuses a running sidecar through its runtime record; 8000 character limit

#### Dashboard auth and provisioning

- `auth.go` — RFC 8628 device login against the Photon dashboard with token extraction across response shapes and validation, token and project credential storage (auth file plus profile `.env`), project lookup, creation and secret regeneration, Spectrum user registration by E.164 number, iMessage line lookup and provisioning, opt-in polling, status tables with secrets masked
- `cli.go` — after setup, allowlists the operator's number and makes it the cron home channel when those keys are unset

#### Registration and CLI

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec (`PHOTON_ALLOWED_USERS`, `PHOTON_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`, `PHOTON_HOME_CHANNEL`), env enablement from stored credentials, and the `icebath photon` command with `setup`, `status`, `install-sidecar` and `telemetry [on|off]`
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/qqbot` — official QQ Bot API v2: websocket gateway in, REST out

*14 files, 4,494 Go lines*

Authenticates with `QQ_APP_ID` and `QQ_CLIENT_SECRET`, exchanges them for an app access token, opens the gateway websocket and handles C2C, group at-message, guild channel, guild DM and button-interaction events. Outbound text, markdown, inline keyboards and rich media go over REST to `api.sgroup.qq.com`. Voice messages are transcribed before the agent sees them. Access is governed by `dm_policy` and `group_policy` (default `pairing`). Implemented and wired.

#### Adapter core and gateway connection

- `adapter.go` — `QQAdapter`: token fetch and refresh, gateway URL lookup, identify, resume and heartbeat, reconnect with backoff (2 to 60 s, up to 100 attempts, quick-disconnect detection, re-identify on session-invalidating close codes), event dispatch, pending-request failure on disconnect
- `constants.go` — API hosts, timeouts, limits (4000 characters, dedup 300 s and 1000 ids), message and media type codes, `QQ_PORTAL_HOST` override
- `utils.go` — User-Agent string, API headers, proxy-safe error descriptions

#### Inbound

- `adapter_inbound.go` — per-event handlers for the four chat kinds, dedup, quoted-message context, attachment processing (images cached, voice transcribed, other files described), at-mention stripping, button interactions acknowledged immediately and routed to approval or update-prompt resolution with session authorization
- `adapter_audio.go` — voice pipeline: download with CDN auth, SILK decode through `pilk`, ffmpeg or a raw PCM wrap as last resort, then QQ's own transcript or an OpenAI-compatible STT call (`stt` config block or `QQ_STT_API_KEY`, `QQ_STT_BASE_URL`, `QQ_STT_MODEL`)

#### Outbound

- `adapter_send.go` — chunked text or markdown send (plain with message reference when markdown is off) with three attempts and a wait for reconnection, approval and update-prompt keyboards for C2C and group chats (guild refused), image, voice, video and file sends by URL or local upload (guild media refused), input-notify typing in direct chats, reactions in guild channels only
- `keyboards.go` — inline keyboard model and builders for approval and update prompts, button-data parsers, interaction event parser
- `chunked_upload.go` — three-phase large-file upload (prepare, PUT parts to presigned COS URLs, complete) with retries, file hashes and a typed daily-limit error
- `send.go` — out-of-process sender for cron: token, text and media over REST with its own client

#### Onboarding, registration and env bridge

- `onboard.go` — QR registration through the QQ portal: create a bind task, render the connect URL as a QR code, poll for the app id and encrypted secret
- `crypto.go` — AES-256-GCM key generation and decryption of the bot secret returned by the bind task
- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec, setup flow (QR or manual credentials, DM policy, home channel)
- `gateway_env.go` — env bridge with the deprecated `QQ_HOME_CHANNEL` names mapped to `QQBOT_HOME_CHANNEL`, authorization env names (`QQ_ALLOWED_USERS`, `QQ_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS`, `QQ_ALLOW_ALL_USERS`)
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/raft` — Raft workspace wake channel: content-free wake hints in, activity telemetry out

*5 files, 1,146 Go lines*

Raft is a workspace product whose `raft` CLI the agent itself uses to read and send messages. This adapter carries no message content in either direction. It starts a loopback HTTP endpoint, spawns `raft agent bridge` as a child pointed at it, and turns each wake hint from the bridge into an internal prompt telling the agent to check Raft. `Send` is a deliberate no-op. It is enabled by `RAFT_PROFILE` and requires the `raft` CLI on PATH. Implemented and wired; there is no standalone sender or cron target.

#### Wake endpoint and bridge child

- `adapter.go` — `RaftAdapter`: listener on 127.0.0.1 with an ephemeral port by default, routes for wake (`/wake`), health, activity post and activity drain, constant-time bridge-token check (`x-raft-bridge-token`), 16 KiB body cap, wake admission that queues behind a busy session instead of interrupting, bridge spawn and termination (kill after 5 s)

#### Activity telemetry

- `activity.go` — bounded at-most-once queue (500 events, schema `raft-activity.v1`) of session, model and tool lifecycle events for Raft sessions, with content capped at 4096 characters and unsafe scalar fields dropped; the plugin hooks that feed it

#### Registration and setup

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec, env enablement, platform hint naming the profile for every `raft` CLI call, and registration of seven lifecycle hooks (`on_session_start` through `on_session_finalize`)
- `setup.go` — setup wizard persisting `RAFT_PROFILE`
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/signal` — Signal through a signal-cli HTTP daemon: SSE in, JSON-RPC out

Requires a running signal-cli daemon in HTTP mode (`SIGNAL_HTTP_URL`) and a registered account (`SIGNAL_ACCOUNT`). Inbound is the daemon's `/api/v1/events` server-sent event stream; outbound is JSON-RPC at `/api/v1/rpc`. Groups are off unless `SIGNAL_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS` is set (`*` allows all). ### `pkg/gateway/platforms/wecom` — WeCom (Enterprise WeChat): AI Bot websocket adapter and a separate encrypted-callback adapter

*12 files, 4,400 Go lines*

Two platforms are registered from this package. `wecom` is the AI Bot mode: one persistent websocket to `wss://openws.work.weixin.qq.com` authenticated with `WECOM_BOT_ID` and `WECOM_SECRET`, with native reply streaming. `wecom_callback` is for self-built apps: an HTTP endpoint that receives AES-encrypted XML callbacks and replies through the `message/send` REST API with a corp access token. The callback adapter is text only and has no setup wizard, standalone sender or platform hint. Both are implemented and wired.

#### AI Bot websocket adapter

- `adapter.go` — `WeComAdapter`: subscribe handshake, listen loop with reconnect backoff, 30 s ping heartbeat, request and ack correlation by req id, DM and group policies (`WECOM_DM_POLICY`, `WECOM_GROUP_POLICY`, `allow_from`, `group_allow_from`, per-group config), startup failure handling
- `adapter_messages.go` — inbound message callbacks (dedup, policy intake, text joined with quoted text or voice transcript), batching that merges an attachment frame with its following text frame, req-id bookkeeping per chat, markdown replies by req id or proactive send, stale-subscription reconnect, error mapping
- `media.go` — inbound images and files from base64 or URL with AES decryption, outbound media through a chunked websocket upload (512 KiB chunks, at most 100) with per-kind size limits (image and video 10 MB, voice 2 MB, file 20 MB) and downgrade notes, image, document, voice and video sends

#### Native streaming and send pacing

- `streaming.go` — `Streamer`: per-turn stream state, `aibot_respond_msg` frames with per-req-id ack tracking, limits (20,480 bytes of content, 85 intermediate frames, 330 s stream lifetime), keepalive every 120 s, expiry detection that falls back to a proactive send, typing through the stream
- `streaming_host.go` — small accessors the adapter uses to inspect reply queues and stream ownership
- `send_queue.go` — `ChatSendQueue`: two FIFO lanes per chat under a 30-per-minute token bucket (24 normal, 6 reserved for control messages)

#### Callback-mode adapter

- `callback_adapter.go` — `WecomCallbackAdapter`: listener on `WECOM_CALLBACK_HOST` and `WECOM_CALLBACK_PORT` (default 8645) at `/wecom/callback`, URL verification handshake, decrypt with the first app whose signature matches (single app or an `apps` list), XML parsing with entity declarations refused, dedup, text events only, access token cache and refresh, text send in 2048-byte chunks through the app that last heard from the chat
- `wecom_crypto.go` — `WXBizMsgCrypt`: SHA-1 signature, AES-CBC decrypt with PKCS7 padding and receive-id check, wire compatible with the official callback crypto

#### Registration, env bridge and setup

- `register.go` — manifest and both platform specs, standalone sender that reuses the live adapter or connects an ephemeral one
- `setup.go` — setup wizard: QR scan that returns bot id and secret, or manual entry, then access policy and home chat
- `gateway_env.go` — env bridges for both platforms (`WECOM_CALLBACK_CORP_ID`, `WECOM_CALLBACK_CORP_SECRET`, `WECOM_CALLBACK_AGENT_ID`, `WECOM_CALLBACK_TOKEN`, `WECOM_CALLBACK_ENCODING_AES_KEY`), authorization env names and moved settings

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/whatsapp` — WhatsApp via the built-in WhatsApp Web client (whatsmeow), driven through an in-process loopback bridge

*14 files, 6,123 Go lines*

The original design ran a Node `bridge.js` child process that the adapter polled over HTTP. The Go port replaced the child with an in-process whatsmeow client but kept the bridge's HTTP API, launch arguments, console output, pidfile handling and port ownership rules, so the adapter still polls `GET /messages` on a loopback port every second and posts sends to it. The session (a `whatsmeow.db` SQLite store, `creds.json` marker, `bridge.pid` and `lid-mapping-*.json` files) lives in `platforms/whatsapp/session` under the profile home. Pairing is by QR code through `icebath whatsapp`. Two modes exist (`WHATSAPP_MODE`): `self-chat` (the user's personal number, outbound text prefixed) and `bot` (a separate bot number). Enabled by `WHATSAPP_ENABLED`. Implemented and wired, apart from an unused location send.

#### Adapter

- `adapter.go` — `WhatsAppAdapter`: bridge start or adoption with health polling, pairing preflight, managed-exit detection and restart, poll loop dispatching inbound messages and logging delivery receipts, read receipts, inbound media caching and small-document text injection, quoted-attachment lookup, chunked text send, reactions, edit, native media, voice note and document sends, native polls for clarify prompts, typing, chat info; `SendLocation` is `[unwired]`
- `whatsapp_common.go` — `[port-artifact]` `WhatsAppBehaviorMixin`, a mixin struct shared with the Cloud API adapter; the behaviour inside is real: DM and group policy gating, allowlist matching across phone and LID forms, mention patterns and bot-mention cleanup, reply prefix, chunk limit, markdown to WhatsApp formatting

#### In-process bridge

`[port-artifact]` in shape only: the loopback HTTP hop and Node-era conventions exist because of the port, while the WhatsApp protocol handling inside is the product behaviour.

- `bridge.go` — `bridgeHost`: settings from arguments and env (`WHATSAPP_MODE`, `WHATSAPP_DEBUG`, `WHATSAPP_SEND_TIMEOUT_MS`, `WHATSAPP_CHUNK_DELAY_MS`, `WHATSAPP_MAX_MESSAGE_LENGTH`, port 3000), whatsmeow session store, socket start with QR pairing, reconnect and logout handling, inbound and delivery queues (100 entries), serialized sends, LID mapping file mirror, `RunPairing`
- `bridge_http.go` — the bridge routes: `/messages`, `/send`, `/edit`, `/send-media` (ffmpeg conversion for voice), `/send-poll`, `/send-location`, `/typing`, `/read`, `/react`, `/chat/{id}`, `/health`, behind a loopback Host check
- `bridge_inbound.go` — message extraction from WhatsApp protobufs: text, quoted context, media download, locations, contacts, reactions, polls and vote aggregation, owner-message and group intake gates (`WHATSAPP_FORWARD_OWNER_MESSAGES`), receipts
- `bridge_helpers.go` — id normalization and allowlist matching, bounded caches, long-message splitting, media file writing, text renderings of locations, contacts, reactions and polls, console line formats
- `bridge_process.go` — pidfile and port hygiene inherited from the child-process design: listener PID discovery (lsof, ss, kernel tables, netstat), stale bridge kill with identity check, cache-directory path allowlist, executable content hash
- `bridge_ownership.go` — bridge port selection per profile: explicit `bridge_port`, a recorded port, 3000 for the launch profile, 3001 to 3999 allocated for secondary profiles, sibling claims respected

#### Registration, CLI setup and status

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec, setup entry
- `main_platform_setup.go` — the `icebath whatsapp` wizard: mode choice, allowed users, QR pairing run
- `standalone.go` — out-of-process delivery through the profile's bridge API, text then each media file
- `session_status.go` — reports whether the session store exists and holds a linked device; used by the doctor command
- `gateway_env.go` — env bridge (`WHATSAPP_ENABLED`, `WHATSAPP_HOME_CHANNEL`), authorization env names and moved settings
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gateway/platforms/yuanbao` — Tencent Yuanbao IM bot over a signed persistent websocket, with five group and sticker tools

*19 files, 8,014 Go lines*

Yuanbao is Tencent's assistant app with group chats; this adapter runs a bot account in it. It authenticates with `YUANBAO_APP_ID` (legacy `YUANBAO_APP_KEY`) and `YUANBAO_APP_SECRET`, obtains an HMAC-signed token from the sign-token endpoint, and holds one websocket that carries both directions in a hand-written protobuf encoding. The same connection is the only way to send, so the standalone sender needs the running adapter. Inbound processing is an explicit twenty-step middleware pipeline. Five tools in the `icebath-yuanbao` toolset are registered directly in the tool registry from the package `init` (not through the plugin context) and are offered only when the session platform is yuanbao or the profile has a live adapter. Implemented and wired.

#### Adapter, connection and signing

- `adapter.go` — `YuanbaoAdapter`: per-profile active-adapter registry, state caches (members, message content, processing sessions), connect and disconnect, text send, typing, group info and member queries, DM send, image, sticker and document sends
- `connection.go` — `connectionManager`: dial, auth bind, ping heartbeat (30 s, two missed pongs), receive loop, request and response correlation, per-sender inbound debounce (1.5 s), reconnect with exponential backoff up to 60 s
- `sign.go` — sign-token fetch with HMAC signature, cache with refresh margin and per-app locks, retry on the retryable code; also shared constants (4000 character text chunks, 50 MB media, cron wrapper text) and error helpers
- `yuanbao_proto.go` — protobuf wire codec written by hand: varints, field parsing, connection and business message envelopes, message body elements, inbound push decoding

#### Inbound middleware pipeline

Order: decode, extract fields, recall guard, dedup, skip self, chat routing, access guard, extract content, placeholder filter, owner command, build source, group at-guard, auto set home, group attribution, classify type, quote context, forwarded records, media resolve, patch anchors, dispatch.

- `inbound_pipeline.go` — `InboundPipeline` (ordered named middlewares with insert and remove) and the `InboundContext` they share
- `middleware_decode.go` — frame decode (JSON or protobuf), field extraction, dedup window, self-message skip, chat routing, `AccessPolicy` for DM and group access (`YUANBAO_DM_POLICY`, `YUANBAO_GROUP_POLICY`, allow-from lists), auto designation of the first authorized conversation as home
- `middleware_content.go` — text, media and share-card extraction, media-placeholder-only filter, owner slash commands in groups without a mention, session source, group at-mention guard that still records unmentioned messages, sender attribution and group channel prompt, message type classification, quoted-message context
- `middleware_forward.go` — renders forwarded chat records into text with media references, and the loading heartbeat helper
- `middleware_media.go` — resolves resource ids to download URLs, downloads into a cache (24 h, 256 entries, bounded concurrency), backfills media from observed group messages and quotes, rewrites resource anchors to local paths
- `middleware_recall.go` — handles message recalls: redacts the recalled message in the stored transcript, notes an unseen one, interrupts a turn still processing it
- `middleware_dispatch.go` — builds the message event and hands it to the gateway, serializing group turns per session through a queue

#### Outbound

- `outbound.go` — markdown-aware chunking (never inside a fence or table), per-chat send lock with per-chunk retry, media handlers for image by URL, image file, document and sticker, reply heartbeat every 2 s until 30 s idle (the loading bubble), slow-response notice after 120 s of silence
- `yuanbao_media.go` — media helpers: MIME and image-size sniffing, URL download, COS upload credentials, request signing and upload, image and file message bodies
- `yuanbao_sticker.go` — `[data]` built-in sticker table (name, id, search keywords) with exact, substring and fuzzy search, random pick, and sticker message bodies; consumed by the sticker tools and sticker sends

#### Agent tools

- `yuanbao_tools.go` — `yb_query_group_info`, `yb_query_group_members`, `yb_send_dm` (text and media to a group member), `yb_search_sticker`, `yb_send_sticker`; each requires the running adapter of the turn

#### Registration, env bridge and scaffolding

- `register.go` — manifest, platform spec, `group:` and `direct:` target syntax, standalone sender through the live connection, setup prompts for App ID and Secret
- `gateway_env.go` — env bridge (`YUANBAO_BOT_ID`, `YUANBAO_HOME_CHANNEL`), authorization env names and moved settings
- `pyhelpers.go` — `[py-shim]` asyncio Future and Lock stand-ins and Python type-error helpers used across the package
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/gatewayrun` — the gateway runner: the long-lived process that owns platform adapters, admits inbound messages, runs agent turns and delivers replies

*358 files, 60,765 Go lines*

One flat package of 352 files, 250 of them named `run_*`, that is the Go form of the Python `GatewayRunner` class: the runner is eight embedded "mixin" state structs and the file split follows the class's methods. It is entered through the hidden argv word `__icebath_gateway_run__` and through `pkg/gatewaycli`. It starts and supervises adapters for the launch profile and every multiplexed secondary profile, runs the inbound pipeline up to the point a turn is claimed, applies the busy rules for input that arrives mid-turn, implements all 69 gateway slash commands, runs one agent turn per session and streams and delivers its reply, relays background-process and delegation results, and handles startup recovery, drain, restart and scale-to-zero. It serves the gateway control socket and a loopback WebSocket at `/api/ws`, and writes the pid file, locks, runtime status and the restart and update marker files under the icebath home. Deduplication, mention and group policy and text batching are not here; the adapters in `pkg/gateway` apply them before calling the runner. Cron, kanban and browser cleanup are bound through nil-checked hook variables that the `icebath_core` and `icebath_noextras` build tags compile out. Nearly everything is implemented and reachable; the scaffolding (hand-made asyncio tasks and futures, `map[string]any` kwargs, recovered panics standing in for Python exceptions, about 45 hook variables) is pervasive but load-bearing.

**Files `api_*` through `run_module*`, plus `session_*`, `slash_*`, `assets/`, `default/`** (190 files, 33,123 Go lines). This part holds the front half of the long-lived gateway process: the entry points (`Main` for the hidden `__icebath_gateway_run__` argv word, `RunGateway` and `StartGateway` called by `pkg/gatewaycli`), the start and shutdown sequence, creation, wiring, supervision and reconnection of platform adapters for the launch profile and for every multiplexed secondary profile, the whole inbound message pipeline up to the point a turn is claimed, every rule for a message that arrives while a turn runs, all 69 gateway slash commands, per-session in-memory state with the agent cache, and the housekeeping, idle-exit, handoff, heartbeat, goal, loop, cron and kanban background work. It writes the pid file, runtime lock, host lock and host record, runtime status, the restart and update marker files under the icebath home, and serves two local endpoints: the gateway control socket and a loopback WebSocket at `/api/ws`. The `GatewayRunner` struct itself, `Start`, `Stop`, the turn runner and delivery live in the other part. Nearly everything here is implemented and reachable. Port scaffolding is pervasive but thin: the file split follows the Python `GatewayRunner` class (`run_class_*`), mixins (`authz_mixin*`) and its `_handle_message` helpers (`hm*` functions), asyncio tasks and `concurrent.futures` are re-created by hand, replies and queue entries are `map[string]any` dicts, panics are recovered as Python exceptions, about 30 exported function variables are assigned from `cmd/icebath` to break import cycles, and about 15 unexported ones are bound by the build-tagged cron, kanban and browser link files. Dedup of inbound platform messages, mention and group-chat policy and text batching are not here: the adapters in `pkg/gateway` and `pkg/gateway/platforms/*` apply them before calling the runner, which only hands them the busy text mode, debounce timing and human-delay range.

#### Process entry, argument parsing and module-import side effects

The gateway is entered either from `icebath gateway run` (`pkg/gatewaycli` calls `ImportRunModule`, `RegisterAtExit` and `RunGateway`) or from the hidden argv word `__icebath_gateway_run__`, which `cmd/icebath/startup.go` dispatches to `Main`; that word is the port of `python -m gateway.run`.

- `run_main.go` — `Main` and `DispatchGatewayRunModuleEntry`: sets `AI_AGENT` and `ICEBATH_AGENT` defaults, arms the startup watchdog, activates the installed runtime, loads `--config`, runs the gateway, maps errors to exit codes (130 on interrupt on Unix)
- `run_main_args.go` — [py-shim] byte-exact argparse emulation (prefix abbreviations, usage wrapping, error text) for `-h`, `--config/-c` and `--verbose/-v` of the module entry
- `run_module_import.go` — `ImportRunModule`, run once: sets `_ICEBATH_GATEWAY=1`, loads the home and repo `.env`, applies `network.force_ipv4`, prints config and deprecated-cwd warnings
- `run_bootstrap_interrupt.go` — `RunGateway` reproduces `asyncio.run`: a first Ctrl-C before signal routing cancels startup, a second ends the wait with `KeyboardInterrupt`; `RegisterAtExit`
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `logger=gatewayrun`

#### Start sequence, instance ownership and shutdown tail

`StartGateway` runs in this order: set `ICEBATH_EXEC_ASK=1`, resolve `TERMINAL_CWD`, raise the open-file limit, load config and settle the multiplex flag, probe the host toolchain, decide attach, refuse or replace against the one host gateway, replace an existing pid (`--replace`), reserve the launch and served profile homes, claim the runtime lock, pid file and host lock. `runStartedGateway` then configures logging, builds the runner, installs signal handlers, starts the control socket and the loopback API, records startup in the lifecycle ledger, connects MCP servers, calls `Start`, starts cron and housekeeping, arms idle exit and waits; teardown always drains, stops, removes the pid file and releases the locks.

- `run_bootstrap_start.go` — `StartGateway`, `runStartedGateway`, SIGINT/SIGTERM handler distinguishing takeover, planned stop and unexpected signal, SIGUSR1 graceful restart, per-profile MCP connect and bounded shutdown, 65 s cron and 35 s housekeeping drain
- `run_bootstrap.go` — at-exit registry, `--replace` (takeover marker, SIGTERM then SIGKILL, reaping the old gateway's children and scoped locks), pid and runtime-lock claim, multiplexer allowed only from the default profile, profile reservation, `TERMINAL_CWD` fallback
- `run_host_gateway.go` — one gateway per host: proves `--replace` ownership from the pid record (start time, home, command line), claims the host lock, publishes the host record, attaches to or refuses beside an existing owner, `--force` override
- `run_bootstrap_control.go` — gateway control socket verbs: `identify`, `pause-for-update`, `rescan-profiles`, `serve-profile`, `unserve-profile`, `migrate-profile-identity`, `purge-profile-identity`, `active-work`, `reload-plugins`; startup aborts without the socket
- `run_active_work_verb.go` — `active-work` verb: lists chat turns, managed turns, cron runs, side agents and async delegations a stop or a profile unserve would interrupt
- `run_bootstrap_logging.go` — syncs bundled skills, sets up gateway file logging, runs the startup security audit, adds a stderr handler by verbosity (0 warning, 1 info, more debug)
- `run_bootstrap_signals_{unix,other}.go` — routes SIGINT and SIGTERM to drain and SIGUSR1 to restart on the gateway loop; the non-unix variant routes nothing
- `run_config_runner.go` — loads the runner's gateway config, settles `gateway.multiplex_profiles`, and reloads under the root home scope when multiplexing
- `run_loop_exception.go` — loop exception handler that logs and swallows transient network errors, matched by Python exception class name up to 12 causes deep
- `run_health_export.go` — shuts down the gateway health OTLP export (started in the other part) once on exit

#### Multiplex mode resolution and `icebath gateway migrate --multiplex`

One default-profile gateway can serve every profile ("multiplexing"). An unset `gateway.multiplex_profiles` defaults to on unless a preflight blocker holds; the migration command folds per-profile gateways and their service units into one multiplexer and can roll back. It is called from `pkg/gatewaycli` and automatically after an update from `pkg/selfupdate`.

- `gateway_multiplex_mode_resolve.go` — `ResolveMultiplexMode` and `ImplicitMultiplexBlocker`: standalone launcher, fewer than two profiles, secondaries still running their own gateway, or plan blockers force standalone for this boot
- `gateway_migrate_cmd.go` — `CmdMigrate` (plan table, `--dry-run`, `--yes`, TTY prompt, exit 0 or 1) and `MaybeAutoMigrateAfterUpdate`, honouring `gateway.auto_multiplex_migration` and a masked default unit
- `gateway_migrate_plan.go` — `BuildMigrationPlan`: per-profile footprint (live pid, installed systemd, s6 or Windows task units), served record, blockers for secondaries binding ports without profile-prefix ingress
- `gateway_migrate_guards.go` — auto-migration refusals: secondary under another service manager or scope, another Unix user, or a home outside the default profiles tree
- `gateway_migrate_credentials.go` — detects one platform credential held by two profiles, reporting profile and env key names only; also feeds `icebath gateway status`
- `gateway_migrate_apply.go` — `ApplyMigration`: enables the default unit at boot, writes `gateway_migration.json`, flips the flag, removes secondary units, restarts the default, waits 90 s for the served set; `RollbackMigration` and manifest resume; systemd, launchd, s6 and Windows legs
- `gateway_migrate_uid_{unix,windows}.go` — owner uid of a stat result, always zero on Windows

#### Runner construction and core lookups (`run_class_*`)

These files are the body of the Python `GatewayRunner` class cut into pieces. The behaviour is real; several one-line exported accessors exist only so `pkg/gateway` interfaces can read runner fields.

- `run_class_init.go` — `NewGatewayRunner` and its init order; warns when a Docker terminal backend serves messaging with no `/output` volume for `MEDIA:` delivery; exit flag accessors (`ShouldExitCleanly` has no caller)
- `run_class_core.go` — session key for a source, profile-route matching to a served profile (rejecting unserved targets), profile home resolution with fallback, channel override lookup by chat, thread, then parent
- `run_class_sources.go` — authorization and bot-loop counting under the transport profile's scope; LRU of the last 512 live sources per session key; async session-store facade
- `run_class_teams.go` — binds the Teams meeting pipeline plugin to the Microsoft Graph webhook adapter when `plugins.enabled` lists it; hook assigned in `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go`
- `run_class_status.go` — publishes gateway state, exit reason, restart flag and active-work units (named only while draining) to runtime status
- `run_class_cached_agent.go` — resets a cached agent's activity clock, flush cursor and API call count for a new turn
- `run_class_accessors.go`, `run_hosted_service_access.go` — [port-artifact] exported getters for the runner config, primary profile name, per-profile configs and the control server

#### Task, future and thread-pool scaffolding

Hand-built replacements for Python concurrency that every background task, watcher and blocking call in the package goes through.

- `asyncio_task.go` — [py-shim] `asyncio.Task` and `Future`: goroutine with cancel, settle-once result, done callbacks and a context-carried "current task"
- `executor_future.go` — [py-shim] `concurrent.futures.Future` with `InvalidStateError`, and named executor "threads" carrying an interrupt identity and join
- `run_executor.go` — two worker pools: an unbounded turn pool for blocking agent work and a 4-worker housekeeping pool; both refuse work once shutdown starts
- `run_home_writers.go` — counts goroutines that write into a profile home so turn end and shutdown can wait for agent releases, lease releases and status writes

#### Adapter creation, wiring and bounded connect or disconnect

Builds one adapter per enabled platform (plugin registry first, then the builtin table) and installs the runner's callbacks on it. Connect and disconnect are time-boxed and detached on timeout so one stuck platform cannot block startup or shutdown.

- `run_adapters_create.go` — instantiates an adapter, passes `group_sessions_per_user` and `thread_sessions_per_user` into its config, binds it to the runner
- `run_adapters_wire.go` — installs message, busy-session, fatal-error, reaction, authorization and platform-event handlers plus busy text mode, debounce timing and human-delay range; per-profile handler variants; Telegram topic recovery and root-DM transfer
- `run_adapters.go` — connect timeout (`gateway.platform_connect_timeout`, else Telegram 45 s cold and 180 s reconnect), 5 s disconnect bound (`ICEBATH_GATEWAY_ADAPTER_DISCONNECT_TIMEOUT`), routing identity canonicalisation, launch session authority accessors
- `run_connect_timeouts.go` — the Telegram and disconnect timeout defaults
- `run_adapters_supervise.go` — supervised background tasks: respawn with backoff of 2^n capped at 60 s, give up after 5 rapid deaths (healthy after 300 s); reaction fan-out to hooks; `on_all_adapters_down` policy

#### Primary adapter failure and reconnection

A fatal adapter error removes the adapter, records platform status and queues retryable platforms for a background watcher. When no adapter and no queued platform remains the gateway exits, with failure status if the error was retryable so a supervisor restarts it, unless `on_all_adapters_down` is `stay_alive`.

- `run_adapters_fatal.go` — detached fatal handler, reconnect watcher (first pass after 10 s, backoff from 30 s doubling), pause flag, slow respawn every 300 s up to 6 times, reinstall with replay of missed restart notices, failed deliveries and pending resumes
- `run_adapters_reconnect_state.go` — reconnect queue entries, NEEDS_ATTENTION after `agent.reconnect_attention_after`, backoff bookkeeping, plugin load re-arm (max 3), unserved shared-ingress warnings, per-adapter authorization callback

#### Secondary-profile adapters, exclusive claims and their reconnect

Under multiplexing each non-launch profile gets its own adapters, connected under that profile's home, secrets and config. A bot token or listener port may be owned by one profile only; a duplicate is refused and parked.

- `run_adapters_secondary.go` — starts each served profile's adapters; skips relay, platforms without a bot credential and listeners the default profile mirrors at `/p/<profile>/`; refuses an open access policy; records `served_profiles`; seeds pairing stores
- `run_adapters_claim_owners.go` — claim table of credentials and listener binds across primary, live, queued and mid-teardown secondary adapters, with a refusal naming where each profile configured the token
- `run_adapters_claims.go` — derives an adapter's credential claim from token-like attributes, the `photon` platform's sidecar bind and port claim, and a salted log-safe credential fingerprint
- `run_adapters_recovery_reconnect.go` — per-profile reconnect task with the same backoff, cold-start reconnects parked until the runner is live, install with replay, give-up rules for a platform that can never build

#### Authorization and adapter selection (`authz_*`)

Decides whether a sender may use the bot and which live adapter receives or answers a source under multiplexing. Order: local session policy, webhook and trusted-inbound platforms, upstream relay delegation, group-chat allowlists, admitted bots, per-platform allow-all env, role authorization, pairing-store approval, then platform, group and `GATEWAY_ALLOWED_USERS` allowlists; with no allowlist anywhere the adapter's own policy, its config allowlist, and finally `gateway.allow_all_users` decide.

- `authz_mixin.go` — the allowlist chain, Nostr npub to hex matching (inline bech32), legacy chat ids in `TELEGRAM_GROUP_ALLOWED_USERS`, bot loop guard per profile, platform and chat, unauthorized-DM behaviour (pair, ignore, decline)
- `authz_mixin_adapters.go` — intake, delivery and authorization adapter for a source; a profile never borrows another profile's bot except as a routed "shared bot satellite"; `ProfileAdaptersAndConfig` used by Discord slash sync
- `authz_mixin_transport.go` — primary and per-profile adapter maps and the transport-owner lookup that maps a source back to the adapter instance that created it
- `authz_mixin_pairing_store.go` — picks the source profile's pairing store, else the global one

#### Inbound pipeline: entry, ingress gates and admission

`handleMessage` is the single entry for every adapter message. Stages in order: hold during a session-store outage; reset per-message tool context; resolve the routed profile and drop rejected routes; drop Slack ignored channels; park messages during startup restore; `pre_gateway_dispatch` plugin hook; authorization (pairing code, decline or owner notice for unauthorized DMs); bot loop guard; emergency-stop gate; replies owned by a pending update prompt, clarify or slash confirm; hand-off to the profile's session authority FIFO; stale or reaped running-slot eviction; the busy path; idle command dispatch; Telegram topic lobby; the `max_concurrent_sessions` slot; then the `post_gateway_admission` hook and the agent turn.

- `run_inbound_handle.go` — `handleMessage` and `handleMessageTurn` (the stage order above), the busy fast path, idle command dispatch table for `new`, `undo`, `queue`, `steer`, `plan`, `learn`, `init`, `blueprint`, `moa`, `egress`, `start`, orphaned-queue rescue
- `run_inbound_admit.go` — ingress gates: route rejection, Slack ignored channel, startup-restore parking, dispatch hook, authorization branch by unauthorized-DM behaviour, bot loop admission
- `run_inbound_pairing.go` — DMs a pairing code with the approve command, or one rate-limit notice then silence; one decline message per sender per window
- `run_inbound_unauthorized.go` — pairing and owner-hint texts; under `ignore`, logs and posts one hint per sender to the platform home channel (2048-sender memory)
- `run_inbound_estop.go` — global emergency stop: only known commands and replies to in-flight prompts pass; heartbeats are dropped silently, others get the paused notice
- `run_inbound_intercepts.go` — routes a reply to a detached update's prompt file, a pending clarify question, or a slash confirm (typed or localized yes/no words)
- `run_inbound_authority_admission.go` — admits non-command messages to the session authority's durable FIFO; a busy follow-up first tries approval words, then steer, redirect or interrupt per busy mode
- `run_inbound_busy.go` — evicts a running slot idle past `agent.gateway_timeout` or whose session row ended; Telegram text within 3 s of turn start is queued (`ICEBATH_TELEGRAM_FOLLOWUP_GRACE_SECONDS`); owner-turn stop
- `run_inbound_hooks.go`, `run_inbound_consumer.go` — `pre_gateway_dispatch` (drop or rewrite) and `post_gateway_admission` (consume with optional reply, fail open) plugin hooks; `quick_commands` config lookup and alias expansion
- `run_inbound_hooks_producer.go` — [port-artifact] exported forms of both hooks for producer ingress in `pkg/gateway`
- `run_busy_active_session_slot.go` — cross-process active-session cap: refuses a new session past `max_concurrent_sessions` and holds a lease for the turn
- `run_inbound_one_turn_restore.go` — restores the model override a one-turn switch (`/moa` or a once-scoped `/model`) replaced, only while the same run generation is current

#### Inbound pipeline: command detection, hooks and rewriting

A leading slash word is resolved through the command registry and aliases, the slash access gate, the `pre_command` plugin hook and `command:<name>` directory hooks (which may deny, handle or rewrite it), then tried as builtin, operator quick command (`exec` or `alias`), plugin command, bound turn-building command, skill or bundle command. Commands that produce a turn are admitted to the FIFO under the route's stop epoch so a later `/stop` or `/new` fences them.

- `run_inbound_commands.go` — command canonicalisation and gate; prompt-rewriting commands `/learn`, `/plan`, `/init`, `/blueprint`; `/queue` and `/steer` when idle; `/moa` one-turn mixture-of-agents; `/start` ignored; `/egress` proxy status
- `run_inbound_hooks_commands.go` — command hooks (handled, rewrite or pass), refusal of new work while draining, `exec` quick commands with sanitized env and redacted output, plugin command dispatch
- `run_inbound_skill_rewrite.go` — rewrites `/<skill>` and `/<bundle>` into the skill invocation prompt; replies for disabled skills and for unknown slash commands
- `run_inbound_wiring.go`, `run_busy_wiring.go` — [port-artifact] hook variables for the command registry, slash-confirm store, config writer and init-prompt builder, assigned in `cmd/icebath/wiring.go`
- `run_command_mentions.go` — rewrites `/command-name` mentions in reply text to Telegram-valid command names on Telegram only

#### Inbound pipeline: text, media and voice preparation

Turns an admitted event into the text the agent reads: sender attribution in shared sessions, image handling (native attachment or vision description by model capability), voice transcription with an optional transcript echo, notes for audio, video and document files, expansion of context references, and reply-to context.

- `run_inbound_prepare.go` — `prepareInboundMessageText` (the order above), per-profile scope variant, context-reference expansion with injection refusal, native-or-text image routing, durable active-turn marker
- `run_inbound.go` — media classification, attachment display names and sandbox-visible paths, file and document notes, reply pointer, Discord triggering-message note
- `run_inbound_text.go` — prefixes `[sender]` in shared multi-user sessions (with Slack user id), prepends backfilled channel context, transcribes and echoes voice
- `run_inbound_transcription.go` — speech to text per clip with a local fallback, once-per-event caching, quoted transcript echo, neutral note naming the file when transcription fails
- `run_inbound_media.go` — moves adapter-cached attachments into the active profile's cache and repoints the event and its notes
- `run_event_media.go` — per-attachment MIME tests (image, audio, speech-to-text input, video) and the placeholder text for media-only and document messages
- `run_inbound_session_slots.go` — clarify reply text from voice transcripts; queue of native image paths consumed by the next turn

#### Busy handling: a message arrives while a turn is running

The mode is `display.busy_input_mode` (`interrupt`, `queue` or `steer`), snapshotted per profile at startup and changed by `/busy`; `display.busy_text_mode` can force plain text to queue, and a bare yes or no answers a blocking approval instead. Interrupt aborts the turn with the new text, or redirects it in place when the runtime supports that, and is demoted to queue while subagents are active or compression is in flight. Steer injects the text between tool calls with the sender's origin attached and falls back to queue; queue appends to a per-session FIFO capped at 32, merging only photo bursts. While draining, messages are queued only for a requested restart in queue or steer mode, else rejected.

- `run_busy_handler.go` — adapter-facing busy handler: authorization, bot loop guard, drain notice, mode resolution, and the busy acknowledgement (at most one per 30 s, optional detail, one-time onboarding hint)
- `run_busy_steer.go` — demotion rules, steer with origin JSON (PII hashed), fan-out to subagents, redirect and re-anchoring of the running turn's reply, plain-text approval routing, voice transcription before interrupt
- `run_busy_queue.go` — FIFO enqueue, promotion and requeue-at-front, photo-burst merge under equal security metadata, goal-continuation clearing, leftover-steer merge, orphaned overflow rescue
- `run_busy_overflow_queue.go` — locked append, push-front, pop, take and drop on the per-session overflow list
- `run_busy.go` — localized approval reply synonyms and session-key slot parsing for same-chat matching
- `run_busy_chat_runs.go` — slash access gate (admins run everything, others `help`, `whoami` and `user_allowed_commands`), other running turns of the same chat or thread for `/stop`, stale `/restart` redelivery check
- `run_config_loaders.go` — per-profile loaders: busy modes, text debounce and hard cap, human delay, drain and restart timeouts, reasoning, service tier, fallback chain, provider routing, prefill messages, channel model and prompt overrides, silence permission

#### Busy slash commands and command-produced turns

Each registered command declares a busy policy.
