While a turn runs, `/status` and `/context` always answer, `/stop` and `/new` interrupt (also fencing the authority's queued turns), `/queue` and `/steer` act on the running turn, goal and loop control verbs pass, `/model`, `/codex-runtime` and `/moa` are rejected with their own text, and anything else without a mid-run handler is rejected.

- `run_busy_dispatch.go` — handler tables: 23 commands valid idle and busy, 35 idle-only, the mid-run special cases and rejection texts
- `run_busy_commands.go` — `/pause` (global emergency stop on or off), mid-run `/stop`, `/queue`, `/steer`, `/egress` and the ignored `/start`
- `run_busy_command_turn.go` — admits a command-produced turn to the authority FIFO under the stop epoch, acknowledging after the row commits; mid-run skill commands queued as turns
- `run_busy_destructive.go` — confirm prompt for `/new` and `/undo` unless `approvals.destructive_slash_confirm` is off (buttons or typed reply, "always" persists the opt-out); command acknowledgement delivery

#### Per-session state, run generations and the agent cache

`SessionState` groups in-memory state per session key into turn scope, conversation scope (cleared at a conversation boundary such as `/new`) and persistent scope. A monotonically increasing run generation fences stale turn unwinds. Agents are cached per session, keyed by a config signature, and released softly so sandboxes and processes survive.

- `session_state.go` — the three scopes (running agent, lease, model, reasoning and fast overrides, queued events, prompt pins, approvals, generation); [port-artifact] dict-shaped views emulating the Python per-attribute dicts
- `run_agent_cache.go` — 16-hex agent config signature and the change key of the pinned session-context prompt
- `run_agent_cache_state.go` — model override snapshot and one-turn restore, run generations, turn lease hold, release and rebind, sidecar notes, session-context and channel prompt pins persisted on the route
- `run_agent_cache_turn.go` — conversation boundary funnel (clears overrides, approvals, slash confirms and persisted yolo), hard interrupt with process reaping, override rehydration after restart
- `run_agent_cache_release.go` — running-slot release checked by generation and holder, `active_agents` status, interrupt-and-clear, cached message-count rebaseline, Discord voice-channel membership note
- `run_agent_cache_evict.go` — cap of 128 cached agents, 3600 s idle TTL, memory-pressure sweep by resident memory, memory-provider commit before eviction, release under the owning profile
- `session_execution.go` — per-turn agent resolution: reuse the cached agent unless its session ended or another process wrote messages, else build fresh; context-file opt-out

#### Turn helpers for local viewers, API and one-shot CLI turns

Functions on the turn runner (defined in the other part) that apply only when the turn belongs to a "local" session watched over the WebSocket, an API-server request, or a one-shot `icebath chat` turn. They publish typed events to the session's stream and bind interactive prompts.

- `local_viewer_events.go` — installs event sinks: `tool.generating`, `thinking.delta`, `reasoning.delta`, subagent and mixture-of-agents progress, tool completion with duration, inline diff and task-list snapshot
- `local_viewer_connections.go` — publishes `connection.request` and routes later `connection.update` events of connector operations to the session that opened them
- `session_secret_prompt.go`, `session_sudo_prompt.go`, `session_vault_prompt.go` — masked secret, sudo and vault (unlock, save-login, code) prompts answered by an attached viewer, 120 to 180 s timeouts
- `session_turn_scope.go`, `session_usage_publish.go`, `session_local_inventory.go` — per-session settings layer and pinned logins, `login.exhausted`, usage frames, end-of-turn session info
- `session_cli_turn_route.go` — applies an admission's one-turn model override and keeps raw result fields a one-shot chat viewer reads
- `session_policy_refused.go` — turns a policy scope refusal into a failed never-run turn result; one-turn reasoning level
- `session_api_turn_runtime.go`, `api_server_runner.go` — API-server turns: model and runtime selection per request, observers for reasoning, status and tool progress; registers `gateway.APIAgentRuntime`

#### Side agents: background tasks, side questions, refine, review and comments

Agents that run beside the main conversation on a fresh instance with the session's route, without touching the live transcript.

- `slash_commands_background.go` — `/bg <prompt>` starts a background agent with task id `bg_<time>_<hex>`; `/btw <question>` answers from a transcript snapshot
- `run_background_task.go` — runs the background prompt in the source's profile scope and delivers text, images and `MEDIA:` files to the chat, or a failure notice
- `session_tui_side_runner.go`, `session_refine.go` — the same background and side-question runs for local sessions on the frozen launch policy route; review guard allowing one review at a time
- `slash_commands_goals_review.go`, `session_cold_review.go` — `/refine` (memory and skill review over the transcript) and `/review` (reviewer subagent), from a cached agent or a cold parent built from stored history
- `comment_agent.go` — `RunCommentAgent`: one tool-limited turn for platform document comments, called by the Feishu comment plugin wiring

#### Runner methods exported to the session authority

The session verbs in `pkg/gateway` run slash commands and session controls for local sessions through small interfaces; these files supply the exported methods.

- `session_commands_runner_export.go`, `session_controls_runner_export.go`, `slash_commands_agent_lookup.go`, `run_idle_exit_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers so `pkg/gateway` session verbs reach slash access, quick and plugin commands, busy dispatch, goal manager, voice mode, fast tier, reasoning and client attach counting

#### History replay, resume notes and media tags

Pure helpers the turn code calls to turn stored transcript rows into the message list sent to the model and to pick up media a tool produced.

- `run_history_replay.go` — builds agent history from stored rows (reasoning fields kept, auto-continue notes stripped, Telegram observed group chatter separated), restart recovery note, text approval prompt fallback, `MEDIA:` tag collection from tool results

#### Automatic context compression ("hygiene") support

Bookkeeping for the pre-turn compression of an oversized session; the compression run itself is driven from the other part.

- `run_hygiene.go` — failure streak and cooldown ladder (base times 1, 3, 9, capped at 3600 s) stored in `state.db`, turn-hold budget error, Codex app-server thread compaction, timeout notice, wait-extension rule

#### Goals, loops and heartbeats

Standing goals are judged after each turn and continued by a synthetic queued turn; loops are recurring wakeups; a heartbeat is one recurring re-entry prompt per session. All three survive restarts through `state.db` and are injected only when the session is idle.

- `slash_commands_goals.go` — `/goal` (delegates to the shared goal command in `pkg/goals`; adding a gate is admin-only), `/subgoal` (add, remove, clear, list criteria), `/heartbeat` (show, set, pause, resume, clear), `/loop`
- `run_goals.go` — post-turn goal judge and continuation, goal status notices after delivery, loop tick completion, loop wakeup watcher (15 s) across served profiles
- `run_goals_heartbeat.go`, `run_heartbeat_restore.go` — heartbeat watch registry, single poller task, restore of active heartbeats from the routing index of every served home
- `run_heartbeat_acceptance.go` — admits a due heartbeat behind the route's FIFO, coalesces overdue ticks, refunds a fire that never ran, binds it to its original session lineage

#### CLI-to-gateway session handoff

A CLI session can hand itself to a chat platform: it leaves a pending handoff row in `state.db`, and a supervised watcher in the gateway picks it up.

- `run_adapters_handoff.go` — watcher (every 2 s) that claims pending `/handoff` rows per profile store, runs each as a full turn, marks complete or failed, reclaims rows stranded by a dead gateway
- `run_handoff_scopes.go`, `run_handoff_watch_resolve.go` — the stores polled: root first, then each multiplexed profile home

#### Loopback session socket

The gateway binds `127.0.0.1` on a free port and serves one route, the WebSocket `/api/ws`, for the terminal UI and managed worker processes. A client must present a one-time ticket as a subprotocol, come from loopback with no `Origin` header, and is refused unless the runtime is ready (workers may attach while draining).

- `run_api.go` — listener, ticket redemption (`interactive` or `worker-adoption`), authority lookup by profile id, hand-off to `ServeSessionSocket`, 5 s graceful close
- `run_api_socket.go` — gorilla WebSocket wrapper: 403 refusal, accept with subprotocol, frame reader, text send, close with service-restart code
- `run_api_handle.go` — handle with API origin and serve task; stop helper

#### Housekeeping loop

A goroutine ticking every 60 s. Each tick: runtime status heartbeat, cron delivery-queue drain, low-disk prompt, plugin update check, FTS rebuild retry, memory trim, MCP config reconcile, checkpoint prune. Every 5 ticks the channel directory is rebuilt; hourly the media caches (24 h age), expired pastes, the curator and `state.db` maintenance run.

- `run_housekeeping.go` — chore table and loop, MCP server reconcile with `mcp_servers` per served profile
- `run_housekeeping_disk_media.go` — prunes image, document, audio, video, screenshot, spillover, terminal-temp and bot-DM caches
- `run_housekeeping_disk_prompt.go`, `run_housekeeping_disk_notice.go` — posts the low-disk auto-prune question to each undecided profile's home channels and snoozes it; clears a local viewer's sticky notice once answered
- `run_delivery_queue_watch.go` — checks each served profile's cron delivery queue file and WAL every second and drains as soon as a stamp changes
- `run_housekeeping_hooks.go` — [port-artifact] hook variable for the paste sweep in `pkg/selfupdate`

#### Idle exit of an auto-started gateway

A gateway started on demand with no supervisor exits after `gateway.unmanaged_idle_exit_seconds` (default 600, 5 under `go run`, 0 disables) once two consecutive probes find nothing holding it.

- `run_idle_exit.go` — watcher and hold reasons: attached or attaching clients, running work, configured or reconnecting messaging platforms, pending admissions, workers, hosted rooms, cron, kanban, heartbeats, loops, handoffs; any probe error keeps it up
- `run_idle_gates.go` — per-profile `state.db` probes for active heartbeat, loop or pending handoff that fail towards "busy"
- `run_idle_exit_kanban.go` — any task in `scheduled`, `ready`, `running` or `review` on an unarchived board counts as busy

#### Cron integration

Cron and kanban are compiled out by the `icebath_core` and `icebath_noextras` build tags; unconditional files hold nil-checked hook variables and fallbacks.

- `cron_hooks.go` — hook variables and fallbacks; `/suggestions` and `/blueprint` reply that this build has no cron when unbound
- `cron_link.go` — starts the scheduler on a supervised ticker thread across served profile homes, refuses dispatch while draining, misfire catch-up every 5 ticks, queue drain through each profile's adapters, interrupted-job notices
- `cron_store_notices.go` — announces an unwritable cron store once to the profile's home channels, and its recovery an hour later unless it degraded again
- `run_cron_homes.go` — profile homes the ticker visits; per-profile log routing under multiplexing
- `run_cron_homes_gate.go` — skips a profile home another live gateway process owns

#### Kanban integration

Two supervised watchers. The dispatcher holds a singleton lock at `kanban/.dispatcher.lock` so only one gateway spawns workers; the notifier delivers task events to subscribed chats and wakes the session that created the task.

- `kanban_hooks.go` — hook variables; `/kanban` fallback reply and idle probe for builds without kanban
- `kanban_watchers.go` — notifier loop (5 s, `kanban.notify_in_gateway`), dispatcher boot and loop (`kanban.dispatch_in_gateway`), artifact uploads as image batches, videos or documents
- `kanban_watchers_dispatcher.go` — per-board dispatch tick with spawn, in-progress, failure and stale limits, default assignee, corrupt-board quarantine until the file changes or a retry interval passes, auto-decompose of triage tasks (`kanban.auto_decompose`)
- `kanban_watchers_notifier.go` — claims unseen events per subscription, formats completed, blocked, gave-up, timed-out and review pings with redacted paths, drops a chat after 12 failures, advances the cursor only after notify and wake succeed
- `kanban_watchers_common.go` — off-loop helpers, board listing, settings readers, the advisory singleton lock
- `slash_commands_kanban.go` — `/kanban <args>` runs the kanban CLI and subscribes the chat to a task it created

#### Event hooks loaded from the home `hooks/` directory

User-installed hook directories receive gateway lifecycle events; a `command:<name>` hook may answer `deny`, `handled` or `rewrite`. This is separate from the plugin hook system in `pkg/plugins`.

- `hooks.go` — loads `hooks/<name>/HOOK.yaml` (events, `command`, timeout) per served profile and runs the command with the event as JSON on stdin; events `gateway:startup`, `session:start|end|reset`, `agent:start|step|end`, `command:<name>`, reactions, `base:*` wildcards; a Python `handler.py` is skipped with a notice

#### Plugin and platform glue

Small bridges between the runner and plugins, the platform registry and the browser tool.

- `plugin_command_choice.go` — lets a plugin slash command ask a multiple-choice question in the chat through the clarify card, with text fallback and expiry
- `plugin_keyless_inject.go` — plugin message injection without a target key: goes to the calling local session, else to the single attached terminal UI session of the plugin's profile; refusals rate-limited in the log
- `platform_notice_label.go` — display label of a platform from the registry, else its title-cased key
- `browser_link.go` — binds the browser-session cleanup run at shutdown; excluded by the `icebath_core` and `icebath_noextras` tags

#### Slash commands: shared plumbing and identity

Every slash command first passes the access gate of the profile whose bot received it, read per platform and per DM or group scope. The gate is off until that platform config lists admin user ids; then admins run everything and other users only `/help`, `/whoami` and the configured `user_allowed_commands`. Mid-run `/status` and `/context` skip the gate; setting `/approvals` and adding a `/goal` gate stay admin-only, with local sessions exempt for `/goal`.

- `slash_commands.go` — bridge to the shared slash executor of `pkg/commands`; `/profile` (serving profile and home), `/whoami` (scope, tier, runnable commands), `/version`, `/bundles`
- `slash_commands_helpers.go`, `slash_commands_shared.go` — resident or cached agent lookup, reply threading metadata, per-platform command prefix, checkpoint manager, session-database-unavailable reply
- `slash_commands_session.go`, `slash_commands_session_guards.go` — who may resume what: explicit admins see all; others only sessions of the same chat origin and participant; Matrix bound to the same room

#### Slash commands: control, approvals and maintenance

Commands that act on the gateway process or on a blocked agent. `/restart` and `/update` leave marker files in the home so the next gateway instance can tell the requester the outcome.

- `slash_commands_control.go` — `/stop` (own turn, then same-chat or sibling-thread turns, then async delegations), `/platform list|pause|resume`, `/restart` (writes `.restart_notify.json` and `.restart_last_processed.json`), `/autoprune`, `/help`, `/commands`, `/sethome`
- `slash_commands_approval.go` — `/approve [session|always|all]` and `/deny [all] [reason]` for dangerous-command approvals blocking an agent
- `slash_commands_maintenance.go` — `/reload-skills`, `/curator`, `/debug` (upload or local report), `/update` (git installs only; writes `.update_pending.json`), `/reload-mcp` with confirm
- `slash_commands_update_spawn.go` — spawns `icebath update --gateway` detached, writing `.update_output.txt` and `.update_exit_code`

#### Slash commands: session management

Commands that end, switch, rewrite, copy or export the chat's session; `/new` and `/undo` sit behind the destructive confirm prompt.

- `slash_commands_session_reset.go` — `/new` (ends the session, finalizes plugins, fires `session:end` and `session:reset`, clears tool state, shows a tip) and `/discard` (drops a turn lost in a restart)
- `slash_commands_session_resume.go` — `/resume [n|id|title]` lists or switches to a titled session; `/sessions` lists previous sessions
- `slash_commands_session_retry.go`, `slash_commands_session_undo.go` — `/retry` rewinds to before the last user message and re-sends it in one admission; `/undo [n]` soft-deletes the last n user turns
- `slash_commands_session_save.go` — `/save` sends the session export as a document; `/title` shows or sets the title and records the chat origin
- `slash_commands_session_branch.go`, `slash_commands_branch_thread.go` — `/branch [here] [title]` copies the session into a new one, in a sibling thread where the platform has threads
- `slash_commands_session_topic.go` — `/topic` manages Telegram DM topic mode and restores sessions into topics
- `slash_commands_session_compress.go` — `/compress [focus]` manual compression with preview, Codex app-server variant and failure reporting

#### Slash commands: model, reasoning and settings

Commands that change how the next turns run. Session-scoped choices live in `SessionState`; global ones are written to the profile's `config.yaml`.

- `slash_commands_model_command.go`, `slash_commands_model_switch.go` — `/model` picker or listing, switch under a per-session lock with global, session or one-turn scope, reset, refusal when the binary is older than the checkout, context-fit warning
- `slash_commands_model_reasoning.go` — `/reasoning` (effort and display, session or global) and `/fast` (priority service tier)
- `slash_commands_model_personality.go` — `/personality` (list or persist) and `/codex-runtime` (show or switch)
- `slash_commands_settings.go` — `/memory` and `/skills` (review pending writes, toggle the gate), `/approvals` (set is admin-only), `/yolo`, `/verbose`, `/busy`, `/footer`
- `slash_commands_voice.go` — `/voice on|off|tts|status|join|leave`: per-chat voice reply mode and Discord voice channel membership

#### Slash commands: status, usage and workspace

Read-mostly reports about the session, its agents and its working directory.

- `slash_commands_status.go` — `/status` (model, context, tokens, queue, platforms) and `/context` (window gauge, compression state, breakdown)
- `run_model_context.go` — effective model route and context window (config pin, custom provider limit, detected or default) for `/context`, session info and startup warm-up
- `slash_commands_status_usage.go` — `/agents` (agents, processes, async jobs, delegations), `/usage` (tokens, rate limits, account credit, Codex reset redemption), `/insights`
- `slash_commands_workspace.go` — `/rollback` (list or restore filesystem checkpoints) and `/diff` (working-tree or session-baseline git diff, truncated)

#### Embedded assets

[data] Both files are embedded by files in the other part of this package.

- `assets/status_phrases.yaml` — default "still working" phrase catalog (`status` and `generic` lists) embedded by `status_phrases.go`; overridable through `display.status_phrases`
- `assets/telegram-botfather-threads-settings.jpg` — BotFather screenshot embedded by `run_topics_slash.go` and sent with the Telegram topic-mode setup instructions

#### Stray icebath home committed under `default/`

[stray] `default/` is a seeded profile home that some run created with the package directory as its home; nothing embeds or reads it.

- `default/SOUL.md` — the default persona seed that `pkg/config/soul.go` writes into a new home
- `default/state.db` — empty schema-only SQLite session database (zero sessions and messages)
- `default/state.db.{fts_rebuild,quarantine}.lock` — zero-byte lock files of that database

**Files `run_notifications*` through `run_write*`, plus `runner_*`, `runtime_*`, `status_*`, `thread_*`, `transcription_*`, `turn_*`** (168 files, 27,642 Go lines). This part holds the `GatewayRunner` struct and most of what the long-lived gateway process does once an inbound message has been admitted: running one agent turn per session and delivering its reply, relaying background-process and delegation results, starting up, recovering the previous run, draining and restarting. Its entry points are `Start`, `Stop`, `RequestRestart` and `WaitForShutdown` (driven by `run_bootstrap_start.go` in the other part and by `pkg/gatewaycli`), `handleMessageWithAgent` (called by `handleMessage` in `run_inbound_handle.go`), a roster of supervised watcher loops spawned at the end of startup, five control-socket verbs, and the contract interfaces through which `pkg/gateway` and `pkg/plugins` call back into the runner. It reads and writes marker files in the icebath home (`.clean_shutdown`, `.restart_notify.json`, the planned-restart marker, `.restart_failure_counts`, six `.update_*` files), `logs/tool_calls.log`, `logs/gateway_faulthandler.log`, `cache/gateway_assets/`, each served profile's `state.db`, the delivery ledger and the runtime status file that `icebath gateway status` reads (`gateway_state` of `starting`, `running`, `degraded`, `draining`, `stopped` or `startup_failed`, `exit_reason`, per-platform `platform_state`, `error_code`, `error_message`, `needs_attention`, `retrying_since`, and `parked_profiles`). Port scaffolding is everywhere but thin: the runner is eight embedded "mixin" state structs, agent results and events travel as `map[string]any` kwargs dictionaries, `recover()` blocks stand in for Python's broad `except`, errors carry Python exception class names, and nearly every file imports `internal/py*`; real behaviour sits inside all of it. Everything here is implemented and reachable except two export shims that only tests call; oddities worth knowing are a surviving `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` environment check in the stop path and a downgrade watcher that greps the Go source files of its own checkout.

#### Runner object and state layout

[port-artifact] `GatewayRunner` is one struct that embeds eight state structs, one per Python mixin or module that used to assign attributes on `self`. The split by "which module sets it" is the artifact; the fields are the runner's real in-memory state, all unexported and reached through methods spread over both parts of the package.

- `runner.go` — the `GatewayRunner` struct: embeds the eight state structs below and declares nothing else
- `runner_state_core.go` — constructor state: gateway config, primary and per-profile adapter maps, session store and delivery router, running, draining, restart and exit flags, executors, per-session state map, turn leases, agent cache, completion dedupe sets and batch queues, pairing stores, hook registries, scale-to-zero clocks; `allocGatewayRunner` defaults (busy modes `interrupt`)
- `runner_state_adapters.go` — session authority handle, bot loop guard, secondary-profile resource claims, supervised watcher set with restart limits, plugin rewire subscriptions, retiring profiles
- `runner_state_inbound.go` — sessions lock, unauthorized-owner notifier, update watcher task, served profile homes, authority registry, Telegram lobby reminder stamps, heartbeat watch table
- `runner_state_turn.go` — agent cache bounds, per-agent process baselines, one-shot model and skills-reload notes, deferred agent workers and cleanups, pending provider-fallback notice, completion batch lock, model switch lock
- `runner_state_startup.go` — startup flags (cleanup only, parked platforms, ownership conflict), downgrade stop task, flood redelivery workers, health export handle, idle-exit counters
- `runner_state_reconcile.go` — served-profile serve signatures, reconcile lock, own-gateway and probe-timeout warning latches, shell-hook consent signatures
- `runner_state_runtime.go` — ticket store, control server and session API handle of the session runtime
- `runner_state_slash.go` — embeds the kanban watcher state and holds the BotFather hint cooldown stamps
- `runner_kanban_absent.go` — empty `runnerKanbanState` for builds tagged `icebath_core` or `icebath_noextras`; the real one lives in `kanban_watchers.go`
- `run_runtime_init.go` — constructor phases: loads prefill messages, reasoning, service tier, busy modes, human delay, drain and restart timeouts, provider routing and fallback chain; builds the session store (resets refused while a session has live processes), delivery router, lease registry (512), source cache (512), completion retention (2048) and 0.1 s batch window, pairing stores, hook registries
- `run_session_state.go` — locked accessors over the per-session `SessionState` map: create, peek, run a function under the session lock, read the running slot's agent, list running agents

#### Runner contracts and export shims for other packages

[port-artifact] Compile-time interface assertions plus exported one-line wrappers so that `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/plugins` and `pkg/gatewaycli` (which cannot import the runner's internals) can call it. Read together they are the runner's effective public surface beyond `Start` and `Stop`.

- `runner_contract_ingress.go` — `gateway.RunnerIngressContract`: profile adapter maps, credential fingerprints (current and legacy salt), adapter flags, user authorization, `HandleMessage`, durable crash-marker clear, running-slot queries and stale or reaped agent eviction, restored source, fallback model refresh, channel system prompt, unauthorized-DM behaviour (`pair`, `decline`, `ignore`)
- `runner_contract_delivery.go` — `gateway.RunnerDeliveryContract` and `plugins.PlatformActionRunner`: ledger redelivery and flood-retry wake, profile route lookup, delivery adapter, thread metadata, session key, plugin session ownership, gateway loop, platform parsing, shared-bot satellite test
- `runner_contract_live_turn.go` — `gateway.LiveTurnRunner`: pending slash-confirm and `/update` prompt checks, pending-reply intercepts, routing a bare approval word to a busy turn, busy-input preempt
- `runner_contract_model.go` — `gateway.RunnerModelContract`: channel override, session model and reasoning overrides, runtime resolution, model reset, switch and record, the runner-wide model switch lock
- `run_notifications_runner_ifaces.go` — exports a completion's identity (type, producer id, incarnation) and the completion-owner verdict to `pkg/gateway` automation ticks and detached-session follow
- `run_session_env_scope_export.go` — exports `SessionEnvScope` so `pkg/gateway` connection owner verbs can act as a session's caller
- `run_process_exit_export.go` — exports `ExitAfterGracefulShutdown` for `pkg/gatewaycli`
- `run_turn_runner_export.go`, `run_turn_prepare_runtime_export.go` — [unwired] exported `ResolutionFailureReply` and `ResolvePolicyAgentRuntime`; only test files call them

#### Turn entry: session resolution and preparation

`handleMessageWithAgent` runs one turn for an event that already holds its session's running slot. Order: resolve the session entry, open the session, bind the session tool environment, build the context prompt, auto-reset notice, auto-load skills, acquire the turn lease, write the durable active-turn marker, load the transcript, run hygiene, add first-contact and voice-channel notes, prepare the inbound text (other part), apply timestamps, then fire `agent:start`, run the agent, shape, persist and deliver.

- `run_turn_handle.go` — `handleMessageWithAgent`: the turn in the order above, the `agent:start` hook with a 500-character message preview, prompt pin persistence, discard of a result whose run generation is stale, reasoning and footer decoration, post-turn hooks, failure notice, exhaustion reset, transcript write, delivery; any error becomes a chat error reply
- `run_turn_prepare_session.go` — session entry resolution: Telegram lobby thread recovery, drop of internally routed events whose session key or pinned session id is no longer current, stopped claimed-turn check, async-delegation owner verification, Telegram topic binding healed to the compression tip, heartbeat owner check, `session:start` hook for new, auto-reset or fresh-reset sessions
- `run_turn_prepare_turn.go` — builds the `preparedTurn`: restores per-session yolo, session context prompt (skipped on the local platform, pinned for internal events), sidecar notes, lease, crash marker, transcript load with a "history unavailable" reply on read failure, hygiene, and a persistence owner id (UUIDv5 over platform, profile, scope, chat, thread and message id)
- `run_turn_prepare_lease.go` — acquires the per-session-id turn lease with `agent.gateway_turn_lease_timeout`; a timeout clears the session environment and refuses the turn
- `turn_lease.go` — `SessionTurnLeaseRegistry`: one lock per resolved session id serializing load, run and flush when two routing keys map to one session; 512 entries with idle eviction, 5 s default wait, fail-closed timeout error, rebind onto a rotated session id
- `run_turn_prepare_notes.go` — first-contact onboarding note for the very first DM and the one-time "no home channel, run `/sethome`" notice; the home channel is read from `<PLATFORM>_HOME_CHANNEL` (or the platform plugin's cron-delivery variable) and then config
- `run_turn_prepare_skills.go` — prepends channel- or topic-bound auto-skill payloads to the first message of a new session
- `run_turn_prepare_timestamp.go` — strips leading timestamps and the Discord trigger note from the text that is persisted, records the event time, and re-renders a timestamp for the model when gateway message timestamps are enabled
- `run_turn_session_info.go` — auto-reset handling: a "previous session was suspended" sidecar note with channel continuity, and a user notice listing model, provider, context length with its source, and a local endpoint URL
- `run_session_env.go` — per-turn `tools.Env`: the scoped profile's config and secrets plus session variables (platform, chat, thread, user, scope, session key and id, message id, profile, no-async-delivery flag)
- `run_session_env_scope.go` — runs a body with a session's variables bound and clears them on every exit; used when a plugin command handler runs
- `run_turn_scope.go`, `run_turn_scope_async.go` — profile runtime scope of a source: the routed profile's home and credentials under multiplexing, the launch scope otherwise (the async variant serves slash handlers)
- `run_turn_media_scope.go` — `MediaDeliveryScopeForSource`: the home, empty secret scope and terminal policy scope in which an adapter validates a turn's media paths under multiplexing

#### Pre-turn session hygiene compression

Before the agent starts, an oversized transcript is compressed by a detached helper agent. It fires for histories of four rows or more when auto-compress is on and the token count reaches 85% of the model context length or the message count reaches the hard limit; it is skipped during a failure cooldown or while another compression is in flight. The stored transcript is never overwritten by a summary that failed to commit.

- `run_turn_hygiene.go` — settings and plan (tokens from the last prompt, else a persisted anchor, else a rough estimate), the detached attempt (four iterations, memory toolset only) under a commit fence, a wait bounded by idle timeout, total ceiling and maximum turn hold, adoption by session rotation or in place, refusal of a rotation that grows the transcript, native compaction for codex app-server sessions, escalating failure cooldown and chat warnings
- `run_turn.go` — context-overflow verdict (provider phrases, or a 400 with more than 50 rows), bounding of the model payload to the hard message limit (setup head plus newest tail, never starting on a tool result) when hygiene does not land, the reason text for a compression that did not commit

#### Model, credential and route resolution

Decides which model, provider and credentials a turn uses. Precedence: a local launch policy's frozen route, then the session `/model` override, then the profile's provider credentials with its fallback chain, then a channel override's model or provider, then the provider's default model.

- `run_turn_prepare_runtime.go` — `resolveSessionAgentRuntime` with the precedence above, a fast path for overrides that carry an API key, an unavailable override provider falling back to config, and a one-shot provider-switch notice left for the next agent
- `run_runtime_agent_kwargs.go` — provider runtime turned into agent kwargs (key, base URL, provider, API mode, command and args, credential pool, request overrides, capabilities), the fallback entry's model and switch notice, deep merge of request overrides
- `run_turn_prepare_config.go` — per-turn route (model, runtime, cache signature) with fast-mode request overrides under a static service tier; writes the model and provider a turn actually ran on into the session row's `model_config.gateway_runtime`
- `run_turn_prepare.go` — remembers the last non-empty model per session and process-wide and recovers it when resolution returns an empty model
- `run_turn_agent_options.go` — copies runtime kwargs onto `agent.AIAgentOptions`; helper for reply-anchored thread metadata

#### Agent run orchestration on the gateway loop

`runAgent` wraps one turn in its profile scope and spawns its companion tasks (progress sender, tool-log writer, stream consumer, agent tracker, interrupt monitor, long-running notifier), starts the turn body on the executor, waits on it, then handles follow-ups and cleanup.

- `run_turn_agent.go` — `runAgent` and `runAgentInner`: proxy short-circuit, display settings (all progress off for scheduled heartbeats), task spawning, worker await, fallback eviction, streaming-TTS finalize, pending drain and recursive follow-up, streamed-delivery marking, bubble cleanup registration
- `run_turn_display.go` — per-platform display settings: tool progress mode (`off`, `new`, `all`, `verbose`, `log`), grouping, live status, interim assistant messages and thinking (opt-in only on Mattermost), Slack native task cards, progress cleanup; thread routing of progress and status sends for Slack, Buzz, Mattermost, Feishu and relay Discord; builds the `TurnContext`
- `turn_context.go` — `TurnContext`: every per-turn field shared between loop tasks and the worker (source, message, history, prompts, run generation, queues, holders for agent, result, stream and TTS consumers) and the unbounded `turnQueue`
- `run_turn_worker.go` — submits the turn body to the executor; an inactivity watchdog that warns at `agent.gateway_timeout_warning`, then at `agent.gateway_timeout` dumps goroutine stacks, hard-interrupts the agent, reaps its processes and returns a timeout reply naming the stuck tool; a 200 ms adapter interrupt monitor with a backup check
- `run_turn_workers.go` — `logs/tool_calls.log` writer (5 MB, three backups, redacting) for `log` mode; streaming TTS start for voice turns; stream consumer task; promotion of the turn's agent into the running slot; barge-in handling that transcribes a pending voice message, interrupts the agent and aborts TTS
- `run_turn_drain.go` — picks the follow-up after a turn: the adapter's pending event, a user interrupt message (gateway control reasons ignored), leftover steer text; drops known slash commands; during a drain keeps only events admitted before it
- `run_turn_followup.go` — runs the follow-up as a recursive `runAgent` (depth cap of three, then requeue), first delivering the previous reply and media unless streaming did; stale goal-continuation discard; processing hooks; keeps the outer history offset and tags the terminal inbound id
- `run_turn_finish.go` — turn cleanup (cancel tasks, flush the stream, abort TTS, release the slot); decides whether streaming already delivered the final (suppress the send, reconcile a stale finalize by edit, or edit in plugin-transformed text); temp bubble deletion after delivery; "still working" heartbeat every `agent.gateway_notify_interval`, edited in place
- `run_turn_finish_tts.go` — evicts the cached agent when a fallback model served a successful run; finalizes streaming TTS (10 s, then abort) and marks the turn so whole-file TTS is skipped
- `run_turn_events.go` — pops generation-owned post-delivery callbacks; stops the typing indicator for the turn's own message
- `run_reap_turn_processes.go` — kills only the background processes started after an abandoned turn's baseline, skipped when a newer turn owns the session

#### TurnRunner: the turn body on the executor thread

`TurnRunner` is the per-turn collaborator whose `runSync` is the worker body. It carries every callback the agent invokes, hops them back onto the gateway loop, and publishes execution events for local viewers and API observers when a session authority owns the session.

- `run_turn_runner.go` — the type and its constructor (binds the owning authority and runtime generation of a live session); execution events stamped with turn segments; API tool events; API runtime-lock settlement; resolution-failure replies (local runtime unavailable, launch credentials gone, rate-limited auth, host error, no credentials)
- `run_turn_runner_sync.go` — `runSync`: enters the local session policy scope, resolves model, provider routing, reasoning and service tier (API request options win), room execution limits, streaming, the cached or new agent, wires callbacks, runs the conversation and projects the result (usage and cost keys, compression flags, history offset, persisted-turn receipt, viewer fields)
- `run_turn_runner_run.go` — replay history (an API admission's own history, or disk with the live cached transcript preferred when disk lags, an error log after three lagging turns); resume-pending and interrupted-tool notes prepended to the message; the `RunConversationContent` call with turn author, persistence overrides and approval notify registered; token usage capture; session-split sync after compression
- `run_turn_runner_wire.go` — installs per-turn callbacks on the agent (progress, tool start and complete, step, stream delta, interim, status, notice, clarify, background review, event hooks), reasoning, tier, sidecar notes and request overrides, never baked into the cached agent; session-title callback that renames a Telegram topic or Discord auto thread
- `run_turn_runner_finish.go` — one-shot session notes, the combined ephemeral prompt (context prompt, channel prompt, channel system prompt), native image content parts, auto-appended `MEDIA:` tags for tool-produced files, stream consumer finish, Telegram thread id restore after a split
- `run_turn_runner_callbacks.go` — credit and out-of-band notices as chat lines, background-review messages held until the main reply is delivered, per-turn request override layering, closing a native stream before an interrupting prompt

#### Streaming to the platform and proxy mode

- `run_turn_runner_stream.go` — decides stream deltas and interim messages from the streaming config, the per-platform display setting, a plugin stream hold and the heartbeat flag; builds the `GatewayStreamConsumer`; fans deltas to the consumer, streaming TTS and local viewers; an unconsumed delta raises so the agent counts the text undelivered
- `run_turn_stream_config.go` — stream consumer config (edit interval, buffer threshold, cursor suppressed on Matrix and uneditable platforms, Telegram fresh-final and typing pause, transport); enabled and disabled toolsets per platform with an adapter override; `GATEWAY_PROXY_URL` lookup; run-generation predicate
- `run_turn_proxy.go` — proxy mode: with `GATEWAY_PROXY_URL` or `gateway.proxy_url` set, the turn is POSTed to a remote `/v1/chat/completions` (model `icebath-agent`, bearer `GATEWAY_PROXY_KEY`, `X-Icebath-Session-Id` header) and its SSE stream relayed instead of running a local agent; 30 s connect, 1800 s idle read, 16 MB line cap

#### Tool progress, status lines and task cards

- `run_turn_progress_callbacks.go` — the agent's tool-lifecycle callback feeding the progress queue, log queue and live status; thinking lines; a one-time spoken acknowledgement in a bound Discord voice channel; Slack task card events; `tool.start`, `tool.complete`, `todo.updated` and `agent.step` execution events and the `agent:step` hook
- `run_turn_progress.go` — progress line building per mode (emoji, verb, preview capped at 40 characters or the configured length, fenced terminal commands, verbose arguments), consecutive-duplicate counter `(×N)`, subagent failure notices, typing-bubble status text, one-time long-tool hint after 30 s
- `run_turn_progress_cards.go` — progress sender task: Slack native plan and task cards (last eight tasks, editable-text fallback; a chat that cannot host a card keeps text progress only when tool progress is on) or one editable bubble edited at most every 1.5 s, rolled into new bubbles at the platform length limit and reset when streamed content lands; platforms without message edit get no progress
- `run_turn_progress_status.go` — agent status, notice and lifecycle-event callbacks: chat status through the adapter's keyed status update, `status.update`, `notification.show` and `notification.clear` for local viewers, gateway hook emission
- `run_status_message.go` — status filter for chat platforms: redacts secrets, drops auxiliary-model, retry and compression chatter unless compression progress notices are enabled, rewrites provider error envelopes into category replies
- `status_phrases.go` — generic status phrase catalog with surfaces `status` and `generic`: embedded `assets/status_phrases.yaml`, then `status_phrases.yaml` or a `status_phrases/` directory in the home, then `display.status_phrases` (legacy alias `generic_status_phrases`) globally and per platform in append or replace mode; 80 phrases of 160 characters per surface; avoids the last six picks

#### Approval and clarify prompts

- `run_turn_runner_approval.go` — dangerous-command approval prompt: pauses typing, closes the native stream, redacts the command, sends native buttons where the adapter renders them (15 s send window, a timeout treated as possibly delivered, a connector decline unblocking the tool) or text with typed approve commands; registers the approval with the session authority
- `run_turn_runner_approval_settle.go` — on approval timeout edits the card to a timed-out body sized to the platform message limit, or sends the notice as a new message
- `run_turn_runner_clarify.go` — clarify tool: one card per question with choices and a skip hint, stopping at the first unanswered one; outcomes `submitted`, `cancelled`, `timed_out`, `undelivered`; a whole-batch panel for one-shot viewers; retirement of expired cards
- `run_turn_runner_clarify_delivery.go` — clarify send disposition: native card, numbered-text fallback, bounded wait, and a late-failure watch that retries once as text or releases the waiting agent

#### Reply shaping, transcript persistence and final delivery

- `run_turn_persistence.go` — after the run: silence-marker policy (rejected on turns that need a reply), `(empty)` explanation, resume-pending clear, session id sync after compression, reasoning block (15 lines, quote style per platform), runtime footer, `agent:end` hook and process watcher scheduling, failed-turn notices, compression-exhaustion auto reset, transcript rows (session meta on a first turn, only the user row on failure, nothing on overflow), voice reply, media and footer for already-streamed replies, HTTP status hints (401, 402, 429, 400, 529)
- `run_response_sanitize.go` — final-reply sanitizer: raw text kept for `local`, `api_server`, `webhook` and `msgraph_webhook`; secrets redacted on egress even with redaction off; short provider error envelopes replaced by category replies (rate limit with reset window, auth, policy, connection interrupted, unreachable); replies for empty, interrupted, storage-failure and overflow results

#### Turn executors

- `turn_executor.go` — unbounded executor for turn bodies: every item starts at once on a parked or new worker, parked workers exit after 60 s; the `gatewayExecutor` interface
- `thread_pool_executor.go` — [py-shim] clone of `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor` (work queue, idle count, shutdown lock, `ValueError`); the four-worker housekeeping pool depends on it
- `turn_thread_reset.go` — clears the interrupt flag, thread-scoped sudo password and log session tag before a worker is reused

#### Background process watchers and completion delivery

Processes the agent starts in the background are watched after the turn. Depending on the tool call's `notify_on_complete` and the profile's background notification mode (`off`, `error`, `result`, `concise`, `all`), the chat gets a notice, the agent gets a synthetic internal turn carrying the result, or both.

- `run_notifications_watcher.go` — per-process watcher (armed at turn end, mid-turn through `tools.ArmProcessWatcher`, and for recovered processes): polls at the watcher's interval, sends running output in `all` mode, builds the completion event (last 2000 characters, redacted), retries a refused injection up to eight times with backoff capped at 60 s, then falls back to a plain notice
- `run_process_notice.go` — concise completion line: finished or failed, shortened command, duration, exit code, the last five output lines and a rerun hint on failure
- `run_notifications_batch.go` — coalesces completions for one route inside a 0.1 s window into one synthetic event (ten shown, 800 characters each); dedupes by producer identity; claims the durable delegation row and verifies owner and transport before the adapter accepts; warns once per missing transport
- `run_notifications_batch_cancel.go` — settles waiting completion batches as undelivered and cancels their flush tasks before adapters are torn down
- `run_notifications_completion.go` — inflight and delivered identity sets (2048 retained), durable claim transitions (drop, release, defer, complete), delivery to a stateless `api_server` session by self-post wake or a persisted delegation row
- `run_notifications_drain.go` — drains the process registry's completion queue after each turn and from the watcher loop, each event inside its owning profile's scope, requeueing refusals
- `run_watch_events.go` — splits the queue: watch-pattern and heartbeat events are taken, async delegations put back, plain completions discarded because the process watcher owns them
- `run_notifications_inject.go` — turns an event into an internal `MessageEvent` and admits it through the session authority or the adapter's wake path; a refusal is permanent when the pinned session is gone
- `run_notifications_routes.go` — rebuilds the source of a synthetic event (persisted origin preferred), resolves the adapter including relay-admitted routes, requeues refused watch events on backoff and drops them after repeated permanent refusals

#### Async delegation completions and session ownership

- `run_notifications_async.go` — `asyncDelegationWatcher` (every 2 s): groups finished background delegations per session into one completion turn, backs off refused groups, and every 30 s offers completions whose owner process died, from the launch ledger and each served profile's
- `run_notifications_ownership.go` — decides where a completion may land: follows compression lineage to the live tip, walks `_delegate_from` provenance (16 hops), refuses sessions the user closed, and returns deliver, retry or terminal
- `run_user_boundary.go` — the end reasons no late completion may cross: `session_reset`, `user_exit`, `session_switch`, `new_session` (the same set is duplicated in `pkg/gateway`)

#### Operational notices, home channels and store outages

- `run_notifications.go` — grab bag: platform notices honouring `notice_delivery` (public or private) and Slack `ignored_channels`; post-stream media delivery (image batch, voice, video, document); queued-lane first reply through the delivery ledger; "gateway restarted" reply to the chat that asked (`.restart_notify.json`); "gateway online" to every served home channel with a planned-restart marker tracking delivered targets; session store outage note, probe write and home-channel warning; held transcript watcher (10 s)
- `run_notifications_home.go` — lists the home channels of the launch and served profiles that have a live transport and sends to one
- `run_store_hold.go` — while `state.db` refuses writes, user messages are held in memory with a "waiting" reply, re-run per chat in arrival order once a probe write lands (600 s wait per message), and spooled to `pending_messages` at shutdown

#### Update progress relay to chat

- `run_notifications_update.go` — watcher for a chat-initiated `/update`: reads `.update_pending.json`, `.update_pending.claimed.json`, `.update_output.txt`, `.update_exit_code`, `.update_prompt.json` and `.update_response` in the home; streams output in fenced chunks every 4 s, forwards prompts (buttons where supported), sends the finished or failed notice, gives up after 30 minutes; at boot waits up to an hour for the requester's adapter

#### Startup sequence

`Start` runs: install crash dumps; bind loop guards and write status `starting`; access-policy check; recover the previous run; close the inbound gate and begin warm-up; create and wire an adapter per enabled platform; connect them concurrently; bring up secondary profiles; handle the no-connection cases; mark running, install the plugin injector and publish `running` or `degraded`; post-connect services and boot notices; pending-message recovery and auto-resume; open the gate; recover native sessions and process watchers; spawn the background watchers. A restart or shutdown requested at any step aborts cleanly.

- `run_startup_sequence.go` — `Start`, `startImpl` and the phases above; the supervised watcher roster (housekeeping 300 s, model catalog, stall 30 s, kanban, reconnect, handoff 2 s, async delegation 2 s, loop wakeup 15 s, held transcripts 10 s, profile reconcile 30 s, downgrade, scale-to-zero 30 s); `gateway:startup` hook, channel directory build, relay self-provision retry, hosted room worker keep-alive, health OTLP export, plugin security advisory log
- `run_startup_access.go` — warns when no chat platform has an allowlist and refuses to start when an enabled platform has `dm_policy` or `group_policy` `open` without an allow-all opt-in (status `startup_failed`)
- `run_startup_connect.go` — concurrent startup connects that tear down cleanly on restart or shutdown; transient failures queued for the reconnect watcher (first retry 30 s); fatal multiplexer config exits 78; with nothing connected the gateway stays up degraded for cron and local clients, parks fatally misconfigured platforms, and exits only on a token or profile ownership conflict
- `run_startup_guards.go` — iteration budget log, parking the last fatally failed platform, loop floor timer, liveness watchdog and heartbeat task, crash output to `logs/gateway_faulthandler.log`, warning for a retired timed session reset in config, systemd `TimeoutStopSec` versus drain mismatch warning, launch profile shell-hook registration
- `run_startup_stop_guards.go` — disarms the loop watchdog, floor timer and heartbeat before shutdown; pauses the hosted room worker
- `run_startup_faulthandler.go`, `run_startup_faulthandler_{unix,other}.go` — all-goroutine stack dump to the faulthandler log on `SIGUSR2`; the two per-OS files only define the signal, none off POSIX
- `run_startup_warmup.go` — boot warm-up overlapping the connects: materializes tool schemas, runs the environment probe, resolves the model context length; bounded by `agent.gateway_startup_warmup_timeout`; the shared wait-bounded-then-release helper
- `run_startup_serving_state.go` — `degraded` while a startup platform failure is parked, otherwise `running`

#### Recovery of the previous run

What survives a restart: `.clean_shutdown` tells a clean exit from a crash; routing entries carry active-turn markers and resume-pending flags; the delivery ledger holds final replies that were owed; process checkpoints and undelivered completion rows are replayed.

- `run_startup_unclean.go` — consumes `.clean_shutdown` (discarding orphan turn markers, failing closed if cleanup fails); otherwise recovers only the turns the dead process left marked: a persisted final reply is ledgered as an owed delivery, the rest are marked for resume; age bound of the larger of one hour and twice the turn timeout
- `run_startup_resume.go` — auto-continues fresh `restart_timeout`, `shutdown_timeout` and `restart_interrupted` sessions with a synthetic empty internal turn after re-checking the owner's authorization and the restart-loop breaker; runs the boot sends (restart notice, planned-restart replay, ledger redelivery) bounded so they cannot pin the inbound gate
- `run_startup_restore.go` — the inbound gate during startup restore: queues messages that arrive while auto-resume runs, waits `agent.gateway_startup_restore_drain_timeout`, then replays them through their adapters
- `run_startup_obligations.go` — delivery ledger at boot and after a reconnect: claims recoverable rows whose exact bot is connected, clears their resume flags first, re-sends final replies (prefixed with a recovered marker when the row asks for one), and runs one deadline-driven flood-retry worker per bot identity
- `run_startup_checkpoints.go` — replays each served secondary profile's background process checkpoint under its own scope

#### CLI-to-chat session handoff

Executes a handoff row queued by a terminal session: the conversation continues on a chat platform's home channel. The polling watcher that finds rows is in the other part.

- `run_startup_handoff.go` — resolves the destination: platform, the queuing profile's own adapters and config (failing closed), home channel, a fresh handoff thread when the adapter can create one, the session key by the adapter's own rules; repoints the route at the CLI conversation's head and moves a viewer's mount with it
- `run_startup_process_handoff.go` — runs the handoff as a synthetic internal turn asking the agent to confirm and summarize, and posts the reply to the home channel or thread

#### Stop sequence, drain and restart

`Stop` runs once (later callers wait on the first) under a thread watchdog: mark draining, withdraw admission and notify chats; mark running sessions resume-pending and drain; on timeout interrupt, wait a grace period and kill tool subprocesses; let authorities settle; finalize agents and disconnect adapters; release state and spool pending messages; quiesce the executor and close databases; write exit markers and the final status. `RequestRestart` first waits for in-flight turns up to `agent.restart_after_turn_timeout`.

- `run_shutdown_stop.go` — `Stop`, `RequestRestart`, `WaitForShutdown` and the phases above; session databases are closed only when no executor, cron, API or deferred worker can still write; `.clean_shutdown` is skipped after a timed-out drain; a signal-initiated stop without restart persists `gateway_state` `running` so a container boot restarts it; the watchdog is disabled when `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` is set
- `run_shutdown.go` — exit verdict (failure, explicit code, 75 for a service-manager restart, 1 for a signal without restart request); stop timing and watchdog leash under launchd; API-server run interrupt hooks; scale-to-zero (an opted-in, relay-only gateway with a registered wake URL quiesces the relay when idle, then suspends its machine through the in-guest Fly API socket or a brokered sleep URL, staying awake on any failure); `/platform` pause and resume of a failed platform
- `run_shutdown_drain.go` — drain wait (chat and deferred work up to the drain timeout, cron and API runs up to the cron budget), hard interrupt of agents, API runs, deferred workers, managed turns and side agents, resume-pending marking with reason `restart_timeout` or `shutdown_timeout`
- `run_shutdown_active_work.go` — the work counts the drain and status expose: running agents, cron jobs, API server runs, deferred executor workers
- `run_shutdown_describe_active_work.go` — one descriptor per in-flight unit (kind, session, model, current tool, idle and elapsed seconds) for restart-wait logs
- `run_shutdown_agents.go` — shutdown transcript flush with a recovery snapshot file on failure; plugin session finalize and reset hooks off the loop (10 s bound) and delivery of their end-of-session messages; `.restart_failure_counts` stuck-loop detector that suspends a session active across three consecutive restarts
- `run_shutdown_cleanup.go` — agent teardown: flush pending memory writes (10 s), end the memory session, close tool resources; run on the housekeeping pool with a 30 s bound, or deferred until the agent's worker finishes
- `run_shutdown_notices.go` — "restarting" or "shutting down" notice to every chat with a running turn and every served home channel, deduped per chat, honouring `gateway_restart_notification: false`; home channels are skipped for an in-chat `/restart`
- `run_shutdown_restart.go` — detached restart helper (a `setsid bash -lc` loop on POSIX, a watcher subprocess on Windows) that runs `icebath gateway restart` once this pid exits; the restart wait that excludes wedged turns and restart-safe cron runs; systemd watchdog start and stop
- `run_shutdown_runtime_status.go`, `run_write_runtime_status.go` — per-platform runtime status write (state, error code and message, needs attention, retrying since) that never fails or blocks the caller
- `run_shutdown_send_result.go`, `run_shutdown_log.go` — send-result failure helpers and suppressed-error loggers used across the package

#### Process exit, self-stop watchers and reconnect policy

- `run_process_exit.go` — planned-stop marker poller that triggers shutdown when the marker names this process; refusal to start on an unparseable `config.yaml` (exit 2); the final exit that removes the pid file and runtime lock, stamps the exit and drains the log queue
- `runtime_downgrade_exit.go` — every 30 s checks whether the checkout moved to a release without the runtime ledger, by reading `pkg/state/*.go` in the repository for the `session_admissions` schema line; after two confirmations, and not during an update, stops with exit 75
- `run_reconnect.go` — reconnect policy helpers for the watcher in the other part: 30 s doubling to a 300 s cap, attention flag after `agent.reconnect_attention_after`, bot-credential presence test (WhatsApp `creds.json`, token or API key, Matrix password login), planned-restart marker path

#### Session runtime: authorities, descriptor and session API

The session runtime is the layer of per-profile `SessionAuthority` objects (defined in `pkg/gateway`) that own durable turn admissions. The runner builds one per reserved profile home, publishes a runtime descriptor (`instance_id`, `runtime_protocol` 1, `state` of `starting`, `ready`, `draining` or `failed`, `served_profiles`, `authority_epoch`, `api_origin`) and starts the loopback listener that serves the native session socket; the control socket's identify verb hands this descriptor to local clients.

- `run_runtime.go` — `initializeGatewayRuntime`: requires process ownership of each reserved home, opens each profile's `state.db`, builds authorities (a secondary with an unusable store is parked, the launch one fails the start) and the bootstrap ticket store; reserve, release and withdraw of profile homes; `parked_profiles` in descriptor and runtime status
- `run_runtime_descriptor.go` — copy-on-write descriptor and parked-profile maps safe to read from other goroutines
- `run_runtime_init_descriptor.go`, `run_runtime_registry.go`, `run_runtime_ticket_store.go` — exported getters for the descriptor, the authority registry and the ticket store
- `run_runtime_ready.go` — publishes `ready` and starts hosted room services, the systemd watchdog and idle exit as one step a concurrent stop waits out; fails the runtime when the session API listener dies unprompted
- `run_runtime_drain.go` — sets `draining`, stops hosted rooms and withdraws every adapter's message handler so no new work is admitted while egress stays up
- `run_runtime_settle.go` — at stop lets authority tasks finish their durable settlement writes (up to 45 s, inside the stop budget less a 10 s tail reserve), ends idle ACP sessions, revokes tickets, stops the session API
- `run_runtime_recover.go` — recovers local sessions, webhook finalizations and native sessions of every serving authority after adapters connect
- `run_runtime_serve.go` — serve and unserve of one profile's runtime at boot or hot: build the authority, recover its Bot Chat mailbox, local sessions and API turns; retire with ownership retained when a turn outlives its stop; session API start

#### Multi-profile serving and reconcile

One gateway process can serve every profile ("multiplexing"): each profile has its own home, adapters, authority and scope. This group keeps the served set in step with the profiles on disk without a restart.

- `run_profile_reconcile_watch.go` — 30 s watcher: re-syncs shell hooks when a home's hook allowlist or `config.yaml` changes; switches a single-profile gateway to multiplexing when a second profile appears (unless opted out or blocked); diffs profiles against the served set, skips ones running their own gateway (5 s probe), and serves, unserves or rebuilds on a config or `.env` change
- `run_profile_reconcile.go` — a profile's serve signature (content versions of its config layer and `.env`), served-name ordering, the reconcile lock
- `run_profile_reconcile_verbs.go` — control-socket verbs `serve-profile` and `unserve-profile` (answering pending after 5 s), `migrate-profile-identity` (rekeys stores and routing on rename) and `purge-profile-identity` (drops them on delete)
- `run_profile_reconcile_served.go` — runs a chore once per served profile inside that profile's runtime scope
- `run_profile_reconcile_claims.go` — rebuilds the resource claim map from the live primary and secondary adapters

#### Session database handles, housekeeping and stall watchdog

- `run_session_db.go` — per-profile `state.db` handle cache (borrowing the session store's handle), the launch store open that fails the start, and state.db maintenance per `sessions.auto_archive` and `sessions.auto_prune` (retention 90 days, vacuum) for every served profile
- `run_watchers.go` — housekeeping loop (300 s): idle and memory-pressure agent cache sweeps, hourly prune of routing entries older than the session store's maximum age
- `run_watchers_stall.go` — stall watchdog: a session with pending inbound and an agent idle past `agent.session_stall_timeout` gets one notice per episode and is never interrupted; also holds the model catalog refresh loop

#### Plugin-triggered turns and hot reload

- `run_plugin_injection_schedule.go` — the process-wide scheduler plugins call to start a turn by session key, by origin, or keyless; refuses when the gateway is not running, when the session is not owned by the plugin's profile, or when the route is no longer authorized
- `run_plugin_injection_dispatch.go` — dispatch of the three forms: a durable FIFO admission through the authority, or an internal strict-session `MessageEvent` through the adapter
- `run_plugin_injection.go` — withdraws the scheduler at stop without clobbering a newer owner
- `run_plugin_rewire.go` — re-installs plugin command and callback handlers on a profile's live adapters whenever its plugin manager reloads
- `run_plugin_rewire_reload.go` — control-socket verb `reload-plugins`: rediscovers plugins under a served home, reconciles their MCP servers (10 s wait), reports active plugins and the rewired adapter count
- `run_turn_mcp_reload.go` — `/reload-mcp`: shuts down and reconnects MCP servers (only the requesting profile's under multiplexing), reports reconnected, added and removed servers, refreshes cached agents' tools and appends a system note to the transcript

#### Telegram DM topic mode, Discord auto threads and thread metadata

Topic mode turns a Telegram private chat with forum topics into parallel conversations: each user-created topic is its own session lane, and the root DM or General topic is a lobby for system commands. The mode flag and the topic-to-session bindings live in `state.db` per profile.

- `run_topics_lane.go` — topic lane test and the topic-to-session binding write (`managed_mode` `auto`), refreshed whenever the session id rotates
- `run_topics_recover.go` — topic mode flag read, root lobby test, the bot's `dm_topic_auto_transfer` opt-in, recovery of the user's newest bound topic for a lobby-shaped message, source normalization before session keys are derived
- `run_topics_lobby.go` — lobby replies and a 30 s reminder cooldown per profile and chat
- `run_topics_transfer.go` — auto-transfer of a root DM message into a newly created topic
- `run_topics_new_header.go` — new-session header text for a topic lane
- `run_topics_slash.go` — `/topic` support: `getMe` capability flags, a managed System topic with a pinned intro, the BotFather Threads Settings screenshot (embedded `assets/telegram-botfather-threads-settings.jpg`, 300 s cooldown), disabling topic mode, status with unlinked sessions, restoring a session into a topic
- `run_topics_title_rename.go` — renames the Telegram topic (120 code points) or the Discord auto thread (80 UTF-16 units) to the model-generated session title; skips operator-declared and rebound topics and honours `disable_topic_auto_rename`; handles threads the relay connector created
- `run_topics_discord_lane.go` — detects Discord threads the gateway auto-created (recovering the markers from the session's stored origin) and relay-delivered channel lanes
- `run_thread_metadata.go` — send metadata per platform: thread id, Telegram DM topic and reply anchors, Slack team and user identity, routed profile, the `non_conversational` flag on Discord lifecycle sends

#### Voice: spoken replies, Discord voice channels, transcription

- `run_voice_load.go` — per-chat voice mode (`off`, `voice_only`, `all`) stored in the process home's settings
- `run_voice_state.go` — voice mode keys (profile-namespaced under multiplexing), mirroring a mode into the adapter's auto-TTS sets, restore on connect with the speak-replies default
- `run_voice_reply.go` — spoken reply decision (chat mode, voice input, adapter auto-TTS; never for errors, `a2a`, local turns, a voice-input turn whose text was not already streamed, or when the agent already called `text_to_speech`), synthesis, playback in a joined voice channel or a voice message send, temp file cleanup
- `run_voice_channel.go` — `/voice channel` (or `join`) and `/voice leave` for the caller's Discord voice channel, binding its speech to the text channel, cleanup when the call times out
- `run_voice_input.go` — voice channel utterance intake: builds the source from the bound text channel, role and user authorization, duplicate suppression (12 s window, 95% similarity), transcript echo with mentions neutralized, dispatch as a voice message event with channel prompt and skills
- `run_voice_guild_id.go` — guild id of a Discord event from a slash interaction or a message
- `run_probe_audio_duration.go` — audio duration for voice transcription notes: WAV header and Ogg Opus granule parsed in-process (hand-ported from Python's `chunk` and `wave` modules and mutagen), else `ffprobe` with a 5 s limit; `pkg/media` has a separate function of the same name
- `transcription_media.go` — binds inbound voice transcription to `pkg/media` speech-to-text unless built with `icebath_core`

#### Unavailable skill hint

- `run_unavailable_skill.go` — reply for a slash command that names a disabled skill or an optional skill that is not installed, giving its `official/…` install name

### `pkg/gatewayapi` — the `api_server` platform adapter: the gateway's HTTP API over real agent turns

*34 files, 12,445 Go lines*

The gateway's programmatic API. `register.go` publishes an `api_server` builtin platform module, and the gateway runner constructs and connects `APIServerAdapter` like any chat adapter; it listens on `127.0.0.1:8642` by default and runs agent turns for OpenAI-compatible clients, external and browser UIs, peer gateways (Bot Chat peers and RoomLink room homes) and the gateway's own wake path. The split with `pkg/gateway/api_server_*.go` is: this package owns the adapter, the route table, every handler, auth, admission, run state and SSE writers, while `pkg/gateway` owns the generic HTTP app (`aiohttp_web*.go`), content normalization, the `/p/{profile}` resolver, the SQLite response and run-idempotency stores and the session-authority operations, all reached through exported wrappers. It persists `response_store.db` per profile home and the run-idempotency store, and reads and writes sessions in `state.db`. Two execution paths exist for every turn: when the runner holds a session authority the turn is admitted to that session's FIFO and only observed here, otherwise the adapter builds an `AIAgent` and runs it on its own worker. The Python shape is heavy (ordered `pyjson.Object` bodies, Python exception names in error paths, a file called `module.go`), but the behaviour is product. The package is linked by a blank import in `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go`, so core and no-extras builds have no API server.

#### Adapter lifecycle, listener, auth and middleware

Construction reads `platforms.api_server` extras (`host`, `port`, `key`, `cors_origins`, `model_name`, `model_routes`, `direct_model_requests`, `tool_progress_events`) with env fallbacks `API_SERVER_KEY`, `API_SERVER_CORS_ORIGINS`, `API_SERVER_MODEL_NAME`, plus `gateway.api_server.max_concurrent_runs` (10) and `history_tool_output_max_chars`. Auth is `Authorization: Bearer` compared in constant time against `API_SERVER_KEY`; the listener refuses to start when the key is missing, a placeholder or under 16 characters, even on loopback, and a `/p/{profile}` request for a named profile must match that profile's own key and fails closed without one. Every route is registered twice, plain and under `/p/{profile}`, and unmatched `/p/{profile}/...` paths are handed to that profile's other listener adapters. Only `/health` and `/v1/health` are open; platform event callbacks are authenticated by the target adapter's own verifier and room routes by a signed grant.

- `register.go` — `init` registering the `api_server` platform module with its adapter constructor and an always-true requirements probe
- `assertions.go` — compile-time checks of the gateway interfaces the adapter satisfies: platform adapter, delegation delivery store, self-post endpoint, internal session turn runner, API turn adapter, run admitter, shutdown hooks
- `adapter.go` — `APIServerAdapter` struct and constructor, bearer auth, per-profile key lookup, CORS origin rules, audit log fields, shutdown interrupt of live agents, daily request, token and p95-latency metrics, 30 s runtime-status heartbeat
- `connect.go` — key startup guard, middleware chain and route registration, bind with five retries on a held port, fatal errors `api_server_key_invalid` and `api_server_port_in_use`, disconnect teardown, `SelfPostTarget`
- `routes.go` — the main route table, `/p/{profile}` prefix middleware, `POST /api/platforms/{platform}/events` callback ingress, `X-Icebath-Session-Key` validation and binding, per-home response store and session DB caches
- `module.go` — grab bag: limits, capabilities table and feature flags, CORS, body-limit and security-header middlewares, OpenAI error envelope, admission wrapper with drain 503, in-memory idempotency cache (1000 entries, 300 s), derived chat session id, SSE event queue, turn process reaping
- `wire_headers.go` — accepts `X-Hermes-*` request headers as their `X-Icebath-*` names and renames them in stored replay records, for older peers
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Health, discovery and session resource routes

`GET /health`, `/v1/health` (open) and `/health/detailed`; `GET /v1/models` (advertised model plus route aliases), `/api/model/options` (picker inventory), `/v1/capabilities` (machine-readable surface for external UIs), `/v1/skills`, `/v1/toolsets`; `/api/sessions` list and create, `/api/sessions/{id}` get, patch and hard delete, `/api/sessions/{id}/messages` (paged across the compression lineage) and `/api/sessions/{id}/fork`. Patch accepts only `title`, `end_reason`, `pinned`, `archived`, `hidden`, `unread`. The capabilities payload advertises `jobs_admin`, `admin_config_rw`, `memory_write_api`, `audio_api` and `realtime_voice` as false, and does not list the jobs or room routes although they are served.

- `sessions.go` — all of the handlers above, client-safe session and message projections, `RunInternalSessionTurn` for the gateway's background wake turns, and the session-authority lookup

#### Session chat routes and runtime selection

`POST /api/sessions/{id}/chat` runs one synchronous turn; `/chat/stream` is the SSE form with `run.started`, `message.started`, `assistant.delta`, `tool.started`, `tool.completed`, `tool.failed`, `tool.progress` (reasoning), `assistant.commentary`, `approval.request`, `assistant.completed`, `error` and `done` events; `POST /api/sessions/{id}/model` acknowledges a browser model lock. Runtime precedence is confirmed session lock, gateway per-session override, stored session model, configured `model_routes` alias, then per-request provider and model (a bare request model is honoured only with `direct_model_requests`).

- `chat.go` — session chat prelude and both chat handlers, one policy-gated re-run of a transient failure, stream approval registration, client-disconnect interrupt, handoff of a turn aimed at a live Bot Chat to its owner
- `runtime.go` — `model_routes` validation, model lock persistence in the session's `model_config`, provider runtime resolution with typed auth errors, last-known-good model fallback, and `createAgent` building the agent with the `api_server` toolsets

#### Agent turn execution

The shared path every route uses to run one turn, with concurrency capped by `max_concurrent_runs` (429 when full).

- `runagent.go` — `runAgent`: binds session variables, builds and runs the agent on a counted worker or defers to the session authority, attaches usage, effective session id and runtime metadata
- `runagent_export.go` — `PrepareTurnRuntime` and `TurnRuntimeMetadata`, called by the gateway when it executes an API admission, applying the admission's route and checking a confirmed lock
- `api_turn.go` — builds the canonical `APITurn` handed to the authority FIFO, observer callback adapters, streaming run id aliases for approval answers
- `memory_sessions.go` — parks one initialised memory manager per profile home and session between requests, bounded by the agent cache size and idle TTL, shut down off the request path

#### OpenAI chat completions and Responses API

`POST /v1/chat/completions` (streaming or not) and `POST /v1/responses` with `GET` and `DELETE /v1/responses/{id}`. Supports `Idempotency-Key` with body fingerprinting, `X-Icebath-Session-Id` continuity, `previous_response_id` and named conversation chaining, stored snapshots, 10 s SSE keepalives, and replay of a settled keyed stream.

- `openai_routes.go` — chat and Responses input parsing, route and override selection, stream agent spawning, the chat completions handler and its non-streaming response
- `openai_routes_sse.go` — chat completion chunk writer, Responses SSE writer and replay, per-principal idempotent execution, implicit chat session resolution
- `openai_responses.go` — Responses handler, stored response get and delete, conversation history rebuilding, extraction of this turn's output items
- `openai_responses_stream.go` — Responses event emitter: sequence numbers, message, reasoning-summary and function-call items, 50 ms text batching, incomplete and terminal snapshots
- `openai_helpers.go` — finish reason and status mapping, response identity, store-unit helpers, tool-output capping for history and completed envelopes
- `response_admissions.go` — durable Responses admission under a session authority: lookup of an already admitted key, session restore, successor binding, first-time validation

#### Structured runs API

`POST /v1/runs` returns a run id at once (202); `GET /v1/runs/{id}` polls status; `GET /v1/runs/{id}/events` streams lifecycle events over SSE with replay from a sequence; `POST .../approval`, `.../clarify`, `.../steer`, `.../stop` and `.../resolve-unknown` control it. Runs are owned by the authenticated principal scope, accept the API key or a room grant, keep 1000 events per stream and 256 queued per subscriber, expire transports after 300 s and terminal status after an hour, and persist keyed runs so a restart answers them with a dead owner failed closed.

- `runs_handle.go` — runs route rows, `handleRuns` admission with idempotent replay, the synchronous worker body, per-run tool environment
- `runs_execute.go` — drives an admitted run to its terminal event, approval bridge, execution through a live Bot Chat owner
- `runs_routes.go` — status, events, approval, clarify, steer, stop and resolve-unknown handlers
- `runs_state.go` — run stream fan-out, per-request state, run status persistence, shutdown marking, progress-event shaping with redaction, run auth and owner scope
- `runs_lifecycle.go` — ownership checks, durable status hydration, conversation history resolution, replay or conflict answers, orphan sweep every minute
- `runs_authority.go` — admits a run to the session authority FIFO and observes its settled result
- `authority_runs.go` — authority-run projection for polling, respond, stop, steer and unknown-admission resolution, store-error responses

#### Bot Chat peer turns

Lets another profile or peer gateway submit a turn into a profile's canonical "Bot Chat" session through the API and wait for the delivery receipt.

- `bot_chat.go` — peer creation of the titled Bot Chat, admission of a peer turn to its FIFO, refusal reasons, bounded wait on the live delivery receipt

#### RoomLink member routes

Cross-gateway rooms: a room's home gateway invites a profile here as a member, then dispatches runs, pushes turn files, pulls reply files and syncs shared room pages. `POST /v1/room-members/invitations` (API key) mints a signed grant with a 60 s to 24 h dispatch TTL and a status horizon up to 30 days; the other routes take `Authorization: IcebathRoom <grant>` (legacy `HermesRoom`).

- `room_grants.go` — invitation, `GET /v1/room-members/capabilities`, `POST .../grants/refresh` and `.../grants/revoke`, grant verification, execution-policy digest check
- `room_dispatch.go` — validates a room-scoped `/v1/runs` dispatch and creates the member's hidden group session
- `room_files.go` — `POST` and `PUT /v1/room-members/files[/{file_id}]` chunked upload, `GET` chunked reply-file read, reply files staged on a finished run
- `room_share.go` — `POST /v1/rooms/sync` storing a room home's sync and returning queued operations

#### Cron jobs REST API

`GET` and `POST /api/jobs`, `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE /api/jobs/{id}`, and `POST .../pause`, `.../resume`, `.../run`, all behind the API key with 12-hex job id validation.
