- `jobs.go` — the eight handlers, prompt length and injection scan, request origin stamped on created jobs, scheduler-provider registration (424 on failure)

### `pkg/gatewaycli` — `icebath gateway`, `send` and `webhook` commands plus the CLI's gateway client

*35 files, 8,416 Go lines*

Implements the `gateway` command group, `icebath send`, `icebath webhook`, the `/snapshot` helper, service-manager detection, the s6 container supervisor backend and its boot reconcile, and the connection and session-store facade the classic CLI chat uses to talk to a gateway-owned session. `cmd/icebath` binds the commands; `pkg/app`, `pkg/acp`, `pkg/selfupdate`, `pkg/profiles/manage` and `pkg/containerinit` consume the rest. It writes s6 service directories under `/run/service`, `logs/gateway-exit-diag.log`, relay credentials into the profile `.env`, and `webhook_subscriptions.json` through `pkg/webhooksubs`; most real service work (systemd, launchd, Windows tasks, the runner itself) lives in `pkg/gateway` and `pkg/gatewayrun`.

#### `icebath gateway` lifecycle verbs

Subcommands: `run` (default; foreground gateway with `--replace`, `--force`, `--no-supervise`, `--external-supervisor`), `start`, `stop`, `restart` (`--all`, `--system`, `--interrupt`, `--detach`), `status` (`--deep`, `--full`), `install` and `uninstall` (systemd, launchd or Windows task), `list`, `setup`, `migrate-legacy` (remove old units), `migrate` (delegates to `gatewayrun`), plus `enroll` and `ensure` below. One gateway per host serves every profile (the "host multiplexer"); verbs on a named profile are routed to it, and stop and restart refuse while sessions have live work unless `--interrupt` or a terminal confirmation.

- `gateway_cmd.go` — dispatch helpers and `setup`, `install`, `uninstall`, `start`, `stop`, `status`, `list`, `migrate-legacy`; Termux and container no-backend messages; refusal of self-targeting verbs from inside the gateway
- `gateway_cmd_run.go` — `run` and `restart`: host-gateway attach or conflict guards, Docker root guard, startup watchdog, respawn-storm backoff, exit diagnostics log, redirect of a bare run to s6 supervision, command dispatcher `GatewayCommand`
- `gateway_cmd_status.go` — status sections: runtime health, process and service mismatch, served ingress URLs, other profiles' gateways, duplicate credential warnings, the `list` table
- `gateway_cmd_support.go` — live-work refusal, incompatible-version owner report, externally supervised restart by SIGUSR1 drain, parked-satellite status, named-profile lifecycle inside the host gateway
- `gateway_command_errors.go` — turns a failed `systemctl` start, stop or restart into guidance lines
- `gateway_cmd_console_{other,windows}.go` — whether a console window is attached and ignoring console control broadcasts for a detached Windows gateway
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Relay enrollment and runtime ensure

- `gateway_enroll.go` — `gateway enroll`: posts a single-use token to the relay connector and saves `GATEWAY_RELAY_ID`, `GATEWAY_RELAY_SECRET`, `GATEWAY_RELAY_DELIVERY_KEY` and optional URLs to the profile `.env`; refused on managed installs
- `gateway_runtime_cli.go` — `gateway ensure --timeout`: ensures a local gateway runtime and prints one credential-free JSON verdict with a state-specific exit code, for other clients

#### Service managers and s6 container supervision

A `ServiceManager` interface with systemd, launchd, Windows and s6 backends; only s6 supports registering per-profile gateways at runtime. Inside the container image each profile gateway is an s6 longrun `gateway-<profile>` with generated `run`, `finish` (no restart after exit 0 or the fatal-config code) and rotating log scripts, run as the `icebath` account.

- `service_manager.go` — backend detection, the interface and host backends, `S6ServiceManager` (register, unregister, start, stop, restart, list, supervised pid), desired-state file, script rendering
- `service_manager_{unix,windows}.go` — `mkfifo` and `lchown`, failing on Windows the way Python's `os` does
- `gateway_multiplex_s6.go` — folds running named-profile slots into the root slot for multiplex mode, parks named slots, installs the s6 hooks `gateway migrate` uses
- `container_boot.go` — `ContainerBootMain`: after a container restart recreates the root and named-profile slots from recorded desired state, clears stale `gateway.pid` and `processes.json`, seeds state for a legacy `gateway run` command, writes a reconcile log

#### Gateway process and service discovery

Read-only facts about running gateways that status, update and doctor commands consume.

- `gateway.go` — maps running gateway pids to profiles through their pid files, strict mode failing on ambiguity
- `runtime_snapshot.go` — one liveness snapshot of the current profile's gateway under Termux, s6, Docker, systemd, launchd or bare process
- `format_gateway_pids.go` — comma-joined pid list with a limit and ellipsis
- `windows_services.go` — finds Icebath-owned Windows services (by name or binary path) and the profile gateways that descend from them
- `windows_services_windows.go` — Win32 SCM enumeration and query-only handles behind that discovery
- `windows_service_get.go` — lookup of one SCM service by name and service discovery for a given process list
- `gateway_windows_names.go` — per-profile Scheduled Task name, Startup folder entry paths and task-registered check, installed as hooks for `pkg/profiles/manage`
- `gateway_windows_exec_{other,windows}.go` — `schtasks` runner, an error off Windows

#### Gateway client for the classic CLI chat

The CLI chat launch in `pkg/app` (the code calls it the one-shot chat) runs as a viewer of a session the gateway owns. This group is that viewer: one socket with redial and resubscribe, cached session state, and a session-store facade whose reads hit `state.db` read-only while writes become gateway verbs.

- `gateway_connection.go` — `GatewayConnection`: dial loop, event pump, epoch-tagged calls, resume with launch key, replay-gap reattach, side-task answer routing
- `gateway_session_store.go` — open, create, attach, mutate, rename, rewind, end and relaunch of the session through gateway requests; titled session creation
- `gateway_session_store_reads.go` — read methods delegated to the read-only reader, and no-op stand-ins for the write and maintenance methods the gateway now owns
- `gateway_chat_policy.go` — which launch flags and env flags ride `session.create` as policy, the allowlisted shell `client_env`, resume overrides
- `surface_label_reader.go` — session listings and search that also match gateway-created rows by their `created_source` label

#### `icebath send`

- `send_cmd.go` — sends text to `--to PLATFORM[:channel[:thread]]` from an argument, `--file` or stdin through the `send_message` tool; `--list` targets, `--subject`, WhatsApp `--mention`, `--json`; exit 0, 1 or 2

#### `icebath webhook`

`subscribe`, `list`, `remove` and `test` for dynamic webhook routes of the webhook platform; each route has an HMAC secret, events filter, prompt, skills, delivery target and optional `--deliver-only`, `--mirror-to-session`, `--script`, `--cron-job` and `--route-profile`.

- `webhook.go` — the four subcommands, validation, secret generation, signed test POST, setup hint when the platform is disabled
- `webhook_cron.go` — resolves a `--cron-job` reference in the route profile's cron store; excluded from core and no-extras builds

#### `/snapshot` command helper

- `snapshot_command.go` — list, create, prune and restore of quick state snapshots, with the hand-off that pauses the owning gateway or parks a satellite profile during a restore
- `gateway_snapshot_rejoin.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers over two host-control acknowledgement checks

#### Cron wiring

- `gateway_runner_ref.go` — gives `pkg/cron` a reference to this process's gateway runner; excluded from core and no-extras builds

### `pkg/acp` — Agent Client Protocol server: icebath driven by an editor over stdio

*27 files, 7,735 Go lines*

`icebath acp` serves ACP on stdin and stdout so an editor can drive icebath. The agent it serves, `GatewayACPAgent`, never runs a model itself: it connects to the profile's gateway, creates or attaches gateway-owned sessions with `source: acp`, and projects gateway events into ACP session updates. The wire types and stdio transport come from `pkg/internal/pyacp`; `wiring.go` binds helpers from `pkg/app` and `pkg/gatewaycli`. Implemented agent methods: `initialize`, `authenticate`, `session/new`, `session/load`, `session/resume`, `session/fork`, `session/list`, `session/prompt`, `session/cancel`, `session/set_model`, `session/set_mode`, `session/set_config_option`; towards the editor it sends `session/update`, `session/request_permission` and `elicitation/create`. Missing: `session/close`, extension methods and notifications, any use of the editor's `fs/*` and `terminal/*` capabilities (the agent uses its own tools), and audio prompt content (only image is advertised). An earlier in-process server survives only as helper code and one unused interface.

#### Entry point, flags and wiring

- `cmd_acp.go` — `icebath acp` handler: exports `--accept-hooks`, `--ignore-rules`, model and provider as env, forwards `--version`, `--check`, `--setup`, `--setup-browser`, `--yes`
- `entry.go` — adapter main: version and check answers, interactive model setup with optional Chromium install, redacted stderr logging, `.env` load, serve until disconnect; hidden re-exec word `__icebath_acp_adapter__`
- `entry_args.go` — [py-shim] argparse-exact parsing, usage and help text for the entry flags
- `auth.go` — auth methods: the detected provider's runtime credentials when configured, and always a terminal method that runs `--setup`
- `hooks.go` — function variables and the `PreparedMutations` interface the core packages fill in
- `wiring.go` — `init` binding those variables to `pkg/app`, `pkg/gatewaycli` and `pkg/commands`
- `commands.go` — seams for rough token estimation and version info
- `log.go` — package logger
- `util.go` — [py-shim] Python truthiness and `str` of decoded JSON values

#### Gateway projection agent

Session mapping: an ACP session id is the logical gateway session, with aliases kept across compression and fork; `session/new` freezes the editor's MCP servers and launch flags into the session policy, and load or resume replay the stored transcript before replying. Prompts go out as `prompt.submit` with a retry fingerprint, the reply is assembled from `message.delta`, `reasoning.delta`, `tool.start`, `tool.complete` and `todo.updated` events, and a connection loss triggers reattach and recovery of the in-flight admission from its receipt. Modes map to edit approval policy: `default` asks, `accept_edits` allows workspace edits, `dont_ask` allows for the session.

- `gateway_server.go` — `GatewayACPAgent`: every ACP method, gateway connect and reattach, event pump, replay-gap recovery, lost-turn handling, model, mode and config pickers, permission and clarify cards, session list paging (50)
- `gateway_reply.go` — projects tool starts and completions, message and thought chunks, plan updates, and closes open tool calls when a reply settles
- `gateway_session_meta.go` — advertised slash commands, mode state, model, reasoning and edit-mode config options, usage and title updates
- `gateway_media.go` — stages a prompt's images (data URLs or SSRF-guarded remote fetch) for `prompt.submit` and fingerprints a prompt for retries
- `gateway_loop.go` — [py-shim] cooperative single-runner loop and lock standing in for the asyncio event loop the agent's coroutines assumed
- `modes.go` — the three modes and their edit approval policies

#### Slash commands answered in the adapter

- `gateway_commands.go` — routes `/help`, `/model`, `/tools`, `/title`, `/undo`, `/retry`, `/compress`, `/new`, `/steer`, `/queue`, `/branch`, `/discard` to session mutations or prompts and forwards other known commands to the gateway's `slash.exec`

#### Prompt content, history replay and tool rendering

- `content.go` — converts ACP text, image, resource-link and embedded-resource blocks to OpenAI user content; reads `file://` resources, maps Windows drive paths under `/mnt`
- `server.go` — turns stored history into replay updates (messages, thoughts, tool calls, compaction summaries); also the `Client` interface and an unused reasoning-callback seam left from the in-process server
- `events.go` — native ACP plan update from a task-list tool result, stable message id per streamed assistant message
- `tools.go` — tool name to ACP kind map, tool call titles, start and completion content including diffs for edits and per-tool result formatting

#### Permission, clarify and edit-approval cards

Gateway approval prompts become ACP `session/request_permission` cards with allow once, allow for session, allow always, deny and (when the schema accepts it) deny always; clarify questions use form elicitation when the editor advertises it and a permission card otherwise.

- `permissions.go` — permission option sets, the pending execute tool call shown on a card, allow detection
- `elicitation.go` — elicitation capability check, clarify form and answer parsing, clarify permission card
- `edit_approval.go` — pending edit tool call carrying the proposal's diff

#### Session catalog, provenance and model picker

- `catalog.go` — lists ACP sessions from `state.db`, one row per logical owner, optionally filtered by cwd
- `provenance.go` — session provenance metadata walked from the compression chain, sent under `icebath.sessionProvenance`
- `session_helpers.go` — WSL cwd translation and comparison, session title fallback, updated-at formatting
- `model_catalog.go` — model picker state from the provider inventory and named custom endpoints, `provider:model` choice encoding

### `pkg/acpclient` — ACP client: an external ACP agent CLI used as a model provider

*7 files, 1,608 Go lines*

Drives another ACP agent (in practice GitHub Copilot CLI, `copilot --acp --stdio`) as the backend of the `copilot-acp` provider. `Client` is shaped like an OpenAI chat client: each completion spawns the CLI, sends `initialize` and `session/new`, flattens the whole message list and tool schemas into one text prompt, collects message and thought chunks, parses tool calls out of the text and reports zero usage. Limits: one process per call with no session reuse, every `session/request_permission` is answered cancelled, only `fs/read_text_file` and `fs/write_text_file` (confined to the cwd) are served, and other client methods return "not supported". Linked by a blank import in every build except core.

#### Generic stdio ACP client

- `client.go` — `Vendor` hooks, `Client`, process spawn and teardown, JSON-RPC request loop, `ListModels`, `CreateChatCompletion`, handling of agent-initiated requests
- `acp_client.go` — error type, `--acp` support probe, child environment with a stable `HOME`, model selection requests, cwd-confined file handlers, timeouts
- `spawn_{other,windows}.go` — hides the console window of the spawned CLI on Windows
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Copilot vendor

- `copilot_acp_client.go` — Copilot defaults, `ICEBATH_COPILOT_ACP_COMMAND`, `COPILOT_CLI_PATH` and `ICEBATH_COPILOT_ACP_ARGS` overrides, disabled-model filter, diagnosis of the deprecated `gh copilot` extension
- `copilot_provider.go` — `init` installing the client builder for the `copilot-acp` provider, with the `copilot login` hint

### `pkg/relayhost` — out-of-process host for the `nemo_relay` Python runtime

*6 files, 3,104 Go lines*

The "relay host" is the bridge to NeMo Relay, an optional third-party Python wheel (`nemo_relay`) whose scope stack, events, plugin host, tool and LLM hooks the tool runtime drives. The icebath binary re-executes itself with the hidden verb `relay-host --python <interpreter>`; the child embeds CPython through `pkg/internal/pyhost`, imports `nemo_relay` and serves the parent over newline-delimited JSON frames on stdin and stdout. `cmd/icebath` registers `Load`, `Ready` and `ProvisionRuntime` with `pkg/tools`. Deployment: the wheel is installed into the PM-managed runtime venv by `icebath pm install --extra nemo-relay`, exists only for targets with a pinned wheel, and is never provisioned implicitly.

#### Parent binding and child process

- `binding.go` — `Client`: starts the child, maps `nemo_relay` scopes, plugins, subscribers, tools, LLM calls and codecs onto Go functions, serves child callbacks, caches a failed import until site-packages changes
- `child.go` — child side: interpreter start and finalize (20 s deadline), ops `hello`, `call`, `run`, `attr`, `cancel`, `release`, Python object references held by id, callbacks into the parent
- `wire.go` — frame type, error transport, request and reply routing with nested calls, tagged encoding of ints, floats, bytes and dicts
- `streams_{unix,windows}.go` — reserves the original stdin and stdout for the protocol and points the process's own stdio at the null device and stderr

#### Test support

- `relaytest/relaytest.go` — [test-support] provisions a cached venv with `nemo_relay` and a loopback wheel index

### `pkg/botmode` — Bot Mode: profiles as teammate agents that message each other

*5 files, 795 Go lines*

Bot Mode is on when any profile's `profile.yaml` has a `ui_meta.icebath-bots` block. Each profile then is a teammate with a handle (the default profile answers to `icebath`) and one canonical session titled "Bot Chat"; agents DM each other with the `message_agent` tool. This package owns the roster and prompt side: it is called by the system prompt builder, the DM send tool in `pkg/agent`, the TUI server and gateway housekeeping. It reads `profile.yaml`, `SOUL.md`, `skills/` and `bot_peers` in `config.yaml`, and owns a per-user temp directory of DM payload files.

#### Roster, handles and the teammate protocol prompt

- `probe.go` — roster of live profiles, handles and friendly-name aliases, peer gateway names, the protocol section added to the Bot Chat system prompt, and a 12-hex capability epoch (config, SOUL, skills, roster, peers) used to detect a stale stored prompt

#### DM payload files and runner entry

- `dm_cache.go` — private `icebath-dm-<uid>` directory under the temp root, refused when owned by another user; sweep of payloads and intents older than 24 h
- `dm_cache_{unix,windows}.go` — current and owning user id, absent on Windows
- `dm_runner.go` — hidden argv word `__icebath_bot_mode_dm__` and lookup of the `icebath` executable a delivery runs

### `pkg/botmode/dmdelivery` — delivery of one Bot Mode DM to its target

*3 files, 827 Go lines*

A DM is written to a private file, then delivered by a runner (the icebath binary re-executed with the hidden word) that the `message_agent` tool in `pkg/agent` starts as a host-local background process through the terminal tool, so the sender's turn can end and the reply arrives as a process-completion notification. For a local teammate the runner pins an intent file `<dm>.live.json` naming the target's live Bot Chat owner, admits the message to that owner under one delivery id (the SHA-256 of the file path) and waits up to 30 minutes for the receipt; for a peer transport it pipes the file to the transport command's stdin. The outcomes are settled with a reply, definitely not sent (safe to resend), or ambiguous (do not resend).

#### Live admission and runner

- `live.go` — DM file and intent handling, delivery id, admission to the canonical live owner, held-chat and unavailable refusals, bounded wait that cancels a queued delivery whose owner vanished
- `runner.go` — runner argv parsing, local versus stdin transport, per-profile turn lock, JSON outcome line and exit code, `DispatchEntry`
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/botdesktop` — a headless Linux desktop per profile for the bot's browser and computer use

*17 files, 3,613 Go lines*

Gives each profile its own X screen: TigerVNC `Xvnc` plus a minimal Xfce (window manager, panel, desktop, settings daemon) on a private D-Bus session, served over RFB on a 0600 Unix socket only. The agent's Chromium and the `cua-driver` computer-use MCP server run on that display, a human can watch or take control, and the TUI server exposes it as `display.status`, `display.start`, `display.stop`, `display.thumbnail`, `display.install` and `display.lease.*`. State lives in `<home>/bot-desktop/` (`display`, `env`, `launcher.pid`, `launcher.log`, `rfb.sock`, `Xauthority`, `xdg/`, `activity`, `lease.json`, `browser-profile/`). Config keys are `bot_desktop.placement`, `auto_start`, `geometry` (1440x900), `idle_stop_minutes` (30) and `min_free_memory_mb` (1536). Linux only; no RFB proxy exists in Go, viewers are handed the socket path.

#### Screen lifecycle on the gateway host

- `runtime.go` — required binaries and per-distro packages, display number allocation (20 to 89) under a host-wide lock, launcher spawn and publish wait, status, stop, orphaned X server reaping, idle stop, published env for child tools
- `launcher.sh` — [data] embedded bash supervisor: seeds xfconf, panel and dock, writes the X cookie, starts `Xvnc` without TCP, runs the Xfce components under `dbus-run-session`, publishes the env file, loops the idle check
- `wallpaper.png` — [data] embedded desktop wallpaper written beside the launcher
- `idle_watch.go` — hidden argv word `__icebath_bot_desktop_idle_watch__`: one idle check that stops the screen or prints the next delay
- `resources.go` — available memory from `/proc/meminfo` and cgroup limits, and the minimum-free-memory start gate
- `platform_{unix,windows}.go` — process group, flock, session and executable-bit primitives, inert on Windows
- `launcher_pid_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported accessor for the live launcher pid

#### Placement and sandbox-hosted screen

The screen runs on the gateway host when the terminal backend is local or placement is forced to `gateway`, inside the terminal sandbox for Docker, SSH or stream-capable plugin backends, and is refused otherwise so the screen never leaves the sandbox the user chose.

- `placement.go` — resolves gateway, terminal or refused placement and fetches the profile's terminal environment
- `sandbox_host.go` — embeds and ships the launcher into the sandbox, starts and stops the screen there (as user `pn` when the image has it), host-side ownership marker, in-sandbox screen grab, Chromium lookup, `cua-driver` and display command lines with telemetry off

#### Human and agent control lease

- `lease.go` — `lease.json` holder (`agent` or `human`), epoch and viewer; acquire, release, change listeners; screen tools are refused while a human holds it, and an unreadable lease counts as human

#### Bot browser binding

- `browser.go` — the Chromium executable and user-data directory shared by the agent and the dock icon, shared launch flags, 256 MB disk cache cap

#### Desktop package install

- `install.go` — runs the distro install (apt, dnf or pacman, sudo when needed) under a per-profile slot with a 15-minute timeout and process-group kill
- `install_{unix,windows}.go` — non-blocking flock, refused on Windows

#### Screen thumbnails

- `thumbnail.go` — read-only JPEG of the running screen scaled into 960x600 for the UI
- `x11grab.go` — minimal X11 client: display parsing, Xauthority cookie lookup, root window capture

### `pkg/batchrun` — `icebath batch`: run the agent over a JSONL dataset and collect trajectories

*8 files, 1,949 Go lines*

Runs one agent conversation per dataset row in parallel workers to produce training or evaluation trajectories. Input is a JSONL file of rows with a `prompt` (text or content parts) and optional `image`, `docker_image` and `cwd`; toolsets are sampled per prompt from a named distribution. Output goes to `data/<run_name>/` in the working directory: `batch_<n>.jsonl`, the combined `trajectories.jsonl`, `checkpoint.json` and `statistics.json`. `--num_workers` goroutines pull batches of `--batch_size`; `--resume` skips prompts whose text already appears in existing batch files. Rows whose assistant turns carry no reasoning are discarded, and failed prompts are retried on resume.

#### Command and run orchestration

- `command.go` — flag handling for `icebath batch`, `--list_distributions`, reasoning effort, prefill messages file, exit codes
- `runner.go` — options, dataset load and batching, checkpoint read and write, resume by prompt-text match, final statistics file
- `pool.go` — worker pool, live progress bar, incremental checkpoint per batch, SIGINT and SIGTERM stop with agent interrupt
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Per-prompt execution and output

- `worker.go` — runs one batch in order, appends and fsyncs one trajectory row per prompt, writes discard tombstones
- `prompt.go` — per-prompt tool environment, Docker image check and pull, agent options (`platform: batch`, no context files), conversation run and panic capture
- `stats.go` — per-tool call, success and failure tallies and reasoning coverage, normalized to one schema across rows
- `combine.go` — merges batch files into `trajectories.jsonl`, dropping rows that name unregistered tools, and prints the summary

### `pkg/trajectorycompressor` — standalone tool that shrinks saved trajectories to a token budget

*5 files, 2,035 Go lines*

Built as its own binary, `cmd/trajectory_compressor`, for post-processing batch output into training data. A trajectory is a row whose `conversations` field is a list of `{from, value}` turns (system, human, gpt, tool). Rows over the target (15 250 tokens by default) keep the first turn of each role and the last four turns, and a middle span is replaced by one LLM-written summary turn. Its default config path `configs/trajectory_compression.yaml` does not exist in the repository, so the built-in defaults apply unless a file is passed.

#### CLI and directory run

- `cli.go` — positional or flag arguments in Python Fire style, file or directory input, optional seeded sampling, dry run, `_compressed` output naming
- `run.go` — JSONL read and write, concurrent processing bounded by `max_concurrent_requests`, per-trajectory timeout (300 s), progress display, `compression_metrics.json` summary

#### Compression engine

- `compressor.go` — token counting, protected-turn selection, span planning, summary prompt and retries through a known provider or a raw OpenAI-compatible client, reassembly with a summary notice
- `config.go` — config struct, defaults (OpenRouter, a Gemini flash summarizer), YAML loading, metrics types; `num_workers`, `skip_under_target` and `save_over_limit` are parsed but never read
- `tokenizer.go` — loads a Hugging Face tokenizer by name from the hub cache or network, honouring `HF_HOME`, `HF_ENDPOINT`, `HF_TOKEN` and offline mode

### `pkg/activesessions` — cross-process registry of live sessions and their owners

*7 files, 1,319 Go lines*

Owns `<home>/runtime/active_sessions.json` and `active_sessions.lock`. Every surface that runs a session (classic CLI, TUI host and server, gateway) acquires a lease recording session id, surface, pid and process start time; a second live owner of the same session is refused with `SESSION_NOT_OWNED`, and a configured `max_concurrent_sessions` cap with `MAX_CONCURRENT_SESSIONS`. It has no CLI of its own; `icebath status`, shared-session attach and data cleanup read it.

#### Lease registry

- `leases.go` — refusal type and messages, file lock, `TryAcquire`, release, transfer to a new session id, orphan release across profile homes, `LivenessGuard` for atomic check-then-write
- `registry.go` — registry paths, tolerant and strict entry reading, pid plus start-time liveness, pruning snapshot, owner detail line
- `max_concurrent.go` — reads `max_concurrent_sessions` from the top level or the `gateway` section, positive integers only
- `lease_flags.go` — two accessors satisfying the TUI server's lease interface
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Re-export shims

- `registry_prune_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports `ReadEntries` and `PruneDead` for data cleanup
- `turn_marker_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports own start time for the TUI host turn marker, and `PidLiveness`, which nothing calls

### `pkg/vault` — encrypted per-profile credential vault

*10 files, 2,708 Go lines*

Owns `<home>/vault/`: `vault.json.enc` (Fernet-encrypted item list), `vault.key` (0600 key file) or `vault.keyref` (pointer to an OS keychain entry under service "Icebath Agent vault key"), and `.vault.lock`. Items are logins (bound to an origin, optional TOTP seed), payment cards and addresses; listings return metadata only and secrets are resolved server-side for browser fill. The CLI (`icebath vault add`, `list`, `rm`, `sources`, `key`, `key migrate`), the browser vault tool and its backends live in `pkg/browser`, the TUI hub calls it too, and profile cloning in `pkg/profiles/manage` gives a copied vault its own keychain entry. `vault.key_storage` chooses `file` (default) or `keychain`.

#### Vault store

- `vault_store.go` — item add, list, remove and secret resolve; origin normalization; TOTP generation; key creation, location report and migration between file and keychain; secret scrubbing from text
- `vault_keychain.go` — keychain pointer file handling, ownership check so a copied vault never deletes another vault's key, backend label
- `log.go` — package logger

#### OS keychain backends

Native Go replacements for the Python `keyring`, `secretstorage` and `jeepney` libraries, keeping their backend names and entry layout so messages and stored entries match.

- `keyring.go` — backend interface, the fail backend, macOS login keychain through the `security` tool with the secret on stdin
- `keyring_native_{darwin,unix,windows}.go` — per-OS choice: macOS keychain, Secret Service or fail on other Unix, Windows Credential Manager generic credentials
- `keyring_secretservice.go` — freedesktop Secret Service client: DH-encrypted session, unlock prompts, search, store and delete
- `dbus.go` — minimal D-Bus wire client (EXTERNAL auth, marshalling, calls, signals) used only by the Secret Service backend

#### Test seams

- `test_seams.go` — [test-support] in-memory keyring and vault-body writer; also holds `RequiredFields`, which the vault command and view use in production

### `pkg/webhooksubs` — store of dynamic webhook subscriptions

*3 files, 390 Go lines*

Owns `<home>/webhook_subscriptions.json` and `.webhook_subscriptions.lock`: the routes created by `icebath webhook subscribe` and by the MCP events tool, which the gateway's webhook adapter serves and also updates (replay cursor, removal of an ended subscription). Writers lock, reread, mutate and publish by atomic rename; readers take no lock. It has no CLI itself; callers are `pkg/gatewaycli`, `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/mcp` and the TUI hub.

#### Subscription store

- `store.go` — load, locked mutate, compare-and-swap replace of one route, key-order-preserving merge, effective webhook config with `WEBHOOK_ENABLED`, `WEBHOOK_PORT`, `WEBHOOK_SECRET`, listener base URL (port 8644) and route URL
- `lock_{unix,windows}.go` — whole-file flock, or a first-byte lock retried ten times on Windows

### `pkg/mcpserve` — icebath as a stdio MCP server

*5 files, 1,709 Go lines*

`icebath mcp-serve` (registered by the `mcp-serve` catalog plugin in `pkg/builtin/mcpserveplugin`) exposes the profile's messaging conversations to another agent. It reads `state.db`, the legacy `sessions/sessions.json` index and `channel_directory.json`, polls `state.db` every 200 ms for new messages into a 1000-event queue, and sends through the `send_message` tool. Only tools are exposed, no MCP resources or prompts; the server name is `icebath`.

#### Bridge tools and optional icebath tools

Bridge tools: `conversations_list`, `conversation_get`, `messages_read`, `attachments_fetch`, `events_poll`, `events_wait`, `messages_send`, `channels_list`, `permissions_list_open`, `permissions_respond`. With `--tools` a fixed allowlist is added: `web_search`, `web_extract`, `browser_navigate`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_press`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_back`, `browser_get_images`, `browser_console`, `browser_vision`, `vision_analyze`, `image_generate`, `skill_view`, `skills_list`, `text_to_speech`; terminal, file, code execution, process, kanban and delegation tools are never exposed.

- `handlers.go` — the ten bridge tool handlers and descriptions, server construction, `RunServer` with `--verbose`, `--tools`, `--accept-hooks`
- `bridge.go` — [partial] event bridge and transcript readers; nothing ever records a pending approval, so `permissions_list_open` is always empty and `permissions_respond` always answers not found
- `icebath_tools.go` — registers the allowlisted tools, drops `text_to_speech.output_path`, refuses non-web URLs, forces secret redaction, registers the profile's shell hooks and outbound webhooks
- `log.go` — stderr-only logger so stdout stays the MCP channel
- `pyops.go` — [py-shim] Python dict access, comparison and sort semantics with Python exception text, used by the handlers

## 9. Scheduling and work tracking: cron, kanban, goals, monitoring

### `pkg/cron` — scheduled agent jobs: job store, scheduler, run path, delivery, `cronjob_manage` tool and `icebath cron` CLI

*124 files, 31,639 Go lines*

Owns everything under `<home>/cron/` of one profile home, addressed through one `Store` value per home: `jobs.json` (the job list), `output/<job_id>/<timestamp>.md` run documents, `executions.db` (attempt ledger plus the `cron_incidents` table), `deliveries.db` (durable send queue), `notepad.db`, `suggestions.json`, `admissions/*.json` journals, `external-workers/` handoff files, `cancels/*.cancel` markers, `bot_chat_pending/*.json`, lock files `.jobs.lock`, `.tick.lock` and `.fire-<uuid5>.lock`, marker files `ticker_heartbeat`, `ticker_last_success`, `ticker_last_error`, `catch_up_occurrences`, `dispatch_held.json`, and four append-only jsonl logs (`usage_audit`, `inflight_forced_releases`, `persisted_error_recoveries`, `timezone_migration_catchups`). The scheduler normally runs inside the gateway process: `pkg/gatewayrun/cron_link.go` resolves a `CronScheduler` (the built-in 60 second ticker, or a plugin-hosted provider named by `cron.provider`), runs it on a supervised goroutine, and adds housekeeping chores (delivery-queue drain, misfire catch-up, ticker restart). Standalone use is `icebath cron tick`, one headless tick meant for an external crontab, which holds agent jobs back unless a ready gateway serves the home. A job is a prompt and optional skills run by a fresh agent, a script whose stdout is the message (`no_agent`), or an agent gated by a change monitor; output is delivered to chat platforms, a Bot Chat, a local chat or only the output file. Agent-backed runs are not executed by the ticker itself: they are admitted to the gateway's per-home "canonical owner" (in process or over the gateway RPC methods `cron.submit`, `cron.status`, `cron.recover`, `cron.cancel`) and, under a managed service, the whole fire is first handed to a re-executed worker process placed in a restart-safe systemd scope. Other callers are `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go` (CLI, worker entry, wiring), `pkg/gatewayapi/jobs.go` (HTTP job API), `pkg/tuiserver`, `pkg/app` (console `/cron`), `pkg/agent` (agent factory), `pkg/selfupdate` and `pkg/agentimport`. Port scaffolding is heavy: a full reimplementation of Python `croniter`, Python exception names and `repr` text in messages (some user-facing texts still name `croniter` or a Python source path), ordered-dict JSON preservation of `jobs.json`, more than sixty package-level "seam" variables that exist because the Python tests patched module attributes, eleven thin export shim files, and a leftover `PYTHONPATH` pin for the worker. The code is real and wired; three exported wrappers have no caller, and two suggestion sources have no producer.

#### Job record model and on-disk JSON codec

The `Job` struct and its custom JSON codec for `jobs.json`. Stored keys: `id` (12 hex characters), `name`, `prompt`, `skills` (plus legacy single `skill`), `model`, `provider`, `base_url`, `script`, `no_agent`, `monitor_script`, `monitor_url`, `monitor_state`, `context_from`, `schedule` (`kind` of `cron`, `interval` or `once`, with `expr`, `minutes`, `run_at`, `display`), `schedule_display`, `repeat` (`times`, `completed`), `enabled`, `state` (`scheduled`, `paused`, `completed`, `error`), `paused_at`, `paused_reason`, `created_at`, `next_run_at`, `last_run_at`, `last_status`, `last_error`, `last_delivery_error`, `last_delivery_unverified`, `last_failure`, `failure_streak`, `deliver`, `origin` (`platform`, `chat_id`, `chat_name`, `thread_id`, `user_id`, `scope_id`), `enabled_toolsets`, `workdir`, and the optional `attach_to_session`, `reasoning_effort`, `failure_deliver`, `interpreter`, `timezone`, `grace_minutes`, `catch_up`, `fire_claim`, `run_claim`, `pending_slot`, `manual_run_at`, `manual_run_restore_at`, `manual_run_prompt`, `last_dispatch`, `last_fire_error`, `preflight_alerted`, `quota_hold_until`, `quota_hold_cron_expr`, `unreachable_retry`, `canonical_completions`, `last_delivery_queued`. Unknown keys, key order and explicit nulls are preserved on rewrite, which is port behaviour (Python dict round trip) rather than a product rule.

- `job.go` — `Job`, `Schedule`, `Repeat`, `Claim`, `PendingSlot`, `Dispatch`, `Stamp`, `MonitorState`, `RetryState` and their ordered marshal and tolerant unmarshal (numbers or strings accepted, unknown keys kept in `Extra`); `Clone`, `Label`, `Kind`
- `constants.go` — fire-claim TTL 300 s, 60 s clock-skew tolerance between replicas, run-claim TTL multiplier 3 over the inactivity timeout; `isRecurring`

#### Job store: `jobs.json`, locks, markers and output files

`Store` is one home's cron directory handle. Every load-modify-save section takes an in-process mutex and an exclusive flock on `.jobs.lock` (30 s wait, then proceeds unlocked with an error log); per-job "fire fence" locks `.fire-<uuid5 of dir::job>.lock` serialise claim and side effects of one job across processes. Loads auto-repair malformed stores (bare list, id-keyed map, non-object entries, control characters, bad `repeat.completed`) and persist the repair; saves are temp file plus atomic replace plus directory fsync with owner-only permissions, and merge back any job found on disk but missing from the in-memory payload (up to five attempts) so a stale writer cannot delete a concurrently created job. Directories are never recreated under a deleted named profile.

- `store.go` — `Store`, jobs lock and fire fence, load with repair, merge-guarded atomic save, ownership restore when root rewrites another user's file, ticker heartbeat and error markers, `cron.*` config readers, per-job output files pruned to `cron.output_retention` (default 50)
- `store_{unix,windows}.go` — owner uid and gid plus inode of a stat result; NTFS file index and no owner on Windows
- `flock_{unix,windows}.go` — polling exclusive flock (100 ms polls) on Unix; first-byte lock retried ten times a second apart on Windows
- `jobs_home_load.go` — [port-artifact] `LoadJobsForHome` wrapper used by the gateway busy probe, the update report and the Grok importer
- `env_settings.go` — reads a tuning variable from the profile's secret scope or `.env` when the gateway multiplexes profiles, else the process environment
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `cron`
- `cronconfig/cronconfig.go` — separate tiny package returning `cron.model_provider`; its one caller is `pkg/provider`, which `pkg/cron` itself imports

#### Store write-health tracking

Tracks a cron store that stops accepting writes (disk full, read-only mount, permissions) as a "degraded" outage: which write sites failed, which scheduled runs were skipped, and when it recovered. While degraded, dispatch is blocked and a write probe (temp file as large as `jobs.json` plus 4 KiB) is retried at most every 60 s; an idle tick re-probes and rewrites `jobs.json` to end the outage. A listener set by `pkg/gatewayrun/cron_store_notices.go` turns the transitions into operator notices, and one-shots due during an outage are not retired as missed.

- `store_health.go` — `StoreDegraded` records, unwritable and recovered transitions, `dispatchBlocked`, `recheckIdle`, `ProbeStore`, `ProbeReport` for `cron status` and doctor, `LowFreeBytes` 100 MiB warning threshold
- `store_health_{bsd,linux,unix,windows}.go` — write-access test and free-space reading per OS (statvfs fragment size, reserved blocks counted for root, volume free bytes on Windows)
- `doctor_exports.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] `SwapStoreProbe` test seam with no caller

#### Clock, time zones and ISO timestamps

All cron time arithmetic runs through a per-store clock whose zone comes from `ICEBATH_TIMEZONE`, then config `timezone`, then the server's local offset. Timestamps are stored as Python-`isoformat` text and naive stamps are read as system-local wall time.

- `clock.go` — `clock` (now, zone, ISO now) and `ResolveZone`
- `timeutil.go` — [py-shim] `FormatISO` and `ParseISO` matching Python `datetime.isoformat` and `fromisoformat`, aware-versus-naive handling, DST fold resolution of a wall time, stored-offset mismatch tests
- `jobs_time.go` — validation of the per-job `timezone` (IANA key) and `grace_minutes` knobs, warn-once handling of corrupt persisted values, one-shot instant parsing

#### Schedule syntax and next-run computation

Accepted schedule strings: intervals (`30m`, `every 2h`, bare `hour`), one-shot delays (`in 30m`), natural day and time phrases converted to cron (`every monday 9am`, `weekdays at 9am`, `every day at 9am`, `noon`, `midnight`), 5 to 7 field cron expressions, and ISO timestamps (one-shot). There is no free natural-language parser beyond those forms. `cronexpr.go` and `croniter_validate.go` are the two halves of one Go port of the Python `croniter` library, not alternatives: the second expands and validates an expression with croniter's exact error messages, the first iterates next and previous occurrences.

- `schedule.go` — `parseSchedule`, `computeNextRun` per kind in the job, profile or system zone, grace window (half the cadence clamped to 2 minutes and 2 hours unless overridden), dispatch lateness classes (`on_time`, `late` over 5 minutes, `catch_up`), stale-error and stale-cron classification, telemetry jsonl appends
- `croniter_validate.go` — [py-shim] croniter expansion: `@hourly`-style aliases, month and weekday names, ranges with wraparound, steps, `?`, `L`, `#` nth weekday, `W` nearest weekday, `r` random forms, seconds and year fields, CPython set `repr` emulation for one error message
- `cronexpr.go` — [py-shim] `CronExpr.Next`, `NextAt`, `PrevAt`: croniter's field-by-field search with relativedelta arithmetic, DST handling and a 50 year search bound

#### Job create, update, pause, resume, trigger and remove

Validated mutations of the job list. Rules: a job needs a prompt, a script or a skill; one-shots default to `repeat` 1 and are refused when already past the 120 s one-shot grace; `no_agent` requires a script and cannot combine with a monitor; scripts must be files, not command lines; prompts and scripts containing gateway lifecycle commands are refused; `pinned` copies the current main model and provider onto the job; a job reference may be an id or a unique name. Pause sets `enabled=false`, `state=paused`, `paused_at` and a reason; resume keeps an occurrence that elapsed while paused as due; trigger sets `next_run_at` and `manual_run_at` to now with an optional one-fire prompt; re-arm gives a completed one-shot a new time; remove also deletes the output directory, notepad rows and fence, and cancels a live run.

- `crud.go` — `createJob`, `updateJob`, `pauseJob`, `resumeJob`, `triggerJob`, `rearmOneshot`, `removeJob`, reference resolution with an ambiguity error, field normalisers, effective state derivation, preflight-alert marker
- `jobs_invariants.go` — mode invariants for `monitor`, `no_agent` and script shape; `timezone` and `grace_minutes` only meaningful with a cron schedule
- `jobs_model_pin.go` — reads the main agent's model and provider for `pinned` jobs; refuses the pin when the config backend is unavailable
- `job_definition.go` — import of job definitions shipped with a profile distribution (`profiles.CronDistributionHooks`): refreshes 24 authored fields on jobs matched by id while keeping scheduler-owned state; new ids arrive paused with a reason
- `scheduler_registration.go` — `createJobWithSchedulerRegistration`: persists a job then registers its first trigger with an external provider, reporting a partial failure as `CronSchedulerRegistrationError`
- `console_ops.go`, `api_server_jobs_export.go`, `crud_export.go` — [port-artifact] home-keyed wrappers (`CreateJob`, `GetJob`, `PauseJob`, `ListJobs`, `UpdateJob`, `RemoveJob`, `TriggerJobWithPrompt`, `ScanCronPrompt`, `CronList`, `ListExecutions`, `ListIncidents`, …) for the HTTP job API, TUI hub and console

#### Due scan, missed runs and catch-up policy

Each tick scans the job list under the jobs lock and decides which jobs fire, persisting repairs as it goes. Policy: a recurring job later than its grace window is fast-forwarded; with catch-up on (per-job `catch_up`, else `cron.catch_up_missed`, default true) the backlog collapses into one run now, otherwise every missed slot is skipped and booked as `missed` in the ledger (counting capped at 1000); a one-shot past 120 s of grace is retired with a diagnostic note unless catch-up is on, a store outage or a gateway drain hold covered its due time. Completed one-shots are pruned after `cron.completed_retention_days` (default 7). The scan also repairs missing `next_run_at`, timezone-shifted cron stamps, expressions hand-edited under a stored instant, recurring jobs wedged in a persisted error, half-paused records, and slots advanced but never claimed.

- `duescan.go` — `getDueJobs` and the per-job evaluation: run-claim stamping for one-shots, `last_dispatch` and `pending_slot` stamping for recurring jobs, all repairs listed above, completed one-shot retention sweep
- `missed_runs.go` — catch-up decision, missed-slot counting, fast-forward of recurring jobs, retirement of expired one-shots
- `occurrences.go` — dedup against an already completed occurrence in the ledger, pending-slot stamps, `catch_up_occurrences` counter file
- `jobs_oneshot_diagnostics.go` — writes a "missed" or "wedged" markdown note into the job's output directory when a one-shot is retired without running
- `dispatch_hold.go` — `dispatch_held.json`: records that the gateway paused dispatch while draining, so a held one-shot's grace restarts when the hold ends (extension bounded to 30 minutes)
- `extra_fire.go` — off-schedule fires (manual trigger, retry rung, quota recovery) leave the regular scheduled slot pending and restore it afterwards

#### Fire claims, run outcome bookkeeping and automatic retries

A fire is claimed by writing `fire_claim` (`at`, `by` as machine id plus a random token) under the fire fence; a live claim younger than 300 s whose owner is not provably dead blocks another fire. One-shots additionally carry a `run_claim` heartbeated every 60 s. Finishing a run stamps `last_status` (`ok`, `error`, `delivery_failed`, `cancelled`), the failure streak, clears claims, bumps `repeat.completed` and recomputes `next_run_at`; a recurring job whose next run cannot be computed is parked in `state=error` instead of being disabled. Two automatic retries exist: a run that never reached the model (transient network error, zero API calls) is re-run on a 5, 15, 30 minute ladder with the failure notice suppressed (`cron.retry_unreachable`), and a provider rate-limit with a retry hint parks the job until the window closes plus 60 s.

- `markrun.go` — `claimJobForFire`, `markJobRun`, `claimDispatch` (finite one-shot budget), claim heartbeats, `advanceNextRuns`, machine id from `ICEBATH_MACHINE_ID` or host and pid
- `scheduler_bookkeeping.go` — final bookkeeping of a completed or interrupted run, empty-response soft failure, delivery outcome classification for the ledger
- `delivery_outcome.go` — applies a queued delivery's terminal outcome back onto the ledger row and the job record
- `unreachable_retry.go` — the unreachable-model retry ladder state (`unreachable_retry`) and its decisions
- `quota_hold.go` — provider quota hold (`quota_hold_until`, `quota_hold_cron_expr`): extraction of the hold length from an auth error, off-lattice recovery fire, user notice

#### Executions ledger, run identity and cancellation

`executions.db` records every claimed attempt: table `executions` (`id`, `job_id`, `source` of `builtin`, `direct` or a provider name, owner process id, pid and start fingerprint, `status` of `claimed`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`, `unknown`, `cancelled`, `missed`, handoff flags, `claimed_at`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `error`, `delivery_outcome`, `scheduled_instant`, `progress_at`). Terminal rows are pruned to 1000. Recovery never retries: attempts whose owner process died, or whose live owner outlived a derived stale bound (at least two hours), are marked `unknown`. Cancellation is a marker file per execution that the run polls; the first recorded reason wins and markers expire after 24 hours.

- `executions.go` — `Ledger`: create, running transition, finish, missed booking, worker handoff adoption, dead-owner and wedged-owner recovery, listing with cursor, live and latest lookups; emits each state change to `pkg/monitoring`
- `execution_identity.go` — `CronExecution` bound on the context of a fire (job, execution id, source, scheduled instant, profile), exposed to plugins as `CurrentCronExecution`
- `cancellation.go` — cancel markers under `cron/cancels/`, combined cancel sources (operator, transport, lost claim), booking of a cancelled run without a failure alert, `cancelRun`

#### Failure incidents

Failures are grouped into incidents in table `cron_incidents` of `executions.db`, keyed by job and a signature of the normalised error text with durations masked. States are `detected`, `alerted`, `resolved`, `closed`; an acknowledged (closed) incident suppresses further failure pings, an alerted one re-pings only after `cron.failure_repeat_alert_hours` (default 6), and a clean run resolves the job's open incidents.

- `incidents.go` — `IncidentStore`: upsert with secret redaction and 500 character bound, keyword classification into `rate_limit`, `timeout`, `auth`, `delivery`, `config`, `script`, `agent` or `unknown`, state changes, ack, listing

#### Scheduler provider interface, ticker and tick

`CronScheduler` is the pluggable "when does a job fire" interface (name, start, plus optional stop, availability, jobs-changed, register-job, recover, claim-fire and fire-claimed hooks). The built-in `InProcessCronScheduler` ticks every 60 s on a monotonic schedule, records heartbeat, last success and last error markers, backs off exponentially up to 15 minutes on file-descriptor exhaustion, and in multiplex mode ticks every served profile home each cycle with per-profile isolation. One tick, under a non-blocking `.tick.lock`: yield if a fresher gateway build owns the runtime, honour the emergency stop and the gateway's drain gate, reconcile admission journals, drain legacy Bot Chat records, reap dead owners (every 5 minutes), start worktree maintenance, scan due jobs, sweep stale in-flight claims, advance recurring `next_run_at` before running, then submit each job to a worker pool (`ICEBATH_CRON_MAX_PARALLEL` or `cron.max_parallel_jobs`, unbounded by default) behind an in-flight dedup guard.

- `scheduler_provider.go` — the interface and optional hooks, default claim and fire implementations, `resolveCronScheduler` for `cron.provider`, misfire catch-up for external providers (`cron.misfire_grace_minutes`, default 10), single-home and multiplex ticker loops, emergency-stop hook
- `scheduler_tick.go` — `tickLocked` as described, tick lock handling with store degradation, per-job claim and dispatch, orphaned MCP child cleanup after the runs finish
- `scheduler_tick_{unix,windows}.go` — one non-blocking exclusive lock attempt on the tick file
- `scheduler_thread.go` — `SupervisedTickerThread`: goroutine handle the gateway uses to start the ticker and restart it if it crashed
- `scheduler_runtime.go` — `.tick.lock` path, lock-contention and fd-exhaustion detection with soft-limit raise, `usage_audit.jsonl` writer
- `scheduler_gateway_gate.go` — headless tick gate: agent jobs are refused while no ready gateway serves the home, stamping `last_fire_error` on each
- `scheduler_ownership.go` — which homes this process's ticker serves, dead-claim-owner detection from host and pid, cleanup when a profile leaves the served set
- `scheduler_mode_export.go`, `housekeeping_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers for the gateway: provider choice under multiplex, delivery-queue drain, misfire sweep, shared-route adapters

#### External scheduler providers hosted in plugins

`cron.provider` may name a user plugin directory that offers a cron scheduler (for example an external trigger service). The provider object lives in the plugin guest; cron hands it a facade with three operations so that claiming, firing and recovery still use the shared store logic. Multiplexed gateways always fall back to the built-in ticker because an external provider cannot reconcile several stores.

- `providers.go` — provider discovery under the user plugins directory, `hostedCronScheduler` proxying every hook to the plugin object
- `scheduler_facade.go` — host facade `cron` with `recover_interrupted`, `claim_fire` and `fire_claimed`, including Python-style argument binding and job wire conversion

#### In-flight registry, worker pool and restart accounting

Process-wide registry of running cron jobs keyed by home and job id, used to skip a job that is still running, to report running and wedged jobs to the gateway's drain, status and restart-wait logic, and to force-release claims that leaked. A claim is force-released when its ledger row already settled or it outlived its allowance (`cron.inflight_max_minutes` or `ICEBATH_CRON_INFLIGHT_MAX_MINUTES`, default 30 minutes, or twice the job's interval when that is longer); each release is logged to `inflight_forced_releases.jsonl`.

- `scheduler_inflight.go` — the registry, wedged detection, external worker pid recording, [py-shim] `parallelPool` reproducing Python `ThreadPoolExecutor` queueing and shutdown
- `scheduler_inflight_guard.go` — stale in-flight sweep, forced-release history, marking running jobs interrupted at gateway shutdown
- `scheduler_restart_wait_counts.go` — split of in-flight runs into awaitable, wedged and restart-safe for the gateway restart wait; `MarkRunningJobsInterrupted`
- `scheduler_inflight_export.go`, `scheduler_inflight_details_export.go` — [port-artifact] `GetRunningJobIDs`, `GetRunningJobDetails`, `GetWedgedJobIDs`

#### Run path: one fire from claim to bookkeeping

`runOneJob` is the shared path every trigger reaches (tick, manual run, provider fire, misfire, webhook event): create or reuse the ledger row, try the external worker handoff, heartbeat the fire claim, win the claimed-to-running transition, run the job, save the run document, compose and deliver the notice, then mark the job and finish the ledger row, with every side effect fenced on still owning the fire claim. `runJob` executes one job: no-agent jobs run their script; agent jobs build the prompt, resolve model, provider and fallback chain, run preflight, open the session store, construct a quiet agent on platform `cron` with session id `cron_<job>_<timestamp>`, and run it under an inactivity watchdog (`ICEBATH_CRON_TIMEOUT`, default 600 s, 0 for unlimited). The agent's final response is the delivered text; `[SILENT]` suppresses delivery and a leading `[CRON_FAILURE]` line turns the run into a failure. Cron agents never get the `cronjob`, `messaging` or `clarify` toolsets (unless `cron.allow_agent_scheduling`), honour per-job `enabled_toolsets` with MCP servers merged in, and use the job `workdir` as tool cwd and context-file root. No git worktree is created for a cron run.

- `scheduler_run_one.go` — `runOneJob` and its body: handoff, fire-ownership fence, save-compose-deliver phase, crash failure delivery, per-fire secret scope
- `scheduler_run.go` — `runJob`, no-agent and monitor outcomes, config and runtime resolution, session store with bounded cleanup, agent run with watchdog, run document framing, fire-claim heartbeat, usage audit record
- `scheduler.go` — inactivity limit from `ICEBATH_CRON_TIMEOUT` and the script timeout default of one hour
- `scheduler_liveness.go` — inactivity watchdog loop and the stamper that refreshes the ledger's `progress_at` while the agent shows activity
- `scheduler_detached_worker.go` — handling of an agent goroutine that outlives the run's wait: late session-store close and deferred teardown
- `scheduler_diagnostics.go` — run-document error section listing the error and its causes with URL credentials redacted, Python-traceback-style stack frames for the log only, redacted stderr tail (1500 characters) of a dead external worker
- `scheduler_agent.go` — `AgentOptions` and the `CronAgent` interface cron needs from an agent
- `scheduler_agent_hooks.go` — [port-artifact] setter functions through which `pkg/agent` installs the agent factory, hard interrupt, turn-summary formatter and max-iteration check

#### Canonical owner admission of agent runs

An agent-backed fire is not run by whichever process ticks; it is submitted to the gateway that owns the profile home, so the run appears as a normal owned session. `runCanonicalJob` writes an admission journal `cron/admissions/<sha256 of job and request id>.json`, submits, then polls status with backoff from 100 ms to 2 s, forwarding cancel and progress. If the outcome cannot be verified the job is paused with the reason recorded and the attempt marked `unknown`, never retried or reported failed; journals are reconciled on later ticks.

- `scheduler_authority_run.go` — submit, recover, status and cancel against the in-process owner or the gateway RPC, journal replay and reconciliation
- `scheduler_authority.go` — journal path and atomic write, `CronExecutionUnknown`, pause and un-pause tied to one uncertain admission
- `gateway_owner_hooks.go` — init-time registration of the owner-side callbacks in `pkg/gateway` (get job, resolve model, run job, progress) and of the webhook-event job runner
- `scheduler_authority_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] `RunCanonicalJob` wrapper with no caller

#### Restart-safe external worker process

When the gateway runs as a systemd-managed service on Linux, a fire is handed to a child process (`<binary> __icebath_cron_external_worker__ --external-worker-file … --ack-file …`) started in its own systemd scope so a gateway restart does not kill the run. The parent writes the payload under `cron/external-workers/`, waits up to 30 s for an acknowledgement file, then watches the child and reconciles the ledger; the worker adopts the execution, runs the same `runOneJob`, and delivers through the durable queue because it has no platform adapters. `cron.require_restart_safe_scope` makes a missing scope an error.

- `scheduler_external_worker.go` — launch, payload and ack files, waiter, worker entry point `DispatchExternalWorkerEntry`, worker-side payload run
- `scheduler_worker_failure.go` — projects an unknown worker outcome onto the job once, fenced against newer fires
- `worker_bootstrap.go` — worker process boot through the dependency manager, driven by a marker env var removed before job children start
- `scheduler_worker_env.go` — [port-artifact] prepends the install tree and its site-packages to the worker's `PYTHONPATH`, a leftover of the Python worker that a Go binary does not need

#### Prompt assembly and injection scanning

The run prompt is, in order: a fixed cron instruction block (delivery is automatic, `[SILENT]`, `[CRON_FAILURE]`, never schedule new jobs), a current-run-time line, the job notepad section, context blocks from `context_from` jobs (the latest non-silent output of each, 8000 characters, `self` meaning the job's own previous output), script output as a data block (an empty successful script skips the run), then the stored prompt plus any per-fire or monitor "Run Context". When the job has skills, their bodies are loaded first and that whole text follows as the user instruction. Prompts are scanned at create time and again when assembled.

- `scheduler_prompt.go` — `buildJobPrompt`, context chaining, skill loading with a notice for missing skills, workdir resolution, wake gate (last stdout line `{"wakeAgent": false}`), credential-exfiltration guard on `provider` plus `base_url`, block-and-pause of unrunnable jobs
- `cronjob_prompt_scan.go` — threat patterns (instruction override, secret file reads, `authorized_keys`, sudoers, `rm -rf /`, curl or wget carrying secret variables), invisible-Unicode stripping that spares emoji joiners, an allowance for GitHub API token curls

#### Scripts and change monitors

Job scripts must resolve inside `<home>/scripts/`; `.sh` and `.bash` run through bash, anything else through the job's absolute `interpreter` or the first Python on PATH. Scripts run in their own process group with a timeout (`ICEBATH_CRON_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT`, `cron.script_timeout_seconds`, default one hour), output is redacted, and the group is terminated then killed on timeout or cancel. A monitor is a script or an http(s) URL (30 s timeout, 256 KiB) whose output hash gates the agent: unchanged output is a silent run, changed output wakes the agent with a unified diff, the first run is a baseline.

- `scheduler_script_run.go` — script path confinement, interpreter validation, process start, timeout and tree termination, tool environment, claim heartbeat while a script runs, gateway-lifecycle command guard
- `scheduler_script.go` — timeout resolution from env then config for scripts and media sends (5 minutes)
- `scheduler_script_{unix,windows}.go` — new session and process-group TERM then KILL on Unix; hidden console and `taskkill` tree kill on Windows
- `monitor.go` — monitor source evaluation, sha256 comparison with `monitor_state`, snapshot file `output/<job>/monitor_last_output.txt`, diff block capped at 4000 characters

#### Preflight checks and failure notices

Before any model call an agent job is checked for a usable provider credential (skipped when a fallback chain exists), attached skills that still need setup, connected delivery platforms and MCP servers named in its toolsets that resolved to zero tools. A failing check blocks the run without charging tokens, alerts once (`preflight_alerted`), and stays silent until a healthy run; `cron.preflight: false` disables it. Failure notices are rewritten into plain language by cause, with a review nudge after `cron.failure_nudge_threshold` (default 3) consecutive failures.

- `scheduler_preflight_job.go` — the provider-key, skills, delivery and MCP checks
- `scheduler_preflight.go` — blocked-config markers and classification of transient network errors in an error chain
- `scheduler_preflight_{unix,windows}.go` — the transient errno list per OS
- `scheduler_preflight_routes.go`, `scheduler_preflight_export.go` — primary-gateway profile routes: a secondary profile without its own bot credentials reaches platforms through the primary's adapters for exact routed targets only
- `scheduler_failure.go` — failure summarisation for delivery, incident upsert and alert bookkeeping, fallback-chain wording, stale-code tick yield, toolset and reasoning resolution for cron agents, session titling, `[SILENT]` and `[CRON_FAILURE]` markers
- `scheduler_failure_copy.go` — the notice texts: provider failure by reason, script timeout, inactivity, blocked configuration, generic failure with the saved output path

#### Delivery of results

`deliver` is a comma list of tokens: `local` (file only), `origin` (the chat the job was created from, else the first home channel), `all` (every platform with a home channel), `bot-chat` or `bot-chat:<profile>`, a bare platform (its home channel) or `platform:chat_id[:thread_id]`; `failure_deliver` overrides the lane for failure notices. Agent-job output is always enqueued in `deliveries.db` and sent only when a gateway drains the queue (20 rows per pass); script-only output is sent directly by the firing process. For each target the live gateway adapter is tried first, then a standalone platform send, with media attachments extracted from the text, secrets redacted, and unverified sends recorded on the job. Output is wrapped in a "Cronjob Response" frame unless `cron.wrap_response` is false. `attach_to_session` makes a delivery continuable: a thread is opened where the platform supports it and the brief is seeded into that session so the user can reply.

- `scheduler_delivery.go` — `deliverJobResult`: target loop, Bot Chat delivery with receipts, live-adapter text and media sends with confirmation, continuable threads and session seeding, standalone fallback, reconnect queueing, delivery verification record
- `scheduler_delivery_targets.go`, `scheduler_delivery_targets_export.go` — token resolution to `Target` values, home-channel lookup from env vars and config, stale Slack thread handling, transcript-mirror eligibility (`cron.mirror_delivery`)
- `scheduler_delivery_lane.go` — deliver-string normalisation, choice of success or failure lane, `bot-chat` token parsing
- `scheduler_delivery_origin.go` — stamps origin scope id and relay user id onto live send metadata
- `delivery_queue.go` — `DeliveryQueue` over `deliveries.db` (tables `deliveries` and `delivery_tombstones`): enqueue, claim, drain, abandoned-row recovery, wait up to 300 s for an outcome, payload redaction and tombstoning beyond 1000 terminal rows
- `delivery_queue_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] `DeliveryQueueOf` with no caller
- `bot_chat_legacy.go` — pending Bot Chat records under `cron/bot_chat_pending/` for a target profile that is not running, drained each tick in sequence order

#### Model-facing `cronjob_manage` tool

One tool in toolset `cronjob` with actions `create`, `list`, `update`, `pause`, `resume`, `remove`, `run` (aliases `run_now`, `trigger`) and `cancel`. It is offered in interactive, gateway, exec-ask and cron sessions. `create` captures the creating chat as `origin`, scans the prompt, validates scripts, base URLs and context references, and returns guidance notes; `run` claims the job and dispatches it in the background so its outcome re-enters the conversation, forwards to the gateway's HTTP job API for relay-fronted platforms, or queues it for the gateway ticker when only the primary gateway can deliver.

- `cronjob_tools.go` — tool registration, action handlers, manual-run claim and background dispatch, forwarding and hand-off cases, run completion summary with session usage
- `cronjob_schema.go` — [data] the tool's JSON schema and parameter descriptions
- `cronjob_job_args.go` — argument normalisation: origin capture from session env, `monitor` split into script or URL, `continuity` as a `self` context reference, deliver validation, base-URL and script-path guards, job formatting for replies

#### `icebath cron` CLI, `/cron` slash command and classifier

Subcommands: `list`, `create` (`add`), `edit`, `pause`, `resume` (with `--run-now` or `--at` to re-arm a one-shot), `run`, `cancel`, `remove` (`rm`, `delete`), `status`, `doctor`, `tick`, `runs` (`history`), `incidents`, `notepad` and `classify`. Mutations go through the same `cronjob` function the model tool uses.

- `cli_cron_cmd.go` — subcommand table and handlers: job listing with warnings, scheduler status and ticker health, per-job doctor checks, execution history, incident list and ack, notepad access, headless tick
- `cli_cron.go` — lateness formatting, overdue next-run rows (15 minute grace), manual-run verdict line
- `cli_cron_lines.go` — `/cron` slash command for chat sessions (`list`, `add`, `edit`, `pause`, `resume`, `run`, `remove`) returning localised lines
- `cli_cron_liveness.go` — active provider name and a three-state "is a scheduler serving this home" probe from gateway status and heartbeat age
- `classify_items.go` — `icebath cron classify`: scores a JSON list of items against criteria in one auxiliary-model call (task `monitor`) and prints only those at or above a threshold; empty output means silence

#### Automation blueprints

Parameterised job templates with typed slots (`time`, `enum`, `text`, `weekdays`), a schedule template and a prompt template. Sixteen are built in and plugins can register more. The `/blueprint` command lists the catalog, starts a guided agent turn that asks for each slot, or creates the job directly from inline `key=value` values.

- `blueprint_catalog.go` — `AutomationBlueprint` and `BlueprintSlot`, slot validation, schedule resolution from slots, `fillBlueprint` producing a job spec
- `blueprint_catalog_data.go` — [data] the sixteen built-in blueprints (morning brief, important-mail monitor, weekly review, reminders, digests, watches, habit and learning prompts)
- `blueprint_plugins.go` — validation and construction of plugin-registered blueprints (`BuildPluginBlueprint` service), keyed `plugin:key`
- `cli_blueprint_cmd.go` — `HandleBlueprintCommand`: matching by key, prefix, substring or close match, the agent seed text, inline fill and job creation

#### Job suggestions

A per-profile list of proposed jobs in `cron/suggestions.json` that the user accepts or dismisses with `/suggestions`. At most five are pending; a dedup key prevents re-offering an accepted or dismissed suggestion. [partial] Sources are `catalog`, `blueprint`, `usage` and `integration`, but only the catalog and the skill-blueprint bridge in `pkg/skills` ever add suggestions; nothing produces usage-based or integration-based ones.

- `suggestions.go` — suggestion records and their load, add, accept (creates the job), dismiss and clear operations; registers the adder hook used by `pkg/skills`
- `suggestion_catalog.go` — [data] four starter suggestions and `SeedCatalogSuggestions`
- `suggestions_cmd.go` — `HandleSuggestionsCommand` for `list`, `accept`, `dismiss`, `catalog`, `clear`

#### Job notepad

A per-job key-value store that survives between runs, injected into every run prompt. It is written only through `icebath cron notepad <job> set|get|delete|list`; there is no model tool for it, so a job updates it by running the CLI.

- `notepad.go` — `Notepad` over `notepad.db` table `cron_notepad`: caps of 128 characters per key, 16 KiB per value and 64 KiB per job, prompt section rendering, clear on job removal

#### Hooks into other subsystems

Init-time registrations and maintenance that other packages reach through hook variables.

- `curator_hooks.go` — installs the skill curator's cron hooks in `pkg/memory`: referenced skill names, skill reference rewrite, locked raw job update
- `skill_refs.go` — collects skill names referenced by any job and rewrites them when the curator consolidates or prunes skills
- `monitoring_sources.go` — registers cron readers (heartbeat ages, job counts, catch-up count, store health) with `pkg/monitoring`
- `scheduler_worktree_maintenance.go` — every six hours per profile, prunes stale git worktrees older than 24 hours in registered repos, the install checkout and job workdir repos; also gives the worktree tool read access to the job list
- `worktree_registry.go` — `<home>/worktree_repos.json`, the list of repos that hold icebath-made worktrees
- `backup_cron_prompts.go` — after a self-update, restores job prompts that were replaced by the job name from the pre-update snapshot under `state-snapshots/`, for every profile

### `pkg/kanban` — shared task board: SQLite store, lifecycle, dispatcher, worker protocol, tools and CLI

*61 files, 23,507 Go lines*

A multi-agent task board shared by every profile of an install. The root is `ICEBATH_KANBAN_HOME` or the icebath root (not a profile home): the default board's database is `<root>/kanban.db`, named boards live in `<root>/kanban/boards/<slug>/` with `board.json` and their own `kanban.db`, `<root>/kanban/current` names the active board, and workspaces, attachments and worker logs sit under `<root>/kanban/` or the board directory. Tasks move through the columns triage, todo, scheduled, ready, running, blocked, review, done (plus archived) and are assigned to profiles; a dispatcher claims ready and review tasks and spawns one detached worker process per task, which runs an agent as that profile and reports back through the kanban tools. The dispatcher loop itself is hosted by the gateway (`pkg/gatewayrun/kanban_watchers_dispatcher.go`), the worker client and owner-side run are in `pkg/gateway`, and the notifier that pushes task events to chats is in `pkg/gatewayrun`; this package supplies the store, the single dispatch tick, and the surfaces: fifteen model tools, `icebath kanban`, and the `/kanban` slash command. There is no HTTP or dashboard surface in the package; the TUI hub calls the CLI entry point. Port scaffolding: Python exception types on errors, a `Row` type imitating `sqlite3.Row`, argparse-namespace option access, and several export shims. Everything is wired; the v2 workflow-template columns and the manual-move table are defined but unused.

#### Board resolution, multi-board metadata, export and import

Boards are identified by a slug (1 to 64 lowercase alphanumerics, hyphens, underscores). The active board is resolved from a context override, `ICEBATH_KANBAN_BOARD`, the `current` file, then `default`; `ICEBATH_KANBAN_DB`, `ICEBATH_KANBAN_WORKSPACES_ROOT` and `ICEBATH_KANBAN_ATTACHMENTS_ROOT` pin paths for a spawned worker. The default board cannot be removed; removing another board deletes it or moves it to `boards/_archived/<slug>-<timestamp>`.

- `db_boardpath.go` — slug validation, kanban root, current-board file, path resolution for database, workspaces, attachments and worker logs with the env pins
- `db_boards.go` — `board.json` metadata (name, description, icon, color, default workdir, project id, archived), create, list and remove
- `transfer.go` — `ExportBoard` to a `tar.gz` holding an online-backup snapshot scrubbed of claims, pids, sessions and subscriptions plus optional attachments and logs with a `manifest.json`; `ImportBoard` as a new board with path relocation

#### Database connection, schema, migration and transactions

One SQLite file per board with WAL, `synchronous=FULL`, foreign keys, secure delete and a 120 s busy timeout (`ICEBATH_KANBAN_BUSY_TIMEOUT_MS`). Tables: `tasks`, `task_links` (parent, child), `task_comments`, `task_events` (kind, JSON payload, optional run id), `task_runs` (one row per attempt), `task_attachments`, `kanban_notify_subs`. First open per path runs schema and migration under `<db>.init.lock`; an existing file that fails integrity checks is backed up as `<db>.corrupt.<hash>.bak` (ten kept), repaired by `REINDEX` when only indexes are damaged, and otherwise refused rather than recreated. A delegated child agent gets a read-only connection.

- `db_connect.go` — connect, init lock, dispatch tick lock `<db>.dispatch.lock`, WAL checkpoint every five minutes, header and integrity guards, corrupt backup, `RepairDB`, refusal to resurrect an archived or missing board
- `db_schema.go` — [data] the `CREATE TABLE` and index statements with column commentary
- `db_migrate.go` — additive column migrations for older databases, legacy column and event-kind renames, rebuild of pre-AUTOINCREMENT tables, backfill of runs for tasks already running
- `db_txn.go` — `WriteTxn` (`BEGIN IMMEDIATE` with jittered retry on busy, five attempts) and a rollback-journal length sanity check
- `db.go` — status, block-kind and workspace-kind sets, 25 MiB attachment cap, `Row` query helpers, claim TTL (15 minutes), crash grace (30 s) and rate-limit cooldown (300 s) settings from env, plugin lifecycle hooks fired on task events, delegated-child mutation fence
- `db_types.go` — `Task`, `Run`, `Comment`, `Attachment`, `Event` structs and row decoding tolerant of missing legacy columns
- `db_ids.go` — task ids (`t_` plus 8 hex), claimer id `host:pid`, model-override validation, assignee normalisation, project link resolution to a repo worktree
- `db_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] `AssertNotDelegatedChildMutation` wrapper with no caller
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `kanban`

#### Workflow columns

The fixed column list with labels and glyphs used by the CLI and TUI. The struct also carries a per-column drag flag and a table of allowed manual moves between columns, intended for a board UI; nothing reads either of them beyond validation at start-up.

- `workflow.go` — [partial] `DefaultWorkflow` (triage, todo, scheduled, ready, running, blocked, review, done), `Archived`, `DefaultStatuses`; the `DragTarget` flag and `Manual` move table are never consulted

#### Tasks, dependency links, comments, attachments and events

Task fields: title, body, assignee (profile), status, priority, creator, tenant, workspace kind and path, branch name, project id, idempotency key, skills, model, provider and reasoning overrides, max runtime, max retries, goal mode and goal turn budget, originating session id, completion contract, block kind and recurrence count, failure counter and last error, claim lock and expiry, worker pid and start fingerprint, current run id. A new task starts in `ready` when it has no unfinished parent, else `todo`; `triage` and `blocked` can be requested. Links form a DAG (cycles refused) and a child inherits the first parent's tenant. `workflow_template_id` and `current_step_key` are stored, filterable and copied onto runs but nothing sets or routes on them (planned v2 workflow routing). Event kinds written to `task_events` include created, assigned, claimed, spawned, worker_registered, heartbeat, commented, attached, linked, edited, completed, blocked, dependency_wait, block_loop_detected, scheduled, unblocked, promoted, review_requested, changes_requested, review_reopened, reclaimed, timed_out, gave_up, respawn_guarded, skipped_nonspawnable, decomposed, specified, archived and pr_acceptance; run outcomes are completed, blocked, crashed, timed_out, spawn_failed, rate_limited, gave_up and reclaimed.

- `db_tasks.go` — `CreateTask` with idempotency key, `GetTask`, `ListTasks` filters and sort orders, assign, model override, link and unlink with cycle check, comments, attachment storage with safe names and size cap, event listing, run rows
- `db_graph.go` — initial status and tenant rules, inheritance of the creator's session and notification subscriptions, `DecomposeTriageTask` fan-out of a triage task into validated children
- `task_event_export.go`, `session_kanban_export.go` — [port-artifact] `AppendTaskEvent`, `AppendEvent`, `RequireSlug`, `RetryStatusForRun` for `pkg/gateway`

#### Task lifecycle and state machine

Transitions are compare-and-swap updates that each open or close a `task_runs` row and append an event. Todo and non-sticky blocked tasks are promoted to ready when every parent is done or archived. Claiming moves ready (or review) to running with a claim lock and expiry. Completion requires evidence (a summary or result), verifies that any cards the worker claims to have created exist and were created by it, preserves declared scratch artifacts as attachments, and for a task with a completion contract requires the GitHub PR gate. Block is typed: `dependency` goes back to todo, `needs_input`, `capability` and `transient` go to blocked, and a second block of the same kind after an unblock is routed to triage as a detected loop.
