Review is a first-class phase with implementer and reviewer provenance; request-changes returns the task to its implementer. Reopening a parent demotes its ready, review, running or done descendants to todo and terminates their workers.

- `db_claim.go` — `RecomputeReady`, `ClaimTask`, `ClaimReviewTask`, heartbeat claim extension, stale-claim release, operator reclaim and reassign, created-card verification, phantom task-id scan of prose
- `db_complete.go` — `CompleteTask` with its evidence, created-card and artifact gates, attachment staging of scratch artifacts, completed event payload
- `db_review.go` — `EditTask`, `BlockTaskWithKind`, `RequestReview`, `RequestChanges`, `PromoteTask`, `UnblockTask`, `ReopenReviewTask`, `ReopenTask`, descendant invalidation, `SpecifyTriageTask`, secret redaction of review handoffs
- `db_lifecycle.go` — `ArchiveTask`, `DeleteArchivedTask`, `ScheduleTask`, `BuildWorkerContext`, `BoardStats`, event and worker-log garbage collection, known assignees, run history and summaries

#### GitHub pull-request completion gate

A task may carry `completion_contract`: `local-only` (default), `OWNER/REPO`, or an exact GitHub PR URL. For the latter two, completion must name the published PR and is accepted only when every required status check of the base branch's protection rule is successful on the PR's current head; the evidence is read with the `gh` CLI under the assignee profile's environment and stored as a receipt event.

- `pr_acceptance.go` — contract validation, GraphQL and REST reads through `gh api`, check classification (`success`, `failure`, `pending`, `missing`, `stale`, `auth`, `infra`), ownership snapshot so the receipt applies only to the run that collected it

#### Workspaces

Each task gets a working directory by kind: `scratch` (a managed directory under the board's workspaces root, deleted when the task finishes), `worktree` (a linked git worktree on branch `wt/<task>` or the task's branch, under the repo's `.worktrees/`, removed only when clean and fully pushed), or `dir` (an existing absolute path, never removed). Cleanup is skipped while another live task on any board uses the same path.

- `db_workspace.go` — workspace resolution and creation, git worktree materialisation, shared-use detection across boards, checked cleanup of scratch and worktree workspaces, deferred parent cleanup, one-time scratch tip, tmux session cleanup

#### Worker context document

The markdown a worker reads about its task: header with metadata, attachments with absolute paths, prior attempts (10), results of parent tasks, role history and comments (30), each field capped (body 8 KiB, fields 4 KiB, comments 2 KiB).

- `db_context.go` — section builders, relative-age formatting, terminal-timeout override for tasks whose max runtime exceeds the terminal default
- `worker_context_export.go` — [port-artifact] `WorkerTerminalTimeoutEnv`, `ProcessFingerprint`, `WorkerAlive` for `pkg/gateway`

#### Dispatcher tick and worker process supervision

`DispatchOnce` is one pass under the board's non-blocking dispatch lock: reclaim phase (expired claims, crashed workers, max-runtime overruns, stale heartbeats, orphaned running rows, workers that outlived a closed run), ready promotion, then spawning. Spawn limits: `kanban.max_spawn`, a global `kanban.max_in_progress` across all boards (default derived from RAM at 512 MB per worker, between 2 and 8), an optional per-profile cap, none while memory pressure is critical and one while elevated; one slot is reserved for a review task. Review tasks are dispatched to their assignee as a reviewer run with the `sdlc-review` skill added, unless `kanban.review_dispatch` is false. A task is skipped when its assignee is not a spawnable profile (`kanban.dispatch_profiles` allowlist), when unassigned and no `kanban.default_assignee` applies, or when the respawn guard holds it (rate-limit or infrastructure cooldown, auth or quota wording in the last error, a success within the hour, an open PR link in recent comments). Failures count toward a circuit breaker (`kanban.failure_limit`, default 2, or the task's `max_retries`) that auto-blocks the task. The worker is this binary with the argument `__icebath_kanban_worker_client__`, started detached in the task workspace with `ICEBATH_KANBAN_TASK`, run id, claim lock, board, database and workspace env vars, output appended to a rotated per-task log, wrapped in a restart-safe systemd scope under a managed gateway.

- `db_dispatch_tick.go` — `DispatchOnce`, respawn guard, profile allowlist, concurrency and memory limits, lane dispatch with claim, workspace resolution and spawn, default assignee
- `db_dispatch_spawn.go` — worker environment and argv, per-task log, `defaultSpawn`, `RunDaemon` loop used by the deprecated standalone daemon
- `db_dispatch_spawn_{unix,windows}.go` — new session on Unix, no console window on Windows
- `db_dispatch_workers.go` — `DispatchResult`, pid liveness with restart-stable fingerprints so a recycled pid is never signalled, worker termination, `EnforceMaxRuntime`, `DetectStaleRunning`, pid adoption by the worker
- `db_dispatch_kill_{unix,windows}.go` — signal delivery; process termination with an exit code on Windows
- `db_dispatch_sweep.go`, `db_dispatch_sweep_export.go` — child reaping and exit registry, crash sweep with exit classification and the worker's last output folded into the error, protocol-violation streak (clean exit without a terminal tool call), orphan reconciliation, heartbeat events
- `db_dispatch_wait_{unix,windows}.go` — raw wait status of a finished worker
- `db_dispatch.go` — `recordTaskFailure` circuit breaker and `RecordBudgetExhausted` for a worker that ran out of iterations
- `owner_recovery.go` — reclaim decisions when the run was admitted to a gateway owner: reads the owner's `session_admissions` row named by the `owner_admitted` event and refuses a new attempt while the outcome is ambiguous
- `worker_log.go` — worker log rotation by size and backup count from the kanban config
- `worker_client.go` — time budget a worker client waits for the owner's `kanban.run` answer

#### Worker-side runtime helpers

Functions called inside a running worker process by `pkg/agent` and `pkg/app`.

- `worker_registration.go` — records the worker's own pid on its run before the first model call; fails when the run was already reclaimed
- `tools_bridge.go` — automatic heartbeat at most once a minute, steering of new operator comments into the running agent (polled every 6 s), goal-mode judge gate for complete and review handoffs; one rejection text recommends a `kanban_edit` tool that is not registered
- `turn_recovery.go` — re-runs a failed worker turn in the same session up to `ICEBATH_KANBAN_TURN_RECOVERY` times (default 3, delays 15, 45, 90 s) with a continue nudge, never for rate-limit or billing failures and only while the claim is still live
- `turn_exit.go` — maps a credential error raised before any turn into exit-code flags

#### Notification subscriptions

A chat (platform, chat, thread, user) or TUI session can subscribe to a task; the gateway notifier and the TUI poller read unseen events per subscription with a compare-and-swap cursor. Creating a task from a chat subscribes that chat automatically (`kanban.auto_subscribe_on_create`), and children inherit their creator's subscriptions.

- `db_notify.go` — subscription rows with delivery mode and metadata, list and count with profile ownership scope, unseen-event claim, cursor advance and rewind, ping record, purge of subscriptions on long-done tasks

#### Triage automation and swarms

Two auxiliary-model helpers work on the triage column: the specifier rewrites a rough idea into a titled spec and moves it to todo; the decomposer splits it into a dependency graph of child tasks routed to profiles from a roster with descriptions. A swarm is a ready-made graph: a planning root used as a shared blackboard, parallel worker cards, a verifier and a synthesizer.

- `specify.go` — specifier prompt, auxiliary call (`ICEBATH_KANBAN_SPECIFY_MAX_TOKENS`, default 6000), JSON extraction, `SpecifyTask`
- `decompose.go` — decomposer prompt, profile roster and default-assignee routing (`kanban.default_assignee`), single-task or fan-out application, `DecomposeTask`
- `swarm.go` — `CreateSwarm`, blackboard comments on the root, `--worker` argument parsing

#### Board diagnostics

Eleven rules computed from a task's events and runs, each yielding a severity and suggested recovery actions: hallucinated cards, triage auxiliary model unavailable, phantom references in prose, repeated failures, repeated crashes, review-dependency deadlock, running with open parents, stuck in blocked, block-unblock cycling, stranded in ready, stale running.

- `diagnostics.go` — rule engine, rule configuration from the kanban config, CLI hint and action payloads

#### Model-facing kanban tools

Fifteen tools in toolset `kanban`: `kanban_show`, `kanban_list`, `kanban_complete`, `kanban_block`, `kanban_schedule`, `kanban_request_review`, `kanban_request_changes`, `kanban_heartbeat`, `kanban_comment`, `kanban_attach`, `kanban_attach_url`, `kanban_attachments`, `kanban_create`, `kanban_unblock`, `kanban_link`; each takes an optional `board`. They are visible to dispatcher-spawned workers and to profiles that enable the toolset, never to delegated child agents; `kanban_list` and `kanban_unblock` are hidden from task workers. A worker may mutate only its own task and must prove its run id.

- `tools_register.go` — the tool table and registration with visibility checks
- `tools_schemas.go` — [data] tool schemas and descriptions
- `tools_gate.go` — call context, visibility and ownership guards, argument coercion, redaction of secrets in text and metadata, result payload shapes
- `tools_handlers.go` — show, list, complete, block, schedule, request-review, request-changes, heartbeat and comment handlers
- `tools_create.go` — create (child of the caller's task inheriting project and workspace), auto-subscribe of the calling session, unblock and link
- `tools_attach.go` — inline base64 attach, URL attach with server-side download capped at 25 MiB and private-address checks on every redirect hop, attachment listing

#### `icebath kanban` CLI and `/kanban` slash command

Actions: `init`, `create`, `swarm`, `list`, `show`, `assign`, `set-model`, `reclaim`, `reassign`, `diagnostics`, `link`, `unlink`, `claim`, `comment`, `attach`, `attachments`, `attach-rm`, `complete`, `edit`, `block`, `schedule`, `unblock`, `request-review`, `request-changes`, `reopen-review`, `reopen`, `promote`, `archive`, `tail`, `dispatch`, `daemon`, `watch`, `stats`, `log`, `runs`, `heartbeat`, `assignees`, `notify-subscribe`, `notify-list`, `notify-unsubscribe`, `context`, `specify`, `decompose`, `gc`, `repair`, and `boards` (`list`, `create`, `rm`, `switch`, `show`, `rename`, `set-default-workdir`, `export`, `import`). `daemon` is deprecated and refuses to run without `--force` because the gateway hosts the dispatcher.

- `cli.go` — `KanbanCommand` entry, action table, delegated-child fence, dispatcher-presence warning on create, and most action handlers
- `cli_ops.go` — `tail`, `dispatch` (one pass, text or JSON), `daemon`, `watch`, `gc`, `repair`, dispatch settings from config
- `cli_boards.go` — the `boards` subcommands
- `cli_output.go` — timestamp, count and task-line formatting, JSON output, bulk apply with per-id results
- `cli_ns.go` — [port-artifact] `kanbanCLI` and typed accessors over the argparse-style namespace map
- `slash.go` — `/kanban` in chat sessions: tokenises the text, runs the CLI with captured output, curated short help

### `pkg/goals` — standing goals: per-session objective, judge loop, gates and `/goal` command

*6 files, 2,603 Go lines*

A goal is a standing objective attached to one session that the agent keeps working toward across turns: after each turn a judge model decides done, blocked, continue or wait, and on continue a synthetic user message is fed back into the same session until the goal is met, paused, or the turn budget (default 20) runs out. State is stored as JSON in the session database `state.db` under meta key `goal:<session_id>`. Callers are the gateway (`pkg/gatewayrun/run_goals.go`, `/goal` slash command), the TUI server, the agent loop and automation viewer in `pkg/agent`, and the kanban worker goal loop. The judge is the auxiliary task `goal_judge` (`auxiliary.goal_judge.timeout`, default 30 s, and `max_tokens`, default 4096). The package is small and fully wired; port residue is limited to Python error kinds and loosely typed state fields.

#### Goal state and persistence

- `goal_state.go` — `GoalState` (goal text, status of active, paused, done or cleared, turns used and max, last verdict and reason, pause reason, judge failure counters, subgoals, wait barrier fields, contract, gates), `GoalContract` (outcome, verification, constraints, boundaries, stop-when), `GoalGate`, cached session-database handle per home, load, save, clear (row kept for audit) and migration of a goal to a continuation session after compression

#### Goal manager and continuation loop

`EvaluateAfterTurn` is the per-turn decision: if parked on a wait barrier, stay parked; otherwise count the turn, run quality gates in order, then call the judge. A failing gate continues with the gate's output; `blocked` pauses; `done` ends; five consecutive judge transport failures or three unparseable replies pause with a configuration hint; exhausting the budget pauses. A wait verdict can park the loop on a background pid, a process-registry session, a number of seconds or running delegations, for at most 30 minutes.

- `goal_manager.go` — `GoalManager`: set, pause, resume, clear, mark done, subgoals (extra criteria added mid-loop, driven by the `/subgoal` command in `pkg/gatewayrun`) and gates management, wait barriers, `EvaluateAfterTurn`, continuation prompt selection, status line, and `RunKanbanGoalLoop` which drives a goal-mode kanban worker until it ends its task

#### Judge, contract drafting and gates

- `goal_judge.go` — judge call and reply parsing, contract parsing from `verify:`-style lines with aliases, contract drafting by an auxiliary model, `RunGate` (shell command in the session workspace, default timeout 300 s, three retries, 3000 character output tail), background-process and delegation gathering for the judge prompt, last-user-message lookup
- `goal_prompts.go` — [data] continuation, gate-failure, judge and contract-drafting prompt templates, plus the kanban goal continuation texts

#### `/goal` command

- `goal_command.go` — `DispatchGoalCommand`: `status`, `show`, `pause`, `resume`, `clear`, `wait <pid>`, `unwait`, `gate list|add|remove|clear` (adding needs caller authorisation), `draft <text>` to draft a contract first, `-- <text>` for goal text that starts with a control word, anything else sets the goal and returns its kickoff prompt
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `goals`

### `pkg/monitoring` — gateway health telemetry: event bus, health snapshots, OTLP export and `icebath monitoring`

*13 files, 3,153 Go lines*

Opt-in export of gateway service health to an OpenTelemetry collector, started by the gateway at boot (`StartGatewayHealthExport`). It covers gateway and platform state gauges, cron scheduler gauges, redacted diagnostic events and warning or error log records; it never exports prompts, messages, tool data, usage or traces of agent work. Settings: `monitoring.gateway_health_export.*` (enabled, metrics, diagnostic events, warning and error events, two intervals with a 5 s floor, resource attributes), `monitoring.export.otlp.*` (enabled, endpoint, header env names) and `monitoring.install_id`. Metrics go through the real OpenTelemetry Go SDK; spans and logs use hand-written OTLP/HTTP exporters. Inputs arrive through hook variables set by `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/tools` and `pkg/cron`. The package is wired; its only command is a read-only status printout.

#### Event bus and event types

- `emitter.go` — process-wide `MonitoringEmitter`: collects only once a subscriber is attached, bounded queue of 10000 that drops the oldest event when full, one dispatcher goroutine delivering batches of 256, flush, stats and close
- `events.go` — `GatewayHealthEvent`, `GatewayDiagnosticEvent` and `CronExecutionEvent` with their ordered dict form

#### Health snapshots and classification

- `gateway_health.go` — bounded classification of gateway error and exit-reason text, opaque sha256 instance ids, lifecycle and platform transition events emitted when the runtime status file changes
- `gateway_health_snapshot.go` — `BuildGatewayHealthSnapshot` (gauges `icebath.gateway.up`, `state`, `active_agents`, `busy`, `drainable`, `restart_requested`, `icebath.platform.up`, `degraded`) and a log handler that turns gateway warning and error records into allowlisted diagnostic events without their rendered message
- `cron_health.go` — cron gauges (`icebath.cron.scheduler.heartbeat_age_seconds`, `last_success_age_seconds`, `catch_up_occurrences`, `icebath.cron.jobs.enabled`, `running`, `overdue`, `icebath.cron.store.writable`, `skipped_runs`) from readers registered by `pkg/cron`, cron error classes, projection of ledger state changes into `CronExecutionEvent`

#### OTLP export

- `gateway_health_export.go` — `StartGatewayHealthExport` and its runtime: observable gauges on a periodic OTel metric reader, diagnostic log streamer, periodic snapshot events, supervisor detection (systemd, s6, container, launchd, manual), shutdown within two seconds
- `otlp_exporter.go` — `OTLPStreamer` turning emitter batches into zero-duration spans, allowlisted and redaction-checked resource attributes, header resolution from named env vars, signal endpoint rewriting
- `otlp_http.go` — hand-written span pipeline: `TracerProvider`, `BatchSpanProcessor`, OTLP/HTTP JSON trace exporter; also holds `InMemorySpanExporter`, a test double compiled into the package
- `otlp_logs.go` — hand-written OTLP/HTTP protobuf log exporter with gzip, bounded retries honouring `Retry-After`, env-var header, timeout and compression resolution, batch log processor

#### Policy, redaction and command

- `policy.go` — `EnsureInstallID`: stable per-install uuid stored in settings, or a per-process one when it cannot be saved
- `redaction.go` — egress redaction: secret scrub, then email, uuid and phone patterns, bounded length, and a fixed marker when the redactor fails
- `monitoring_command.go` — `icebath monitoring` (only action `status`): prints which exports are enabled, the OTLP endpoint and the linked OTel SDK version
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `monitoring`

## 10. Terminal UI

### `pkg/tui` — terminal UI client: session windows, composer, transcript, slash commands, management screens and the gateway link

*153 files, 53,430 Go lines*

Owns the whole interactive client. `tui.Run(ctx, Host)` is called from `pkg/app/tui_launch.go` with a `Host` built in `pkg/app/tui_host.go`; `cmd/icebath/wiring.go` and `link_extras.go` plug in the clipboard-image reader, the plugin widget source and the speech output. It is a bubbletea v2 program drawn with the project toolkit (`pkg/ui/wm` tiling window manager with workspaces, tabs, overlays, palette and leader key; `pkg/ui/cards`, `pkg/ui/keys`, `pkg/ui/gfx`, `pkg/ui/tty`). No agent work runs here: every session, tool, setting and screen is served by the background gateway service over one WebSocket carrying JSON-RPC 2.0, typed by the method, event and request tables of `pkg/tuigateway`. Files it writes itself: `tui-layout.json`, `keybinds.json`, `input_history.jsonl` and `logs/tui_gateway_crash.log` in the profile home (`home.Dir`), `tui-pending-inputs/<id>.json` and `cache/images/` in the session's profile home, `tui-theme-boot.json`, `heapdumps/`, `perf.log` and `sessions/saved/` in the process home (`home.Process`), and `after-exit/window-<pid>.json` in the root home. The port scaffolding in this package is JavaScript, not Python: it imports no `internal/py*`, but it was ported from a Node "reference terminal UI" and still carries UTF-16 string offsets and `slice`, `toFixed`, `replace` and `parseInt` semantics (`text.go`, `queue.go`, `colortones.go`, `content.go`, `usermessages.go`), a hand-written WHATWG URL parser (`gatewaylog.go`), promise-style continuations (`eventhandler.go`, `sessionlifecycle.go`) and one argparse-shaped parser (`slash_journey.go`). The package is wired and working end to end; dead helpers are named in the groups, and pets, the arena and voice exist only in builds that link the extras tier.

#### Program entry, launcher contract and the window shell

`Run` starts optional CPU profiling (`ICEBATH_CPUPROFILE`), builds one `shell` (window manager, gateway client, keymap, shared display preferences, theme negotiation, prompt history, widget host, pet) and the first `app` (one per session card), runs the program, then detaches from the gateway, hands `/worktree new` trees to the host and prints the exit summary. `shell.Update` is the event loop: it routes each message to the window manager or to the session it belongs to (gateway events by session id; `gateway.*`, `skin.changed` and `sessions.changed` to every session; microphone events to the session holding the microphone; prompts of sessions shown in no card to a "waits on you" toast and bar notice), then settles each touched session (turn timers, completion, git branch, loop ticker, dialogs, queue drain) and repaints only when something changed. Session cards tile inside workspaces ("spaces"); closing a card or a space only detaches, the session keeps running in the gateway. The layout and the session each card shows are saved to `tui-layout.json` at exit and restored at launch; `ICEBATH_TUI_REDUCED_MOTION` and the plain theme switch animation off.

- `app.go` — `app` per-session object and `Run`; keymap of the `tui` context (ctrl+o model, ctrl+t agents, ctrl+g editor, ctrl+l redraw, f1 help, ctrl+d exit on an empty prompt, super+k send queued, shift+tab yolo, shift+up/down line scroll); routing of a sent line (slash command, `!shell` line via `shell.exec`, `{!cmd}` interpolation, busy input, offline queue, setup-required redirect); interrupt-key and escape layering (second ctrl+c within 2 s quits); palette commands; status facts with width thresholds and give-way ranks; terminal tab title with a waiting, busy or idle mark; roster refresh every 1.5 s busy and 10 s idle; quit with a 1.5 s detach limit; the `stickyPrompt` field is written but never read
- `shell.go` — `shell` shared by all cards: message routing, one live-session poll for the window (titles, background notices), `attention` jump to what waits on the user, bar lane per workspace showing its most urgent session, new session beside or in a new space, open stored session in a card, gateway-exit handling with restart budget, one-second status clock, `saveLayout` and `restoreLayout`; `liveCount` has no caller
- `bootstrap.go` — `Host` contract the launcher fulfils: `Attach(start, recover)` returning a `Grant` (private WebSocket URL, subprotocols, profile and instance ids, build it replaced), `RestoreSnapshot`, `SettleWorktrees`, optional `ReplaceOwner`
- `messages.go` — `sessionScoped` marker on 23 message types and the `sessionMsg` wrapper that brings a command's result back to the card that issued it; a new session message type not listed here reaches no session
- `mailbox.go` — ordered, never-blocking handoff of messages into the program from goroutines and from inside the update loop
- `resizecoalescer.go` — leading and trailing throttle of terminal resizes (32 ms) before every transcript reflows
- `tier_surfaces.go` — link-tier seams over `pkg/linktier`: `petCard` and `arenaView` interfaces with `noPet` and `noArena` null objects, tier filter for the voice key, the `/voice` and `/wake` commands and the `/setup` sections (voice and chat-apps need the plugins tier, import the extras tier); `quickSetupDetail` has no caller
- `exitsummary.go` — exit reason and status (128 plus signal, 2 on panic, 1 on a dead terminal or error, 137 after a memory-critical exit), stop-signal and lost-terminal handling recorded in the crash log, printed summary per open session (title, id, turns, duration, `icebath --resume <id> [-p profile]`)

#### Gateway link: WebSocket JSON-RPC client, bootstrap, heartbeat and reconnect

One `gatewayClient` per window. It attaches to `ICEBATH_TUI_GATEWAY_URL` when set, else to the home's gateway owner through `Host.Attach` (bounded to 40 s; start on first launch, re-ensure a lost owner at most three times a minute, never retry a "gateway unavailable:" verdict), dials with no proxy and no frame cap, and refuses a server that does not choose the first offered subprotocol. Readiness is the `gateway.ready` event (start timeout 15 s via `ICEBATH_TUI_STARTUP_TIMEOUT_MS`, floor 5 s); requests time out after 2 min (`ICEBATH_TUI_RPC_TIMEOUT_MS`, floor 30 s); a `gateway.ping` heartbeat every 15 s drops a socket silent for 45 s, with one grace probe after a local stall; reconnect delay doubles from 1 s to 30 s. On ready the client sends `client.capabilities` with `server_requests: true`. Events arriving before a subscriber exists are buffered (newest 2000), frames of a session whose resume is in flight are held and replayed only past the snapshot's replay epoch and sequence, `session.create` is stamped `source: "tui"` with a request id that a create without a clear answer reuses, and the client raises its own events `gateway.stderr`, `gateway.reconnecting`, `gateway.start_timeout` and `gateway.protocol_error`. With an explicit URL the gateway may be remote: images are uploaded instead of copied and typed paths resolve against the launch folder.

- `gateway.go` — `gatewayClient`: bootstrap flight, socket generations, outbox delivery in order, wire event stamping with authority epoch and execution generation, server requests answered once (`respond`, `fail`, method-not-found), 200-line client log tail, launch tool-progress pin (`ICEBATH_TUI_TOOL_PROGRESS` written as session setting `display.tool_progress`), `kill` that only detaches; `jsErrorText` (JavaScript error wording) has no caller
- `wirelink.go` — `wireSocket` over gorilla WebSocket and `wireLink`: numbered requests matched to answers, every other frame queued in order, refusal and link-gone errors
- `wiretyped.go` — generic typed helpers over `tuigateway.Method`: `ask` (prints its failure), `call` and `callWithin`, `fire`, `quietAsk`; contract misfits reworded to name another gateway build when `gateway.ready` reported one
- `subscriptions.go` — registry of the subscription id each card holds per session, waiters behind a detach in flight, wholesale loss on disconnect
- `gatewaylog.go` — `logs/tui_gateway_crash.log`: `[tui-parent]` lifecycle breadcrumbs, panic first lines, Go fatal crash output via `debug.SetCrashOutput`; URL redaction of user info and query, built on a WHATWG URL parser that stands in for the JavaScript `URL` constructor
- `gatewayrecovery.go` — restart budget of a locally started gateway (3 within 60 s), start-timeout report with up to four problem-looking stderr lines, confirm dialog offering to restart a background service of another build through `Host.ReplaceOwner`

#### Per-session store, gateway event dispatch and server requests

State is plain structs mutated on the update loop, with no reducer or subscription layer. `tuiStore` (one per session) holds `uiState` (session id and stored id, session info, usage, busy, status line, yolo, busy input mode, notice, background tasks) over one `sharedUI` for the window (theme, details modes, status bar place and fields, mouse mode, paste thresholds, streaming, timestamps, gateway reachability), the live `turnState`, `overlayState` (open prompts), ten finished spawn trees, delegation caps, the connection operation, goal and loop controls and the replay cursor. `eventHandler.handle` drops events of another session, fences `session.info`, `message.start`, `message.complete` and `error` by authority epoch and execution generation, then dispatches. Events handled: `gateway.ready`, `gateway.stderr`, `gateway.reconnecting`, `gateway.start_timeout`, `gateway.protocol_error`, `skin.changed`, `skills.changed`, `sessions.changed`, `session.info`, `session.updated`, `session.replay_gap`, `session.usage`, `session.control.update`, `session.resume_progress`, `session.reclaimed`, `message.start`, `message.delta`, `message.interim`, `message.complete`, `error`, `thinking.delta`, `reasoning.delta`, `reasoning.available`, `moa.reference`, `moa.progress`, `moa.phase`, `moa.aggregating` (ignored), `tool.generating`, `tool.start`, `tool.progress`, `tool.complete`, `tool.output_risk`, `todo.updated`, `status.update`, `notification.show`, `notification.clear`, `notice`, `reaction`, `request.cancel`, `clarify.request`, `approval.request`, `clarify.settled`, `approval.settled`, `connection.request`, `connection.update`, `login.exhausted`, `background.complete`, `btw.complete`, `review.summary`, `browser.progress`, `subagent.spawn_requested`, `subagent.start`, `subagent.thinking`, `subagent.progress`, `subagent.tool`, `subagent.complete`, `voice.partial`, `voice.status`, `voice.transcript`, `voice.interrupted`, `voice.speech`, `wake.detected`, `display.status`, `display.lease`, `display.install.log`, `display.install.done`. Server-to-client requests answered: `clarify`, `approval`, `sudo`, `display.install.sudo`, `secret`, `vault.unlock_prompt`, `vault.save_login`, `vault.code`; a prompt of a session not in view stays open on the gateway and is redelivered when that session is attached.

- `turnstore.go` — `tuiStore`, `uiState`, `sharedUI`, `turnState`, `subagentProgress`, `spawnSnapshot` history (newest 10, also loaded from disk), submission destination (session, stored id, profile, canonical `ICEBATH_HOME` path), replay cursor, end-of-turn archive of the task list
- `sessionstores.go` — delegation caps and spawn pause, pet reaction flash (1.6 s), affection heart of the status row (650 ms), bubbles already painted for an admission, voice capture state, connection operation snapshots (64 remembered ids), goal and loop control snapshot
- `overlay.go` — request structs of every prompt kind (approval, confirm, clarify, sudo, secret, vault unlock, vault save-login, vault code, connection card) and `overlayState`; a finished turn drops flow prompts but keeps the agents panel, connection card and confirmation
- `eventhandler.go` — `eventHandler`: first-ready sequence (apply skin, start the wake-word listener on the first card, load `commands.catalog`, reattach a recovering session, else resume `ICEBATH_TUI_RESUME`, else the most recent session when `display.tui_auto_resume_recent` is on, else create one), single shared `config.get full` fetch, batched thinking status, prompt bell, abandoned-clarify block, `spawn_tree.save` of finished fan-outs, once-per-turn agents nudge (`display.tui_agents_nudge`), voice transcript routing (submit, draft or queue by `voice.submit_mode`), wake-word handling; `quietRequest` has no caller
- `eventdispatch.go` — the event switch itself plus status-update kinds (goal verdicts, compaction), tool completion to trail row or inline diff plus image, turn completion (final rows, late interrupt rewrite, completion bell, usage merge, billing wall), error events (a "no provider" error opens setup), session-info application, subagent lifecycle, deferred model-pick outcome, resume progress, reclaimed-session warning
- `eventhelpers.go` — opening URLs with the OS handler (http and https only), billing-wall and setup-required dialog copy, usage counter merging that keeps known values, abandoned-clarify formatting
- `canonicalevents.go` — epoch and generation fence, shared approval and clarify cards opened from `approval.request` and `clarify.request` events and cleared by the `*.settled` events
- `serverrequests.go` — opens the prompt card of each server request, remembers the request for its answer, withdraws cards on `request.cancel`, leaves other sessions' prompts unanswered
- `usermessages.go` — table mapping wire error codes and message patterns (4000, 4001, 4018, -32601, version skew, unsupported command, shell and slash failures, turn failures, prompt timeouts, credential warnings) to user-facing copy, backend gave-up and reconnecting notices, stderr problem detection
- `configsync.go` — pushes `config.get` results into UI state (bells, theme mode, voice record key, destructive-confirm, battery, compact, details and section modes, focus view, indicator, inline diffs and images, mouse, paste thresholds, reasoning display, status bar, streaming, timestamps, arena, pet render mode, turn summary, token flow, language), polls `config.get mtime` every 5 s, reloads MCP on a new revision with backoff from 5 s to 5 min after a refusal

#### Turn state machine: streaming, reasoning, tool trail, interrupts and the turn summary

`turnController` turns the event stream of one turn into transcript segments. Reply deltas are batched (16 ms, 80 ms while the user types, 96 ms while scrolling) and the live text is bounded to 16,000 characters and 240 lines; reasoning arrives as deltas or a whole block, is kept to its newest 60,000 units past 80,000 and is shown only with reasoning display on; inline `<think>`-style tags are split out of the reply. Tool calls move from an active row with progress to finished rows merged into a "shelf", or into an inline diff segment for edits; the final message is deduplicated against streamed segments. An interrupt calls `session.interrupt` with the execution generation and is sealed into the transcript only when the answer shows the same turn still running.

- `turncontroller.go` — the state machine: five generation-cancelled timers, notices held until the turn ends, activity and trail lines (newest 8), mixture-of-agents reference segments, todo list capture, image segment under a tool call, interim messages, subagent upsert, interrupt and its 1.5 s cooldown, token-flow estimate
- `liveprogress.go` — `msg` transcript row type (role, kind, text, thinking, tool rows, todos, images, paste sections), todo tree ordering, tool-shelf merging rules
- `reasoning.go` — strips `think`, `reasoning`, `thinking`, `thought` and `REASONING_SCRATCHPAD` tags from replies into reasoning text
- `turnsummary.go` — per-turn tally of tool calls into verbs ("edited 2 files +10 -3", "ran 3 commands") with elapsed time, printed as the closing line of a turn when `display.turn_summary` is on and the turn used tools or took 2 s; fixed English map of 16 tool names
- `subagent_key.go` — id the store gives a subagent of an event payload

#### Session lifecycle: create, attach, resume, detach, list, mutate

`sessionLifecycle` owns what a card shows. A new session first asks `setup.status`; with no provider configured and no launch route it shows the setup-required panel and opens the get-started screen instead of creating. `session.create` takes its options from the launch environment (`ICEBATH_MODEL`, `ICEBATH_TUI_PROVIDER`, `ICEBATH_CWD`, `ICEBATH_TUI_CWD`, `ICEBATH_TUI_BASE_URL`, `ICEBATH_TUI_API_KEY`, `ICEBATH_TUI_REASONING`, `ICEBATH_TUI_TOOLSETS`, `ICEBATH_TUI_SKILLS`, `ICEBATH_TUI_CLIENT_ENV`, `ICEBATH_TUI_MAX_TURNS`, `ICEBATH_YOLO_MODE`, `ICEBATH_IGNORE_RULES`, `ICEBATH_SAFE_MODE`, `ICEBATH_IGNORE_USER_CONFIG`, `ICEBATH_TUI_CHECKPOINTS`, `ICEBATH_TUI_PASS_SESSION_ID`, `ICEBATH_ACCEPT_HOOKS`) and inherits the logins of the session it was opened from. Resume uses `session.resume` with a display projection; a reattach after reconnect passes the replay cursor so missed events are replayed over the transcript on screen, else the transcript is read anew. Every change to a session goes through `session.mutate` as compare-and-swap on the revision read from `session.revision` (operations seen: `model`, `reasoning`, `branch`, `compress`, `rename`, `rewind`, `workspace`, `sidebar`, `archive`, `delete`), retried under the same request id.

- `sessionlifecycle.go` — start, resume by id, reattach, switch to a live session, detach with waiters, stale-attachment disposal, new-session notices (credential, config, redaction off, inventory), the banner's update line, `ICEBATH_TUI_ACTIVE_SESSION_FILE` writer, busy-switch guard; `clearSession` (blank transcript then fresh session, meant for a `/clear` command) has no caller
- `sessionattach.go` — `attachment` built from a session snapshot
- `sessioninfo.go` — nil-safe session-info accessors and patching, pending rows (owner admissions and forwarded submissions)
- `sessionlist.go` — `session.list` in live or stored scope as `listedSession` rows
- `sessiondelete.go` — delete and other record mutations of a stored session not open in a card
- `canonical.go` — `session.create` parameters: `source: "tui"`, request id, launch-environment options, tool-progress mode validation (`off`, `new`, `all`, `verbose`)
- `canonicalcontrols.go` — `asyncDoneMsg` continuation, `mutateCanonical`, model payload parsing (`--provider`, `--reasoning`, `--login`, `--global`, `--session`), guarded-model confirmation dialog, superseded-answer check, model switch application with optional login pin
- `backgroundsessions.go` — watch over sessions this window left running: a transcript notice when one finishes its turn or starts waiting on an answer

#### Session window: layout, status row, control bars and banner

`sessionCard` is the window of one session. Top to bottom: widgets docked above, the transcript (with the pet in its corner and widget corner overlays), then "chrome" rows (queued inputs panel of four rows, goal bar, loop bar, dock of working agents and background processes, prompt-stash panel, rewind hint, quick-help card while the draft is a single question mark), a gap, and the composer with its completion popup. The status sits in the window's bottom edge: spinner (styles `unicode`, `emoji`, `ascii`), rotating status verb, elapsed time, token flow, turn facts and spawn read-out at the left; notice, live voice transcript, attachment count or key legend plus session facts at the right. Facts: yolo, model with effort and fast mark, context use (warm at 50 percent, red at 80), cost, session duration, folder with project and git branch, battery, voice, live sessions elsewhere, stash pin, compressions, cache-hit share, average latency, tokens per second, background tasks, subagents; `display.status_bar.fields` and `display.tui_statusbar` (`top`, `bottom`, `off`) decide which show and where. Mouse tracking is `off`, `wheel`, `buttons` or `all` (`ICEBATH_TUI_MOUSE` at boot, off under Termux or `ICEBATH_TUI_NATIVE=1`).

- `sessioncard.go` — the card: view composition, footer status line, mouse (wheel, scrollbar drag, click to place cursor, double click selects all, right click copies or pastes, tap opens a block part or a link), key actions for scrolling, details and paste folding, queue panel, quick help, legend and hints
- `controlbars.go` — goal bar (active, paused or parked goal with its barrier) and loop bar (cadence and countdown, repainted each second) from session control snapshots
- `bannerart.go` — session banner art from the skin's rich-markup logo: wordmark when the window fits it, else the stacked mark, else none
- `content.go` — composer hint texts, 15 spinner verbs, `/fortune` texts (random, and a daily one hashed from session id and date with JavaScript string hashing)
- `paths.go` — folder labels (home as tilde, left ellipsis, project name, branch cut to 15 units) and the terminal tab title (marker, session name, model, folder)
- `gitbranch.go` — branch of the session folder via `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` (500 ms timeout, cached 15 s, one call per folder in flight)
- `batterypoll.go` — `system.battery` poll every 30 s while the battery indicator is on

#### Transcript view: blocks, details, reading mode, scrolling

The transcript is a flat list of `msg` rows capped at 800 (intro kept), each rendered once into a block cached by content, width, look and what the user opened in it (cache of 4000 blocks); every frame concatenates all block rows and windows them by scroll offset, so there is no height virtualisation despite the file name. Blocks: session banner (click opens the system prompt), user prompt with collapsed pastes, assistant markdown, reasoning, tool rows (call label, duration, verdict, note, output folded to three lines), task list nested to four levels, inline diffs, delegation results folded to four lines, long system messages folded past 400 units, slash panels, usage gauge rows, images. Detail sections `thinking`, `tools`, `subagents`, `activity` each take `hidden`, `collapsed` or `expanded`; focus view shows only prompts and replies; compact drops blank rows; `[HH:MM]` timestamps are optional. The window follows the newest row until scrolled, keeps the current prompt sticky on the top row, shows a draggable scrollbar, and has a reading mode (leader v, leader /) for cursor movement, search and copy.

- `transcriptview.go` — `transcriptView`: block cache, renderers per block kind, live-turn rows (settled segments, running tools, stream with a stable boundary so only the tail re-renders, activity, tasks), sticky prompt, scrollbar
- `transcriptparts.go` — clickable parts of a block (`thinking`, `tools`, `activity`, `todos`, `system`, `prompt`, `paste:N`, `tool:N`), per-block open state, scroll anchoring across layout changes, shift or ctrl click opening every section
- `transcript.go` — stored-session rows replayed through a turn controller on stored timestamps so history renders exactly like a live turn, settled clarify rows, shell output rows, history cap, block grouping and gaps
- `transcriptlines.go` — message timestamp and usage-gauge row painting
- `usagegauge.go` — detects ten-cell `[|||||     ]` gauge bars in system lines and colours them green, yellow above half, red above 80 percent; short session label (8 hex of a local id or a hash of a stored id)
- `pastesections.go` — remembers the paste bodies behind the chips of a sent prompt and renders them as unfoldable sections under it
- `viewmode.go` — `cards.Readable` adapter for reading mode, sweep-selection scrolling, the area a dialog sheet may cover
- `details.go` — section names, defaults and mode resolution; `parseDetailsMode` and `nextDetailsMode` have no caller (leftovers of a cycling `/details` command)
- `virtualheights.go` — Termux detection (`ICEBATH_TUI_TERMUX_MODE`), slash panel types, a JavaScript-compatible djb2 hash and `messageHeightKey`, which survives only as the block cache key; the height-estimate constants are unused
- `text.go` — UTF-16 unit helpers and JavaScript `slice` and `toFixed` equivalents used across the package (port scaffolding), next to real behaviour: ANSI stripping, live-render bounds, paste chip labels, tool call labels, verdict marks and trail grouping
- `wheelaccel.go` — mouse wheel acceleration with separate curves for native terminals and xterm.js, bounce filtering, one-row precision mode while alt or ctrl is held, base speed from `ICEBATH_TUI_SCROLL_SPEED` or `CLAUDE_CODE_SCROLL_SPEED`

#### Inline images and PDF attachment

Pictures in the transcript (attached images, images a tool made or viewed, `/screen shot`) are laid out by the gateway (`image.render`) as kitty Unicode placeholders or half blocks within 64 by 16 cells, the form chosen from the client's own environment; on other terminals that answer the graphics probe with kitty placement, sixel or iTerm2 support, the client reads the file itself and draws real pixels over blank rows within 120 by 20 cells. Images attached to a prompt are staged first: copied into `<profile home>/cache/images/` or, for a remote gateway, uploaded with `image.attach_bytes`.

- `inlineimages.go` — layout cache (48 entries, least recently used), terminal graphics pick (kitty for kitty and ghostty, else Unicode; tmux, screen, VS Code and WezTerm forced to Unicode), half-block painting, retry after config change
- `placedimages.go` — pixel pictures: protocol choice, fitting to the cell box, placement boxes, redraw 120 ms after movement stops and after full repaints, release on exit, `clearScreen`
- `images.go` — image sniffing (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP), 20 MiB limit, path resolution of quoted paths and `file://` URLs with trailing text kept as the prompt, staging
- `pdfpages.go` — `/image file.pdf [N|N-M]`: renders up to 25 pages at 150 dpi with poppler (`pdfinfo`, `pdftoppm`) and attaches each page as an image

#### Composer: editing, tokens, paste, clipboard, editor, history, completion, stash

The composer widget is `cards.Composer`; this group is what the TUI adds. Long pastes (5 lines or 2000 characters by default) collapse into a `[[ head.. N lines .. tail ]]` chip token that expands when sent and can be unfolded and edited in place; images become `[[ Image N ]]` tokens; at most 32 tokens and 4 MiB of token text are kept. A paste that is a single path is tried as an image or PDF, then offered to `input.detect_drop`; an empty paste tries the clipboard image. Paste reads the system clipboard tool first (`pbpaste`, PowerShell, `wl-paste`, `xclip`) and the terminal's own clipboard first over SSH. Completion asks `complete.slash` and `complete.path` after a 60 ms debounce: slash names, inline skill triggers after a space and slash, `@` references, and plain paths only on tab; arguments of local commands complete from their own lists or from models, providers, sessions, profiles and paths.

- `composerio.go` — attach, paste and clipboard flows, external editor round trip, `{!cmd}` interpolation runner, details and thinking toggles, yolo toggle, cut, suspend to shell, voice record toggle, the `tui` action switch; exported hooks `ClipboardImage` and `ClipboardImageBlocker`
- `composertokens.go` — token model, expansion at submit, slash and interpolation detection, completion request shaping, dropped-path detection, paste chip expand and collapse; `sessionScopedModelArg` and `hasPasteChip` have no caller
- `completion.go` — debounced completion of the composer that takes typing (session card or room card), tab path completion with common prefix, widget commands merged into offers
- `slash_args.go` — argument completion per command with a 15 s cache of gateway values
- `fuzzyscore.go` — ranking of slash menu entries: names and aliases before descriptions
- `history.go` — prompt history shared by every composer: `input_history.jsonl`, 1000 entries, duplicates collapsed, 4 MiB of paste chips kept newest first, atomic rewrite on each send
- `clipboard.go` — clipboard text backends per platform, 4 MiB cap, binary-residue filter
- `editor.go` — `$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`, then notepad on Windows or the first fallback editor on `PATH`, run on a temp file with the screen suspended
- `promptstash.go` — ctrl+s prompt stash: park the draft with its tokens, restore the only one, or browse several in a panel; status-bar pin and composer hint
- `promptstash_model.go` — stash stack (20 drafts, in memory for the process) and the ctrl+s decision table, written as an exported dictionary-shaped API left from the port; `PanelRows`, `AsDict` and `Peek` have no caller

#### Submission, input while busy and the durable queue

Every input is journaled before it is sent: one JSON file per submission under `tui-pending-inputs/` (written to a temp file, fsynced, renamed, directory fsynced) and removed when the owner's admission receipt confirms it, so queued and in-flight inputs survive a crash and follow a session across resume or migration. `prompt.submit` carries the input id, attachments, a voice-turn flag and whether it queues behind a turn. While a turn runs, enter follows the busy input mode: `queue` submits behind the turn, `steer` sends `session.steer`, `interrupt` sends `session.redirect`; corrections are text only, are sent once and never resent, and a correction refused as undelivered is readmitted as a queued prompt. Inputs typed with no session or while offline wait in the local queue and drain when the session is idle; the queue panel also lists the owner's own pending rows, which can be edited, cancelled or, when lost in a gateway restart, discarded.

- `submissioncore.go` — `promptSubmitter.submitPrompt`: owned-turn bubble, journal preparation, correction settlement, admission receipt check against stored session and profile, busy-session fallback to the queue, a bare image path sent as an attachment with a default question
- `queue.go` — `composerQueue` per destination: enqueue, stage, claim, dequeue, edit in the composer (up and down step through entries), take (an edited entry re-expanded with JavaScript `replace` semantics and given a new delivery identity when its text changed), remove, receipt reconciliation, owner rows, typed-interpolation splicing; `prependQ` has no caller
- `queueslash.go` — `/queue` argument plan (`list`, `add`, `edit N [text]`, `rm N`, `move A B`, `clear`, anything else queues the text) and its execution
- `pendinginputs.go` — journal record format, load by destination, successor chains for migrated sessions
- `slash_recovery.go` — `/discard <admission_id>`: resolves a turn the gateway lost in a restart without rerunning it; texts are hard-coded English

#### Prompt dialogs and the pager

One `dialogCard` type renders every prompt as a sheet attached to the session card, most urgent first: approval of a dangerous command (once, session, always, deny, or deny and tell the agent what to do instead, with the words steered into the held turn; enter on an untouched approval denies), masked sudo and secret prompts, vault unlock, vault save-login, vault one-time code, the connection card (per-target states, open link in browser, credential fields, retry, skip, check now), clarify question sets (single or multiple choice, free text, answers locked one by one) and generic confirmations. Answer keys are held back briefly on dialogs the user did not open, losing focus never declines, and text typed into a dialog carries over when a newer copy replaces it.

- `dialogs.go` — `dialogCard`, `dialogState`, builders per prompt kind, answers via the stored server request or `approval.respond`, `clarify.respond` and connection methods, interrupt-key behaviour on prompts, `pagerCard` used for long command output; the `settingSecret` and `loginKey` kinds named in `Guarded` are never built

#### Rewind, undo, retry and fork

`/rewind`, or escape twice on an idle empty composer, lists earlier prompts of the session; picking one puts it back in the composer with its images and arms a rewind, and the next send cuts the session back to just before that prompt (`session.mutate` operation `rewind`) and sends the edit. `/rewind fork N` branches a new session holding everything before the prompt.

- `rewind.go` — rewind targets from the owner's rows (prompts with media keep their number but are not offered), arm, cancel, send, fork, busy refusals, typing and pasting while the list is open

#### Agents, background processes and the arena

Delegated subagents are tracked from `subagent.*` events merged with a polled `subagent.list`. The dock above the status row shows up to five working agents and background processes (f7 folds it). `/agents` opens the spawn tree window: tree with heat marks, Gantt strip, sort (depth first, tools, duration, status) and filter (all, running, failed, leaf), node detail, live output tail (`subagent.tail` every 1.5 s), steer (`subagent.steer`), kill one or a subtree (`subagent.interrupt`), pause spawning (`delegation.pause`), history of finished trees and a side-by-side diff. Commands: `/agents [pause|resume|status]`, `/processes` (list, read output, kill), `/replay [N|last|list|load <path>]` for finished or saved trees (`spawn_tree.list`, `spawn_tree.load`), `/replay-diff <a> <b>`, `/arena`.

- `spawntree.go` — tree building and aggregates, `spawnTreeCard` whose keys other than back are hard-coded in the card rather than in the keymap, status-row fan-out read-out against depth and concurrency caps, dock rows, diff view, saved-tree list
- `agentroster.go` — merges live events with the polled list, failed delegations of the session
- `processroster.go` — process snapshot, dock rows (exited ones kept 60 s), `/processes` list with read and kill keys
- `slash_agents.go` — the four commands above
- `arenafeed.go` — extras tier only: feeds session state (tools, todos, agents, approvals, usage) into the `pkg/vxl/arena` voxel view and implements its harness (interrupt, steer, open tail, pause, stop, retry); registers `/arena`

#### Slash command runtime, palette and help

A line starting with a slash runs in this order: tier refusal, a local command, a widget id, a gateway catalog alias (exact, else a single fuzzy match, else an "ambiguous" list), then `slash.exec` on the gateway, falling back to `command.dispatch` whose result is `exec` or `plugin` output, an `alias`, a `skill` or `send` message to submit, or a `prefill` of the composer. Output longer than 180 characters or two lines opens in the pager. Most typed local commands report themselves once through `command.observe`. Every local and catalog command is also a palette entry; one that needs arguments opens a form generated from its usage line. Unknown names get up to three nearest suggestions by edit distance, and commands that exist only in messaging chats say so. Core commands: `/help`; `/quit [--delete]` (delete this session after a confirmation); `/update [check]` (queue `icebath update` for after exit, or check now); `/mouse [on|off|toggle|wheel|buttons|all]`; `/new [title]` (a running session keeps running in the background); `/redraw`; `/status` (pages the gateway's status output); `/density [on|off|toggle]`; `/timestamps [on|off|status]`; `/palette`.

- `slash.go` — `slashCommand` and `slashRun` (answers dropped once the session left the view), dispatch chain, hotkey rows for help, destructive confirmation (`ICEBATH_TUI_NO_CONFIRM`), the core commands, unknown-command refusal
- `slash_lane.go` — joins the tools, snapshot, profile-archive, journey, worktree and handoff command sets
- `slash_wm.go` — `/palette`
- `hub_command_args.go` — parses usage lines (`[a|b]`, `<required>`, flags) into form fields for palette-run commands and builds the palette entries for local, catalog and alias commands
- `hub_help.go` — help screen: session hotkeys, leader keys, reading keys, then every command and alias; enter puts a command in the composer

#### Slash commands: transcript, session and display

Transcript and input: `/detail [minimal|normal|detailed|everything] [--session]` (writes `display.detail_level`); `/copy [n]` (selection or nth newest reply, OSC 52 over SSH or without a clipboard tool); `/paste` (clipboard image); `/image <path> [pages]`; `/prompt [text]` (compose in the editor); `/history [chars]`; `/save [json|md|html] [file] [redact]` (`session.export`, default `sessions/saved/`); `/queue`; `/steer <text>`; `/rewind [N | fork N]`; `/undo` (drops the last exchange and names files to `/rollback`); `/retry` (text prompts only); `/fortune [random|daily]`; `/logs`; `/client-log [lines]`; `/terminal-setup`. Display: `/statusbar [on|off|top|bottom|toggle]`, `/battery [on|off|status]`, `/theme [auto|light|dark]`, `/skin [name]`, `/indicator [unicode|emoji|ascii]`. Session: `/model [model] [--provider p] [--reasoning level] [--login name] [--global]` (bare opens the picker, `--refresh` rereads providers), `/reasoning [none|minimal|low|medium|high|xhigh|max|ultra] [--global]`, `/fast [normal|fast|ultrafast|status|on|off|toggle]`, `/personality [name]`, `/approvals [manual|smart|off] [--session]`, `/yolo`, `/pause [reason]` and `/resume` (emergency stop), `/busy [queue|steer|interrupt|status]`, `/bg <prompt>` and `/btw <question>` (side agents answered by `background.complete` and `btw.complete`), `/compress [here [N] | focus topic] [--preview] [--aggressive]`, `/branch [title]`, `/title [title]`, `/usage [reset [--force]]`, `/setup [section]`, `/voice [on|off|tts|status]`, `/wake [on|off|status]`. Operations: `/stop` (interrupt and `process.stop`), `/reload` (`reload.env`), `/reload-mcp [now]`, `/reload-skills`, `/browser [connect [url]|disconnect|status|close-profile]` (default `http://127.0.0.1:9222`), `/rollback [list|diff <hash>|<hash> [file] [--all]]` (filesystem checkpoints), `/skills [list|inspect|search|install|browse]`, `/plugins [update | enable|disable <name>]`; other `/skills` and `/plugins` verbs are forwarded to the gateway.

- `slash_commands.go` — transcript and operations commands, `session.mutate` rewind for undo and retry, undo rollback hint, session export writer, skills verbs as panels, plugins update-all (10 min budget)
- `slash_session.go` — `/bg`, `/btw`, `/model`, `/personality`, `/theme`, `/skin`, `/indicator`, `/approvals`, `/pause`, `/resume`, `/yolo`, `/reasoning`, `/fast`, `/busy`, and `/detail` handling with its level-to-fold map; `/busy status` reports `interrupt` for an empty value although the client default is `queue`
- `slash_control.go` — `/compress` (preview, aggressive, keep last 1 to 100 exchanges, transcript reloaded from the owner), `/branch`, `/setup`, `/wake`, `/usage`, `/voice`, `/title`
- `slash_usage.go` — usage panel sections: token totals, context line, compressions, provider rate-limit windows with a warning at 80 percent

#### Slash commands: tools, snapshots, worktrees, handoff, profile archives, bot screen

`/tools [list | enable <name>... | disable <name>...]` lists session tools by toolset and toggles toolsets and MCP tools, starting a fresh session when the gateway says so and refusing when the launch pinned toolsets. `/snapshot [list|create [label]|restore <id>|prune [N]]` manages state snapshots; restore confirms, releases the gateway socket, restores through the launcher and reopens the session. `/worktree [new [name]|list|prune [--dry-run]]` creates an isolated git worktree, moves the session's workspace and this process's working directory into it and records it for cleanup at exit. `/handoff <platform>` queues the session for a messaging platform and polls `handoff.state` (60 s unclaimed, 15 min running), then opens a fresh session. `/export [profile] [-o file]` writes a profile archive; `/import <backup.zip> [--force]` queues a home restore for after exit. `/screen [status|start|stop [force]|take [reason]|release [force]|shot|install|switch|keep]` drives the profile's bot desktop: status panel, viewer lease, thumbnail into the transcript, package install, sandbox image switch.

- `slash_tools.go` — `/tools` over `tools.list`, `tools.show`, `tools.configure`
- `slash_snapshot.go` — `/snapshot` and `releaseForMaintenance`, which blocks reconnects while the launcher restores
- `slash_worktree.go` — `/worktree` over the `worktree.*` methods; changes `TERMINAL_CWD`, `ICEBATH_CWD` and the creation environment of later sessions
- `slash_handoff.go` — `/handoff` state machine and its texts from the shared CLI catalog
- `slash_profiles.go` — `/export`, `/import`, and `commandText` for `cli.commands.*` catalog lines
- `slash_screen.go` — `/screen` over the `display.*` methods with a random viewer id kept for the process

#### Learning journey

`/journey` opens a window over `learning.frames`: a pre-rendered timeline chart of learned skills and memories (animated with `--play`, partial with `--reveal`) above a tree of time slices and nodes, with node detail, edit in the external editor (`learning.edit`) and delete after confirmation (`learning.delete`). `/journey list`, `--json`, `delete <id> [-y]` and `edit <id>` work without the window over `learning.graph` and `learning.detail`.

- `slash_journey.go` — `journeyCard` and the command; the argument parser reproduces Python argparse usage and error wording, and every string is hard-coded English
- `colortones.go` — chart palette derived from the theme's primary and text colours, written with JavaScript `parseInt` and 32-bit integer semantics

#### Key bindings, terminal windows and IDE terminal setup

Nearly all keys go through the `pkg/ui/keys` map and are rebindable in `keybinds.json`. `/keys [filter|edit|reload|reset|option on|off]` shows every action by context with keys this terminal cannot send marked, edits the file in a terminal window, reloads, resets, or toggles reading macOS Option characters as alt chords. `/terminal [command]` and `/terminal-tab [command]` open a pty terminal window or tab in the session folder. `/terminal-setup [auto|vscode|cursor|windsurf]` adds shift+enter, ctrl+enter, cmd+enter, undo, redo and, on macOS, copy bindings to the IDE's `keybindings.json` (comment-tolerant parse, backup copy, conflict check).

- `slash_keys.go` — keybind file load at launch, the `/keys` panel and subcommands, chord sendability notes
- `terminals.go` — terminal windows and tabs, programs run for setup flows with their output handed back, shutdown of open terminals
- `terminalsetup.go` — IDE detection and keybinding writer, one-time startup hints for an IDE terminal not set up, Apple Terminal, tmux and SSH

#### Voice input and spoken replies

Extras tier only. Voice capture and transcription run in the gateway (`voice.toggle`, `voice.record`, wake word via `wake.*`); the TUI toggles recording, shows the partial transcript in the status row, submits or drafts the final transcript, and plays reply audio clips sent as `voice.speech` events. One session at a time holds the microphone.

- `voicekey.go` — parses `voice.record_key` (modifier plus letter or named key, reserved chords refused), binds it unless another action holds the chord, falls back to the leader key
- `speechplayer.go` — process-wide clip queue written to temp files and played through the injected `SpeechOutput`, thinking sounds, cut on interrupt, reports sounding state to the gateway

#### Text catalog and languages

Every UI string is a typed key from `pkg/ui/txt` resolved against the embedded English catalog; other languages are fetched from the gateway (`i18n.catalog`, surface `tui`) and applied only for keys English has, with `{key:action.id}` placeholders replaced by the chord bound now. `/language [id]` lists the profile's languages or sets `language`. Coverage is partial: some command texts come from the shared CLI catalog (`cli.commands.*`, `cli.tools.*`, `cli.tui.*`) and `/timestamps`, `/discard`, `/journey`, `/snapshot restore` and widget messages are hard-coded English.

- `i18n.go` — catalog loading, `tr`, `trOr`, `trCount`, positional formats, locale switch with in-flight de-duplication, error and warning line wording
- `language.go` — `/language` and the language picker
- `locales/en.tui.yaml` — [data] English catalog: 3,821 lines of literal `strings` and positional `formats`, embedded by `i18n.go`

#### Themes and skins

A theme is a palette of 34 colour slots plus brand (name, prompt symbol, welcome, goodbye, tool prefix, help header) and banner art. It is built from a gateway skin (`gateway.ready` and `skin.changed` carry colours split by polarity, branding and banners) or from built-in light and dark seeds, with neutral tones derived and lifted to WCAG contrast, and ANSI foregrounds normalised on light terminals. Light or dark is decided in order by `ICEBATH_TUI_LIGHT`, `ICEBATH_TUI_THEME` (also set by the `theme` config), `ICEBATH_TUI_BACKGROUND` (filled from the terminal's OSC 11 and OSC 10 answers), `COLORFGBG`, `TERM_PROGRAM`, and on macOS `defaults read -g AppleInterfaceStyle` when nothing else answered. The resolved theme is saved for the next launch's first frame.

- `theme.go` — palette type, seed derivation, contrast maths, light-mode detection, skin-to-theme mapping
- `themesync.go` — skin application, terminal default colours painted from an authored background, background and foreground probes, macOS appearance probe, repaint after a theme change
- `themeboot.go` — `tui-theme-boot.json` (version 2): read at startup to seed the theme and background hint, written 400 ms after a theme commit
- `paint.go` — tone-to-colour conversion, plain mode for `TERM=dumb`, `TERM=linux` or `NO_COLOR`, mapping of the session theme onto the toolkit theme

#### Hub kit: the shared shape of management screens

A "hub" is an overlay screen for things to manage, built on `cards.Hub`: a root list with a detail pane, on which pickers, forms, per-row action lists and output pages are pushed, with a note line for busy, failed and done. Each hub file registers itself from `init` with an id, order, slash command, palette entry and extra keys; the keys shared by every hub come from `pkg/ui/cards` (`hub.use`, `hub.add`, `hub.edit`, `hub.remove`, `hub.rename`, `hub.toggle`, `hub.default`, `hub.refresh`, `hub.back`, `hub.help`) plus `hub.pick` and `hub.run` here. `/hubs` lists them: `/sessions`, `/logins`, `/settings`, `/fallback`, `/mixes`, `/memory-provider`, `/projects`, `/plugins`, `/mcp`, `/system`, `/cron`, `/kanban`, `/profiles`, `/hooks`, `/secrets`, `/vault`, `/chat-apps`, `/after-exit`, `/run`.

- `hub_kit.go` — `hubDef` registry, slash and palette commands of every hub, `hubCall`, `hubPick`, `hubForm`, `hubAsk`, two-step model picker, action lists with confirmation, clipboard copy, `hubRunCLI` running the icebath binary with `NO_COLOR=1` and streaming its output into a page

#### Hubs: sessions, logins and models

- `hub_sessions.go` — `/sessions [id|search]`: live and stored sessions (200 each) with marks for shown here, shown elsewhere, running, live and pinned; open here, beside or in a new space, rename, pin, archive, export (Markdown, JSON, HTML, optional redaction), delete, close a background session, prune older than N days; reloads on `sessions.changed`
- `hub_logins.go` — `/logins [provider]`: every provider's logins with session, default and rotation marks and usage windows; add an API key, link a key from an environment variable or another detected source, OAuth sign-in with link and code (open, copy), rename, remove, set default, rotation, move an environment key into icebath's store, pin a login to this session, and the `login.exhausted` prompt
- `pickers.go` — model picker palette: models of signed-in providers with the login they go out with, sign-in rows, reasoning-effort step, session or global scope (ctrl+g), jump to logins (ctrl+d); `closeHeld` has no caller
- `hub_fallback.go` — `/fallback`: ordered chain of models tried when the main model fails; add, move, remove, check
- `hub_mixes.go` — `/mixes`: saved model mixes, one model that acts plus models that advise it; add, edit slots, set default, remove

#### Hubs: settings, setup and first run

- `hub_settings.go` — `/settings [group|search]`: every registry setting by group with value, source and where else it is asked; everyday and advanced tabs, search, edit by kind, global or session scope, reset
- `hub_setup.go` — `/setup [model|helpers|agent|voice|terminal|tools|chat-apps|quick|blank|import]`: forms that read settings, `.env` keys and facts of this computer and write them back, long-running setup actions started and polled, toolset selection, blank-slate reset, quick setup, agent import
- `hub_firstrun.go` — get-started screen shown when no model is configured: pick a provider (signed-in first) or your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, add a login, pick the model for every session

#### Hubs: plugins, skills, MCP, hooks, memory

- `hub_plugins.go` — `/plugins`: seven tabbed parts (installed plugins, catalog, installed skills, skill hub, bundles, skill sources, trusted projects) with install after capability consent, enable, settings form from the plugin's schema, update, trust update URL, doctor, remove; widget rescan after changes
- `hub_mcp.go` — `/mcp`: configured servers with runtime state; add from the catalog or by hand, enable, test (tool count), OAuth sign-in, API key, per-tool allow list, remove
- `hub_hooks.go` — `/hooks`: shell hooks per agent event with consent state and event webhooks; add, allow, revoke, toggle, test run, check, remove

#### Hubs: scheduled jobs, kanban, projects, profiles, chat apps

- `hub_cron.go` — `/cron [verb …]`: jobs with schedule and last outcome refreshed every 5 s; create and edit form, run now, pause, resume, cancel, rename, remove, run history with saved output, per-job notepad, health screen with incident acknowledgement, service install queued for after exit; other words run as the CLI's cron command
- `hub_kanban.go` — `/kanban [verb …]`: board grouped by column refreshed every 3 s; create, move with a reason where required, complete or reopen, comment, assign to a profile, rename, remove, archived toggle, switch or create boards

- `hub_profiles.go` — `/profiles`: profiles with model, skills and purpose; switch (queued for after exit), describe by hand or by the auxiliary model, rename, remove, export, alias, create or clone, import an archive, install from git or a folder
- `hub_chatapps.go` — `/chat-apps`: messaging platforms with state, pending pairings, webhook routes and peers; set up a platform, approve a pairing code, add or edit webhooks and peers, send a message to a peer agent, print the Slack manifest, queue the service install

#### Hubs: secret stores and autofill vault

- `hub_secrets.go` — `/secrets`: Bitwarden and 1Password as key sources; set up, new token, check, turn off, map environment variables to 1Password references, preview what the next start would load
- `hub_vault.go` — `/vault`: autofill items (logins, cards, addresses), password-manager sources on or off, vault key moved between keychain and file

#### Hubs: system, CLI commands and the after-exit queue

Commands of the icebath binary are read from the gateway (`commands.tree`) with a class: runnable inside (in a hub page or a terminal window), internal (hidden), or after-exit. After-exit commands (update, profile switch, backup import, service install, restart) are queued in `after-exit/window-<pid>.json` and run by the launcher once the TUI exits (`TakeAfterExit`); queues of windows that died are offered for adoption or dropping.

- `hub_system.go` — `/system [section]`: service (state, restart, emergency stop read from the `ESTOP` file), health, logs (files of the profile and root `logs/` with level filter and follow), storage (sizes of the home's parts), packages, updates, security, LSP, computer use, proxy, migrations; sections hidden when the build lacks their commands; also `/update`
- `hub_afterexit.go` — the queue file format and operations, `TakeAfterExit`, orphaned queues of dead pids, `/after-exit` screen with "quit and run"
- `runcommand.go` — `/run [command]`: every runnable icebath command with a form generated from its flags and arguments, or a typed command line (ctrl+t), run in a terminal window or queued for after exit

#### Rooms

Rooms are multi-agent group chats hosted by the gateway (`groups.*` methods), not a layout concept: two to six seats filled by local profiles or profiles on peer gateways. `/rooms` lists rooms here and those peers share (rename, stop, disband, share or unshare with peers, continue a shared room here, show disbanded). A room opens as its own window with a live log, a composer, file attach (15 MB limit) and download, and a list of pending approvals and stuck turns to approve, retry or discard.

- `rooms.go` — rooms list panel, creation flow with member seating, keys of both contexts and the leader-key room group
- `roomcard.go` — `roomCard` window: log polling, event lines, send with uploads, files, pending actions, room menu

#### Widgets

A widget is a small view opened by its slash command: modal (a window that takes keys) or ambient (docked top or bottom or in a corner of the session card in view, optionally ticking). Built-in ids are `ticker` (fake price sparkline), `weather` (Open-Meteo and ipwho.is over HTTP), `grid-test` and `dialog-test` (layout demos); plugins add more through `PluginWidgets` and `ScanPluginWidgets`, announced in the transcript when they appear, vanish or fail.

- `widgets.go` — `Widget` contract (`Open`, `Input`, `Tick`, `Render`, `Back`, `Rows`), `RegisterWidget`, `OpenWidget`, `widgetHost` (scan, launch, ambient refresh, docks, corner overlays), `widgetCard`
- `widgets_builtin.go` — ticker, weather and dialog-test widgets
- `widgets_gridtest.go` — interactive grid demo with flat, zoomed, areas and streams modes
- `widgetgrid.go` — flow-grid and area-grid track solver and a cell canvas used by the demo; `autoFlowGrid` has no caller

#### Pets

Extras tier only. An animated pet sits in the corner of the session card in view and reacts to the session (awaited input, running tool, reasoning, busy turn, turn done, failure, user reaction) and to the `pet.changed`, `pet.generate.progress` and `pet.hatch.progress` events. Frames come from the gateway as half blocks or kitty placements (`pet.cells`) or as sixel or iTerm2 sprite sheets (`pet.sprite`), by `display.pet.render_mode`; a poll every 2.5 s follows changes made elsewhere. `/pet [toggle|list|select <slug>|off|scale <n>|rename|remove|export|info|<slug>]` manages pets and opens the gallery; `/hatch <description>` generates a new pet (base look up to 10 min, animation rows up to 30 min, cancellable) with progress and a preview box.

- `petview.go` — `petView`: state derivation, placement (right gutter or bottom band by window size), frame clock (160 ms), graphics protocols
- `slash_pet.go` — `/pet` and the gallery
- `slash_hatch.go` — `/hatch` job over `pet.generate` and `pet.hatch`

#### Diagnostics: frame meter, profiles, memory watchdog

`ICEBATH_TUI_FPS` overlays a frame-rate read-out; `ICEBATH_DEV_PERF` logs frames slower than `ICEBATH_DEV_PERF_MS` (default 2 ms) as JSON lines to `perf.log` or `ICEBATH_DEV_PERF_LOG`; `ICEBATH_CPUPROFILE` writes a CPU profile re-merged every 2 s. A watchdog samples the live heap every 10 s against a budget from the Go memory limit, cgroup limit or physical memory: it warns once on fast growth; at 70 percent it sheds render caches and writes a diagnostics file, plus a heap profile when `ICEBATH_AUTO_HEAPDUMP` is set, at most once per 10 min (`ICEBATH_AUTO_HEAPDUMP_COOLDOWN_MS`); at 88 percent it dumps and exits with status 137. Dumps go to `heapdumps/` or `ICEBATH_HEAPDUMP_DIR`, pruned to 2 GiB or `ICEBATH_HEAPDUMP_MAX_BYTES`; `ICEBATH_HEAPDUMP_ON_START=1` dumps at launch. Commands: `/theme-info`, `/mem`, `/heapdump`, `/widgets-reload`.

- `slash_debug.go` — the four commands and their panels
- `framemeter.go` — frame listener, read-out overlay, timing log
- `cpuprofile.go` — rotating merged CPU profile
- `heapdump.go` — memory snapshot, diagnostics JSON, heap profile, dump directory pruning
- `memwatch.go` — thresholds, watchdog loop, cache shedding, transcript notices, critical exit
- `memfacts_{linux,darwin,windows,other,unix}.go` — per-OS process probes used by the watchdog and dumps (resident and anonymous bytes, open descriptors, physical memory, cgroup limit, smaps rollup, resource usage); five variants, not a user-facing feature
