- `testdata/worktree-fixture.bundle` — [test-support] git bundle fixture; no Go file in the repository references it

### `pkg/tuiserver` — session-socket WebSocket handler and service method table of the gateway process, plus the retired in-process session runtime

*188 files, 30,394 Go lines*

Port of the Python `tui_gateway` server (`server.py`, `ws.py`, `entry.py`). It is compiled into the one `icebath` binary and runs inside the gateway process: `pkg/gatewayrun` admits a loopback WebSocket (one-time ticket in the subprotocol, no `Origin` header, peer 127.0.0.1 or ::1) and hands it to `HandleWS` through `cmd/icebath/session_socket.go`; there is no stdio JSON-RPC child and no unix socket any more. `HandleWS` forwards every request to `gateway.SessionAuthority`, which owns sessions, turns, config and slash execution (`pkg/gateway/session_controls_dispatch.go`) and falls back to this package's method table (`gateway.ServiceVerbs`) for 134 hub, setup, pet, voice, display, browser, MCP, worktree and composer methods. The package also starts process-wide services on the first connection (change watcher, backend heartbeat row in the launch `state.db`, startup orphan-row sweep, idle reaper, bot-desktop lease watcher) and exports helpers that `cmd/icebath/wiring.go` plugs into `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/agent` and `pkg/mcp`; outside the socket path `pkg/app` calls only `SettleWorktree` (terminal UI exit) and `ProjectInfoForCwd`, and `cmd/icebath` runs `AtExit`. Roughly half of the files are the old in-process session runtime (session records, per-session agent build, prompt turns, queueing, model switch, notification poller, teardown): its RPC handlers (`session.create`, `session.resume`, `prompt.submit`, `config.set`, `slash.exec`, `command.dispatch` and the rest) were deleted, the stdio entry loop is gone, and no code ever inserts a record into the `pkg/tuihost` session registry, so that runtime cannot execute and is tagged `[unwired]` below even where a live caller still loops over the empty registry. Handlers are Python-shaped throughout: untyped `map[string]any` params, panics used as exceptions, `internal/py*` helpers in most files.

#### WebSocket connection loop

One reader, one serial dispatcher and bounded side lanes per accepted socket. The first frame sent is the `gateway.ready` event (skin, replay epoch, Go build id); `gateway.ping` is answered inline with `{ok: true}`; every other text frame is parsed as JSON-RPC and answered by the connection's `gateway.AuthorityConnection` under the identity the ticket verified. Requests run in arrival order from a 256-frame queue, except `session.context_breakdown` and `session.account_usage` (side lane, 2 running and 8 waiting), response frames and `clarify.lock` (settled at once), and frames naming a profile that is still starting (held in a per-profile lane for up to 20 s, dropped if the client leaves first). Teardown closes the authority connection, unregisters the transport, releases the wake-word lease, voice claims and setup jobs it owned, and logs message, parse-error, crash and send-failure counts.

- `ws.go` — `HandleWS`, `ServedSocket`, `SocketPeer`, `SocketDisconnect`; TCP_NODELAY and keepalive (30 s idle, 10 s interval, 3 probes); -32700 parse error, -32603 dispatch crash; closes with code 1000

#### JSON-RPC method table, dispatch and worker pool

The registry every handler module installs into at `init`, the typed-contract wrapper (params fitted against `pkg/tuigateway`, results checked, misfits logged or panicking under `ICEBATH_TEST_ISOLATION`), the pool that runs slow methods off the reader, and the bridge exposing the table to the gateway as service verbs. A service verb requires every `interactive` capability on the connection and runs with the ticket's profile home bound; profile and config-backend outages answer 4064.

- `server_requests.go` — method map, `ok` and `rpcErr` frames, request normalising (-32600, -32602); also the approval, clarify and `ask` server-request bridges, image metadata and tool-env binding used almost only by the retired runtime
- `method_ctx.go` — `handlerRegistry`: per-module deferred registrar, optionally wrapping a handler in the profile scope of its params
- `rpc_dispatch.go` — `Dispatch`: binds the transport, settles response frames, runs long methods on a pool sized by `ICEBATH_TUI_RPC_POOL_WORKERS` (default 8, minimum 2); -32601 unknown method, 4000 params misfit, -32000 handler error
- `server_long_handlers.go` — names dispatched to the pool; still lists removed methods such as `session.branch`, `session.compress` and `session.workspace.move`
- `methods_tools_rpc.go` — `guardedRPC`, `scopedRPC` and `mcpRPC` wrappers (missing required param 4063, unknown profile 4064, body failure a per-area code) and `system.battery` for the status bar
- `service_verbs.go` — installs `gateway.ServiceVerbs`; binds a non-launch ticket profile, injects the `profile` param where the contract takes one, refuses an unresolved profile with 4064 and reason `profile_unavailable`
- `client_capabilities.go` — `client.capabilities`: records whether the client answers server requests and returns the request names the contract declares
- `methods_session_interrupt.go` — registers nothing since `session.interrupt` moved to the gateway; keeps the `callerTransport` and `strParam` helpers live handlers use

#### Process start-up, exit hooks, crash log and environment knobs

Once-per-process effects run by the first `HandleWS` call, the exit queue `cmd/icebath` drains at shutdown, and the crash record for goroutines that panic.

- `server_shutdown.go` — `loadServerModule` (loads the home `.env` and the repo `.env`, registers the session-settings store and the exit teardown, starts the idle reaper) and `shutdownSessions`
- `atexit.go` — `registerAtExit` and `AtExit`, run newest first with panics contained; `failureText` and `sortedKeys` helpers
- `server_crash.go` — appends an unhandled panic with its stack to the crash log and prints `[gateway-crash]` on stderr; the goroutine recover hook
- `env.go` — float and int environment knob readers that fall back to a default on absent or malformed values
- `float_value.go` — [py-shim] Python `float()` coercion of numbers, bools and numeric strings; live use is pet scale parsing
- `log.go` — package logger carrying `logger=tuiserver`

#### Stdio entry remnants

[unwired] What is left of the stdin and stdout JSON-RPC entry point, where the server ran as its own process with stdout reserved for frames: seam variables, signal name tables and MCP discovery helpers. There is no read loop, and nothing references `stdioEntry` or the `entry*` variables.

- `entry.go` — `stdioEntry` struct, unused seam variables and `logExit`; `appendCrashLog` is live and writes `logs/tui_gateway_crash.log` under the launch home
- `entry_mcp.go` — spawn, wait and join of the profile's background MCP discovery; called only from the retired agent build
- `entry_platform_{unix,windows}.go` — termination signal name tables per OS (2 files); Windows adds an unused routine that moves RPC stdin to a private handle

#### Launch home, profile scope and session stores

How a request is bound to a profile: the launch home captured on first use, named-profile resolution that also switches the process into multi-profile hosting, and context scoping of home, secrets and terminal policy.

- `server.go` — launch home, shared launch `state.db` handle, `profileHome` (unknown profile raises the 4064 error), storage-failure replies with gloss and remedy, `profileScoped`; also `sessionInfo` and `getUsage` payload builders that only local sessions reach
- `model_switch.go` — `ProfileRuntimeScope`: context bound to a profile's home, hydrated secrets and terminal policy (wired into `pkg/mcp`); the per-session variants are unreachable
- `server_profile_db.go` — read-only probed open of another profile's `state.db`, one schema reconcile per store, seeding of an empty served-profile store
- `server_project_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the cwd-to-project lookup in the profile projects db to `pkg/app`

#### On-disk change watcher

One goroutine per process, started by the first connection and ticking every 500 ms. It broadcasts `skin.changed`, `pet.changed` (checked every 2 s), `sessions.changed` (checked every 0.5 s, at most one broadcast per 2 s) and `skills.changed` (checked every 2 s) to every connected client when a cheap signature moves; the first sighting only seeds the baseline.

- `change_watcher.go` — session signature (digest of list-relevant `sessions` columns keyed on db and WAL mtime, activity stamps excluded so heartbeats stay silent) over the launch home and every served profile home, skills signature, broadcast loop
- `change_watcher_pet.go` — pet signature (slug, spritesheet revision, scale) and the `pet.changed` payload; extras build tag
- `change_watcher_skin.go` — skin payload of the active config and the profile home whose skin a peer follows

#### Backend heartbeat, startup orphan sweep and idle reaper

[partial] Started by the first WebSocket connection. The heartbeat row and the startup sweep act on the launch `state.db` and are live; this file is the only writer of `gateway_heartbeats`. The idle reaper still ticks every 300 s but walks the empty local registry, so its flush, TTL, cap and orphan-reap steps find nothing. Two of its side effects do run: an idle memory trim, and `activesessions.ReleaseOrphanedLeases` called with an empty owned set, which as written drops every active-session registry entry this pid created more than 30 s ago, including the `gateway:<platform>` leases `pkg/gatewayrun` claims.

- `session_reaper.go` — heartbeat row `profile@host:pid:nonce` refreshed every `ICEBATH_GATEWAY_HEARTBEAT_REFRESH_S` (60 s) and cleared at exit; one sweep after `sessions.ws_orphan_reap_grace_s` ending open `tui`, `subagent` and `unknown` rows idle past `ICEBATH_TUI_SESSION_TTL_S` (6 h) that no heartbeat covers, pinned rows spared, gated by `sessions.startup_orphan_sweep`
- `session_reaper_idle.go` — 300 s loop: incremental transcript flush (`ICEBATH_TUI_SESSION_FLUSH_INTERVAL_S`), TTL eviction with reason `idle_timeout`, re-arming of lost orphan reaps, cap, lease reclaim, memory trim when quiescent
- `session_reaper_cap.go` — evicts least recently active reapable sessions above `max_live_sessions` with reason `lru_evict`
- `session_reaper_flush.go` — exit path: flush every transcript within `ICEBATH_TUI_EXIT_FLUSH_BUDGET_S`, interrupt running turns and kill foreground commands still alive halfway through the settle budget
- `session_reaper_quiescent.go` — reap exemptions: never mid turn, awaiting input, building, delegating, on a live transport, or the sole receiver of a pending loop, heartbeat or process notice

- `slash_fuzzy.go` — exact, prefix and substring scoring over name and description, merging catalog entries the prefix filter missed
- `methods_commands_tree.go` — `commands.tree`: every CLI command path of this binary with plugin commands, built by `cmd/icebath`; fail code 5020

### `pkg/tuihost` — host-side plumbing shared by the session socket and the gateway: transports, event replay, server requests, transcript projection, logins

*57 files, 6,164 Go lines*

Shared library split out of the Python `tui_gateway` package so that `pkg/tuiserver` and `pkg/gateway` can both use it without an import cycle; it is not a process or supervisor, and it runs inside the gateway process. Live parts: the `Transport` abstraction with the per-connection `WSTransport` and the per-session `FanoutTransport`, event framing with per-session sequence numbers and a bounded replay ring, contract checks for server-to-client requests, the stored-transcript display projection, provider login management, the skin payload and watcher, the per-session settings store, and small payload helpers the gateway's turn runner calls. It also holds the registry of local session records with the transport-membership, parking, lease and journal code built around it; nothing ever inserts a record, so those parts serve only the retired runtime in `pkg/tuiserver`. It reads `config.yaml` and `skins/<name>.yaml`, stores session settings and login choices in the `model_config` column of `sessions` rows, and on the dead path writes `interrupted_turns.json` with a `.lock` beside it. Many files import `internal/py*` helpers, and several are one-line re-export shims or empty.

#### Transports: stdout lines, WebSocket and per-session fanout

`Transport` is anything a JSON-RPC frame can be written to. `WSTransport` coalesces `message.delta`, `reasoning.delta` and `thinking.delta` frames for 33 ms, keeps batches in wire order with a FIFO send lock, warns after a 10 s stalled write and closes the socket with 1011 after a 30 s send deadline. `FanoutTransport` gives each subscriber of a session an ordered mailbox bounded at 16384 frames or 4 MiB; an overflowing peer is detached, optionally handed a notice frame, and its socket aborted so the client reconnects and replays.

- `transport.go` — `Transport` interface, frame serialisation with an error-frame fallback, `FanoutTransport` with per-peer writer goroutines and generation-guarded batches
- `ws_transport.go` — `WSConn` and `WSTransport`: token coalescing, ordered batch sends, lone-surrogate sanitising, verified upgrade identity, the profile home whose skin the peer follows, abort on overflow
- `ws_transport_conn.go` — [port-artifact] accessor for the socket under a transport
- `stdio_transport.go` — line-per-frame writer to a stream resolved at each write, flush suppressed by `ICEBATH_TUI_GATEWAY_NO_FLUSH`; request-context transport binding (`BindTransport`, `CurrentTransport`)
- `stdio_transport_{unix,windows}.go` — errno values meaning the peer is gone, per OS (2 files)
- `stdio_sink.go` — the module stdout sink a frame falls back to when no transport is bound

- `stdin_recovery.go` — rate-limited recovery decision and fd 0 state description for the crash log
- `stdin_recovery_{unix,windows}.go` — fcntl and socket-option probes on POSIX, no-ops on Windows (2 files)

#### Event frames, broadcast and replay ring

Every event is a JSON-RPC notification with method `event` and params `{type, session_id, payload, seq}`, checked against its declared payload type on the way out. `StampEvent` numbers events per session key and keeps frozen copies: 512 frames and 4 MiB per session, 64 sessions and 64 MiB per process, with a truncation watermark so a resume can tell replayable from lost; the process-wide epoch token invalidates cursors across restarts. `pkg/gateway/session_events.go` uses the ring for its own per-session keys.

- `event_replay.go` — sequence stamping, ring eviction, `EventsSince`, `IsTruncated`, `LatestSeq`, key release, `ReplayEpoch`
- `global_events.go` — registry of connected transports, `EventFrame`, session-less broadcast to every client; the stdout-is-the-client flag it consults is never set
- `global_events_export.go` — [port-artifact] `LiveTransports` for the gateway's client count
- `server_emit.go` — the (never populated) session map, `WriteJSON` routing to the session transport, else the bound one, else stdout; `Emit` with the presentation mute `pkg/agent` installs for diagnostic-only turns
- `stream_segments.go` — turn id, segment index and UTF-16 offset stamped on the `message.start`, `message.delta` and `message.interim` frames of a running turn; used by `pkg/gatewayrun`

#### Server-to-client requests

Questions the backend asks a client (`approval`, `clarify`, `sudo`, `secret`, vault prompts, `display.install.sudo`) as JSON-RPC requests with ids `srq-<12 hex>`. A client answers, or declines with error 4404 when none of its windows shows the session; a request is refused only when every answering client declined. Withdrawals are announced with the `request.cancel` event and a reason (such as `interrupted`, `timeout` or `shutdown`), and batch clarify requests settle with locked answers and an outcome of `submitted`, `timed_out` or `cancelled`. The gateway keeps its own pending-request table and uses only the contract checks and the batch settle rule from here; the blocking `Send` path is still used for the session-less `display.install.sudo`.

- `server_requests.go` — open-request list, `Send` and `SendAsync`, response and decline resolution, cancel, per-transport capability advertisement, `CheckRequestParams`, `FittedAnswer`; `ResetForTests` test hook
- `settle_batch_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the batch clarify settle rule

[port-artifact][unwired] `Session` is a mutex-guarded string-keyed slot map standing in for the Python dict each live session was. The registry map is only ever read or deleted from, so every lookup returns nothing. The membership code models one session watched by several clients: a single transport is promoted to a fanout when a second attaches, viewers are tracked by attach time, a second login attaching is logged, and a disconnected session is parked on a sink that drops frames.

### `pkg/tuigateway` — typed wire contract between clients and the gateway: every method, server request and event

*46 files, 9,459 Go lines*

The schema of the JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol spoken over the gateway's session WebSocket by the Go terminal UI (`pkg/tui`), ACP, `gatewaycli` and workers: 235 method-table methods, 49 canonical (session authority) methods, 8 server-to-client requests and 68 events, each declared once with Go param and result types and registered in a name table at package init. `Strict` and `Loose` fitting validate params on the server (an unknown or missing key is refused with the field named and a hint that client and gateway run different builds) and results on the client; `SealPayload` checks every emitted event; `BuildID` lets a client detect a gateway of another build. The package holds no transport, discovery or reconnect code: attach, heartbeat and redial are in `pkg/tui/gateway.go`, socket admission in `pkg/gatewayrun`, handlers in `pkg/gateway` and `pkg/tuiserver`. Two routes coexist: `KindCanonical` entries are what the Go UI uses for sessions and prompts, while `KindMethod` duplicates of eighteen of those names (`session.create`, `session.resume`, `session.list`, `prompt.submit`, `session.interrupt`, `session.steer`, `session.redirect`, `approval.respond`, `clarify.lock`, `shell.exec`, `image.attach_bytes`, `profiles.list` and six `groups.*`) are shadowed by the canonical lookup, and fourteen method entries have no handler anywhere; both sets are leftovers of the original non-Go client's protocol [port-artifact]. Other traces of that client are camelCase pet fields, UTF-16 stream offsets, `rendered` fields no server fills, and aliases kept for older senders.

#### Contract registry, wire fitting and build identity

- `contract.go` — `Entry` table per route, `Method`, `Request` and `Event` generics with `Params`, `Result`, `Payload` and `Wire`, `ParamsRefusal` and `FitError` naming the field
- `fit.go` — reflection-based `Strict` and `Loose` decoding with typed enums (`Values()`), unions, open objects keeping extra keys, exact numbers; `Plain` (typed value to wire maps) and `Merge` (patch over base)
- `misfit.go` — `ReportMisfit` (panic under `ICEBATH_TEST_ISOLATION`, else error log), `SealPayload`, the shared unknown-method message
- `build.go` — Go build id read from the running image (ELF note, Mach-O text, raw markers) at start, and `SameBuild`

#### Session lifecycle, attach and transcript

A client attaches with canonical `session.create` or `session.resume` (by id, exact title or latest of a source; a `replay_from` cursor of replay epoch and last sequence asks for missed events instead of the transcript) and receives a `CanonicalSnapshot`: runtime and stored ids, messages, `running`, `authority_epoch`, `replay_epoch`, `last_sequence`, `subscription_id`, `revision`, `execution_generation`, pending admissions, open approval and clarify prompts, open server requests, todo state and `SessionInfo`. `session.detach` ends one subscription, `session.list` enumerates `live` or `stored` sessions, `session.revision` reads the fences without attaching, `session.mutate` applies a named edit fenced by request id, expected revision and generation, and the other canonical verbs are `session.info`, `session.stats`, `session.account_usage`, `session.prune`, `session.export`, `session.automation` and `runtime.describe`. Method-route entries: served by the gateway are `session.active_list`, `session.save`, `session.history`, `session.context_breakdown`, `session.control.read`, `setup.status` and `setup.runtime_check`; served by the tuiserver table are `session.most_recent` and `spawn_tree.save|list|load`; shadowed are `session.create`, `session.resume`, `session.list`; with no handler are `session.activate`, `session.delete`, `session.title`, `session.workspace.move`, `session.close`, `session.branch`, `session.undo`, `session.status`, `session.usage`, `session.compress` and `terminal.resize`. Events: `gateway.ready`, `skin.changed`, `session.info`, `session.usage`, `session.title`, `session.resume_progress`, `session.reclaimed`, `session.updated`, `session.replay_gap`, `session.control.update`.

### `pkg/ui` — terminal UI kit layered on Bubble Tea v2 (overview; the directory itself holds no Go files, only the twelve subpackages below)

*0 files*

`pkg/ui` is Go written directly on the Charm stack rather than a from-scratch toolkit, and it carries none of the port markers found elsewhere (no `pkg/internal/py*` imports outside `render/recap`, no `*_export.go` shims, no mixin structs). The event loop, input decoding (keys, the kitty keyboard protocol, mouse, bracketed paste, focus reports) and the `tea.View` model come from `charm.land/bubbletea/v2`; styling from `charm.land/lipgloss/v2`; cell buffers, grapheme widths and the escape-sequence parser from `charmbracelet/ultraviolet` and `charmbracelet/x/ansi`; markdown from `charm.land/glamour/v2` (which brings Chroma code highlighting); the multi-line prompt from `charm.land/bubbles/v2/textarea`; spring physics from `charmbracelet/harmonica`; colour-profile detection from `charmbracelet/colorprofile`. What the kit adds on top: its own terminal output stage that replaces Bubble Tea's renderer (`tty`), a tiling window manager (`wm`), reusable cards and widgets (`cards`), a rebindable keymap (`keys`), a line editor (`field`), clipboard access (`clip`), pixel-image protocols (`gfx`), themed text formatters (`render`), themes (`theme`), springs and the frame clock (`anim`) and the translation seam (`lang`, `txt`). The only consumers are `pkg/tui` (the application) and `pkg/vxl/arena`; `pkg/ui/cards` in turn imports `pkg/term` for terminal windows. Files the kit reads or writes under the profile home, with paths chosen by `pkg/tui`: `keybinds.json`, `drafts/<session>.json`, and `tui-layout.json` (the JSON form of `wm.Layout`). No stubs or TODO markers exist anywhere in `pkg/ui`; the dead pieces are named in the sections below.


### `pkg/ui/tty` — owner of the user's terminal and diffing output stage that replaces Bubble Tea's renderer

*25 files, 4,827 Go lines*

`tty.NewProgram` wraps a `tea.Program` created with `WithoutRenderer` and `WithoutSignalHandler`: Bubble Tea still reads and decodes all input, while `tty` owns raw mode, every byte written, mode sequences, the alternate screen, resizes, signals, job control and the restore on exit or crash. Its renderer parses each view's styled string into a cell grid, keeps a model of what the terminal currently shows, and writes the cheapest byte sequence that reaches the target, after measuring how many columns this terminal really gives each grapheme cluster. The sole consumer is `pkg/tui` (`app.go` runs the program, `tty.Exec` launches `$EDITOR`, `tty.Suspend` hands the terminal back to the shell, `FrameStat` feeds a frame meter). Environment: `ICEBATH_TTY_GUARD` and, on Windows, `ICEBATH_TTY_GUARD_HANDLES` mark the guard child; `COLUMNS` and `LINES` stand in for an unreported size (else 80 by 24). Capability detection here is limited to output behaviour (synchronized output, grapheme mode, REP, sized text, colour profile); image protocols are probed in `gfx`.

#### Program lifecycle, signals and job control

Opens stdin and stdout, or `/dev/tty` for an end that is redirected, enters raw mode, starts the guard and runs Bubble Tea at 60 frames per second behind a message filter that swallows the replies to tty's own probes. An interrupt, terminate or hangup reaches the model as `TerminateMsg`, a vanished terminal (five failed writes in a row, or five failed size requests checked one second apart) as `GoneMsg`; either way the program is killed if the model has not ended it within 5 s.

- `program.go` — `Program`: open, run, close; input filter; release and reclaim of the terminal around `Exec` (child process on the real terminal) and `Suspend`; `TerminateMsg`, `GoneMsg`, `SuspendRefusedMsg`, `ErrTerminalGone`; panic listener
- `terminal.go` — saved terminal state of both ends and its restore; `COLUMNS`/`LINES` size fallback
- `terminal_{unix,windows}.go` — raw mode per OS (VT input and VT processing on Windows consoles); signal loops (SIGWINCH, SIGTSTP, SIGCONT, SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP); `JobControl` test for an orphaned process group; hang-up check; Windows refuses every suspend
- `stop_{darwin,linux}.go` — [partial] stops the process group by resetting SIGTSTP to its default action through a raw `sigaction` call, and finds a parent pid; exists only for darwin and linux although `terminal_unix.go` and `guard_unix.go` are tagged for the BSDs, Solaris, illumos and AIX too, which leaves those targets without `stopDefault` and `parentOf`
- `stop_darwin.s` — assembly trampoline that jumps to libc `sigaction`, needed for the darwin raw call
- `sigset_linux{,_mips}.go` — size of the kernel signal set passed to `rt_sigaction`: 8 bytes, 16 on MIPS
- `ioctl_{bsd,linux}.go` — termios get and set ioctl request numbers per platform family

#### Crash guard process

At start the program re-executes its own binary with `ICEBATH_TTY_GUARD` set; a package `init` (present in every binary that links `tty`) turns that child into the guard and exits when it is done. Descriptor 2 is redirected into a pipe the guard spools, so Go runtime crash reports and stray stderr writes cannot land on the alternate screen. The program streams framed messages to the guard: the saved terminal modes (`T`), the bytes that would undo the session as it stands (`R`, resent whenever they change) and a clean end (`D`). If the control pipe closes without `D`, the guard writes the undo bytes, restores the saved modes and only then prints the captured stderr.

- `guard.go` — program side (`startGuard`, framed sends, handing stderr back when the guard dies early, end marker and acknowledgement) and guard side (`runGuard`, the `spool` that holds stderr until the terminal is restored)
- `guard_{unix,windows}.go` — stderr duplicate and redirect, guard spawn (descriptors 3 to 8 on unix, inherited handles listed in the environment on Windows), signals the guard ignores, termios or console-mode save and load

#### Renderer: session entry, handshake, modes and the frame loop

- `renderer.go` — `Renderer`: takes views and foreign writes (it is the program's output writer); opening handshake that queries synchronized output (mode 2026) and grapheme clustering (mode 2027), tests REP and OSC 66 sized text by cursor reports, and ends on DA1; routes cursor, mode and DA1 replies back to its own probes, 1 s handshake limit
- `flush.go` — frame loop and `compose`: alt-screen entry with autowrap off, mode deltas, synchronized-update bracketing, cursor hiding; classifier for foreign bytes (CSI, OSC, DCS, APC, tmux passthrough) deciding what the screen model must forget; width reconciliation per row; `Release` and the undo sequence
- `modes.go` — maps `tea.View` fields to terminal modes and writes only the difference: bracketed paste, focus reports, mouse modes with SGR encoding, window title, kitty keyboard flags with modifyOtherKeys 2, cursor shape and colour, default colours, progress bar, program status; matching undo

#### Cell model and frame planner

- `frame.go` — `Cell` and `Frame`; parser from a styled string into cells by grapheme width, with SGR, OSC 8 links and "rider" string sequences (APC, DCS) that travel with the next cell, which is how image placements pass through
- `style.go` — packed `Color` (default, 16, 256, RGB) and comparable `Style`; SGR reader, shortest SGR transition writer with its byte cost, colour-profile downgrade, interned hyperlink table
- `screen.go` — model of the real terminal with per-cell known flags, cursor, pen and charset; every emitted operation (print, REP, ECH, EL, ED, IL, DL, scroll region) applied to the model; cheapest cursor motion
- `plan.go` — per-row plan: dirty chunks split by style, link and encoding, then a search over skip, print, erase and clear steps including REP runs
- `paint.go` — frame paint: scrolls first, then rows in the cheapest visiting order (exact up to 8 rows), optionally inside DECSC and DECRC
- `scroll.go` — row hashes and a dynamic program (at most 6 distinct shifts) finding regions worth scrolling, written as IL and DL or as DECSTBM with LF or RI

#### Measured grapheme widths

- `width.go` — width table learned by printing unknown clusters on a scratch row and reading cursor reports; a class is trusted after three agreeing probes; fallbacks for clusters drawn too wide: DEC special graphics, text presentation selector, ASCII lookalikes, base rune, `?`
- `pict.go` — [data] Extended_Pictographic code point ranges (taken from the uniseg tables) that keep emoji out of width inference

### `pkg/ui/wm` — tiling window manager for cards: workspaces, floats, tabs, overlays, sheets, command palette, top bar and toasts

*13 files, 7,882 Go lines*

`wm.Model` is the root Bubble Tea model of the UI: it tiles cards per workspace, floats dialogs, routes keys and mouse, composes the screen into one cell buffer and animates every move with springs (motion scale 0 snaps). Its `View` asks for the alternate screen, all-motion mouse tracking, focus reports and key-release events. `pkg/tui` holds one model (`wm.New` with theme, keymap, window title `icebath` and motion), opens session, room, terminal, hub and arena cards in it, feeds the bar through `SetBar`, contributes commands through `SetCommandSource`, and saves `Layout()` to `<home>/tui-layout.json` and restores it at start. Exported methods with no caller outside tests: `SetCascade` (so the comet that runs round the focused border can never turn on), `SetProgress`, `OpenAside`, `Attention`, `OnToast`, `SetRatio`, `CloseKey`, `OwnerOf`, `WorkspaceByID`.

#### Card contract and manager core

- `card.go` — `Card` interface (`Title`, `Init`, `Update`, `View`) plus about 25 optional capability interfaces such as `Keyed`, `Sized`, `Floater`, `Raw`, `Passer`, `Painter`, `Tracker`, `Animator`, `Waker`, `Positioned`, `Transparent`, `Stateful`, `Hinter`, `Footer`, `Contexter`, `Addressed`; `FocusMsg`, `ClosedMsg`, `ActionMsg`
- `wm.go` — `Model`: message routing, frame clock that rests on blur or after 240 idle frames, workspace add, switch and remove, card open, close, focus, move, zoom, float and resize, per-owner command routing (`As`, `SetRoute`), theme, motion, spring stepping
- `intent.go` — commands a card returns to ask the manager for something (`RequestClose`, `RequestOverlay`, `RequestDismissOf`, `RequestAttention`, `Notify`); toasts (4 s default life, 5 at most); the focus, open, float and zoom intent kinds are handled but nothing constructs them

#### Layout, tabs and persistence

- `layout.go` — `Workspace`; master-and-stack arrangement (master share 0.62 by default, 0.3 to 0.8, columns when rows run short) and the dwindle split tree; neighbour lookup by direction, float pile, tile weights
- `fit.go` — `Fits`: dry-run layout reporting whether one more tile keeps every card at its minimum size
- `tabs.go` — `Tabs` card: several cards in one frame behind a scrolling tab strip, forwarding input, status, footer and cursor of the active one; active tab saved by key
- `tabs_ops.go` — joins the focused window into its neighbour as a tab, splits a tab out, cycles, opens a card as a tab, closes one tab
- `persist.go` — `Layout` JSON: theme, motion, ratio, mode, main count, active workspace, recent command ids, and per workspace tiles with weights, floats with boxes, split tree, focus, zoom and each `Stateful` card's state; `Restore`, `RestoreWorkspace` with key renaming

#### Input, overlays, sheets and the palette

Keys go first to the action bound in the contexts of the overlay or focused card, then to global commands, else to the card as text. `ctrl+x` is a leader key showing a strip of second keys. For a `Raw` card (a running terminal) only actions of the card's own contexts fire, plus global ones for keys its `Passes` lets through; every other key goes to the card as typed.

- `input.go` — key dispatch and the leader strip; mouse: focus on press, drag by title with live tile swap, edge resize, close button and middle-click close, double-click on a title to zoom, hint and footer clicks; text sweep with edge auto-scroll that copies through `clip`; overlay show and dismiss, sticky overlays kept beneath newer ones
- `sheet.go` — sheets: dialogs shown inside the frame of the card that asked, queued per card; keys and clicks reach a sheet or guarded overlay only 600 ms after it appears and 300 ms after a typing burst; `FocusAttention` jumps to the window waiting on the person
- `palette.go` — `Palette` fuzzy picker and `NewPrompt` text prompt typed in the bar field; `Command` registry with about 40 built-in window, tab, layout and workspace commands listed after the app's own, `Run`, `Fire`, recently used list of 12

#### Painting

- `render.go` — `View`: bar, sliding workspaces, veil, overlay, toasts and leader strip composed with alpha blending; card frames with title, glyph, close mark, status, key legend and clickable footer; focus ring, urgency glow, hyperlink hit testing, cursor placement, background-free holes for images
- `bar.go` — top bar: one chip per workspace with a signal (idle, working, fresh, failed, blocked) and detail, a centre field holding the waiting notice or the palette input, right-hand dials dropped least important first

### `pkg/ui/cards` — reusable cards and widgets built on `wm`

*15 files, 6,901 Go lines*

Generic building blocks the application composes screens from; no session, transcript or agent logic lives here. `Env` hands every card the theme, keymap, a settings lookup, working directories, the program version, the graphics probe and a `Send` hook. Consumers: `pkg/tui` (session and room cards embed `Composer`; every management screen uses `Hub`, `List`, `Form` or `Page`; terminal windows are `Terminal`; transcripts use `Reader`) and `pkg/vxl/arena` (`Painter`, `Toolbar`, `Sections`). Persists prompt drafts as `<dir>/drafts/<session>.json` with mode 0600, where `pkg/tui` sets the directory to the profile home.

#### Shared environment and messages

- `cards.go` — `Env`; `SubmitMsg`, `CommandMsg`, `RunMsg`, `SettingChangedMsg`, `Attachment`; list-movement and table-window helpers; `ShellWords` POSIX-style splitter; `DefaultScrollback` of 10000 rows
- `helpers.go` — home directory shortened to `~`; width (40) below which no scroll gutter is drawn

#### Prompt composer

- `composer.go` — `Composer`: multi-line prompt on `bubbles/textarea` (2 to 6 rows) with editing keys from the `text` context; per-session drafts on disk; history ring over an app-supplied store with reverse search; completion popup (8 rows) fed by the app; image attachments (png, jpeg, gif, webp) and `/attach`; chips saved with drafts; undo and redo (200); send button with busy, stop and offline states; submit rule: leading `!` yields `RunMsg`, leading `/` yields `CommandMsg`, anything else `SubmitMsg`

#### Terminal window card

- `terminal.go` — `Terminal`: runs the login shell, a command line or an argv on `pkg/term` with `ICEBATH=1`; settings `terminal_shell` and `terminal_scrollback`; forwards keys, paste, mouse and focus; scrollback, word and line selection, search, shell-prompt jumps, reading mode, key lock, restart; bell and notifications become attention and toasts, OSC 52 goes to the clipboard; saves its working directory; `OnEnd` reports exit and captured output

#### Management screens: hub, table, form, page

- `hub.go` — `Hub`: overlay holding a stack of views over a root list with shared `hub.*` keys (use, add, edit, rename, remove, default, toggle, help, back, refresh), a note line for progress and errors (6 s for passing notes), a generated help page, sticky question mode
- `list.go` — `List` and `ListSpec`: the table card a caller describes with columns, rows, detail, actions keyed by keymap action, filter bar, a row typed into, digit quick-pick, pick-list mode and columns that yield when narrow
- `lister.go` — table engine under `List`: cursor, filter, detail pane, yes/no question line, key capture for the keybind editor, in-place row input and cell edit
- `list_edit.go` — [unwired] `List.EditCell`, the only entry to in-place cell editing (the `edit` keymap context); nothing calls it
- `form.go` — `Form` and `FormSpec`: fields of kind text, secret, number, bool, choice, note and button with per-field checks, a "more options" fold, submit on `ctrl+s`, the `form.*` keys
- `page.go` — `Page`: scrollable lines read on every view with optional follow-the-end, for help, sign-in progress and command output

#### Reading mode and scrolling widgets

- `reader.go` — `Reader` over a `Readable`: cursor row, paging, jumps between prompts, search forward and back with matches, row selection and copy of the selection or the block under the cursor; shared by transcripts, terminals and long dialogs
- `widgets.go` — scrollbar gutter with paging caps, turn ticks and search-hit marks; detail pane under tables; search and filter bar

#### Cell painting helpers

- `paint.go` — `Painter`: text, labels, panels, tints and fills written into a cell buffer for cards that paint themselves (the arena); grapheme splitting and styled wrapping helpers also used by `pkg/tui`
- `sections.go` — `Sections`: foldable, scrollable dock sections sharing a column's height, flex sections split by a draggable rule, clickable rows; used by the arena dock
- `toolbar.go` — `Toolbar`: row of buttons labelled with their bound keys, the least needed dropped first; used by the arena

### `pkg/ui/keys` — rebindable keymap: action registry, contexts, chords and `keybinds.json`

*3 files, 1,254 Go lines*

Every key the UI answers is an `Action` in a named context; legends, palette rows, the leader strip and the keybind editor all read one `Map`. `pkg/tui` loads `<home>/keybinds.json` over the defaults, registers further contexts and actions of its own, and saves, reloads and resets the file from its keybind screen; `cards` (hub, form) and `vxl/arena` add contexts through `AddContext`. `Map.Stale`, which detects an edit of the file made outside the program, has no caller, so nothing reloads the file automatically.

#### Keymap

- `keys.go` — `Map`: register, lookup by contexts, chord parsing and formatting (`cmd` for super on macOS), per-context conflict refusal, `SetDefault` migration that respects user binds, which chords need the kitty keyboard protocol, file read (a chord, a list or null per action; unknown names reported; `options.option_as_alt`), save grouped by context
- `actions.go` — [data] the 18 built-in contexts with their editor descriptions and the default registry of about 220 actions: global window, layout, tab and workspace keys, the `ctrl+x` leader strip, session and composer, text editing, completion, search, confirm, palette, list, reading view, approval and terminal keys
- `option.go` — reads the characters macOS Option types on a US layout as alt chords while `option_as_alt` is on

### `pkg/ui/field` — single-line (optionally multi-line) text editor used by every text field

*1 file, 350 Go lines*

#### Line editor

- `field.go` — `Field`: rune buffer with caret driven by the `text` context actions (moves, word and line deletes), select-all-then-replace, undo and redo (100), paste through Bubble Tea's clipboard read, copy through `clip` (never for a masked field), masked display, wrapped and windowed rendering

### `pkg/ui/clip` — clipboard writes and terminal clipboard queries

*1 file, 244 Go lines*

#### Clipboard

- `clip.go` — `Copy` combines a native tool (`pbcopy`, PowerShell `Set-Clipboard`, `powershell.exe` under WSL, `wl-copy`, `xclip`, `xsel`; 2 s limit), tmux `load-buffer` and OSC 52; OSC 52 is always sent over SSH and not inside tmux or screen locally, the tool never runs over SSH; overrides `ICEBATH_TUI_FORCE_OSC52`, `ICEBATH_TUI_CLIPBOARD_OSC52`, `ICEBATH_TUI_COPY_OSC52`; `Send` and `Query` write OSC 52 wrapped for the multiplexer

### `pkg/ui/gfx` — pixel images over terminal cells: kitty, iTerm2 and sixel

*7 files, 1,648 Go lines*

Decides what the terminal can draw from its identity in the environment plus probes (kitty graphics query, cell and window pixel size, sixel colour registers and maximum image size, DA1) and streams frames to a `Surface`. Four protocols: kitty with Unicode placeholder cells (the only one usable through tmux), kitty placed at the cursor, iTerm2 inline PNG and sixel. Consumers: `pkg/tui` (pet view, placed and inline images; `app.go` creates the `Terminal` with `gfx.New()` and calls `gfx.Sweep()` after the program ends) and `pkg/vxl/arena`. For local kitty and ghostty on Linux, frames travel as `/dev/shm/icebath-<pid>-…` objects instead of base64.

#### Detection and surfaces

- `gfx.go` — `Terminal`: identity table of 15 terminals and their traits, probe text, answer handling, verified protocol (`Protocol`, `Draws`) and the forced `Guess`, cell size measured or assumed 9 by 18, tmux passthrough wrapping, `Describe`
- `surface.go` — `Surface`: two alternating kitty image ids, answer tracking with a 400 ms timeout, resolution divisor adapted to answer latency, rate caps (kitty 30, sixel 8, iTerm2 6 per second), pixel budgets, placeholder grid painting, protocol marked broken after 3 errors, `Release`, `Sweep`
- `pack.go` — `Pack`: RGB frame to a packet (zlib and base64 in 4096-character kitty chunks or a shared memory name; sixel tiles; iTerm2 PNG); `Encoded` wraps a sequence encoded elsewhere, used for pet frames

#### Encoders and shared memory

- `sixel.go` — sixel encoder on a fixed colour cube with ordered dither, tiled to the terminal's largest image
- `png.go` — minimal RGB PNG writer (up filter, fastest zlib) for iTerm2 frames
- `shm_{linux,other}.go` — shared memory objects as files in `/dev/shm`, removal of objects left by dead icebath pids; errors or no-ops off Linux

### `pkg/ui/render` — themed text formatting: markdown, tables and small formatters

*4 files, 744 Go lines*

Stateless helpers called by `pkg/tui`, `pkg/ui/cards` and `pkg/vxl/arena`. Markdown goes through glamour with a style derived from the theme, and code blocks get a Chroma style name chosen per theme; the package contains no highlighter and no diff algorithm of its own.

#### Formatters

- `markdown.go` — `Markdown`: glamour renderers cached by theme and width, raw text on failure; reopens hyperlinks on each wrapped line and trims glamour padding; `CodeStyle` picks catppuccin-mocha, github, github-dark or bw
- `format.go` — truncate, wrap, pluralised counts, elapsed time, token, byte, money and percent formats, spinner frame, divider, glyph by tool name, theme-coloured text helpers
- `table.go` — table renderer: fixed and flex columns, right alignment, columns dropped from the right when narrow, selected and marked rows, one cell shown while edited
- `diff.go` — [unwired] `Op`, `Line` and `MaxDiffLines` (6000) for a line-diff view; nothing computes or renders a diff with them

### `pkg/ui/render/recap` — plain-text session recap builder

*1 file, 346 Go lines*

The only part of `pkg/ui` that depends on `pkg/internal/py*` and `pkg/tools`; it reads messages as Python-style dicts. Nothing in `cmd` or `pkg` imports the package and no recap command exists.

#### Session recap

[unwired] Meant to summarise where a session stands when it is resumed or on request.

- `session_recap.go` — `BuildRecap(messages, title, id)`: turn counts over the last 20 visible turns, tools used with counts, up to five files touched (from `write_file`, `patch`, `read_file`, `skill_manage`, `skill_view` arguments), last ask cut to 140 characters and last reply to 200

### `pkg/ui/theme` — palettes, glyph sets and brand art

#### Themes

- `theme.go` — `Theme` (12 colour roles, focus-ring stops, border, glyph set, 16 ANSI colours for embedded terminals); seven themes: blackwall (default), light, taro, contrast, plain (16 colours, ASCII glyphs and border), cyberpunk, dracula; `Named`, `Mix`, `Shade`, `Ring`; two `Glyphs` sets of about 100 marks; `Names` has no caller
- `art.go` — [data] the ICE | BATH wordmark (77 by 6 cells) and the braille hero mark (30 by 15) in two inks, shown by the `pkg/tui` banner

*1 file, 217 Go lines*

#### Motion

### `pkg/ui/lang` — translation hooks the application installs into the kit
