### `pkg/ui/txt` — typed keys for the terminal UI message catalog (not text layout)

*3 files, 7,790 Go lines*

Despite the name this package does no width, grapheme or wrapping work; that comes from `x/ansi` and ultraviolet. It declares one `Key` per entry of `pkg/tui/locales/en.tui.yaml` (the only catalog in that directory) so code can only ask for a text the catalog holds. 97 files of `pkg/tui` and the kit's own cards and window manager name their texts with these keys.

#### Catalog keys

- `txt.go` — `Key` with an unexported name, `Named` run-time lookup, `All` (no caller), the `go:generate` directive
- `keys.go` — [data] generated: 3,815 key variables and the ordered `all` slice
- `internal/keygen/main.go` — generator: reads `strings` and `formats` of the English YAML, derives Go identifiers, refuses duplicates and reserved names, writes `keys.go`

### `pkg/vxl` — software 3D voxel rasterizer drawing into terminal cells or pixel frames

*20 files, 7,113 Go lines*

A CPU renderer written for the arena card: voxel grids meshed into quads, posable voxel figures defined by text layers, an orbit camera, deferred per-pixel lighting (sun with shadow map, baked radiance volume, binned point lights, screen-space occlusion and reflections, volumetric haze, fog), layers and dirty-pixel runs so a mostly static scene is relit only where it changed, and a finishing stage (outline, bloom, grade, vignette). Output is either terminal cells, by fitting one glyph and two colours to every 4 by 8 pixel cell, or RGB bytes handed to a `gfx.Surface`. The only consumer is `pkg/vxl/arena`; `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go` also blank-imports the package. It imports no `pkg/internal/py*` package and has no stubs; `Dirt.Hull`, `Grid.BoxTex` and `Part.Orient` have no caller, besides the unused passes named below.

#### Math, parallelism and primitives

- `math.go` — `RGB` colour in floats, `Vec3` (x east, y up, z south) with rotations and heading helpers, smoothstep, integer hashes, a small linear congruential `RNG`
- `parallel.go` — process-wide helper goroutine pool, `SetWorkers` cap (the arena sets three quarters of the CPUs), row-band parallel loops
- `dirt.go` — `Dirt`: changed pixels as merged runs per row with union, grow and bounds; `Changes` pairs the drawn and the relit sets
- `texture.go` — procedural face patterns (panel, grate, circuit, noise, grain, pulses) filtered analytically by pixel footprint

#### Scene content

- `grid.go` — `Grid` of voxels (colour, pattern, gloss, glow) by integer cell; open faces merged into rectangles per chunk with corner occlusion; chunks outside the view skipped whole; `LineCells`
- `model.go` — `Model`: rigid parts built from text layers of palette keys, parent links, per-part `Pose`, `Stance`, drawing through the raster
- `particles.go` — capped pool of glowing motes with lifetime and gravity, drawn as billboards
- `lights.go` — point lights binned over a floor grid for fast lookup per face

#### Rasterizer and lighting passes

- `raster.go` — `Camera`, `Quad`, `Light`, `Raster`: projection, near clipping, banded triangle fill with depth and packed facing buffers, deferred shading with specular and fog, billboards and boxes, `Flush`, `FlushInto`, `FlushOver`, `Relight`
- `frame.go` — `Frame` pixel buffers (colour, surface, depth, facing, pixel aspect); its whole-frame `Outline`, `Bloom`, `Vignette` and `Grade` passes have no caller outside tests since `Output.Finish` does the same incrementally
- `shadow.go` — orthographic sun depth map keeping the two nearest depths per texel
- `ao.go` — ambient occlusion sampled on a shrunken grid, depth-aware spread and blur, partial redo over a layer
- `gi.go` — `Volume`: radiance baked on a 3D grid from emitters with line of sight, smoothing, sun bounce off the voxel grid
- `reflect.go` — reflections for glossy faces by marching mirrored view rays through the depth buffer
- `haze.go` — light scattered by the air, marched at reduced resolution and laid over the frame by depth
- `layer.go` — `Layer`: a lit static frame kept with its lights, occlusion, shadow depths, mirror and haze grids so later flushes redraw only what moved in front
- `finish.go` — `Output` and `Finish`: outline, bloom chain, colour fringing, filmic grade and vignette recomputed only for changed pixels

#### Cell encoding and the glyph table

- `encode.go` — `CellMode` glyph libraries (half, quadrant, sextant, octant, shapes, legacy, all); `Encoder` picks the best-fitting glyph with foreground and background per cell and holds a cell's previous choice while it still fits; `ANSIQuantizer` for 16-colour themes; `Frame.Encode` and `GlyphMask` have no caller outside tests
- `glyphs.go` — [data] generated table of 422 glyphs: character, library bits, lit-pixel mask and 32 coverage bytes
- `internal/glyphgen/main.go` — generator run by `go generate`: rasterizes block, quadrant, sextant, octant, triangle and box-drawing characters from the geometry their Unicode names describe; the header it writes still credits a `scripts/glyphs.py` that is not in the repository

### `pkg/vxl/arena` — the `/arena` card: a session's agents shown as a voxel crew working on a platform

*21 files, 8,863 Go lines*

The user-facing feature built on `pkg/vxl`. The `/arena` slash command (extras tier only: build tags `!icebath_core && !icebath_noextras`) opens a card that draws the current session's orchestration as a small 3D scene: the main agent is the director, each delegated subagent a crew member (reviewer when its goal reads as review work, architect once it delegates, else builder), and every delegation and todo item a "ticket" shown as a data core sealed in ice. Around the floor sit a toolbar, a dock (sprint and crew, tickets, log), a timeline with replay and an inspector. Through the `Harness` interface, implemented by `pkg/tui/arenafeed.go`, the card can interrupt, steer and open a member, pause spawning, stop the turn and retry it. All state is in memory: the `Journal` keeps up to 64 turns per session and nothing is written to disk. Settings come from the `display.arena` config mapping (`display` auto, glyphs or image; `glyphs`; `world`; `camera`; `fps` 5 to 120; `quality`; `labels`); in `auto` the floor goes out as an image only when kitty placeholder cells are verified, otherwise as glyph cells.

#### Data model, settings and journal

- `model.go` — roles, ticket status and kind, turn stages (brief, plan, report), message kinds and verdicts; `Member`, `Ticket`, `Message`, `Usage`, and `Snapshot` of one turn at one moment
- `config.go` — `Config`, `Default` and `Parse` of the `display.arena` mapping with one error per bad key; crew handles and outfits by order of arrival
- `journal.go` — `Journal`: folds each `Report` from the harness (busy, prompt, tools, todos, agents, approval, clarify, usage, context) into per-session sprints, one per turn, recording every change on a tape; derives members, tickets, messages and verdicts; `View` at any moment
- `keys.go` — the `arena` keymap context and its 35 actions with default keys; `RegisterKeys`

#### Card: layout, input and panels

- `arena.go` — the card: construction, `Refresh`, `Configure`, `Retheme`, status line, selection and inspector state, turn browsing with a 30 s finale hold before the lobby returns, action dispatch to the `Harness`, protocol choice, surface lifecycle
- `arena_input.go` — pointer routing: toolbar, panel edge drags, dock rows, timeline scrub, inspector, member windows, camera orbit and zoom on the floor, picking actors and cores
- `arena_paint.go` — `Paint`: toolbar, dock, the newest floor frame as cells or as an image under transparent holes, name and ticket labels placed without overlap, key legend, telemetry, timeline
- `dock.go` — dock sections: sprint (turn state and a row per member, or the list of turns in the lobby), tickets, log
- `sheet.go` — scrollable sheet of everything reported for one member, shown in the inspector and in the member windows that replace the floor when `world` is `off`
- `replay.go` — replay cursor over a turn's tape: play and pause, speeds 1, 2, 4 and 8, step to the previous or next change, seek, silences squeezed to 1.5 s

#### Scene simulation and render worker

- `scene.go` — platform simulation synced from a snapshot: tool classification by harness tool name (read, edit, shell, fetch, agent, call), per-member live state and budget heat, spawning and stations, message and verdict effects, finale by outcome, up to 900 particles, static and dynamic draw passes, radiance bake, shadows and lights
- `crew.go` — voxel figure models per role and head rig (nine rigs), actor state, poses and drawing
- `behavior.go` — actor duties (idle, spot, node, wait, spire, gather) planned into walk, face, hold, leap and emit steps; separation, ambient idling, huddles, bystanders
- `nodes.go` — ticket cores: ice shell that breaks away by status, glow and point light, conduits between dependent tickets, data packets flying along arcs
- `world.go` — `dive`: platform layout from the ticket plan (levels and rows of pedestals, conduit routes, perches, stations) and heap-driven grid path search with an octile heuristic
- `stage.go` — render worker goroutine taking posted closures and returning `frameMsg`; camera rig with overview, orbit, follow and cinematic presets; pacing by what the card painted (8 per second when calm, 2 when the terminal is blurred), quality easing, layered static frame, finishing, cell encoding or pixel packing

#### Worlds

- `worlds.go` — `world` interface (terrain, materials, sky, light, emitters, bake, finish, decor, dress, lights, update, bounds), quality presets low to ultra, shared voxel and sky helpers
- `world_{blackwall,den,nightcity,soulkiller}.go` — the four selectable looks: a red strand wall over a glossy black floor (default), a den of screens and server racks, a rooftop over a city at dawn, a sea of cyan data blocks with red-lit figures

### `pkg/pet` — petdex mascots: store, manifest, config, sprite decoding and terminal frame encoders

*11 files, 1,587 Go lines*

A pet is an animated pixel-art mascot shown in the terminal UI that reacts to agent activity. Each one is a directory `<home>/pets/<slug>/` holding `pet.json` (`id`, `displayName`, `description`, `spritesheetPath`, `createdBy`) and a WebP or PNG atlas of 192 by 208 pixel frames, one row per animation state. Pets are installed from the public manifest at `https://petdex.dev/api/manifest` or hatched locally by `pkg/pet/generate`; config sits under `display.pet` (`enabled`, `slug`, `scale`, `render_mode`, `unicode_cols`). Consumers: `pkg/app/pets.go` (`icebath pets list|install|select|show|off|scale|remove|doctor`), `pkg/tuiserver` (the `pet.*` RPC methods and the `pet.changed` event) and `pkg/tui` (`petview.go` draws the pet; `/pet` and `/hatch` slash commands). The package is a Python port leaning on `pyjson`, `pystr`, `pyrepr`, `pypath`, `pyzip`, `pyhttpx` and `pypil`, with Python exception texts in some errors. It keeps its own image encoders and environment-only protocol detection, separate from `pkg/ui/gfx`.

#### Animation states and sheet geometry

- `constants.go` — frame size, 6 frames per state, 1100 ms loop, scale bounds 0.1 to 3.0 (default 0.33), seven states (idle, wave, run, failed, review, jump, waiting), row names of 8-row legacy and 9-row Codex sheets with aliases
- `state.go` — `DeriveState`: first true of error, celebrate, just completed, awaiting input, tool running, reasoning, busy, else idle
- `sheet_rows.go` — real frame count of each sheet row (frames before its first blank cell) and the row count of a sheet

#### Store, manifest and config

- `store.go` — `<home>/pets`, `pet.json` reading, spritesheet lookup (declared path, then `spritesheet.webp`, `spritesheet.png`, `sprite.webp`, `sprite.png`), slug sanitising, `LoadPet`, `InstalledPets`, `ResolveActivePet` (configured slug, else first by name)
- `store_local.go` — slug and display-name derivation, collision-free slug, `RegisterLocalPet` writing a lossless WebP sheet and a `pet.json` marked `createdBy: generator`
- `store_remote.go` — `InstallPet` from the manifest (only `petdex.dev` hosts, download through a `.part` file, 60 s limit), `ExportPet` as a zip, `RemovePet`, `RenamePet` moving the directory and its `pets/.thumbs/<slug>.png` thumbnail
- `manifest.go` — manifest fetch behind the SSRF check with user agent `icebath-agent-petdex`, 10 s timeout and a five-minute in-process cache; `Prefetch`, `FindEntry`
- `run.go` — `Run`: reads and writes `display.pet` in the profile config (`SetActive`, `SetPetScale`, `HasActivePet`, conditional `UpdatePetConfig`)
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Frame decoding and terminal encoders

- `render.go` — render modes auto, kitty, iterm, sixel, unicode, off; protocol guessed from environment variables only; frame cropping with an LRU cache; encoders for kitty (direct, and Unicode-placeholder placement with the image id carried in the foreground colour), iTerm2 and half-block cells; `Renderer`, `BuildRenderer`; `SupportsKittyPlaceholders` has no caller
- `sixel.go` — DEC sixel encoder with up to 255 adaptive colours, transparent pixels left unpainted

### `pkg/pet/generate` — hatching a new pet with an image-generation provider

*6 files, 2,045 Go lines*

Turns a text concept into an installed pet in two RPC-driven steps called only from `pkg/tuiserver/methods_session_pets.go`: `pet.generate` drafts candidate base looks, then `pet.hatch` generates one animation strip per state from the approved base image, slices and normalises the frames, composes the 1536 by 1872 atlas, validates it and registers it in the pet store. It needs an image provider that accepts reference images (openai, openai-codex, openrouter or krea, found through `pkg/media` and plugin discovery); `ICEBATH_PET_IMAGE_PROVIDER` forces one. A Python port: Pillow arithmetic is reproduced so slicing results match the original.

#### Orchestration, provider access and prompts

- `orchestrate.go` — `GenerateBaseDrafts` (4 by default, 4 in parallel, backdrop keyed out, provider errors rewritten into advice) and `HatchPet` (8 rows generated with 3 attempts each, `running-left` mirrored, idle falling back to the base image, required rows idle, running-right and waving, at least 6 usable rows, progress events, cancellation)
- `imagegen.go` — `ResolveProvider` (env override, preferred, active, then first with credentials) and `Generate` (asks for a transparent background and retries without it when refused, passes reference images, downloads URL results)
- `prompts.go` — [data] prompt text: action per state, eight style hints, the magenta-or-green chroma-key background rule, base and row prompt builders with pose spacing, base variations
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Sprite image processing

- `atlas.go` — background removal by border flood fill, alpha-hole repair, strip slicing into frames by connected components or column runs with bleed and outlier cleanup, cell normalisation, mirroring, `ComposeAtlas` (8 cells by 9 rows) and `ValidateAtlas`
- `pilimage.go` — [py-shim] Pillow-compatible RGBA helpers over `internal/pypil` (alpha composite with Pillow's rounding, crop, paste, bounding box, nearest resize, flip, 3 by 3 alpha erosion, Python `round`) that `atlas.go` is written against

### `pkg/term` — embedded terminal emulator and pty sessions behind the UI's terminal windows

*20 files, 4,621 Go lines*

The mirror image of `pkg/ui/tty`: `tty` drives the user's real terminal, while `term` pretends to be a terminal for a child program. It starts the child on a pseudo terminal and interprets what the child writes into a cell grid with scrollback, so `cards.Terminal` can show a shell inside an icebath window; children see `TERM=xterm-256color`, `COLORTERM=truecolor` and `TERM_PROGRAM=icebath`. It uses the `x/ansi` parser and ultraviolet cells, and its only project dependency is `internal/proc` for killing a process tree. Importers: `pkg/ui/cards/terminal.go` (the product use) and `pkg/termlab` (a mirror of the screen in tests); the agent's shell tool does not use it. Pty code exists for linux, darwin and Windows ConPTY. Pixel-image sequences from children (sixel, kitty graphics, iTerm2 inline images) are not interpreted. The `BracketedPaste`, `FocusEvents` and `KittyFlags` accessors of the emulator have no caller.

#### Sessions and pseudo terminals

- `session.go` — `Session`: `Open` starts a command on a pty feeding a fresh emulator; reader and writer goroutines, wake channel, queued input, resize, exit record, `Close` with a 2 s grace before the process tree is killed
- `shell.go` — default shell and the child environment (sets the terminal variables and `TERM_PROGRAM_VERSION`, drops `LINES` and `COLUMNS`)
- `pty_unix.go` — unix `Process`: new session with a controlling tty, exit code and signal, working directory from `/proc/<pid>/cwd`, window-size ioctl, `$SHELL` or `/bin/sh`
- `pty_{linux,darwin}.go` — opening a pty pair through `/dev/ptmx` on each OS
- `pty_windows.go` — ConPTY `Process`: pseudo console creation, process start, working directory read from the process parameters, shells tried in order `pwsh.exe`, `powershell.exe`, `cmd.exe`

#### Emulator core

- `term.go` — `Emulator`: main and alternate screens, scrollback ring, mode flags, palette, title stack, host events (bell, title, clipboard, notify, cwd, progress), `Draw` into a cell buffer with theme colours and selection or match highlights, synchronized updates held for at most 1 s
- `screen.go` — one grid with cursor, saved cursor, scroll region, margins, tab stops and charsets
- `line.go` — `Line`: cells, soft-wrap flag, OSC 133 shell marks with exit code, selective-erase guards
- `print.go` — printing with wrap, insert mode, wide and combining graphemes and flag pairs; erase, insert and delete of cells, lines and columns; index, region scrolling, alt-screen switch
- `reflow.go` — resize: main screen and scrollback rewrapped on a width change, rows moved between screen and scrollback on a height change
- `exec.go` — C0 controls, plain escape sequences, charset designation (DEC special graphics and UK)

#### Control sequence handlers

- `csi.go` — CSI dispatch: cursor motion, erase, insert and delete, scroll, tabs, REP, margins, device attributes and status reports, window size reports (assuming 8 by 16 pixel cells), cursor style, soft reset, checksum, ANSI and DEC private modes (mouse 9 and 1000 to 1016, focus, alt screen, bracketed paste, synchronized output), mode queries, kitty keyboard stack, modifyOtherKeys, XTVERSION
- `sgr.go` — SGR: attributes, underline styles, 16, 256 and RGB colours in semicolon and colon forms
- `osc.go` — OSC 0, 1, 2 titles; 4 and 104 palette; 7 working directory; 8 hyperlinks; 9 and 777 notifications and 9;4 progress; 10, 11, 12 dynamic colours with queries; 52 clipboard; 133 shell marks
- `dcs.go` — DCS: status string requests (DECRQSS), termcap queries (XTGETTCAP) and the DCS form of synchronized updates

#### Host-side input and text access

- `keys.go` — key encoding for the child: legacy xterm sequences under cursor-key and keypad modes, modifyOtherKeys, the kitty keyboard protocol; paste (bracketed or stripped of controls) and focus reports
- `mouse.go` — mouse encoding (X10, normal, button, any motion; UTF-8, SGR, urxvt and SGR-pixel formats) and the alternate-scroll test
- `selection.go` — selection by cell, word or line across soft wraps, text extraction, word and line bounds, lookup of OSC 133 prompt rows
- `search.go` — text search over scrollback and screen, case-insensitive unless the query has capitals, matches split per row

### `pkg/termlab` — Linux-only end-to-end test lab for the terminal UI (no product code)

*9 files, 1,817 Go lines*

Runs the real `icebath` binary inside real terminal emulators (`konsole`, `xterm`) on a private `Xvfb` display, injects input through a pty relay, mirrors the output through `pkg/term` and judges results from framebuffer screenshots. Nothing in `cmd` or `pkg` imports it and no Makefile target names it; only its own in-package `_test.go` files use it. It builds `cmd/icebath` itself with `-tags goolm` under a 12,000,000 KiB address-space limit and `GOMEMLIMIT=4GiB`, or takes a prebuilt binary from `TERMLAB_ICEBATH`.

#### Test lab

- `doc.go`, `lab_linux.go`, `session_linux.go`, `driver_linux.go`, `probe_linux.go`, `pty_linux.go`, `watch_linux.go`, `build_linux.go`, `image.go` — [test-support] Xvfb lab, emulator sessions, pty relay driver, probe program, cell-change recorder, build helper, screenshot comparison

## 11. Plugins, built-ins and skills

### `pkg/plugins` — plugin system: manifests, discovery, loading, guest runtime, hooks, catalog and the install/update lifecycle

*146 files, 41,512 Go lines*

Owns the whole plugin subsystem of one profile home: manifest parsing, discovery across compiled-in, user, project and pip-entry-point sources, the enable gate, loading through one registration `Context`, hook, middleware and event dispatch, and the `icebath plugins` and `icebath hooks` command families (bound in `pkg/commands/cli_tree_plugins.go` and `cli_tree_hooks.go`, mirrored by RPCs in `pkg/tuiserver`). Plugin code runs in exactly three forms: Go compiled into the binary (the `Plugin` interface, registered by other packages at init), a WebAssembly module run in-process by wazero (`runtime: wasm`), or an external program in its own process group (`runtime: program`); both guest forms speak one line-delimited JSON request/reply protocol to a `PluginHost`. Python plugin source is detected and refused at load, install and validate, yet Python-era machinery is still here: pip entry points, shared-venv dependency consent through `pkg/pm`, a Python capability probe, and Python AST audits against a snapshot of the old Python source tree. It persists `plugins/.install-metadata.json` (with a `.lock`), `plugin-data/<namespace>/state.json`, `shell-hooks-allowlist.json`, `plugin-update-checks/`, several files under `cache/`, and the `plugins.*` and `hooks.*` blocks of `config.yaml`; it talks to git remotes, raw.githubusercontent.com and `https://icebath.app/api/plugin-catalog.json`. Higher packages are reached only through the `Services` struct that `cmd/icebath/wiring.go` installs. 63 of the 138 Go files import `internal/py*` shims, and the guest protocol still uses Python method names, Python exception class names and Python argument-binding error wording.

#### Manifest formats: native `plugin.yaml` and portable `plugin.json`

A plugin is a directory holding `plugin.yaml` or `plugin.yml` (native), or `plugin.json` with optional `mcp.json` and `skills/` (a portable "Agent Plugins v1" package that contributes only skills and MCP servers and never runs code). Native fields the loader knows: name, version, description, author, label, kind (standalone, backend, exclusive, platform, model-provider), manifest_version (highest supported 2), api_version, requires_icebath (retired alias requires_hermes), requires_env, optional_env, requires_plugins, requires_auth, oauth, capabilities, provides_tools, provides_hooks (alias hooks), provides_middleware, provides_locales, provides_browser_providers, provides_web_providers, provides, platforms, external_dependencies, pip_dependencies, python_dependencies, python_runtime, config_schema, config_keys, settings, license, homepage, tags, emits, listens, update_url, depends, entry, runtime, grants, limits, skills, commands, mcp_servers, and the vendor blocks icebath and hermes. Unknown fields warn and are ignored; no malformed field fails a load.

- `manifest.go` — `Manifest` struct and `ParseManifestFile`; derives the registry key (`<category>/<dir>` under a category directory, else the name), checks `config_schema` types, orders loads by `requires_plugins` with alphabetical fallback on a cycle
- `agentplugin.go` — portable package loader: validates `plugin.json`, discovers `skills/*/SKILL.md`, translates `mcp.json` stdio and streamable-http servers (SSE refused, `${PLUGIN_ROOT}` and `${PLUGIN_DATA}` expanded), reads `extensions["app.icebath"]` server declarations (app, requires, liveness, trust, timeout, costs)
- `install_manifest.go` — the manifest an install candidate publishes, a `manifest_invalid` error when it is unreadable or malformed
- `pm_host.go` — init hook handing `pkg/pm` the supported manifest version, the running version and the `requires_icebath` fit check
- `version.go` — running version from build info and the comma-separated comparator clauses behind `requires_icebath`

#### Manager, per-home registry and service wiring

One `Manager` per resolved profile home holds every registry a plugin can add to. Everything the package needs from higher layers (gateway, agent, memory, MCP, secrets, TUI) arrives as a callback in `Services`, installed once at process start.

- `manager.go` — `Manager` and `LoadedPlugin`: the per-home maps of hooks, middleware, commands, CLI commands, skills, widgets, blueprints, auxiliary tasks, approval transports and guest hosts
- `manager_order.go` — keeps loaded records in the order their keys were first stored
- `registry.go` — `GetPluginManager` (one manager per home), gateway and TUI message-injector slots, package-level `InvokeHook`, `HasHook`, `HasMiddleware` and `FirePreCommandHook` wrappers
- `module.go` — `Services` (53 callbacks and interfaces) and `InstallServices`; `DiscoverPlugins` and background discovery with a 30 s join; `cache/plugin_toolset_keys.json`; merging of `pre_tool_call` directives (block, approve, modify), `pre_verify` continue message, first-wins `transform_api_error_classification`
- `plugin.go` — `Plugin` interface (`Manifest`, `Register`), the `RegisterBundled` set of compiled-in plugins, readers of `.install-metadata.json`, kill-list verdict for an installed plugin
- `configio.go` — config load and save under one process lock, `plugins.enabled` and `plugins.disabled` readers, plugins directory creation; `GetBundledPluginsDir` has no caller
- `log.go` — package logger; `ICEBATH_PLUGINS_DEBUG` tees plugin logs to stderr and attaches error detail to failure warnings
- `tools_config_catalog.go`, `tools_discovery_hooks.go` — init hooks giving `pkg/tools` the plugin toolset rows for the tools picker and an idempotent ensure-discovered call
- `skill_host.go` — init hook implementing `skills.PluginSkillHost`: plugin skill lookup, listing, removal and pruning of inactive memory-provider skills for one home

#### Discovery sources and the enable gate

Sources in order: compiled-in Go plugins (always source `bundled`), a directory named by `ICEBATH_BUNDLED_PLUGINS`, `<home>/plugins/` with one level of category nesting, `./.icebath/plugins` when `ICEBATH_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS` is set, then pip entry points. A later source wins a key collision unless a differently named directory claims a bundled key. The gate: `plugins.disabled` beats `plugins.enabled`; `exclusive` and `model-provider` kinds are left to category discovery; a bundled `backend` loads at once and a bundled `platform` is deferred until the gateway asks for it; everything else needs a `plugins.enabled` entry and must not be on the catalog kill list. `ICEBATH_SAFE_MODE` skips all plugins and hooks.

- `discovery.go` — directory scan, source collection, winner resolution and `GateManifest`; skips dunder and foreign-harness directories (`.claude-plugin`, `.codex-plugin`, `.cursor-plugin`, `.devin-plugin`, `.kimi-plugin`) and the category directories memory, context_engine, model-providers, cron_providers, computer_use, config_backends
- `entry.go` — `DiscoverAllPlugins`: the rows the commands list (embedded tree, user directories, entry points) and name-to-entry resolution by key, manifest name, bare leaf or catalog name
- `bundled_tree.go` — reads the embedded `pkg/plugintree` manifests, or the override directory, for listing, default-on kind checks and `provides_tools`
- `bundled_tiers.go` — maps tree directories and catalog ports to link tiers (`plugins`, `extras`); hides or refuses plugins whose Go code this binary was built without
- `ports.go` — "ports": compiled-in Go implementations of catalog plugins (`RegisterPort`), active only once installed into a home; a catalog install at the pinned sha writes the embedded tree instead of cloning; `builtin:` installs for ports no catalog lists
- `entrypoints.go` — [partial] lists pip entry points of groups `icebath_agent.plugins` and `icebath_agent.plugin_capabilities` through `pkg/pm`; the loader refuses every one as Python source, so they are listed and never load
- `config_keys.go` — registers the settings blocks of each discovered plugin and the selected memory provider with `pkg/settings`; `PortableMCPServers` for the MCP bridge

#### Loading, registration ledger and unload

Every registration a plugin makes is recorded with its inverse, so a failed load, an unload or a forced reload removes exactly what that plugin added and restores what it replaced.

- `manager_load.go` — `DiscoverAndLoad` under a per-manager discovery lock (force unloads first, then re-registers shell hooks and webhooks and re-pulls secret sources); listing accessors; the `PlatformRegistry`, `SecretSources` and `PlatformDeclarations` interfaces the gateway implements
- `loader.go` — loads one plugin as portable package, guest, installed port or compiled-in plugin; `plugins.load_timeout_seconds` (default 10, max 600) with at most 8 abandoned loaders; deferred platform loaders and their re-arm; tool-override policy lease
- `ledger.go` — `Registration` handles, the per-plugin ownership ledger, `Unload` disposing in reverse order, fallback hooks of memory providers
- `lifecycle.go` — `ReplacementCoordinator`: generation leases so a plugin that replaced a registry slot restores its predecessor on unload, in any unload order

#### Registration context: every extension point

`Context` is what a plugin's register function receives. Through it a plugin adds tools (overriding a built-in only with the `tools.override` capability), lifecycle hooks, middleware, slash commands, `icebath <name>` CLI subcommands, skills resolvable as `plugin:name`, terminal UI widgets, system prompt sections, locales, automation blueprints, auxiliary LLM tasks, redaction patterns, approval transports, gateway platforms, Slack action and Telegram or platform handler factories, a context engine, a context reference prefix, a memory provider, event subscriptions, unload callbacks and supervised background tasks, plus twelve scope-keyed provider kinds.

- `context.go` — `Context` type; `GetConfig` and `SetConfig` under `plugins.entries.<id>.settings`, `State`, `HasPlugin`, `RegisterHook`, `RegisterMiddleware`
- `context_home.go` — context bound to the home of the manager loading the plugin
- `context_registrars.go` — most registrars and host calls: tools, commands, CLI commands, platforms, skills, locales, blueprints, auxiliary tasks, approval transports, `CallMCP` (per-plugin `mcp_allowlist`, 1 to 600 s), `InjectMessage` (`allow_gateway_injection`), `SideQuestion`, `DispatchTool`, `SpawnTask`, `OnUnload`
- `context_registry.go` — system prompt sections (lowercase id, position `after_memory`, at most 4000 characters), `Emit` and `Subscribe`, the guard that ignores registrars after a timed-out load
- `context_providers.go` — table-driven provider registrars: login_backend, browser_page_backend, image_gen, video_gen, web_search, browser, terminal_environment, secret_source, tts, transcription, delegation, context_reference; login and page backends are accepted only from bundled plugins or official and verified catalog installs at the reviewed pin
- `provider_registries.go` — `RegisterProviderRegistry`: lets a tier package supply the registry of a provider kind at init
- `widgets.go` — widget registration: modal or ambient, six dock zones, refresh no faster than 100 ms, open, input, tick and render callbacks; rendered by `cmd/icebath/tui_widgets.go`

#### Hook, middleware, event and stream dispatch

The 46 hook names: pre_tool_call, post_tool_call, transform_terminal_output, transform_tool_result, transform_llm_output, pre_llm_call, post_llm_call, on_stream_start, on_stream_delta, on_stream_end, on_interim_message, pre_verify, pre_api_request, post_api_request, api_request_error, pre_auxiliary_call, post_auxiliary_call, transform_api_error_classification, on_session_start, on_session_end, on_session_finalize, on_session_reset, on_session_delete, on_skill_lifecycle, subagent_start, subagent_stop, pre_gateway_dispatch, post_gateway_admission, agent_loop_stopped, pre_approval_request, post_approval_response, on_human_input_request, on_human_input_resolved, on_room_member_activity, pre_transcription, kanban_task_claimed, kanban_task_completed, kanban_task_blocked, on_kanban_worker_spawned, on_kanban_worker_exited, on_kanban_worker_stale_claim, on_kanban_task_updated, on_kanban_dispatch_tick, gateway_platform_event, pre_command, post_compaction. The four middleware kinds are tool_request, tool_execution, llm_request and llm_execution. Callers are the agent loop, the tool executor and the gateway.

- `dispatch.go` — hook name table, hook entries and `TrackHook`, stream holding by `transform_llm_output`, system prompt section formatting between `icebath-plugin-sections` markers (32 sections, 8000 characters in total)
- `dispatch_hooks.go` — `InvokeHook` and `AInvokeHook`: `plugins.hook_callback_timeout` (default 30 s, max 600) on bounded hooks, a timed-out `pre_tool_call` callback blocks the tool, 60 s suppression of a hung callback, slash-command results awaited at most 30 s
- `dispatch_events.go` — plugin event bus: `<plugin>:<event>` names with `icebath:` reserved, one worker goroutine, 64 pending, chain depth 8, deep-copied payloads; renders system prompt sections per session
- `middleware.go` — request-rewrite chains and execution wrappers for LLM and tool calls, with a rewrite trace; stamps `icebath.observer.v1` and `icebath.middleware.v1` schema versions
- `relay_intercepts.go` — forwarder to `tools.ApplyRelayToolRequestIntercepts`, applied ahead of tool request middleware
- `streamhooks.go` — one bounded queue (1024, drop oldest) and worker per `on_stream_*` observer so plugin code never runs on the streaming path; `plugins.stream_reasoning_deltas` opt-in
- `plugin_events.go` — `plugin.<id>.<event>` wire names and `BroadcastPluginEvent` to connected terminal UI clients

#### Guest runtime: WebAssembly modules and external programs

A manifest with `entry` selects a guest: `runtime: wasm` (implied by a `.wasm` entry) or `runtime: program`. One `PluginHost` per plugin key starts the guest on first use, performs a `hello` handshake (30 s), restarts it after an unexpected exit (giving up once it has died more than 3 times in 600 s) and stops it when no loaded plugin or category instance uses it. Frames are one JSON document per line: requests `{id, method, params, origin}`, replies `{id, result}` or `{id, error}`, and a `cancel` notification; the `hello` reply carries a protocol version that the host stores and never compares. A guest has no ambient file, network or environment access: manifest `grants` (read, write, net, env) gate its `io` requests and `limits` set `memory_mb` (16 to 4096, default 256) and `call_seconds` (default 120).

- `guest.go` — `guestSpec` built from `runtime`, `entry`, `limits` and `grants`; one `PluginHost` per plugin key kept for the manager's life; wazero compile cache at `<root>/cache/plugin-wasm`
- `guest_module.go` — wazero instance with WASI preview1 and host module `icebath` (`host_call`, `host_read`, `cancelled`); requires exports `_initialize`, `icebath_alloc`, `icebath_call`, `icebath_free`; one owner goroutine, nested calls, a run budget that excludes time waiting on the host
- `guest_program.go` — starts the entry (a file of the plugin directory, else a program on PATH) in its own process group, optionally behind the `plugins.host.launcher` prefix; frames on stdin and stdout, stderr to the log; sets `ICEBATH_PLUGIN_NAME`, `ICEBATH_PLUGIN_DIR`, `ICEBATH_PLUGIN_HOST_PROCESS`
- `guest_io.go` — serves `io` requests under the grants: read_file, write_file, list_dir, remove, env and http (every redirect hop re-checked, 30 s default, 64 MB cap); path variables `$ICEBATH_HOME`, `$PLUGIN_DIR`, `$PLUGIN_DATA`
- `guest_profiles.go` — reads a wasm plugin's model provider profiles through the `icebath_profiles` export of a throwaway instance whose host calls answer nothing
- `host.go` — `PluginHost`: start, restart budget, idle shutdown and child generations; `Load`, `LoadInstance`, `ProfileCall`; serves guest requests (ctx, facade, parent_call, parent_event, parent_object, release_parent, io, dispose); `HostedCallable` and `HostedObject` proxies released on garbage collection
- `wire.go` — `Channel` (line-delimited JSON), value markers (`__bytes__`, `__record__`, `__opaque__`, `__callable__`, `__object__`, `__handle__`), remote errors mapped onto Python exception class names, Python-compatible JSON dump and load
- `host_tables.go` — host environment variable names and the tables of context methods that are refused, skipped, served through callbacks, or accept provider objects across the boundary

#### Host side of the guest protocol: replaying plugin-context calls

Each guest `ctx` request names a plugin-context method by its Python name (`register_tool`, `get_config`, `emit`, …); these files bind the arguments with Python semantics and replay the call on the real `Context`. The port's Python shape is most visible here: method names, keyword binding with TypeError wording, dataclass and type-annotation restoration.

- `host_ctx.go` — dispatch table of 39 context methods with their Python signatures (sibling files add 8 more); adapters turning hosted callables into tool handlers and hook callbacks; exported binder for facades other packages implement
- `host_ctx_cli.go` — `register_cli_command`: the argument parser is built and run inside the guest (`build_cli`, `run_cli`)
- `host_ctx_inprocess.go` — registrars that take live callbacks: approval transports, platforms, Slack action handlers (Python `re` patterns and flags converted to Go regexps)
- `host_ctx_requests.go` — `credentialed_provider_request`: the host attaches the sign-in the plugin declares in `requires_auth` or `oauth` to an outbound provider request
- `host_event.go` — `HostEvent`: a set, wait and clear flag living in the host that a guest drives through `parent_event`; the cron scheduler stop signal
- `host_platform.go` — calls into a hosted gateway platform adapter (`platform_bind`, `platform_call`, arguments built in the guest), used by `pkg/gateway/platforms/hosted`
- `host_restore.go` — [py-shim] parses Python type annotations and rebuilds wire values as the dataclasses provider bases declare (`FetchResult`, `ContextReference`, …); hosted provider proxies in agent, memory and gateway read results through it
- `state_facade.go` — exposes `PluginState` get and set to guests as the `state` facade

#### Category plugins loaded outside the general manager

Model providers, memory providers, context engines, cron schedulers and computer-use providers are not loaded by the discovery sweep: the owning package selects one by config and asks the guest host for the single provider object the plugin registers (`load_instance` with a capture method). A guest plugin offers a category through `provides:` (memory_provider, context_engine, cron_scheduler, computer_use_provider) or `kind: exclusive`.

- `hostprofiles.go` — `HostedProfile`: a model provider profile whose data fields were extracted once and whose overridden methods run in the guest
- `hostprofiles_extract.go` — profile extraction by a credential-free throwaway run (`--extract-profiles`, or the wasm export; 60 s), cached at `cache/plugin_host/model-providers/<name>-<hash>.json` by a file fingerprint; `LoadCategoryInstance`; `plugins.host.launcher`
- `provider_plugins.go` — `LoadProviderPluginProfiles` for `pkg/provider`; an overridden `create_client` keeps the client in the guest behind a live object proxy
- `memory_host.go` — `CollectMemoryProviderInHost` for `pkg/memory`: collector mode keeping a memory provider's hooks and skills apart; also the host callables a guest calls back through `parent_call`
- `context_engines.go` — discovers and loads guest context engines for `pkg/agent`, forwarding their slash commands to the command registry
- `computer_use_providers.go` — `LoadComputerUseProviderInHost` for `pkg/codeexec`
- `plugin_loader.go` — shared helpers of the category loaders: user plugins directory, manifest description, availability probe, named load that warns and yields nothing on failure

#### Services a plugin can call back into

Host-owned facades reached as `ctx.llm`, `ctx.platform_actions`, `ctx.subagent_lifecycle` and plain context methods; guests reach them through the `facade` request.

- `plugin_llm.go` — plain and structured (JSON schema) completions on the host's model and credentials; provider, model, agent-id, profile and task overrides gated per plugin by flags and allowlists under `plugins.entries.<id>.llm`
- `platform_actions.go`, `thread_rename_options.go` — add a reaction or rename a thread through the live gateway adapter (built-in Telegram and Discord paths), gated by the `gateway.platform_actions` capability and audit-logged
- `subagent_lifecycle.go` — launch, status, wait, cancel, result, reconnect and steer of delegated subagents through serializable handles carrying an HMAC capability; 8 workers, 16k goal, 32k context and 32k result character limits, results kept one hour
- `plugin_messages.go` — `post_message`: posts into the session bound to the call and returns a handle whose edits replace the message in place
- `plugin_choices.go` — `ask_choice`: asks the slash-command user to pick an option through an asker the dispatching surface binds; `ClarifyAsker` has no caller
- `plugin_command_dispatch.go` — invokes a plugin slash command once with the raw arguments and the session keywords its signature accepts
- `plugin_session.go` — client surface or messaging platform, and working directory, of the calling session
- `plugin_live_notes.go` — per-agent queue of "plugin is now live" notices appended to the next tool result or user turn of an open chat

#### Per-plugin settings, state and data

- `state.go` — settings writes under `plugins.entries.<id>.settings` (reserved roots, managed keys and traversal refused); `PluginState`: JSON key-value store at `plugin-data/<namespace>/state.json`, 10 MB quota, atomic 0600 writes
- `state_lock_{unix,windows}.go` — exclusive flock, or a first-byte lock retried ten times, on the sibling `.state.json.lock`
- `settings.go` — settings form for the terminal UI built from `config_schema`: field types, choices, validation; secret fields are saved as env variables named by the field's `env` or the upper-snake plugin id and key
- `plugin_storage.go` — [unwired] `PluginStorageDir`: creates `plugin-data/<name>` for a validated plugin name

#### Capabilities and consent

Eight declarable capabilities: tools.override, llm.provider_override, llm.model_override, llm.agent_id_override, llm.profile_override, llm.task_override, llm.side_question, gateway.platform_actions. Grants and a hash of the consented set live under `plugins.entries.<id>` as `granted_capabilities` and `capabilities_consent`; the older boolean gates (`allow_tool_override`, `llm.allow_*_override`, `allow_platform_actions`) still count as grants.

- `capabilities.go` — capability registry, manifest parsing, grant lookup, consent recording, pending and changed-set detection
- `capabilities_cmd.go` — `icebath plugins capabilities [name]` and the consent screen shown on install, update and enable

#### Curated catalog, kill list and catalog commands

A catalog entry pins a plugin to a 40-hex commit: name, repo, sha, subdir, description, maintainer, tier (official, verified, community), category (memory, platform, web, tools, voice, automation, models, general), version, requires_icebath, docs_url, image, screenshots, platforms, title, onboarding, default, capabilities and known_issues. The in-tree catalog is embedded; a published copy is fetched from `https://icebath.app/api/plugin-catalog.json` (5 s, 2 MB), cached at `cache/plugin-catalog.json` for 6 hours and usable stale for 24, and the newer source wins a differing pin. The `removed` kill list, matched by name or normalised repository URL, blocks install, load, update and enable unless the install record carries `allow_removed`.

- `catalog.go` — entry type and validation, embedded and directory loaders, filters, image URL allowlist (https on GitHub hosts only)
- `catalog_live.go` — live fetch, cache, 60 s failure back-off, merge with the in-tree entries
- `catalog_removed.go` — embeds `catalog/*.yaml`; kill-list loading and matching; stale-cache reader that needs no network
- `catalog_presence.go` — for catalog cards: fetches the pinned `plugin.json` from raw.githubusercontent.com and reports whether the local app each declared server needs is present
- `catalog_cmd.go` — `plugins search`, `browse`, `info`, `validate`; catalog install and re-pin (never a pull) with consent when the new pin widens tools, hooks, capabilities, Python dependencies or sign-ins; carries user files across updates; provenance block plus `.icebath-catalog.json` sidecar; platform and version gates
- `catalog_dir_override.go` — [unwired] test seam that swaps the catalog directory
- `catalog/{agent-importers,camofox,homeassistant,langfuse,mcp-serve,spotify}.yaml` — [data] six official entries, each pointing at this repository under `pkg/plugintree/catalog/<name>` at a pinned sha; none is marked default
- `catalog/removed.yaml` — [data] kill list: or-picker, github-copilot, singularity

#### Install from git, GitHub or the catalog

`icebath plugins install <catalog name | owner/repo[/subdir] | git URL[#subdir]>` resolves the source, clones shallowly at an exact commit into a temporary directory under `plugins/` (sparse for a subdirectory, credentials scrubbed from the origin), reads the manifest, checks version fit, runs the security scan and then publishes tree and metadata together. The metadata record per plugin holds `source`, `revision`, `pinned`, and optionally `update_url`, a `catalog` block and `allow_removed`. With the package manager linked, the swap and the dependency sync are one `pm.SyncVenv` transaction; without it, a rename swap with a `.previous-<name>-<pid>` backup that is rolled back on failure. A tree with `__init__.py` and no `entry` is refused as Python source unless it is the manifest of a compiled-in port.

- `install.go` — `CmdInstall` and `UnattendedInstallPlugin`; clone at the reviewed commit (a source that moved is refused); prompts for `requires_env` into the home env file; enable decision; memory provider selection
- `facade.go` — identifier to git URL resolution (GitHub browser URLs, `owner/repo/path`, `#subdir`); scan policy (`plugins.scan_on_install`; a caution verdict needs confirmation, a reviewed catalog pin or force); manifest reading; copying of `*.example` files
- `git.go` — git subprocess layer: 60 s default timeout, exact-revision checkout, credential fallback through `pkg/gitcred`, autostash pull; atomic `.install-metadata.json` writes under a pid-stamped lock file (10 s wait)
- `inspect.go` — pre-install inspection for the terminal UI dialog: clones outside any profile and reports whether the source ships a plugin and at which sha; concurrent requests joined, results kept 10 minutes
- `admission.go` — admits a change of the enabled and disabled sets through `pkg/pm` (refused on a dependency conflict) or writes config directly in a build without it
- `transaction.go` — `publishPlugin` (staged tree swap plus metadata) and `updatePlugin` (catalog re-pin or git pull prepared in a staged copy)
- `install_deps.go` — consent prompts for declared Node (`package.json`) and Python dependencies; new Python requirements in an update need interactive review
- `install_display.go` — prints the plugin's `after-install.md`, else an "installed" panel with its location
- `python_deps.go` — declared Python requirements, missing-dependency warnings at discovery, restart hints naming the processes that lack them
- `provenance.go` — classifies each installed directory as git, manual, self-cloned or drift from its metadata row and `.git` presence

#### Update checks, updates and the gateway cadence

- `updates.go` — `CheckResult`, local provenance check, `update_url` feed parsing (version, min_icebath, notes_url, artifacts), https-only rule
- `updates_checks.go` — `RunChecks`: compares the catalog pin, a saved feed or `git ls-remote` HEAD with the installed revision and never mutates anything
- `update.go` — `plugins update <name>`, `adopt` (record the origin of a self-cloned directory), `trust-update-url`, `check-updates`; unattended variant for the terminal UI
- `update_all.go` — `plugins update` with no name: plan table, one confirmation, per-plugin outcome, exit 1 when any failed
- `cadence.go` — gateway housekeeping tick: `plugins.auto_update_check_hours` (default 24, 0 disables), marker and `results.json` under `plugin-update-checks/`, a pm receipt, opt-in `plugins.auto_apply` for git installs

#### Enable, disable, remove, list and go-live

- `selection.go` — `plugins enable` and `disable` under a per-home selection lock; alias handling; sync of saved toolset lists; `SetAgentPluginEnabled` for chat and RPC; entry of `plugins doctor`
- `toggle.go` — bare `icebath plugins`: interactive screen of the general plugins plus Memory Provider and Context Engine pickers (`memory.provider`, `context.engine`)
- `listing.go` — `plugins list` (table, plain or JSON, with status, provenance, pin and kill-list note) and `plugins show`
- `remove.go` — `plugins remove`: deletes tree and metadata together and forgets the plugin's config; a tree a Windows process still holds is parked in `cache/plugin-pending-delete` and swept at gateway start
- `activation.go` — makes a change live without a restart: forced rediscovery here, refresh of open chats, a reload request to the running gateway, and the restart hint when dependencies are missing
- `activation_live.go` — connects the MCP servers of a just-activated portable plugin and gathers its skills for the live notice
- `cmd.go` — `Console` markup printer (stands in for Python rich), `CommandExit`, plugin name sanitising, `plugins.clone_timeout_seconds` (default 300, max 3600)

#### Install-time security scanner

Applies the skills guard engine of `pkg/skills` to plugin trees at install, update and validate, with every external plugin treated at community trust.

- `plugin_guard.go` — `ScanPlugin` (version `plugin-guard-v12`): pattern scan of every file plus structural checks (symlink escape, binaries, tracked bytecode, 400 files, 10 MB total, 1 MB per file); verdict safe, caution or dangerous, and force never overrides dangerous
- `plugin_guard_context.go` — context classifiers that only ever lower severity: documentation prose, CI workflows, test trees, locale catalogs, comments, trusted installer pipes, base64 media, loopback URLs

#### Supply-chain advisories for the managed Python environment

- `security_advisories.go` — hard-coded advisory list (one entry, mistralai 2.4.6), detection in the managed venv, startup banner at most daily (`cache/advisory_banner_seen`), gateway log line, dismissal by `icebath doctor --ack <id>` into `security.acked_advisories`
- `advisory_dist.go` — [py-shim] importlib.metadata-style lookup of an installed distribution's version in site-packages; used only by the advisory check

#### `plugins validate` and `plugins doctor`

- `validate.go` — admission report (the catalog CI gate, exit 0 or 1, optional JSON): manifest fields, `requires_icebath`, config schema, `requires_env`, OAuth, loadable form, built-in tool collisions, security scan; portable packages get server trust, cost and availability rows
- `validate_locales.go` — language pack check of `provides_locales` files against the English reference keys of `pkg/i18n`
- `plugin_dev.go` — Plugin Doctor: stages a copy, loads it through the real runtime under a temporary home with guest network denied, restores every registry it touched, and compares declared with registered tools and hooks

#### Python-source audits kept from the Python plugin era

[port-artifact] Reachable from `plugins validate`, but they inspect only Python plugin source, which the same report fails as an unsupported form and the loader never runs. They were the admission rules for third-party Python plugins: declare what you register, do not monkey-patch core, do not import private core modules.

- `validate_probe.go` — runs an embedded Python script in a subprocess to record what `register()` registers and compares it with the manifest; also validates the declared Python dependency block
- `validate_core_override.go` — Python AST taint analysis that fails a plugin rebinding core modules at runtime
- `validate_private_imports.go` — warns on imports of private core modules and private attribute access on core handles
- `core_tables.go` — loads the table below once and walks its tree to decide whether a dotted module name exists in core
- `core_tables.txt.gz` — [data] 13,370-row snapshot of the original Python application: 97 top-level modules, 94 packages, 1,318 private names and its file and directory tree; read only by the two audits above
- `module_names.go` — reads a retired `hermes_` module prefix as `icebath_` for those audits

#### Plugin packs

- `packs.go` — `plugins pack install|export|show`: a YAML pack (name, description, author, version, plugins pinned by catalog name or repo and ref, non-secret config seeds, skills) from a file or https URL (1 MB, 15 s); secret-shaped keys are refused and seeds never overwrite user values

#### Shell hooks, hook directories and outbound webhooks

Extension by configuration, without a plugin. A `hooks.<event>` entry in `config.yaml` runs a command with a JSON payload on stdin (`hook_event_name`, `tool_name`, `tool_input`, `session_id`, `cwd`, `profile`, `extra`) and may answer a JSON directive on stdout; exit code 2 blocks a `pre_tool_call`. Every event and command pair needs consent recorded in `<home>/shell-hooks-allowlist.json`, given by a terminal prompt, `--accept-hooks`, `ICEBATH_ACCEPT_HOOKS` or `hooks_auto_accept`. `hooks.outbound` targets receive the same events as signed HTTP POSTs.

- `shell_hooks.go` — entry parsing (`command`; `matcher` regex for the two tool events; `timeout` default 60 and max 300 s; `fail_closed` for `pre_tool_call` only), consent and allowlist, wiring as ordinary hook callbacks, response dialects (block, modify, approve, context, continue)
- `shell_hooks_proc.go` — starts the hook process with piped stdio in its own group and reaps the whole tree on timeout
- `shell_hooks_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS process attributes, PATH resolution, return code and allowlist lock
- `hooks_cmd.go` — `icebath hooks list|test|revoke|doctor`
- `hooks_view.go` — hooks model for the terminal UI hub: overview with script-mtime drift, approve, add, remove, test and check
- `hook_dirs.go` — runs the command of a gateway hook directory with the event name and context on stdin; called from `pkg/gatewayrun/hooks.go`
- `outbound_webhooks.go` — `hooks.outbound` delivery: 256-entry queue, one worker, 2 attempts, headers `X-Icebath-Event`, `X-Icebath-Delivery` and HMAC `X-Icebath-Signature-256`

#### Helpers housed here that are not about plugins

- `github_api.go` — GitHub token lookup (`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GH_TOKEN`, then `gh auth token`) and rate-limit failure wording; its callers are in `pkg/selfupdate`
- `console_hide_{unix,windows}.go` — starts the `gh` child without a console window on Windows
- `session_reset_policy.go` — detects a timed `session_reset` config block (idle, daily, both) and whether the external `icebath-session-reset-policy` plugin that applies it is enabled; that plugin is not in this repository
- `verify_command.go` — body of the `icebath verify` command (project smoke test), driving `pkg/plugins/verify` and recording the run in the verification evidence ledger
- `verify_process.go` — init hook handing the verify runner the process-ownership helpers of `pkg/tools`

#### Re-export shims

[port-artifact] Exported wrappers around unexported helpers for `pkg/gatewayrun` and the `pkg/tuiserver` plugin hub.

- `manager_scope_export.go` — `Manager.ScopeKey`
- `plugin_keys_export.go` — `Manager.PluginKeys`
- `plugin_sets_export.go` — `EnabledPluginSet`, `DisabledPluginSet`
- `plugins_hub_export.go` — category-active names, listed status, portable-directory test, pinned revision, catalog install record, portable MCP server name, plugin event id test

### `pkg/plugins/defaults` — one-time install of catalog plugins marked `default` into every home

*3 files, 694 Go lines*

Installs and enables each catalog entry marked `default` (official or verified tier only) once per profile home, recording what a home was given in `plugins/.default-plugins.json` so a later removal or disable stays the user's choice. It runs from the `install_default_plugins` post-update step, from the update command tail, and from a detached child re-executed with the argv marker `__icebath_default_plugins__` (dispatched in `cmd/icebath/startup.go`, spawned at profile provisioning) that logs to `logs/default-plugins.log`. It honours `security.allow_lazy_installs` and `ICEBATH_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS`. No in-tree catalog entry is marked default, so it acts only on entries the live catalog marks.

#### Default plugin installer

- `defaults.go` — per-home pass, all-homes pass under a file lock, `InstallAndRecord` coordinator with `cache/default-plugins.{lock,rerun,settled}` state files, `SpawnInstall`, `RunChild`, the non-blocking `StepInstall` boot step
- `attempts.go` — failure stamps `cache/default-plugins.failed-<name>` with back-off of one hour doubled per failure up to a week; one-line cause extraction from git errors
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/plugins/verify` — `icebath verify`: detect a project's run recipe and smoke-test it

*9 files, 1,716 Go lines*

Not plugin verification: this is the project smoke-test engine behind the `icebath verify` command and the agent's verification stop gate, placed under `pkg/plugins` by the port. It detects how the project in a directory is bootstrapped, built, tested and started, or loads a saved recipe from `.icebath/environment.json`, then runs bootstrap, build, test, start in background, readiness poll and teardown. Callers are `pkg/plugins/verify_command.go`, `pkg/commands/cli_tree_verify.go` and `pkg/agent` (recipe detection, nudge limit, evidence ledger).

#### Recipe detection and manifest

- `recipes.go` — `Recipe` and detection in order package.json (framework decides kind and port), Python (Django, FastAPI or Uvicorn, Flask), Go, Rust, Maven or Gradle, Makefile, docker compose; port inference from the start command
- `environment.go` — load and save of `.icebath/environment.json` (versioned wrapper around the recipe, bare shape also accepted)

#### Run, readiness and teardown

- `runner.go` — runs each phase command through the shell (600 s per phase), starts the app in an owned process group, polls readiness (60 s), tears the group down, probes `docker compose ps`; keeps 2000-character output tails
- `readiness.go` — polls the app URL until any HTTP status answers, with a 5 s socket timeout and environment proxies
- `terminate_{unix,windows}.go` — signal, terminate and kill of the started child per OS

#### Command surface and agent hooks

- `command.go` — declarative argument table of the `verify` subcommand (path, --detect-only, --save, --skip-start, --phase, --port, --timeout, --ready-timeout)
- `hooks.go` — `agent.max_verify_nudges` (default 3) bound on consecutive `pre_verify` continue directives, and the coding guidance text switched by `agent.verify_guidance`
- `evidence.go` — `EvidenceRecorder` variable the agent package assigns so a run is written to the verification evidence ledger

### `pkg/pluginsdk` — Go SDK for plugin authors: the guest end of the plugin protocol

*15 files, 4,866 Go lines*

The library a third-party plugin imports; it has no dependency on any other project package. A plugin calls `Register(fn)` (and optionally `RegisterProfile`) from `init` and `Main()` from `main`; built normally it is an external program serving frames on stdin and stdout, built with `GOOS=wasip1 GOARCH=wasm -buildmode=c-shared` it is a WebAssembly module driven through exported functions. The only in-repo user is the `clock-widget` template under `pkg/skills/bundled/autonomous-ai-agents/icebath-agent/templates/`; `pkg/plugins` imports it only for the `--extract-profiles` flag name.

#### Core surface and wire peer

- `sdk.go` — `Register`, the 53-method `Host` interface (every registrar and host call), `Object` (the form every provider takes), `Tool`, `Command`, `Widget`, `Blueprint`, `AuxiliaryTask`, `Section`, `HTTPRequest`, `ProviderRequest`, `Handle`, `HostFunc`
- `host.go` — `Host` implementation: each method is one `ctx`, `facade` or `io` request; granted file, HTTP and env access; `InjectMessage`, `AskChoice`, `SideQuestion`, `CallMCP`, `DispatchTool`
- `peer.go` — guest end of the wire: tables of callbacks and objects the host addresses, request and reply framing, value encode and decode, dispatch of hello, load, invoke, obj_*, release, unload, shutdown
- `link_stdio.go` — non-wasm build: `Main` reads frames from stdin, writes to the real stdout and redirects `os.Stdout` to stderr; answers `--extract-profiles` and exits
- `link_wasip1.go` — wasip1 build: imports `icebath.host_call`, `host_read`, `cancelled`; exports `icebath_alloc`, `icebath_free`, `icebath_call`, `icebath_profiles`; cancellation polled from the host
- `hostobject.go` — `HostObject` (an object living in icebath read and called by name) and `Message` (a posted message whose text can be edited or refreshed)
- `event.go` — `Event`: a flag living in icebath that the plugin reads, waits on, sets and clears

#### Typed extension surfaces

- `provider_base.go` — required members and default behaviour per provider kind: image_gen, video_gen, web_search, browser, terminal_environment, cron_scheduler, computer_use, secret_source, tts, transcription, delegation, context_reference, login_backend, browser_page_backend, context engine and memory bases
- `hosted.go` — `Profile` and `RegisterProfile` for model providers; profile description and calls; capture of the one provider a category load asks for
- `platform.go` — `Platform`: a messaging platform for the gateway with setup questions, env-to-config steps, target syntax, standalone send; `Gateway` callbacks, `SessionSource`, `MessageEvent`, `SendResult`
- `platform_adapter.go` — `Adapter`: 67 optional hooks of one connection (send, edit, media, typing, approvals, text batching, stream rendering, streaming TTS) and their wire bindings
- `terminal.go` — `TerminalBackend` selected by `terminal.backend`, with environments that run the commands of the terminal, code and file tools
- `cron.go` — `CronScheduler` selected by `cron.provider`, and `Cron` operations (ClaimFire, FireClaimed, FireDue, RecoverInterrupted)
- `login.go` — `LoginBackend`: a browser vault backend resolving saved logins by handle (list, metadata, password, OTP, secret), with result type checks
- `cli.go` — `CLICommand`: an `icebath <name>` subcommand answering output and exit code

### `pkg/plugintree` — embedded manifests of bundled plugins and embedded trees of catalog plugins

*123 files, 44 Go lines*

Carries plugin metadata, not plugin code: the Go implementations live in `pkg/gateway/platforms/*`, `pkg/media`, `pkg/browser`, `pkg/builtin/*`, `pkg/memory` and `pkg/provider` and register themselves with `plugins.RegisterBundled` or `plugins.RegisterPort`. `plugins/` is embedded whole (`go:embed all:plugins`) and read by plugin listing, the gateway's bundled platform scan, the config facade and the photon sidecar mirror; `ICEBATH_BUNDLED_PLUGINS` replaces it with a directory. `catalog.tar.zst` is the packed copy of `catalog/` and is what a catalog install at the pinned sha writes into a home instead of cloning. Bundled plugins repeat these manifest fields by hand in their Go `Manifest()`, which is what the loader reads, while catalog ports read theirs from the embedded catalog tree (`plugins.CatalogPortManifest`).

#### Embedding

- `tree.go` — `Compiled()` (the embedded `plugins` tree) and `CatalogTree(name)` (one plugin's subtree of the archive); `go:generate` packs `catalog/` with `cmd/packtree`
- `catalog.tar.zst` — [data] zstd tar of the six catalog plugin trees, the only form of them the binary embeds
- `catalog_manifest.txt` — [data] sha256 and mode of each of the 14 packed files, written by the packer

#### Bundled plugin manifests by category

[data] One `plugin.yaml` per plugin; the category directory becomes the key prefix (`platforms/telegram`). Categories memory, model-providers, computer_use and config_backends are skipped by the general manager and found by their own subsystems.

- `plugins/platforms/*/plugin.yaml` — 27 gateway platforms (kind platform, label, required and optional env with setup prompts): a2a, bluebubbles, buzz, dingtalk, discord, email, feishu, google_chat, irc, line, matrix, mattermost, ntfy, photon, qqbot, raft, signal, simplex, slack, sms, teams, telegram, wecom, weixin, whatsapp, whatsapp_cloud, yuanbao
- `plugins/platforms/photon/sidecar/{index,patch-spectrum-mixed-attachments,send-format,stream-staleness}.mjs` — Node sidecar bridging iMessage through the `spectrum-ts` SDK over a token-protected loopback HTTP API (NDJSON inbound, send, react, typing, poll); mirrored to `<home>/photon/sidecar` at run time
- `plugins/platforms/photon/sidecar/package{,-lock}.json` — sidecar dependency pin (`spectrum-ts` 12.10.1) with a postinstall patch step
- `plugins/model-providers/*/plugin.yaml` — 38 model providers (kind model-provider): actual, ai-gateway, alibaba, alibaba-coding-plan, anthropic, arcee, azure-foundry, bedrock, commandcode, custom, deepinfra, deepseek, fireworks, gemini, github-copilot, gmi, huggingface, kilocode, kimi-coding, lmstudio, meta-ai, minimax, nebius-token-factory, novita, nvidia, ollama-cloud, openai-codex, opencode-zen, openrouter, qwen-oauth, router, stepfun, tencent-tokenhub, upstage, vertex, xai, xiaomi, zai
- `plugins/image_gen/*/plugin.yaml` — 8 image generation backends: deepinfra, fal, krea, meta-ai, openai, openai-codex, openrouter, xai
- `plugins/video_gen/*/plugin.yaml` — 4 video generation backends: deepinfra, fal, openrouter, xai
- `plugins/web/*/plugin.yaml` — 11 web search and fetch backends (`provides_web_providers`): brave_free, ddgs, exa, firecrawl, keenable, openai_native, parallel, perplexity, searxng, tavily, xai
- `plugins/browser/*/plugin.yaml` — 3 cloud browser backends (`provides_browser_providers`): browserbase, browser_use, firecrawl
- `plugins/memory/*/plugin.yaml` — 2 external memory providers selected by `memory.provider`: byterover, retaindb
- `plugins/computer_use/cua/plugin.yaml` — cua: the default computer-use backend when `computer_use.backend` is unset
- `plugins/config_backends/remote/plugin.yaml` — remote: serves profile config from `ICEBATH_CONFIG_REMOTE_URL`, selected only by `ICEBATH_CONFIG_BACKEND=remote`
- `plugins/delegation/default/plugin.yaml` — default: delegation strategy following the `delegation` config section, else the parent's model
- `plugins/disk-cleanup/plugin.yaml` — disk-cleanup: hooks that track and delete ephemeral files a session created
- `plugins/google_meet/plugin.yaml` — google_meet: tools meet_join, meet_leave, meet_status, meet_transcript, meet_say (Linux and macOS)
- `plugins/security-guidance/plugin.yaml` — security-guidance: appends warnings to file-write tool results that contain known-dangerous patterns
- `plugins/teams_pipeline/plugin.yaml` — teams_pipeline: Microsoft Teams meeting transcript and summary pipeline with operator CLI flows

#### Catalog plugin trees

[data] Source of `catalog.tar.zst`: the published tree of each catalog plugin whose Go port is compiled in. All six were formerly built into core.

- `catalog/*/plugin.yaml` — 6 manifests: agent-importers (`icebath import-agent`), camofox (anti-detection Firefox browser tools), homeassistant (platform adapter plus four tools), langfuse (tracing hooks), mcp-serve (`icebath mcp-serve`), spotify (seven tools)
- `catalog/*/README.md` — 6 user-facing READMEs, one per catalog plugin
- `catalog/agent-importers/skills/openclaw-migration/SKILL.md` — skill shipped with agent-importers that walks an OpenClaw import
- `catalog/agent-importers/skills/openclaw-migration/scripts/openclaw_to_icebath.py` — 153 KB Python migration script the skill runs; the one Python program shipped inside a plugin tree

### `pkg/pluginservices` — assembles the provider registry map handed to the plugin manager

*1 file, 21 Go lines*

A one-function package that exists only to break an import cycle: `pkg/agent` and `pkg/provider` import `pkg/plugins`, so the map of their registries is built here and passed in by `cmd/icebath/wiring.go` as `Services.ProviderRegistries`.

#### Provider registry assembly

- `registries.go` — `ProviderRegistries()`: core kinds web_search_provider, terminal_environment_provider, secret_source and delegation_provider, plus every kind a linked tier registered through `plugins.RegisterProviderRegistry`

### `pkg/providerregistry` — generic name-keyed provider registry with per-profile scopes

*2 files, 451 Go lines*

`Registry[P]` is the shared container behind several provider categories: a global map plus one map per profile home, generation counters callers use to invalidate caches, and exact-slot snapshot and restore so the plugin manager can undo a registration on unload. Instantiated by `pkg/tools` (web providers, terminal environment backends), `pkg/browser` (vault login backends), `pkg/provider` (its generic constructor and secret sources) and `pkg/agent` (context references). Error types and messages reproduce the Python registry module it was ported from.

#### Registry

- `registry.go` — `Registry[P]`: register (same name overwrites, built-in names refused), merged and per-scope lookup, generations, snapshot and restore, the untyped `Scoped()` view the plugin context drives, `IsAvailableSafe`; `API` struct re-exposing the old module-level function names
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/builtin` — compiled-in plugins: the embedded EGM, Hallmark and Impeccable payload and the link point for eleven plugin subpackages

*411 files, 2,503 Go lines*

The root package holds three plugin "ports": Go code compiled into the binary that only becomes a loaded plugin after `icebath plugins install <name>` writes a manifest into a home with source `builtin:` (the `pkg/plugins` port mechanism). The three are third-party skill packs vendored under `payload/`: Google's Elephant-Goldfish Model (`egm`), Nutlope's Hallmark and Paul Bakaus's Impeccable. `cmd/packtree` packs `payload/` into `payload.tar.zst` plus `payload_manifest.txt`; both are embedded, and on first plugin load the tree is written to `<root home>/cache/builtin-plugins/<version>-<digest>/` as a `payload/` mirror and a derived `host/` layout that skills are registered from. The eleven subpackages (own sections below) are one plugin each and register at init through `plugins.RegisterBundled` (always discovered, gated by kind or `plugins.enabled`) or `plugins.RegisterPort` (catalog plugins whose manifest comes from `pkg/plugintree/catalog`). What is linked is decided by blank imports in `cmd/icebath`: `link_core.go` links `delegationdefault`; `link_plugins.go` (absent under build tag `icebath_core`) links this package, `camofox`, `diskcleanup`, `langfuse`, `mcpserveplugin`, `securityguidance`, `spotify`, `teamspipeline`, `webbackends`; `link_extras.go` (absent under `icebath_core` or `icebath_noextras`) links `agentimporters` and `googlemeet`. Other compiled-in plugins (gateway platforms, image and video generation, cloud browsers) register from their own packages, so this directory is not the complete list.

#### Payload archive, manifest and materialization to disk

The payload never runs from the source tree: only the archive and manifest are embedded. `Materialize` is called by each of the three ports at registration and by the hook and script runners.

- `gen.go` — `go:generate` directive running `cmd/packtree pack -dir payload` to rebuild the archive and manifest
- `payload.tar.zst` — [data] deterministic zstd tar of the 398 files under `payload/`, embedded and read through `pkg/tarzst` as a filesystem
- `payload_manifest.txt` — [data] one line per payload file (path, sha256, octal mode); embedded, supplies file modes (twelve scripts are 0755) and feeds the cache digest
- `payload.go` — `Materialize`: writes payload and host layout once per 16-hex digest of running version, host layout version and manifest; builds in a temp sibling, renames into place, marks `.complete`, tolerates a racing writer
- `log.go` — package logger named `builtin`

#### EGM port: spec drafting and fresh-context design review skills

Plugin `egm` (Elephant-Goldfish Model, Apache-2.0, version 0.1.0). It contributes skills only: seven workflow skills and nine reviewer or orchestrator personas, each registered as a plugin skill resolvable as `egm:<name>`. No tools, hooks or commands.

- `egm.go` — registers all three ports at init; reads the manifest from `plugin.json`; registers the 7 skills and 9 personas; builds `host/egm` with `agents/` and `resources/` copied beside every skill and persona, broken relative links repointed at the payload, and `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` replaced by the materialized path

#### Hallmark port: design skill, lint hook and install commands

Plugin `hallmark` (MIT, version 2.0.0). Registers the skill `hallmark:hallmark` straight from the payload path, a `transform_tool_result` hook, and two slash commands. Its scripts are Node `.mjs` files run on the `pkg/pm` managed Node runtime, so Node is an external dependency of the hook and the install gates.

- `hallmark.go` — manifest from the Claude plugin manifest; registers the skill, the lint hook and the commands `/hallmark-install` and `/hallmark-install-hook`; `HallmarkCommand` runs one of ten whitelisted scripts through `pm.Ensure("node")`
- `hallmark_install.go` — `/hallmark-install [--dry-run] [--force] [--remove]` enables or disables the plugin after `refcheck --errors` and `theme validate` gates; `/hallmark-install-hook [--global] [--print] [--remove]` stores `lint_hook` or `lint_hook_projects` under `plugins.entries.hallmark.settings`

#### Impeccable port: rendered skill, `/impeccable` command and native engine resolver

Plugin `impeccable` (version 4.8.0). The upstream project builds one skill per harness from a source template; this port re-implements that build in Go for an `icebath` target and re-implements the upstream shell launcher that finds or downloads a native `impeccable` engine binary. The skill is registered from `host/impeccable/skills/impeccable/`, and `/impeccable` hands a built skill turn to the invoking surface.

- `impeccable.go` — manifest from the upstream Claude plugin manifest; registers the rendered skill, the `/impeccable` command (24 subcommands from `command-metadata.json`, alias `teach` for `init`) and the design hooks; `TurnSubmitter` is implemented only by `gateway.BoundTurn`
- `impeccable_render.go` — the build: keeps `<icebath>` provider blocks and drops 21 other harness tags, fills `{{model}}`, `{{config_file}}`, `{{command_prefix}}`, `{{scripts_path}}`, strips rule markers, regenerates YAML frontmatter, renders references, turns agent files into `reference/degraded/<role>.md` for a harness without subagents
- `impeccable_source.go` — [port-artifact] ECMAScript `String()` coercion of frontmatter values so the Go render matches the upstream JavaScript build byte for byte
- `impeccable_engine.go` — engine resolution in the launcher's order: `IMPECCABLE_BIN`, bundled `bin/<os>-<arch>/`, `~/.impeccable/bin`, version cache under `IMPECCABLE_HOME`, `PATH`, then a download from GitHub releases (`IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE`) verified against `engine-checksums.txt`; separate Windows `impeccable.cmd` flow

#### Edit-time design hooks shared by Hallmark and Impeccable

Both hooks translate icebath tool events into Claude Code hook JSON (`PostToolUse` with `Write` or `Edit`, and `Stop`), pipe it to the upstream hook program and fold its `additionalContext` back into the tool result. Upstream Impeccable also declares a `SessionStart` hook; no icebath event is mapped to it.

- `hooks.go` — Impeccable: per-edit findings added to `write_file` and `patch` results (5 s), a `pre_verify` deep pass that can block or continue the turn (30 s), launcher looked up in a trusted project `.icebath/skills/impeccable`, the home, then the materialized tree, off with `IMPECCABLE_HOOK_DISABLED`; Hallmark: `lint-hook.mjs` findings added when the hook is installed (10 s)

#### Vendored payload trees

[data] Source of `payload.tar.zst`. At run time every file is written under the cache directory; the bullets say which parts Go code actually reads.

- `payload/elephant-goldfish-model/{plugin.json,.codex-plugin/plugin.json}` — plugin manifests; the root one supplies name `egm`, version, description, license and homepage, the Codex one is only mirrored
- `payload/elephant-goldfish-model/skills/*/SKILL.md` — the 7 skills: `egm-bootstrap` (directory READMEs), `egm-brainstorm`, `egm-draft`, `egm-review`, `egm-review-loop`, `egm-resolve`, `egm-drift-report` (spec versus implementation)

- `payload/hallmark/skills/hallmark/references/*.md`, `payload/hallmark/skills/hallmark/references/{genres,macrostructures}/*.md` — 24 topic references (layout, imagery, craft, gates, fonts, dark mode, microinteractions and more), 4 genre briefs, 21 page macrostructures

- `payload/hallmark/skills/hallmark/scripts/fixtures/**` — 17 HTML, CSS, TSX and Vue exemplars and pass or fail cases that `refcheck.mjs` lints as part of the install gate
