### `pkg/builtin/agentimporters` — catalog port that adds `icebath import-agent` and `icebath claw`

*1 file, 85 Go lines*

A wrapper with no logic of its own: once `icebath plugins install agent-importers` lands the catalog tree in a home, it registers two top-level CLI commands that call `pkg/agentimport`, and one skill whose file ships in the installed tree (`pkg/plugintree/catalog/agent-importers/skills/openclaw-migration`). Flags are built by `pkg/commands/cli_plugin_parsers.go`, not here. Linked only in the extras tier.

#### Plugin registration and command handlers

- `plugin.go` — registers `import-agent` and `claw` with their help text and the `openclaw-migration` skill; maps the parsed namespace to `agentimport.Args` and `ClawArgs` and the exit code to `commands.ExitError`

### `pkg/builtin/camofox` — catalog port driving a self-hosted Camofox browser server as the `camofox` toolset

*11 files, 2,483 Go lines*

Client for the REST API of an external `jo-inc/camofox-browser` server (default `http://localhost:9377`); icebath never installs or starts that server. It adds eleven `browser_*` tools under toolset `camofox`, an auxiliary vision task, a `browser_vault` page backend, two session hooks and `icebath camofox setup|status`. Configuration is `CAMOFOX_URL` and optional `CAMOFOX_API_KEY` in the profile `.env`, the `browser.camofox.*` block and several `browser.*` keys of `config.yaml`. It writes screenshots under the home `browser_screenshots/` and full snapshots under `cache/web/`; the path `<home>/browser_auth/camofox` is only hashed into the managed identity and nothing is stored there. Eight of eleven files import `internal/py*`, mostly to reproduce Python `requests` error text.

#### Plugin registration, tool schemas and CLI

- `plugin.go` — registers aux task `camofox_vision` (inherits `vision`), the tools, the page backend, hooks `on_session_end` (cleanup unless `browser.headed`) and `on_session_finalize`, and the `camofox` CLI command
- `schemas.go` — model-facing schemas of `browser_navigate`, `browser_snapshot`, `browser_click`, `browser_type`, `browser_scroll`, `browser_back`, `browser_press`, `browser_get_images`, `browser_vision`, `browser_console`, `browser_import_cookies`
- `cli.go` — `icebath camofox setup [--url]` saves `CAMOFOX_URL` and an optional key to the profile `.env`; `status` prints server, identity mode, reachability and VNC address, exit 1 when unset or unreachable
- `log.go` — package logger named `camofox`

#### REST client, sessions and identity

One session per profile home and task holds a Camofox `userId`, session key and tab id. Identity precedence: external (`CAMOFOX_USER_ID`, `CAMOFOX_SESSION_KEY` or config), managed persistence (stable uuid5 per profile, `browser.camofox.managed_persistence`), else a random ephemeral user deleted at session end.

- `client.go` — authenticated requests (`/health`, `/tabs`, `/sessions/<user>`), bearer header, timeout from `browser.command_timeout` (floor 5 s, default 30), loopback URL rewrite to a Docker host alias (`CAMOFOX_REWRITE_LOOPBACK_URLS`), tab adoption (`CAMOFOX_ADOPT_EXISTING_TAB`), resync after 404 or 410, VNC address from the health reply
- `pyvalues.go` — [py-shim] Python exception class names, `dict.get` and truthiness helpers behind the tool error text the model sees

#### Tool implementations

- `tools.go` — the eleven tool bodies: navigate with title and compact snapshot, click and type by `@eN` ref, five-step scroll, screenshot analysed by the auxiliary vision model, JavaScript evaluation, Netscape `cookies.txt` import (under `browser.camofox.cookies_dir`, 5 MB cap, needs the API key); availability checks; per-task cleanup

#### Output redaction, navigation and evaluate policy

- `policy.go` — forces secret redaction on all browser text returned to the model, masks typed secrets, refuses URLs carrying keys or blocklisted targets, refuses risky JavaScript when `browser.restrict_evaluate` is on, truncates snapshots at `browser.snapshot_threshold` and stores the full tree under `cache/web`
- `nofollow_{unix,windows}.go` — `O_NOFOLLOW` open flag for the snapshot cache file on Unix, no flag on Windows

#### Credential vault page backend

- `vault.go` — `browser_vault` backend named `camofox`: evaluates fill scripts on the task's existing tab; a secret-bearing script is sent only over HTTPS or loopback HTTP, without proxy or redirect

### `pkg/builtin/delegationdefault` — default delegation strategy for `delegate_task` subagents

*1 file, 68 Go lines*

The one built-in linked in every build tier. It registers the delegation backend named `default`, which routes every subagent through the `delegation` section of `config.yaml` and otherwise inherits the parent's model and credentials.

#### Default delegation provider

- `plugin.go` — bundled backend plugin `delegation/default`; `RouteTask` returns the delegation config minus `service_tier`; picker label and summary text

### `pkg/builtin/diskcleanup` — tracks ephemeral files an agent creates and deletes them safely

*3 files, 1,316 Go lines*

Bundled plugin `disk-cleanup` (opt-in through `plugins.enabled`). Hooks on `write_file`, `patch` and `terminal` calls record paths that did not exist before the call and exist after it and classify them; when a test file was tracked, the session-end hook runs the prompt-free quick cleanup. State lives in `<home>/disk-cleanup/`: `tracked.json` (with `.bak` and `.tmp`), and the audit log `cleanup.log`. Only paths under the home or `icebath-*` entries of the temp directory are ever eligible.

#### Hooks and the `/disk-cleanup` slash command

- `plugin.go` — `pre_tool_call` snapshot of absent argument paths (1 h TTL), `post_tool_call` tracking, `on_session_end` quick cleanup when a test file was tracked; `/disk-cleanup status|dry-run|quick|deep|track <path> <category>|forget <path>`
- `log.go` — package logger named `disk-cleanup`

#### Tracking store, categories and deletion rules

- `library.go` — categories temp, test, research, download, chrome-profile, cron-output, other; auto-delete rules (test always, temp after 7 days, cron-output after 14), prompt-only buckets (research after 30 days, chrome profile after 14, files over 500 MB); never-track and protected top-level home entries; cron control files protected; test files inside a git worktree skipped; empty-directory sweep

### `pkg/builtin/googlemeet` — Google Meet bot: join a call, scrape captions, optionally speak, locally or on a remote node

*19 files, 4,513 Go lines*

Bundled plugin `google_meet` for Linux and macOS, opt-in through `plugins.enabled`. It adds five tools in toolset `google_meet`, the `icebath meet` command family and an `on_session_end` hook that leaves a running call. The bot is this same binary re-entered through a hidden first argument and drives a headless Chromium over CDP via `pkg/browser`; all per-meeting state is files under `<home>/workspace/meetings/`. Realtime speech needs an OpenAI Realtime key (`ICEBATH_MEET_REALTIME_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY`) and a virtual audio device (PulseAudio `pactl` on Linux, BlackHole plus `ffmpeg` on macOS). Fifteen of eighteen Go files import `internal/py*`, largely for Python exception text in tool results.

#### Plugin registration and model tools

- `plugin.go` — manifest (version 0.2.0), registers the tools, the `meet` CLI and the session-end hook; skips registration on other platforms
- `tools.go` — schemas and handlers of `meet_join` (url, mode transcribe or realtime, guest_name, duration, headed, node), `meet_status`, `meet_transcript` (last), `meet_leave`, `meet_say`; node resolution with `auto` meaning the sole registered node
- `pyexc.go` — [py-shim] `KeyError`, `ValueError`, `TypeError`, `AttributeError`, `OverflowError` types so tool errors carry the Python class names
- `jsonfile.go` — tolerant JSON file read and the cross-process lock on `say_queue.jsonl` (10 s timeout)
- `log.go` — package logger named `google_meet`

#### Bot process lifecycle on the local machine

Exactly one meeting is active per home, named by `.active.json`. Each meeting directory holds `transcript.txt`, `status.json`, `bot.log`, and in realtime mode `say_queue.jsonl`, `say_processed.jsonl` and `speaker.pcm`.

- `process_manager.go` — start (refuses non-Meet URLs, stops a running bot first, passes options as `ICEBATH_MEET_*` env), status merged with `status.json`, transcript tail, say enqueue (realtime only), stop with SIGTERM then SIGKILL after 10 s
- `spawn_{unix,windows}.go` — detached child process attributes and signal delivery per OS

#### The bot itself: Meet page automation and caption scraping

- `meet_bot.go` — hidden entry `__icebath_google_meet_bot__` dispatched from `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go`; URL allowlist regex, guest join or ask-to-join, lobby timeout (`ICEBATH_MEET_LOBBY_TIMEOUT`, 300 s), caption observer injected into the page, de-duplicated transcript lines, duration auto-leave, barge-in cancel when a human speaks
- `meet_page.go` — minimal Playwright-like page and locator layer over raw CDP: launch Chromium, isolated context with viewport, user agent, permissions and saved storage state, role and CSS locators, click and fill

#### Realtime speech path

- `realtime_openai_client.go` — websocket client for `wss://api.openai.com/v1/realtime` (session update, speak text, cancel response, PCM written to a sink file) and the speaker loop draining the say queue one entry at a time
- `audio_bridge.go` — virtual microphone: on Linux a `pactl` null sink plus virtual source, torn down in reverse; on macOS a check that BlackHole 2ch is installed

#### `icebath meet` CLI

- `cli.go` — `meet setup` (preflight), `install [--realtime] [--yes]` (pm-managed Chromium, then `apt-get` or `brew` audio tools after a prompt), `auth` (headed Google sign-in saved to `auth.json`), `join`, `status`, `transcript [--last]`, `say`, `stop`

#### Remote node host

[partial] Lets the gateway run the bot on another machine over a token-authenticated websocket (default port 18789). The server's `start_bot` whitelist drops the `mode` and realtime options the client sends, so a node-hosted bot always runs transcribe-only and node `say` writes a queue nothing drains.

- `node_protocol.go` — JSON envelopes (request, response, error) with shared token and correlation id; request validation
- `node_server.go` — hand-rolled RFC 6455 server; RPCs `ping`, `start_bot`, `stop`, `status`, `transcript`, `say`; 32-hex token minted into `node_token.json` owner-only
- `node_client.go` — gateway-side client opening one short-lived websocket per call
- `node_registry.go` — approved nodes (name, url, token) in `nodes.json`
- `node_cli.go` — `icebath meet node run|list|approve <name> <url> <token>|remove|status|ping`

#### Unregistered skill document

- `SKILL.md` — [data][unwired] skill text for the plugin (modes, locations, prerequisites); not embedded and never passed to `RegisterSkill`, and the bundled plugin tree ships only `plugin.yaml`

### `pkg/builtin/langfuse` — catalog port tracing turns, model calls, tools and subagents to Langfuse

*10 files, 3,982 Go lines*

Active once `icebath plugins install langfuse` lands it. It is a hook-only observer: no tools or commands. One client per profile home exports OpenTelemetry spans over OTLP HTTP to the Langfuse endpoint (default `https://cloud.langfuse.com`) and uploads media separately; `AtExit` is registered in `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go` to end open traces and flush. Credentials are `ICEBATH_LANGFUSE_PUBLIC_KEY` and `ICEBATH_LANGFUSE_SECRET_KEY` (standard `LANGFUSE_*` names accepted as fallback), plus `BASE_URL`, `ENV`, `RELEASE`, `SAMPLE_RATE`; missing or placeholder keys disable tracing with one warning. Telemetry failures are swallowed so they never block a turn.

#### Plugin registration, hook handlers and trace state

- `plugin.go` — registers eleven hooks (`pre_api_request`, `post_api_request`, `api_request_error`, `pre_llm_call`, `post_llm_call`, `pre_tool_call`, `post_tool_call`, `on_session_finalize`, `on_session_end`, `subagent_start`, `subagent_stop`); `AtExit` finalizer
- `hooks.go` — the handlers: open or reuse a turn root, one generation per model request, tool and subagent observations, error marking, one generation per mixture-of-agents advisor
- `state.go` — per-turn trace state keyed by task and session with an ordered map, root tags (platform, `trigger:cron`, `cron-job:<id>`), child start and end, finalize-all at exit
- `log.go` — package logger named `langfuse`

#### Client and OpenTelemetry export

- `client.go` — builds and caches one client per profile; refuses template-looking keys, and keys without `pk-lf-` or `sk-lf-` prefixes on langfuse.com hosts (elsewhere a wrong prefix only warns)
- `sdk.go` — a Go stand-in for the Langfuse SDK: tracer provider, OTLP exporter, `langfuse.*` span attributes for traces and observations, propagated user and session ids, flush and shutdown; honours `LANGFUSE_FLUSH_AT`, `LANGFUSE_TIMEOUT`, `LANGFUSE_TRACING_ENABLED` and related variables

#### Payload capture, redaction, media and cost

- `capture.go` — capture mode `ICEBATH_LANGFUSE_CAPTURE` (metadata, sanitized default, full), forced secret redaction, truncation (`ICEBATH_LANGFUSE_MAX_CHARS` 12000, `MAX_DEPTH` 4), message and tool-call serialization; opt-in sender attribution via `plugins.entries.langfuse.settings`
- `media.go` — finds base64 data URIs in traced values, uploads them through the Langfuse media API from background workers with backoff, replaces them with media references before export
- `usage.go` — maps canonical token usage to Langfuse usage buckets (reasoning split from output) and computes cost from the provider rate card, including tiered rates
- `values.go` — [py-shim] Python dict, list, `getattr` and truthiness helpers over hook arguments

### `pkg/builtin/mcpserveplugin` — catalog port that adds `icebath mcp-serve`

*1 file, 43 Go lines*

Wrapper over `pkg/mcpserve`: once `icebath plugins install mcp-serve` lands it, the command runs icebath as a stdio MCP server that exposes conversations and, with `--tools`, the web, browser, vision, image generation, skills and TTS tools.

#### Plugin registration and command handler

- `plugin.go` — registers `mcp-serve` and passes the `--verbose`, `--tools` and `--accept-hooks` flags to `mcpserve.RunServer`

### `pkg/builtin/securityguidance` — warns or blocks when a file write contains known-dangerous code patterns

*3 files, 303 Go lines*

Bundled plugin `security-guidance` (opt-in through `plugins.enabled`). It scans the content arguments of `write_file`, `patch` and `skill_manage` against 25 rules forked from Anthropic's Claude plugin (Apache-2.0). Default is warn mode: the write happens and a markdown warning block is appended to the tool result. `SECURITY_GUIDANCE_BLOCK` switches to refusing the write in `pre_tool_call`; `SECURITY_GUIDANCE_DISABLE` turns scanning off. Content over 256 KiB is not scanned.

#### Hooks and rule table

- `plugin.go` — rule compilation and matching, warning block format, `pre_tool_call` block mode, `transform_tool_result` warn mode that leaves error results alone
- `patterns.go` — the rule table: GitHub Actions workflow injection, `eval`, `new Function`, `child_process.exec`, `innerHTML` family, pickle and other unsafe deserialization, `os.system`, shell subprocess, unsafe YAML load, ECB, disabled TLS verification, XXE, missing SRI, unsafe `torch.load`
- `log.go` — package logger named `security-guidance`

### `pkg/builtin/spotify` — catalog port with seven Spotify Web API tools and `icebath spotify`

*5 files, 1,422 Go lines*

Active once `icebath plugins install spotify` lands it. The tools appear only when the profile holds a Spotify login; login itself (loopback PKCE with the user's own Spotify app, token refresh, storage) is implemented in `pkg/provider` and only driven from here. All five files import `internal/py*`.

#### Plugin registration, schemas and login command

- `plugin.go` — registers toolset `spotify` and the `spotify` CLI command
- `schemas.go` — schemas with their action enums: `spotify_playback` (11 actions), `spotify_devices`, `spotify_queue`, `spotify_search`, `spotify_playlists` (7 actions), `spotify_albums`, `spotify_library`
- `cli.go` — `icebath spotify [login|status|logout]` with `--client-id` (or `ICEBATH_SPOTIFY_CLIENT_ID`), `--redirect-uri`, `--scope`, `--no-browser`, `--timeout`

#### Web API client and tool handlers

- `client.go` — request helper with one refresh-and-retry on 401, empty-body handling, friendly error mapping, Spotify id and URI normalization from URLs
- `tools.go` — per-action dispatch for all seven tools, argument coercion, paging limits, error rendering

### `pkg/builtin/teamspipeline` — Microsoft Teams meeting pipeline: Graph notification to transcript to summary to sinks

*9 files, 4,057 Go lines*

Bundled plugin `teams_pipeline` (opt-in through `plugins.enabled`). When the gateway runs the `msgraph_webhook` adapter and `plugins.enabled` lists `teams_pipeline`, `BindGatewayRuntime` (installed by `cmd/icebath/link_plugins.go` into `gatewayrun.BindTeamsPipelineRuntime`) attaches a pipeline that turns Graph change notifications into durable jobs. Its only user surface is the operator command `icebath teams-pipeline`. It talks to Microsoft Graph (`MSGRAPH_TENANT_ID`, `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_ID`, `MSGRAPH_CLIENT_SECRET`), the Notion and Linear APIs, the speech-to-text stack in `pkg/media`, an auxiliary model, and `ffmpeg`; state is one JSON file, `<home>/teams_pipeline_store.json` (override `MSGRAPH_WEBHOOK_STORE_PATH`).

#### Plugin registration and gateway binding

- `plugin.go` — manifest and registration of the `teams-pipeline` CLI command
- `runtime.go` — builds pipeline config from `teams.extra.meeting_pipeline` with Teams delivery targets mirrored in, constructs enabled Notion, Linear and Teams sinks, binds the notification scheduler to the Graph webhook adapter
- `log.go` — package logger named `teams_pipeline`

#### Data model and durable store

- `models.go` — `GraphSubscription`, `TeamsMeetingRef`, `MeetingArtifact`, `TeamsMeetingSummaryPayload`, `TeamsMeetingPipelineJob` with snake and camel case dict conversion
- `store.go` — buckets `subscriptions`, `notification_receipts`, `event_timestamps`, `jobs`, `sink_records`; atomic temp-file replace; notification receipt keys for de-duplication

#### Pipeline run and output sinks

[partial] A retryable failure is stored as `retry_scheduled`, which is treated as terminal; nothing reruns such a job except the operator `run` command.

- `pipeline.go` — job creation with dedupe key, resolve meeting, prefer transcript else transcribe the recording (audio extracted with `ffmpeg`), model summary with a heuristic fallback, sinks in Notion, Linear, Teams order with stored sink records
- `meetings.go` — Graph helpers: parse meeting, transcript and recording ids from resources, organizer-scoped lookup, list and download artifacts, choose the best transcript, enrich from call records

#### Graph subscriptions and operator CLI

- `subscriptions.go` — Graph client from environment credentials, subscription record sync, renewal of managed subscriptions near expiry (`MSGRAPH_WEBHOOK_CLIENT_STATE` marks ownership)
- `cli.go` — `teams-pipeline list|show|run|fetch|subscriptions|subscribe|renew-subscription|delete-subscription|maintain-subscriptions|token-health|validate`, with aliases `ls`, `replay`, `test`, `subs`, `token`

### `pkg/builtin/webbackends` — registers the eleven bundled web search and extract backends as plugins

*1 file, 55 Go lines*

Each backend is a bundled `backend`-kind plugin keyed `web/<dir>`, so it loads without `plugins.enabled`. The provider implementations themselves live in `pkg/tools`; this package only wraps their constructors.

#### Backend plugin table

- `plugin.go` — table of `brave_free`, `ddgs`, `exa`, `firecrawl`, `keenable`, `openai_native`, `parallel`, `perplexity`, `searxng`, `tavily`, `xai` with descriptions naming each required key or URL; registers each into the web search provider registry

### `pkg/skills` — the skills subsystem: discovery, prompt index, model tools, slash commands, bundled sync, telemetry, hub and scanner

*66 files, 24,747 Go lines*

Owns everything about skills for one profile home, always through a `Scope` (home, config, platform, cwd). A skill is a directory with `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter plus markdown) and optional `references/`, `templates/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`. The package registers three model tools at init (`skills_list`, `skill_view`, `skill_manage`, toolset `skills`), builds the `<available_skills>` block of the system prompt, turns skills into slash commands, seeds bundled skills from the embedded archive, and implements the hub and the `icebath skills` and `icebath bundles` commands (bound in `pkg/commands/cli_tree_skills_hub.go` and `cli_tree_bundles.go`, mirrored by `pkg/tuiserver`). On disk it owns, under `<home>/skills/`: `.bundled_manifest`, `.usage.json`, `.archive/`, `.curator_suppressed`, `.curator_ledger.jsonl`, `.locks/`, `.hub/` (`lock.json`, `taps.json`, `audit.log`, `quarantine/`, `index-cache/`, `scan-cache/`); and under the home: `.skills_prompt_snapshot.json`, `.no-bundled-skills`, `.curator_backups/blobs/`, `skill-bundles/`, `cache/osv_check.json`, plus the `skills.*` block of `config.yaml`. Lower and higher packages are reached through hooks installed at init (`RegisterPluginSkillHost`, `RegisterCoreCommandResolver`, `RegisterStablePrefixSink`, `RegisterSecretResolver`, `RegisterCronBlueprintHooks`, `RegisterLifecycleDispatch`). 36 of 61 Go files import `internal/py*`; result objects, error text and sort orders are kept Python-exact throughout.

#### Embedded skill archives and shipped index

The source trees `bundled/` and `optional/` are mapped elsewhere; these are their packed forms, the code that embeds them, and the offline hub index.

- `embed.go` — embeds both archives and exposes `BundledFS` and `OptionalFS`; `go:generate` lines for `cmd/packtree`
- `embed_modes.go` — table of the 38 embedded files that must be executable when copied to disk; repeats the non-0644 rows of the two manifests
- `bundled.tar.zst` — [data] the default skills seeded into every home
- `optional.tar.zst` — [data] the official optional skills, installed on demand through the hub's `official` source
- `bundled_manifest.txt`, `optional_manifest.txt` — [data] packer output (path, sha256, mode; 301 and 825 lines); not embedded and read by no Go code
- `skills-index.json.zst` — [data] 7.5 MB snapshot of the central skills index, embedded by `hub_search.go` as the fallback when the network index and its cache are unavailable

#### Scope, config access and frontmatter parsing

Frontmatter keys the code reads: `name`, `description`, `platforms` (macos, linux, windows), `environments` (kanban, docker, s6), `requires_apps`, `deps`, `required_environment_variables`, `required_credential_files`, `setup` (`help`, `collect_secrets`), `prerequisites.env_vars`, `compatibility`, `tags`, `author`, and under `metadata.icebath` (legacy spelling `metadata.hermes` still accepted): `tags`, `related_skills`, `requires_toolsets`, `fallback_for_toolsets`, `requires_tools`, `fallback_for_tools`, `session_platforms`, `config`, `blueprint`, `upstream`.

- `scope.go` — `Scope` and its constructors from a home or a tool environment; platform from `ICEBATH_PLATFORM` or `ICEBATH_SESSION_PLATFORM`; skills directory override; JSON result helpers
- `rawconfig.go` — raw `config.yaml` read through a cache keyed by path and config backend version; external-dirs cache
- `yamlfm.go` — `ParseFrontmatter` with YAML 1.1 scalar rules and a key-value line fallback on bad YAML; typed accessors; the `icebath` then `hermes` metadata lookup
- `log.go` — package logger named `skills`

#### Skill roots, precedence and gating

Roots in precedence order: trusted project dirs (`.icebath/skills`, `.agents/skills` under the git root, only when listed in `skills.trusted_project_dirs` and `skills.project_discovery` is not false), the home skills dir, `skills.create_dir`, then `skills.external_dirs`. A same-tier name collision between different content is refused as ambiguous. Skills are hidden by OS, by environment, by missing apps, by `skills.disabled` and `skills.platform_disabled`; `icebath-agent` can never be disabled. Conditional rows: `session_platforms` must contain the session platform; a `fallback_for_*` skill is hidden when the named tool or toolset is available; a `requires_*` skill is hidden when it is not.

- `skillutil.go` — root tiers, candidate ranking and ambiguity, platform, environment (container, s6, kanban) and app gates, disabled sets, project root detection and trust, quarantine of project skills that scan dangerous, config variable declarations and resolution under `skills.config`, description clipping to 60 characters, symlink-following tree walk
- `catalog.go` — scanned skill catalog cached 30 s per scope behind a directory change signature (depth 6); category from path; `FindAllSkills` and sort order
- `catalog_kanban_scoped.go` — catalog listing with kanban-only skills forced relevant for one scan, used by the gateway's local skill inventory for chat clients
- `excluded_path.go`, `index_files.go` — exported wrappers over the excluded-path test and the sorted `SKILL.md` walk; `SwapWalkReadDir` is a test seam
- `detect_kanban_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] exported `DetectKanban`; no caller

#### Skills index in the system prompt

The index is a category-grouped list of `name: description` rows inside `<available_skills>`, with mandatory-load guidance (softer wording for single-query sessions), `[project]` labels, `[names only]` categories outside the coding context, and conditional rows filtered by available tools and toolsets. Plugin skills are appended as `plugin:name` rows.

- `index.go` — `BuildSkillsSystemPrompt`: in-process LRU (32 entries) and the disk snapshot `.skills_prompt_snapshot.json` (version 5, validated by a file manifest of every `SKILL.md` and `DESCRIPTION.md`); empty under a safe worker
- `index_delta.go` — `SkillsIndexNotes`: compares the index in the stored system prompt with the live one and stages a `[System: ...]` note naming added and removed skills for the next turn (and an "accurate again" note on reversal); skipped for provider `moa` and the Codex app server

#### Read tools: `skills_list` and `skill_view`

`skill_view(name, file_path?)` returns `SKILL.md` content, tags, related skills, `linked_files`, a readiness status (`available`, `setup_needed`, `unsupported`), and installs declared `deps` through `pkg/pm`. A repeat view of unchanged content in one task returns a short stub (200 digests per task). Successful views bump usage counters.

- `tools.go` — schemas and handlers of `skills_list(category?)` and `skill_view`; tool registration
- `view.go` — listing, lookup across roots and plugin namespaces, path-escape and disabled checks, prompt-injection phrase warnings, linked-file serving, required env var capture through a secret prompt callback, env passthrough and credential file registration for sandboxes, setup notes, view de-duplication
- `preprocess.go`, `preprocess_{unix,windows}.go` — `${ICEBATH_SKILL_DIR}` and `${ICEBATH_SESSION_ID}` substitution (`skills.template_vars`), and opt-in inline shell expansion of `` !`cmd` `` (`skills.inline_shell`, 10 s default, 4000 characters, never for community hub skills); per-OS child handling
- `secret_capture_context.go` — process-wide secret capture callback that resolves its session from the calling context

#### Write tool: `skill_manage` and its guards

`skill_manage(operations[])` applies an ordered batch atomically; each op is `create`, `patch` (find and replace, or full rewrite), `write_file`, `remove_file` or `delete` (sole op, optional `absorbed_into`); the legacy flat single-action shape and `edit` are still accepted. Limits: 100,000 characters per `SKILL.md`, 1 MiB per support file, names of lowercase letters, digits, dots, hyphens and underscores. Writes pass the write-approval gate (may be staged as a pending approval and replayed), per-skill file locks, and record ledger and usage events.

- `manage.go` — validation, skill lookup with other-profile hints, the six action handlers, guarded atomic write with optional post-write scan (`skills.guard_agent_created`), approval gate and staged replay, locks under `.locks/`, tool schema and registration, lock queries for the terminal and file tools
- `manage_batch.go` — operations array: shape checks, snapshot of every touched skill, per-op dispatch, rollback of all touched skills on any failure
- `manage_guards.go` — delete-target validation (inside a root, not a link), pinned and essential guard, user-locked guard, background-review rules (read before write, delete only curator-managed skills, consolidation delete must name an umbrella)
- `provenance.go` — write origin on the session env (`foreground` or `background_review`), attended flag, the set of skill files the review fork has read
- `linter.go` — advisory lint attached to write results: name and directory match, description length and marketing words, missing metadata, oversized body, shell-utility references, missing "When to Use", incident-log shape, dangling references, forbidden files, references sprawl

#### Skill slash commands, invocation messages and auto-load

Every enabled skill becomes `/slug` unless a core command owns the name; plugin skills join on interactive surfaces. Several leading skill tokens can be stacked in one line. Invocation produces a scaffolded user message whose stable prefix is registered as a prompt-cache boundary, and whose markers are shared with the session store's preview SQL.

- `commands.go` — slugging, scaffold markers and parsers, payload loading through `skill_view`, missing and ambiguous labels, the `[Skill config ...]` block of resolved `skills.config` values
- `commands_scan.go` — per-scope command table with change signatures, plugin skill projection, reload diff, key resolution, single and stacked invocation messages, session preload prompt (CLI skills argument, gateway policy, kanban worker, TUI startup) and `skills.auto_load` prompt
- `commands_message.go` — message assembly: activation note, skill body, supporting file listing, setup note, runtime note, user instruction; multi-skill header
- `commands_message_export.go`, `commands_payload_export.go`, `inject_skill_config_export.go` — [port-artifact] one-line exported wrappers used by the agent lane and the cron prompt builder
- `core_command_resolver_export.go` — [test-support] swap hook for the core command lookup

#### Skill bundles

A bundle is a YAML file in `<home>/skill-bundles/` (override `ICEBATH_BUNDLES_DIR`) with `name`, `skills`, optional `description` and `instruction`; it becomes one slash command that loads all member skills.

- `bundles.go` — scan with content-signature cache, slug collisions resolved alphabetically, invocation message with loaded and missing members, create, delete and get
- `bundles_cli.go` — `icebath bundles list|show|create|delete|reload`

#### Blueprints: skills that carry a scheduled automation

- `blueprints.go` — parses `metadata.icebath.blueprint` (schedule, prompt, deliver, model, provider, toolsets, no_agent) into a cron job spec and offers it as a cron suggestion after a hub install; never schedules by itself

#### Bundled skill sync and preservation of user edits

`SyncSkills` runs at chat launch, gateway bootstrap, profile creation, self-install and container staging. Rules: a skill never offered before is copied; a tracked skill is updated only while its directory hash still equals the recorded origin hash, otherwise it is reported as user-modified and left alone; a skill the user deleted stays deleted; names provided by `external_dirs` or suppressed by the curator are skipped; `.no-bundled-skills` limits seeding to essentials.

- `sync.go` — manifest `.bundled_manifest` (name and origin MD5), copy with `.bak` rollback, rename recovery, category `DESCRIPTION.md` seeding, source override `ICEBATH_BUNDLED_SKILLS` and `ICEBATH_OPTIONAL_SKILLS`, reset, diff, list-modified, opt-out and pristine removal, official optional skill restore and lock backfill

#### Usage telemetry, lifecycle state and locks

`.usage.json` holds one record per skill: `created_by`, use, view and patch counts with timestamps, patch generation, `state` (active, stale, archived), `pinned`, `locked`, `archived_at`, `first_seen_at`. It feeds the curator in `pkg/memory` and the `on_skill_lifecycle` plugin hook.

- `usage.go` — record load, save and locked update; bump view, use and patch; provenance (hub, bundled, external, agent); curation eligibility; adopt, pin, lock; archive to `.archive/` and restore; suppression list `.curator_suppressed`; reports
- `usage_names_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported wrappers for bundled and hub-installed name sets
- `filelock_{unix,windows}.go` — exclusive lock file primitive: `flock` on Unix, first-byte lock with ten one-second attempts on Windows

#### Skill mutation ledger and rollback

- `ledger.go` — append-only `.curator_ledger.jsonl` of every skill mutation with before and after file manifests stored as content-addressed blobs; actor (agent, curator, user); size bound `skills.ledger_max_bytes` (5 MB) by compaction and oldest-first trim; blob GC after 1 h; list, get and rollback of an entry, used by the curator CLI

#### Hub core: state directory, lock file, taps and guarded HTTP

- `hub.go` — hub paths under `skills/.hub/`, SSRF-safe HTTP client with per-hop redirect checks and website blocklist, TTL file cache, `lock.json` provenance records (source, identifier, trust, verdict, content hash, install path, files, metadata, scan provenance, timestamps), `taps.json`, `audit.log`
- `hub_models.go` — `SkillMeta`, `SkillBundle`, the `SkillSource` interface, trust ranking (builtin, trusted, community), bundle and install path validation, allowed support dirs, cached JSON and text fetch helpers
- `hub_lock_export.go` — [port-artifact][unwired] lock entries keyed by identifier with ClawHub aliases; no caller

#### Hub sources and search

Nine adapters in priority order: `official`, `skills-index`, `skills-sh`, `well-known`, `url`, `github`, `clawhub`, `lobehub`, `browse-sh`. When the central index is available it answers unfiltered searches and the API sources are skipped; an index miss falls back to the registries except GitHub.

- `hub_search.go` — index from `https://icebath.app/api/skills-index.json` (6 h cache, stale cache, then the embedded copy), source router, parallel fan-out (8 workers, 30 s budget), trust-ranked de-duplicated results
- `hub_official.go` — `official` source over the embedded optional tree with a live-repo fallback and `metadata.icebath.upstream` pointers; `skills-index` source over the central index
- `hub_github.go` — credential chain (token, `gh` CLI, GitHub App, anonymous), default taps (OpenAI, Anthropic, HuggingFace, NVIDIA, W&B, Qdrant, Pinecone, gstack, two science collections) plus user taps, Contents and Trees API fetch, rate-limit handling, revision probe
- `hub_skillssh.go` — skills.sh search API, sitemap catalog, detail-page scraping (installs, audits), resolution to a GitHub bundle
- `hub_clawhub.go` — ClawHub registry at `clawhub.ai/api/v1`: search, catalog walk, version resolution, zip download and extraction
- `hub_sources.go` — `/.well-known/skills/index.json` domains, direct `SKILL.md` URLs with allowlisted support files, LobeHub agents converted to `SKILL.md`, the browse.sh catalog

#### Hub install, update check and uninstall

- `hub_install.go` — quarantine a bundle with path validation, refuse installs that nest in a skill or clobber a category, move from quarantine into the skills tree, record provenance, uninstall, compare content hashes and revisions for updates

#### Security scanning

Install policy by trust and verdict: builtin always allowed; trusted blocked only when dangerous; community allowed only when safe; `--force` overrides caution but never a dangerous verdict.

- `guard.go` — scanner `skills-guard-v10`: 134 regex threat patterns in twelve categories (exfiltration, injection, persistence, obfuscation, supply chain and more), invisible Unicode, structural limits (50 files, 5 MB), `.skillignore`, verdicts safe, caution, dangerous, attestation cached by content hash
- `guard_export.go` — [port-artifact] exported pattern lookup, binary-extension test and verdict function used by `pkg/plugins` install scanning
- `skillevaluator_scan.go` — optional advisory run of an external `skillevaluator` binary on quarantined installs (`skills.tier1_advisory`); silently unavailable when the binary is not on `PATH`
- `skills_ast_audit.go` — `audit --deep`: Python AST diagnostics (dynamic import, computed `getattr`, `__dict__` access) through `internal/pyast`
- `osv.go` — OSV malware lookup (`MAL-` advisories) for `npx`, `uvx` and `pipx` packages before an MCP server launch (called from `pkg/mcp`), cached in memory and `cache/osv_check.json` for 1 h (`OSV_ENDPOINT`, `OSV_CHECK_CACHE_TTL`)

#### `icebath skills` command family

- `hub_cli.go` — `browse`, `search`, `inspect` and their programmatic forms for the TUI; short-name and identifier resolution; prompts for name and category
- `hub_cli_install.go` — `install`: built-in shortcut, fetch, quarantine, scan, advisory, confirm, install, blueprint offer; blocked installs are logged and removed
- `hub_cli_manage.go` — [partial] `list`, `check`, `update` (reinstalls from the recorded source, skips locally edited skills unless `--force`), `audit [--deep]`, `uninstall`, `reset`, `list-modified`, `diff`, `opt-out`, `opt-in`, `repair-official`, `tap list|add|remove`, `snapshot export|import`, `publish` by GitHub fork and pull request; the `clawhub` publish target only prints a manual-submit link
- `skillsconfig.go` — `icebath skills config`: interactive enable and disable of skills globally or per platform, writing `skills.disabled` and `skills.platform_disabled`; skill config variables for `config show`
- `skills_trust_cli.go` — `icebath skills trust|untrust [path]`: edits `skills.trusted_project_dirs`

### `pkg/agentimport` — `icebath import-agent`: import another agent product's setup into a home

*14 files, 4,652 Go lines*

Imports from six sources: OpenClaw (delegated to the subpackage), Claude Code (`~/.claude`), Codex CLI (`~/.codex`), Cursor (`~/.cursor`), Grok Bot (a JSON export the bot writes about itself) and OpenBot (its SQLite database). Every run is preview first, then confirm, then apply; credentials are never imported and stripped secret names are listed. Conflicts are skipped unless `--overwrite`. No importer migrates conversation sessions or history. Entry points are `ImportAgent` and `Claw`, reached from the `agent-importers` plugin and from the setup wizard through `provider.AgentImportRunner`. It writes `config.yaml` (`mcp_servers`, `command_allowlist`, `approvals.deny`), `memories/MEMORY.md` and `USER.md`, `SOUL.md`, `skills/<agent>-imports/`, cron jobs, and `import-sync.json`.

#### Command flow and report

- `cli.go` — `ImportAgent`: agent auto-detection, flag ownership checks, settings summary, preview, confirmation (preview only when stdin is not a terminal), apply, grouped report, exit codes; `Claw` dispatch for `migrate` and `cleanup`
- `openclaw_hook.go` — registration slot through which the `openclaw` subpackage installs its `FindDirs`, `Migrate` and `Cleanup`, so this package does not import it
- `log.go` — package logger named `agentimport`

#### Claude Code, Codex and Cursor directory importer

Claude Code: `CLAUDE.md` into memory, `settings.json` allow and deny Bash rules into `command_allowlist` and `approvals.deny`, MCP servers from `~/.claude.json` and settings, `skills/`; slash commands are reported as not importable. Codex: `AGENTS.md`, `config.toml` MCP servers, `memories/*.md`, `skills/`. Cursor: `AGENTS.md`, `rules/**` (`.md`, `.mdc`), `mcp.json`, nested `skills/`.

- `importer.go` — shared item and report model, markdown-to-memory-entry extraction, de-duplicated merge into memory files within 20,000 characters with a timestamped `.bak`, MCP server translation with secret env stripping, skill directory copy with conflict rules
- `toml.go` — [py-shim] TOML parse that keeps document key order, standing in for Python `tomllib` dict ordering so imported MCP servers keep their order

#### Re-import of changed sources

- `sync.go` — `import-sync.json` per home: source path, content digest and per-skill digests; `--sync` re-imports sources whose digest changed and refreshes only imported skills the user has not edited

#### Grok Bot and OpenBot importers

Both normalize to "bots" with instructions, memories, user facts, skills, routines and apps. Instructions become `SOUL.md` only when it is empty or still the seeded default and one bot is imported, otherwise memory entries; scheduled routines become cron jobs created paused unless `--activate-routines`; event-triggered routines are written as notes under `<home>/<agent>-import/`; apps with a remote MCP URL become MCP servers.

- `grok_bot.go` — the export prompt text and format (`grok-bot-export` version 1), tolerant JSON extraction from files or chat replies, multi-file bot merge, refusal of documents carrying credential keys, secret redaction, the shared `BotImporter`
- `grok_bot_cache.go` — reads the Grok Bot desktop app's local cache to warn about bots and routines no export covered
- `grok_bot_input.go` — export discovery (`--source` file, folder, `-` for stdin, `~/Downloads`), printed instructions with the prompt saved to `grok-bot-import/export-prompt.txt`, clipboard and pasted-reply intake
- `paste_termios.go`, `paste_other.go`, `termios_{bsd,linux}.go` — reads a long pasted reply from a terminal with line mode off up to Ctrl-D and drains leftover input; plain read without termios elsewhere
- `openbot.go` — opens a private snapshot of `openbot.db`, reads agents, routines, memories and MCP servers from `projection_*` tables, converts OpenBot schedule objects (interval, custom, advanced) to cron expressions, collects workspace skill folders

### `pkg/agentimport/openclaw` — OpenClaw migration engine behind `import-agent openclaw` and `icebath claw`

*8 files, 5,077 Go lines*

A port of a standalone Python migration script, registered into `pkg/agentimport` at init. It migrates from `~/.openclaw` (legacy `~/.clawdbot`, `~/.moltbot`) across 35 selectable options in two presets (`full`, and `user-data` without the secret groups). Flow: warn if OpenClaw or the gateway is running, preview, confirm, zip backup of the home through `pkg/backup` (unless `--no-backup`), apply, then a redacted `report.json` and `summary.md` under `<home>/migration/openclaw/<timestamp>/`. Existing differing targets are conflicts unless `--overwrite`; a `config.yaml` conflict blocks later config writes; skill name conflicts follow `--skill-conflict skip|overwrite|rename`.

#### Commands: migrate and cleanup

[partial] Per-option `Include` and `Exclude` selection, a custom report directory and a JSON-only mode are implemented here but no CLI flag sets them, so only presets are reachable.

- `command.go` — `Migrate` (preflight process probes with `pgrep`, settings, preview, apply, next steps) and `Cleanup` (`claw cleanup`: renames leftover OpenClaw directories to `.pre-migration` after listing their state files)

#### Migration engine and option catalog

- `engine.go` — the 35 options and two presets, selection resolution, statuses (migrated, archived, skipped, conflict, error), YAML and `.env` file helpers, backup of overwritten files, brand rewording of imported text, memory entry extraction and merge
- `migrator.go` — the run: `SOUL.md`, workspace instructions, `MEMORY.md` and `USER.md` merge with overflow files (limits 2200 and 1375 characters), command allowlist, Telegram allowlist and working directory, Discord and Slack tokens and allowlists written to `.env` without the secrets flag, WhatsApp and Signal settings, the six allowlisted secrets and provider keys only with `--migrate-secrets`, default model, TTS, skills, daily memory, archive of unmapped docs
- `migrator_config.go` — config-derived steps: MCP servers, agent defaults, gateway, custom providers, extended channels, browser, tools and approvals into `config.yaml`; plugins, cron jobs, hooks, session settings, memory backend, skills registry, UI and logging archived for manual review; migration notes

#### Report and redaction

- `report.go` — item results, status summary, recursive redaction of secret-looking keys and values, `report.json` and `summary.md` writers

#### Python-semantics support

- `pyops.go` — [py-shim] Python exceptions carried by panic and recovered at entry points, dict and truthiness helpers over both JSON and YAML values; the migrator is written against these
- `xattr_{linux,other}.go` — [py-shim] copies extended attributes with file metadata on Linux as Python `shutil.copystat` does; no-op elsewhere

### `pkg/skills/bundled` — skills that ship active by default (44 skills, 302 files)

*302 files, 67 Go lines*

Source tree of the built-in skills. Each skill is a directory holding a `SKILL.md` (YAML frontmatter: `name`, `description` capped at 60 characters, `version`, `author`, `license`, `platforms` OS gate, `metadata.icebath.{tags,category,related_skills,config}`) plus optional `references/`, `scripts/`, `templates/`, `assets/` and `tests/` directories that the agent reads or runs through its own tools. `go generate ./pkg/skills/` packs this tree with `cmd/packtree` into `pkg/skills/bundled.tar.zst` and `bundled_manifest.txt`, which the binary embeds and syncs into `<home>/skills/` at startup (`pkg/skills/sync.go`). Nothing in this tree is Go product code except one plugin template; the scripts are Python, shell and JavaScript run by the agent at skill time, so they are payload, not part of the Python-port layer. Skill `tests/` directories are test payload and are not described.

#### Tree-level documents

- `AGENTS.md` — contributor guide for both skill trees: the two surfaces, frontmatter fields, the authoring standards (60-character description rule, native-tool wording, platform gating, section order, per-skill tests) and the curator lifecycle

### `pkg/skills/optional` — official skills that ship inactive (144 skills, 825 files)

*825 files*

They are packed into `pkg/skills/optional.tar.zst` and `optional_manifest.txt`, surfaced through the skills hub as the `official` source (`pkg/skills/hub_official.go`), and installed on demand with `icebath skills install official/<category>/<skill>`. They are the heavier, niche, paid-service or experimental skills.

- `DESCRIPTION.md` — explains what optional skills are, why they are not active by default and how the hub installs them
