## 12. Media, memory, tokenizers

### `pkg/mediacache` — per-home cache directories for inbound chat media: size cap, type sniffing, age-based cleanup

*4 files, 428 Go lines*

Owns the directories under the icebath home where media received from chat platforms is stored (`cache/images`, `cache/audio`, `cache/videos`, `cache/documents`, `cache/screenshots`) and the writers every platform adapter uses. Callers are `pkg/gateway` and its adapters (Slack, Telegram, Discord, WhatsApp, Signal, Feishu, WeCom, email, buzz), `pkg/acp`, `pkg/mcp`, `pkg/tuiserver`, `pkg/agent` and `pkg/media`. Eviction is by file age only: gateway housekeeping (`pkg/gatewayrun/run_housekeeping_disk_media.go`) calls the five cleanup functions hourly with the 24 hour constant; there is no size-based eviction, quota or index. Native Go apart from a Python-style `ValueError` type and a few `internal/py*` path and string helpers; fully wired.

#### Cache directories, inbound size cap and writers

Each media kind has a new subpath and a legacy directory name (`image_cache`, `audio_cache`, `video_cache`, `document_cache`, `browser_screenshots`); a populated legacy directory wins. Directories are created owner-only (0700) unless the install is a managed system.

- `cache.go` — directory resolution, `gateway.max_inbound_media_bytes` cap check, writers (`img_`/`audio_`/`video_<12hex><ext>` at 0600, `doc_<12hex>_<name>` with traversal refusal), image magic-byte check, per-kind age cleanup, accepted video and document MIME tables
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Audio container sniffing and voice-note transcode

Magic-byte detection so cached audio gets the extension of its real container, and the ffmpeg encode the gateway uses to turn audio into platform voice notes.

- `audio_container.go` — sniffs m4a/mp4 (ftyp brand), ogg, flac, mp3 (ID3 or frame sync), aac (ADTS), wav, webm; generic MP4 audio is named `.m4a`
- `transcode.go` — runs `ffmpeg` to mono Ogg Opus (libopus, voip, VBR, caller bitrate) with timeout, in-place safe; returns empty when ffmpeg is missing or the encode fails

### `pkg/media` — image and video generation, text to speech, speech to text, terminal voice mode and wake word

*81 files, 29,236 Go lines*

Owns five model-facing tools registered in `register.go`: `image_generate` (toolset `image_gen`), `video_generate`, `xai_video_edit`, `xai_video_extend` (toolset `video_gen`) and `text_to_speech` (toolset `tts`). Speech to text has no model tool; it is called by the gateway for inbound voice notes, Discord voice, the Teams pipeline, doctor and voice mode, and voice mode plus wake word are driven by `pkg/tuiserver` voice RPCs. Backends are chosen by the config sections `image_gen`, `video_gen`, `tts`, `stt`, `voice` and `wake_word`, and image, video, TTS and STT each also accept plugin providers through four scoped registries. Output lands in `<home>/cache/generated/{images,videos}` and `<home>/cache/audio`; ffmpeg and ffprobe are found on PATH and used for Opus conversion, STT transcoding, silence trimming, splitting and playback. Piper and sherpa keyword spotting run natively through `pkg/internal/sherpaonnx`, while NeuTTS, KittenTTS, faster-whisper and SILK decoding run embedded Python scripts in the `pkg/pm` managed interpreter; voice mode, wake word, live STT and the speaker pipeline are compiled out of the `icebath_core` and `icebath_noextras` builds. Port residue is heavy (SDK-shaped OpenAI and FAL clients, Python exception classes as error types, function-variable seams); there is no vision or image-analysis code here (that tool is `pkg/tools/vision.go`) and no Kokoro engine.

#### Tool registration, picker bridge and shared helpers

Package wiring plus the HTTP, config and cache helpers every backend shares.

- `register.go` — init registering the five tools and the plugin provider kinds `image_gen_provider`, `video_gen_provider`, `tts_provider`, `transcription_provider`
- `tools_config_bridge.go` — installs hooks into `pkg/tools` so the tools picker can read STT model catalogs, Piper voices, FAL and DeepInfra models and the image, video and TTS registries
- `common.go` — config section and scalar coercion, env, home and secret lookup, JSON POST and GET with idle-read timeout and transport failure classification, `UserAgent` `Icebath-Agent/1.0`
- `log.go` — package logger
- `provider_media.go` — writes generated media to `<home>/cache/<kind>/<prefix>_<timestamp>_<hex>.<ext>`; URL downloads are SSRF-checked on every redirect hop (max 5), size-capped and leave no partial file
- `deepinfra.go` — DeepInfra base URL (`base_url`, `DEEPINFRA_BASE_URL`, default) and live model catalog by surface tag, cached per base URL and key with a 60 second negative cache
- `xai_http.go` — xAI Imagine storage options from `<section>.xai.storage.{enabled,public_url,expires_after}` (30 day cap) and the once-per-home billing notice marker in `<home>/state/`

#### Image generation: tool, provider contract and dispatch

The `image_generate` tool takes `prompt` and `aspect_ratio` (landscape, square, portrait) and, when the active backend declares the capability, `image_url`, `reference_image_urls`, `upscale` and creative controls. `image_gen.provider` picks a registered provider; unset or `fal` uses the in-tree FAL pipeline.

- `imagegen_dispatch.go` — tool handler and capability-driven dynamic schema; routes to the plugin provider or FAL; under a non-local terminal backend resolves local source paths to data URLs and adds `host_image` and `agent_visible_image`
- `imagegen_provider.go` — `ImageGenProvider` interface and request type, registry lookup and active provider resolution, aspect normalization, result envelopes, base64 and URL saving (25 MiB cap), adapter for plugin-host providers
- `imagegen_plugin_common.go` — shared backend helpers: gpt-image-2 low, medium, high tiers, model precedence (argument, env var, `image_gen.<provider>.model`, `image_gen.model`, default), one-key setup schema, source image collection, cache materialization, token usage recording
- `save_url_image_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the image URL downloader with 60 second and 25 MiB defaults for `pkg/pet/generate`

#### FAL image pipeline (default image backend)

Queue submit and poll against FAL with user-interrupt checks, per-model payload shaping from a static catalog, edit endpoints with reference images and an optional Clarity upscale pass. Needs `FAL_KEY` (or `FAL_KEY_ID` and `FAL_KEY_SECRET`).

- `imagegen_tool.go` — builds text and edit payloads from catalog whitelists, submits with an idempotency key, waits while polling the interrupt flag, optional `fal-ai/clarity-upscaler`, inlines local sources, `IMAGE_TOOLS_DEBUG` session, no-backend setup message
- `imagegen_catalog.go` — [data] 26 FAL image models (FLUX 2, Z-Image, Nano Banana, GPT Image, Ideogram, Recraft, Qwen, Krea, Seedream, MAI, Grok Imagine, Kling, Muse) with sizes, defaults, allowed keys and edit endpoints; default `fal-ai/flux-2/klein/9b`
- `imagegen_shrink.go` — [py-shim] Pillow stand-in (decode incl. WebP, TIFF, AVIF, HEIC, EXIF transpose, bicubic thumbnail, bomb guard) that re-encodes a data URL until it fits the request budget; used only by FAL source inlining
- `fal_common.go` — [py-shim] stand-in for the Python `fal_client` SDK: key auth, `https://queue.fal.run/` (or `FAL_RUN_HOST`) submit, status events, result fetch, jittered retry on 408, 409, 429 and non-JSON 502 to 504; used by FAL image and video
- `imagegen_plugin_fal.go` — wraps the pipeline as the bundled `fal` provider and defines the bundled image backend plugin type (manifest key `image_gen/<name>`) all backends register through

#### Other bundled image backends

Each file registers one bundled provider in init and implements availability (through the profile secret scope), model listing, capabilities and generate.

- `imagegen_plugin_openai.go` — `openai`: images.generate and images.edit for gpt-image-2 tiers and GPT Image 2.5 Flare and Sunburst; `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_IMAGE_MODEL`, config base URL or a named custom endpoint
- `imagegen_plugin_openai_codex.go` — `openai-codex`: gpt-image-2 through ChatGPT/Codex OAuth credentials instead of an API key; normalizes input images to checked data URLs
- `imagegen_plugin_openrouter.go` — `openrouter`: chat-completions image output plus the dedicated Image API, live catalog, per-model aspect, resolution, quality, seed knobs, up to 16 references, model fallback chain; `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`
- `imagegen_plugin_xai.go` — `xai`: grok-imagine-image, 2.0 and quality models with live catalog merge, edit model fallback, resolution choice, xAI storage options; credentials from the shared xAI resolver (`XAI_API_KEY` or OAuth)
- `imagegen_plugin_krea.go` — `krea`: Krea 3 (generate and edit) and Krea 2 Medium, Large, Medium Turbo via `https://api.krea.ai` job submit and poll, style references, creativity, optional enhance upscale; `KREA_API_KEY`
- `imagegen_plugin_meta.go` — `meta-ai-image-gen`: Meta Model API `muse-image-1.0` over OpenAI-compatible images.generate; `META_MODEL_API_KEY` aliases, `META_BASE_URL`, `META_IMAGE_MODEL`
- `imagegen_plugin_deepinfra.go` — `deepinfra`: OpenAI-compatible images.generations over the live image-gen catalog with price rows; `DEEPINFRA_API_KEY`, `DEEPINFRA_IMAGE_MODEL`
- `openai_images.go` — [py-shim] stand-in for the `openai` SDK client: env-resolved key, org, project and base URL, JSON generate and multipart edit, SDK retry and error classes; used by the OpenAI, DeepInfra and Meta image backends and the shared videos provider

#### Video generation

`video_generate` takes prompt, duration, aspect ratio (eight ratios, default 16:9) and resolution (480p to 1080p, default 720p), with image and reference inputs added per provider capability; `video_gen.provider` and `video_gen.model` select the backend. `xai_video_edit` and `xai_video_extend` appear only when the profile's video provider is xAI with credentials. Videos download into `<home>/cache/generated/videos` with a 180 second and 200 MB default cap.

- `videogen_tool.go` — handlers and dynamic schemas for the three video tools, plugin discovery refresh before provider resolution, argument coercion, missing-provider message
- `videogen_provider.go` — `VideoGenProvider` interface and request type, registry and active provider lookup, envelopes, video saving, the shared OpenAI-videos-API provider (create, poll, download), plugin-host adapter, bundled video backend plugin type
- `videogen_plugin_fal.go` — `fal`: 20 model families (LTX, Pixverse, Seedance, Veo 3.1, MiniMax H3, FLUX 3, Grok Imagine, Gemini Omni, Kling, Wan, Happy Horse) with text and image endpoints, duration clamping; default `pixverse-v6`; `FAL_VIDEO_MODEL`
- `videogen_plugin_openrouter.go` — `openrouter`: every generative model on `/videos` with live catalog, nearest-supported duration, resolution and aspect, job poll and content download; offline fallback catalog, default `minimax/hailuo-3-max`
- `videogen_plugin_xai.go` — `xai`: Grok Imagine text, image and reference to video, plus edit and extend of a stored public video URL; local media inlined as base64 after the read guard; storage options
- `videogen_plugin_deepinfra.go` — `deepinfra`: the shared OpenAI-videos provider pointed at DeepInfra with the live video-gen catalog as picker rows
- `openai_videos.go` — [py-shim] `openai` SDK videos surface (create, retrieve, download content) with getattr-style job attribute access; used by the shared OpenAI-videos provider

#### text_to_speech tool, chunking and platform delivery

`tts.provider` (default `edge`) selects a built-in engine, a command provider under `tts.providers.<name>` or a plugin; a caller-supplied provider that disagrees with config is ignored. Text over the provider cap is split at sentence boundaries into ordered chunks; results come back as `MEDIA:<path>` lines, prefixed `[[audio_as_voice]]` when the file is Ogg Opus for a voice-bubble platform (telegram, matrix, feishu, whatsapp, signal). The schema text promises `~/voice-memos/` in CLI mode but no code writes there; the default is `<home>/cache/audio/tts_<stamp>.<ext>`.

- `tts_tool.go` — tool schema (text, output_path, speed, instructions; `voice_id` and `find_voices` when ElevenLabs is configured), built-in dispatch table, output path safety checks, per-provider availability, chunk synthesis loop, error envelopes
- `tts_tool_delivery.go` — per-provider and per-ElevenLabs-model character caps, sentence splitting, platform upload profiles (`tts.delivery_profiles`, Discord 10 MB, Telegram 50 MB, 0.85 safety), ffmpeg Opus conversion, Ogg repair, concat, PCM-to-WAV wrapping
- `tts_elevenlabs_voices.go` — `find_voices` argument: paginated search of the ElevenLabs shared library or account voices with filters and compact rows
- `tts_config_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the `tts` config section loader for the gateway streaming consumer

#### Cloud TTS engines

Eight hosted engines behind the built-in dispatch table; the REST engines read responses through a 16 MiB bounded, idle-timed body and write one audio file per chunk.

- `tts_tool_providers.go` — Edge (default voice `en-US-AriaNeural`), ElevenLabs, xAI (speech tags, speed clamp), MiniMax (global and CN endpoints), Mistral Voxtral, Gemini (persona prompt, audio tags rewritten by an auxiliary model); key resolution, managed interpreter command
- `tts_tool_openai.go` — OpenAI audio.speech (default `gpt-4o-mini-tts`, voice `alloy`, `tts.openai.api_key` or `VOICE_TOOLS_OPENAI_KEY`/`OPENAI_API_KEY`, instructions passthrough, two retries) and DeepInfra TTS through the same client

#### Local TTS engines and model lifecycle

Piper is native; NeuTTS and KittenTTS run Python in the managed interpreter and need the matching `pm` extra. Loaded models are held in small LRU caches and kept warm while voice mode holds a lease.

- `tts_tool_local.go` — NeuTTS one-shot script (default `neuphonic/neutts-air-q4-gguf`, reference voice sample), KittenTTS long-lived worker (default `KittenML/kitten-tts-nano-0.8-int8`, voice `Jasper`), Piper synthesis (default `en_US-lessac-medium` or an `.onnx` path), model LRU caches
- `neutts_samples/jo.wav`, `neutts_samples/jo.txt` — [data] embedded NeuTTS reference voice and its transcript, materialized to `<home>/cache/neutts_samples`
- `tts_tool_lifecycle.go` — warm and release of local models and plugin providers, named TTS leases, `tts.keep_warm_seconds` (default 60) delay before unloading after the last lease

#### Command and plugin TTS providers

User-declared shell command providers and the plugin provider contract, both reachable when `tts.provider` names something that is not built in.

- `tts_command_provider.go` — `tts.providers.<name>.command` template with shell-quote-aware `{input_path}`, `{output_path}`, `{format}`, `{voice}`, `{model}`, `{speed}`; runs in a process group with idle timeout (120 s default), tree kill, env passthrough, `voice_compatible` opt-in
- `tts_command_provider_{other,windows}.go` — per-OS spawn flags: Win32 creation flags and hidden console on Windows, no-ops elsewhere
- `tts_provider.go` — `TTSProvider` interface (synthesize, optional stream, warm, release, voices, PCM streaming opt-in), embeddable defaults, adapter proxying a plugin-host provider object
- `tts_registry.go` — TTS provider registry with the eleven reserved built-in names (edge, elevenlabs, openai, minimax, xai, mistral, gemini, neutts, kittentts, piper, deepinfra)
- `tts_tool_plugins.go` — plugin routing: discovery with one forced retry, voice, model and speed options, panic-to-error isolation, voice-compatibility and availability probes

#### Streaming TTS and speaker playback

Speaks a reply while the model is still streaming it: deltas are cut into sentences, each sentence is synthesized as PCM chunks by a streaming-capable provider (or per-sentence files otherwise) and played in order. Used by terminal voice mode and by the gateway streaming TTS consumer.

- `tts_sentence_chunker.go` — cuts streamed text into sentences, drops think blocks, merges fragments shorter than `tts.streaming.min_len` (default 20)
- `speak_stream_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the chunker's held-back buffer and the 20 second live-STT finalize timeout
- `tts_streaming.go` — two-minute latch recording that the user barged in on a spoken reply
- `tts_streaming_providers.go` — streamer registry and resolution (`tts.streaming.provider`, `auto` order elevenlabs, gemini, openai, xai, else plugin PCM); ElevenLabs `pcm_24000`, OpenAI `pcm`, Gemini SSE streamers; 16 MiB per-sentence cap
- `tts_streaming_xai.go` — xAI WebSocket TTS streamer (base64 PCM deltas at 24 kHz) with its own websocket connect, keepalive and close handling
- `tts_tool_speaker.go` — playback pipelines: PCM straight to the output device with temp-WAV fallback, prefetch of the next sentence, per-sentence file synthesis for non-streaming providers, and a variant handing each sentence file to a deliver callback

#### Speech to text: dispatch and audio preparation

`stt.provider` is honoured when set; otherwise local backends are tried first, then cloud providers in the order groq, openai, mistral, xai, elevenlabs, deepinfra. `stt.enabled` gates everything, and language comes from `stt.<provider>.language`, `stt.language`, then `ICEBATH_LOCAL_STT_LANGUAGE`.

- `transcription_tools.go` — `TranscribeAudio` entry, provider resolution and auto-detect, cached faster-whisper model with reference counts and idle unload watcher, CUDA-to-CPU retry, credential-file read guard, model precedence, local-only fallback entry
- `stt_common.go` — defaults and catalogs (local `base`, `whisper-1`, `whisper-large-v3-turbo`, `voxtral-mini-latest`, `scribe_v2`, xAI transcribe models), base URL env overrides, 25 MB default cap, accepted formats, result envelopes
- `stt_audio.go` — ffmpeg, ffprobe and whisper binary discovery, 16 kHz mono AAC transcode, file validation, SILK and CAF to WAV conversion, ffprobe duration, silence trimming before cloud upload (`stt.cloud_trim_*`)
- `stt_chunking.go` — upload caps (OpenAI and Groq 25 MB, Mistral and xAI 500 MB, ElevenLabs about 5 GB, per-model seconds); oversized files are split at silencedetect pause midpoints and transcribed piecewise
- `silk_export.go` — decodes SILK voice notes to WAV with the `pilk` Python package in the managed interpreter; used by the QQ bot adapter

#### Speech to text backends

Built-in names are local, local_command, groq, openai, mistral, xai, elevenlabs and deepinfra; anything else resolves to a command provider or a plugin.

- `stt_local.go` — faster-whisper worker process in the managed interpreter (VAD, beam 5, hallucinated-segment filter), managed whisper.cpp engine with pinned `ggml-base` and Silero VAD downloads into `<home>/cache/whisper.cpp`, `ICEBATH_LOCAL_STT_COMMAND` template
- `stt_cloud.go` — Groq, OpenAI and DeepInfra via an OpenAI-compatible multipart client with retries, Mistral, xAI `/stt`, ElevenLabs `/speech-to-text`; credential resolution per profile, private base URLs allowed keyless
- `stt_command.go` — `stt.providers.<name>` shell command providers (optional 16 kHz normalization, transcript from output file or stdout), plugin dispatch, `pre_transcription` plugin hook, whisper-family prompt truncation
- `stt_registry.go` — `TranscriptionProvider` and live stream session interfaces, registry reserving built-in names, plugin-host adapters; the direct `RegisterTranscriptionProvider` function has no caller, plugins register through the scoped registry

#### Live streaming transcription

When `stt.streaming` is on and the active provider supports it, captured PCM is streamed to the provider during recording and partial transcripts are reported. Excluded from the core and noextras builds.

- `transcription_streaming.go` — session with resampler to 16 kHz, audio queue and worker; websocket drivers for OpenAI Realtime, xAI streaming and ElevenLabs realtime; plugin stream driver; `OpenStreamingSession` selection
- `transcription_streaming_manager.go` — chunk resampling, websocket send and receive loop with stall deadline and backlog flush, plugin session pump
- `transcription_streaming_base.go` — build-tag-free constants (default OpenAI model `gpt-live-transcribe`, ElevenLabs `scribe_v2_realtime`, 10 second connect, 20 second finalize)

#### Terminal voice mode: capture, playback and the continuous loop

Push-to-talk and hands-free voice in the terminal: PortAudio capture through `pkg/internal/pysounddevice` (or `termux-microphone-record` on Termux), silence auto-stop, transcription, spoken replies and barge-in. Excluded from the core and noextras builds; recordings go to the system temp dir under `icebath_voice`.

- `voice_mode.go` — audio environment detection (PortAudio, PulseAudio sockets, WSL, containers, Termux), cue beeps and thinking blips (`voice.beep_volume`, `voice.thinking_sound`), file playback through sounddevice or system players, requirement check, temp recording cleanup
- `voice_mode_recorder.go` — recorder interface with PortAudio and Termux implementations: speech confirmation, silence auto-stop (RMS 200, 3 seconds), length cap, live STT session feed, WAV writing, `TranscribeRecording`
- `voice_mode_recorder_peak.go` — peak RMS accessor of the current capture
- `voice_mode_listen.go` — full-duplex listen with barge-in detection: ambient floor calibration, playback grace, sliding trip window, capture until quiet
- `voice_cli.go` — continuous loop (start, stop, three silent cycles end it, busy probe), transcript delivery callbacks, `SpeakText` via streaming or whole-file synthesis with capture paused, `voice.beep_enabled`, `ICEBATH_VOICE_DEBUG` breadcrumbs
- `voice_mode_transcript.go` — `voice.stop_phrases` matching, TTS echo detection by difflib similarity, spoken stop hint
- `voice_mode_transcript_base.go` — build-tag-free Whisper hallucination filter (known phrases and filler repeats); also used by Discord voice
- `voice_transcript_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports stop-phrase, echo and stop-hint checks for `pkg/tuiserver`
- `wave_read.go` — reads PCM WAV header fields and frames for playback

#### Wake word

Background hotword listening configured by the `wake_word` section (enabled, surface, input_device, provider, phrase default `hey icebath`, sensitivity 0.6, confirmation_frames, start_new_session). One process may own the microphone, enforced by a lock file at `<root>/runtime/wake-word.lock`. Excluded from the core and noextras builds.

- `wake_word.go` — config loading and clamping, provider aliases and auto order (openwakeword, sherpa, porcupine), per-profile enrolled phrases, input device diagnostics, frame resampling, requirement check with remediation hints
- `wake_word_detector.go` — background reader: opens the input stream, feeds frames to the engine, fire cooldown, silence alert, pause and resume, reopen retries on device failure
- `wake_word_engines.go` — engine contract and three engines: openWakeWord (model file, confirmation streak), sherpa-onnx keyword spotter (pinned gigaspeech KWS model download, phrases tokenized to a keywords file), Porcupine (`PORCUPINE_ACCESS_KEY`)
- `wake_word_libs.go` — binds the engines to `pkg/internal/pyopenwakeword`, `pkg/internal/pvporcupine` and `pkg/internal/sherpaonnx`, locating native libraries inside installed `pm` extras
- `wake_word_listener.go` — process singleton with owner checks and the cross-process lock; start, pause, resume, stop, last match and device status
- `wake_word_base.go`, `wake_word_libs_base.go` — build-tag-free probe of whether the native speech engine supports this platform

### `pkg/media/edgetts` — native client for the Microsoft Edge read-aloud TTS service

*2 files, 530 Go lines*

A self-contained reimplementation of the Edge browser's read-aloud websocket protocol, used by the default `edge` TTS provider in `pkg/media/tts_tool_providers.go`. Needs no API key; output is 24 kHz 48 kbit mono MP3. No project dependencies and no Python residue.

#### Edge read-aloud websocket client

- `client.go` — dials `wss://speech.platform.bing.com/.../readaloud/edge/v1`, sends SSML per text piece (split at byte limit, never inside an entity), collects MP3 frames, corrects clock skew from a refused handshake
- `token.go` — computes the `Sec-MS-GEC` request token: a salted, modified SHA-256 over the current five-minute window

### `pkg/media/speech` — Piper voice catalog and loader for the native speech engine

*2 files, 456 Go lines*

Fetches, converts and loads Piper voices for `pkg/internal/sherpaonnx`; called by the Piper TTS engine, the tools picker and the wake-word platform probe. Voices and espeak-ng data are downloaded from sherpa-onnx GitHub releases through `pkg/fetch` with pinned size and sha256.

#### Piper voices

- `piper.go` — engine handle and platform support check, catalog fetch on first use, adoption of a user `.onnx` voice (writes tokens and ONNX metadata to convert it), synthesis scale defaults
- `piper_voices.go` — [data] 185 Piper voice archives pinned by size and sha256, consumed by `piper.go` and the voice picker

### `pkg/memory` — built-in memory store and tool, memory providers, skill curator, learning views, insights

*41 files, 19,811 Go lines*

Core: the built-in store (`<home>/memories/MEMORY.md` and `USER.md`), the model-facing `memory` tool, the provider contract and the per-session `MemoryManager` that `pkg/agent` builds to prefetch, sync turns and mirror writes to at most one external provider. The package also holds the skill curator (scheduler, LLM consolidation fork, backups, `icebath curator`), the learning graph and `icebath journey`, session-history insights, session Markdown export, memory setup CLI and TUI views, egress redaction wrappers and a process-heap trim. Only two external providers are compiled in, ByteRover and RetainDB; there is no Honcho, Mem0, Hindsight or Supermemory code anywhere in the repository (only a `mem0_` secret-prefix pattern in `pkg/tools/file_safety.go`), and the in-tree plugin catalog ships no memory provider, so any other provider must be an installed plugin directory loaded through the plugin host. Session search and the background memory review are not here (`pkg/tools/session_search.go`, `pkg/agent/background_review*.go`); this package supplies only the review's delete gate. Python residue is dense: twenty of the twenty-four `register*` calls in the package init are empty, and the store and learning files carry their own Python str, repr, int and datetime emulation.

#### Package init

- `memory.go` — [port-artifact] init calling 24 `register*` functions in Python import order; only the memory tool, ByteRover, RetainDB and migration seams actually register anything
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Built-in memory store (MEMORY.md and USER.md)

Two bounded text files of entries separated by `\n§\n`, limits `memory.memory_char_limit` (2200) and `memory.user_char_limit` (1375), enabled by `memory.memory_enabled` and `memory.user_profile_enabled`. The prompt block is a snapshot frozen at session load (header, usage percent, entries); mid-session writes hit disk but not the prompt. Every write rereads under a `.lock` sibling file lock, dedupes, threat-scans and writes atomically.

- `store.go` — add, patch, remove, legacy replace and all-or-nothing batch against the final budget; tolerant old_text matching, closest-entry hints, three-failure retry cap per turn, drift guard with `.bak.<ts>` snapshot, prompt block rendering; also Python str/repr helpers
- `store_{unix,windows}.go` — per-OS exclusive lock on `<file>.lock` (flock refusing symlinks; msvcrt-style byte lock with retries) and newline translation
- `threats.go` — injection and exfiltration scanner: 38 regex rules in three cumulative scopes, invisible and bidi code points, hardcoded-secret rule, 65536 char cap; a near-duplicate of `pkg/tools/threat_patterns.go`, used only by the store

#### memory tool and write approval

The `memory` tool (toolset `memory`) takes `target` (memory or user) and an `operations` array of add, patch and remove; the legacy single-op shape is still accepted and `replace` is refused. Committed writes are mirrored to the external provider.

- `tool.go` — schema narrowed to the enabled stores, argument validation, gate then store call, 2048 char error bound, per-session `Manager` lookup, store construction from settings
- `approval.go` — write-approval gate and staging; unattended background reviews may add but have patch and remove staged with the matched entry pinned; `/memory` and `/skills` pending, approve, reject, diff and approval-mode subcommands

#### Prompt guidance and recalled-context fencing

- `prompt.go` — system prompt guidance text adapted to which stores are enabled and whether `skill_manage` is available
- `context.go` — wraps provider recall in a `<memory-context>` block with a system note, drops repeated recall bullets, and scrubs such spans from streamed model output across delta boundaries

#### Provider contract and the session memory manager

The contract an external memory backend implements and the manager that drives it for one agent session. One built-in plus at most one external provider; a failing or stuck provider never blocks the turn.

- `provider.go` — `Provider` interface (initialize, system prompt block, prefetch, sync turn, tools, session end and switch, pre-compress checkpoint, delegation, memory-write mirror, setup schema, backup paths, profile hooks), defaults, trivial-prompt test, context-bound background jobs
- `manager.go` — provider registration and tool routing with reserved core names, 8 second prefetch bound, stuck-call gates per home and provider, serialized background worker with 5 second shutdown drain, oversized-prefetch spill, write mirroring with provenance, provider tool injection
- `scope.go` — profile isolation: a provider instance is bound to one profile home, and calls from another profile or an unresolved caller are refused and logged
- `redact.go` — secret masking for display and thin wrappers over the `pkg/tools` redactor for egress, with token learning across values sent to a provider
- `query_rewrite.go` — optional LLM rewrite of the user message into one retrieval question (auxiliary task `memory_query_rewrite`), validated and offered to provider plugins through the plugin host

#### Provider registry, discovery and external providers

Providers resolve bundled first, then `<home>/plugins/<name>`, then `./.icebath/plugins/<name>` when `ICEBATH_ENABLE_PROJECT_PLUGINS` is set; `memory.provider` names the active one and `plugins.disabled` can park it.

- `registry.go` — registration table, discovery with availability probe, load with skill tracking and pruning for inactive providers, parked-provider notice, CLI subcommand contributed by the active provider
- `discovery.go` — scans user and project plugin directories for guests providing the memory-provider category and loads them through the plugin host
- `hosted_provider.go` — `Provider` implementation proxying every hook to a provider object living in the plugin host
- `plugin_hooks.go` — entry points `cmd/icebath` wires into the plugin system (provider directory, hosted name, dependency preparation) and the `icebath curator` argument adapter
- `byterover.go` — bundled `byterover` provider over the `brv` CLI: tools `brv_query`, `brv_curate`, `brv_status`; context tree in `<home>/byterover`, `BRV_API_KEY`, `memory.byterover.auto_extract`, background curate of turns and pre-compress flush
- `retaindb.go` — bundled `retaindb` provider over `https://api.retaindb.com`: ten `retaindb_*` tools (profile, search, context, remember, forget, files), SQLite write-behind queue `<home>/retaindb_queue.db`, background context and dialectic prefetch; `RETAINDB_API_KEY`

#### Memory setup, status and profile handling

`icebath memory setup|status|off|reset`, the equivalent TUI hub views, and what happens to provider config when profiles are created or renamed.

- `setup.go` — interactive provider picker, schema-driven prompts, dependency install through `pm`, secrets written to `.env`, post-setup hook, status report
- `memory_view.go` — non-interactive overview, configure, turn-off and erase operations for the TUI memory screen
- `agent_cmds.go` — `memory off` (clears `memory.provider`), `memory reset` (deletes MEMORY.md and USER.md after confirmation) and the `icebath insights` terminal command
- `migration.go` — at agent init reports a configured provider that resolves nowhere; from self-update installs a catalog-listed provider into every profile home missing it
- `profile.go` — copies `<home>/<provider>/` and `<provider>.json` into a new profile (0600) and notifies the provider of profile creation and rename

#### Skill curator

Lifecycle manager for agent-created skills: marks skills stale then archives them by inactivity, optionally forks an LLM review that consolidates narrow skills into umbrella skills, and keeps snapshots for rollback. Runs from gateway housekeeping when `curator.enabled`, the interval has passed and the session is idle; usage records and the ledger themselves live in `pkg/skills`.

- `curator.go` — state file `<home>/skills/.curator_state`, schedule gates (`curator.interval_hours`, `min_idle_hours`, `stale_after_days`, `archive_after_days`, `consolidate`), transitions sparing pinned, locked and cron-referenced skills, review fork, cron reference rewrite, `logs/curator/<stamp>/` report
- `curator_prompts.go` — [data] the consolidation review prompt and dry-run banner given to the review fork
- `curator_cli.go` — `icebath curator` and `/curator`: status, usage, run, pause, resume, pin, unpin, lock, unlock, list-unmanaged, adopt, restore, list-archived, archive, prune, backup, rollback, ledger, purge
- `curator_backup.go` — `skills.tar.gz` snapshots with manifest and cron job capture under `<home>/skills/.curator_backups/`, pruning to `curator.backup.keep`, staged rollback with safety snapshot and cron skill-link restore
- `skillusage.go` — thin adapters over `pkg/skills` usage records and archiving for the learning views

#### Learning graph, journey and /learn

A view of what the agent has learned: agent-created or used skills plus memory entries as nodes on a timeline, shown by `icebath journey` and the TUI learning panel, with delete and edit of individual nodes.

- `learning.go` — builds skill nodes from bundled and profile skill trees with usage records, memory cards from the two store files, related-skill and token-overlap edges, cluster and density stats
- `learning_mutations.go` — node detail, delete (archive skill or remove memory entry) and edit (rewrite SKILL.md or replace memory entry) addressed by fingerprinted node ids
- `learning_render.go` — terminal timeline renderer: recency inks, date buckets, palette derived from the theme primary, golden-angle category hues, animation frames for the TUI
- `journey_command.go` — `icebath journey` show (once, `--play` animation or `--json`), list, delete and edit (opens `$EDITOR`), with contrast-checked ANSI output
- `learn.go` — prompt for the `/learn` command, embedding the skill authoring standards

#### Session insights

Usage analytics over the session database (`sessions`, `messages`, `session_model_usage` in `state.db`) for `icebath insights` and the gateway `/insights` command.

- `insights.go` — queries over a day window and optional source filter; overview, per-model cost estimates from provider pricing, platform, tool, skill and activity breakdowns, top sessions
- `insights_report.go` — report types and the terminal and messaging-platform text renderers
- `insights_values.go` — [py-shim] Python int and float arithmetic, coercion and formatting over SQLite cells so totals match the original; used only by the insights engine

#### Session Markdown export

- `session_export_md.go` — renders a session (with compression segments) to Markdown or QMD with frontmatter and a body SHA-256, secret redaction, deterministic filenames, verify, and `manifest.jsonl` append; used by `icebath sessions export` and `/save`

#### Process memory trim

Unrelated to agent memory: releases Go heap pages back to the OS.

- `trim.go` — runs GC and `FreeOSMemory` after compression, agent close and when idle, with cooldown and logging from `context.memory_trim.*`, plus RSS telemetry from `/proc/self/status`

### `pkg/tokenizers` — native Hugging Face tokenizer pipeline and snapshot loader

*7 files, 3,243 Go lines*

A Go reimplementation of the Hugging Face `tokenizers` library sufficient to count tokens for an arbitrary model snapshot, with no Python and no cgo. The only consumer is `pkg/trajectorycompressor`, which resolves a local folder or Hugging Face Hub snapshot and calls `Load`. `Decode` and the decoder components are implemented but have no caller outside tests.

#### tokenizer.json pipeline

Normalizer, pre-tokenizer, model, post-processor and decoder components parsed from `tokenizer.json`, with added-token matching.

- `tokenizer.go` — `Tokenizer` built by `FromJSON`: added-token cutting (raw and normalized matchers), encode through the pipeline, decode
- `text.go` — normalized text with origin tracking, pattern types (rune, literal, regexp2 regex with class translation), split behaviours, byte-level mapping
- `normalizers.go` — Bert, Strip, StripAccents, NFC/NFD/NFKC/NFKD, Lowercase, Nmt, ByteLevel, Prepend, Replace, Precompiled (SentencePiece charsmap trie), Sequence
- `pretokenizers.go` — Bert, ByteLevel, CharDelimiterSplit, Digits, FixedLength, Metaspace, Punctuation, Split, UnicodeScripts, Whitespace, WhitespaceSplit, Sequence
- `models.go` — BPE (merge ranks, dropout, byte fallback, word cache), WordPiece, WordLevel and Unigram models
- `decoders.go` — post-processors (ByteLevel, Bert, Roberta, Template, Sequence) and decoders (BPE, ByteLevel, ByteFallback, Fuse, WordPiece, Metaspace, CTC, Replace, Strip, Sequence); decoders are [unwired]

#### Snapshot loader for legacy tokenizer files

- `load.go` — `Load` picks `tokenizer.json`, `tiktoken.model`, a SentencePiece model, `vocab.json` with `merges.txt`, or `vocab.txt`; reads `tokenizer_config.json` and `special_tokens_map.json`, applies per-class special tokens and framing (Bert, Roberta, T5, Llama, Gemma, Whisper, CLIP, Moonshot and others)

### `pkg/tokenizers/tiktoken` — tiktoken byte-pair encoder and cl100k_base

*2 files, 384 Go lines*

Native BPE over a tiktoken rank file. `CL100kBase` is used by `pkg/tools/tools_config_tokens.go` to estimate the token cost of each tool schema, and `New` and `ParseRanks` by the `pkg/tokenizers` loader.

#### Encoding and rank file loading

- `encoding.go` — `Encoding` with regexp2 split pattern, special-token handling, byte-pair merge (linear scan under 100 bytes, heap above); cl100k_base definition loaded once per process
- `load.go` — no vocabulary is embedded: fetches the cl100k rank file from `openaipublic.blob.core.windows.net`, verifies sha256, caches under `TIKTOKEN_CACHE_DIR`, `DATA_GYM_CACHE_DIR` or the temp `data-gym-cache`; parses base64 rank lines

### `pkg/tokenizers/sentencepiece` — native SentencePiece model reader and encoder

*4 files, 890 Go lines*

Reads a serialized SentencePiece `ModelProto` and encodes text without the C++ library. Used by the `pkg/tokenizers` loader and by `pkg/internal/sherpaonnx` to turn wake-word phrases into model tokens.

#### Model parsing and segmentation

- `processor.go` — `Processor`: load a model file, encode to pieces or ids with unknown-run and byte-fallback handling, piece lookup
- `model.go` — protobuf wire decoding of the pieces, trainer and normalizer specs; piece tables with reserved and user-defined ids
- `models.go` — the four segmenters: unigram best path over a piece trie, BPE by pair score, word and character models
- `normalizer.go` — precompiled character map (double-array trie) normalization, whitespace collapsing and the word-start space symbol

## 13. Install, self-update, package manager, profiles

### `pkg/selfupdate` — `icebath update`, the passive update check, and the doctor, status, dump, debug-share and security-audit commands

*141 files, 39,177 Go lines*

Owns `icebath update` end to end plus support commands that landed in the same flat directory: `icebath doctor`, `status`, `dump`, `debug share|delete`, `security audit` and `fallback check`. Entry points are bound in `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go` (update, the hidden child verbs `update-completion`, `update-finish`, `update-takeover`, `update-restart-recovery`, `source-completion`, `venv-sync`, `import-health`, the custody launcher entries, and hooks in six startup phases) and `cmd/icebath/host_commands.go` (doctor, status, dump, debug); `pkg/app` calls doctor, status and the banner update check, and the gateway reaches the debug report, drain report and steward lookup through hooks set in `cmd/icebath/wiring.go`. Most update files carry the build constraint `!icebath_core && !icebath_noextras` (doctor, status, dump and debug carry none); the package writes receipts, the update marker, pause and obligation records through `updaterecord`, `install-stamp.json` in the install tree, `<home>/source-checks/*.json`, `<home>/pastes/pending.json` and `<home>/.update_prompt.json`, and talks to api.github.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, github.com archives, paste.rs, dpaste.com, api.osv.dev, `systemctl`, `launchctl` and `sc.exe`. An update applies in one of three ways: a release-binary swap (the only one the trees `pkg/install` creates can reach), a git pull of a source checkout, or a ZIP overlay of a source tree on Windows. The last two, together with `venv_*`, `bytecode_*`, the Python syntax gate and the import-health probe, are the Python application's source-install updater ported whole: they run only for a tree that has `.git` and also carries the installer's `.icebath-bootstrap-complete` marker, a combination the installer never creates on its own, and several of their steps test for `pyproject.toml` or `.py` files a Go tree never has. Condition: the release path, fleet restart, doctor and debug share are implemented and wired, port scaffolding is heavy throughout (Python exception class names on errors, `map[string]any` tokens and argparse namespaces, argparse help emulation for hidden verbs, test seams as package variables), and the snapshot safety nets in `update_cmd_config.go`, the backup helpers in `post_update_base.go` and `DoctorCheckConfigFile` have no callers.

#### Update command boundary, admission and refusals

`CmdUpdate` runs the command: optional re-exec into an owning install, the read-only flags (`--install-id`, `--set-channel`, `--plan`, `--list-venv-holders`, `--check`), the admission ladder that refuses installs that must not self-update, SIGHUP protection with both streams mirrored to the root home update log, the cross-process update lock (exit 2 when another update holds it), then the implementation, and finally closes the receipt with the real exit code. Admission refuses, in order: a commit build, an image-managed install (provenance marker), a tree sealed by a steward (the package manager or image that owns the binary), a Docker, Nix, apt or other package-manager install method, and any tree without the installer's bootstrap marker, each with the command to run instead and a `refused` receipt. A "steward" is that external owner; a source checkout is refused with `git pull` plus `./setup-icebath.sh`.

- `update_cmd_entry.go` — `CmdUpdate` and `UpdateInvocation`, preflight handling, update lock acquisition, exit-code and failure mapping onto the receipt and the gateway exit-code file; also `clearBytecodeCache` (removes `__pycache__` dirs)
- `update_cmd_impl.go` — `cmdUpdateImpl`: stale git lock cleanup, option resolution, receipt and fleet plan, pre-update backup, gateway pause, then dispatch to the release, git or ZIP route and their failure handling
- `update_cmd.go` — shared helpers: `updates` config section, receipt step recording, git runner (300 s network timeout reported as exit 124), `--gateway` prompt relay through `<home>/.update_prompt.json` and `.update_response`, subprocess failure classification, Python startup-file syntax gate over a fixed `.py` list
- `update_cmd_common.go` — `bestEffort`: runs a non-critical step, logs its failure at debug, lets only exits and interrupts through
- `update_contract.go` — `evaluateUpdateAdmission`, `UpdateRefusal` (code, message, replacement command), `recordRefusalReceipt`
- `contract.go` — `IsCommitBuild`: install stamp `source: commit-build` never updates
- `steward.go` — `SealedSteward` detection (install stamp `distribution`, package-manager path layout, `dpkg-query`/`rpm`/`pacman`/`apk` ownership query); 12 steward names, update refusal texts for 11 and uninstall texts for 3, each with a generic fallback
- `image_provenance.go` — reads and validates `/etc/icebath/image-provenance.json` (schema 1, `deployment_kind: image`, `manager`, optional `image`, `version`, `revision`); an invalid marker still means image-managed
- `update_owning_install.go` — [port-artifact] re-runs the command through the checkout whose `venv` holds the running binary, detected by `pyvenv.cfg` and `PYTHONPATH`; never triggers for a Go binary
- `update_internal_commands.go` — `UpdateInternalCommand`: the hidden verbs an update spawns, which skip startup debt recovery
- `check.go` — `deepCopyRecord` for the channel retirement baseline, `recordStop` writing the closed stop token on the receipt
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `logger=selfupdate`

#### Update channels and release discovery

Each install has a channel persisted per install in `config.yaml` under `update.installs.<16-hex install id>` (`path`, `channel`). Two names are built in: `stable` (latest published GitHub release, the default for the official repository `nickheyer/icebath`) and `main` (branch tip, the default for anything else). Every other name, `canary` included, is resolved from a channel archive at `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nickheyer/icebath/main/releases/channels/<name>.json`, whose head names a build manifest under `releases/channel-builds/<id>/` by SHA-256; redirects are refused and objects are capped at 4 MiB. Channel records can be `retired` and point to a stable destination, which the update adopts in config only after a verified completion and never when it would downgrade.

- `channel.go` — channel name grammar (lowercase hyphenated, at most 32 characters, no Windows device names), `InstallID`, `ChannelRecord`, `DefaultChannel`, `ResolveUpdateChannel`, locked write of `update.installs`, `AdoptRetiredChannel`, `StaleChannelRecords` for doctor
- `channel_manager.go` — `update --set-channel` and `--install-id`: persists the channel, refuses commit builds and externally owned installs, prints canary and stable data warnings
- `run_channel.go` — `SourceUpdateChannel`: `main` for an explicit `--branch`, else the transient `--channel`, else the install record
- `release_channels.go` — `ChannelReader`: fetches and validates channel records, heads and build manifests (policies `preview`, `stable-release`, `canary-release`, `source-branch`), retirement resolution, optional retrying reads
- `source_releases.go` — `ResolveSourceTarget`: stable through the GitHub latest-release API cross-checked against `git ls-remote` of the tag, named channels through the archive, forward-only pinning, retirement downgrade refusal
- `source_releases_base.go` — `gitArgs` argv join helper
- `release.go` — `CompareVersions` (semver precedence) and `ClassifyFetchFailure` (one-line diagnosis of a failed fetch from its HTTP code or git text)
- `source_github.go` — api.github.com GET with a token ladder and anonymous retry on a rejected token, compare API helpers, read-only promptless git probe runner
- `source_github_{other,windows}.go` — hides the console window of a git probe on Windows; no-op elsewhere (2 files)

#### Update check: passive banner check and `icebath update --check`

`CheckForUpdates` answers "is an update available" without fetching or writing git state, for the app banner (`BannerUpdateCheck`), the fast version output (`startupfast.UpdateCheck`) and `update --check`. Results are cached per install and profile in `<home>/source-checks/<install id>.json` for 24 hours (failures 1 hour), keyed by an identity object (root, home, head, origin, branch, channel, embedded revision); `updates.check: false` disables the passive form. An offered release that predates the gateway runtime ledger is reported as held, not available.

- `source_check.go` — checkout facts, branch tip lookup through GitHub then `git ls-remote`, behind count, cache read and write, `GitStdout`/`GitCount` helpers other packages use, `BannerUpdateCheck` hook
- `source_check_manager.go` — `CheckForUpdates` and `PassiveCheckForUpdates`, unsupported-install reasons, release-install result from the release plan, runtime-schema verdict cache `<home>/source-checks/release-runtime.json`
- `update_cmd_check.go` — git debris cleanup, scoped fetch and behind-ness verdicts for `--check` on a checkout, plus `selectApplyTarget`, which resolves the channel target, pin and retirement before any tree write

#### Release-binary update path and downgrade hold

The route a script or installer tree takes: plan the release for the channel (`install.PlanRelease`), order it against the running build, download and verify the archive and swap the binary (`install.ApplyRelease`), then hand over to the new binary's completion child. A pinned channel may move back to an older release; an unpinned one never does. A target that predates the gateway runtime ledger while any profile's `state.db` holds ledger rows is refused or held, with per-profile restore instructions.

- `update_release_binary.go` — `releaseBinaryInstall` test (no `.git`, an install binary, detected method `script` or `setup-app`), repository precedence (`ICEBATH_REPO_URL`, `.install_repo`, official), `planReleaseUpdate`, `checkReleaseUpdate`, `updateViaRelease`; also `rebuildSourceCheckout`, a `go build` of a Go source checkout run after any route
- `downgrade.go` — runtime-ledger downgrade refusal: scans profile stores for `session_admissions` or `worker_executions` rows, asks git or GitHub whether the target defines the ledger schema, names the newest pre-ledger snapshot per profile

#### Source-checkout update: git fetch, stash, branch guard, pull and rollback

Port of the Python source-install updater, reachable only for a git checkout that also carries the installer bootstrap marker. It handles forks and an `upstream` remote, a checkout parked on another branch (`updates.parked_branch_strategy`, `--switch-branch`), a detached HEAD, local changes (stash, prompt, restore, or discard per `updates.non_interactive_local_changes`), diverged history (rescue ref under `refs/icebath-update-backups/` then hard reset), shallow and partial clones, a broken Git for Windows shim, and rollback to the pre-pull commit when a startup file stops compiling. Before any tree move it arms obligations and writes an interrupted-pull marker so a killed update can be repaired at the next launch.

- `update_cmd_git.go` — fork and upstream sync, parked-branch assessment, detached-HEAD rescue refs and their expiry, fetch failure diagnosis, real-git lookup past a trampoline shim, `package-lock.json` churn discard, `core.autocrlf` normalisation
- `update_cmd_prepare.go` — pre-pull phase: preflight refusal, parked-branch guard, branch switch under the commit point, autostash, new-commit count, post-pull HEAD verification
- `update_cmd_pull.go` — the checkout move onto the target commit, diverged-checkout reconciliation, syntax-failure rollback, off-target landing refusal; `updateExit`
- `update_cmd_stash.go` — local-change scan scoped to what the update can overwrite, stash push, restore with conflict handling and safety rejection, park under `--keep-stash`, orphaned autostash warnings
- `update_cmd_commit.go` — commit point: arms the completion and fleet obligations, writes the interrupted-pull marker and a recovery closure, settles a failed move; also the Python gate that compiles `.py` startup files of the target and honours `requires-python`
- `update_cmd_validation.go` — [stub] `import-health` hidden verb always answers an empty failure list; the caller treats the binary starting as health, where Python imported critical modules
- `git_pack_tidy.go` — bounded (60 s) tidy of a partial clone's promisor packs: erases packs proven redundant, merges the smallest toward 50 packs, state in `icebath-pack-tidy.json`
- `gitlock_run_git.go` — binds `tools.GitlockRunGit` to the custody git runner so git-lock sweeps in `pkg/tools` run under the update's custody

#### Source-checkout update: ZIP overlay

Windows-only route for a source tree without `.git`, and the fallback when git file I/O fails there: downloads `https://github.com/<repo>/archive/<ref>.zip`, extracts with path-escape and symlink rejection, checks free space, stages every top-level entry beside its target and swaps them in two phases under a journal (`.icebath-update-zip-swap`) and an owner lock, so a kill is finished or rolled back at the next launch. Same reachability limit as the git route.

- `update_cmd_zip.go` — download, safe extraction, staging, hardlink or copy backups, journaled swap and rollback, dirty-tree refusal, `updateViaZip`
- `update_cmd_zip_{darwin,linux,unix,windows}.go` — per-OS mode and timestamp application through the open file handle (4 files)
- `early_recovery_zip.go` — swap journal format and owner lock, `RestoreInterruptedZipSwap` finishing or rolling back each journaled entry by file identity

#### Repair of an interrupted checkout move at launch

Startup hook run before the command is parsed (`phaseAfterLauncher`) and in cron workers: if the interrupted-pull marker or the ZIP journal exists and no live update owns the checkout, it puts back every path the killed git already wrote, redoes a killed rollback, retires the marker, and re-executes the command. Only a git or ZIP source tree ever has these markers.

- `early_recovery_restore.go` — `RestoreInterruptedPull`: marker fields, restore claim file `icebath-update-pull.claim`, attribution of written paths by blob id, foreign `index.lock` handling, `RelaunchAfterRestore`, `GitOperationInProgress`
- `early_recovery_exec_{unix,windows}.go` — re-exec in place on POSIX; spawn and exit on Windows (2 files)
- `early_recovery_lock_{unix,windows}.go` — non-blocking claim lock, ZIP swap owner lock, and file identity (inode or volume index) probes (2 files)

#### Custody of update child processes

"Custody" is the rule that every process the update starts stays tied to the update's ownership of the install tree, so the tree lock cannot be released while a child still writes. On POSIX a child that mutates the tree inherits the checkout lock descriptors and any other child gets a parent-death signal; on Windows every child starts suspended, is bound to a kill-on-close job object and then resumed, and a refused bind is printed and receipted. Three hidden argv entries of the binary act as launchers for runners that hide their child.

- `custody.go` — `Run`, `RunGit`, `PopenPostCommit`, `ContainedCommand`, child options and results, partial-clone prefetch before a move, `DispatchCustodyLauncher` for `__icebath_custody_reap__`, `__icebath_custody_custodian__`, `__icebath_custody_join__`
- `custody_base.go` — registers the lock hooks `pkg/pm` calls (bind child, resume suspended, lock held, lock descriptors)
- `custody_unix.go`, `custody_windows.go` — owner-watched git run and process-group kill on POSIX; `CREATE_SUSPENDED`, inheritable job handle and the kernel32 job API on Windows
- `custody_join.go`, `custody_join_other.go` — Windows launcher that joins the update job before running its command; refuses everywhere else
- `custody_reap_unix.go`, `custody_reap_windows.go` — POSIX stand-in and custodian launchers that hold the lock descriptors until no descendant is left; absent on Windows
- `custody_reap_linux.go`, `custody_reap_nosubreaper.go` — child subreaper through `prctl` on Linux; `ps` tree sampling on other Unixes

#### Completion after the commit point

Once the binary or tree has moved, the updater freezes a completion request (JSON with source, home, branch, expected sha, plan, snapshot ids, resume token, receipt) and runs the new binary twice: `update-completion <request> <result>` syncs the pm dependency environment, then `update-completion ... --prepared` publishes launchers, installs configured-feature dependencies, runs maintenance, writes the install stamp, restarts and verifies the gateway fleet. Every failure after the commit point is recorded as an owed follow-up on the receipt instead of failing the update, and a lost completion result is settled as owed work. `update-takeover`, `update-finish` and the `update --post-swap` form exist only to finish an update handed over by an older shipped updater.

- `update_cmd_complete.go` — completion request construction, `handOffSourceUpdate`, exit hooks that resume paused gateways, `cmdUpdateCheck` for `--check`
- `update_completion.go` — `runCompletion` (child with inherited lock, output relay), `UpdateCompletionMain`, bootstrap and prepared stages, `completeSelected`, lost-completion settlement, gateway-mode success publication
- `completion_child_{unix,windows}.go` — new session and group kill for the completion child; suspended windowless child and `taskkill` tree kill on Windows (2 files)
- `source_completion.go` — `CompleteSourceCheckout`: launchers, feature dependencies, maintenance and stamp under the update lock; `source-completion` hidden verb with argparse-style parsing; `ExposePMGit` for Windows
- `configured_features_refresh.go` — installs missing dependencies of configured features, then the plugin of each configured memory provider a profile lacks
- `update_finish.go` — `update-finish` child: maintenance, stamp and fleet restart of a tree a historical updater committed; `LegacyPostSwapMain`
- `update_takeover.go` — `update-takeover`: takes the lock, provisions dependencies, runs the finish child and writes the acknowledgement a waiting old updater reads

#### Post-update maintenance, install stamp and boot-time home steps

`RunPostUpdateMaintenance` runs in the completion: Windows home ACL repair, macOS TCC anchor refresh, `state.db` integrity check with automatic restore from the newest valid snapshot (all profiles), commit-graph fetch for version identity, model catalog seeding, plugin catalog cache drop, bundled skills sync, per-profile skill and `.env` sync, default plugin install, relay runtime and provisioned-extras refresh, the completion line after probing the new binary's SQLite, then notices (FTS rebuild, curator, FHS PATH guard, launcher exposure, cua-driver, default tools, checkpoint footprint). Separately, every launch other than `update` (and the gateway at start) compares the install identity with a per-profile record and re-runs five home steps when the code changed; the identity comes from `install-stamp.json` or git HEAD, so a script-installed release tree, which has neither, never triggers them.

- `update_cmd_maint.go` — `RunPostUpdateMaintenance` and its steps; pre-update backup mode resolution (`--backup`, `--no-backup`, `updates.pre_update_backup` off, quick or full; `updates.backup_keep`), quick snapshots capped at 1 GiB per file, full zip
- `update_cmd_config.go` — [unwired] `restoreSnapshotSafetyNets`: meant to restore cron jobs, cron prompts and protected model settings an update emptied or rewrote, per profile; only the `lastSiblingSnapshots` variable is used
- `state_db_autorestore.go` — restores `state.db` from a snapshot through `backup.SafeRestoreDB` and re-verifies it
- `update_relay_runtime.go` — brings the NeMo Relay runtime to the version's pins once Relay is switched on
- `update_cua_refresh.go` — seams for the cua-driver refresh (`pm.Installed`, `codeexec.InstallCuaDriver`)
- `update_multiplex_notices.go` — re-prints the gateway multiplex opt-out notice and the standalone-gateway warning box after an update
- `source_stamp.go`, `source_stamp_manager.go` — `WriteSourceStamp`, run after every completed tail: rewrites `install-stamp.json` (schema 2, `updateMechanism: self`) from plain `git` run in the tree's directory, deletes it when git names no commit, then moves the bootstrap marker to that commit
- `boot_bootstrap.go` — `MaybeRunBootBootstrap`: install identity (stamp commit or git HEAD), record `<pm install state>/bootstrap/<profile>.json`, existence-lock with 600 s staleness, retry of owed steps
- `post_update.go` — `BootHomeSteps`: adopt a stampless checkout at a blessed root, `state.db` integrity guard, drop the live plugin catalog, expose the CLI, install default plugins; `RunSteps`
- `post_update_base.go` — [unwired] timestamped `bak-<stamp>` copies of files before a step rewrites them (`BackupExisting`); only `pathPresent` and `copyFile2` are used
- `store_activation.go` — `ActivateRuntime`: puts the pm store's tools first on `PATH` at every startup and in the gateway

#### Python dependency environment, bytecode and interpreter scaffolding

[port-artifact] What only makes sense for a Python install. The launch hook and `venv-sync` verb return early unless the tree has `pyproject.toml`; the bytecode sweep deletes `__pycache__` directories when a git checkout's fingerprint changes; the TCC anchor concerns a uv-managed Python interpreter inside the pm tool runtime. All are still called from startup or the completion, and the real behaviour left inside is `pm.RecoverIfNeeded` plus `pm.ActivateDependencies` at boot and the owed-completion retry policy.

- `venv_sync.go` — `PrepareLaunch`: finishes an owed source update before the app runs; completion-pending marker and attempt record (backoff after 2 failures, 15 minutes, give up after 6), foreign-owner refusal, relaunch marker `--icebath-relaunched`
- `venv_sync_main.go` — `BootLaunch` startup hook and the `venv-sync` hidden verb with emulated argparse usage and help; Python exception class tables used for error text package-wide
- `venv_sync_{unix,windows}.go` — owner uid of a path for the foreign-owner refusal; none on Windows (2 files)
- `bytecode_sweep.go`, `bytecode_fingerprint.go` — `SweepStaleBytecodeIfCheckoutChanged` at launch and the `.bytecode-fingerprint` stamp in the install tree
- `macos_tcc_anchor.go` — replaces a venv's symlinked uv store interpreter with a signed real copy so macOS privacy grants survive updates; marker `.tcc-anchor-source`, boot gate before install

#### Gateway pause and drain before the install changes

The updater records and stops this install's gateways so they do not run half-replaced code, persisting a token of what it stopped through `updaterecord` so this run, a later launch or the next update can resume them. On Windows it pauses at once, before any route: SCM services through `sc.exe` after identity verification, profile gateways through a planned-stop marker plus control-socket drain, then tree kill of survivors. On POSIX it only arms the pause and performs it at the git commit point: systemd units, launchd jobs and bare `gateway run` processes are drained over the control socket within a budget (at least 45 s), stopped through their supervisor, and replayed or restarted later. The release-binary route never reaches that commit point, so on Linux and macOS a release update swaps the binary under running gateways and relies on the fleet restart afterwards.

- `update_cmd_posix_pause.go` — POSIX discovery (systemd by cgroup, launchd, bare processes), self-protection when the updater runs inside a gateway unit, drain, stop, supervisor disarm, replay of a bare gateway from recorded argv, resume
- `update_cmd_posix_pause_{unix,windows}.go` — new session for a replayed gateway; nothing on Windows (2 files)
- `update_cmd_pause_gate.go` — binds each git step to the pause record with a tree baseline so a resume can tell a whole tree from a torn one
- `update_cmd_windows_gateways.go` — Windows discovery, service stop and start with rollback, socket pauses, cold-start plan for an installed autostart, relaunch watchers, readiness polling, launcher script regeneration, bootstrap-cache script refresh
- `update_cmd_windows_holders.go` — `--list-venv-holders` (exit 3 when present): processes running from the install's venv interpreter, classed gateway, `icebath:<subcommand>` or python; the guard itself is gone, and `--force` and `--force-venv` are never read
- `windows.go` — planned-stop marker `<profile home>/.gateway-planned-stop.json` (target pid and start time, stopper pid, written time)
- `windows_gateway_profile_home.go` — thin wrappers over gateway start attestation, live pids, detached spawn and ready wait
- `holder.go` — parses a command line to the icebath subcommand it runs (still recognises `-m icebath_cli.main`) and registers the "is a long-lived gateway host" matcher with `updaterecord`
- `gateway_restart_watcher.go` — re-exports the restart watcher timeout constant
- `drain_report.go`, `drain_report_export.go` — every 30 s while draining prints what the gateway still waits on (cron job, chat turn, delegation, with pid and elapsed) from `gateway_state.json` `active_work`; installed as the gateway's systemd and launchd drain reporter and reused by the gateway CLI

#### Runtime inventory and update plan

Read-only picture taken before any mutation and printed by `update --plan`: install method and whether it can update in place, every profile, and each running gateway with its pid, supervisor (`systemd`, `launchd`, `windows-service`, `manual`, or a generic `service`), code sha and version, and how it will be restarted. It is stored on the receipt and reconciled afterwards.

- `update_inventory.go` — `UpdatePlan`, `RuntimeRecord`, `CollectRuntimeInventory` (control-socket identity, then `gateway_state.json`, then pid file), JSON round trip
- `update_inventory_plan.go` — `printUpdatePlan` and attaching the plan to the receipt
- `update_inventory_outcomes.go` — one outcome row per planned runtime against the restart bookkeeping; warns about runtimes the restart never touched

#### Fleet restart after the update

The "fleet" is every running gateway of this install across the default home and all named profiles. After maintenance each is moved onto the new code: systemd units in user and system scope (drain, then reset-failed and restart, with passwordless `sudo` when needed and timeouts from the unit's own stop and start budgets, 90 s default, 15 minute cap), launchd labels on macOS (drain then `kickstart`, 20 s supervision check), and manual processes (drain or SIGTERM, force kill after 3 s); Windows services and profile gateways come back through the pause token instead, and s6 services are not restarted here. Gateways of another icebath home are announced and left alone. If the phase aborts, a detached fresh process retries supervised restarts and reports per-profile buckets.

- `fleet_restart.go` — `restartGatewayFleetAfterUpdate`, restart bookkeeping on the receipt, manual gateway handling, retired service-name migration, abort recovery verdict, skip reasons
- `fleet_restart_systemd.go` — unit listing per scope, ownership check, collapse of units sharing a main pid, privilege resolution, repair of a unit lacking the fatal-exit park, per-unit restart
- `fleet_restart_launchd.go` — restart of the invoking profile's label and every sibling label in its domain
- `launchd_supervision.go`, `launchd_supervision_base.go` — waits until launchd supervises a new gateway pid (20 s, 0.5 s poll), immediate on the detached fallback
- `fleet_unit_budget.go` — stop and start budgets of a unit, client timeout that outwaits them, unit job state and settle test
- `fleet_scope.go` — which home a unit or launchd plist serves (`ICEBATH_HOME`), the left-alone notice, legacy launchd labels
- `update_abort_recovery.go` — runs `update-restart-recovery` detached with the profile payload and judges whether every planned gateway is covered
- `update_restart_recovery.go` — `update-restart-recovery` hidden verb: reads profiles and supervisors as JSON on stdin, restarts each once per host gateway process, prints verified, attempted and failed buckets
- `recovery_attr_{unix,windows}.go` — detaches the recovery child into its own session or console-less process group (2 files)

#### Fleet verification and the owed-restart obligation

After the restart a version matrix is printed: one row per profile gateway (`profile`, `pid`, `code_sha`, `code_version`, `state`, `code_root`, `served_profiles`) with state `current`, `stale`, `restart_pending`, `down`, `external` or `unknown`, polled over a settle window. A gateway proven stale is drained once more; anything still not current keeps the restart owed as a follow-up and as a host obligation record that every later launch warns about until the live fleet proves current.

- `fleet_versions.go` — `CollectFleetVersions`: per-profile socket identity, code root of each gateway, row classification, matrix printing
- `fleet_verify.go` — `verifyFleetAfterUpdate`, settle polling, crediting failed units proven current, owed inventory on the obligation, legacy unit warning
- `fleet_obligation.go` — arms, reads, discharges the obligation; decides from receipt, marker inventory and live fleet whether a restart is still owed; `WarnPendingFleetRestartOnStartup`
- `fleet_gatewayless.go` — a host where no profile expects a gateway and none runs owes no restart
- `fleet_checkout.go` — `CheckoutContains`: whether a sha is an ancestor of the running code (build stamp or `git merge-base` without lazy fetch); defines `fleetProjectRoot`
- `update_cmd_stale_survivors.go` — drain-first restart of live gateways the matrix stamped stale that the restart phase never touched
- `receipt_rows.go` — [py-shim] dict and list access helpers with Python error texts for decoded receipt and request JSON

#### Windows launcher and quarantine repair at startup

Startup hooks, Windows only. Old updaters renamed locked `venv\Scripts\*.exe` shims to `<name>.exe.old.<unix ms>`; nothing in this codebase creates those names any more, but the sweep still restores a shim whose original is missing, deletes quarantine files older than 15 minutes, and drops matching `PendingFileRenameOperations` registry entries. A second hook re-stages the `icebath` and `icebath-acp` launchers in `<home>\bin` or a legacy `<install>\bin` when they vanished or still boot through a venv.

- `install_repair.go` — `CleanupQuarantinedExes`, `RestoreQuarantinedShims`, `EnsureWindowsBinLaunchers`, `RecoverPausedGateways` startup entry, and the configured-feature gap scan handed to `pkg/pm`
- `install_repair_{other,windows}.go` — registry user `PATH` read and pending-rename cleanup; process `PATH` and no-op elsewhere (2 files)

#### `icebath doctor`: walk, rows and summary

`RunDoctor` loads `.env`, prints a banner and the build line, runs the checks in a fixed order, optionally runs live probes (`--live`), and prints a summary; exit 1 when any issue remains. `--fix` lets individual checks repair what they found; `--ack <id>` only dismisses one security advisory. Repairs performed with `--fix`: create an empty `.env` (0600), seed `config.yaml` from the template or defaults, create missing home subdirectories, write a `SOUL.md` template, rebuild a corrupt `state.db` FTS index or malformed schema, checkpoint an oversized WAL, remove duplicate Windows gateway logon launchers, republish the `icebath` commands in the user bin, bring helper programs to this version's pins, fetch Chromium through pm, and install the macOS TCC anchor.

- `doctor.go` — check order table, `RunDoctor`, advisory ack, summary, OAuth status rows for Codex, MiniMax and xAI, parallel connectivity section
- `doctor_report.go` — `Doctor` and `Finding` (auto-fixable issues, manual issues, fix count), ok, warn, fail and info row printers, guarded check wrapper, `doctorEnsureDir`

#### `icebath doctor`: configuration, state and platform checks

The static checks over one home. Sections in order include Security Advisories, MCP Server Security, Runtime and SQLite, SSL / CA Certificates, optional capabilities, Configuration Files, config drift, xAI Model Retirement, Auth Providers, Directory Structure, `state.db`, cron store, checkpoint store, gateway supervision and command installation.

- `doctor_state.go` — home layout, `SOUL.md`, memory files, scratch dir, cache hogs, `state.db` health, repair, stats and WAL, cron store, checkpoint cap, Skills Hub, memory provider, plugins disabled by an update or listed twice, profiles and orphan aliases
- `doctor_platform.go` — compromised-package advisories, Go and linked SQLite versions, journal mode and holders of every managed database, TLS trust store, optional capability rows, systemd linger, s6 slots, Windows autostart duplicates, `icebath` on `PATH` and published commands
- `doctor_platform_fda.go` — macOS Full Disk Access probe by listing `~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC`, with the settings link when denied
- `doctor_platform_manager.go` — binds the staged tool-runtime row and the macOS interpreter TCC anchor row (installed with `--fix`)

#### `icebath doctor`: tools, connectivity, live probes and tier rows

Checks of external programs and the network. Connectivity probes run on at most eight workers with a ten-second limit per phase and no redirects; `--live` adds one bounded real call per configured tool backend with timeout `doctor.live_probe_timeout`.

- `doctor_tools.go` — git and ripgrep (pm store first, then `PATH`), terminal backend (Docker or Podman, SSH batch probe, Daytona, Vercel, plugin backends), Node.js, Chromium and Lightpanda, WhatsApp session, Termux notes, per-toolset availability and setup gaps

- `doctor_tier_extras.go` — binds rows for voice, wake word, `execute_code`, browser tools and the cron store, and the Chromium launch probe, when the extras tier is linked
- `doctor_tier_plugins.go` — binds rows for Discord voice, FFmpeg, Matrix E2EE and the WhatsApp session, and local speech probes, when the plugins tier is linked

#### `icebath dump` and `icebath debug share`

`dump` prints a plain-text support summary: version, OS, Go version, profile, home, model, provider, terminal backend, API keys as set or not (first and last four characters with `--show-keys`), toolsets, MCP server count, memory provider, gateway status, platforms, cron jobs, skill count and config overrides. `debug share` uploads that dump plus log tails (`agent` 200 lines by default, `errors`, `gateway` and `update` at most 100) as a report, and the full `agent.log`, `gateway.log` and `update.log` (512 kB cap each), to paste.rs with dpaste.com as fallback, after a privacy notice and confirmation; `--local` prints instead. Secrets are redacted before upload unless `--no-redact`; paste.rs uploads are recorded in `<home>/pastes/pending.json` and deleted after six hours by a sweep that runs on every debug command and in the gateway. `debug delete <url>` removes paste.rs pastes.

- `debug_redaction.go` — support-text redaction: sensitive URL parameters (raw and percent-encoded), header values, secret argv flags, bearer credentials, optional length cap
- `debug_gateway_slash.go` — the gateway `/debug` slash command forms: local redacted report with no network call, and summary-only upload reply
- `debug_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports `SweepExpiredPastes` for the gateway housekeeping hook

#### `icebath status`

One-screen summary by default; `--full` (alias `--all`) or `--deep` prints every section: header, environment, API keys, OAuth providers, API-key providers, terminal backend, messaging platforms, gateway service and rows, cron, sessions, deep checks, footer.

- `status_auth.go` — OAuth provider blocks with expiry formatting, API key rows, API-key provider rows

#### `icebath fallback check`

Checks every entry of the model fallback chain statically and, with the live flag, probes the ready fixed routes in parallel using the doctor probe runner; `auto` and `moa` are never probed. Registered on the provider package's fallback command dispatcher and also called by the TUI server.

- `fallback_check.go` — `RunFallbackChecks`, seven-column table and JSON output, `FallbackCheckCommand`

#### `icebath security audit`

On-demand supply-chain scan against api.osv.dev: PyPI distributions in the pm-committed Python environment, exact Python pins declared by plugins under `<home>/plugins`, and pinned `npx` or `uvx` MCP server packages in config. Flags `--json`, `--fail-on <severity>` (default critical), `--skip-venv`, plugin and MCP skips; exit 1 when a finding meets the threshold.

- `security_audit.go` — component discovery, batched OSV queries, advisory detail fetch in parallel, severity tiers and fixed versions, human and JSON reports, `CmdSecurityAudit`

### `pkg/selfupdate/updaterecord` — on-disk records of an update: receipt, lock, pause, restart obligation, and the version identity

*28 files, 7,349 Go lines*

Leaf package that the updater, `pkg/pm` and the gateway share so they need not import each other; about twenty packages import it, most only for `GetVersionInfo`, `GetCodeIdentity`, `BuildVersion` and `UserAgent`. It defines the update receipt and where it is written, the two-layer update lock, the paused-gateways record, the host restart obligation, the custody-aware git runner, and the version identity of the running build. Files it owns: `<root home>/logs/update_receipts/update_<date>_<time>_<pid>_<update id>.json` and `latest.json` (also mirrored into a named profile's logs), `<root home>/.icebath-update-in-progress` plus `.lock` sidecar, `.icebath-update.lock` in the install tree (or `icebath-update.lock` in the git common dir), `<root home>/.icebath-update-paused-gateways.<12-hex install key>.json` with claim and retired files, `<XDG state>/icebath/gateway-locks/host-update-restart-<16 hex>.json`, and `<home>/.update_exit_code`. Scaffolding: Python truthiness and `int()` helpers, receipt state kept per context to mimic ContextVars, and two exported test seams.

#### Update receipt

One JSON document per `icebath update` run, written durably when the run begins (outcome `running`) and rewritten at each stage, so a killed run is visible. Fields: `schema` 1, `update_id`, `started_at`, `finished_at`, `argv`, `pid`, `outcome` (running, success, partial, failed, refused, interrupted), `stop_reason`, `pre_update` and `post_update` code identity, `steps`, `skips`, `stages`, `followups`, `user_action`, `gateway_restart` (restarted services, relaunched profiles, killed pids, failed units, fresh-recovery buckets), `fleet`, plus the plan and pm sync sections. The newest 20 run files are kept; a later launch marks a `running` record whose process is gone as interrupted.

- `receipt.go` — `UpdateReceipt`, begin, record step, skip, stage, fact, follow-up, finalize exactly once, command-boundary safety net, interrupted-run reconciliation, pruning, latest-receipt readers, git stop classes; `WriteLatest`, `RunFile`, `ReceiptPayload`, `ClearCurrentReceipt` have no callers
- `receipt_reset.go`, `receipt_resume.go` — restore the enclosing receipt; reopen a run from its persisted data in a completion child
- `exit_code.go` — `<home>/.update_exit_code` (`0` or `1`) that the gateway's update watcher polls for a `/update` run

#### Update lock: shared marker and checkout lock

Two layers.
