The marker `<root home>/.icebath-update-in-progress` is a text claim (pid, start time, `ct:<process creation time>`, optional `delegate:` and `run:` lines) mutated only under a kernel lock on its sidecar and judged by pid and process creation time (2 s tolerance); a claim whose owner is alive but unprovable is honoured for at most 20 minutes. The checkout lock is a kernel lock on a file in the install tree that child processes inherit (POSIX descriptors, or lease bytes and a job object on Windows), so it stays held while any update child lives. A process tree may re-enter its own claim as delegate.

- `lock.go` — paths, marker parsing and liveness judgement (`JudgeMarker`), process creation time, `GitCommonDir`
- `lock_claim.go` — `UpdateLock` acquire and release, exclusive publish, adopt-or-refuse for ancestors and the handoff partner (`ICEBATH_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID`), checkout lock take and join, `ReadLiveUpdate`, `DescribeHolder`, `UpdateInProgress`
- `lock_claim_{unix,windows}.go` — `flock` on POSIX; byte-range owner and 16 lease locks, kill-on-close job and suspended-child resume on Windows; `SwapUpdateTreeJob` has no caller (2 files)
- `lock_probe_{unix,windows}.go` — pid liveness (zombie-aware) and creation time from `/proc` or `ps`, or process handles and `GetProcessTimes` (2 files)
- `lock_ticks_{linux,other}.go` — clock ticks per second for `/proc` start times (2 files)

#### Custody git runner

Runs git on behalf of the update with the right containment: a parent-death signal or owner watcher on POSIX, suspended start and job binding on Windows, tree kill on timeout. Also classifies which git subcommands write the local tree, and keeps the first refused child of a run for the failure message.

- `custody_run.go` — `RunGitQuery`, `GitArgv`, `IsLocalMutator`, `RefuseCustodyChild`, `RefusalNotice`, `CheckoutHeld`, timeout and refusal error types
- `custody_run_{linux,nodeathsig,unix,windows}.go` — `Pdeathsig` on Linux, none on other Unixes, owner watcher process, job-bound run on Windows (4 files)

#### Host restart obligation

A per-install record on the host, outside any profile home, saying "the gateways of this install still owe a restart onto sha X": `version` 1, `started`, `pid`, `armed_by_profile`, `expected_sha`, `owners`, `found` (what the first owner found, restored on release), `inventory` of owed runtimes, and `restarted` (sha, pid, time) once the host restarted. Armed before the tree moves, released or cleared after verification; a legacy per-home `fleet_restart_pending` marker and an unkeyed `host-update-restart.json` are still read.

- `obligation.go` — `HostObligationPath`, arm, read, release, clear, mark completed, legacy field view, collapse of units sharing a host process

#### Paused-gateways record

Persistent token of the gateways an update stopped, so they can be resumed by this run, by a later launch, or by the next update if this one is killed. Carries profiles, unmapped pids and argv, services or units, stop requests and markers, the owner identity, a tree baseline (HEAD and dirty-file digests) and move targets; orphaned records are claimed, merged and retired under a mutex with a retired-id list to prevent double resume. A resume is refused while the tree is torn or its dependencies are stale, and relaunch attempts back off from 60 s to one hour.

- `pause.go` — record path and key, identity of a process, mutex, atomic write, read, stop-accepted and stop-consumed marks the gateway writes
- `pause_record.go` — write, sync, discharge, claim and adopt orphans, redundancy sweep, absorb another pause, resume under the checkout lock with backoff, `RecoverPauses` at startup
- `pause_tree.go` — tree baseline stamping, torn-tree detection after a move, `TreeIsWhole`, git executable choice

#### Version identity

What build is running, for `--version`, banners, receipts, user agents and the fleet matrix: from `install-stamp.json` in the install tree first, then the linker-stamped version and embedded VCS revision, then unknown. Derives a display version with distance, short commit and dirty marker.

- `version.go` — `VersionInfo`, `SetBuildVersion`, `GetVersionInfo`, `GetCodeIdentity`, `ReadCheckoutSHA`, `UserAgent`, stable tag pattern, stamp validation
- `version_git.go` — `GitVersionInfo`: identity of a checkout from git, including nearest release tag and distance
- `update_status.go` — `UpdateAvailableNoCount` (-1): an update exists but the commit count is unknown

#### Test seams

[test-support] Exported seams with no non-test caller.

- `custody_run_export.go`, `obligation_stderr_export.go` — reset and redirect seams

#### Profile enumeration and logger

Two small helpers: the profile home enumeration the gateway uses to scope an update's fleet, and the package logger.

- `profile_homes.go` — `ProfileHomes`: default home plus every valid named profile directory; its one caller is `pkg/gateway/update_fleet_scope.go`
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `logger=updaterecord`

### `pkg/install` — `icebath install-self`: release install ladder, release selection and download, and the binary swap used by updates

*17 files, 2,126 Go lines*

Implements the hidden `install-self` verb that `scripts/install.sh`, `install.ps1` and `setup-icebath.sh` hand over to, and the release primitives `pkg/selfupdate` reuses (`PlanRelease`, `ApplyRelease`, `ReplaceFile`); `pkg/app` uses its tree classification for uninstall. It writes the binary and two config templates into the install tree (default `<home>/icebath-agent`), the stamps `.install_method`, `.install_repo` and `.icebath-bootstrap-complete` beside it, seeds the home, and edits shell startup files. It talks to the GitHub releases API, release download URLs and the smart-HTTP ref advertisement. Command publication, launchers and dependency download are delegated to `pkg/pm`; shell completions are not installed here. Little port scaffolding; the event sink abstraction has only the CLI sink.

#### Install ladder and stages

`Main` runs eight stages in order and stops at the first failure: `prerequisites` (supported OS and amd64 or arm64, Termux refused, parent directory writable), `repository` (place the binary, stamp method and repository), `config` (home subdirectories, `.env` 0600 and `config.yaml` from templates, recorded opt-outs), `products` (publish commands, wire `PATH`), `runtimes` (`icebath pm install`), `setup` (runs bare `icebath` on the controlling terminal for first-run setup), `gateway` (`icebath gateway install --if-missing`), `complete` (bootstrap marker, WinGet entry, saved channel). `setup` and `gateway` are skipped with `--non-interactive` or when no terminal can be opened. Signals map to exit 129, 130 or 143.

- `runner.go` — `Options`, `Runner`, `Main`, option validation and env fallbacks (`ICEBATH_REPO_URL`, `ICEBATH_INSTALL_CHANNEL`, `ICEBATH_INSTALL_DIR`), stage dispatch, signal handling, banner, shell reload hint
- `stage_impl.go` — the eight stage bodies, release target resolution (commit, stable, or newest release of a branch), `--binary` shortcut for an already verified binary, verified download with progress, `InstalledRelease` (asks a binary via `install-self --release-info`)
- `stages.go` — `StageNames` in run order
- `events.go` — `Event` and `LogStream`: one output line on stdout or stderr for the sink
- `console_{unix,windows}.go` — hides the console window of stage child processes on Windows (2 files)

#### Release selection, checksum verification and binary swap

Release archives are named `icebath_<version>_<os>_<arch>.tar.gz` (`.zip` on Windows) and hold the binary plus `cli-config.yaml.example` and `.env.example`. The expected SHA-256 comes from the release's `checksums.txt` and must agree with the API asset digest when one is published; there is no signature verification. Latest stable is found through the API, then the `releases/latest` redirect, then the highest advertised `vX.Y.Z` tag. The swap renames the staged binary over the installed one; on Windows the running binary is first moved aside to `<name>.old-<pid>`, and that file is not swept later.

- `release.go` — `ParseRepo`, release listing (ten pages of 100), `LatestStableRelease`, `LsRemote`, release for a commit or branch, `ExpectedSHA256`, HTTP client with proxy and timeouts, token from `ICEBATH_GITHUB_TOKEN` or `GITHUB_TOKEN`
- `release_archive.go` — archive naming, extraction of only the binary and companion files, placement beside the install binary
- `release_plan.go` — `PlanRelease`: chosen release ordered against the installed build by commit ancestry (compare API) or stable tags; `.install_repo` read and write
- `binary_update.go` — `ApplyRelease` (download, verify, unpack, swap), `ReplaceFile`, `.install_method` stamp with methods `script`, `winget`, `git`

#### Install tree identity, marker and paths

How other code tells an installer-created tree from a source checkout or a foreign tree: the bootstrap marker `.icebath-bootstrap-complete` (JSON with `schemaVersion`, `pinnedCommit`, `pinnedBranch`, `completedAt`) written only by the `complete` stage, and a `go.mod` module-path match for a source checkout.

- `paths.go` — `Home`, `InstallRootOf`, `InstallerCreated`, `IsSourceCheckout`, checkout update and installer command texts, atomic file copy, Windows-aware replace
- `marker.go` — bootstrap marker writer through a synced temp file; `ISO8601UTC`

#### Shell PATH wiring and source-checkout publish

On POSIX the user bin `~/.local/bin` is added to the login shell's startup files under the marker comment `# Icebath Agent command` unless a line already sets it up: `.zshrc` and `.zprofile` for zsh, `config.fish` for fish, otherwise `.bashrc`, `.profile` and existing `.bash_profile` or `.bash_login`. On Windows `PATH` registration is left to command publication in `<home>\bin`. `--from-checkout` publishes a checkout's built binary instead of a release.

- `shellpath.go` — `WireShellPath`, per-shell targets, guarded export line, already-configured detection
- `checkout.go` — `SetupFromCheckout` (stamp `git`, publish launchers, one rc edit, skills dir), `CopySkillsNoClobber`, `ResolvedPathsJSON` for `--show-resolved-paths`

#### WinGet Apps and Features entry

With `--install-method winget` the install registers `HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall\nickheyer.icebath` so WinGet can correlate and uninstall it (`icebath uninstall --yes`).

- `uninstall_entry.go` — registry key and identity constants
- `uninstall_entry_{other,windows}.go` — register and remove the entry on Windows; refusal and no-op elsewhere (2 files)

### `pkg/containerinit` — container init, service supervisor and s6-compatible verbs for the Docker image

*12 files, 2,424 Go lines*

Go replacement for s6-overlay and tini inside the image: one binary (`cmd/icebath-init`, also linked into `icebath` unless built `icebath_core`) that acts as `/init`, `tini`, `s6-svscan`, `s6-svc`, `s6-svstat`, `s6-svwait`, `s6-svscanctl`, `s6-setuidgid`, `with-contenv` and `s6-log` according to its program name, plus `container-init` and `container-health` as first arguments. As init it prepares the data volume (default `/opt/data`, or `ICEBATH_HOME`), supervises service directories under `/run/service`, runs the main program as the `icebath` account and reaps orphans. Linux only; everything is a no-op elsewhere. Native Go, no port scaffolding.

#### Init, main program and shutdown

`s6-svscan` becomes PID 1 or a subreaper, refuses an arbitrary `--user` uid with instructions, saves the container environment, writes `/run/s6/basedir/svscan.pid`, runs the bootstrap, starts the supervisor, runs `container-stage reconcile` as the account, then runs the main program (bare `icebath`, a command found on `PATH`, or `icebath <args>`) in its own process group with signals forwarded. When it exits, services are stopped within `S6_SERVICES_GRACETIME` (3 s default) and, as PID 1, everything left gets SIGTERM then SIGKILL after `S6_KILL_GRACETIME`.

- `init_linux.go` — `Dispatch` by program name, `runSvscan`, shutdown, `DropRootInImage` (re-executes a root `docker exec icebath` as the account unless `ICEBATH_DOCKER_EXEC_AS_ROOT`)
- `dispatch_other.go` — non-Linux stubs of `Dispatch` and `DropRootInImage`
- `names.go`, `paths_linux.go` — verb and binary names; image layout (`/opt/icebath`, `/opt/data`, `/run/service`, `/run/s6/container_environment`, `/etc/icebath/*`), `DataHome`, `ChromiumPinPath`

#### Volume bootstrap: UID/GID remap, ownership and seeding

Runs as root before any service. Remaps the `icebath` account to `ICEBATH_UID`/`ICEBATH_GID` (aliases `PUID`/`PGID`, range 1 to 65534) with `usermod` and `groupmod`, joins the group owning a mounted Docker socket, chowns the home and known state files without following symlinks, creates the standard subdirectories and `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`, removes a stale `docker` `.install_method` from the volume, seeds `.env`, `config.yaml` and `SOUL.md` from image defaults, generates `API_SERVER_KEY` into `.env` unless the environment supplies one, grants group access to the Fly Machines API socket, seeds `auth.json` from `ICEBATH_AUTH_JSON_BOOTSTRAP` and a running gateway state from `ICEBATH_GATEWAY_BOOTSTRAP_STATE`, then delegates dependency refresh and skills sync to the account.

- `bootstrap_linux.go` — `runBootstrap` and each step, symlink-component refusal, the arbitrary-uid error texts
- `accounts_linux.go` — `/etc/passwd` and `/etc/group` lookup, child credentials, thread credential switch before exec, shadow tool runners
- `creds_linux_32.go`, `creds_linux_std.go` — `setuid`/`setgid` syscall numbers for 32-bit and other ABIs

#### Service supervisor

Each directory under the scan dir with an executable `run` is supervised: started in its own session, restarted with a delay doubling from one second to a one-minute cap until a run lasts ten seconds, `finish` run with exit code and signal (exit 125 means stay down; 5 s limit or `timeout-finish`), optional `log/run` logger fed by a pipe, a `down` file keeping it stopped. State is persisted atomically to `supervise/status.json`, and control arrives over FIFOs with s6 command letters.

- `supervise_linux.go` — reaper table, `service` state machine, control FIFO reader, scan and prune, halt letters, ordered stop of services then loggers

#### s6 control verbs, environment and health

The command-line side of the supervisor, each verb selected by the program name it is invoked under, plus the Docker `HEALTHCHECK` verb.

- `verbs_linux.go` — `s6-svc` (letters `udoOxtrhiq12akpcy`), `s6-svstat` (line or `-o` fields), `s6-svwait` (exit 99 on timeout), `s6-svscanctl`, `tini` flag stripping, `container-health` (init alive and every wanted service up and ready)
- `env_linux.go` — container environment snapshot as one file per variable, `with-contenv` (honours `S6_KEEP_ENV`), `s6-setuidgid` by name or `uid:gid`
- `log_linux.go` — `s6-log`: script directives for keep count, size cap, ISO and TAI64N timestamps, select and deselect patterns, locked log directory with rotation to `@<tai64n>.s` and rotate on SIGALRM

### `pkg/containerinit/stage` — bootstrap steps the init runs as the service account

*2 files, 125 Go lines*

Separate package so the init does not import the product: `icebath container-stage <step>` is dispatched early in the main binary and exits. It is called by the bootstrap and init in `pkg/containerinit` and by the image build.

#### Delegated container steps

Four steps that need the product's packages (pm, skills, gateway CLI), each run as a child process under the service account.

- `stage_linux.go` — `dependencies` (pm refresh, collect generations unused for a day), `skills-sync`, `reconcile` (`gatewaycli.ContainerBootMain` writes the service directories), `image-tools` (symlinks pm's python3, node, npm, npx, ffmpeg, ffprobe, rg into `/usr/local/bin` and pins Chromium)
- `stage_other.go` — non-Linux no-op

### `pkg/backup` — `icebath backup`, `icebath import`, quick state snapshots and safe SQLite copy and restore

*21 files, 4,269 Go lines*

Owns the full zip backup of the icebath home, its import, and the quick snapshots under `<home>/state-snapshots/` that the update, the `/snapshot` slash command (`pkg/gatewaycli`), session repair and the TUI use; `VerifySQLiteIntegrity` and `SafeRestoreDB` are also called by the updater and doctor. Bound to the CLI in `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go`. There is no scheduler: backups happen on demand, before an update (`pre-update-*`), and before an agent import (`pre-migration-*`). A lock file `.backup.lock` in the home serialises writers (0.25 s wait; a full backup exits 2 when busy, an automatic one is skipped). Restores take the gateway's exclusive maintenance reservation for every affected home. Scaffolding: Python zipfile and pathlib emulation (`pyzip`, `pypath`), Python error class names, many test seams as package variables.

#### Full backup: file selection and archive writing

`icebath backup [-o path] [--keep N]` writes a deflate level 6 zip of the root home (all profiles) to `~/icebath-backup-<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMMSS>.zip` through a hidden `.partial` sibling renamed on success. Every `*.db` goes in as a consistent snapshot taken through the SQLite backup API; files the active memory provider declares outside the home but inside the user home are added under `_external/`. Excluded: the `icebath-agent` install tree at the root, `backups`, `state-snapshots`, `checkpoints`, browser profiles, secret caches, the root trees `models`, `runtimes`, `node`, `installs` and `tools`, everything under `cache` except `images`, `audio`, `videos`, `documents`, `screenshots`, `citations` and generated files, VCS and Python or Node dependency dirs, SQLite sidecars, `.pyc`, `gateway.pid`, `cron.pid`, emergency and retired `state.db` copies, symlinks and non-regular files. A file that cannot be added is listed and the archive is reported incomplete; `--keep` (default 3) prunes older `icebath-backup-*.zip` in the output directory only after a complete run.

- `run_backup.go` — `RunBackup`, backup slot lock, atomic output, memory-provider external paths, zip entry loop with failed-member truncation, summary and pruning; two exported test seams (`SwapMemoryProviderExternalPaths`, `SwapGatewayService`)
- `files.go` — exclusion tables and `iterBackupFiles` walk
- `files_{other,windows}.go` — Windows reparse-point detection so junctions are not followed (2 files)
- `backup_lock_{unix,windows}.go` — gives an empty lock file the byte Windows byte-range locking needs (2 files)
- `auto_backup.go` — `CreatePreUpdateBackup` and `CreatePreMigrationBackup` into `<home>/backups/` (keep 5), an incomplete archive published as `*.incomplete.zip` salvage (newest one kept), abort when a database snapshot fails

#### Safe SQLite copy and integrity check

Every database enters a backup or snapshot as a consistent copy, never a raw file copy, and is verified before any restore; a copy that cannot be made safely is reported and skipped.

- `backup_sqlite.go` — `safeCopyDB`: backup API from a read-only source with a 10 s busy window; rollback-journal databases copied in 0.1 s steps with up to 20 restarts, refused when the read lock would be held over 0.25 s
- `secure_create_{unix,windows}.go` — pre-creates the destination 0600 without following a symlink; no-op on Windows (2 files)
- `integrity.go` — `VerifySQLiteIntegrity`: size at least 100 bytes, header magic, then `PRAGMA integrity_check`, or a schema probe above the size cap

#### Quick state snapshots

A snapshot is a directory `<home>/state-snapshots/<UTC YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>[-label][-n]/` holding copies of the critical state files and a `manifest.json` (`id`, `timestamp`, `label`, `file_count`, `total_size`, `files` with sizes, `failed_dbs`, `oversized_skipped`), built in a private `.partial` directory, modes 0700 and 0600. Captured: `state.db`, `config.yaml`, `.env`, `auth.json`, `cron/jobs.json`, `cron/executions.db`, gateway state and channel files, `processes.json`, `projects.db`, `response_store.db`, `memory_store.db`, `verification_evidence.db`, `kanban.db`, `kanban/boards` (without workspaces and attachments), pairing stores. The newest 20 are kept; pruning is skipped when a database failed or was skipped for size.

- `quick_create.go` — `CreateQuickSnapshot`, `RunQuickBackup` for `icebath backup --quick [--label]`, per-file size limit, pre-update snapshots of every sibling profile
- `quick_snapshot.go` — snapshot root, listing with a placeholder entry for an unreadable manifest, id validation against path traversal, pruning
- `all_profiles.go` — `SiblingProfileHomes`: every other profile of the install
- `doctor_exports.go` — [port-artifact] `QuickStateFiles` accessor for doctor's database list

#### Restore and import

`icebath import <zip> [--force]` validates that the archive looks like an icebath backup, strips a leading `.icebath/` or `icebath/` prefix, confirms overwrite when the target already has config, checks every member's CRC before writing anything, reserves every touched profile, then publishes each member atomically. Runtime files (`gateway_state.json`, pid and lock files, `processes.json`), the root trees `installs`, `tools` and all of `cache`, and SQLite sidecars are never overwritten, so the durable cache subdirectories a backup archives are not restored by import; secrets are tightened to 0600; databases are restored page by page into the live file so its inode survives, with an unlink-and-move fallback refused while any process holds the file. Afterwards profile alias wrappers are recreated and an installed gateway service is started. Snapshot restore follows the same rules and merges `auth.json` under the auth store lock without rolling back live single-use OAuth grants; a `state.db` restore never lowers the destination's runtime epoch.

- `import.go` — `RunImport`, member classification, path traversal blocking, reservation of affected homes, shrunken-session-store warning, profile alias restore, gateway revive
- `restore.go` — `safeRestoreDB` and epoch floor handling, page restore and file-replace fallback, `/proc` scan for foreign holders, `auth.json` merge restore, atomic member extraction preserving mode and owner, archive validation and prefix detection
- `restore_{unix,windows}.go` — link count, full mode bits, staged file mode and default new-file mode per OS (2 files)
- `quick_restore.go` — `RestoreQuickSnapshot` (offline, all-or-refuse on epoch proof); `RestoreCronJobsIfEmptied` and `RestoreConfigModelSettingsIfRewritten` with all-profile forms, whose only caller is the unwired update safety net

#### Logger

Package-wide logging helper.

- `log.go` — package logger tagged `logger=backup`

### `pkg/pm` — in-binary package manager: pinned tool store, uv-driven Python environments, extras, launchers and install recovery

*169 files, 39,585 Go lines*

Owns everything icebath downloads and installs for itself at runtime, in two halves split by build tags: the binary store (untagged files, linked into every build) fetches sha256-pinned upstream archives named in the embedded `lock.json` into `<root home>/tools` and composes their `PATH` and env for callers (`pm.Ensure`, `pm.Installed`, `pm.EnvFor`: Chromium for the browser tool, cua-driver for computer use, llama.cpp backends for local models, Node and npm for MCP bridges, plugin sidecars and the Photon and hallmark helpers, tools a skill declares; the catalogue also carries ffmpeg, ripgrep, gh, bws, iron-proxy, whisper.cpp and Git for Windows). The package manager proper (54 files tagged `!icebath_core && !icebath_noextras`, absent from the `icebath-core` and `icebath-noextras` builds, where the facade in `manager.go` answers with a "this build leaves it out" refusal) drives the pinned `uv` and CPython to build virtualenvs: one shared plugin environment, one environment per extra of the embedded `extras_lock.json` (TTS, STT, wake word, document, Google and YouTube skills), the NeMo Relay runtime, and named side environments (LSP servers from PyPI); it also carries the `icebath pm` command family bound in `pkg/commands/cli_tree_pm*.go`. State lives under the root home: `tools/` (store entries, `facts.json`, `.install.lock`), `installs/<first 16 hex of sha256 of the install tree path>/` (`facts.json`, `environments/`, `extras/`, `relay-venv`, `core/`, `publication.json`, `declined-*.json`, `.recovery.lock`), `cache/partials`, `cache/uv`, plus `<active home>/environments/<name>` and `<active home>/logs/update_receipts`. There is no icebath registry: every artifact is an upstream URL with a pinned sha256 (GitHub releases, nodejs.org, the npm registry, cdn.playwright.dev, packages.termux.dev, files.pythonhosted.org, download.pytorch.org), the single icebath-hosted source being GitHub release mirrors of Termux pool archives. The package is on the startup path because the launcher concept lives here: `RepoRoot` is the directory of the running executable, `LauncherStart` strips the hidden home-pin flag and Python env vars, `PinLauncherHome` pins `ICEBATH_HOME`, and in full builds `selfupdate.BootLaunch` (from `cmd/icebath/link_extras.go`) then calls `RecoverIfNeeded` and `ActivateDependencies` on every launch. A large share is Python-project residue: 65 of 165 Go files import `internal/py*`, every error carries a Python exception class name (`PyError`, used 57 times outside the package), and the tree this repository builds from has no `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` or `package.json`, so the `uv.lock` relock, pre-pm venv migration and startup repair paths have no input here.

#### Launcher bootstrap and published commands

A launcher is a tiny wrapper (`#!/bin/sh` script, or `.cmd` on Windows) that execs the install's own `icebath` binary; it records the tool store it was published for in an `icebath-store` comment line so a second home borrowing the checkout never rebinds it. Persisted service and helper commands use `<binary> --icebath-pin-default-home[=HOME] ...`, which `LauncherStart` consumes first thing in `main` (setting `ICEBATH_HOME` when unset, unsetting `PYTHONHOME`, `PYTHONPATH` and, when pinned, `VIRTUAL_ENV`). Published names are `icebath` and `icebath-acp` (runs `acp`) under `<tree>/.icebath/bin`, with forwarding conveniences plus `icebath-agent` (runs the `__icebath_run_agent__` entry) in `~/.local/bin`, and in `<root home>/bin` and `/usr/local/bin` where the install already owns a launcher; on Windows the commands go to `<root home>/bin`, which is added to the User PATH. The need is real for a Go binary (stable service command, PATH exposure, multi-install safety); the `.exe` shim parsing, venv-bound exe detection and emulated import path are Python-installer leftovers.

- `launchers_runtime.go` — `LauncherStart`, `PinLauncherHome`, `InstallRuntimeCommand`/`InstallationCommand` argv builders, and `--print-runtime-command [--module M]` (JSON argv); its `pm publish-launchers OUT_DIR` branch has no caller and is unreachable
- `launchers.go` — reads `install-stamp.json` (`updateMechanism` self or external), writes atomic sh/cmd wrappers, detects ownership of existing launchers, `ExposeCLI` PATH conveniences gated by config `cli.expose_on_path`, Windows stale-exe retirement
- `launchers_console.go` — decodes a Windows UTF-16 environment block to learn which `ICEBATH_HOME` a new console of this user resolves
- `launchers_{unix,windows}.go` — execute-bit test and path normcase; Windows reads the user environment block, prepends `<root home>/bin` to the registry User PATH and broadcasts the change

#### Install tree identity, stamp and path resolution

Decides which tree, store and install-state directory a process uses. Store precedence: context override, `ICEBATH_RUNTIME_DIR`, the `store` key of a sealed payload `manifest.json` (keys `repo`, `venv`, `store`, `target`, `runtime.commands.icebath`, `runtime.storePython`), `runtimeDir` of the nearest `install-stamp.json`, the tools dir of the home that already owns the checkout's state, else `<root home>/tools`. A store beside a `manifest.json` is sealed (read-only) and writes go to `<root home>/tools`; no producer of such a manifest exists under `packaging`, `scripts`, `docker` or `nix` in this repository.

- `paths.go` — `RepoRoot`, `InstallRoot` (`ICEBATH_INSTALL_ROOT`), `InstallStampPath`, `StoreRoot`/`WritableStoreRoot`, `InstallKey`, `InstallsRoot`/`InstallStateDir`, `OwningHomeRoot`, payload manifest reader, `PartialsRoot`, venv bin and interpreter paths, a Python-style `realpath`
- `dunder_version.go` — `DunderVersion`: the `baseVersion` of the install stamp, `0.0.0` when absent
- `git_fingerprint.go` — reads `.git` HEAD, packed-refs and worktree commondir without spawning git to fingerprint a checkout; used for gateway code-skew detection, the Termux bundled-skills sync fingerprint and the update bytecode-sweep stamp
- `live_checkout_guard.go` — production file importing `testing`: reports the running checkout while `go test` or `PYTEST_CURRENT_TEST` drives the process so automatic repair skips it
- `log.go` — package logger tagged `pm`

#### Tool lockfile and installed-state facts

`lock.json` is `{"schema": 1, "packages": {name: {"version", "artifacts": {target or "any": {"url", "sha256"} or a list of such rows}}}}` and pins 18 tools for nine targets (`win32-x64`, `win32-arm64`, `linux-x64`, `linux-arm64`, `linux-x64-musl`, `linux-arm64-musl`, `linux-arm64-bionic`, `darwin-x64`, `darwin-arm64`); a list means several archives merged into one entry. `facts.json` has the same envelope and records per tool `entry`, `version`, `env` (store root templated as `{{store}}`), `target`, `artifacts` (sha list) and `digest` (tree digest), and for the `venv` state `stamp`, `extras`, `environment`, `resolved_lock`. A damaged facts file is copied aside as `.corrupt` and read as empty.

- `lock.go` — `Lockfile` (snapshot, `SetPin`, conflict-checked `Save` under a `.<name>.lock` byte lock raising `StaleLockRowError`), `Facts` (merge-on-write `Record`, `RecordState`, `Retain`, `Forget`, `EntriesInUse`), JSON deep-equality helpers
- `lock.json` — [data] embedded pins of bws, chromium, cua-driver, ffmpeg, gh, git, iron-proxy, five llamacpp backends, node, npm, python 3.14, ripgrep, uv, whispercpp-cpu; read by every install
- `.lock.json.lock` — [stray] zero-byte advisory lock file `Lockfile.Save` creates beside `lock.json` during `pm lock --bump` or `pm update`; committed by accident

#### Byte store: extraction, tree digest and atomic publish

A store is one directory of immutable entries named `<name>-<version>-<target>`, with `.staging-*` scratch dirs, `fetch-<sha256>/` download caches, `.previous-*` rollback copies and `.reclaim-*` trees a held file prevented deleting. Extraction is the security boundary: tar members pass a reimplementation of Python's `data` filter (no absolute paths, no escapes through `..` or links, no device or special files, modes masked to 0755 and made owner read-write), zip names are sanitised, and symlinks are judged from their own directory.

- `store.go` — `CurrentTarget` (arch plus musl or bionic detection from ELF loader strings), `HashURL`, tar and zip extraction with containment, `FlattenSingleDir`, `MergeTree`, `TreeDigest`, `Store` (`FetchMany`, `Scratch`, `Publish`, `InstallLock`)
- `tarfile_reader.go` — [py-shim] full port of Python `tarfile` reading (ustar, GNU, pax, sparse; gzip, bzip2, xz, lzma, lzip, zstd) with Python's exact exception classes and messages; only the store and deb unpacker need it
- `tarfile_reader_{unix,windows}.go` — set an extracted member's access and modification times (utimensat or SetFileTime)
- `filesystem.go` — Windows long-path spelling, junction test, polling byte locks (`LockFD`, `LockPath`), `DurableWriteBytes` (temp file, fsync, rename, directory fsync), `RetryHeld`, `RemoveTree`, `FileDigest`
- `filesystem_{unix,windows}.go` — flock versus one-byte LockFileEx, reparse-tag read, held-file and permission errno classes, `unlink` that refuses directories
- `access_{unix,windows}.go` — may this process execute a file (X_OK on unix, always true on Windows)

#### File copy with metadata

[py-shim] Reproduces Python `shutil.copy2`, `copyfile` and `copystat` (times, mode bits, xattrs, BSD flags, CopyFile2 on Windows); used to copy bundled store entries, the uv cache seed and plugin trees.

- `packages_copy.go` — `copy2`, `copyFileData` (refuses same file and named pipes), `copyStat`
- `packages_{bsd,linux,otheros,otherunix,posix,windows}.go` — per-OS access time, xattr and flag copying, CopyFile2 fallback, and `hideWindow` (CREATE_NO_WINDOW for console children on Windows)

#### Resumable pinned downloader

One `Download` fetches a plan of sources with up to 8 parallel 1 MiB range requests, checkpoints coverage every 5 s to a `.ranges` JSON sidecar beside the `.part` file under `<root home>/cache/partials` (key is the sha256 of the URL, owned through a byte lock on `.locks/<key>`), resumes only when length, strong ETag and pinned sha256 still match, verifies the sha256, then copies durably into place. Redirects must stay on https (plain http only loopback to loopback); a pause flag stops between chunks keeping partials; mirrors take over on 401, 403, 404, 410, 5xx, DNS failure or transient errors. It is also used outside the store by local model downloads (`pkg/provider`), local STT models (`pkg/media`) and installer staging and binary update (`pkg/install`).

- `downloader.go` — `Download`, `Source`, `DownloadError` kinds (failed, range, hash, paused, transport), `PauseEvent`, `ProgressFunc` with per-destination byte ranges, probe, ranged and single-stream transfer, sidecar, finalize; user agent `Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) icebath-pm/1.0`
- `download_state.go` — `PartialLock` and `CollectPartials`: unowned `.part`/`.ranges` pairs older than six hours are deleted by gc
- `network.go` — `HTTPError`, transient classification (TLS trust failures never retried), `RetryNetwork` (four failures without progress, exponential backoff honouring Retry-After, 30 s or 300 s caps), `EdgeBlock` wording for Cloudflare and Vercel firewall refusals
- `pinned_source.go` — `PinnedSource`: npm tarballs follow the user's registry, Termux pool URLs gain a fallback `termux-<sha256>.<ext>` asset on this build's icebath GitHub release (`SetBuildTag`, else latest)
- `index_config_base.go` — npm registry resolution (`npm_config_registry`, then the user `.npmrc`, else registry.npmjs.org), `~` expansion, strict UTF-8 check

#### Package model and registry

A package definition says what a tool is (name, deps, per-target gaps, optional, default, internal, off-PATH); versions and hashes live only in the lockfile. Verification checks the binary exists, matches the target architecture by reading PE, ELF or Mach-O headers, and on the native target passes a `--version` smoke probe within 60 s.

- `package.go` — `Package` interface, `BasePackage` defaults, `InstallError` (package, cause, remedy), `EnvDiff` and `ComposeEnv`, `DebPackage` (ar and tar extraction of `.deb`, zstd data, never dpkg or scripts), `MachineMatchesBinary`, `Runner`
- `registry.go` — name registry, dependency-first `Walk` with cycle refusal, `SourceInstallPackages`/`ToolRoots`, and `PackageDefinitions` identity checks that only matter to a foreign-checkout worker
- `packages.go` — `BinaryPackage` (one binary per archive, flatten, probe), `bionicDebArm` (Termux deb on Android, archive elsewhere), child process runner with capture and timeout, registration of the built-in catalogue
- `binary_rel_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports `BinaryPackage.Rel`

#### Tool catalogue and upstream sources

Each definition knows its download URL shape, staging fix-ups and env contribution; the `*_manager.go` files add "what is the newest version" lookups used only by `pm update`.

- `packages_runtimes.go` — uv (astral-sh releases; internal, depends on python), python (python-build-standalone `install_only`; macOS re-sign, `python3.exe` copy on Windows), node (nodejs.org, unofficial musl builds; libatomic repair), npm (self-installed offline with the pinned node)
- `packages_tools.go` — git (PortableGit self-extractor, Windows only), gh, ffmpeg (BtbN, martin-riedl on macOS), ripgrep (static musl build), cua-driver (default; telemetry off in probes), chromium (default; Chrome for Testing laid out for Playwright, sets `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`)
- `packages_llama.go` — llamacpp-cuda, -vulkan, -hip, -metal, -cpu from ggml-org releases with an Ubuntu `libgomp1` deb and CUDA runtime archive merged in; whispercpp-cpu for Windows ARM64 only
- `security_packages.go` — bws (Bitwarden secrets CLI) and iron-proxy (egress proxy): release `checksums.txt` must cover the pinned archive and its GPG signature is verified when `gpg` exists; env allowlist for proxy children
- `packages_runtimes_manager.go` — latest versions of uv (GitHub tags), python (same minor from python-build-standalone), node (nodejs.org index), npm (dist-tags)
- `packages_tools_manager.go` — latest versions of git, gh, ripgrep and cua-driver from GitHub release tags, and ffmpeg's versions and download URL from the BtbN and martin-riedl asset indexes
- `packages_llama_manager.go` — llama.cpp latest from the Hugging Face `ggml-org/install.sh` bucket, then GitHub; reuses GitHub's published asset digests instead of downloading to hash

#### Install engine, lazy-install policy and PATH activation

`ensure` makes a package closure match the lockfile: under the store's `.install.lock` it settles any half-finished publish, fetches, unpacks, merges, stages, verifies (with one package-specific repair attempt), renames into place keeping the previous entry for rollback until the fact is recorded, then drops the fetch cache. On-demand installs are refused when `ICEBATH_DISABLE_LAZY_INSTALLS` is `1`, `true` or `yes`, when config `security.allow_lazy_installs` is anything but true or absent, or when config is unreadable; explicit commands always install.

- `install.go` — `InstalledLocation`, `Installed`, `IsInstalled`, `UvLauncher`, `InstallPackage`, `ensure`, cross-target `stageOnly` (entries marked with `.pm-stage-pin.json`), env refresh, `StorePathDirs`/`StoreFirstPath`, `Sealed`, lazy-install policy and refusal receipts
- `install_manager.go` — `Drift`/`Check`/`Outdated` (stamp comparison only, never installs), `Activate`/`ActivatePath` put installed tool dirs first on the process `PATH`
- `uv_toolchain.go` — `Toolchain`: the pinned uv and python binaries, optionally installing them; a sealed Windows payload gets a writable Python copy
- `defaults.go` — optional default packages (chromium, cua-driver) and the per-install `declined-packages.json` opt-out written by `pm install --without`; retired name `agent-browser` maps to chromium
- `user_facing.go` — sealed Windows payloads only: verified writable copies of npm, node and python so user-started commands can run them, and PATH rewriting to those copies
- `shell.go` — `Bash`: the store's Git for Windows bash first, then `ICEBATH_GIT_BASH_PATH` and Git roots (never WSL or MSIX launcher stubs); `/usr/bin/bash`, `/bin/bash`, `$SHELL`, `/bin/sh` elsewhere
- `node_probe.go` — `WithIcebathNodePath`: env with the installed npm and node on `PATH`, installing nothing

#### Host repairs: libatomic and macOS signing

Platform fixes applied while staging runtimes.

- `libatomic.go` — official Linux Node needs `libatomic.so.1`: detects it via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, `ldconfig -p` and lib dirs, picks apt, dnf, yum, zypper, pacman or apk from os-release, tries `sudo -n` once per process, and prompts interactively before the install lock only on a terminal
- `libatomic_{unix,windows}.go` — the `O_NOCTTY` constant for the `/dev/tty` probe
- `macos_signing.go` — ad hoc `codesign` of the managed Python with identifier `ai.icebath.managed-python` so macOS privacy (TCC) grants survive Python upgrades

#### Termux pool pins

The Android target installs Termux `.deb` archives, and the Termux pool deletes an archive when it rebuilds a package, so pins can vanish. The Go code only audits and repins; the library archives in the table are consumed by `packaging/termux/fetch.sh`, which republishes them as release assets.

- `termux_libs.go` — loads and saves the pin table, parses the pool `Packages` index, finds pins whose archive was replaced or dropped, repoints table rows and bionic lock rows after re-hashing; Python `urlsplit` emulation
- `termux_runtime_libs.json` — [data] embedded table of 85 pinned Termux runtime libraries (`libs`) and the `licenses` package, each with url, sha256 and version; read by `pm update --termux`

#### Locks, generation leases and orphan collection

A process pins the dependency generation it booted from by holding a byte lock on a random file under `<generation>/.leases/`; generations carrying `.lease-managed`, not selected, older than 24 hours and with no live lease are deleted. Install-state directories of deleted checkouts are reclaimed once their recorded `inputs/.project-root` is provably gone, or missing and unused past config `worktrees.install_state_retention_days` (default 14).

- `leases.go` — `RuntimeLock` (per-install `.install.lock`, readers wait 10 s then continue without it), `LeaseGeneration`, `ReleaseAllLeases` (called at exit), `LeasesHeld` with pruning of abandoned lease files
- `leases_{unix,windows}.go` — open a lease for probing (delete-sharing on Windows)
- `install_states.go` — `CollectOrphanInstallStates`: orphan test, retention, removal that spares the record and held lock; also called from worktree cleanup in `pkg/tools`
- `pid_alive_{unix,windows}.go` — is a pid alive, treating zombies as dead and other users' processes as alive
- `process_state.go` — single-letter process state from `/proc/<pid>/stat` or `ps`

#### Sync receipts and child-output progress

Every dependency sync writes a JSON receipt (`schema`, `kind`, `update_id`, `started_at`, `steps`, `venv_rebuild`, `feature_list`, `outcome`, `warnings`, `refusal`) to `<home>/logs/update_receipts/pm_<stamp>-<kind>-<pid>-<hex>.json` plus `latest.json`, keeping the newest 20; `icebath pm status` prints the latest and `icebath update` correlates by `update_id`.

- `receipt.go` — context-scoped receipt recorder (`BeginReceipt`, `RecordStep`, `RecordVenvRebuild`, `RecordRefusal`, `FinalizeReceipt`), worker receipt hand-back, rotation under `.pm-write.lock`
- `progress.go` — `LiveTail`: hides a child's output behind one redrawn status line and prints the last 80 lines on failure; `VerboseOutput` (`ICEBATH_VERBOSE`, `CI`, `GITHUB_ACTIONS`); `RunContained`
- `progress_{unix,windows}.go` — signal number to Python-style signal name for exit messages

#### Facade, in-process "worker" boundary and the foreign-checkout worker

Callers use the facade functions; each is a nil-checked function variable bound by `manager_bind.go` in full builds. In the Python original every mutating operation ran in an isolated child process; here `workerCall` runs it in the same process with a fresh receipt scope and lazy-install policy, and a real child (`icebath pm worker`, hidden) is spawned only when the target project root differs from the running binary's tree. That child speaks one JSON line per message over stdin/stdout: a request `{id, operation, arguments, update_id, callbacks, packages, context:{repo, lockfile}}`, `callback` messages for `progress` and `download_progress` answered by the client, control lines carrying a `cancel` flag, and a final `result` with `error` (Python class name, message, install-error fields) and the receipt.

- `manager.go` — exported facade (`SyncVenv`, `EnsureExtra`, `EnsurePythonTool`, `VenvCommand`, `ActivateDependencies`, `CollectGenerations`, `RuntimeRequirements`, ...), `ManagerLinked`, `ManagerAbsentError`
- `manager_bind.go` — binds the 21 facade entries to their implementations at init
- `client_base.go` — `Ensure` (answers from facts without crossing the boundary when everything is installed), policy for a non-explicit sync while lazy installs are disabled (refused unless uv and python are already installed, then run with installs off), observer-failure capture
- `client.go` — child-process request and callback relay for foreign checkouts, `managedSyncVenv` routing (binary installs provision extras directly), `EnsureToolsForSync`, `LockProject`, `EnsureEnvironment`, `CheckProjectLock`
- `worker_base.go` — [port-artifact] `PyError` and `errorClass`: the Python exception class name every pm error carries and callers branch on
- `worker.go` — `ServeWorker` and `WorkerMain`: reads the request, restores repo and lockfile paths, dispatches, relays callbacks, writes the result
- `worker_operations_base.go` — operation table entry for `ensure`, and [port-artifact] Python keyword-argument binding with Python's TypeError wording
- `worker_operations.go` — routes `sync_venv`, `venv_is_current`, `lock_project`, `ensure_environment`, `ensure_python_tool`, `check_project_lock`, decoding snake_case keywords into option structs by reflection
- `worker_{unix,windows}.go` — move the protocol pipes off the standard streams so children print to stderr; terminate a lingering worker
- `worker_pipe_{unix,windows}.go` — recognise a broken stdin pipe
- `runtime.go` — child environment for the worker (ambient Python and uv variables stripped, `ICEBATH_HOME` and `ICEBATH_RUNTIME_DIR` pinned)

#### uv engine

`PythonEnvironment` wraps one venv and runs the pinned `uv` with a scrubbed environment: `PYTHON*`, `VIRTUAL_ENV` and unforwarded `UV_*` removed, `UV_PYTHON`, `UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT`, `UV_CACHE_DIR` set, `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never`, an empty XDG config dir, default timeout 30 minutes. Index and transport settings (`UV_INDEX_URL`, `UV_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `UV_INDEX_*` credentials, `UV_INSECURE_HOST`, `UV_HTTP_TIMEOUT`, ...) are forwarded, and pip settings (`PIP_INDEX_URL`, `pip.conf` index-url, `PIP_EXTRA_INDEX_URL`, `PIP_TRUSTED_HOST`) are bridged to uv. Failures are classified from uv's output into resolver conflict, build failure (with a compiler install hint) or plain install error, and a corrupt cache entry is purged and the step retried up to three rounds.

- `environment_base.go` — `ResolutionConflict`, child exit status helper
- `environment.go` — `ManagedEnvironment`, `Create` (`uv venv`), `Lock`, `CheckLock`, `Sync`, `Check` (`uv pip check`), streaming and captured runners with tail capture, `ClassifyUVFailure`, cache recovery, `PruneSitePth`
- `index_config.go` — forwarded and redirecting `UV_*` setting sets, pip config file discovery and INI parsing, `BridgedIndexSettings`, the timeout hint text
- `uv_cache_health_base.go`, `uv_cache_health.go` — detect wheels uv reports as failing from cache and torn files in the uv cache; used by sync retry and `pm doctor --repair`
- `pip_check_base.go`, `pip_check.go` — filter `uv pip check` complaints down to those not explained by the lock's manifest overrides
- `build_compilers_base.go`, `build_compilers.go` — `shutil.which` equivalent; substitute gcc for the clang family the pinned interpreter recorded when the host lacks it; missing-compiler remedy text
- `native_build.go` — Windows ARM64 only: runs a checkout's `scripts/build/windows-deps.ps1` to prepare a build environment; that script is absent from this repository
- `venv_interpreter.go`, `venv_interpreter_{unix,windows}.go` — for sealed payloads, repoint a venv's `pyvenv.cfg` home and launcher at the payload's store interpreter

#### Shared plugin environment: generations, selection commit and boot activation

Plugins that declare Python packages share one venv per install. A sync computes a stamp (core lock digest, enabled extras, pinned python identity, member inputs), and when it differs builds a fresh generation `installs/<key>/environments/<hex>/{venv,workspace}`: the workspace is a generated uv workspace whose root is the core project and whose members are the plugin trees, locked and synced by uv; the new generation is selected by rewriting the `venv` fact and the old one stays until collected. For a binary install the core is a virtual empty project named `icebath-agent` written to `installs/<key>/core`, and a selection with no members records the stamp with no environment at all. At boot `ActivateDependencies` recovers any interrupted publication, leases the committed generation, sets `PYTHONPATH` to tree plus site-packages and prepends the launcher and venv bin dirs to `PATH`; the Go binary imports nothing from it, and consumers hand the selected venv to Python children (local execution env in `pkg/tools`, cron worker env, plugin probes and catalog commands in `pkg/plugins`).

- `packages_venv.go` — `Venv` state package (`Stamp`, `Prepare`), repair mode replaying the recorded workspace and validating it, machine uv cache `cache/uv` seeded once per lock from a payload's shipped cache
- `install_venv_base.go` — `SyncVenvOptions` (extras, explicit, repair, automatic, carried, project root, eviction, plugin input, output)
- `install_venv.go` — `syncVenv`: dependency lock, declined-extras policy, currency check, build, publish plugin change, record selection, receipt; retries without failing carried extras
- `workspace.go` — generates the workspace `pyproject.toml`, trims each member's metadata to what installs, renames virtual members, narrows resolution to the installing interpreter's platform, judges plugin requirements on the core version
- `environments_base.go` — `SelectedVenv`/`CommittedVenv`/`BaseVenv`, `SitePackages`, payload venv and launcher lookup, plugin publication rollback, and the [port-artifact] emulated Python import path (`EnsureProjectRootOnPath`)
- `environments.go` — `managedActivateDependencies`, activation env for children, publication journal recovery, generation collection, `recordProjectRoot`
- `environments_{unix,windows}.go` — machine name as Python `platform.machine` reports it
- `binary_core_base.go`, `binary_core.go` — `BinaryInstall` test (tree with no `pyproject.toml` or `uv.lock`) and the embedded virtual core project and its toolchain store
- `project_venv.go` — [py-shim] finds a checkout's pre-pm in-tree `venv` or `.venv` and reads `importlib.metadata` records to tell whether a venv installs this checkout
- `site_dirs.go`, `site_dirs_{bsd,other,windows}.go` — [py-shim] Python `site.addsitedir` and `.pth` processing (with hidden-file checks) for the emulated import path

#### Plugin membership, config publication and eviction

Decides which plugin trees are members, and makes plugin enablement and plugin code replacement transactional with the environment build. Enabled plugins are read from `plugins.enabled`/`plugins.disabled` of the root home and every live profile under `profiles/`. A change is journalled in `installs/<key>/publication.json`, then pm itself rewrites the home's `config.yaml` (comment-preserving YAML round trip) or swaps a staged plugin tree into `plugins/<name>` (with `.previous-*` backup and `.install-metadata.json` update), and rolls back on failure or at next start. During `icebath update`, a plugin that makes the environment unsolvable is disabled and recorded under `plugins.disabled_by_update` so it can rejoin later.

- `plugin_declarations.go` — `ReadPythonDeclaration`: a plugin's effective Python surface from its `pyproject.toml` or the manifest's `pip_dependencies`/`python_dependencies`/`python_runtime`; manifest version check via a host installed by `pkg/plugins`
- `plugins_state.go` — dependency homes (root plus live profiles), ordered enabled-plugin lists per home, active memory provider joining its home's list
- `workspace_base.go` — enabled plugin directory resolution (home plugins dir, then bundled), `shutil.copytree`-like copy, and `InstallNodeSidecar` (`npm ci` or `npm install` in a plugin with `package.json`, 900 s limit)
- `plugin_inputs_base.go`, `plugin_inputs.go` — the four sync inputs (`Candidates`, `Members`, `Selection`, `StagedUpdate`) and their JSON wire form
- `publication_base.go`, `publication.go` — `PluginSelection` and `StagedPlugin` publishers, config snapshots that refuse concurrent edits, journal writer, YAML node helpers
- `plugin_eviction.go` — eviction verdicts (bad declaration, Python version misfit, resolver trials per member), `disabled_by_update` record edits, rejoin of plugins that fit again
- `carried_extras.go` — finds which carried-forward extra makes the environment unbuildable, leaves it out and records why; refuses when the failure is transient
- `native_manifest_tree.go` — reads `plugin.yaml` from an `fs.FS` tree
- `plugin_python_deps_base.go`, `plugin_python_deps.go` — installed distribution lookup in the selected site-packages, `entry_points.txt` reader, marker test "does this requirement apply here"
- `python_spec_export.go`, `distribution_pins_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports: specifier-set test, pinned Python version, name and version of every installed distribution (used by the update security audit)

#### Extras: optional Python feature sets

`extras_lock.json` is `{"schema": 1, "python": "3.14", "extras": {name: {feature, aliases, anchors, requires, sources, tools, unsupported, build, packages, build_requires}}}`: `requires` and `sources` are hand-written specs, the rest is the resolution `pm lock` writes (every wheel and sdist with sha256 per package, per-target source-build lists with hash-pinned build requirements, and per-target `unsupported` reasons). Each extra is provisioned only when the user turns its feature on (never by a lazy sync) into its own generation `installs/<key>/extras/<name>/gen-<hex>/venv` (toolchain in `installs/<key>/extras-runtime` when the main store lacks uv and python), installed exactly as locked with `uv pip install` from a generated `pylock.toml`, no index, hash-checked build requirements. "Installed" is judged without running Python, by finding the anchor module's folder or file in site-packages.

- `extras_lock.json` — [data] embedded lock of 11 extras: documents, documents-pdf, google, kittentts, nemo-relay, neutts, silk, stt-whisper (alias voice), wake-openwakeword (alias wake), wake-porcupine, youtube
- `extras_catalog.go` — lock types, name and alias resolution, marker and wheel-tag matching per target, `pylock.toml` and build-constraint rendering, preflight (unsupported target, missing C/C++ compiler or git, with per-distro install commands)
- `extras.go` — anchor table and importability, platform gates from a checkout's `[tool.icebath] extras-platforms`, `declined-extras.json` with update-supplied reasons, `DroppableExtras`, `LegacySelection` (extras found in a pre-pm venv)
- `extras_base.go` — `InstallHint`: `icebath pm install --extra <name>`
- `extras_provision_base.go`, `extras_provision.go` — `managedEnsureExtra`, pinned-generation build with 90 minute limit, merged multi-extra side environments, `ExtraStates` (provisioned, current, unsupported), `ExtraPythonCommand` (`python -I`), `RemoveExtra`
- `extras_lock_gen.go` — `pm lock` in a Go checkout: re-resolves every extra with the pinned uv for six release platforms, records unsolvable targets, fetches sdists to learn build requirements, rewrites the lock when changed
- `features.go` — reads a checkout's `pyproject.toml` optional-dependencies and `[tool.icebath] opt-in-extras`
- `configured_features.go` — after an update, installs the extras that configured gateway platforms report missing and lists what is still missing
- `module_files.go` — is a dotted module present under site folders and their `.pth` additions (package dir, source file or compiled extension)

#### NeMo Relay runtime environment

The `nemo-relay` extra gets a fixed venv `installs/<key>/relay-venv` beside a private toolchain store `relay-venv-runtime` (its own facts, uv cache, `.provision.lock` and `provision-unfinished` marker), provisioned when the user switches Relay plugins on; `pkg/relayhost` consumes it.

- `runtime_environment_base.go` — `RuntimeUnprovisioned` error and the "tree has no pyproject" test
- `runtime_environment.go` — `RuntimeSet` requirements and build constraints with hashes, `EnsureRuntimeEnvironment`, readiness check by dist-info presence, private toolchain bootstrap, `uv pip install --require-hashes --no-deps`
- `runtime_provision_gate.go` — cross-process provisioning lock and unfinished marker forcing a reinstall after an interrupted run
- `nemo_relay.go` — the locked nemo-relay wheel for a target

#### Named side environments and project lock operations

`icebath pm environment NAME` and `EnsurePythonTool` build isolated venvs under `<active home>/environments/<name>/gen-<hex>/venv`, selected by `active.json` (`generation`, `inputs` digest of requirements, python pin, target and interpreter path) under a per-root `.install.lock`; a new generation is built only when inputs change. The lock and build operations on a `pyproject.toml` project serve a Python checkout only.

- `operations_base.go` — `LockProjectOptions`, `EnsurePythonToolOptions`
- `operations.go` — `ensureEnvironment`, `ensureGeneration`, `ensurePythonTool` (validates the entry point exists), `EnvironmentPython`, `buildEnvironment`, `lockProject`
- `build_operations.go` — `checkProjectLock`: refuse a missing or stale `uv.lock` without writing anything

#### Startup dependency recovery

On launch, when `<tree>/.update-incomplete`, `<tree>/.lazy-refresh-incomplete` or `installs/<key>/.repair-incomplete` exists, or the recorded site-packages is gone, rebuilds the recorded environment without changing its graph, under `.recovery.lock`, at most three automatic attempts per marker. It returns immediately when the tree has no `pyproject.toml`, so it never acts for a binary install; `icebath pm repair` forces it.

- `early_recovery_base.go` — CLI argv splitter hook (`SetCommandArgv`), `ShouldSkipExternalSecretSources` (update and import-health processes must not resolve external secrets), interrupted-pull marker path inside the git dir
- `early_recovery.go` — marker attempt counters (JSON or legacy `attempts=` line), live-owner check, recovery lock, `RecoverIfNeeded`
- `recovery.go` — `ValidateEnvironment` runs a Python script importing ruamel.yaml, dotenv, click, certifi, rich, cryptography and jwt (the old Python app's startup imports) in a candidate venv; `RepairDependencies`; `RefreshDependencies`, called from container init

#### Git lock holder probes

Finds which live process holds a checkout's `index.lock` (via `/proc`, else `lsof` and `ps` with a 20 s budget), names it for messages, and deletes the lock only when the owner is proven gone. Despite the file name nothing in pm calls it; the callers are `pkg/selfupdate` and the git lock handling in `pkg/tools`.

- `early_recovery_locks.go` — git argv parsing, checkout path matching, holder rules (daemons never, read-only subcommands only when asked), `/proc` and lsof probes, `ReleaseDeadLock`, `IndexLockHolder`
- `early_recovery_locks_{unix,windows}.go` — file owner uid, liveness, and which unlink errors mean permission denied

#### Old-updater handoff

[port-artifact] Compatibility with updaters shipped by earlier versions: an `icebath update ... --post-swap FILE` command emitted by an old updater is finished by spawning the hidden `update-takeover` entry of this binary with a request and result JSON file pair, passing checkout lock descriptors (or a Windows job) installed as hooks by `pkg/selfupdate`.

- `old_updater.go` — `SystemExit`, receipt and lock hook tables, takeover child env (no `PYTHON*`, `UV_*`; sets `ICEBATH_UPDATE_HANDOFF_PID`), `runChild`, custody wait
- `old_updater_incomplete.go` — `StopForRelaunchIncomplete`: tells the user to run `icebath update` again and exits 1
- `old_updater_{unix,windows}.go` — pass lock file descriptors to the child, or start it suspended for job binding
- `update_handoff.go` — recognises the legacy post-swap command line, maps old field names, runs the takeover
- `gateway_cmdline.go` — hook variable "does this command line look like a gateway", set in `cmd/icebath/wiring.go` and read by `pkg/selfupdate`
- `import_health.go` — name of the hidden `import-health` entry

#### `icebath pm` commands

`pm lock` (with no arguments relocks `uv.lock` in a Python checkout, or re-resolves `extras_lock.json` in a Go checkout; `--bump NAME VERSION` hashes and pins a tool for every target), `pm install [NAMES] [--extra] [--without] [--tools-only] [--trust-recorded] [--target]`, `pm env`, `pm doctor [--repair]`, `pm repair`, `pm environment NAME (--extra|--requirement)`, `pm gc`, `pm status`, `pm update [NAMES] [--check] [--target] [--skip-target] [--uv] [--npm] [--termux]`, and hidden `pm worker`. A bare `pm install` installs every required tool of the lock, puts them on `PATH`, syncs the venv (extras only when asked in a binary install), installs the optional defaults and records the owning checkout; `--without` records an opt-out and removes a provisioned extra. `pm doctor` checks each pin's facts, verification and tree digest, extras currency and uv cache corruption; `pm gc` sweeps the store, generations and orphan install states; `pm env` prints the composed env as JSON; `pm update --check` exits 1 when updates exist.

- `cli_base.go` — argument structs, stderr override, Python-style path equality and sibling sort
- `cli.go` — every command body, per-package live download progress (in-place on a terminal, throttled lines otherwise), first-install extra selection, store gc (unreferenced entries, fetch caches, old partials), `Main` error mapping
- `cli_{unix,windows}.go` — enable VT processing on a console; point stdout at stderr so `pm environment` prints only the interpreter path
- `update_base.go` — `UpdateArgs`, Unicode digit parsing
- `update.go` — `pm update`: per-target candidate intersection within the locked minor, credential-scoped index fetches (`GH_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_TOKEN`, `HF_TOKEN`, never forwarded across origins), re-pin, Termux pass; `--uv` (uv.lock), `--npm` (package-lock.json) and the `scripts/gen-bootstrap-pins.py` step act on files this repository does not contain

#### Python packaging and stdlib reimplementations

[py-shim] Format handling ported from Python libraries with their exact error classes and output spelling. What depends on it is the Python environment machinery only: requirement strings, markers, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and the state JSON files.

- `pep508.go`, `pep508_eval.go` — `packaging`: requirement, specifier, PEP 440 version and marker parsing and evaluation; used for plugin requirements and extra target matching
- `toml.go`, `toml_write.go` — `tomllib` loads with key order and `tomli_w` dumps; used for `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` and generated workspaces
- `pyjson.go`, `orderedjson.go` — `json` loads and dumps with Python number spellings, NaN and Infinity, ASCII escaping, and key-order-preserving objects for the wire, receipts and pin table
- `pylit.go` — evaluates a quoted Python string literal (marker values)
- `build_env_base.go` — `argparse` colour theme and help width (`PYTHON_COLORS`, `NO_COLOR`, `FORCE_COLOR`); used by hand-rolled argument parsers in `pkg/selfupdate`, `pkg/gatewayrun` and `pkg/acp`

#### Test seams

[test-support] Non-test file of override hooks.

- `test_seams.go` — overrides for repo root, publication writes and the uv toolchain

### `pkg/profiles` — profile identity: names, home layout constants, sticky selection, aliases, metadata and the gateway serving set

*19 files, 1,946 Go lines*

A profile is an isolated icebath home: `default` is the root home itself and every named profile is the directory `<root home>/profiles/<id>` (id grammar `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`, lower-cased). A directory counts as a profile only if it holds one of `config.yaml`, `.env`, `SOUL.md`, `profile.yaml`, `auth.json`, `state.db`, and is live unless a tombstone `<root home>/profiles/.deleted/<id>` exists (both tests live in `pkg/home`). This package holds the read-mostly core that many packages import; mutations are in `pkg/profiles/manage`. Selection is done in `cmd/icebath/profile_override.go` before parsing: `-p NAME`/`--profile NAME`/`--profile=NAME`, else an `ICEBATH_HOME` already shaped like `.../profiles/<id>`, else the sticky file `<root home>/active_profile` (ignored for supervised gateway children), and the result is exported as `ICEBATH_HOME`; a missing sticky profile is an error except for `profile list`, `profile use default` and a data-keeping `uninstall`, and `sudo icebath -p NAME` falls back to the invoking user's profiles. Eight of its 19 files import `internal/py*`, and five files are function-pointer tables that other packages fill at init so this package need not import them.

#### Names, layout constants and selection

Validation, directory resolution and the sticky active profile. Reserved names are icebath, default, test, tmp, root, sudo; a fresh profile gets the subdirectories memories, sessions, skills, skins, logs, plans, workspace, cron, home.

- `names.go` — id normalisation and validation, name suggestion, `GetProfileDir`, `ProfileExists`, `IterNamedProfileDirs`, `ListProfileNames`, the clone file lists (config files, memory files, runtime files stripped, default-home and history roots excluded), `.no-bundled-skills` marker, placeholder `.env` text, CLI subcommand names an alias may not shadow
- `active.go` — read and atomically write `active_profile` (the `profile use` switch; `default` removes the file), retarget it on rename or delete, `GetActiveProfileName` (default, id, or custom for a home outside the tree), `CurrentProfileName` (`ICEBATH_PROFILE_NAME`, then `ICEBATH_PROFILE`, then the home), `ResolveProfileEnv`
- `log.go` — package logger

#### Credential stores and export sets

The lists that decide what never leaves a profile.

- `private_paths.go` — `ProfileCredentialPaths` (auth.json, .env, OAuth and token files, vault, browser profiles, pairing and messaging session stores, `home`, backups, secret caches, OS credential dirs such as .ssh and .aws) with case-folded prefix matching and backup-copy patterns
- `export_sets.go` — pm runtime roots never exported or imported (installs, tools, cache), root entries excluded from a default-home export, and the allow list a default-profile export keeps

#### Alias wrapper scripts

Each profile can have a command named after it in `~/.local/bin`: `#!/bin/sh` plus `exec <icebath> -p <profile> "$@"` (a `.bat` on Windows). A wrapper is recognised as ours by containing `icebath -p`.

- `wrappers.go` — collision check (reserved names, subcommands, `which`/`where` with a 5 s limit), create, remove, find the alias of a profile, build the alias map, PATH membership test

#### Profile metadata and cached reads

`profile.yaml` holds presentation data: description, description_auto, display_name, bot_title, previous_names. Reads are cached by file signature.

- `meta.go` — `ReadProfileMeta`, `WriteProfileMeta` (in-place field update keeping key order), `FormatProfileLabel`, `SetProfileDisplayName` (64 character limit)
- `info_meta.go` — name, version and source from `distribution.yaml`; model and provider from a raw `config.yaml` read
- `cache.go` — derived-value cache keyed by path and kind, invalidated by mtime, size and inode, dropped whole past 512 entries
- `fileinfo_{unix,windows}.go` — inode or Windows file index for the signature

#### Distribution manifest

A profile distribution is a packaged profile with `distribution.yaml` at its root: name, version (default 0.1.0), description, icebath_requires (retired key hermes_requires still read), author, license, env_requires (name, description, required, default), distribution_owned, plus source and installed_at stamped at install.

- `distribution_manifest.go` — manifest and env-requirement types, parse and serialise in fixed key order, `ReadManifest`, `WriteManifest`, `DistributionError`

#### Gateway serving set

Which profiles one gateway process serves: without multiplexing only the active one; with it, default plus every live named profile except those whose config sets `gateway.standalone` or that hold a `gateway.parked` marker file (both ignored, with a warning, for default).

- `serve.go` — `ProfilesToServe`, `ProfileIsStandalone` (memoised on config version, tolerant of unreadable config), `ProfileIsParked`
- `shared_warning.go` — warns when another verified live installation uses the same home, from the install ledger in `pkg/tools`

#### Cross-package hook tables

[port-artifact] Function-pointer tables that `pkg/gateway`, `pkg/gatewaycli` and `pkg/cron` fill at init, because those packages import this one; `manage` panics or degrades when a table is empty.

- `gateway_status_hooks.go` — gateway liveness, served profiles, change notification, exclusive maintenance lock, pid operations, identity migrate and purge verbs; `GatewayOwnershipConflict` error
- `gateway_service_hooks.go` — service name, systemd and launchd paths, Windows task and startup entries, container service manager interface
- `gateway_channel_hooks.go` — messaging platform members, registry entries and credential table
- `cron_distribution_hooks.go` — load and import cron job definitions
- `session_search_hooks.go` — the reverse direction: hands profile name and directory resolvers to the session_search tool in `pkg/tools`

### `pkg/profiles/gatewaycreate` — create a profile through the gateway that already serves this terminal

*2 files, 339 Go lines*

Not a per-profile gateway feature: it sends one `profiles.create` RPC to a running gateway so the process that owns the home performs the create and can start serving the new profile at once. With `ICEBATH_TUI_GATEWAY_URL` set (must be a `ws://` or `wss://` URL with a host) it targets that gateway and names this terminal's profile; otherwise it discovers this home's gateway within 2 s and returns nil, meaning "create locally", when none is ready. The answer budget is 300 s. Called from `icebath profile create` in `pkg/commands`.

#### Gateway-mediated create

Classifies every outcome so the user knows whether a profile may exist: refusals answered before any handler ran (codes 4000, 5035, unknown method, invalid params, draining) fall back to local create for the home's own gateway, routing refusals and lost connections become a `GatewayCreateError` saying to check `icebath profile list`, and the wrapper script is written locally only when the gateway proved to be this machine's.

- `gatewaycreate.go` — request params, gateway naming without credentials, discovery, instance check via `runtime.describe`, `CreateThroughGateway`, refusal mapping, local alias write, redaction of warnings
- `log.go` — package logger

### `pkg/profiles/manage` — profile lifecycle: create, clone, delete, rename, export, import, distributions, listing and description

*34 files, 6,058 Go lines*

Implements every mutating `icebath profile` action (`create`, `delete`, `rename`, `export`, `import`, `install`, `update`, `info`, `describe`, `purge-identity`, `migrate-identity`, plus data for `list`, `show`, `use`, `alias`), called from `pkg/commands/cli_tree_profile.go` and the RPC methods in `pkg/tuiserver` (profile hub, `profiles.create`); gatewaycli, gatewayrun, kanban, selfupdate and app use its listing and service helpers. It reaches the gateway, service manager and cron only through the hook tables in `pkg/profiles`, and directly imports config, provider, skills, memory, mcp, state, vault, plugins and tools. A create is staged in a hidden sibling `.<id>.staging-<pid>` and published with one rename. 18 of 34 files import `internal/py*`; the process scan in delete still matches Python-era command lines.

#### Create and provision

`ProvisionProfile` runs the core create and then best-effort steps whose failures become warnings (only the core create or a config-backend outage fails it): seed bundled skills (60 s limit) and default plugins for a fresh profile, write the alias wrapper, mirror the launch profile's `.env`, logins and voice config sections, then pin a requested model or inherit the launch model. Flags map to `--clone` (config.yaml, .env, SOUL.md, skills, MEMORY.md, USER.md, plugins, memory provider config), `--clone-all` (whole tree minus history, infrastructure and runtime files; vault given its own key), `--clone-from`, `--clone-channels`, `--sync-imports`, `--no-alias`, `--isolated-auth`, `--no-credentials`, `--no-skills`, `--description`.

- `create.go` — `CreateProfile` validation and staging, clone-all and config-clone bodies, model seed for fresh profiles, reuse of a tombstoned leftover directory, multiplexer notification, `SeedProfileSkills`, `BackfillProfileEnvs`
- `initialization.go` — staging directory, placeholder `.env` (0600), default `SOUL.md`, `.no-bundled-skills` marker, description written to `profile.yaml`
- `provision.go` — `ProfileCreateRequest`, `ProvisionResult`, per-name in-process create lock, step runner, `WriteAlias`
- `provision_credentials.go` — `MirrorLaunchCredentials`: copy `.env` over a comment-only stub, strip channel keys, copy `auth.json` unless logins are shared, drop single-use OAuth grants, copy speech and voice sections
- `provision_model.go` — `WriteProfileModel` (validated assignment under the profile's own config scope) and `InheritLaunchModel` (unvalidated copy when the profile names no provider and model)
- `provision_receipt.go` — `ReceiptOf`: what `profile create` prints (path, skills, alias, mirrored items, model, served-now flag), every read best effort
- `provision_refusal.go` — failure text in errno form, refusal kinds (exists, not found, value), forced secret redaction, chunked wire form of the message
- `profile_services.go` — bridges to vault key copy and delete, log handler release, and the auxiliary LLM call

#### Clone filesystem rules

What a copy may carry and how links are treated.

- `clonefs.go` — never-copied entries (caches, sockets, temp files, non-regular files), full-clone ignore lists, symlinked root files materialised so a clone never writes through to its source, `multiplex_profiles` dropped from cloned config, plugins tree copy skipping installer staging
- `junction_{other,windows}.go` — read and recreate NTFS directory junctions instead of descending into them

#### Messaging channel inventory and strip

Two profiles holding one bot token collide, so clones drop messaging credentials unless `--clone-channels` is given, and that flag is refused when a live multiplexed gateway already serves the source. Ownership of each env key is derived from the gateway platform registry, plugin platforms in the source profile's scope, prefix aliases and policy suffixes (`_ALLOWED_USERS`, `_HOME_CHANNEL`, ...).

- `channels.go` — env key to platform index, strip of `.env` lines, config platform blocks and per-bot state entries, detection of credentials shared with the source, notices printed after a channel-less clone; also feeds the tools secret policy table
- `gateway_channels.go` — typed readers over the gateway channel hook table

#### Delete, rename and identity settlement

Delete (typed-name confirmation unless `--yes`) removes the service registration, stops the profile's gateway and stray backends, writes the tombstone, notifies the multiplexer, purges routing identity, shuts down MCP servers, closes session databases and log handlers, removes the wrapper and the tree (waiting up to 60 s for `gateway.lock` to be released, three removal attempts), and resets the sticky profile. Rename does the same teardown, moves the directory, records the old id in `previous_names`, rewrites the alias and sticky pointer and rekeys identity; renaming `default` only sets a display name. Identity is settled through the live gateway's control verb, else directly in the root and profile `state.db`; a failure leaves the action done and tells the user to run `profile purge-identity` or `migrate-identity`.

- `delete.go` — `DeleteProfile`, summary print, scan for this user's icebath processes bound to the profile by `-p`/`--profile` (still matching Python interpreter and `icebath_cli.main` command lines), graceful then forced kill, container service registration, per-OS service cleanup, pid-file gateway stop
- `delete_seams_export.go` — tree-removal function variable used by delete
- `rename.go` — `RenameProfile`, refusal when the config backend keys settings by profile name, rollback of the unroute when the move fails
- `identity.go` — `PurgeProfileIdentity`, `MigrateProfileIdentity`, checkpoint project rekey, control-answer interpretation
- `remove.go`, `remove_{unix,windows}.go` — `WaitProfileUnowned` polling the gateway maintenance lock, read-only flock probe of `gateway.lock`, make-writable retrying tree removal
- `bot_desktop.go` — full build only: stop the profile's Bot Desktop and release its lease before the directory moves or goes

#### Gateway service and liveness bridges

Thin readers over the hook tables plus the service teardown commands.

- `gateway_status.go` — gateway running, served-profile record, change notification, maintenance lock, pid helpers; panics naming the hook when `pkg/gateway` is not linked
- `gateway_service.go` — service name, unit and plist paths, pinned-home parsing, Windows task facts, identity verbs, service manager lookup
- `service_cleanup.go` — remove a system-wide systemd unit when root (else print the manual command), delete the Windows Scheduled Task and Startup items, skip definitions pinned to another home
- `stop_gateway_process_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports the pid-file gateway stop

#### Export and import

Export copies the profile to a temp tree without credential stores, pm runtime trees or non-exportable entries (the default profile keeps only an allow list of root entries), force-redacts secret-shaped strings in text and config files, and writes `<id>-<timestamp>.tar.gz` to `<root home>/profile-exports` (or a fallback outside any git checkout; symlinked or foreign-owned export dirs refused). Import requires exactly one top-level directory, extracts safely to a temp dir, drops pm runtime trees, tightens `.env` to 0600, refuses `default` and existing names, and moves the tree into place.

- `transfer.go` — `GetProfileExportPath`, `ExportProfile` (with caller-supplied extra text files), secret scrub, `ImportProfile`
- `owner_{unix,windows}.go` — owner uid of a path (unknown on Windows)

#### Profile distributions

Not asset sharing between profiles: `icebath profile install SOURCE` creates a profile from a git URL (shallow clone, `github.com/user/repo` shorthand accepted) or local directory holding `distribution.yaml`, and `profile update` re-pulls from the recorded source. The distribution owns SOUL.md, config.yaml, mcp.json, skills, cron and the manifest unless `distribution_owned` says otherwise; user data dirs and credential stores are never written, `config.yaml` is kept on update unless `--force-config`, shipped cron jobs are merged by id and arrive paused, skills merge per authored skill, and any symlink in the payload or at a target is refused before the first write.

- `distribution.go` — `PlanInstall`, `InstallDistribution`, `UpdateDistribution`, `DescribeDistribution`, `icebath_requires` version check, `.env.template` generation from `env_requires`, ownership and merge rules, swap-in replacement of directories

#### Listing and descriptions

Data for `profile list`, `show` and the kanban orchestrator's routing.

- `listing.go` — `ProfileInfo` (path, gateway running, model, provider, has .env, skill count, alias, distribution, description, display name, bot title, previous names), `ListProfiles`, skill count cached 600 s with background refresh
- `profile_info_export.go` — [port-artifact] exports single-profile info with a synchronous skill count
